## Chapter 1

The sound and even more horrifying smell of burning flesh where he couldn’t escape it, pain growing until he couldn’t stand it anymore and then continuing until he was granted with unconsciousness, the sounds of familiar voices cheering over his pain, laughter at his failure is still so fresh in his mind. Far too fresh. He can still feel, smell, and hear it all happening all over again when he thinks too hard about it.

Zuko is still in disbelief over what had happened. Sometimes not sure if he had imagined the whole thing. The pain on the left side of his face shooting through his head and down his neck is what brings him to his senses every time. Pain that is so intense that it blurs the vision in his good eye. Sometimes he can’t believe it even as the bandage completely obscures the vision of his left eye. The bandage that his hands still shake horribly from with pain as he removes it at night to clean the wound. All that time, trying to hold back tears that want to fall so badly from the pain, utter betrayal, and humiliation he feels so deep in his soul.

He learned that he shouldn’t cry on the first day he woke up. Crying only made it hurt so much more. Pain so intense he had vomited and screamed in agony, begging for his mother. His only comfort had come from his uncle. That hadn’t lasted long. Iroh had informed Zuko that he had only a week in the hospital to recover before he would be banished from the Fire Nation. Zuko had screamed himself hoarse and back into unconsciousness when he had learned that. Grief and pain overwhelming him far too much for any cohesive response to come forth.

Now, Zuko is alone. He is alone on a small ship sailing towards the Earth Kingdoms. A place he can hopefully hide in. Maybe someone would take pity on a scrawny, burned, 13 year old boy and give him a job in return for food and a place to stay.

*You need a story. Something sad so people won’t push too hard about your past. You need a name.* *Zuko is uncommon and is distinctly Fire Nation* . He tells himself.

Zuko looks across the sea, biting his lip. “My name is…Lee.” He says to himself, unsure. “My name is Lee.” He repeats with more confidence, convincing himself of his new identity. “I am from South Osoku.” Zuko has never been to South Osoku, but he saw it on a map once and overheard some description of it. He could tell people where it is if they doubted his story. Also, it is very spread out and has a low population, many of them farmers with large families. It wouldn’t be odd for someone who claimed to be from the area as well to have never seen Zuko before. He doubts he would ever run into anyone considering the low population and it being in the eastern side of the continent.

“My parents are…no, my parents *were* Fi Lo and…Nava. They were farmers. We were traveling after we lost our home and were attacked by Fire Nation soldiers. They killed my parents, and gave me this scar to leave me with a physical reminder of this day…as if killing my parents in front of me wasn’t enough. I have nowhere to go…do you know where I can find any kind of work for anything? Even for food and to sleep in a barn, please.” He can hear the desperation in his voice, hating it despite no one is around to hear the former prince begging. Or, more accurately, practicing to beg. No one is around for miles.

*You* are *desperate. You have no home, no family, no allies, you’re alone in the world. The only lie* *about that story is how you got to where you are now. You’re just as desperate and unwanted as* *the boy you're pretending to be.*

Zuko forces himself not to cry at that last thought, knowing he can’t take the pain that would be associated with it.

Zuko’s hand strays to his head, feeling the prickles of new hair growing in. He had completely shaved his head, top knot and all. That was for two reasons. The first is cultural. Zuko had lost an Agni Kai and was expected to shave his head except the top knot. However, Zuko had been banished. He had lost his country, his home, and his family. A loss akin to death. The top knot had gone too. It also had to go because Zuko would be traveling to the Earth Kingdom and the top knot would give away his nation very quickly. The second reason is because Zuko has a severe facial burn and his hair would only hinder his healing. It had to go. It all had to go.

He pulls his hand away, looking at his palm sadly. His once brilliant red robes are now a dirty grey. Zuko had done everything he could think of to get rid of the color. It would be harder to dye them green, so he had left them grey, aligned with no nation. He has no nation. It is the most accurate color for him now. It’s how he feels. Trapped somewhere between life and death, feeling too much and not feeling enough. Partially dead but forced to walk among the living as if he is still one of them.

All Zuko can do is sail forward.

He wishes that he could stay on the ship. Unfortunately, he has little experience with sailing and it has been hard enough manning the ship by himself without a crew. Every night he is left exhausted with barely half of what he has to do getting done. It leaves his body trembling in exhaustion and pain, sometimes tears leaking out as he screams in more pain to try and stop more tears from falling. He will have to leave the ship behind. Anyways, he’ll run out of food eventually. He can’t fish and sail alone at the same time. He can’t stay docked either. A ship run alone by an injured 13 year old boy is a perfect target. He would be dead or homeless within a week. May as well be on his own terms.

As he sails, Zuko is barely able to find the energy to pack a bag with the bare essentials. He packs food, a sleeping bag, the money he had brought along, hoping Fire Nation money could be spent somewhere, one other change of clothes, basic medical supplies, and his broadswords. It’s all he is able to carry. It will have to be enough. If it isn’t…well then it will be too late.

He is careful to land after sunset, not wanting anyone to see him leaving the Fire Nation ship. He has a distinct face now. Someone might recognize him later. He wouldn’t be able to explain why he was walking off of a Fire Nation ship not in shackles or running away from soldiers. All would be lost to one mistake.

Even if that is unlikely, he doesn’t want everything to end because of something so simple. He can’t do something that stupid while injured. He knows he could take most trained soldiers in combat, but not like this. Not while this injured he can’t.

Zuko just walks away from the shore. He would most likely be caught by the shore by any passing ships. The Fire Navy just grows in strength. Before he can fight, he needs to heal. His injury takes a lot of energy from him, he can only see out of one eye for now, and jostling movements send pain shooting through his body. He wouldn’t survive an attack. He has to hide until he is healthy again.

The first two nights go fine. He is able to get something in his stomach, build a fire, and sleep with relative ease. The next day he heads out again, covering ground, moving slowly away from the ocean, unsure where his destination would be. Just away, hoping to find a town.

On the third night, a storm comes. Freezing rain and high winds accompany it. He spends the better part of half an hour looking for a cave or anything that could shelter him. The rain hurts his wound as it pours down on him, his whole body swimming in pain. All too soon, he falls to his knees, unable to walk any further from pain and exhaustion. He crawls towards a large tree, trying to get any form of shelter from the wind and pouring rain.

He tries several times to build a fire, but it keeps going out no matter how hard he tries. No matter how much he begs Agni for any amount of warmth. His fire just comes out in spurts, holding it in his hands until a mix between his own exhaustion and the rain puts it out.

He tries to hold back tears but he can't. He just starts crying from cold, fear, regret, and pain. He wants to go home. He wants his uncle, his mother, anyone who would help him.

The tears feel like the fire that marked him on his injured eye and he can’t stop himself from crying out in pain from it, more tears falling. His whole body is shaking from pain and cold as he curls up, waiting for death to come find him. Waiting for death to take mercy on him. Zuko knows that he would give just about anything to go back in time and just keep his mouth shut. To learn his place. Now he is going to die in the cold, alone and forgotten. No one would recognize his body when it was found the next day.

Zuko tries to keep his little flame alight, shaking, crying in pain until he feels a large hand touch his shoulder. Zuko yelps, scrambling away, throwing his flame at the owner of the hand. His fire dissipates before it even reaches the target. It’s an Earth Kingdom man. A man who now knows that Zuko is a firebender in his country. A firebender who just attacked him.

Zuko yelps again, scrambling back, too exhausted, injured, and weak to fight anyone at all. “Please I-I’m sorry! Don’t hurt me!” Zuko begs, scrambling back against the trunk of a tree, whimpering loudly. *You’ve trapped yourself, idiot.* Zuko lets out another loud sob of fear and pain, cupping his hand over his injured eyes as pain shoots from it again.

The man steps forwards, kneeling in front of Zuko, examining him with an unreadable expression.

“Please…I-I know I’m an enemy but just…just please make it quick. Please sir, just make it quick. Please. At least have that much mercy.” Zuko begs, pulling his legs closer and shielding his face, waiting for death. Praying that the man would see that Zuko is just a scared kid, not think he had any intel on the Fire Nation and just kill him quickly. Not make him suffer anymore.

“You’re alone, aren’t you, son?” The man finally asks, touching Zuko’s arm.

Zuko presses against the tree a little harder, the hilt of his right broadsword digging into his neck. “Yessir.” Zuko whimpers. “I-I understand if you want to kill me…just please make it quick. Please, sir. I don’t know anything about anything and I-I’m banished from the Fire Nation. They don’t want me. Just… *please* have mercy.” He continues to beg, peaking at the man’s face. He doesn't care how weak and pathetic he looks. He just can't take anymore. Can't suffer anymore for just existing.

The man exhales slowly. “Come on, son, you’re freezing, let’s get you warmed up. I’m not gonna hurt you, I’m not gonna kill you. It’s bad out. As long as you don’t do anymore firebending, no one will have any reason to hurt you, alright?”

Zuko nods, whimpering a little, deeply confused, but willing to let this man do anything. It's not like Zuko could get away even if he tried. Anyways, he'll die if he stays here. Die slowly and in agony.

“I’m gonna pick you up now. Don’t attack me, the storm is only gonna get worse from here. We need to get inside quickly. You aren’t doing too well.” The man explains calmly.

Before Zuko can say anything, the man has Zuko in his arms hurrying through the woods and then through a field. Zuko can’t stop himself from whimpering the whole time as the quick movements jostle his injury.

Soon, Zuko is carried into a warm building where the wind and rain isn’t tearing at him. He is vaguely aware that it is a house made of solid stone. *An earthbender must have made this.* He thinks, clutching tighter to the man, still shivering despite the warmth in the house.

“Kani! Can you bring down your medical supplies? I found a kid alone out in the storm. He’s freezing and he has a nasty looking burn on his face. He’s hurt badly.” The man calls to someone as he takes off his shoes before carrying Zuko over to the fireplace, letting Zuko huddle next to the flames.

“Th-thank you sir.” Zuko stammers out through his chattering teeth, moving closer to the heat, the warmth slowly leaching into his ice cold body. He isn’t sure what the man wants from him, but all Zuko can focus on right now is getting warm. If he runs away now, he’ll die from hypothermia and possibly infection. His odds of survival are better here.

A tall woman, likely Kani, with long brown hair hanging freely around her shoulders in green robes comes towards them, carrying a small box, sitting next to Zuko. She touches Zuko’s face, sucking in air through her teeth when she looks at the bandage over Zuko’s eye. He isn’t sure how bad it looks after everything. He hasn’t had a chance to look.

“Oh, sweetheart, you must be in so much pain. Don’t worry, we’re gonna fix you up, you’re gonna be alright. Come on, lay down, it’s alright. Oh, and Chen, can you get me a clean cloth, a bowl of clean water, the strongest liquor we have? Also, find anything dry that might fit him at all.” Kani asks, sitting cross legged, beaconing for Zuko to lay down.

Zuko looks nervously between the man and the woman. “What do you want from me? Please just tell me. I have no chance of surviving in a storm like this and I have nowhere to go. I can’t do anything to stop you, just please tell me what you want. I’ll do whatever you want. Just please don’t hurt me and I’ll cooperate. Just what do you want? Wanna know. Need to know.” He begs, forcing his fresh tears back.

Fighting has only seemed to make Zuko’s life worse the past several years. Maybe it is time for complacency in favor of better treatment. It’s not like he had much to give anyways. They couldn’t ransom him, Zuko’s knowledge of Fire Nation war tactics is limited, and he has no allies to help him escape. Zuko could only pray that these two believe him.

“Hey, sweetheart, no one is going to hurt you. Chen, what’s going on?” Kani asks, looking at the man.

*Is he her husband? Her brother? A friend?* They’re about the same age and Zuko doesn’t know enough about either of them to accurately guess the nature of their relationship.

“He’s a firebender, Kani. He was scared, hurt, cold, and alone when I found him. I’m certain he’s alone, not just by his word, but no one would leave an injured child in the open during a storm like that. At least no one who will come looking for him. I couldn’t let him die out there.” He explains before looking at Zuko again. “You’re from the Fire Nation, not the colonies, aren’t you, son?”

Zuko nods at the question Chen asks. “Yessir…I’m sorry, sir.” Zuko isn’t sure if he is apologizing for being here, for being a firebender from the Fire Nation, or for having Chen feel bad for him. He’s just sorry. Sorry for being born.

Kani’s expression is unsure for a moment but softens. “That’s alright. We’ll figure out details in the morning but we won’t hurt you. I can promise you safety tonight. Just let me help you, please, you're in pain.”

Chen walks away, gathering supplies as Kani helps Zuko lay down. Chen sets down a large bowl of water, a bottle filled with amber liquid, and hands Kani a cloth before disappearing again.

“Do you have a name?” Kani asks as she slowly pulls off Zuko's bandage and begins to carefully clean his wound, probably better than Zuko had ever done himself. He can’t stop whimpers of pain as the cloth touches the burn. “My name is Lee, thank you for helping me, ma’am.”

“It’s nice to meet you, Lee, you can call me Kani if you would like. What are you doing out here all alone? And what did you mean that you didn’t have anywhere to go? Are you in danger? You might want to squeeze my hand, this is going to hurt.” Kani takes Zuko’s hand in her own before he can reply and presses a brandy soaked rag to his burn, causing him to cry out in pain. It stings horribly and he can’t stop from kicking his leg from it and trying not to cry again.

“There you go, there you go. The worst is over. You did so well. I’m going to put some salve on it and then re-bandage it, then you’ll be done.” Kani’s voice is encouraging as she opens a jar or foul smelling salve, but Zuko can feel it easing the pain as she applies it.

“Kani…I don’t really want to talk about my past…at least not tonight. A lot of the bad stuff is really recent and just…please, I don’t want to talk about it. Not yet at least.”

“It’s alright, Lee, thank you for being honest.” Kani says, wrapping a fresh bandage around Zuko’s wound. “There you go. Now you just need some rest and you’ll be doing much better.” Zuko just sits up slowly, moving closer to the fire again, still cold.

“Hey, this will be a little big on you, but I’m sure it will be better than your wet clothes. You go wash up and change in there. I put some warm water and a clean cloth in there for you.” Chen says, pointing towards a door on the other side of the room. “We’ll set up some blankets for you so you can sleep by the fireplace. That sound good?”

Zuko nods, tentatively taking the clothes from Chen. “Thank you sir, for everything.” Zuko whispers, standing on shaky legs and walking slowly towards the room he had been directed to.

He has to believe that these people have good intentions. That these people don’t want to interrogate him for information that he doesn’t have. That they don’t want to take any anger they have towards the Fire Nation out on him. That they don’t try to use him as some bartering chip with a country that doesn’t want him. If they did that, they would find out he isn’t Lee who is… who *is* Lee in this context? He can’t have his old story about being an Earth Kingdoms farmer, they know he’s from the Fire Nation and Chen knows that Zuko is banished.

He has to come up with something that doesn’t make him appear as a threat. Something a Fire Nation commoner could be banished for that isn’t malicious. So they don’t think that he is dangerous. As long as they don’t try and hurt him, Zuko won’t be a threat. They’ve shown him kindness so far and he doesn’t want to repay that with cruelty. He doesn’t want to be his father.

*Your older brother, Lu Ten, was killed in the war. Despite your age, you were expected to join the* *military because your father is a commanding officer. It will explain your military training, they* *might see you fight at some point. Opposed to just refusing, you publicly denounced the Fire* *Nation, the war, and your father’s lack of care for the death of his eldest son and prepared to send* *his youngest into war directly after with no hesitation. Your father burned you for saying that,* *when you woke up, you were informed that the powers that be had decided on your banishment by* *your father’s request due to your public defamation of the Fire Nation.*

Zuko nods slowly at his new story. It holds the perfect amount of truth in it that it won’t be hard to fake. These people probably think the worst of the Fire Nation and will likely believe that the Fire Nation wanted to send a 13 year old kid to war.

Once Zuko is decently cleaned up and dressed, he slowly walks out of the room back towards the fire, missing its warmth. His whole body hurts and he is exhausted. He just wants to sleep and pray that these people have pure intentions.

When he gets back, there are blankets set up, presumably for him to sleep in, and a pot hanging over the fire.

“Lee, you look exhausted. I’ll take your clothes, you sit down. Can you stay up a little longer? We’re heating up some soup. I know that Chen hasn’t eaten and I’m sure you haven’t either. Also, something hot will do you some good. Then you can get some rest. How does that sound?” Kani asks, giving Zuko a small smile as she takes his soaked, filthy clothes.

Zuko nods tentatively before he sits down, moving close to the fireplace again. “Thank you, sir, for rescuing me. I-I would have survived the night. Thank you for looking past me being a firebender. I don’t know how to thank you enough for what you did. How did you find me, anyways? What were you doing in the woods during this storm?” Zuko asks, but then anxiety that he may have started asking questions that would get him thrown out fills him. He can't go back into that storm. Not tonight. He needs to rest. “If you don’t mind me asking. I won’t ask again if you don’t want me to.” He adds hastily, looking at the ground, praying the man doesn’t throw him back out for that.

“It’s alright, Lee, I promise.” The man says, sitting down next to Zuko, putting a hand on his shoulder. “I was making sure the animals were safe before the storm got worse. I thought your fire was a flair for help and I heard screaming. You weren’t really deep in the woods, when the storm dies down I’ll show you where you were.”

Zuko nods, moving a little closer to Chen. “Thank you, sir. For everything.”

The man doesn’t reply. They sit in silence for a few minutes before Kani comes back towards them holding three bowls and a ladle. She fills the bowls with soup and passes them around before sitting down with the two.

Zuko has never tasted anything quite like this before. It’s interesting, but it isn’t bad. Most importantly, it is hot and filling. As far as Zuko is concerned, it is one of the best meals he has ever had in his life.

“Lee, Chen and I had talked while you were changing and we just need to make a few things clear. You are welcome to stay here as long as you like. We'll just need you to follow a few rules and keep your head down. We want to avoid trouble with The Fire Nation as much as you want to avoid trouble with the Earth Kingdom. Most importantly, no one else can know you're a firebender. Some people do live close by and we can’t have them see you firebending. I have no idea how they’ll react considering everything going on, some of them have lost people to this war. So just no firebending. You can start fires in the fireplace when no one besides Chen and I are inside, but that’s it. Chen has nine siblings, so if someone asks, you're our nephew and were told to not give details because of the war. People are being more secretive now. They won’t push. Better to keep it vague. If you can agree to this, you can stay, alright?”

“You’re not gonna throw me out after the storm passes?” Zuko asks in disbelief. He was going to consider himself lucky if these people even let him stay that long. He had expected to be kicked out the next day no matter the weather. He forces himself to not cry, unable to handle the pain.

Kani gives him a mournful look. “Oh, sweetheart, no. You’re injured. I understand if you want to keep moving, but at least stay until your burn heals. It was already getting infected when I looked at it earlier and still is. If you aren’t careful, you might lose your vision in that eye permanently.”

Zuko puts his half finished bowl down, wrapping his arms around Kani’s waist. “Thank you. For everything. Thank you.” Zuko mumbles into her shoulder.

Soon after, the pot of soup is put back outside on the porch with a heavy lid on it and the bowls are put away. Kani and Chen encourage Zuko to get some sleep before they disappear up the stairs. It isn’t hard for Zuko to comply. He is exhausted. He drifts off warm, safe, and dry.

The next morning, Zuko opens his eyes slowly, moaning a little in pain. His burn still hurts horribly despite the treatment, his whole body hurts despite sleeping inside, and he can’t stop shivering despite being huddled near the dying embers of the fire.

He slowly sits up, breathing heavily and unevenly, looking around at his surroundings. He is in the same position and spot that he fell asleep in last night. He hasn’t been bound, thrown out, or locked away while in his sleep. He still isn’t sure if he can trust these people, but not taking advantage of his weakened and confused state after rescuing and feeding him is a step in the right direction.

He *needs* to be able to trust Kani and Chen, even if just for a few days. Just until he is back on his feet. He might not be able to wait for his burn to be fully healed, but it can at least improve. He can wait until it significantly lowers his chance of infection. At least so he can run from here and survive. He needs that much.

He can still hear the wind and rain outside. It still sounds bad. He wouldn’t have made it this long if it wasn’t for Chen. He doubts that these people will trap him before they can do anything with him. It wouldn’t make any sense to show that they have bad intentions while being trapped inside of the house with a trained firebender.

As long as the weather inhibits travel, Zuko should be safe. When the skies clear up and they can organize what to do with him, that is when Zuko needs to worry. When they might do something to hurt him. To hand him over to someone else who would. Possibally to the military.

The sound of shuffling feet comes from his right and Zuko sits a little straighter, whimpering from the pain caused by the sudden movement. He cups a hand over his eyes, a sick feeling spreading through his body. He prays that he won’t get sick. He can’t ruin his impression on these people if they really do only mean well.

He needs to hope that they really want to help him and will allow him to leave peacefully when he fully heals. He needs just a little bit of kindness in his life to get through all of this. Unfortunately, Zuko needs to remain aware of the possibility of them stabbing him in the back. He can’t be dragged back to the Fire Nation. His father would know Zuko had no intention of looking for the Avatar, defying his father, the Fire Lord, and committing treason.

Zuko doubts his father would be merciful enough to only execute him.

“Hey, sweetheart, it’s alright, it’s okay.” Kani’s voice comes from outside of his periphery before she kneels next to him, raising her hand, silently asking permission to touch Zuko’s shoulder.

Zuko shakes his head. He needs to know if she’ll let him say no this early on. He can gauge her reaction to see what she really thinks of him. Zuko just also doesn’t really want to be touched right now.

He is surprised when she doesn’t really react, she just lowers her hand, giving him a sad smile. “I know you’re hurting. I know you’re scared. Do you want something to eat? Something to drink? When you're feeling up to it, I want to clean your eye again. Also I want you to tell me if you feel off. You might have gotten sick in that storm. It’s easier to treat it early on than to just get sicker. Alright?”

Zuko nods slowly. He doesn’t really want to talk right now or think too hard. He just needs to relax. “Can I have some tea? Any kind.” He finally whispers. He wants something nice and hot, but more importantly, he wants a small reminder of Iroh. If Iroh had found him here, he would take Zuko in, put him by the fire, and give him a nice cup of jasmine or ginseng tea.

“Of course. I have some medicinal teas, good for colds and immunity. It also just tastes good.” She walks away, filling a kettle with water and walking over towards the fire.

Zuko flinches a little when she gets close to him to hang the kettle over the fire. She gives him an apologetic look. “Do you mind stoking the fire back up for me?” She asks, walking away again.

Zuko doesn’t respond, he just begins bringing the embers back to life as he brings his knees to his chest. It doesn’t take long for the fire to begin crackling as it did last night. Zuko can’t take his eyes off it. Not for any other reason but pure exhaustion. He can’t look anywhere else or feel anything else but the flames.

“Hey…I know that you must have been through a lot in the past few weeks, especially the last few days…but are you alright? Do you wanna talk about it?” Kani asks, sitting next to him with two cups and a tin, presumably full of herbs for the tea.

Zuko just shakes his head. No, he isn’t okay, and no, he doesn’t want to talk about it. At least night right now. Maybe later. Maybe when he can bring himself to speak without it seeming like intense labor. Maybe when he can actually feel something that isn’t just…hollow despair. He isn’t even sure if that is the right description for what he is feeling. He just knows that he can barely feel anything and all too much simultaneously. It’s horrible.

“That’s alright. You don’t have to talk about it now, or ever. Neither Chen nor myself will expect you to feel better today, tomorrow, or even in a month. Healing takes a long time for both your physical wounds and emotional ones. Just give yourself time. Be patient. You have time and you have help. Alright?”

Zuko just nods once, unable to think of anything else to say or do.

Kani takes the kettle off of the fire, putting a pinch of herbs from the tin into the diffuser basket and replacing the lid, allowing the tea to steep. She doesn’t say anything else as they wait. She just sits next to Zuko, watching the fire absently. He likes that.

After several, peaceful minutes, she pours tea into each cup, handing one to Zuko.

He turns it in his cup in his hand, looking at the liquid for a long moment. He watches Kani silently, refusing to drink from his cup until she drinks from hers.

It takes several sips until he is convinced that she is actually drinking the liquid and isn’t faking it before Zuko begins to drink from the cup that she poured him.

It’s good. It soothes his throat and warms his body. He closes his eyes again, taking another sip. It really is comforting. He hopes that these people are good and kind who only want to help him. He would love to stay here. He will work hard for them, do whatever they want if they treat him well, give him shelter, and feed him.

He wants to be able to drink tea and eat soup in front of a fire, have someone tend to his wounds, feel loved and wanted like he had last night despite Zuko being a stranger to these people, they took him in. He wants them to love him. He has no idea what he would give for that.

Just about anything. Everything, maybe.

“Can I clean your burn again? It's going to take a lot for it to heal without complications, and keeping it clean is important to warding off infection.” Kani asks, setting down her now empty cup of tea, looking at Zuko with a soft gaze.

Zuko bites his lip, nodding once.

Kani stands up, collecting supplies. Zuko just looks at his cup, occasionally taking small sips, still not feeling all that well. He really has no idea what would help him. He isn’t sure if his discomfort is caused by physical injury and illness or emotional distress. Both almost certainly play a role.

“Will you put your head on my lap again? It will be easier. I’ll be able to clean your burn better.” Kani offers as she sits cross legged, gesturing for Zuko to come closer to her.

He slowly lays down, nestling his head in her lap like he had the night before. He closes his eyes. He feels safe and comfortable like this. He’s exhausted despite sleeping well for the first time in weeks.

The bandage is pulled gently from his face and he winces a little as the dried fluids attached to it pulls on the sensitive skin.

Zuko can’t stop a few whimpers from escaping his lips as she cleans the damaged area. He hears her quiet apologies and comforting words as she continues. Finally, he feels the salve being applied before rewrapping his eye with a clean bandage.

“Hey, Chen, can you come over here? Lee feels a little warm…wanna make sure that it isn’t just me.”

Zuko flinches a little as he sits up when Kani is talking to Chen. He hadn’t heard the man walk into the room. He has no idea how long Chen had been there.

“Is it alright if he touches you? You might have a fever from infection, being in that storm, or both. Just need to be sure so I can properly monitor you. I promise he won’t hurt you.” She says softly, likely in reference to Zuko’s desire to not be touched and not any mistrust of Chen. He had saved Zuko’s life last night even after Zuko had tried to attack him.

Zuko nods once as the farmer kneels in front of him, moving a hand forward, touching Zuko’s upper back and then his forehead before pulling his hand away. “Yeah, you feel a little warm, son. You look pretty flushed too. It might not be her profession, but Kani is a skilled healer. You’re in good hands, kid.” He reassures.

Zuko nods once, biting his lip before speaking. “I do have a good amount of control over my temperature…but firebenders do tend to run a little warm.” He explains softly, wrapping the blanket around his shoulders again, seeking the warmth.

“Alright, thank you for letting us know. There won’t be too much to do outside besides feeding the animals so it will be easy to keep an eye on you. Please tell one of us if you start feeling bad. Illness and injury is easier to treat early on. In the meantime, it will be good to keep up your strength. Do you want something to eat?” Kani offers, filling her cup again and offering it to Chen who takes it, drinking the tea silently.

“Promise.” He mumbles, laying back down, not answering the part about eating. He isn’t sure if he has the energy to eat right now. He isn't all that hungry. Maybe later today. Right now, he just feels exhausted, like his body is demanding sleep above anything and everything else.

He moves a little closer to the fire, cocooning the blankets around him, slowly syncing his breathing with that of the fire, inhaling and exhaling as the flames rise and fall. As they come alive from his breath. He can hear the voices of the farmers, not paying close enough attention to understand what they’re saying before he drifts off to sleep again.

A hand rests on his arm, he feels his body being gently shaken, flickering his eyes open a little, moaning softly. He feels horrible. His vision in his good eye swims, he feels nauseous and in overwhelming pain. He feels sticky and gross. It’s hard to breathe and he is just so cold.

“I’m sorry for waking you up, son, but you’re burning up. You need to drink something. Kani made some tea for you and is making something simple for you to eat. You need to stay hydrated.” Zuko hears Chen say distantly despite knowing that the man is right next to him, practically talking into his ear. Close enough that he can feel the man’s breath.

Zuko just whimpers a little in response, clutching the blankets tighter, too weak to pull them back on himself if they fall from his grasp.

He feels his body propped up in a sitting position against Chen’s chest, he nestles his head closer, seeking warmth in any way.

He feels a cup being pressed to his lips and tipped back and feels lukewarm liquid trickle past his slack lips. It isn’t good, it isn’t exactly bad either. Its mediocrity is likely brought on by the temperature.

“Sorry that the tea isn’t hot, Lee, but I didn’t want to give you anything too warm. I figured being close to the fire is more important to you than eating something hot.” He hears Kani say out of his field of vision. Zuko can only bring himself to whimper softly in response.

Chen takes the now empty cup of tea from Zuko’s mouth and then begins to slowly feed him lukewarm rice and broth. It really isn’t that good, but he’s hungry, and he can’t bring himself to think about anything that he would actually want to eat. He’s just exhausted and far too weak.

He can hear gentle encouragement from the man. He still isn’t sure if he can trust these people but he feels safe. They could do anything they wanted to him right now and Zuko would be unable to stop them. He likely wouldn’t even be able to form anything cohesive in just words. However, they are choosing kindness when they don’t have to. It helps ease his nerves a little.

After eating his soupy rice, Chen prompts Zuko to drink a little more water before laying him back down by the fireplace. He says something that Zuko can’t fully make out as he drifts back into a deep, uneasy sleep.

When Zuko had left in the night without him, Iroh had mourned his nephew's death. When Iroh had heard of the hurricane in the Earth Kingdom, he had truly mourned all over again. It had been a hard night even while he was already processing his grief. For thirteen days after the sun had set, Iroh would go to the courtyard with the turtle ducks, Zuko’s favorite place in the palace, and he would light a candle.

Each candle he lit would last an hour. An hour of mourning for each year of Zuko’s short life. He would pray that he would see his son and his nephew again after his own passing. Apologize that he couldn't protect them. Because he failed to protect them, their lives had been cut too short.

Every day, for just under the fortnight of his mourning, Iroh would travel into the city during the day. He would find a candle the color, shape, or the scent of something that reminded Iroh of Zuko. A way he could remember the poor boy’s life.

On the first day, he had been too distraught to think of anything abstract, and he had found a simple, purple colored candle, Zuko’s favorite color. He hadn’t bothered to smell it and found he didn’t like it after he lit it. He still kept it for the full hour and thought of his nephew.

His sweet, gentle nephew who just wanted to be loved by a man who didn’t know what it was to care for another living being in any way. Only saw them as things to be useful to him. Exploited them and then left them behind when they had nothing left to give, when they could no longer be used. Even his own child.

The first night, Iroh had just cried the entire time the candle was lit while thinking this. He had cried hours after the candle went out as well. He had cried himself to sleep that night, waking up to a servant shaking his shoulder, offering him tea and comfort.

The second day, Iroh had found a candle shaped like a turtle duck, he still hadn’t been able to think past the basics of what Zuko liked. Of what reminded him of his nephew, taken from this world far too painfully at an age far too tender. He hadn’t even thought that when he burned it at night, the turtle ducks wouldn’t take kindly to Iroh burning one of their own, even if made of wax. However, Iroh had more important things on his mind than an unhappy turtle duck.

The third day, Iroh had found a candle that smelled like fire lilies. They had become one of Zuko’s favorite flowers after Ursa had disappeared. One of the guards would put a fire lily in Zuko’s room every morning while they were in bloom. Iroh isn’t sure if there was any significance to the flower that the guard had chosen other than she just liked it, but it has quickly become a symbol of protection and kindness to Zuko. he pressed and saved every flower that the guard gave him. Iroh isn’t sure if Zuko still knows where those flowers are or if Ozai found them and disposed of them.

When fire lilies would bloom in the years after that, Zuko would spend time finding and smelling the bright, delicate flowers. Somehow, Ozai either never found out, or never cared enough to punish Zuko for being happy.

Ozai would of course frame it as wasting time and acting like a child. What it all would really boil down to is Ozai wanting to take every bit of joy from Zuko’s life that he could. Break him in every way possible before killing him at 13.

The fourth day, Iroh had found a candle that smelled like roses, that was Ursa’s favorite flower. She would spend hours tending to rose gardens she planted. Zuko would help her when he wasn’t being mercilessly drilled by his father. When Ursa died, Zuko had done his best to tend to the roses, Ursa had always wanted to tend to those herself opposed to letting the gardeners do it. Zuko’s hands would be cut up from the thorns in his stubbornness.

Unfortunately, within two weeks of Ursa’s disappearance, Ozai had burned down the roses while Zuko was forced to watch. The boy had cried for days afterwards, clearly feeling like he had lost his mother all over again.

The fifth day, he had found a candle that smelled like jasmine, Zuko’s favorite tea. Iroh had always suspected that Zuko didn’t actually have a strong enough opinion on tea to have a favorite and had said jasmine to make Iroh happy. It had. Iroh had never confronted his nephew about it on the grounds that it wasn’t all that important.

Despite Iroh having a definitive favorite tea, ginseng, he would sometimes drink jasmine tea just to remember his sweet nephew. The night he burned the jasmine candle was one of those nights. It was also one of the nights he cried himself to sleep in the courtyard.

On the sixth day, he found a candle kind of shaped like a fig. He is pretty sure that it was just deformed, but Iroh didn’t care. When in season, he and Zuko would sometimes go find a fig tree and eat them when he had told his brother he would teach Zuko that day so Ozai could focus on Azula. He still regrets that he hadn’t taken Azula under his wing sooner. He had watched her suffer for three years and done nothing. He had only done something when he needed her. When Zuko had died too. When Iroh had gotten a second son killed within three years of each other.

On the seventh day, Iroh had found a candle that smelled like lavender. A few months after Ursa disappeared, Zuko began panicking more often when Ozai would strike him or scream at him. It became easier to work the boy into a panic and harder to calm him down. Iroh would find him far too often curled up in a corner, sobbing, trembling, and barely able to breathe out of fear. It would always break Iroh’s heart to see.

One of the servants had said lavender had a calming effect and that it would work on his wife while she was pregnant. He would wash Zuko’s clothes with lavender and keep it by his bed. On bad days, he would help prepare a hot bath with lavender oil in it.

It didn’t fix the underlying problem, but it seemed to help Zuko calm down a little faster, help him sleep better, and keep him somewhat calmer for longer. Anything that helped Zuko feel even a little better was worth doing.

On the eight day, Iroh found another lavender candle, but it was purple, and he couldn’t stop himself from wanting to do it again. The smell had helped calm Iroh a little as well. It didn’t bring back his dead nephew, but it made him feel a little less horrible.

On the ninth day, he found a candle that smelled like orange and lemon. There wasn’t anything in particular that Iroh could attribute the smell to, he just thought that Zuko would enjoy it. That it might make him a little happy if he were still alive and well in the palace. If Ozai hadn’t been the man he was. The man he is.

On the tenth day, Iroh found a candle that smelled like silver wisteria. The plant grew in the palace gardens and Zuko always loved the smell of them. He loved to lay in the grass by the vines when they were in bloom on a warm sunny day. He liked the way the vines grew and had pure while flowers producing a delicate smell that somehow filled the air. It was one of the few things that Zuko was allowed to enjoy without ridicule.

On the eleventh day, Iroh had found a pine scented candle. Where pine isn’t common in the Fire Nation, but Zuko did enjoy the way the trees smelled and it is something Iroh had always enjoyed as well. When in the Earth Kingdom, he did not enjoy how easily sap from the trees would get on his clothes and would be nearly impossible to get off. They still smelled nice though.

On the twelfth day, Iroh had found a candle that smelled like sandalwood. It was a common soap at the palace and one that both Zuko liked and Ozai didn’t criticize him for using. Iroh never understood why Ozai gave a shit about what soap Zuko was using or why the man was smelling his son. He had come to the conclusion long ago that Ozai is just crazy and wants everyone to be just as miserable as he is.

Tonight is the thirteenth day after his nephew’s disappearance, Iroh can only bring himself to just burn an unscented, uncolored, standard, wax candle. He can’t stop crying.

He sees a figure in the corner of his eye, turning towards them, not bothering to wipe his eyes, expecting it to be a guard coming to check on him to make sure that Iroh is just mourning and not injured.

To his surprise, he sees his niece, Azula. She walks towards him, sitting next to him silently, pulling her knees to her chest and resting her chin on them.

The two of them sit in silence as the candle burns. Silent tears fall from Iroh’s eyes and Azula just looks dead ahead.

When the candle burns out, Azula finally speaks. “Zuzu’s in a better place now. He’s safe, uncle.” Her voice is unusually hoarse. She must have been crying and done a good job of covering it up. More likely, she had been screaming. She gets her emotions out with anger, not grief.

“Since when do you believe in an afterlife?” Iroh half jokes, wiping his eyes again, more tears falling.

“I don’t.” She replies flatly, still looking ahead.

Iroh cocks his head, confused by the whole interaction.

She must be able to see him in her periphery because she addresses his confusion. “I mean father can never touch him again. Zuko can never be hurt by that man again. He’s safe now. He’s safe even if I’m not. If we’re not.”
