## Chapter 2

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

You guys actually get a much earlier chapter than expected, written on mobile. My Americorps crew is awesome, they're all super cool people and the woods are great but I am constantly wet bc that is how the east coast is (I'm actually working in Ohio now so not really east coast but still, wet town).

### Text

Lee hasn't been able to do much the past four days. He mostly lays on his bed near the fire, sleeping. Sometimes he starts making small whimpers of pain and fear. He usually needs to be woken up and coaxed into eating or drinking something, likely unaware of what is being pressed to his lips.

He must be in so much pain.

He's so young, so scared, and so fragile. Someone who was supposed to protect and love him unconditionally had broken him.

Kani has cleaned his eye as often as possible, whispering encouragement she isn't always sure he hears as she does.

His illness is a mix of his infection and being out in that storm. He probably wouldn't have made it if Chen had found him even an hour later. He's barely pulling through now.

Anything he says isn't very coherent, it's mostly garbled apologies and thanks.

Kani is well aware that she barely knows Lee, but he's so sweet and gentle. She doesn't understand how anyone could want to hurt him. How anyone could have hurt him this horribly with no remorse.

She nor Chen are sure how much of his story is true. How much he is concealing about himself, if any. He would have to be an outstanding actor to spin a story as horrible as the one he had told. There *has* to be an element of truth to it.

She doubts a kid his age could lie that well about something that horrible. Especially when burned, freezing, and absolutely terrified.

Kani and Chen have tried to stay on task as much as possible around the house and farm. However, it has been hard for one of them to not gravitate towards Lee. They both always want to be checking on him, rubbing his stomach, head, or shoulders to try and soothe his pain and fear. Try and let him know that he's somewhere safe where people will protect him and not lash out at him for nothing. Not burn him for wanting to mourn and live.

It's nearly impossible not to mourn for the little boy they barely know. He is in so much pain. Clearly faced so much cruelty in his short life.

He's mostly lean muscle, like he's strong, but she can see almost all of ribs. His stomach is a little caved in, his face is gaunt and shoulders are bony. She can see them sticking out when the borrowed robes fall down the arms of his slender figure.

She doesn't know how long he has been traveling alone, it could be the answer for being so skinny. Unfortunately, she knows he is from a punishment based abusive household whether or not Lee knows that. No one that loves their child or even somewhat *cares* would send their young son to war after their first one died. Not only that, but then proceeded to punish Lee when he didn't want to go. Had hurt him so badly that he saw the cruelty of his entire nation as he was thrown away.

What she is mostly worried about is that as soon as Lee is back on his feet he'll run, scared of being hurt again if he allows himself to settle.

Where Lee isn't naive to cruelty, he's likely naive to how the world is. What some people might do to a young boy traveling alone who can't use his bending without exposing himself. Whose a fugitive from two nations.

She doesn't know what might happen to Lee if he runs, but she doubts it will be good.

While he is still recovering, she and Chen have been explaining to the neighbors that their nephew had come to stay with them. That he had been attacked by a Fire Nation soldier in his home town and doesn't feel safe there anymore. That he doesn't want to talk about his burn or, eventually, his scar. That he doesn't want to talk about his past at all.

They have refused to give anymore details on what happened to Lee's parents, Chen's sister and brother in law. Saying that it isn't important for their business if pressed.

One thing Kani has learned about lying is that it's better to keep it simple. Some things aren't people's business. She likely wouldn't tell them these details if it really happened, so why would she now?

Also, less information to keep up with. The more detail, the easier it is to back oneself into a corner.

She hears another soft cry pass Lee's lips as his body twists in pain.

"It's alright sweetheart." She reassures, rubbing Lee's stomach as she speaks. "You want some more water?" She pours some water into a cup with her free hand, watching Lee's flushed face.

Lee cracks his good eye open, closing it before opening it again slowly.

Kani takes this as a yes, propping Lee's head up on her lap, helping him swallow small sips of water, praying it helps with his rising fever. It had gotten to the point Kani had to put the fire out. Lee still got upset when Chen tried to move him from the hearth. So they left him there. He seems somewhat comfortable.

"There you go sweetheart. There you go. How do you feel?" She asks, wiping sweat from his forehead.

Lee opens his eyes again, looking at her distantly. "Mom?" He whispers, trying to lift his hand which quickly falls back down to the floor.

Kani feels a pang of pain for the little firebender on her arms. "It's Kani, sweetie, but I can be your mom if you like, okay? You need a home. I'll keep you safe." She kisses his hot, sweaty forehead affectionately.

"Mom?" He repeats, voice a little more high and winey, eye squeezed shut now, fear and pain on his face.

Kani sighs, looking at the little boy sadly. "Yeah, sweetheart, I'm right here." She replies, cupping his cheek, trying to get him to feel safe. He doesn't know where he is and is looking for a child's most innate protector.

"I'm right here, I've got you. You're safe." She reassures him, pulling the tiny firebender into her arms. The little boy many may have killed or arrested upon discovery, left to suffer and probably die in a cell, terrified the entire time.

Lee nestles the uninjured side of his face against her shoulder, still trembling a little. "Why did you leave me?" He half sobs, clutching tightly to her robes, unwillingly to move away from her.

Kani pulls him a little closer, slightly confused. "I'm not leaving you. I'm right here." She tries to reassure him, rubbing his back, rocking him gently in her arms.

"Y-you left me with him. He hurt me. You said you loved me...then you left." He whimpers, now crying quietly, no tears falling, at least not yet. Kani hopes it stays that way or Lee will be in for a world of pain.

To be safe, she rests Lee's head back on her lap, beginning to make a fire in case she needs to boil water as she talks to Lee quietly.

"I don't know what happened to you, Lee, but I will love you like your mother should have. I won't let anyone hurt you. I won't leave you, sweetheart. All you have to do is stay." She whispers, kissing Zuko's forehead again before standing and filling a kettle with water, grabbing a bowl and clean cloth before sitting back next to Lee.

The firebender is breathing heavily. She puts the kettle on the fire before sitting down next to Lee again, pulling his head into her lap and rubbing his heaving stomach.

"Can you hear me? Please talk to me. What do you need?" She's worried about Lee's lack of awareness. Worried about how many horrible things this poor kid has been through. Worried about how little kindness he has likely received throughout his life.

If Lee chooses to stay with them, she and Chen will have their work cut out for them in teaching this kid about kindness. How people should talk to him and touch him. How he deserves to be treated well and not thrown out just because.

She isn't sure if it's the best idea to keep a firebender kid she knows nearly nothing about, especially one as clearly mentally unstable as Lee. But she nor Chen can send the boy away in good conscious.

If his father burned his face and requested for his banishment over an argument, the man likely escalated the fight into Lee denouncing the Fire Nation. She had no clue what other abuse Lee had faced.

She now knows that his mother left when he was young. Possibly to get away from an abusive husband.

In most circumstances, Kani would applaud anyone escaping a situation like that, but she left her *child* . Her child who must have been old enough to remember her. Old enough to be close to her. Close enough to have her absence break his little heart.

Close enough to her that a lot of Lee's pain may have been the boy's father redirecting cruelty from the boy's mother onto a fucking child when she left. It's a story far too common.

Lee had expected to be thrown out as soon as the storm passed. If that were true, he wouldn't have made it to the tree line. He's really sick. If he isn't any better by tomorrow, she'll take him into town to a proper healer with supplies and more hands to help.

Kani has no idea what kind of person would throw a sick, injured child out. The man Lee had come from must have. Lee's banishment had begun long before he could heal properly. Lee's father had sent his boy to die. His kid who can't be much older than twelve. He's so young.

If that is the kind of abuse this kid has faced, she has no idea what kind of cruelty he would accept if he were to be just sent into the world without teaching him how he should be treated.

Lee would likely look for work if he left here. He doesn't have anywhere to go. He's only a child so he would likely work as a farmhand or something similar in exchange for somewhere safe to stay and food. Maybe some wages, but likely just for some person who needed an extra hand.

There are good people in the world who would give Zuko what he needed in exchange for his work, not push him beyond his limits, and treat him fairly.

Unfortunately, Lee is vulnerable, naive, alone, and could easily be exploited. There are definitely far more people who would take advantage of his ignorance and youth.

What she is most worried about is that Lee is used to violence. Being hurt is something normal to him. Kindness is something that would make him want to stay, but violence wouldn't drive him away.

If he were struck by someone, he would likely sooner accept he had done something wrong than he has been abused his entire life and it has warped his perception of reality. He might even stay somewhere if his fingers or nose were broken. It might take until a concussion or broken arm for him to leave. Possibly not even then.

Lee hasn't even left willingly when his own father burned a third of his face. He had to be thrown out of his country. He might stay somewhere thinking he could prove himself, thinking he could get someone to care about it until it ends in him losing his life.

It wouldn't be because Lee had done anything wrong, there are just horrible people in this world. People incapable of compassion.

It is what she is most worried about. If they don't persuade Lee to stay here when he's back on his feet, if they don't try to help him, something irreversible will happen to him. She wouldn't be able to live with herself if something happened to Lee while trying to find somewhere he could be safe.

She also can't get the thought out of her head that Lee is very vulnerable to assault. He's young, alone, desperate, and wants someone to love and care about him so desperately. He doesn't know what love looks like.

She hates that there are sick, twisted people in this world who would willingly hurt a child, or anyone, like that or at all. She needs to help protect this boy while he falls apart. While not only is he thrown into an unfamiliar nation, but his past will be warped as he understands what was done to him. Really understand. Understands why and how he is damaged and how he needs to heal and protect himself. How he needs to move forward.

He'll need support. He needs help that neither she nor Chen can give him. What they can do is treat him well and not take advantage of him.

The bare minimum.

They can at least offer him safety which he can't be guaranteed elsewhere.

She can hear the water boiling and takes it off the fire, setting it on the hearth. If they don't need it now, good. It doesn't need to be warm to clean Lee's eye, just sanitary.

"Lee?" She asks quietly, looking at the boy's now slack expression. Better than being twisted in pain.

"Can you hear me, love?" She whispers, kissing his forehead as she moves him a little further from the fire again.

Lee mumbles something that sounds a lot like 'love you too.'

Kani smiles, hugging him gently. She won't let anyone hurt this sweet little boy again. He doesn't deserve what's been done to him and she doubts he can take much more without it changing him.

She doesn't care who she has to stand between. They aren't touching Lee.

It takes almost a full week for Zuko to be fully back on his feet. Kani told him he was having so much trouble recovering because his body had been fighting illness brought on by prolonged exposure to freezing rain and malnutrition since his banishment and then fighting an infection from his burn.

He isn't really sure what had happened the last four days. He had been plagued with a terrible fever, chills, fatigue, and nausea.

Today, Kani and Chen still want him to rest today after being so sick for that long.

Every so often, one of them will come and check on him, ask him how he is doing, and just talk to him. It's nice.

Most of their work is outside on the farm. They clean the house together, Kani does all maintenance as she is an earthbender, and does most of the cooking. Chen does blacksmithing which is apparently set up outside the barn. Zuko hasn't seen it yet.

Zuko still isn't sure what he should expect from these people or what they want. They haven't hurt him yet, but there are so many ways to hurt a person with so much time to do that.

He isn't sure if he should run. He isn't healthy yet and he has nowhere better to go. He doesn't know anyone. He's trapped with no walls or chains. He can't go anywhere. If he didn't know better and didn't have years of experience with forcing himself not to, he would cry.

Tears would burn his eye after it is finally down to just painful as opposed to excruciating. He doesn't want it to become worse again. He also knows that things can always get worse when he starts crying. Now that he can control it, he might get in trouble for his tears. He doesn't want to anger these people so soon.

Zuko is looking at the glowing embers when he hears the door open, he can't stop himself from flinching a little, hugging himself a little tighter.

"Hey, it's alright, son." Chen says softly, taking off his boots and walking towards Zuko slowly, one hand extended like he were approaching an injured animal.

Zuko looks down at the floor, wishing he wasn't so weak. Wishing he had been good enough for his father who threw him out, for his uncle who Zuko was only a bandage to cover a Lu Ten shaped hole in his heart, or his mother, who had left Zuko behind. Who may have claimed to love Zuko, but she left him behind with his father. She left him to his mercy. His mother should have known how little his mercy his father has for anyone.

Zuko wishes he could ever be good enough for anyone. He just wishes he could belong somewhere. That someone, anyone, could want him. Could at least tolerate him. He doesn't need them to love him, he needs them to just be kind.

"Would you like some tea? Lavender might be good for your nerves." Chen offers, voice coming from the kitchen. Zuko hadn't heard the man walk away.

Zuko bites his lip, nodding once, unsure what answer would be preferred. He hopes he picked the right one.

The man picks up a tin, fills a kettle with water, and carries over two cups. He sets the kettle on the fire before looking at Zuko. "Can you start up the fire, Lee?" He asks.

Zuko nods jerkily, shooting fire at the hearth, hands shaking as the fire rises higher.

He doesn't want to firebend in front of Chen. He always wants to pretend he is an Earth Kingdom nonbender. He just wants to fully be a new person. He wants Prince Zuko to die like he is sure the Fire Nation thinks.

As soon as the fire is a good height, he wraps his arms around his knees again, hoping he didn't just do anything wrong. It's been almost a month since anyone has hit him. The longest he has gone in years without being struck. He doesn't want that to change even though most of that time he was alone.

"What do you like to do? Like before everything happened when you were back in the Fire Nation?" Chen turns towards Zuko as he speaks.

The question catches Zuko off guard and he jumps a little. He composes himself and shrugs. "I'm decent at sword fighting...not allowed to do it anymore, though. Still have my swords. Not really particularly good at anything else. Sorry, sir." He whispers.

He knows he isn't a good firebender. His father had made sure Zuko knew that. He could never be a good firebender. He's a disappointment. A failure. He needed melee weapons to make up for his weakness. Eventually, despite the fact Zuko had gotten good with swords, the sight of his son using swords disgusted Ozai enough to forbid Zuko from practicing in sight of anyone ever again.

It hadn't been long after his mother disappeared.

"Do you like sword fighting?" Chen asks.

Zuko shrugs. "I-I dunno...should I not? Or should I? I'm sorry." He whimpers, closing his eyes, willing himself not to cry, unsure what he should say. He wishes he could actually be good at something so as to not disappoint everyone.

"Hey, hey, Lee, son, I'm not trying to scare you or stress you out. There isn't a right or wrong answer. I just wanna get to know you a little. You won't be made fun of or hurt for anything you enjoy. For instance, I enjoy playing music. I'm terrible at it, but I like doing it after a stressful day." Chen offers forward as he moves the kettle off the fire and puts lavender in to steep.

Zuko looks up at the man, searching for dishonesty. "I-I guess I like theater, other arts but mostly theater...and animals. Like theater a lot." He admits quietly, waiting for a blow that doesn't come.

"Lee...can I touch you? I won't hurt you, I promise." The man says softly, pouring the tea, setting a cup near Zuko.

Zuko swallows, looking away from the man's large, calloused hands and burly arms from years of farming and blacksmithing. He tries to not think of how horribly the man could hurt him with little effort and no bending.

He nods quietly, closing his eyes, bracing himself for whatever the man wants to do, unsure why he is asking for permission. It might be for the illusion of choice and freedom. Wanting Zuko to know he is responsible for everything strike brought upon him. Zuko isn't sure what he has done to warrant punishment or cruelty, but he usually doesn't understand. His father had always attributed that to stupidity.

"You can say no if you want, Lee. I want to hug you because you seem upset but I don't want to touch you if you don't wanna be touched and scare you more. Please say no if you don't want to be touched, son." Chen reassures him.

Zuko looks up at the farmer skeptically for a long moment before nodding slowly, moving towards Chen a little.

He can't stop his body from tensing when he feels Chen wrap his arms around Zuko's waist, resting a large hand on the back of Zuko's head, pulling the good side of his face against Chen's chest.

They stay like that for a long time before Chen speaks. "Lee, I don't know what has happened to you, but I know it's bad. If you ever need or want to talk about this, we'll listen. If you only want to talk to one of us, that can happen. If you never want to talk about your past, you don't have to. Whatever you need. I want you to know that you're safe now. You're safe." He swears, pressing his lips against the top of Zuko's head.

Zuko can't hold back a loud sob. Carefully nuzzling his face closer to Chen's chest, conscious to not touch his injury to the fabric of the man's clothes that he grasps at desperately, trying to not let tears fall.

"Hey, hey, it's alright, it's alright, I've got you. You're safe now, I've got you." Chen promises as he rubs Zuko's back methodically.

Zuko wants to stay here forever. He wants these people to truly be kind, needs them to be. He wants to heal and live here. He'll work hard, do whatever Kani and Chen want him to if he can just be held like this and comforted. He never wants to leave.

"Can I r-really stay here until I heal?" He chokes out. If that's the case, he never wants to heal. The pain shooting through his face would be worth easy praise and gentle touches. He doesn't want to go. He knows it's dangerous and stupid to trust these people, but his options are limited and all pretty bad. He has met people who are at least not only going to give him time to heal but help him heal. People who will at least pretend to care about him.

The young soldier who has been raised to be just that since birth says to go. He says to run. As soon as he figures out everything that Kani is doing to mend his wound and it is doing a little better, he should pack some supplies and run.

These people have shown him kindness whether it was genuine or not. The soldier in him holds no ill will against them, doesn't want to hurt them, it just doesn't trust them.

Right now, his options are very limited. Once they are better, he needs to go. He can't just rely on hope and good will. He needs to find a job from people who think he's an injured Earth Kingdom kid and work for them. They still need to see him injured, his burn can't be fully healed. He'll be more likely to get a job, get a chance to get his feet on the ground.

He will be able to network from there. He can meet new people, get a better job based on merit opposed to pity. He needs pity for now. No one would hire an inexperienced 13 year old kid for no reason.

Then, there is the child who just wants a family. Just wants someone to love him. Wants a place to call home. That part of him is screaming to stay, begging for this gentle touch, craving to be held.

It wants to belong here, wants for Zuko to prove himself, have Kani and Chen eventually think of him as their own. Just love Zuko in a way his father never could. In a way he was stupid enough to think his mother did.

"Yes, please stay until you're well again. Neither of us want you to leave until you're healed, but we won't keep you here. However, you can stay as long as you like. As long as you behave, this can be your home."

Zuko swallows nervously. He's always managed to break rules. He wouldn't have been punished so much if he hadn't done something wrong. His father may have not loved him, but he was trying to make Zuko better, stronger, something Zuko couldn't achieve on his own.

"How do I behave myself? What are the rules? I-I swear I'll do.my best to follow them. I promise." He whimpers, closing his eyes.

"Well, no firebending. I don't want other people seeing you firebend. I have no idea how they'll react. Just when you're alone in the house, with permission for utility, and as a last resort to defend yourself. Only if you absolutely need to. That's the most important rule. Does that sound fair?" Chen asks, patting Zuko's back affectionately.

Zuko nods once, not looking up. "What else? Please, anything. I-I want to stay. I'll be good, I'll do what you say, just don't wanna be thrown out." He begs, clutching Chen closer, more desperately.

"We'll I don't want you to fight with the other people in the village, and I'm sure Kani feels the same way. If you don't like someone, use your words or walk away." Zuko can definitely handle that. If he can stay here, if he is safe here, he doesn't want to fight anymore. He wants to be a farmer and be happy. He doesn't want to be a soldier.

"Kani and I are telling people that you were attacked in your home village by a Fire Nation soldier and don't feel safe there anymore. We said that you're my nephew and felt safe coming to live with us. If you give any more information about parents or location or anything, you need to tell Kani and I, just please don't make it complicated. We said you were still pretty shaken up and wanted to be away from people for a bit. You can say that you don't want to talk about it if anyone presses you for details."

Zuko nods, that's even easier. He braces himself for the other shoe to drop though. He is sure that there has to be a bad rule in there.

Possibly something about Zuko needing to participate in the work and if he doesn't meet certain expectations he can't come inside that night to sleep or eat, that he's on his own in the barn until the next day.

He's more than willing to pull his weight and do work here. He would like to learn how to coax plants from the ground, to raise animals, to heal wounds. He wants to learn, there is just always a catch with it.

Ozai would lean towards beatings or burning, lockup, and hunger, sometimes he would mix them together. It would all depend on how badly Zuko had failed and how many times in a row he failed.

His father didn't seem to understand that if Zuko couldn't do a form right, a punishment would make it harder the next day.

A beating would make it harder to move his body properly and he would be filled with terror of more pain.

After a full day of being denied food, he would get jumpy and lightheaded. He had started to be able to go longer without food from a pretty young age due to that, so Zuko would be denied food for so much longer. It would get to the point where he would feel nauseous with pain shooting through his body from hunger, body demanding food as he writhed in pain on his bed when it got up to four days by the time he turned ten.

He could see all the pitying looks from the servants, all too scared to bring him something to eat. They were only allowed to bring him water. Some of them would make odd teas for Zuko to drink that tasted bad but tricked his body into thinking it had eaten something even of just for a little bit. It soothed the pain.

Being locked up for days at a time is why Zuko still sometimes has trouble closing a door behind him fully in a small room. Why he has trouble fitting into small spaces, not by lack of skill, but from fear. The reason why he doesn't like the dark.

Zuko has no idea how long he would be locked away for, but it would have to be days. He would be locked in a small, nearly pitch black room with a bottle of water and sometimes some food.

There would never be anything for him to burn so he would need to keep fire in his hands. He would always wake up in the dark. It took more energy to make fire after prolonged time underground, so he would be left panting in exhaustion near the end, feeling like he couldn't breath, that he would be left to die in there.

No matter how carefully he rationed his food and water, it would always run out. The times he was left with food, he would still go hungry. It was far worse to be thirsty. He would always be so thirsty. Sometimes he wondered if drawing his own blood and drinking it would help. He never tried, but he thought about it a lot.

By the time he was let out, all he could think about was going to a sunny field, not doing something right. He would almost always fail.

Once, his father threw him right back in the dark cell when he failed, but that only happened once. Zuko had been recovered half dead only a few hours later after screaming hysterically and throwing himself and fire against the walls until he broke enough bones, lost enough blood, and hit his head hard enough that he couldn't move.

He had been hospitalized and bedridden for nearly two weeks from burns, head trauma, and bone damage.

Zuko remembers that the night he was brought to the hospital wing, bandaged and left to rest and recover, his father had come to see him.

He had expected another burn, break, or bruise to be added to the collection that Zuko had inflicted upon himself out of fear. He thought he was going to be screamed at and berated, but his father didn't say anything.

For the first and last time ever, Ozai sat on the bed next to Zuko and had gently rubbed his back for a long time. It had to be at least an hour. Zuko hadn't been able to stop himself from crying a few times, and he hadn't been yelled at. His father just gently brushed the tears away from his face.

Zuko had been convinced that it wasn't his father, that it was someone else, that he was imagining things. However, every time he looked at the man's face, it was his father.

Then, Ozai had left. That affection had never been repeated. It was never mentioned. Zuko didn't dare mention it and sour the memory with a blow for mentioning a moment where his father was almost human.

It is Zuko's most treasured and most scorned memory.

He treasures the fact that even if just for a moment, even if it was for show, his father at least pretended to love him, to care about him. Maybe for that hour, Ozai realized that he had hurt his child opposed to training him and regretted it.

He hated that memory because it gets into his head whenever he thinks his father is incapable of love. He knows his father hurt him, doesn't love him, is a cruel and uncaring man, but he can't forget that night. It happened. His father isn't just a monster.

"We'll figure out the other rules as we go." Chen squeezes Zuko a little tighter as he speaks before pulling back. He moves his fingers under Zuko's chin, tipping his head up a little, meeting his good eye. "Is that alright, son?"

Zuko swallows, closing his eyes and nodding. It isn't alright, not at all, but he can't say that. It has to be alright. He has to listen, do whatever Chen and Kani want him to.

He wants to know the rules, all of them. He doesn't want to be punished for something he could try to avoid if he just knows what to do.

"Lee, if you do something wrong, we'll talk. We'll just talk to you and tell you what we need from you in the future. We won't hurt you. No one is going to hurt you here."

Zuko wants to tell the man that he's lying. It wouldn't be long until he got fed up and struck Zuko out of irritation.

The man would realize he enjoyed the terror taking over Zuko's body, filling his lungs and coursing through his veins. He would like that at the very least it silenced Zuko immediately. It would all fall apart soon after that.

Instead, Zuko moves his head, resting his right cheek against Chen's shoulder, wanting comfort when it is allowed. When it is being offered. Zuko has no idea when he'll be held again.

"If you need reassurance, you can always talk to us, always ask questions. We won't punish you for asking questions. If it's something we don't want to talk about, we'll just say so." Chen whispers, running his thumb over Zuko's growing, prickly hair.

Zuko nods a little, unable to think of anything to say to express his gratitude to the man. Unable to think of anything that might make this bad. He can't jeopardize his first potentially good situation.

"Lee, you haven't been drinking enough water especially after your fever, drink your tea. It's getting cold. I'll be right here." Chen presses his lips to Zuko's forehead after talking.

Zuko nods, shifting away from the man a little, keeping his knee against the man's leg, not wanting to fully break contact as he picks up his cup.

The tea has a nice, soft, herbal scent, calming his nerves a little as he sips at his cup, looking at Chen every so often.

"Lee, if you don't want to talk about this right now we don't have to, it might be personal. I won't be angry at you. Kani won't be angry at you, I promise." He looks at Zuko sadly.

Zuko nods, looking away nervously. "What do you wanna talk about sir?" He whispers.

"I don't know your past, but I know people have hurt you badly. I'm sure they've hurt you in ways that might make normally uncomfortable things terrifying to you. If you want to talk about fears, we'll listen. If you want to just tell us we're scaring, upsetting, or hurting you, I want you to tell Kani or me. Even if you just don't like it. We don't know your past, you need to tell us so it doesn't happen again or even better, never happens."

Zuko shrinks away, unsure what to say. The man would almost certainly use Zuko's fears against him. He might have good intentions now, but Zuko has a habit of making everyone reach their limits. Of ruining everything.

"S-second option, if that's okay, sir." He whispers, sipping at his tea. He prays that Chen doesn't punish him for choosing the harder option. The one where the man had to discover what makes Zuko scream in terror.

"Yeah, of course that's okay." Chen replies softly, resting a hand on Zuko's shoulder. "Just let us know if we need to stop doing something to you." He gives Zuko a warm smile.

"You alright if I go back outside? Gardens and animals need tending."

Zuko nods. "D-do I need to do anything? To help?" He asks in a too high pitched voice.

Chen shakes his head. "Not yet, wait till you're back on your feet. If you're staying here we'll need some help, but not yet. You're still in critical recovery. Kani wants you to rest for a few more days before you can start helping with work inside. You gotta fully heal till we want you working on the farm. More danger of infection there."

Zuko nods, thankful. His own father hadn't even allowed Zuko to be able to stand probably before he was to be banished. These people he barely knows are doing so much for him, so concerned with his recovery and health he wants to cry.

Chen stands, walking towards the door and Zuko wants to beg him to stay. He doesn't want to be alone. He doesn't want to leave these people.

The man walks out of the door all the same and Zuko covers his mouth , crying quietly, forcing tears to not fall, hating how dependent he had become on these people. Whether they know it or not, have good intentions or bad, they have a hold on Zuko. He can't just leave anymore, he is in dangerous territory that he can't leave. He needs to figure out how to do this without hurting himself.

He either has to leave now or these people do truly need to be kind.

"Hey, Lee, sweetie, wanna help me make dumplings today?" Kani asks as she finishes bandaging Zuko's eye, giving him a warm smile.

Zuko nods tentatively. For one, he knows that it's expected, he needs to learn how to pull his weight around here. It will only be so long before someone gets sick of him laying around and throws him out. He also wants to do something. He doesn't really know how to cook.

Ozai had forced Zuko to learn how to do so many things perfectly to avoid punishment, but Zuko was still a prince. He was to never do anything that was beneath him. That was servants' work.

Zuko wants to spend a day by a warm stove, creating something. He wants to smell like herbs and spices. He wants to learn something he might actually be good at and enjoy.

The fact that he knows it would infuriate his father is a bonus, cooking something nice not out of necessity but out of choice. Something that is domestic. Something a servant would do, not a soldier.

"Well we can start making the dough now, we can decide what we want to put in them later." She slowly helps Zuko stand, gently rubbing his arm.

Zuko nods as she leads him towards a low table that Zuko has seen them eat off of before and is pretty sure Kani uses as a prep table as well. He isn't sure about that second one because when he saw her prepping food he was feverish.

She pulls jars of flour, sugar, yeast, and oil from a chest resting them on the floor before putting a bowl on the table.

Kani explains the different measurements to Zuko in detail, showing him how to measure different ingredients. Telling him if he should pack it or just level it, how it changed if it were a liquid.

Zuko can't help but feel nervous as he carefully measures the ingredients, worried he would do it wrong.

Thankfully, Kani talks him through the whole process, rubbing his back as he tries to steady his hands, promising that no harm would come to him.

After several tries, he gets the first few ingredients into the bowl and he watches Kani stir them.

He likes the way it smells. It makes the room smell warm and homey. Before he knows what he's doing, he rests his head on Kani's shoulder smiling a little.

A hand touches his head, fingertips gently brushing his prickly hair. "I'm sorry for what led to the situation, but I'm thankful Chen found you in that storm. You're safe now."

Zuko nods a little. He has no idea what could have happened if someone else had found him. If it wasn't someone who was willing to give him a chance.

If no one had found him, Zuko is sure that he would have died. He barely survived while next to a warm fire, with good food, and a trained healer tending to him.

"Thank you for giving me a chance." He whimpers as Kani pours the forming dough onto the table, beginning to knead it.

"Of course. We would never leave an injured child like that, no matter where they were from. You need a home and some kindness. We can give you both. As long as you want to stay here, this can be your home, we'll take care of you."

Home is the word that sticks out to Zuko the most as he nestles a little closer to Kani. He wants this to be his home. He needs that so badly.

"Can I help with the dough?" He eventually asks, pulling away a little when Kani breaks off a chunk, handing it to Zuko.

When the dough has been kneaded enough, Kani combines them and puts it into a bowl, covering it with a cloth.

Zuko cleans the table while Kani looks at spices she has crushed in jars or hanging from the ceiling.

"We slaughtered one of the moo-sows yesterday, Chen is curing some of the meat so it will last and we have a little still fresh. I'm thinking we go out to the garden, see what veggies we have, sauté them with the meat and then spice it for the filling. That sound good to you, Lee?" Kani asks, smiling at them.

Zuko has always known that meat came from an animal, he just never really had to think about it. He hadn't even seen it happening or really knew the animal. Despite that, he can't help but feel sad for the creature.

He can't say that. Can't get upset. He's been given a pass for being upset because of being so sick and in so much pain the last few days. He can't get upset over a farm animal that was likely treated fairly while it lived here.

Zuko just nods, giving the woman a small smile.

She rests her hand on his shoulder, leading him out the door to a large garden.

Zuko isn't sure what most of the vegetables are, most he's seen have already been cut up and cooked. Hopefully he'll learn quickly. He doesn't want to admit he's never cooked before, they would know that he is nobility.

As they get closer, Zuko notices that Chen is standing in the field. He blinks a few times, trying to see what he's doing.

Zuko's depth perception has decreased while only being able to use one eye and his good eye still isn't that great yet. He really hopes his vision gets better with time.

He notices that Chen is talking to a woman with short black hair. Zuko clutches Kani's arm, hoping that this new woman isn't dangerous, that Kani could protect him if she is. He's worried that his features might be too distinctly Fire Nation. He can't be recognized as a firebender by the others. He needs to be allowed to stay here.

"It's alright, Lee, that's just our neighbor, Gela, she won't hurt you. If you wanna go back inside now, we can, if you decide you wanna go inside when we're talking to her, squeeze my hand twice and I'll send you inside to do something that you don't actually have to do. Is that okay?"

Zuko smiles gratefully, nodding, still holding her arm, needing to feel safe.

The unfamiliar woman turns to Zuko, smiling at him, dark green eyes sparkling. "You must be Lee, I'm Gela." She nods at him.

Zuko shrinks behind Kani, nodding nervously, clutching her clothes.

Gela gives him a sad look. "I'm sorry for frightening you. I can't imagine what you've been through. If you're ever feeling up to it in the future, I have a son and daughter about your age if you ever want to play."

Zuko looks up at her, he doesn't think he's ever really played with anyone besides occasionally with Lu Ten and when his mother made him play with Azula.

Azula had been strong and successful. She had proved that she could have free time and friends without it affecting her performance. Zuko wasn't given a chance at that. He's sure he could have done better if he were just allowed to be happy for even a moment. To be loved.

He isn't sure if he would be allowed to play now either. If as soon as he is really back on his feet he will be required to work in every free moment if he wants this to be his home. If he wants to earn love.

He doesn't want to promise anything in case he would get in trouble for trying to get out of work. He doesn't want to refuse the offer in case he is allowed to, or worse, he's being rude.

He plays it safe and closes his eyes, moving closer to Kani, praying Kani or Chen will make a decision for him so he doesn't have a chance to mess it up.

"Thank you, Gela, we'll talk to him later." Chen speaks up, Zuko relaxes with relief as someone else takes over. He can't mess up if he doesn't make choices.

"He's been through a lot very recently, he has trouble around new people right now. Once he is healed and feels more confident he might. Do you just need some space for now, son?" Chen asks.

Zuko can't bring himself to look up but he feels the man's eyes on him.

He nods nervously, moving his hand down Kani's arm, squeezing her hand several times frantically. He needs to be somewhere safe, somewhere he knows the variables. He can't be here right now with the unknown woman even if she has offered the possibility of friendship to him. Even if she has been kind.

Zuko just doesn't know what will happen. He doesn't know what she is really like, how she might react if she found out he is a firebender, most importantly, he doesn't know how Kani and Chen will react if he takes up or denies her offer. It just leaves so much, too much, unknown.

"Lee, why don't you go put on some water for tea. Want me to come with you or can you do it yourself?" Kani asks, kissing the top of Zuko's head.

Zuko is grateful that she is offering him the choice to be alone or with people. He would normally want to be with someone, but he needs to cry.

Nothing bad happened, there hasn't been any threat, he hasn't been hurt, but he needs to cry and he doesn't understand why. It will hurt and he doesn't want Kani to see.

Zuko isn't sure if he can talk so he just pulls away, running towards the house, curling up in a corner with his blanket, and crying.

"Is it something I did? That poor boy. Is there anything I can do?" Gela asks, looking between Kani and Chen as Lee races towards the house like his life depends on it. Chen is almost certain the kid is on the edge of a meltdown. It's been a long time coming.

Chen can't imagine how scared Lee must constantly be after years of perpetual abuse. He has to be stressed from pain, being fully reliant on two strangers, being in a new country while banished from his own, trying to come to terms with everything that happened, and adjusting to a new way of life all so suddenly.

That would be a lot for a grown man to handle. Lee is just a little boy. He's so young and tiny. Too young, too thin, and too scared.

Lee is probably only eleven or twelve. He's nothing but a child and a lot of people would treat him like the enemy if they found out his nationality. Like he is a seasoned soldier and not a child who is in desperate need of a hot meal and some kindness.

Chen isn't sure why Gela set him off or what did, but it's likely a result of whatever that man who had the audacity to call himself Lee's father did.

"He's just really stressed out, in a lot of pain, and still very confused at what has happened to him. He just needs time and space. He'll come around." Kani reassures Gela as she gathers vegetables up in her skirts.

"We'll talk to him later about if he wants to meet other children. At some point you two can meet when he's expecting it. He's a very sweet kid, he's just run into some really horrible people in his life." Chen adds.

He doesn't want to give too much of Lee's life away, but he wants people to understand that Lee needs help and reassurance. That he isn't trying to be rude, he's just scared. That he so desperately wants to be touched and to be given attention but has had bad experiences with both from the wrong people.

"Eventually having him meet new people will be good for him. He seems to like the arts, mostly theater, but he might like painting too. If you wanted to teach him some about painting, it might be good for him, and might calm his mind." Chen offers.

The nearby town will sometimes have a community theater performance. They aren't always good, but they can be fun. He and Kani don't really go, but when he isn't scared of his own shadow anymore, Lee would probably love it. Anything that might make that sweet little boy smile a little.

He deserves a little bit of happiness in his life. He has likely gotten so little in his life so far.

An issue that they'll eventually have to face is that Lee is a firebender from the Fire Nation.

If Lee chooses to stay, he would have to hide a very big and important part of himself. He would never be able to truly be himself, never be able to share his past even with his closest friends, and never be able to firebend again.

Chen is pretty sure that Lee has some pretty bad self esteem issues. Being forced to hide such a big part of himself, something that isn't inherently evil, something that is likely very important to him, might teach Lee to hate himself in a new way. That is the last thing the poor kid needs.

However, telling these others what he is could be worse. Lee would be exposing himself to so much more potential trauma. Chen is worried the other villagers might even go as far as to get violent. Lee would almost certainly learn to hate himself. He might even become callous and cruel if forced out of the village.

There really isn't a good way to approach this. He can't think of a way that Lee can be exposed as a firebender without getting hurt.

Chen just wants to show the village that Lee is a firebender but wouldn't dream of hurting anyone. Tell everyone that he is just a sweet little boy who has been abused and exploited over and over again and just needs someone to love him. Just needs some friends and family.

All the little firebender wants is a safe, warm place to sleep, a good meal, and warm, loving arms. It's what every child deserves. Lee doesn't deserve any less just because he is a firebender. He didn't start this war, he is just another victim of it.

"Lee and I are going to make dumplings and I want to go check on him even if he did want to be alone." Kani speaks up, skirt full of vegetables. She nods to Gela before walking back towards the house.

Chen can only hope that that little boy is alright.

### Text

Zuko had hidden in the room he had changed in the first night he stayed here. He hadn't been able to bring himself to close the door all the way due to the small size and lack of windows so it hadn't taken long for Kani to find him.

He hadn't been able to keep himself from crying. She had found him hunched over, whimpering erratically, one hand over his mouth to try and keep himself quiet with the other over his left eye from pain.

Kani hadn't said anything at first, she just left. She came back a few minutes later with tea and a bowl of hot water.

Zuko is now holding a cup of tea in shaking hands, sipping it silently as Kani looks at him with concern.

He stopped himself from crying a while ago, but he's still shaking. He can't stop himself no matter how hard he tries. He doesn't even understand why he's so upset, he just is.

"Lee, love, are you alright? Do you want to talk about it?" Kani eventually asks.

Zuko just shrugs silently. He doesn't really know what there is to talk about. He really doesn't know what's wrong. Gela had only offered him something he had always wanted…but she had done it in front of Kani and Chen. He also just isn’t sure what to think of *anything* that has been happening recently. It’s all just so contrary to everything he is used to and so far the other shoe hasn’t dropped. He’s back on his feet, it should have by now.

"Do you want something to eat? I know we were making dinner, but that won't be ready for a while. Are you hungry now?" She asks.

Zuko is sure that if he eats something he'll throw up. He's too anxious. He is, however, not completely stupid. He knows food won't always be so freely given.

He might be able to keep a small stash of nonperishable foods for times when he disappoints Kani and Chen and is denied food. They'll likely still expect him to work. He can eat just enough to keep up his strength and work until he's allowed to eat again. He won’t eat enough to not be hungry, they'll be suspicious if he does.

He doesn't want to be thrown out for being too weak. He can’t break before he has a chance to prove himself to them.

Zuko nods silently, finishing his tea, turning his cup in his hands.

"You want some jerky?" Kani offers, they always have an abundance of dried meats and fruits that they collect and dried throughout the days. Zuko assumes it's for when things get hard or for traveling. He's never asked. It isn’t his place. He doesn’t want to get in trouble anymore for simple curiosity.

Zuko nods, accepting the offer, dried food would be perfect. He could accept it and then hide it in his pack that is still resting in a back corner near where Zuko now sleeps. He figures neither Kani nor Chen have really looked through his bag after the first night. There isn't much of interest considering he just has his swords, some old, gray clothes, a few bandages, and a sleeping bag.

"Will you come out? You don't have to if you don't want to. You can think about it while I get something for you to eat." Kani stands as she speaks, walking away.

Zuko wants to run to her and cling to her as tight as he can. He doesn't want her to leave. Not yet. He needs her here. Kani and Chen's presence just make him feel so safe.

Despite that desire, Zuko forces himself from the room and towards the fire. It would be easier if he is near his bag. He also wants to start a fire. He feels so cold. Maybe he’ll stop shaking at least a little despite being sure the cold he is feeling is coming from the pit of his stomach.

When Kani comes back into the room, she is holding some jerky and a fresh apple in her hands, sitting next to Zuko, offering them forward.

Zuko puts the jerky in the pockets of his robes, he can put it in the sack later, for now he can busy himself with eating the apple, hoping he can keep it down.

"Lee, do you need your eye cleaned? I'm sure it hurts when you cry." Kani offers, wrapping an arm around Zuko's shoulders, rubbing his arm gently.

Zuko can't help but to rest his head on her shoulder, feeling loved and safe, her long, dark brown hair falling around his face like a veil of safety. "Just wanna leave it, if that's okay." He whispers, closing his eyes briefly.

"Of course, sweetheart. You can do whatever you need. Let me know if you change your mind. Is there anything you can think of that might help you right now?"

"Can you just hold me like this?" He asks quietly as he feels her hand brush over his head gently. He barely knows her but Zuko loves her so much. He wants to stay here forever. He'll do anything she or Chen wants if he's allowed to stay.

"I love you." He whimpers without thinking. "Thank you for saving me. F-for healing me."

"I love you too, sweetheart. This can be your home for as long as you need it to be." She replies, kissing his head as she speaks, bright green eyes smiling at him.

Zuko can't imagine what he would give or do to be born here as her and Chen's son. They are probably old enough to be his parents, a little on the older side, but they could have a thirteen year old child. He would give so much just to be loved like this sooner. He could have had thirteen years of hard work but with support and affection opposed to thirteen years of hard training and cruelty.

"I'm going to start chopping up vegetables. You eat and then join me when you want to. Please take your time, love." Kani says after several long minutes, kissing Zuko's forehead as she pulls away from him.

Zuko forces himself to not throw himself back into her arms, the loss of contact makes him feel too vulnerable and cold. He wants Kani to hold him again, to tell him that she loves him. He never wants her to let go.

He is sure Kani could carry him around with ease. She is long and lean, but when she wraps her arms around him and pulls him close he can feel lean muscle making up most of her body. He would never ask her to do that, but he never wants her to stop holding him.

"Lee, it's alright, I'm just going to be on the other side of the room, I'm not leaving you." Kani reassures him, likely seeing the panic in his expression. "I'll be right there." She promises as she slowly stands, walking away.

Zuko just bites into his apple, doing his best to not vomit or start crying again.

Kani is worried about Lee to say the least. His physical state has drastically improved over the course of the past week but his mental state hasn't. If anything, she's realizing more about his poor mental health as she spends time with him than she even considered.

He seems to lack individuality, needing direction and understanding exact expectations and consequences. He is trying to live his life in black and white, likely something he was taught in an abusive military upbringing.

He doesn't seem to understand that rules can come up depending on need and their implantation doesn't necessarily need to be done with punishment. He can just be talked to and reasoned with.

He seems to think every kind of punishment is cruel, not more common punishments for children such as not being allowed to play for a few days or cleaning up after the animals in the barn more because no one wants to do that. He seems to constantly expect to be struck over seemingly nothing. Kani is honestly more worried about how Lee will react when he *actually* makes a mistake opposed to the mistake itself.

She is also getting worried with his obvious separation anxiety. Chen isn't as good at picking up emotional subtleties as Kani is but even he has noticed that Lee looks on the verge of tears when one of them pulls away. Like he wanted to cling onto them for dear life. Like they're leaving him for good and aren't just going to be outside for a few hours.

That fear is likely from experience. Probably after his mother left and left him to the mercy of his father. Kani is ready to march up to that man and bury him. She doesn’t care who he is. He is the kind of man who destroys a little boy.

Even now, when Kani is just on the other side of the room, Lee hadn't wanted her to go. He keeps giving her nervous looks, curled up by the bag he came with, clutching his barely eaten apple to his chest.

His weight is something that she is still worried about. She hasn't wanted to bring it up to him yet, not sure how he would react. Kani isn't sure if he's self conscious about it or if it might make him that way.

She has settled on just trying to offer him food regularly, trying to get a little more weight on his tiny body.

Kani is mostly worried that because Lee has grown up in the Fire Nation, he isn't used to a real winter. It's still summer, but if he is that thin when winter comes around and he gets sick, it could very easily chronically damage or kill him.

Chen had brought up that Lee certainly shouldn't start doing regular physical labor until he starts eating more regularly and putting on weight. It is easy to see that Lee seems to have trouble eating when his anxiety is particularly high. He could do a little bit of weeding, feed the animals, maybe pick some vegetables for a meal but not much more. They really need to get some weight on him.

Kani just chops vegetables into small pieces, throwing them into a wok to put on the stove later after chopping everything.

As she is humming a song her mother used to sing to her and her sister, Lee slowly approaches her, sitting next to her silently, resting his head on her shoulder.

Kani isn't sure what exactly Lee has been through, but he has been horribly abused. Lee is so sweet, small, and gentle. He just wants a gentle touch in return. She doesn't understand who could ever want to hurt such a sweet little boy.

"Hey, sweetheart, are you feeling a little better?" She asks, pressing a kiss to his prickly head.

Lee nods a little, looking up at her with his golden eye, expression somehow filled with both fear and hope. "Can I help with anything?" He asks quietly, moving a little closer to her.

"Do you want to get the fire started in the stove? Use the smaller pieces in the bin to the right of it, the large pieces are for the hearth."

Lee reluctantly begins to stand up, fingers wrapped in the sleeve of her robe before almost forcing himself to let go and moving towards the cookstove, putting firewood below the burners, lighting it. Even from this distance, Kani can see him trembling.

Before Lee is able to get back to the table, Kani has begun to pull chunks of dough off of the lump from the bowl, rolling them into balls before flattening them so they could be filled later.

"Can I help you with that?" Lee asks softly, pointing at the dough, face looking down at the table, leaning towards her a little as if begging for contact.

"Of course. You take about this much dough." She helps Lee grab the proper amount, not wanting to worry him over doing something wrong so soon after breaking down. It's something they would have to work on in the future, but first Lee needs to really trust them.

She shows him how to roll and flatten the dough. He has a surprising amount of difficulty with all of it. She isn't sure if his coordination had been thrown off or if Lee just doesn't know how to cook in any capacity. The former seems more likely. Every kid, even those a little younger than Lee, boy or girl from any nation knows how to cook. It's a very basic life skill.

Lee works silently and methodically, face slowly becoming more slack as he gets the hang of the process. Kani hums softly as she works. She can only assume that Lee slowly moving towards her is subconscious as he seeks comfort.

She can't imagine ever wanting to hurt the sweet little boy to her. She can't imagine anyone wanting to. Somehow, someone did. Over and over again.

It doesn't take long to finish. As soon as they do, they move over to the now hot stove, beginning to sauté the vegetables and meat.

As they work, Kani figures it is a good time for her to talk to Lee. Get him to come out of his shell a little and feel a little safer, even if just a little.

"Lee, remember Gela from earlier?" She begins, looking at the little firebender who just looks down, nodding silently.

"Well, she is a very nice woman with two friendly children. I completely understand if you just want to stay here with just us for a while. If you're nervous I could invite them over here first so you're in familiar territory when you get to know them, if that's something you'd like. I think it would be good for you to play with some other kids your age."

Lee looks up at her, almost shocked. "I can play?" He whispers, good eye looking almost pleading.

Kani can feel her heart break for the little boy. She can't fathom what he has been through. She can't imagine what it could be like to be raised as a soldier and not a child. There will be so much she and Chen will have to teach him, but so much more he will have to relearn, something so much harder.

"Of course, sweetie, of course." She cups his injured cheek gingerly. "Most of the other kids help their families in the morning and late afternoon but then play during the hottest part of the day and after dinner. When you feel comfortable meeting the other children, you should go try and make some friends." She kisses his forehead after speaking.

Lee just looks at her almost shocked as if he hadn't even considered the possibility. Before she can say anything else, Lee flings himself into her arms.

"I promise I'll work hard for you, I'll do whatever you need, thank you." He whimpers, clutching at her closely.

He tries to continue making more promises but Kani gently shushes him softly, rocking him gently against her body as he presses his face into her stomach, trying to calm him a little.

"Lee, I trust that you'll help and pull your weight around here, but you aren't just a worker, you're a child. It sounds like you haven't been treated like the latter. You're a *child* , Lee. How old are you, love?" She asks, realizing she doesn't even know.

Lee is silent for a long moment before whispering; "I'm thirteen."

Kani can't stop thinking that he can't be thirteen. He's too small. The only reason she and Chen thought he was eleven or twelve was because of how he acts. If she just saw him, she would guess nine or ten.

That knowledge makes her stomach turn a little. Him being so skinny isn't just because he was traveling alone, he must have been malnourished enough to stunt his growth. He's far too tiny to be thirteen.

She is surprised that he hasn't been trying to eat everything in sight if he grew up without regular access to food. She has seen people live their lives close to starving and then be unable to break the habit of eating whatever they could get their hands in when given the chance. It wasn't about greed, it was about survival, not being sure where their next meal would be coming from or when it would be.

There is a lot about Lee that doesn't quite add up, but not in a way that makes her feel like he is unsafe. It just makes her worry for the sweet, tiny boy in front of her.

She doesn't have a single doubt that he has been abused severely and longitudinally. She has now doubt that Lee got that burn from his father and is absolutely terrified of the man now. She has no doubt that he is just a scared kid fleeing from the Fire Nation and just looking for a place to call home with people he can call family.

She isn't sure if Lee had truly been banished or just run. She isn't sure if Lee is his real name or all of the details surrounding the fact that Lee's father burned him. Kani believes that the Fire Nation can be calloused, but it not only seems extreme but impractical to want to send a 13 year old boy to war where he would surely die, possibly even get in the way of grown soldiers.

She has no doubt that Lee's burn has something to do with him realizing the Fire Nation's cruelty. She suspects that Lee found something out and it is either something so horrible he blocked it from his mind or something he feels is shameful or humiliating.

Kani knows that people can do sick, twisted things to each other. Children aren't spared from it. Many times, they are targeted for various reasons. She wouldn't be surprised if something like that happened to Lee. Her heart would break for him, but she wouldn't be shocked.

None of the details are what matters. She fully believes that Lee has no ill will towards anyone here. He has no intentions of fighting. He just wants to be given the simple life of a farmer with a family who can love and take care of him in a way he desperately needs. Even if his reasons may be lies, his intentions and motives are almost certainly pure. He's just scared. He needs help and has no where to go and no one to turn to.

Kani moves the wok off of the stove with one hand before resting her hand on Lee's upper back again, still trying to comfort the sweet little boy in her arms.

"You wanna start filling the dumplings with me? You don't have to if you don't wanna, I won't be upset with you if you need to lay down, I know it's been a stressful day for you." She kisses the top of his head, smoothing his still prickly, but growing, black hair.

Lee nods, not moving his head from her stomach. "Wanna help." He mumbles, gripping her robes a little tighter, not wanting to be out of her embrace.

"Okay, love, let's go. We'll eat as soon as they're ready." She promises, wanting to feed the firebender probably as much as he wants to eat.

She finally gets Lee to move away from her, kissing his forehead before picking up the wok and walking over to the table with it.

She can only hope her little boy will be alright.

Zuko really isn't sure what to think exactly about everything. He isn't sure if there is a catch to what Kani has offered him. She nor Chen have hidden anything from him so far, but they all still barely know each other. Things can still change.

He watches Kani's hands carefully, mimicking her movements in making the dumplings. The filling smells amazing. He doesn't want to mess up his chances of being allowed to eat with them tonight.

Now that anxiety is wearing off, he can feel hunger beginning to gnaw at him. He doesn't want to eat the jerky he just stored away earlier today.

He wants to save in incase he messes up later. If he eats it in secret, he'll have energy to work so hard for Kani and Chen. He'll get a chance to prove himself even if he fails the first time.

Every time he messes up properly wrapping a dumpling, Kani gently corrects him, sometimes helping position his hands properly, guiding him through the process.

She doesn't yell at him, threaten him, or hit him. The only additional contact she makes is affectionate and gentle.

He wants to cry and doesn't fully understand why. He just wants to curl up in her arms and sob until he exhausts himself.

He doesn't. She has seen him cry enough. She'll get sick of it soon enough.

As they continue, Zuko slowly relaxes, feeling safer in her presence. He becomes more confident that she won't strike him for a mistake.

That doesn't mean he is going to let himself slip up. He is going to be so good for them. They'll let him stay if he's good. If he can prove himself as useful.

It doesn't take all that long for the two of them to fill and wrap the dumplings, putting them in a woven basket.

"It's a one person job from here, love, I'll finish making these if you go get Chen, they'll be ready in about fifteen minutes." Kani squeezes Zuko's hand after speaking, smiling at him.

Zuko nods, reluctantly letting go of her hand. He never wants Kani to stop touching him. He would love it if her hand would constantly be touching his shoulder, back, head, or hand. Same for Chen. Being reminded of their proximity makes him feel safe, something he had only ever felt with his mother and uncle. He may have had that feeling with some of the guards and servants, but they were all too scared of Ozai to get close to Zuko for more than just small acts of kindness that couldn't be traced back to them other than by Zuko.

Zuko walks out of the door, looking across the gardens. He loves the farm, it’s so beautiful. The barn filled with animals is surrounded by a large pen allowing them to roam and graze takes up most of behind the house. To the left, there are berry bushes that Zuko wants to try some of, but hasn’t worked up the courage to even ask if he is allowed. He’s worried he’ll be struck for being greedy.

The front and right side of the house is surrounded by a large curved garden filled with a variety of plants, some of which he knows but most he hasn’t looked at closely enough to recognize. Some of them he might just not know because he hasn’t seen them not cut up. It makes him feel stupid.

Zuko scans across the garden before seeing Chen crouched down near the ground between rows of plants, looking at something close to the ground.

Zuko slowly begins to walk across the garden towards the large Earth Kingdom man, wrapping his arms around his stomach, hoping he isn't disrupting anything. He feels like it might be more risky yelling. If he were to yell and Chen got mad, Zuko would be given more time to panic and run, making things so much worse. If he were to be right next to him, Chen could just strike him then and there without giving Zuko time to think.

Zuko wouldn’t risk making things worse. He could be punished and get it over with and move on. It’s always better to not let himself think and try and avoid punishment. It could get *so* much worse.

"Chen...sir?" He asks quietly as he approaches the man, eyes on the ground, unsure why Kani would set him up to be struck, but there is a lot he doesn't understand. If he weren't so stupid he would know and be able to stop it.

"Hey, Lee, are you alright? Is something wrong?" Chen asks, standing, pulling off a glove and resting his hand on Zuko's shoulder.

Zuko nods as he feels fresh tears prick in his eyes, he doesn't understand why he's so emotional, so stupid, and so weak. He wishes what his father had done had beaten the weakness out of him, not made him so scared and pathetic.

Zuko hates himself for not forcing himself to make his punishments make him stronger, less scared, opposed to the opposite. He hates his father for just becoming crueler as time went on and not finding a new method of training opposed to just making it so much worse. He hates his sister for teasing him as he sat in fear and pain. He hates his mother, uncle, cousin, and grandfather for allowing Ozai to just hurt him so badly every day. He hates them all even if three of them are gone. He hates Kani and Chen for not making the rules clear enough, for toying with him, for setting him up for a shattered heart like nothing he had ever felt before.

He knows that as soon as they beat him or throw him out, it will leave him with physical screaming pain in his chest because the stupidest part of him really believes they love him. He wants to believe they love him. He needs to.

Zuko just feels so angry, scared, confused, and just so exhausted with everything going on, he can't stop a few tears from rolling down his cheeks.

"Hey, hey, it's alright, son. Did something happen?" Chen asks, Zuko shakes his head, moving closer to Chen, wrapping his arms around the man's thick, strong waist, wanting to be held again.

"Dinner will be ready in a little." He mumbles into Chen's chest. He comes up higher on Chen than Kani as she stands a full head taller than her husband.

Chen runs his hand through Zuko's short hair before pulling away and kneeling down in front of Zuko, one large finger under Zuko's chin.

Despite how kind and gentle Chen has been the entire time Zuko has been here, he can't stop thinking how horribly the man could hurt him. He isn't a bender and isn't particularly tall but is absolutely enormous in terms of muscle mass. The man has given no reason for Zuko to feel anything but safe with him, but he can't stop thinking what Chen could do to him with little effort.

"Hey, Lee, do you promise nothing happened today besides being overwhelmed by Gela? Did someone do something to you?" Chen asks, gently brushing at Zuko's tears.

Zuko shakes his head. "N-no sir...sorry sir, don't know what's wrong." He admits which is mostly true. He's just so overwhelmed and doesn't understand most of what he is feeling. It just comes out as tears.

"Lee, if I'm ever asking you something you don't wanna talk about, just say so, I won't be angry, but have you been hurt before?" He asks, looking sad.

Zuko frowns, unsure what to say to that. Chen can see the scarring skin on his face, so it can't be about that, he doesn't understand.

Chen exhales, cupping Zuko's right cheek, looking at him sadly. "You said your father burned you, did he, or anyone else, regularly hurt you before for any reason? You don't have to give me details or tell me anything about it, but are you used to being hurt?"

Zuko closes his eyes, nodding once, leaning back towards Chen. "Wanna forget." He whimpers quietly as Chen rubs his back gently. He just never wants to think about it again.

"Son, I want you to know, I'm not going to hurt you. I don't want to hurt you. You don't deserve to be hurt. We don't have to talk about this now if you don't want to, but I want you to know, I won't *ever* hurt you. I won't let anyone else hurt you either."

Zuko just nods, not wanting to talk about it or drag it out anymore than necessary.

"Wanna see a cool lizard snake I found?" Chen asks after a moment of awkward silence.

Zuko looks up, swiping at his face, nodding. He wants to just move past this conversation. Forget about it. He just wants to be a farmer boy with no past.

Chen crouches down again, gesturing for Zuko to do the same before pointing to the long, bright red and purple body of the creature curled up by the tomato plant, flicking its tongue at them.

Zuko can help but to smile a little, trying to ignore the mild pain from crying in his left eye. His wound has gotten better with Kani's help.

"It's beautiful." Zuko whispers, smiling a little more as Chen rests a hand on Zuko's back.

"Come on son," Chen begins after a few minutes. "Kani is waiting, let's go eat."
