## Chapter 4

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

It's really fucking hot out back here at home and I am not being forced outside by my job to do things so I am just vibing so we have another rapid update, I head back to the woods on Sunday.

### Text

“Lee, I know you’re a little nervous, but this will be good for you, but you don’t have to go if you don’t want to. Gela has talked to her children and they know that you’ve had a hard time lately and know to not push you if you don’t want to talk about or do something. They’re good kids from a good family, if you want them to leave, they’ll know it isn’t personal. They’ll understand you’re just still overwhelmed and having trouble with trusting people. I promise nothing will happen. But if you don’t want to do this, you don’t have to, love.”

Kani holds Lee a little closer, wanting to be sure that he feels fully secure and safe with her. She is careful to repeat the fact that he doesn't have to meet the other children. She’s worried he might feel obligated to and gets scared, especially if they want to leave the property. She wants him to feel like this is his home where he will be protected.

“Wanna meet them.” Lee whispers, clutching her hand as if his life depends on it. Right now, he probably feels like it does.

“I’m so proud of you, sweetheart.” Kani kisses his forehead again before standing up, smiling at her little boy.

His eye has gotten so much better, it’s still tender to the touch but he doesn’t need the bandage anymore as long as he isn’t going to be doing hard or dirty work. It’s fully scabbed over and starting to heal well beneath it. He’s mostly out of danger for infection as long as he doesn’t do anything too stupid.

Thankfully, he can see out of his left eye, something she was worried he wouldn’t be able to do.

Kani had done her best approximation of a vision test for him with what she could remember from her training before she gave up being a town’s healer for Chen. She regrets nothing, it’s been a better life than she assumes her life as a healer would have been. Not that she thinks it would have been bad, she’s just happy to be here. She loves Chen, her friends, and her life here.

Lee’s vision thankfully doesn’t end in a sharp cut off, it slowly degrades as his field of vision shifts to the left until it turns to black.

When Lee had covered his right eye and just looked at his surroundings with his left, they discovered that his color perception is distorted a little. It’s not horrible, but far from ideal. His peripheral vision in his left field is atrocious.

Lee had been pretty upset but had apologized and pulled himself together. She would have preferred him to have lashed out at her and screamed when she told him that he was lucky to be able to see out of his left eye at all. She doesn’t want him to start getting worked up over something that is a really big deal and then force himself to calm down, trying to brush it off like it’s nothing when he is clearly upset.

The fact that he doesn’t feel like he is allowed to be upset at being partially visually impaired is concerning. He deserves to be angry, throw a rock over the field, punch a bale of hay, break down in a fit of crying and screaming, and just be upset and angry that his own father intentionally crippled him and then sent him to die.

She can’t imagine what was done to the little boy to make him feel like he wasn’t allowed to show emotion that portrayed anything *real* . She’ll need to have a couple of words with Lee’s father. And by ‘words’, she means ‘send rocks through his chest’.

A knock comes from the door and Lee moves closer to Kani, looking up at her with concern.

“It’s alright, sweetie. Remember, you have control here. They don’t have to stay here, and if they want to go somewhere else with you, you don’t have to. You only do what you want to.” She takes Lee’s hand, leading him to the door.

As soon as she opens it, Lee hides behind her, peaking at the three people standing there, thankfully not running away. She’s glad that he’s at least looking at them, she wishes he wasn’t so scared, though.

She holds Lee’s hand, looking at the two children walking into the house, one waving at Lee, grinning.

Kani gestures to the young girl with black hair, piercing green eyes, and freckled, chubby cheeks. “Lee, this is Kyira,” Kyira is ten. When Kani told Gela that Lee was about her children's’ ages, she was assuming Lee was eleven, not thirteen, but she hopes that her sweet little boy can still make friends with a ten and twelve year old.

She then gestures to the boy with dark brown hair and almost black eyes, waving at Lee, likely excited to have another boy his age to play with, most of the other children close to his age are girls. “And this is Fao.”

Lee steps out from behind her waving back at Fao, still holding her hand.

“Lee, wanna come see our fort? It’s in the woods a little behind our house.” Fao offers, grinning ear to ear, surly excited to finally have another boy his age to play with.

Kani kneels now near Lee, cupping his cheeks in her hands. “Do you wanna go, love? Gela will be here with me, you can always come back if you feel like you need to, alright?”

Lee tentatively nods. “I-I wanna have friends.” he whispers softly, saying the word ‘friends’ like it is something almost foreign to him, something he shouldn’t be allowed to say. Kani can only feel so sorry for him. Feel so sad for what he was deprived of and angry at the man who likely intentionally deprived friendship from his sweet little boy who grew small and scared from isolation, abuse, and neglect.

“Okay, Lee, either be back here before sunset or when Fao and Kyira need to go home. I don’t want you out there alone yet, okay?”

Lee nods, giving her a small smile. “Thank you.” He whispers, hugging her, before beginning to pull away. That takes a little bit, because like always, it takes him awhile to fully let go over her, less of his fingers clutching at her clothes or hand, grip switching between loose and clutching onto her for dear life.

He always seems to have trouble forcing himself to let go of her. She hopes that gets better at some point. Some separation from her with new people will be good for him. He needs to learn that she’ll still be here when he gets back. She won’t leave him like so many have.

When he and Gela’s kids finally make it out the door, Gela walks towards her, handing her a bundle of green and brown. They look like clothes that Lee could fit into, certainly better than the muddy looking clothes that were stripped of their red color that Lee brought with him or Kani’s smallest clothes wrapped around him decently.

“Kani, we’ve known each other for twenty years, I know that boy isn’t your nephew. Even so, he seems like a sweet kid who’s been through a lot. I brought some of Fao’s old clothes that don’t really fit him anymore. Not great, but likely better than clothes that don’t really fit him at all.”

Kani takes the clothes from Gela, smiling warmly at her friend, grateful she can at least be halfway honest with who Lee is with her. Grateful that, despite Lee being some boy they don’t really know, Gela trusts Kani’s judgment enough to let her children play with him. That she is able to understand that Lee is just a scared little boy who needs some love.

“Thank you, Gela. He’s a good kid, I promise. I can’t tell you everything about him because I don’t know everything and some of it is very personal. He’s been through a lot and all he wants is a home and some good people in his life.” She assures her friend. It’s the truth, the full truth. She would consider the facts that Lee is a Fire Nation firebender as personal in this situation.

“Is there anything about him that you are willing to tell me? Like how do you know him? Where did he come from? I won’t press if you don’t want to tell me, I promise I won’t tell anyone that he isn’t your nephew. I know it’s probably for simplicity and for his own safety with everything going on.” She offers Kani an encouraging smile.

Kani has always been able to trust her friend.

Gela can be trusted. She isn’t the most conventional person, but she is honest and upfront. She doesn’t play games with people and doesn’t let people try to do that to her. Anything she has to say, she’ll say it. If she had any ill will against Lee, Gela would never have brought her children over and would have made this a much more serious discussion.

She’s kind but doesn’t change who she is for even a moment to make someone else feel more comfortable in her presence. The only exception that Kani has ever seen is she drops the large, aggressive personality around scared or injured children. Her own or others.

Gela is a lean, but very muscular earthbender with jet black hair almost always falling down her shoulders, dark green eyes shining with a fierce protective light, and dark skin. Even as she passes forty, she is just as breathtakingly beautiful as when she was in her twenties.

To the people she is close to, Gela is generous and caring. She does a lot for those around her from cooking, to mending, to a shoulder to cry on, to beating up someone who wronged her or a loved one.

She also doesn’t take shit from anyone. Kani is worried that one day Gela will stand her ground against an small army of Fire Nation shoulders with bending as her only backup.

Kani can already see her friend glaring at trained soldiers surrounding her, making dead eye contact, ready and willing to kill as others get a chance to escape.

Gela had moved to the outskirts of Naofan a few months before Kani and Chen had eloped and moved here together. Kani knows that she comes from a hard past, Gela had firmly told anyone who asked that it was a personal matter that she would rather not discuss with anyone. If pressed a second time, she would tell them to fuck of. If pressed a third, she would show them an answer in broken bones.

She had moved here alone, no husband or children. Several young men had tried to woo her. Those who had found her interesting and genuinely wanted to get to know her typically left with a hot meal and a new friend, accepting that she had no intentions of marrying. Those who hadn’t yet married due to poor personal qualities making them undesirable husbands assumed that Gela was trying to hide the fact that she was embarrassed that she wasn’t married yet when reaching her mid twenties left with broken bones and fear in their hearts.

Gela isn’t one to lie or deceive, if she doesn’t want to tell someone something, she makes that very clear. Anyone who values their bones intact drops it. She isn’t one to spread rumors, especially ones that could hurt someone, a child at that.

Gela doesn’t enjoy hurting people, she sees it as a universal language when reason no longer seems to work. It is a message that goes further and a threat that it can always get worse. To Kani’s friend, pain is solely used for utility, never just to hurt someone.

Kani can trust that Gela won’t do anything to hurt Lee.

Kani sighs, gesturing for Gela to sit down with her, resting the clothes by Lee’s bag. She hasn’t tried to move his things. She doesn’t want the little boy to feel like he doesn’t even have control over some basic things that he owns. He’s likely been given so little freedom, she won’t take any bit of it from him now.

“You promise you won’t tell anyone about Lee? He’s still injured and still so scared. He needs a home and I don’t know if he’ll make it if he leaves now. He’s a little boy who can’t go home with no family anywhere else.” She practically pleads, trusting that Gela would comply.

Her friend nods. “I won’t do anything to hurt Lee. He seems like a good kid and I wouldn’t ever hurt a child.” She swears, taking Kani’s hand on her own.

“Chen found him in that storm almost two weeks ago. He was injured, sick, and half dead. We took him in and healed him. I don’t know too much about his past, he isn’t very open about it, but he was burned by someone he thought cared about him and would protect him. He’s been exploited, abused, and neglected almost his entire life. He’s such a sweet little boy. He just wants someone to love him, I promise that.”

She gives Kani a reassuring smile, squeezing her hand. “I believe you. Where is he from?” Gela asks, a knowing look in her eyes.

Kani shakes her head. “No. Leave that out of this. He’s a scared little kid who was forced out of his home by people who did nothing but hurt him his entire life and now he thinks it’s normal to be hurt by people who care about him.”

She doesn’t want to talk about Lee’s heritage. Gela could easily think that he is just a nonbender from the colonies, but if she were to look much closer, Lee looks like a firebender. He’s paler than almost anyone in the Earth Kingdom with jet black hair and golden eyes. He has a burn that is in the shape of the palm of a grown man.

Gela is observant. She’s smart. She will likely think that Lee is the child of an Earth Kingdom and Fire Nation couple that went very badly. She doubts that her friend will think less of Lee for the circumstances of his birth, something out of his control, but Kani can’t be sure. Lee can’t survive much more abandonment or cruelty.

“Kani, I do–”

“Stop. He can’t help where he’s from. I’m worried if anyone pushes him too soon, he’ll run. If he runs, he’ll probably die or be hurt by someone else. He wants to forget about his past. He won’t talk about it even with me or Chen outside of the first night. Please respect that.” She can’t let curiosity be the reason her little boy gets hurt.

Thankfully, Gela just sighs, letting go of Kani’s hand. “Is he one of them, Kani?” She asks after a moment of silence.

Kani swallows, sure she knows what Gela is implying, but looks at her hands instead. “What do you mean, by ‘one of them’? Who’s them?” She asks despite being sure of the answer.

“He’s from the colonies, isn’t he? Is he a firebender?” She asks, touching Kani’s arm. “I won’t hold that against him. I understand that he’s just a boy, if raised well he wouldn’t be a threat, maybe even helpful if the need arose. If my children are going to spend time with him, I just want to know. You have my word. I would never use that against him if he truly isn’t a threat, you know what my word means to me.”

“He’s a firebender.” Kani finally whispers after a long moment of silence. “He doesn’t really firebend, just starts fires in the hearth and the stove for me. I think he’s actually afraid of fire after what was done to him, but he won’t talk about it. Don’t talk to him about it, he really does get upset when pressured about his past.”

Kani feels a hand rest on her upper back in a comforting way. “I just wanted to know, thank you. I promise I hold no ill will against him just for existing. I’ve had time to come to terms with the very likely possibility of that. I won’t say anything to anyone. As long as he really isn’t a threat, he’s not my enemy.”

“Thank you, Gela. Once he settles, I think it might be good for him to hear that from you.” She whispers, smiling a little, feeling almost relieved that someone had learned Lee’s secret and isn’t angry. It's a small step forward for Lee to get a chance to live more authentically here. To be safer.

For now she can only hope for that for her little boy.

The siblings lead Zuko to the woods near a small river. Fao pulls Zuko into a thicket of brush and rocks and they come to a cleared space. There are a bunch of cool, broken artifacts that the siblings have likely found and collected over the years from abandoned camps and in rivers after storms.

It isn’t really much besides a little hidden place in the woods, but that is likely the point. A place where they can come and be alone with who they choose to bring here. Just a little space of their own they can do essentially whatever they want in and put old things they might not be allowed to bring into the house in.

Zuko highly doubts anyone would want a broken, rusty sword or dirty bottles in their house, but they’re like little treasures out here. He also isn’t sure if the small pile of long, thick sticks against the rock wall is intentional or just junk that got in here no one had gotten rid of yet.

“What do you guys do in here?” Zuko finally settles on asking, looking around the open space.

“When mom is baking something sweet we’ll usually grab some of it and eat it before dinner so we can enjoy it.” Kyira offers, grinning.

“And then after dinner as well when we’re allowed to, if mom doesn’t catch us. Ma doesn’t really mind, she thinks it’s funny, we’ll try to get out of doing chores by hiding from her.” Fao adds. “And sword fight with friends.” He continues, picking up one of the sticks, showing it to Zuko.

Zuko really wants to show the boy his real swords. He might like that. However, Zuko’s mind is mostly focused on the previous thing the siblings were talking about. He is a little confused by the ‘mom’ and ma thing.

“Which one is your mother? Do you have a father” He asks, confused. He doesn’t want to say something stupid and ruin his first chance at friends already.

“They both are. Ma, the one you met, she helped our mom raise us. We probably have a dad, but I don’t really care, he’s not the one who’s always been there for us, mom and ma have. They’re really great. Do you know how to sword fight, Lee?” Fao asks, offering Zuko a stick.

Zuko nods, taking it tentatively, never having considered the concept of having two mothers. He would have loved that. His life would have been so much better if He had been raised by his mom and then another mom. Then again, Zuko has started to think of Chen as his dad and the man has never even tried to raise a hand at Zuko for…anything. Zuko can’t stop thinking maybe the issue isn’t with fathers in general but with Ozai. He really doesn’t know though. It’s still too early to tell. Chen could also be the one who is an exception.

“I actually have dao blades I was trained to use when young. My family wanted me to learn it because I’m not a bender.” He hopes that explanation is sufficient enough. He can’t tell them his father hit him because he was a bad firebender so he needed to pick up the slack somehow by his mother’s plea.

Fao looks at him with wide-eyed excitement. “Lee, do you think you could teach me? Teach me anything at all? We’ll have a lot more time after the harvest is in even if it is cold.”

Zuko hasn’t started working much yet, so he isn’t sure how much work will change after the harvest is over, he also isn’t quite sure when the harvest is over, or how well he will do in the cold considering he hasn’t experienced a real winter. He knows that this part of the world gets snow, something he has never seen before. He doesn’t want to make himself too obvious that he isn’t from here in any capacity.

Zuko bites his lip, nodding a little. “Yeah, I’ll see what I can do. Haven’t practiced since…” He gestures to his face, looking down. He hadn’t considered that he might not be able to use his dao blades as well or at all now that his left field of vision and left ear are suddenly not what they once were. He might have to almost completely retrain himself. He isn’t sure how that will go considering he would have no master.

“Dunno how good I’ll be, but I’ll see what I can do.” He offers quietly, eyes shifting and focusing on a tall, scraggly tree. “But I can give it my best shot.”

“Lee, Kani was talking to our moms when you first got here, but didn’t really talk to us. What happened?” Kyira asks, looking at Zuko’s face with curiosity and sorrow.

Zuko just shakes his head. “Don’t wanna talk about it.” He whispers, wrapping his arms around his waist, looking down.

He expects to hear the siblings demand an answer, threaten to leave if he doesn’t tell them something about it, but he feels a hand on his shoulder. Zuko looks over at Fao giving him a small smile.

“It’s alright, Lee, wanna go catch crab-spiders in the river? As long as we keep them in some water and put them back in the river later, they’re fine.” Fao offers, mercifully changing the subject.

Zuko nods, smiling, letting the siblings lead him out of the fort and through the woods.

The next several hours involve the three of them wading through the water with their shoes off and pants rolled up, looking through the sand and mud at the bottom of the river. The spider-crabs have eight, long, armored legs, eight eyes covering their heads, and beautiful shells. The smallest one they find is a little bigger than Zuko’s thumb and the biggest about the size of his palm.

He hasn’t really ever waded around in water looking for anything before, and he doubts it would be much fun under any other circumstance. He likes talking to the siblings and watching them splash each other with water. They had tried to space Zuko as well but Kani had been very specific about him being careful with his eye. He doesn’t want it to get worse again. It would be painful and he would risk angering her.

He is really starting to settle. Zuko isn’t sure what would happen if he started to ignore the warning that Kani and Chen gave him. They may very well throw him out. He isn’t sure if he could live with that. It might fully break his heart. He isn’t sure where he would go, if he could even survive getting somewhere he might be safe.

He is certain he would never find two people who are kind and accept the fact that he is a firebender.

Zuko learns a little more about Fao and Kyira. He learns that their mom is from further east and left before Kyira was born. They aren’t sure about specifics, but it deals with natural disasters. She had met Gela in the central part of Naofan who had offered her a place to stay for a few months and it kind of turned into a permanent situation.

They don’t know all of the details. Zuko assumes it’s bad. They have been given the luxury of shelter of how horrible the world truly can be. They don’t have to live it, even through someone else. Zuko can’t help but envy them. His father hadn’t given him that luxury.

Zuko first learned what death really is when he was five, he first encountered it at seven.

One of the servants had taken a hand in bringing Zuko up when he was young. The man worked in the gardens and would teach Zuko about different flowers and insects. He would tell Zuko old Fire Nation stories about spirits and great creatures. Zuko could follow the man around all day and listen to him. Between that man and Ursa, Zuko actually felt somewhat happy and loved.

One day, Zuko had been near the gates before the man was going to leave for the day and Zuko had embraced him, thanking him for everything he had done. It was something he had never been brave enough to do before then.

Zuko hadn’t understood at the time how he hadn’t even seen his father there before embracing the gardener, but Ozai had grabbed Zuko by the arm, pulling him away from the servant man, and thrown Zuko in a dark room for several days. He hadn’t understood at all. No one would tell him what he had done wrong.

As soon as Zuko was allowed out, he was forced to watch the man be hanged for the crime of trying to abduct the Prince. Zuko hadn’t understood in the least why his father had done that at the time considering Zuko hadn’t been struggling, wasn’t being led out of the gates, and the man had never done anything to Zuko that he wasn’t okay with. Every touch was gentle and friendly, his words were soft and kind.

All Zuko can think of now is that his father thought that the man was corrupting him or just that Ozai has always hated Zuko so much that he would rather kill some random servant than see Zuko be happy for even a moment.

Zuko can’t imagine it being jealousy. Ozai had never shown any interest in Zuko for anything but a soldier and something to take his anger out on. That is all his father had ever seen in him. If Ozai had wanted to spend time with Zuko, there was more than enough time where Zuko was just alone that his father could have approached him.

Zuko is positive now it was purely out of malice.

After the gardener had been executed, Zuko had trouble eating and sleeping. Ozai didn’t care much about how Zuko slept, but he would get angry when Zuko didn’t eat. It was completely opposite to the man forbidding Zuko from eating and equally as horrible if not worse.

Zuko would have to eat while already feeling sick from the vivid memory of watching the man, his friend, die, and almost always forced to eat past satiation, threatened with more pain. He’s sure that feeling was almost as bad as going hungry for days at a time.

Zuko isn’t sure if it was intentional to hurt him. His father kept calling him a liar when he said he was full and felt sick. His father really could have just not known or cared that after occasionally starving Zuko, he wasn’t able to eat as much as Azula could.

It made him feel impossibly nauseous and dizzy throughout the day and hadn’t been able to keep it down, ending up sobbing on the floor, unable to stop throwing up most days.

Every day, his father would get worse, screaming that Zuko was trying to get himself killed over a servant and every day Zuko would get sicker. The servants were all too scared to even comfort him after what the gardener and there was very little his mother could do without making it worse for him. The servants hadn’t shown him much personal kindness until Ursa left. Even then, they were very careful.

This continued for a little over two weeks before could barely breathe and Zuko passed out. He woke up several days later in the infirmary. He isn’t sure why it happened, but he had almost died. His father gave him time to recover, but ignored the whole incident like he hadn’t perpetrated it. He didn’t even visit Zuko once. Zuko was in bed for weeks.

His father didn’t even *look* sorry.

His mother had visited him almost every day, Azula would sometimes come as well. Ursa would hold him, rub his stomach or back, sing to him, or read to him. It helped a little, but not much. Zuko ended up crying most of the time or just staring off distantly.

Azula once brought in two pastries, Zuko felt too sick to eat his, he had only been able to even think about eating broth and thin soups for months after what had happened. Thankfully, his father didn’t scream at him to eat anything solid. There was at least that.

However, that night, Azula stayed with him. She had snuggled up under the covers and slept with him, snuggled up in his arms. It’s really his last good memory of his sister. He hopes that the spark of that little girl is still in her somewhere. That maybe at some point they can at least talk and spend a little time together if he ever sees her again.

Because of that incident, it was still why Zuko would have trouble eating a lot even after being starved. He would tend to pick at several small meals throughout the days, working his way back up to more regular ones. He still has trouble taking a long time to really eat anything. He can’t force himself to eat a lot at a time anymore.

It hasn’t come up in front of Chen and Kani yet, as of now, they’re still likely assuming he’s sick and scared, which he is. He hopes that that doesn’t come up, or that they’ll allow him to leave it as his father had hurt him. Zuko doesn’t want to go into detail. Not even with them. He wants all of it to be over. He just wants to live safe and happy with Chen and Kani.

He wishes he could have been born a peasant farmer but as their child than to be born a prince as Ozai’s. His title, throne, riches, and luxuries aren’t worth it. None of it was worth it. It’s better living as a simple farm boy here. He’s happier, safer, and more loved.

He doesn’t care about anything that he had as a prince. He was absolutely miserable day in and out. He only misses a few people.

They have found about twenty spider-crabs when Kyira taps his shoulder. “Hey, Lee, we should probably get going. We need to help get the animals in before dark. Are you going home too?” She asks.

Zuko nods before they both begin setting the little creatures back in the river, saying goodbye and giving them increasingly less creative names. Zuko can’t stop himself from grinning as the little creatures scuttle back into the silt and hearing the siblings laughing a little at the critters and the names.

When they finish, the three begin walking back towards the farmland through the woods. “Thank you for showing me your fort, and for spending time with me, I had a lot of fun. Thank you.” Zuko says softly.

He means it. He really had never been given the luxury of being able to do something like this. He wants to be able to do it again. He doesn’t care if all they do is walk around and throw rocks at trees, he just likes having this freedom.

“We had fun too. I’m sorry about whatever happened to you, but I’m glad you’re here now.” Fao offers, taking hold of Zuko’s hand, smiling at him.

“Me too.” Zuko replies softly. He really can’t imagine what he would give to have been born into a life like this. He could have lived a simple life with gentle, loving people who allowed him to play and find a little space for himself, not just living within restrictions set for him long before he was even an idea.

If he had been born into this life, he wouldn’t have a scar taking up a third of his face, he wouldn’t sometimes feel panic when heat pressed on his face, even from the safe flames in the hearth, he might not have nightmares with his father’s face always lurking in the shadows. There might still be more of him left. At least he can try and salvage the pieces that he still has.

When Kyira and Fao reach the edge of their farm, they hug Zuko goodbye before he starts running in the other direction back towards Kani in Chen with real hope in his heart that his life might be ready to turn around for the better.

### Text

The next two weeks consist of learning a little more about the gardens and animals, learning to cook a little more, and spending a little more time with Fao and Kyira. However, for the most part, he stays near home.

At least he hopes that he can call Kani and Chen's home his as well. He needs to be able to. He wants to stay with them for as long as they allow it. He never wants to leave.

Zuko wakes up before Kani and Chen like he has since his fever had broken. He doesn't want to be asleep while they walk around the house. It's when he's the most weak and vulnerable. Worse, he might appear worthless and lazy. He might be thrown out if seen sleeping later than them.

Anyways, Agni pulls him out of sleep with Their rise now that he isn't plagued with perpetual fatigue.

He sits with his hands cupped in front of him, holding fire in his hands, trying to shape it into the lizard snake Chen had shown him.

He's mostly just getting the snake part down...the body of the snake, not the head. It's getting better though. It now looks like a rope and not just...long fire.

Footsteps start coming down the stone staircase and Zuko puts out his flame, pulling his knees under his chin, looking at Kani as she comes into Zuko's view.

"Hey, sweetheart, you want to help me make breakfast?" She asks, walking over to him, offering Zuko her hand.

Zuko nods, taking it eagerly, standing up before being pulled into a gentle embrace.

He leans closer against Kani, feeling her warmth and comfort seeping into his soul. He just wants her to hold him forever. If she holds him like this, she might not leave too. He needs her to stay.

The embrace ends as she presses an affectionate kiss to the top of his head. Zuko can't help but smile at the casual affection.

Kani leads Zuko to the kitchen, rubbing his back as he starts a fire in the stove. "What are we making?" He asks quietly, standing up as the fire crackles.

"We're going to make jook and eggs. If you would go collect the eggs from the barn, I'll start the jook. They're in the nests on the ledges to the right of the door." She kisses the back of his head after speaking.

Zuko nods, slowly moving away from her, slipping on his shoes, and walking out the front door. He is careful to close it behind him as silently as possible, not wanting to irritate Kani with unnecessary noise. He wants to please her. He *needs* to prove himself. He needs to do anything he can to be allowed to stay.

The early rays of sunlight cause the dew on the blades of grass and surrounding garden to almost glow. Despite all the wealth and power Zuko's family had growing up, their decorations have nothing on this. It was all so formal and threatening. That was likely the point. It always made Zuko feel so small and trapped.

He slowly walks to the barn, opening the door quietly, not wanting to bother the animals too badly. For the most part, they are still laying down in the hay.

Zuko doesn't want to let them into the pen yet, he knows Chen does that and he doesn't want to intrude. He doesn't want to get in trouble for something so simple when just trying to help. He knows better than to make assumptions now. His father made sure to teach him that.

Taught him that over and over again.

The variety of chicken akin creatures are resting on the ground, perched on rafters, or still in their nests, some still asleep, some looking at him as he walks in.

Zuko quietly collects eggs, carefully putting them in his pockets, avoiding the nests with animals in them after one hisses at him.

When he's done, he makes his way back to the house, leaving his shoes at the door and walking in, head down.

When he walks into the kitchen, he sees the pot of jook on the stove cooking and Kani laughing while gently shoving Chen's face away from her ear as he grins, arms wrapped around her waist, semi dragging her around the kitchen while they're both still standing.

Zuko *knows* that Chen isn't hurting her. He knows that Kani wouldn't allow anyone to hurt her, that Chen isn't that kind of man. Zuko knows that Chen and Kani love each other. Every interaction with Chen has been gentle.

Despite that knowledge, Zuko can't help but take a few steps back away from the couple. He knows how just about every interaction between his own mother and father went. So much of him knows that this isn't the same...but so many parts of him still don't.

He can't force distant memories and fears from his mind as he continues to back away, unsure where he is trying to get to. Unsure what to do at all.

He feels walls pressing against him as he backs himself into a corner, eyes falling on him. He can hear his new name being repeated with concern and feel wet, cold slime soaking through a small part of his robes, not fully sure what is even wrong.

He feels a hand touching his cheek, meeting Chen's dark brown eyes.

"Hey, son, what's wrong? Did something happen? Do you need something?" Chen asks softly, Kani kneeling near Zuko's blind side, holding his hand.

Zuko shakes his head, reaching into his pocket, feeling the eggs. He's pretty sure only one is broken. Maybe repercussions won't be as bad if six are still intact.

"Broke one of the eggs, s-sorry sir." He whispers, dabbing gently at his face, avoiding re-aggravating his eye.

"Is that all? Are you sure nothing else happened? Anything at all? Neither of us give shit about the egg. It's just an egg, son."

Zuko nods once, closing his eyes, not sure what to say or feel. He feels stupid, ashamed, and terrified.

Chen had taken Zuko into his home with almost no hesitation knowing full well that Zuko is a firebender. From that moment that Zuko has been here the man has only treated Zuko kindly. Gone out of his way to be gentle and accommodating.

He can't stop the guilt and shame from filling his chest and throat for accusing Chen of something Zuko knows he would never do, even if not out loud. It's so thick Zuko can feel it choking him. Part of him wishes Chen had never found him or had just killed him upon discovery.

Kani wraps her arms around him, careful to avoid the eggs, helping him stand, pressing a kiss to the side of his head.

Zuko can see the worry in Chen's expression. Zuko just looks down, feeling more guilty for lying about something Chen hadn't done. Sorry for making him worry because Zuko doesn't have thick enough skin. He should have thicker skin. It's why his father had trained him. Zuko just kept failing. He would always be the failure son.

Zuko rests his forehead against Kani's stomach, closing his eyes, gripping her robes. "H-he'd hurt her…my father would." He whispers, wanting to give an explanation for something no one here has done.

"Who would he hurt, love?" Kani asks softly, running the tips of her fingers through his hair. "You can tell us anything you need, you're safe here. You're safe."

"My mom." He whimpers. Maybe if Ozai hadn't hurt her, his mom wouldn't have been so easily driven away by Zuko's shortcomings.

Maybe if Zuko had been a better son, his father wouldn't have hurt her so much. He wouldn't always be so angry about Zuko's failures and disappointments. He wouldn't have needed someone to let his anger out on when Zuko wasn't enough.

Wouldn't be driven to violence by his failure son.

"Did you think I was hurting Kani this morning?" Zuko can see Chen kneeling down out of the corner of his eye. Zuko turns a little to look at him.

"No?" He answers it more like a question. "I dunno. Y-you've been so good to me and I *know* you're not like that but…I'm sorry. " Zuko shakes his head, not sure how to explain it. He just feels so ashamed and for being unable to differentiate Chen from his own father for even a moment.

There is a painful moment of silence before Chen speaks again. "Lee, can I touch you? I promise I won't hurt you but you can say no if you want."

Zuko nods tentatively, pulling away from Kani, moving towards Chen a little, praying he keeps his word about no pain.

Strong arms slowly wrap around him, hugging him gently, rubbing his back carefully before pulling back, fingers now on Zuko's cheek.

"Lee, you're not the one who should be apologizing and I'm not the one who needs an apology. Your father was supposed to love and protect you when you were small and defenseless but instead he hurt you over and over again in ways I'm sure I'm not aware of. You're healing and being introduced to a completely new way of life. There is no right or wrong way for you to react to any of this."

Zuko isn't sure how to respond to that, none of what Chen says is expected.

"Both Kani and I had parents who did their best to treat us well and bring us up in a healthy home, something you didn't have. We have no idea what you're going through right now. You don't need to tell us everything that happened and what you're feeling if you don't want to, but we don't know what you need right now. If you ever need something, just ask, we won't get angry at you for asking. If you want to talk about something at any time, we'll listen. I would never hurt Kani and I would never hurt you, I'll do what I need to do to make you feel like that's true."

Chen rests his forehead on the top of Zuko's head, hands gently holding his shoulders. "I'm sorry if I scared you, son. I love Kani, and I would never do anything to hurt her. Not only would I never hurt you, but we'll protect you from anyone who might ever even *think* about hurting you."

A small sob Zuko escapes his lips as he wraps his arms around Chen's neck. "Thank you for saving me. For everything." He whimpers.

"Please just try and keep in mind that you're safe now. You can have bad days, you can be scared and upset if you feel that way. We won't ever hurt you for just expressing yourself."

Zuko grips onto Chen's robes a little tighter before jumping back, feeling for the eggs, thankfully, still only one is broken.

"Don't wanna break anymore...sorry sir." He explains, wincing at the apology, remembering Chen had just told him to not apologize, hoping he doesn't get in trouble.

"It's alright, Lee, it's okay, let's finish making breakfast." Chen kisses his forehead before standing, walking into the kitchen with Kani, hand still on Zuko's back.

Chen has never been one for violence, most people are intimidated enough by his stature to back down from any physical altercation. However, in the occasions that it came to it, Kani would handle any aggressive interactions. She may be a healer, but still.

Despite that, Chen is ready to find out just exactly who Lee's father is and who he thinks he is and settle their differences.

Chen is ready to kill that man for whatever horrors he had put Lee through.

He's always so scared over little things he does by mistake. They're likely only made because he is already jumpy and having trouble paying attention.

If Chen could just prove to Lee that he would never do anything to hurt him right here and now, he would. Unfortunately, what Lee needs is to learn to trust him, and that takes time, persistence, and patience.

Lee might even need a little bit of space from him after talking about something clearly so personal. He's alway gravitating towards Kani but seems to back up a little when Chen comes in. Just letting the kid settle and feel like this is really his home could do a lot of good.

Chen *does* need to go into town soon anyways. The weather is supposed to be good for the next few days. It isn't a hard trip, especially not with an ostrich horse, just a long one. With the sun barely risen, he has more than enough time to make it. His sister in law has always let both him and Kani stay the night unannounced when in town.

Neither he nor Kani really drink, but Kani uses liquor to sanitize wounds. They certainly won't drink with Lee around. His father's abuse could be attributed to heavy alcohol use. The last thing they need to do is traumatize the little boy all over again. Keep him from thinking that it would only be so long until blows started.

They'll usually try and get spices from town, he'll have to see if they have dried chilies or chili powder. Chen doesn't know much about Fire Nation cuisine but he knows it's spicy. Lee might miss his culture even if not his home. It would be good for him to be able to remember some of it.

They'll sometimes sell hard candies as well. That's something Lee might like. He seems to have a lot of trouble eating. It might be something good to give him.

He and Kani are trying to think of a way to get Lee to eat more, smaller meals throughout the day considering he slowly picks at his larger meals, not able to eat much in one sitting. Might be a good way to get him used to eating throughout the day.

Lee really needs to put on some weight during the summer before food gets more scarce in the winter. They've never gone hungry, but Kani had pointed out that the firebender might get really sick with how thin he is.

He watches as Lee slowly eats the whites on the fried egg on top of his jook. Chen wouldn't be too surprised if Lee only eats the egg and a few small bites of his jook over the course of twenty minutes.

Chen does *not* want to know what led to this. Likely another thing Lee's father did. It's not how someone who grew up with little food to eat reacts.

"Hey, Kani, Lee, I was thinking it would be good for me to go into town today. Weather is supposed to be good for a few days. Is there anything you think we need besides spices and medicinal liquor?" He asks, nodding towards Lee while looking at Kani when the firebender is preoccupied with looking at his food. He mostly just stirs it with his chopsticks, occasionally taking a small bite.

Chen is almost certain it's something stress induced. His appetite is heavily affected by his day. If there aren't any issues that day, he'll usually be able to pick his way through most of what he is served. Even though nothing really bad happened this morning, it still caused the little boy stress and is heavily affecting him.

Chen has no idea what someone could do to another person to make eating this difficult for anyone. Especially a child.

"If you could get some cloth I want to be able to make some clothes at some point for Lee. He'll probably grow out of Fao's old ones soon enough." Her voice sounds somewhat hopeful. Getting Lee to eat more might help some with his stunted growth.

Lee looks up at her, opening his mouth to say something before looking back down at the table. Chen feels his heart ache for his sweet boy.

"You can talk whenever you want to, son. No one will be upset with you for talking." Chen rests his hand on Lee's as he speaks, hoping it calms him.

"I'm alright I…" He trails off for a moment, furrowing his brows...well...brow, technically, before speaking again. "Just not really used to people looking out for me so much is all." He moves a little closer to Chen as he speaks, giving him a hint of a smile.

"Are there any spices or foods you like, Lee?" Chen asks, hoping there would be anything that could help the scrawny boy eat.

Lee bites his lip for a moment, thinking. "I-I like ginseng and jasmine tea...and any kind of noodles. Reminds me of my uncle." He says softly, eating another small bite of his jook.

Chen hadn't been expecting Lee to share anything personal with him, but it's a good step in the right direction. He seems to trust them a little more at least.

"I dunno if the town accepts Fire Nation money...I have some in my bag. If I'm really allowed to stay here, I don't really need it and nowhere really to spend it."

Chen's biggest takeaway from that is Lee feels like he can start parting with some of his possessions. He hopes it's because Lee is beginning to feel safe here and like he doesn't need to run at a moment's notice. He's sure some of it might have to do with if a boy traveling alone with distinctly Fire Nation features was spending Fire Nation money he may easily give himself away.

Hopefully most of it is the former.

"I'm not sure if they'll accept it, love, but you can keep it. It's alright. As long as you want to be, you're family. We'll make sure you have what you need." Kani rests a hand on Lee's shoulder. "I'm sure we can make some noodles here if you want. They're excellent for a cold day, and grain stores well."

Chen smiles at the two. "I'm sure they'll have the tea, I'll get some for you if they have it." He nor Kani drink much tea outside of for health purposes and for warmth in the winter. He's glad Lee is finally expressing preference, even if hesitantly.

"Please?" Lee whispers nervously. "You've already done so much for me and I haven't been able to really do much to help yet."

The look Lee gives him is near desperate. He is certainly used to needing to earn his place. Not just by following some basic rules and participating in the household like most children. He is too aware that the love by his father and any other people from his home is so conditional. That he could be thrown out at a moment's notice. That he actually *was* thrown out for being human.

Sighing quietly, Chen nods. "Okay, son, but you don't have to. This can be your home and it won't be taken from you just because." He tries to reassure the kid.

Lee almost immediately stands up, walking away from the table and kneeling in front of his bag.

As he digs through it, Chen notices that he doesn't take anything out and set it on the ground like most people would. He doubts the kid is hiding anything in there, Chen had seen the contents of it the second night. Mostly just expected supplies for someone traveling by foot.

Unfortunately, it's very likely he still feels very possessive over his belongings, worried they'll be snatched at a without warning.

When Lee comes back over, he hands Chen a bag of almost all gold coins. It sounded like Lee had moved some of the money either out of or into this bag from another one. Either way, this isn't all the money a banished 13 year old kid has. Chen has no idea where the actual *fuck* this kid got so much money and what kind of family he comes from.

Despite that, he doesn't ask. Probably not the best thing to say to a traumatized boy who is still nervous around him. He would likely only get Lee to shut down.

Almost immediately after, Lee walks back over to his breakfast, picking at it again. It's almost as if he knows the question Chen wants to ask and knows he wouldn't like the answer. The real answer. Not the one he might give hastily.

Chen doesn't know what Lee's family life was like other than bad. He doesn't know what kind of life the boy is used to.

He understands why Lee is keeping things from them and holds no ill will against him, but he wishes the little firebender felt like he could talk to them. Like he could tell them anything about his life without fear of rejection.

If he were born into nobility or as a peasant, it wouldn't be Lee's fault. He didn't choose where or how he was born. He's just trying to find a place now.

That's all that really matters now.

One thing that might help Lee settle is making him feel more like family. Chen will be staying with Kani's sister Feya tonight. He could tell her about Lee, let Lee know what he's doing, make it so he could understand that they *want* him in the family.

Chen really doesn't care if Lee has been here for less than a month.

He and Kani had wanted children, but it hadn't been able to happen. Lee needs a family and not everyone would take in a damaged firebender boy. He needs safety.

It might be good to begin making it somewhat official. Chen really would like Lee to stay here.

Lee needs a lot of help, but they live on a farm and don't need to go somewhere to work. They can spend the time with Lee that he really needs, help him learn to feel comfortable around people. Not everyone would be able to put in the time and effort that Lee really needs to get anywhere besides being small, isolated, and scared.

A lot of people wouldn't accept him being a firebender and it would put him in so much danger. Chen has no idea what could happen to Lee if someone wanted to take their anger towards the Fire Nation out on a scared kid.

As Lee is preoccupied with his food, Chen rests his hand on Kani's shoulder. "Hey, love, can I talk to you for a moment?"

Kani nods, standing, following him out of earshot from Lee.

"So, I was thinking it might be good to tell Feya about Lee. You'll be seeing her eventually come winter and Lee might want to come. She'll definitely come up here eventually. Think it might help Lee feel more like he belongs here if we start telling family about him." He hopes Kani is alright with that. He really thinks it might help. "Only if Lee is alright with it, of course." He adds hastily.

Kani smiles, nodding a little. "I think that would be good for him. Also, Feya is stubborn. It might be good for her to have some time for her to accept that we have taken in a firebender child while she isn't around him. I think it's a wonderful idea."

Chen smiles, standing on the balls of his feet, pressing a kiss to Kani's cheek before walking back over to Lee, Kani following close behind.

Before he can say anything to the kid, she takes his hand, making eye contact, mouthing 'he trusts me more.'

It isn't a secret and it isn't something that Chen is offended by. Lee had been horrifically abused by his father for years and Chen knows his stature is intimidating.

It is probably best for Kani to bring it up. It would make sense for Lee to be hesitant about revealing himself to more people. It will be better for him in the long run. Hopefully.

"Lee, sweetheart?" Kani starts, sitting next to Zuko, taking one of his hands, looking at him.

Lee nervously looks between the two of them before his body tenses, looking down. "Yes?" He whispers, barely audible.

"Chen is going to be staying with my sister tonight when traveling. I usually go to see her for a few weeks in the winter and she will periodically come up here to visit. We would love to have you stay with us if that's something you want. We want to know if it would be alright to tell her that we've taken you in. Tell her you're going to be a part of the family."

The expression Lee has when he looks up indicates he was not expecting anything like that. Likely expecting ridicule.

"I-I can stay? Like *really* stay? I want to stay just…" he trails off, likely thinking about how he had to leave his last home by force while so horribly injured.

Before Kani can speak, Chen steps in. "We want you to stay, son. You're a good kid and you need a good home. If you're not ready for us to tell others about you, we won't be upset. We just want you to feel like you're wanted here and at home."

Lee starts nodding, moving closer to Kani, whimpering quietly. "Wanna stay." He repeats. "Y-you can tell her. Wanna stay so bad."

Kani rests her chin on the top of Lee's head, pulling him closer, rubbing his back. "Is it okay if Chen tells her that you're a firebender? She won't come here unless she is ready to accept you as a part of the family, firebender or not." She explains, gently rocking the trembling little boy against her chest.

"Promise she won't hurt me?" Lee asks after a few moments of hesitant silence.

Sadness wells back up in Chen's chest as he moves a hand forward, resting it on Lee's shoulder. "She wouldn't ever hurt you. She's stubborn, but kind. I can assure your complete safety." He promises.

Raising his head a little, Lee gives a jerky nod. "O-okay. I trust you."

Only a few minutes after Chen leaves the house, Lee says something about letting out the animals before fleeing towards the barn.

Kani is sure that he knows that Chen already let them out when getting the ostrich horse. She's sure he's just overwhelmed.

It concerns her how scared Lee is about showing emotion in front of her and Chen now that he's healed. That's a big thing that he needs help with. Whatever family he came from, genuine emotional displays were either frowned upon or punished.

Kani starts cleaning up from breakfast, wanting to give Lee awhile to calm down.

She doesn't want to leave him alone for too long, worried he might get too into his own head without knowing what's wrong. He gets emotionally overwhelmed pretty easily. Likely because he was around emotionally abusive people his whole life, isn't used to others displaying emotions and has no idea how to control his own outside of repression.

She also doesn't want to approach him too soon. He needs a moment to calm down alone and to not have her hovering over him. He just needs a little time before anything she does to help just makes things worse.

After cleaning, she walks out the door towards the barn. As she approaches, she can hear quiet whimpering and heavy breathing.

Walking towards the sound, she rounds the corner to see Lee crying quietly, a chicken cat in his lap, looking up at his tearstained face.

"Sweetheart?" She asks quietly, feeling so sorry for him as he flinches at her voice before hiding his face. She can hear him trying to force his breaths to even out in a concerningly effective manner. He must be far too used to this.

"Lee, it's alright, you can cry, you can be upset and don't need to understand why. Emotions can be very difficult." She reassures him, kneeling next to the kid, resting a hand on his shoulder.

"I think you're just a little overwhelmed right now and it's okay if you feel like you need to cry. If you need to be alone, I'll give you space, if you want company, I'll stay here. We can talk about how you're feeling, we can talk about something else, or we can be quiet. Just let me know what you need. I won't be upset at any choice you make. I promise. I just want to help you."

It's several minutes of Lee whimpering quietly, petting the creature in his lap, and looking at Kani nervously before he answers.

"Wanna just listen to you talk about something else. Wanna help with something and just listen to you." He mumbles, resting his head against her chest.

As he talks, he coaxes the chicken cat off of his lap which jumps through the boards of the fence into the pen with the other animals.

"Okay, love, okay, wanna help in the garden? Some weeds need to be pulled and I need to dry some herbs as wells. I can teach you more about the medicinal ones. Does that sound good to you?"

Lee nods silently.

Kani pulls him into a gentle embrace before they stand up and begins walking towards the garden. She can only hope that she can offer enough help for the little boy to be okay.

Kani and Chen had met for the first time at 16 and 17 almost 23 years ago. Chen's family would regularly travel into town to sell produce at the market.

Coming from a big family, it was easy to have enough people coming to town and staying at the farm.

Chen didn't mind the trip to town like many of his siblings did, so he would almost always go.

At one point, he had gotten stung by a bumble-scorp and had gone to the local healer to get it looked at before it got worse.

That was where he met Kani, working with her mother and younger sister, all skilled healers.

After that, Chen would go to the healing hut after the market closed, giving poor descriptions of minor ailments and bringing fruit, flowers, and candy.

He and Kani would talk for awhile, eating whatever he had brought. When he had to get back go his family and she to hers that night, he would always ask her on a real date. Every time, she would give him a small smirk and a shrug before leaving.

One day during the market, she found him at his family's stand. She had told him that if he really wanted to take her out, he could take her to the harvest festival that night.

She had barely been able to finish her sentence when he agreed.

Chen's father had found his love interest sweet and his brother made fun of him non stop. However, he did get to leave the stand early to meet Kani on time.

They spent several hours at the festival, trying food, dancing, and playing games.

When the festivities died down, they went down to the beach and tried to find interesting rocks and shells without too much luck.

As it got late, he walked her home and she had kissed him goodnight. He wasn't able to get over that excitement for days.

They saw each other for a little more than three years before Chen asked her parents' blessing to ask for Kani's hand in marriage. It wasn't too long after that they got married.

Kani and Feya were supposed to take over for their mother's healing hut and work together. Feya has enough hands to help her, but it's more that she felt that Chen had taken her sister from her as they moved into the countryside.

It had taken her three years to come around to him. She was never mean or anything, she just didn't like him and didn't hide it.

She didn't think he was good enough for Kani and missed her sister. But after spending some time together for awhile, Feya and Chen started becoming friends.

Their relationship has improved ever since. What he's worried about is that her stubbornness will come out about Lee being a firebender. It isn't his fault and he's been following all the rules about only firebending in the house when no one else is there.

Lee just needs to be accepted and loved for who he is.

When Chen reaches town, the market stands are beginning to close, but not all of them. He remembers that Lee had said that he loves theater, something Chen doesn't know too much about.

A stand selling masks, books for plays that were originally just stories, and scrolls of some actual plays.

Chen tells the man running the stand about the 13 year old kid hurt by the war who is definitely not a firebender that he and his wife had taken in. That this kid really likes theater and Chen hopes that it will help him settle a little.

After some discussion, Chen buys a book called 'love amongst the dragons' and a blue mask with long teeth. The man said that the mask is the character of The Blue Spirit, an entity that holds no alignment to a side in human history but brings aid to those of all walks of life who need it.

To his surprise, the man does accept Fire Nation money. He still wants to know where Lee got so much. He also really doesn't know if he wants the answer.

When he finishes buying the things for Lee, the rest of the market is closing. He will have more than enough time to get what he actually came for tomorrow tomorrow. He usually does all of his shopping the next day, not always making it here this early.

He begins leading his ostrich horse towards Feya's healing hut, trying it outside where it has access to food and water.

He walks into the room and sees her bandaging a man's hand. Chen sits down, waiting for her to finish.

When the man leaves, Chen walks over to her, embracing her warmly. "How are you doing, Feya?" He asks as they pull away.

"Decent." She replies before gives him a warm smile, walking over to the door, shutting and locking it before beckoning him up the stairs leading him to her home. The home that she, Kani, and her mother used to live in together.

Feya's husband had once lived here as well, but he had gone to war seven years ago. No one had heard from him since. No reports if he were alive or dead.

They all know, though.

Despite that, Feya had never remarried.

Feya begins making a fire and putting a pot on it before turning to Chen. "Have you eaten?" She asks, sitting by the table before Chen joins her. Chen shakes his head in response to the question.

"You're earlier than normal, is anything in particular bringing you here?" She asks, perceptive as always.

Chen looks at the table silently for a moment before looking up at her again. "Kani and I kinda have a kid." Unsure how else to start this conversation.

Feya raises her eyebrows. "What is that supposed to mean? The 'kinda' part. How long has this been?"

"Well, I found him injured and sick in the storm almost a month ago. His father had burned him and sent him to die. He was halfway there when I found him. Kani healed him and he's been staying with us. He's so scared but he's such a sweet kid and he really wants to stay." He explains, unsure how to break the news about his element.

Feya smiles warmly. "I'm glad you two found him. He has a good home now, at least. What's his name? How old is he?" She asks, standing and bringing the pot of chili and two bowls to the table, scooping some into the bowls, handing one to Chen.

"He's 13 and his name is Lee. The thing is…'' He takes a slow breath before continuing. "Lee is a firebender from the Fire Nation. He denounced the war, was burned by his father who then requested the powers that be to throw him out of the country. He's completely traumatized and he just wants to be safe. We were hoping you would be willing to accept him as part of the family." Chen explains quickly, sure that there were much better ways to explain that that how he just did.

Feya just looks at him, mouth half open.

Chen takes a bite of his chili, trying to distract himself before trying to fill the silence. "He doesn't firebend outside of starting fires inside the house for us. He knows the dangers of someone seeing him. He's been very good about following that. He knows that's the main part about him being able to stay. He's safe."

Feya blinks, exhaling slowly. "You're a fucking idiot, Chen." She scolds, taking an aggressive bite of her food. "You have a good heart, but you're an idiot. That kid could be *anyone.* Do you even know if Lee is his real name?" She asks.

Chen shakes his head. "I know what I'm doing, Feya. I wasn't just going to let a little kid die in a storm like that. I don't think he's anyone really. We thought he was nine or ten when we found him, he looks half starved. Kani said stunted growth goes hand in hand with chronic malnutrition. We can see all of his ribs and he's clearly been abused his whole life. Probably just the son of some peasant, war loving, nationalists."

He doesn't really think that is the case. It doesn't explain the money or why Lee doesn't act like he didn't have access to food but someone who is used to food being used as a weapon against them. He's also sure that Lee isn't his real name.

Chen isn't about to share any of that with Feya. Not yet at least. Once she meets Lee, sees how small he is, has him fall asleep while curled up to her side, and just sees how sweet of a kid he is, Chen will share the doubts he has.

For now, it's about Lee's safety.

Feya shakes her head. "You're still an idiot. He hurts my sister, you better hope he kills you, I won't do anything so merciful." She threatens.

Chen nods, he knows she isn't bluffing.

With that, Feya eats her chili quickly before standing and leaning the room. He doesn't know why he thought that this would go any better than it just had.
