### Text

Zuko quietly smashes spices with the pestle in mortar, careful to get all of it evenly and to not spill any onto the floor. He doesn't want to mess this up. It's so simple. He *can't* mess this up.

Kani had shown him the one that she uses for cooking and the one she uses for healing. Zuko isn’t sure why she doesn’t wash one out and use one. He’s sure there’s a reason that he just doesn’t understand. There is so much he doesn’t understand. Whatever that reason is, Zuko knows that it isn’t his place to ask. Best case scenario, she would answer and it would make him feel even more stupid. Worse cast, she would make sure he knew his place. Would remind him he isn't here to ask stupid questions.

Ozai might not be here anymore, but he’s right about Zuko’s intelligence. He was right about so much that Zuko wanted to deny. He could deny it to himself now, but not without knowing he’s a liar. There is so much that he wanted to be wrong, *needed* to be wrong.

Unfortunately, that isn’t the case. Zuko is nothing but a failure and a disappointment.

Zuko had failed his mother over and over again. She had taken on the burden for so many of Zuko's failures until she couldn't anymore. Until she had to leave. She had given Ozai what he needed, heirs. He didn't need her anymore. She was able to flee Ozai's cruelty, leaving Zuko to suffer under it alone for a long time.

He had suffered alone until Iroh came back and used Zuko to fill the gaping hole in his heart. Zuko knew from the beginning that is all he was. That if he shared what Ozai was really doing to him with his uncle, Iroh would leave. He couldn't greif and protect Zuko. He would move on to Azula, leaving Zuko alone again. Silence was better than abandonment.

Kani and Chen have been far kinder than anyone else ever had been to him.

Well, his mother had been this kind, but there was only so much that she could do. She could hold him by the turtle duck pond, read and tell him stories, tell him how much she loved him, and make him feel safe even if for a moment.

Unfortunately, she couldn’t protect him. She couldn’t stop his father’s blows or cruel words, could only help bandage his wounds and kiss him gently. She could only sit outside the door where Zuko was locked away, talking to him when permitted. She could only hold him, crying, as he was starved. Unable to feed him, only ease his suffering through distractions, gently rubbing his stomach, and teas suggested by servants to help ease the pain and nausea.

They had both learned that her intervention would only make things worse for both herself and for Zuko. It could always get so much worse. Unbearably worse

Kani gently pulls Zuko into hugs and kisses him throughout the day, most for no real reason. He always wants her to be touching him like that. He always wants to be in her arms. Even when she is just gently touching him, such as a hand on his back, shoulder, or head, he has trouble pulling away. He doesn’t want her to disappear too. He isn’t sure if he could take that. He is almost positive it would leave him shattered, unable to find a way to move on.

Every logical part of Zuko’s mind knows that Chen is good, kind, and honest. The man had lifted him from the ground soaked with rain, mud, and his own blood. He had taken Zuko into his home with little hesitation despite knowing that Zuko is a firebender because all Chen saw was a scared, injured kid.

Zuko is sure that the man knows that Zuko feels hesitant around him. Instead of yelling at Zuko and telling him to be brave, Chen has given Zuko space and extended so much of his patience. He’s been so gentle and kind, never once getting angry at Zuko for making mistakes or being scared. Chen has even tried to help him feel more secure.

Chen has done so much for him without being asked or thanked. Zuko doesn't understand, but he's grateful. The innate part of him keeps waiting for the other shoe to drop, for Chen to show his true colors. So far, it hasn't happened.

Zuko *knows* that Chen is safe but he can’t believe it no matter how desperately he wants to.

Zuko wants Chen to hold him to his chest, rub his back, and tell him that he’s loved and wanted. He wants to fall asleep against Chen’s side, wrapped in the safety of his arms. Zuko just can’t get past how easily the man could hurt him. How easily Zuko’s own father had hurt him with no care or concern. How Chen would only need one hand to break Zuko's bones.

Zuko had tried to keep his mind off of Chen as Zuko and Kani had worked in the gardens. It had been difficult, but the work at least helped soothe him a little. He needed that at least.

She had shown him how to properly harvest different vegetables so that it would damage the plant the least and it could grow more. He had helped clean out the barn and take care of the animals. The chicken cat Zuko had kind of befriended had followed him around most of the day, rubbing it’s soft feathers against Zuko’s legs, purring and then clucking happily when Zuko had given it corn.

After working, Zuko had helped cut up the vegetables as Kani prepped the meat and found the right spices for him to mash. Most of them he had never heard of even though they smell familiar. He's likely eaten them, just never thought too much about them.

Zuko had done most of that silently, knowing that Chen would be returning any moment. He had gotten Chen off of his mind earlier today, but now that evening is approaching, Zuko can almost exclusively think of Chen.

Every worst case scenario, no matter how ridiculous it seems, plays out in his head. Zuko has been given plenty of horrible beatings that left him in pain for days over trivial things.

Zuko prays that the market accepts Fire Nation money. If it had been declined, Zuko isn’t sure how Chen might react, possibly thinking that Zuko had tried to set him up. Zuko isn’t sure what he would have set Chen up for…but the man could probably think of a reason to ruin Zuko’s nice day and hit him. The man could easily beat Zuko into unconsciousness with minimal effort.

As soon as Zuko finishes mashing the spices, he slides the mortar over to Kani, unsure what to do next. He moves a little closer to her, gently resting his head against her side, wanting to feel her presence. Wanting to feel safe and loved.

Kani gives him a warm smile as she takes the mashed spices, rubbing them over the meat and vegetables that have been prepared and then putting them in the oven. The smell slowly filling the room.

“Thank you for helping me, love.” She praises, leaning down, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s head. He can’t stop himself from grinning, forgetting about his fears for a moment.

Zuko really wants to do more. He wants to prove himself, wants to be helpful. He wants to be allowed to stay here. He *needs* to be allowed to stay. He isn't sure what he would do.

“Um, Kani?” He asks tentatively, still trying to remind himself that he can start a conversation with her without urgency. That unless she is having an important conversation with someone, he isn’t speaking out of turn. Even then, she would simply shoo him away if what he had to say wasn’t important, not hurt him.

“Yes, sweetheart?” She asks, handing Zuko a pitcher to go fill with water in the spigot as she begins to put bowls and cups at the table.

“I usually get up earlier…I was wondering if it would be alright if I started making breakfast. I know how to make the jook by myself now.” He offers quietly. He wants to be seen as helpful. If he is helpful, he won’t be thrown out so easily.he needs to take initiative. If he can be of use to them, they might be more inclined to keep him.

Kani smiles at him. “That would be really helpful, thank you.”

Zuko nods once before darting outside to fill up the water. He hopes that maybe it might help him earn his keep a little. Especially because winter is coming. He’s never experienced a real winter, never seen snow, but he knows that nothing grows and it’s cold. He knows he wouldn’t survive if he were thrown out. He knows he might misjudge people. That they might hurt him.

All he can do for now is not let that happen. He wouldn’t be able to bear it. Either from exposure or from heartbreak, it would kill him.

It hadn’t taken long for Chen to get what he needed at the market. Most of the stuff he got is pretty standard. Cloth not yet turned into clothes is something that he was able to come across pretty easily. He settled on a deep green, hoping Lee would like the color.

After he shopped at the market, he got on his ostrich horse and began the trek home, not wanting to discuss Lee with his sister in law again. He hopes that she understands that if she wants to come visit, she will need to respect that Lee is there and that he is a firebender. She doesn’t have to like that, but she has to be nice to him.

As soon as Feya meets the sweet little boy, he doubts it will be an issue. She just needs proof that Lee only ever uses his firebending for domestic help and only wants to be loved, even if he tends to shy away from it. That he’s just a scared little kid who needs help. He needs so much help. Maybe more than Kani and Chen could give him.

When he gets back to the house and puts the ostrich horse up along with plenty of food and water, the sun is beginning to get low in the sky. He’s likely home just in time for dinner. He hopes that it hasn’t been sitting out on the table for too long and gotten cold. Maybe Lee could heat it up again if it had, perks of having a firebender as your adopted son.

As he walks up to the house, he makes sure to put one of the bags of candy in his pocket, he bought eight. One he wants to just give to Lee, the others he will just give him pieces throughout the day to make sure that Lee can begin to eat more regularly.

When he walks into the house, he sees Kani putting a plate of spiced meat and vegetables on the table that smells delicious. It does make him feel a little sad to see Lee standing against the wall, arms around his waist, looking down. He doesn’t seem to know what to do with himself without direction. He probably doesn’t. A result of abuse from a militant father.

Chen rests his bags on the ground and walks up to Kani, wrapping his arms around her waist, kissing her cheek. “Hey, love.” He mumbles, smiling.

Even though it had only been two days, he’d missed her. He doesn’t care if his brothers would make fun of him for that. He likes being around Kani. She’s the love of his life and his best friend and he doesn’t really like being away from her. If they don't have that relationship with their spouse, then Chen isn't the one lacking here.

She turns around, kissing him gently before sitting down, gesturing for Lee to join them.

The firebender slowly moves forward, sitting down like he’s a stranger who doesn’t know if he’s welcomed. He might still feel that way even after nearly a month. Chen just wishes he knew what was happening in Lee’s brain right now. It could help him understand and aid the kid better. Know what kinds of things might help him and what sets him off.

There are so many little things that set Lee off that seem to have no correlation. Sometimes Lee is fine with something some of the time, and then others, he panics. Chen just doesn't understand. He wants to. He needs to.

Kani and Chen put food in their plates and begin eating long before Lee even touches any of the food, hesitance in his movements, almost pointedly not looking at them. Something he doesn’t do that often. No matter what, Lee seems nervous. More off than usual.

“Son, are you doing alright? Are you feeling alright?” Chen asks the firebender, almost sure that the kid is trembling a little. He has no idea what could have happened to do this to him. He’s just a kid. He’s so young. Too young for any of this. If it wouldn’t scare him, Chen would wrap his arms around the kid and just let him scream and cry even if he didn’t know what it is about.

Lee nods shakily. “I-I’m okay, sir.” He whispers, now just looking at the food in his bowl.

Chen looks at his wife and she doesn’t seem to know what is wrong either. “Lee, please, you’re worrying me, are you sick? You can tell us if you’re not feeling well, love. We can’t help you if we don’t know what’s wrong.”

Lee shrugs, shaking his head. “I-I dunno.” He sounds on the edge of tears as he speaks, lowering his head further, letting out a tiny whimper. “I-I just think I might be broken. Don’t wanna be. I’m sorry.”

Lee shrinks further in on himself, quickly wiping at his face, refusing to let Kani or himself see the tears that they both know are falling for some unknown reason.

Against better judgment, Chen slowly moves closer to the whimpering firebender, slowly extending a hand. “Lee, son, can I touch you? I wanna hug you, I won’t hurt you. You can say no if you want, I won’t be upset. You don’t need to hide the fact that you're crying. We just want to understand what’s happening. We can’t help you if we don’t know what’s wrong.”

Chen half expects Lee to flee from the room and go cry out in the field or the barn. Instead, he slowly moves towards Chen, resting against his side, head still down, tears still falling. He doesn’t say anything, just slowly positions himself closer, flinching the first time Chen runs his hand down Lee’s arm before beginning to relax.

After a full minute, it becomes clear that Lee either doesn’t know what to say or doesn’t want to.

“Lee, can I tell you what I think is going on? You can tell me if I’m wrong, I won’t be upset. Kani and I just want to help you. We just don’t understand.” He mumbles against the crying boy’s head.

Chen is once again so grateful that it was him who found Lee. Even if someone else would look past him being a firebender, horribly injured, and clearly lying about a lot of his past, Lee is a really challenging kid.

He isn’t trying to be. He’s so sweet and gentle. He is so eager to learn and contribute to the household and the farm. But he has issues. A lot of them.

Lee won’t share what’s really bothering him and Kani and Chen just have to watch him suffer sometimes. It’s heartbreaking. Chen is well aware that there would be many families who wouldn’t want to put up with whatever is still haunting the firebender. Not give him the time and energy that he needs to start recovering and healing from what was done to him. They would just see him as a problem, not a suffering child who’s just been broken far too many times and doesn’t need to be scared of it being done all over again.

Thankfully, Lee nods slowly, clutching Chen’s robes, fists clenched so tight that his knuckles begin to turn white.

“I think you’re scared of me, son, really scared.” He can feel Lee tense at that comment, Chen continues rubbing his arm, hoping to reassure the kid.

“I’m not upset or offended, just sad. Your father broke you over and over again. The fact that you’re still trying to learn how to trust is astounding. I want you to talk to me. What would make you feel more comfortable? If you need me to give you some space at a particular point, you just have to tell me. If you want to be around me to do something, just talk to me. You’re suffering and I hate to be part of the reason you’re having trouble recovering. Okay?”

Lee nods slowly. “Y-you’ve been so good to me. Saved me. Ne-never hurt me. I don’t understand why I don’t feel safe.” He whimpers into Chen’s shoulder.

Kani moves around the table towards Lee’s other side, resting a hand on his shoulder. “Sweetheart, you’re suffering from horrible, traumatic experiences. That kind of thing doesn’t go away with logic. It takes time. You can’t force it. You need to talk to us. We hate seeing you suffer like this.” She whispers, leaning forward and pressing a kiss to the back of Lee’s head.

“On top of that, I’ve been watching how you react to anything you ever do wrong and how you respond to people. I think you’ve been taught that a mistake is a mistake and that you’ll be punished for it no matter what, is that right?” Kani asks, Chen can hear the dread in her voice as she asks the question.

Unfortunately, Lee nods slowly.

“I’m not sure what exactly your father did to you, but you aren’t going to get punished for making a mistake. If you break something, you fix it or clean it up. If you lose something, you try and find it, or if not able to, you replace it the best you can. If you mess something up, you make sure that you know how to do it correctly the next time and do what you can to make it better. You’re human, you make mistakes. Chen and I make mistakes every single day and will continue to for the rest of our lives. We just do our best to fix them. You aren’t going to get punished for an accident. If no one got hurt, it's okay. It’s usually easy to fix.”

Lee raises his head a little looking between Kani and Chen nervously. “P-promise?” He whimpers, voice sounding as if he expects it to be some kind of cruel joke. Some twisted game that they wanted to play with the poor kid’s life.

“We promise, son.” Chen reassures him. “Also, you don’t need to wait for directions for every little thing. I understand that you come from a militant household and it was probably expected, but you can do things on your own accord. If you genuinely don't know what you’re doing, ask. You don’t need to wait for permission or direction to eat, to get up, or to come inside. If you’re doing something wrong we’ll just tell you. Neither of us will hurt you. Ever.”

Chen cups the little boy’s cheek as he raises his head to look up at him, a lost look in his expression, so much of his world coming apart. So much that needs to come apart. Waiting for Lee to come to the conclusion that he had been abused his whole life on his own hasn’t been working. They need to talk to him. He doesn’t seem to understand if they aren’t direct with him.

Chen is about to try and get Lee to eat something when Kani moves herself into Lee’s line of vision, an apologetic look on her face.

“Lee, there is one more thing we need to talk about. Chen and I haven’t been sure how to bring it up, but it’s getting very concerning and likely very dangerous for your health.”

Lee raises his head at her, confused and concerned, an apology on his lips.

“You don’t have to tell us anything if you don’t want to, you don’t need to explain yourself. We’re worried about you not eating enough. You don’t really eat meals, we’ve tried getting you to eat jerky and dried fruits and vegetables but…you’re really skinny, Lee. Winter is harsh and cold. There is less food. When you’re this skinny, you’re more likely to get sick and less likely to recover. We aren’t going to force you to do anything, but what do you think would help you eat? More, smaller meals? Anything you want to eat in particular? If you can’t really think of anything I want you to do most of your work in the house. It’s less strenuous and uses less of your energy than in the fields. You don’t have to answer now, just think about it, love, alright?”

Chen expects Lee to kind of ignore the question and try to avoid it in the future. Instead, he finally starts sobbing.

"It's alright, son, it's going to be alright. We weren't sure how to bring that up, but it's almost been a month and you aren't doing any better. We're not mad or disappointed or anything. We just need you to talk to us. Please talk to us." Chen whispers, pulling Lee a little closer, hoping Kani hadn't brought up his anxiety around eating too soon.

Lee doesn't respond, but he isn't trying to pull away. Hopefully that's a start, even if a small one.

"You don't need to talk to us now, or tomorrow, or even the day after that. Take your time to think. We won't push you. We'll be able to help you more if you talk to us. So much more." Kani adds.

Lee doesn't move besides rhythmic shaking of his body, crying too quietly for how upset he seems.

Chen knows that learning how to remain silent when falling apart like this comes with abuse, but it's horrible to watch. Painful, even.

A hand rests on his shoulder and he looks up at Kani, now standing over him and Lee.

"I'm going to leave our bowls on the table for later but start cleaning up. You take Lee and try and help him calm down. He really likes the animals, especially the chicken cat." Kani informs him before picking up what is left of the meat and vegetables.

Whatever they don't eat for dinner is usually what they eat for lunch the next day before it goes bad.

Chen has always thought that the chicken cat was a silly looking creature. But it lays eggs just as well as the others and eats unwanted bugs and rodents. It's an unusual, kinda stupid, but helpful animal. He's even more grateful that Lee has taken a liking to it.

He gently lifts the shaking firebender into his arms, feeling like he had the first night Chen had found him. Despite everything, Lee seems just as terrified and lost now as he did then. Chen has no idea how to help him.

Carrying Lee out of the house, Chen begins to make his way towards the barn, hoping spending a little time with the animals would help Lee calm down a little.

Chen feels like an asshole and an idiot for dumping what he just did on Lee, making him think about his trauma when he was already scared. Making him more anxious around a meal. Although, Chen is pretty sure Lee's anxiety was too high to eat anyways.

In his head, if Chen just talked to Lee like a rational adult, he would start coming around and begin to understand that he is safe. Chen knows that trauma like Lee's takes a lot of time to recover from, but apparently being that direct *isn't* the way to go.

Chen should have just kept his mouth shut, offered Lee some candy, and let the kid come to him. He needs to remember that Lee isn't a rational adult. He's a scared little kid who was forced to be an adult but never allowed to properly mature. He's never been allowed to express himself. When it comes to emotion, he's completely irrational.

When they get to the barn, Chen hopes that Lee will just slump into the hay and snuggle with the chicken cat, slowly catching his breath.

Instead, Lee's body goes rigid and he starts apologizing over and over again before slipping out of Chen's arms. Kneeling on the ground, Lee presses his head against the floor at Chen's feet, whimpering and apologizing.

Chen can feel his blood turn cold.

It was at that moment Zuko realized that he fucked up.

He can see the inside of the barn. Kani and Chen are finally losing their almost endless sea of patience with him. Of course Zuko managed to find where they ended. He's always been good at that.

Too good. Painfully good. It seems to be the *only* thing he's good at.

This is going to be the first step to him being thrown out. They're moving him into the barn.

Chen is sick of him flinching from him half the time despite the compassion the man has shown him. They're both sick of him not understanding what to do. If he were smarter, he might be able to figure it out. He can't. They don't even like the way that he eats. It will only take so long before they force him to eat or starve him, not understanding it would make things so much worse.

They're angry at him for not eating. He's glad he stashed some food away, they'll probably deny him food for a few days to make him more willing to eat when food is finally offered again. They'll wait until hunger is gnawing at his sides and he would do just about anything for scraps.

He won't eat much, just enough to keep a little bit of strength up. He can't let them think he's eating. It will get so much worse if they find out. They might even throw him out for real.

Kani and Chen keep talking about winter and that it's hard. They might let him stay until it's over, then throw him out so they can keep a decent conscience about it. If he really messes up, they might throw him out just so he dies from exposure.

Zuko kneels on the ground in front of Chen, resting his forehead on the ground in front of his feet, crying, begging for another chance, apologizing over and over again.

He's sorry for being weak and scared. He's sorry for being stupid and a failure. He's sorry for being a firebender. Sorry for being born.

He feels a hand resting on his back, a forehead against the back of his head. He can hear an echo of crying and apologies in a lower, more controlled voice.

"Lee, what's wrong?" Chen finally whispers, after apologizing for something Zuko doesn't understand, voice cracking a little. "I shouldn't have pushed you earlier, I didn't think what I was doing through well enough and I hurt you. I'm so sorry, son. Kani said you liked the animals and so I took you here. What do you want?" The man asks, carding his fingers through Zuko's short hair.

Zuko isn't sure if he feels more scared, confused, or angry right now. He isn't sure if this is some kind of twisted punishment, forcing Zuko to let all of his walls come down before Chen breaks him. He has no idea what Chen wants...what Kani wants. No one would put up with this just because...would they? No, they wouldn't. Zuko's own father and mother wouldn't. Two Earth Kingdom farmers who had been hurt by firebender wouldn't do all of this for him if they didn't want something. No one would.

Zuko scrambles away from the man, unsure what to do. He can't run. He doesn't have anywhere to go. Everywhere else might be worse. Even though he isn't sure if he is safe here anymore, the stupidest part is that he wants Kani and Chen to love him.

He wants Kani to hold him, to teach him how to heal and to make different dishes. He wants her to teach him about the garden and the animals. He still wants Chen to show him creatures he finds in the field. He wants to belong here despite the fact everything screams that he doesn't.

Chen takes a step forward, reaching a hand out towards Zuko to touch him.

Without thinking, Zuko swats it away, standing up on shaky legs, taking a step back. Even if just for a moment, taking control of the situation makes him feel better. Less scared and vulnerable.

Zuko swipes at his eyes. Taking another step back, shaking his head. "A-are you gonna hit me? Because I'm a failure? Punish me? Wh-what are you gonna do? Don't pretend that it's okay. D-don't pretend like you don't want me to be better! Everyone wants me to be better! I-I didn't ask to be born! I didn't ask to be his!" Before he knows it, Zuko is screaming at the second man who has ever shown Zuko this much unconditional love.

Only the second man who Zuko could lose his temper at completely without panic choking and drowning him before the first hand was even raised.

He wishes his uncle were here. Wishes he could at least understand. He wants to sob into Iroh's shoulder, but here. Not back at the palace. A prison would be safer than anywhere near Ozai. Despite the anger and fear he feels right now, part of Zuko still feels safe here. Even if it's distant.

Zuko looks up at Chen's face, expecting resentment and fury. The closest thing he can label Chen's emotions as is...anguish.

"Lee, I can't imagine how much you've suffered. I am so sorry I pushed you earlier. Do you want to come inside? Eat something? Go to bed?"

Zuko had never been more grateful for anyone's patience before and has never been more furious for someone being this patient with him. He feels both ways and he can't figure out which he feels more, but anger is a more powerful emotion.

Hot, angry tears begin to roll down Zuko's cheeks before he takes a few steps forward, shoving Chen. Zuko is sure that the step backwards Chen takes is more out of surprise especially considering Zuko isn't using all of his strength.

"Why are you so fucking calm?!" He screams, shoving Chen again, the man doesn't move this time, but doesn't react either. "What do you get from this?! What do you want?! I'm disrespecting you! Do something!" He continues, leaning against Chen and shoving him with some of his weight as well as partial strength. Part of him is scared of really hurting Chen despite the man being built like an elephant ox.

Despite that, he is surprised at how heavy Chen must be if he can't even get the man to budge now. Not even a little.

"Hit me! Starve me! Lock me up! Just do something! Don't just fucking stand there! Fucking punish me!" He howls before beginning to punch Chen's stomach, mostly hurting his own fists on Chen's muscular build.

It is only at that where Chen moves, taking Zuko's wrists in his hands with only enough force to stop Zuko from punching him.

When he looks up, Zuko can see the first flash of irritation that he has *ever* seen on Chen's face. Zuko can't stop himself from pulling away and shrinking back, unsure what would happen now that he has managed to get under Chen's skin of all people. A man with an unlimited amount of patience for almost everyone and everything.

Instead of beginning to descend on Zuko, Chen takes a deep breath, closing his eyes before looking at Zuko.

"If you need some space, you can stay in the loft. The ladder is to your right."

Zuko's eyes flit over at a wooden ladder against the wall leading higher in the barn.

A lump begins to form in Zuko's throat. He's being banished to the barn. He won't be allowed back in the house anymore. If he's lucky, they might let him get his bag without checking what's inside of it. He'll have some food for when they decide to not feed him or forget to.

"It's dry, clean, and stays decently warm up there. I've stayed there when I'm worried about one of the animals. I'm gonna go get you a blanket. You're welcome back into the house when you're ready." Chen says softly before leaving.

Zuko picks up the chicken cat, walking towards the ladder as fresh tears begin to roll down his cheeks.

When he reaches the loft, he buries his face in the chicken cat's soft feathers, letting himself weep.

He isn't sure 'when he's ready' is supposed to mean. He doesn't know what he has to do to earn a place back in there. He doesn't understand why he couldn't just control himself. Everyone else seems to be able to. Why can't Zuko?

He isn't sure how much time has passed when the door opens and he hears someone walking up the ladder. Zuko closes his eyes, holding the warm animal a little closer, careful to not hurt it.

A warm blanket is draped over him wrapped around his shoulder before a kiss is pressed to his cheek.

Zuko cracks open his eyes, seeing Kani leaning over him, gently rubbing his arm.

"Chen told me what happened, love. It's alright. You're alright. I understand if you need some space. I brought you your dinner and some dried food for tomorrow. Chen got you some candy from the market. There's also a jug of water for you." She presses another kiss to Zuko's cheek.

"You're welcome to come home whenever you like, love. Take your time. Just whatever you do, please don't run. Please. Summer is ending. It's going to get cold. It's going to get dangerous. We aren't going to force you to do anything, but at least stay until spring." Kani pleads, kissing Zuko's forehead.

Zuko lets out a soft cry. He wants Kani to stay. He wants her to hold him, to pull him close, to keep him safe.

He wants to go back into the house, to make his way up to Kani and Chen's room and snuggle up between them, apologizing to Chen over and over again, begging for forgiveness.

Unfortunately, Kani's hand dissapears, making Zuko feel cold and alone.

When the door closes, he pulls the chicken cat close, burying his face back in it's soft feathers, and sobbing.

## Chapter 7

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

I know it's kinda short but some of my documents when on my phone have stopping giving me access to them saying i don't have permission to access them so I wanted to put this out before that happened. I also didn't want to leave everyone on too much of a bad note for too long

### Text

Zuko only gets about two hours of restless sleep, all divided into five non consecutive chunks filled with anxiety fueled nightmares.

He had ruined everything. Kani and Chen had done so much for him and Zuko had ruined it like everything else. He should have known this was inevitable. He was still stupid enough to think otherwise.

Ozai was right. Zuko ruins everything he touches, no matter how hard he tries. He can't help but to be a failure. He can't help but to scorn the world by his very existence.

Part of him almost wants to go back to the Fire Nation and let his father know that Zuko is alive. Let the man tear him apart until there is nothing left. Until Zuko can't keep doing stuff like *this*. He can at least then blame someone else for his shattered heart.

He had managed to get himself banished to the barn. He had pushed Kani and Chen's nearly unlimited patience and gotten himself thrown out. There was only so much of Zuko breaking down over nothing that they could take. He wishes that he could control it, he just *can't* .

Pain and fear always wells in his chest and rises in his throat until he can't breathe. Zuko would either have to drown or release it. This could start over something so little and he would manage to blow it out of proportion every single time. Every time. He can't think clearly enough to not do so when that happens.

*You should have just fucking drowned in your suffering and kept quiet. You shouldn't have let Chen* *take you in that night. You're only dragging out the inevitable. It will end the same. You'll die* *alone and in pain, you're just making it worse. Just lying to yourself that you could be anything but* *a failure. A disgrace.*

A loud sob escapes Zuko's lips and he covers his mouth as terror shoots through his body, praying no one had heard him. If he is weak enough to cry, he needs to at least be able to hide it. His father had been right about everything else, he's almost certainly right about this too. If Zuko couldn't learn in the palace, he could at least learn now.

A small meow comes from Zuko's side as he feels paws rest against his shoulder.

Opening his eyes and turning his head, he can see the chicken cat standing against him.

Zuko runs his fingers through the creature's soft feathers, sniffing. It leans its face towards Zuko, licking at the tears on Zuko's cheeks.

"Thanks for staying with me, little guy." Zuko whimpers, voice cracking as he speaks. The creature meows again, nuzzling him.

As soon as he talks, Zuko can hear his stomach rumble before tensing painfully in hunger. Kani had brought him dinner and dried meat and vegetables for breakfast.

Unfortunately, Zuko knows that the fresh food won't last long before it spoils and he has no idea when he'll next be given a meal like that again. Maybe if he does something particularly good and is granted a real meal. That likely won't happen too often.

Kani and Chen keep talking about winter and how it will be here soon. How food doesn't grow.

As of now, in the worst case scenario, Zuko could pick something from the garden in the dead of night no matter how much he hates the idea of stealing. He isn't even sure if he can get his bag from inside. He should have stored it in the barn. He was stupid enough to think he would have an ounce of control over a second banishment.

Zuko doesn't know when he can get more dried food. He can't dip into those stores now. He can't let fresh food go to waste.

With a lot of force, Zuko slowly sits up, wiping at his eyes as the creature crawls in Zuko's lap, purring.

He picks up a piece of meat, nibbling on it. It's good. Really good.

Tears begin spilling down his cheeks again as he remembers the time and care that he and Kani had put into making it. He remembers her humming quietly as they cooked. Gently instructing Zuko how to help her.

He picks up a piece of cabbage after finishing the meat before the little creature swats it out of his hand, eating it.

For a moment, it helps Zuko forget about what is going on. "You like cabbage, don't you little guy?" Zuko asks, scratching the creature behind the ear, sniffing.

"Can I call you Cabbage?" He asks, Cabbage clucks a little before walking back and sitting in Zuko's lap.

Zuko begins to slowly nibble on the food again. It would have been nice to eat it at the table and listen to Chen talk about town. Nice if he could have just held it together opposed to freaking out. Instead of getting violent with Chen. Fuck. he had forgotten about that.

He's pretty certain he hadn't actually hurt Chen, but Zuko attacked him in an uncontrolled outburst.

His breaths begin to pick up as his chest constricts. Chen is so calm and gentle, but Zuko may have pushed him over the edge. Violence is almost certainly his limit. The man will almost certainly retaliate with his own fists.

Terror begins taking over Zuko's body. If he had his bag or even just his swords, he would run. Maybe even without anything running would be his best option. His memories of the last month wouldn't be tainted by his own blood.

He clutches Cabbage to his chest, burying his face in the creature's soft, golden feathers. He wants to run to the door and bang on it until his fists are bloody, begging for forgiveness. He wants to run into the woods and never look back.

Staying here really might be worse. He could find something he deserves out there. Something horrible.

If it wouldn't make everything impossibly worse. Zuko would scream. He would keep screaming until he couldn't breathe. He wants to so badly. Scream until someone forces him to stop.

"Cabbage...should I go?" He whimpers, scratching the chicken cat's eat absentmindedly.

Cabbage is silent, curled up, half asleep, leaning into Zuko's touch. Cabbage might not know the answer, but Zuko knows that Kani and Chen will eventually really throw him out. Not just banish him to the barn, but throw him off the farm. Zuko is sure the grief would kill him in the most painful way possible.

He'll wait until morning. If things are worse in the morning, he'll run. He might even be able to get his bag that way. If he thinks he's going to be punished, he *will* run.

With that in mind, he falls into another fitful sleep.

Kani hadn't even tried to sleep. She couldn't even bring herself to pretend. Thankfully, Chen is on the same page.

Kani is more worried about Lee fleeing in the night than anything else. She worried that he'll just disappear into the woods. She can't stop herself from diligently watching the barn doors, praying the terrified firebender doesn't slip out of them. She really doesn't want to chase him, likely terrifying him impossibly more at the thought that she was coming to hurt him opposed to stopping him from getting himself killed with no allies or supplies and no idea where he is going. She certainly doesn't want to use her bending to trip or stop him. Unfortunately, letting him run would probably end in a far worse fate for the traumatized little boy.

Chen can't sleep because of what had happened with Lee. Apparently the look in the kid's eyes keeps haunting him. She can only imagine.

Apparently, Lee had essentially admitted that he was starved. *Intentionally* starved. That his father had deprived his child of food as some twisted form of punishment so often that it made a thirteen year old boy barely look like a starved nine year old. It makes her want to cry. She feels too empty to cry right now.

If food was regularly used as a punishment for Lee, he probably just got really weird and unhealthy habits around it. Most people would stuff themselves after being deprived of food. It seems like eating just became something very anxiety-inducing for Lee making it hard to eat ever even with food is available.

The fact that Lee really likes tea and noodles makes even more sense. Some teas can help with hunger or pain. Some can help calm nerves. He might have used it either when being starved to take his mind off food or to settle his stomach when he could eat. Likely also to calm him down a little.

She knows that ginger can help settle stomachs and chamomile can help with nerves, she hopes that jasmine does something considering that is the kind he wanted. Maybe serving dinner after drinking tea could help Lee a little bit.

Eating is probably one of the most stressful things that Lee has to do most days considering his history. She and Chen have been treating it like something relaxing in itself. She would be completely willing to start treating meals like preparing for something stressful if it could help Lee eat. She doesn't care if it is annoying. She would rather be a little irritated that she has to wait fifteen minutes longer to eat than to see her child be unable to at all with how scared he is.

After an extended period of eating and it getting more regular, she and Chen could slowly ease Lee into it being just something easy and regular. It would take time and effort, but it would be worth it for Lee to develop normal eating habits. He needs it.

The firebender probably likes noodles because it's a meal very easy on the stomach. Lots of broth with some noodles and a little bit of meat and vegetables.

Kani herself has suggested eating noodles or even just drinking bone broth when someone is feeling sick. It would probably be good for Lee to have something that reminds him of his uncle. Someone who had loved and cared for Lee when no one else had.

"Hey, darling, could you get some onions from the garden? I'm going to start making broth. I think we should have noodles for dinner."

The sun won't be up for hours, but it takes a few hours to make just the broth. It would be good for Lee to be able to start out his morning with a cup of broth opposed to jook. It might be easier on his stomach and help calm his nerves.

Chen doesn't say anything, he just stands and walks out of the house.

Kani takes the pot outside, filling it up in the spigot before coming back in and setting it on the stove.

She had forgotten how irritating it is to bring coals back to life. Lee had been making all of the fires for the last month. It had gotten so easy. She hopes that the sweet little boy wants to stay. Not just to start fires for her, he really needs a good, safe home where people won't punish him for being a firebender or for being unable to function properly after a lifetime of abuse.

By the time that Chen has come back in with onions he has cleaned in the spigot, Kani is adding bones from dinner and vegetable scraps to the pot of water.

All she has to do now is chop up the onions and let the broth boil...and then calm down a horribly traumatized child for which she has no idea how to help.

She needs to find a way to help him. The herbalist that Feya gets her supplies from may be crazy but has seen just about everything. She sort of lost it due to all of that, now with only her cat to keep her regular company.

It might take awhile to get straight answers out of that woman, but she might be able to offer some advice as to what to do for Lee. Kani doubts that she'll care that Lee is from the Fire Nation or a firebender. If she does, she won't say anything to anyone. Hopefully.

Unfortunately, Kani can't leave for town with Lee in this state. She could send a carrier pigeon to Feya and she could relay that message to the old woman.

Kani really doesn't have a better option. Lee *needs* help. He's traumatized to the point his mind and even body have become ill. She has no idea how to help the boy besides trying to be gentle with him. Unfortunately, that doesn't seem to be working all that well anymore.

"Do you think I should ask Feya about if there is someone who could help him?" Kani asks, looking at her husband. He looks just as lost as she feels. "I'm only hesitant because...what if it puts him in danger?" She continues.

It would make everything so much worse if people came to drive out the firebender fugitive staying in the Earth Kingdom. She has no idea what Lee would do to himself.

Chen just shrugs, looking down. He hadn't really spoken since his fight with Lee. It isn't too surprising.

"Who would willingly starve their own son?" Chen finally whispers, looking out at the barn. "What kind of person could ever do something like that to *anyone* . A child at that. He was so scared, Kani. I've never seen anyone look that scared...ever."

Kani looks up from her broth, resting a hand on her husband's shoulder, giving him a sympathetic look. "All we can do now is try and help him recover. We'll start by doing our best in the morning. Hopefully he's had time to eat and calm down and he can talk to us some."

Chen just nods once, not saying anything. Kani doesn't feel all that optimistic either.

As soon as the sun rises, Zuko climbs out of the barn, kneeling in the grass a few feet from the front door of the house. He'll be ready for whatever they want him to do. He needs to show initiative.

Things might be tolerable if he proves that he's still willing and ready to work. Even if he's still banished to the barn, he might at least be allowed to stay. His punishment for attacking Chen might not be as bad. He might be allowed to get his pack. Even without the food, it has his sleeping bag, two changes of clothes, money, and his swords.

If he cooperates now, things might be okay he might survive this.

Zuko isn't sure how long he stays kneeling at the door when he hears it open. Instead of looking up, he touches his head to the ground, trying to prove how sorry he is. Begging for mercy. Trembling violently in fear.

"Sweetheart, what are you doing?" He hears Kani's gentle voice before she touches his back with a comforting hand.

"Waiting for when you need me." He whispers, sitting up on his knees a little but not raising his gaze to meet hers.

A kiss is placed gently on Zuko's forehead, arms holding him in a close, loving embrace. He wants to cry.

"Come inside, love. I made some broth. I'm going to make noodles tonight. If you don't want to talk about last night, you don't have to. I don't want you to work today, I want you to rest. One of us will be with you all day. I want you to try and eat, though. You can take your time. Do you want to come inside?" She offers.

He's being given a choice. He has no idea if he is supposed to come in and eat and it's fully allowed. He doubts it. It's more likely that he is supposed to know that he is no longer allowed in the house. That he should stay out here on his knees until he is instructed to do something else.

Zuko doesn't understand why Kani is trying to play with him like this. It isn't funny and he doesn't understand. He could work with her telling him what she wants him to do. He just wants her to tell him that he isn't allowed in the house anymore. He could live with that. He doesn't understand why she wants to painfully twist his punishment by giving him false hope.

"I-I'll stay here, ma'am. I do whatever you want when you need me to. I'll do whatever you say. I'll be good, I promise." He swears, needing things to become clear. He needs to understand.

Kani doesn't respond for a long moment. Fear begins to fill his mind, terrified that he had done something wrong. Scared he was actually supposed to come inside. So that he could face the consequences of his actions behind closed doors where the neighbors wouldn't see. Where they might nor hear him scream.

"Okay, love." Kani finally whispers, sounding sad above anything else. Zuko knows enough to be sure that his voice isn't wanted. He keeps his head down and mouth shut as Kani stands and walks away.

Zuko expects to be left here for the better part of an hour as Kani and Chen eat. However, in less than five minutes two sets of footsteps come towards him. Zuko can't stop himself from flinching.

"Hey, sweetheart, will you drink this? It's jasmine tea." Kani sits in front of him, holding out a cup. Chen is sitting to her right.

Zuko slowly reaches out, clutching it in his hands, praying that it isn't a trick.

As he sips the tea, he can only think of his uncle. How Iroh would make this tea for him and they would sit together, talking some. How he would be kind to Zuko no matter what happened.

Zuko wants to see Iroh again so badly that it hurts. He can't stop a few silent tears slipping down his cheeks as he drinks the tea.

"Lee, are you all right?" Chen asks softly. "Neither of us are angry. Not in the least. We're worried about you. Very worried. You can tell us what's wrong if you want, but we won't do anything you don't want us to."

Zuko meets the man's eyes. He looks exhausted. He looks like he's been crying.

Looking back down, Zuko swallows, unsure what to say. "I miss my uncle." He finally whimpers. He doesn't know what he would give to have his uncle here for even ten minutes.

He wants to apologize and beg for forgiveness for leaving Iroh behind with no warning. He wants the old man to know that Zuko is alive and that he hasn't lost a second son. He wants his uncle to hold him, rub his back, press kisses to his face, and brush his tears away.

He misses Iroh so much. So painfully much.

"Love, you could send a carrier pigeon to him if you would like. You could let him know that you're alive. Reconnect with him that way even if you don't see him." Kani suggests, slowly offering her hand to Zuko.

He ignores her hand, unsure what he is supposed to do. Unsure what is expected of him. After several long seconds, she retracts it.

He wants Iroh to know he's alive. He wants his uncle to come for him, for then to live in the Earth Kingdom together. He could be safe and loved while understanding the motive.

Zuko eventually shakes his head. "M-my father might find out I'm alive." He chokes. Zuko wouldn't be surprised if his father could intercept mail. He *is* the Fire Lord. He's the man of Zuko's nightmares.

"If he finds out I'm alive, h-he might come for me. I-I rebelled and didn't die nor comply with his wishes after banishment. H-he'll hurt me. He'll hurt me so bad. I'm so scared of him. He won't stop hurting me." He admits, trying to calm himself with another sip of tea.

The look Kani gives him is pained. "Lee, I can promise you, I will *never* let that man even look at you again. You don't have to write to your uncle, but I promise you, we will protect you from that monster. I don't know what we can do to make you feel safe here, but we'll try. We'll protect you." She swears.

Zuko puts his empty cup down on the ground, brushing at his face. "W-will you tell me what the consequences for last night are?" He whimpers, needing to know what's going to happen to him. "I-If I'm banished to the barn, can I at least get my bag? Please?" He begs, digging his nails into his arm.

"What do you mean by banished to the barn?" Chen asks, Zuko isn't sure if the man looks more confused or sad.

Zuko feels the same way. "I-Isn't it where I need to stay now? A-am I allowed back in the house?" He hates that there is hope in his voice, he'll almost certainly be struck for thinking he would be allowed back there. That he could ever be wanted by anyone.

Instead of yelling, Kani just looks shocked and Chen starts...crying. Openly without trying to hide any of it. Something Zuko's own father would never *dream* of doing. Something he would strike Zuko or Azula for doing where they could be seen. If they had to cry, they were to hide from the world. Showing emotion as someone grown and accustomed to the world was something only uncle did. Or so he thought.

"Sweetheart, this is your home. You're always allowed inside. Whenever you want. You won't be punished for last night. No one got hurt and you were just scared. Whatever happened wasn't malicious. You've almost certainly already suffered the most from what happened. Come inside, love." Kani pleads.

"Promise I'm not in trouble?" He squeaks, hugging himself. "I understand if I need to be punished...just...don't like being lied to. Happened so much back home."

Azula would always manipulate him, usually just for fun. She would manage to raise Zuko's anxiety to unbearably high levels. It would make it so much harder for him to complete any task their father gave them. She managed to make his life so much worse.

The lie he still can't get out of his head is when she said their father was going to kill him. Was going to kill Zuko for Ozai to keep his titles after trying to take Iroh's position after Azulon.

Zuko knows that Azula always lies...but it was the night mom left and their grandfather died. It all seems too much like a coincidence.

On top of that, Ozai had even told Zuko that he wanted to kill Zuko when he was born, that he didn't have that spark in his eye. Ozai had thought Zuko was a nonbender and wanted to kill him just for that. He had begun reminding Zuko of that once Azula began to excel at firebending despite being younger.

He still tries to remind himself that Azula always lies despite the fact that he knows that his father doesn't love him. That he doesn't even want Zuko alive.

Zuko isn't in denial about his father not loving him, the issue is with his mother. Anxiety keeps telling Zuko that his mom left because of him. However, if Ozai really was going to kill him, she would have definitely left because of Zuko. No matter the reason, she really would have left because of him.

"I promise we're not lying to you. Just please come inside, drink some broth, lay down. We're so worried about you." Kani offers her hand again.

Zuko slowly begins to reach towards her hand when he remembers that *he's* lying to Kani and Chen. They don't even know what his real name is. A lot of what he's said is true, but he keeps lying to them over and over again.

Taking his hand back, he wraps his hands back around his stomach, whimpering. "I-I'm lying to you." He squeaks out.

Part of him almost wants one of the farmers to strike him and cast him out. It would force him to leave, to move on. It would force him to accept that he doesn't belong anywhere. It might be able to help him find somewhere he could manage to keep his head above water.

Chen brushes away his own tears before slowly reaching a hand towards Zuko, stopping before his fingers reach Zuko's face.

"Lee, you're a terrible liar." Chen whispers after a moment of silence, sending a jolt of fear through Zuko's chest.

"We know that you're lying about and hiding a lot of details in your life and we don't care. Kani and I have already talked about that. We both trust that you're genuinely scared and need help. We trust that you can't go back to the Fire Nation. We trust that you're telling the truth about the things that matter. If you don't want to tell us the truth, you don't have to." He says softly, reaching his hand towards Zuko again.

Zuko leans forward, moving his face against Chen's hand. "Thank you." He whimpers, leaning into Chen's touch. "Thank you."

It takes nearly an hour to coax Lee inside the house. Under most circumstances, they wouldn't let animals in the house, but Lee had grown attached to the chicken cat that he had named...Cabbage.

Chen isn't about to tell Lee that it is a stupid name, but it is. Granted, it is a stupid looking creature. The important thing is that Cabbage seems to calm Lee down. That's all that matters. If Lee is happy, Chen is happy.

He nor Kani have dared to bring up knowing that the kid had been starved. Lee reacted so horribly last night when his eating habits were brought up. He needs to feel safe again before they ask him about anything else.

Right now, Lee is lying nearly motionless by the fire, likely from not sleeping last night.

Chen is exhausted. He had taken care of the animals and started tending to the gardens a little while Kani got Lee inside. Now Kani is finishing necessary garden work for today. It should be completely done in two hours. They can leave everything that doesn't *need* to be done right now for tomorrow.

Today, Lee needs them. He can't be left alone completely after thinking he had been banished. He needs so much help. So much love.

Cabbage is laying on Lee's stomach, curled up, clucking softly as she drifts off. Lee's chest rises slowly and evenly as if in sleep but eyes open, staring dead ahead.

Chen runs the tips of his fingers through Lee's inky hair. It's getting greasy. Chen knows that hair is important to the Fire Nation but is sure Lee hasn't washed his hair besides with just water in the spigot.

He is fairly certain that Lee is nervous to properly bathe and resorts to hiding in the small room downstairs without closing the door fully and wiping himself down with a wet cloth. It's likely a vulnerability thing. He hopes that's all it is and not something someone had specifically done to him.

"I love you son. I'm sorry we haven't been able to help you more." Chen whispers, looking at the tiny firebender. He can't imagine what would have happened if someone else had found Lee. If no one had found Lee, Chen is certain the kid wouldn't have made it until morning.

Lee makes eye contact with him, taking Chen's free hand, holding it in both his own before looking back at the ceiling.

"Lee, I want you to know you're safe here. You're safe." He promises, meaning it. "Your father is a horrible man and we will never let anyone even think about treating you like that again."

Lee opens his mouth before closing it again and exhaling slowly but heavily. "Zuko." He finally whispers, taking one hand from Chen's and resting it on Cabbage.

Chen cocks his head, a little confused for a moment.

"It's my name… *was* my name. I think I like Lee more. Even if I don't, I wanna go by that." He mumbles, eyes fluttering closed.

The name sounds familiar to Chen, but he can't place it. That isn't what's important. What's important is that Lee just put a lot of trust in Chen.

"Thank you for trusting me, son." He replies, leaning down, pressing a kiss to his forehead. "I love you. You're so kind and good despite everything you've been through. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise."

Zuko whines sometimes that sounds something like 'love you too'. He's half asleep, the chicken cat sleeping soundly as well. Chen can't stop himself from smiling at the sight.

His boy is going to be fine. He's going to be okay.

## Chapter 8

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

I am just getting back with my crew and was able to finish this. I figured i wouldn't be abble t ok post tomorrow (im going to go to moticello w a friend bc hey we're in VA). Sorry jts kinda short

### Text

Zuko doesn't understand any of what is going on. He had screamed at and hit Chen in a fit of rage. He had screamed and cried over nothing. He had lied to them. He had stolen food to avoid punishment, although he isn't sure if Kani and Chen know about the jerky.

Maybe if they find out, they'll finally have had enough and throw him out. Finally throw him out for good and not be burdened with him anymore.

Despite that, neither Kani nor Chen had even yelled at him. Not even insulted him. They certainly didn't even try to hurt him. He doesn't understand.

They had stayed up all night making broth, coaxing him into the house and into sipping on it throughout the day.

Zuko has been drifting in and out of fitful sleep. He would wake up to find Cabbage in a different position every time. Usually it would also switch if it were Kani or Chen sitting with him.

They would usually be quietly reading a book, knitting, petting Cabbage, or napping next to Zuko, a hand holding his own. He doesn't have to worry about being alone.

When he wakes up, one of them usually tries to coax him into drinking some tea and broth, never pushing it too hard.

Kani has claimed that she is making soup but wants Zuko to make sure he's getting enough to eat if he doesn't feel up for solid foods throughout the day.

None of it makes sense. He doesn't understand any of it. The longer he waits, the more he begins to believe he won't actually be punished.

The next time Zuko wakes up, Chen is half asleep next to Zuko, holding his hand as Cabbage is curled up against Zuko's side, enjoying the heat he gives off. Kani is in the kitchen, humming to herself, stirring the pot of noodles. It's the first time he has seen both of them since this morning.

Zuko gently picks up Cabbage, moving her to his other side as she clucks slightly with annoyance. Zuko ignores her, moving closer to Chen, snuggling up against the man before pulling Cabbage close again.

He can feel a gentle hand in his hair and Chem mumbling something he can't quite make out. Zuko can't stop a small whimper in response, snuggling closer into the man's chest, needing the proximity. Despite everything that had happened, Chen feels safe.

Zuko had lied about his name and identity and Chen hadn't cared. When he came clean about his name, Chen had only thanked him for his trust, not yelled at him for lying in the first place. Chen had cried at Zuko's pain, not trying to hide it. He had proved over and over again that not only is he not dangerous, but he's kind. Chen will treat him in a way only uncle and mom ever had before.

"Lee, love, are you up?" Kani asks, coming into his field of vision.

Zuko meets her green eyes, nodding once, looking back down at Cabbage, touching her nose gently. Cabbage meows in response, butting her head up under Zuko's chin. He can't help but to smile.

"Would you like to eat some soup? It's done now. It's good. Cabbage can have some to if she likes." Kani offers, sitting down.

Zuko shrugs, genuinely unsure. He doesn't understand why they've been so diligent and gentle with getting him to eat so much.

It isn't like it was with father when he forced Zuko to eat until he got sick. It's so gentle and caring. It isn't about control like it was with Ozai.

"Kani...ma'am, my are you being so kind to me? Both of you? I just...I just don't understand. I want to. Want to be better. I'm sorry." He mumbles, unsure what to say exactly. Unsure what he is apologizing for exactly except for...everything.

Kani sighs, looking down. "Lee, I want to talk to you about something we've noticed. If it makes you uncomfortable or upset, *please* tell me. I'll stop talking about it. We never have to bring it up again if you don't want to. You won't upset me or anyone else if you tell me to stop. Do you understand?" She asks, raising her head to meet Zuko's eyes.

Zuko nods once, a little confused but he feels like she is being genuine. At least not getting angry with him. Hopefully.

"Lee, sweetheart, when we first found you, you were very skinny and still are. I know we've brought up eating habits a little but it's worrying. I got more worried when you told me you were thirteen. You barely look ten, chronic hunger and malnutrition can stunt your growth and it looks like it has." She begins to explain.

Zuko nods once, wrapping his arms around Cabbage, having a sinking feeling that he knows where this is going. He doesn't want to talk about what hs father did to him. How scared and hungry he would be all the time. How he would get so hungry he would be in burning agony. That he could barely see straight.

He feels a hand on his back as Kani tries to comfort him. It only works a little.

"You asked Chen if he was going to starve you when you got angry. If you don't want to talk about it, we don't have to. Ever, if you don't want to. Or you can talk to someone else that isn't us at some point. You don't have to make any choices now." Her voice is steady but moments away from cracking and her breaking down in tears.

"What your father put you through was cruel and inhumane. No one, especially a child, should ever have to go through something like that. We can't offer you much, but I can promise you that Chen and I will never willingly deprive you of something you need. We will never hurt you. We won't let anyone else hurt you, either. Food in the winter gets very repetitive and not as good, but you won't go hungry. We would certainly never starve you. I swear to you, my love."

Zuko can now hear the tears in her voice. He turns around, seeing some rolling down her cheeks.

He carefully moves away from Chen, wrapping his arms around Kani's waist, the jerky in his pack weighing heavily on his mind.

"I'll have some soup." He finally mumbles against her chest, not making any more to pull away.

Kani's fingers run through Zuko's hair with so much care he wants to break down again.

"Lee, if you want me to stop talking about this I will, just tell me. I won't be upset. I didn't think that food had been used as a punishment against you and I'm sure meals are stressful for you." Zuko nods once, not saying anything at that observation.

He's never sure if he's really allowed to eat, what or how he is supposed to, what the rules are, and if what he is being given will be the last for a long time. Maybe ever. He doesn't know how to explain that now.

"If there is something you need regularly or one day, tell us. If you need to drink tea or meditate before you eat to calm yourself down, you can. If you need us to not talk to you or to encourage you, just ask. If you need to be alone, just tell us. It's going to take a while for you to feel comfortable eating regularly again, but please tell us what you need. Okay?"

Zuko lets out a quiet whimper, clutching Kani's robes tighter in his fists, unsure how to thank her.

"Will you come eat some soup, sweetheart? Anything else you need?" She asks as Zuko slowly pulls away, looking up at her face, shaking his head.

Kani leads him to the table, helping him sit down before serving him a bowl of fresh noodles. He can't stop a small smile from forming as he thinks of his warm, kind, loving uncle.

"Can you stay with me?" He asks as her hand begins to leave his shoulder. "I like it when you're touching me." He admits, needing Kani with him right now.

"Of course, my love." Kani responds, sitting next to him, wrapping arms around him. Zuko feels so safe, loved, and wanted. He wants to fall asleep in the safety of Kani's arms and stay there forever.

Zuko takes a small bite of the noodles. They're good. Really good. Maybe some of the best he's ever had.

Zuko isn't sure if they're so good because he's hungry and stressed but is being reassured about everything. It could be because Kani made them and everything she makes is amazing. They could also just be good.

He doesn't really care. It's easy to eat and good. "I love you." He mumbles unintentionally after a few bites, snuggling closer to Kani.

"I love you, too. This is your home now. We're your family now, Lee." Kani whispers, pressing a kiss to Zuko's head.

Zuko just smiles a little, wiping his eyes and taking another bite.

It takes about half an hour for Zuko to slowly eat his fill of noodles. He feels warm and sleepy, resting his head on Kani's shoulder again, having trouble keeping his eyes open.

"Tired, love?" Kani asks distantly. Zuko can only nod.

"Lee, you seem to be doing a little better now, but I'm still worried. Chen and I had talked earlier, and we don't want you to be alone tonight. Would it be okay if I woke him up and for you to come upstairs and sleep with us?" She asks, cupping Zuko's cheek in her hand.

Zuko isn't sure how he feels about that but is too tired to really consider it. He just nods once, not moving from Kani's arms.

He isn't sure what he's supposed to do, but then Kani slowly stands, lifting Zuko with her.

He always forgets how strong Kani is with how gentle and precise every touch of her's is. How she never uses her strength for show or harm.

Zuko rests his head against her shoulder, feeling so safe despite everything that had happened the last two days.

Kani stops walking almost too soon. He's about to try and force his eyes open when Kani starts talking.

"Hey, Chen, you up?" She asks right before Zuko hears a quiet groan.

"I'm taking Lee upstairs. Can you put the noodles away before coming up. He ate already." She explains.

"Yeah, of course." He replies as Zuko can hear him standing up, too exhausted to open his eyes or even turn his head. He barely has the stregnth to grip Kani's clothes.

"Thank you, son. I was so worried about you." Chen whispers, resting a hand on Zuko's shoulder before pressing a kiss to the side of his head.

Not long after, Kani begins walking again. Zuko can feel him being carried up a flight of stairs before finally being layed down. He can feel Kani's arms still wrapped around him, holding him close.

He was unsure about sleeping with Kani and Chen tonight at first, but now he isn't sure if he has ever felt more safe akd comfortable in his life.

He feels himself growing impossiblly more exaughsted as Kani runs her fingers through his hair, soothing him in such a loving manner.

It isn't long before Zuko can hear footsteps as Chen lays on the other side of Zuko, resting his hand on Zuko's sholder.

"I'm sorry I upset you earlier. I love you, son." Chen mumbles. "Please let us know what you need. We'll do what we can to help you. This is your home now." He promises.

Zuko only has enough energy to smile a little before falling asleep while wrapped in kind, loving arms.

The fear and dread of what could happen is still weighing painfully on his chest, but he feels hopful for the first time in so long. Genuinely hopful. Like he might genuinely be able to be safe and happy. Like he might be okay.

Azula has been getting stronger. A lot stronger.

Iroh isn't sure if it is because she is just coming more into her power as she grows and matures or if it is influenced.

He doesn't doubt that it's because she is learning as she goes, gettng stronger and more confident in her abilities. Getting more control over her bending and her mind.

It also seems to be like Ozai has been spending far more time with her or wanting her to train with others. He puts more energy into her alone than he had into her and Zuko combined.

When Iroh's sweet, sensitive nephew was alive.

When Azula had someone to compete against. When she was safe.

Iroh has always knows that his brother is cruel and twisted. When he had forced Zuko to fight him in an Agi Kai, Iroh had expected Ozai to hurt and humiliate Zuko, not kill him.

Iroh had expected that Zuko would talk away with bad burns on his chest and arms. Expected him to publically humiliate Zuko for speaking out and use it as an example. He expected Zuko's trust and hope to be shattered. His little spark of indiduanity and defiance extinguished.

However, Iroh had thought that Zuko would still be here in the palace where he could be safe. Whatever happened, it would just be a reminder for Zuko to keep his mouth shut and head down. Zuko's fate was so much worse.

Ozai had pushed Azula particularly hard today. Directly after training, she had bathed while Iroh made sure to get her something to eat and drink. He had rarely seen her trembling from exaughstion while walking. Never allowed Iroh, or anyone for that matter, offer an arm for support as she walked to keep herself upright.

Now she's laying on her bed, propped up with pillows, sipping on eucalyptus tea and picking at a mix of kimodo chicken, rice, and vegetables.

Iroh sits on the edge of her bed, watching her silently, unsure what to say to his neice. He wants to talk to her, but he can't think if a single thing that he could say.

Thankfully, it's Azula who finally breaks the silence, but Iroh hates what she has to say more than he could ever express. Mostly because it holds too much validity and honesty. Far too much.

"Uncle, do you think I'm safe?" She glances at him before popping some rice in her mouth. "Be honest, after what father did to Zu Zu...do you think I might be next?"

Azula has always been good at hiding her emotions and intentions. She has been a skilled liar her entire life. Part of it is just how she was born. More horribly, she understood from a very young age that showing emotions in front of her father wasn't safe. Manipulation, physical strength, and callosed behavior would protect her far more than any relationship she could ever form.

Despite that, he can tell that it isn't just a question. Azula is scared of what might happen to her if she doesn't maintain Ozai's nearly impossible expectations.

After Ozai had killed her brother with so little care and so much malice, it would strike terror into anyone's heart. They both know that that was the point. It was meant to show that Ozai woukd never tolerate anyone, not even an heir, his own child, if they weren't ready to meet the demands of war. To kill and harm with only power in mind.

She, too, had expected to see Zuko injured, not murdered. After the reality of it had found it's way to her soul, when she could no longer keep up the facade that she didn't care about her brother's fate, she had taken comfort in her uncle. Iroh is sure she came around when Iroh began to mourn Zuko's death. That she realized that her father murdered his own 13 year old son for speaking out. Azula hadn't needed to worry for her saftey for a long time. Most of her father's abuse and crulty had been directed at Ursa and Zuko and then just Zuko.

Azula had excelled at firebending and fighting far past Zuko. Her performance was always used against Zuko. Not only is she a prodigy but she used to be better in clear compassion to someone. She was safe.

That buffer is gone now. She's being pushed harder than she ever has been before over and over again. She has kept on task so far, but it's only a matter of time before she fails at something. Before she begins taking Zuko's place. Ozai always seems to feel the need to assert his power over someone. Outside of servants and gaurds, Azula is all thats left. When it comes to Iroh, his brother mostly ignores the fact that he even exists.

Iroh sighs, taking Azula's hand. "Azula...I don't know what to say. I won't lie to you, but I really don't know what's going to happen."

It's the truth. Ozai could have a second forced marriage, no matter how inconvenient, if Azula dissapointed him. Iroh isn't sure if he would actually do it, but he may use it as a threat. Iroh isn't sure if that will happen.

"If you start having genuine and immediate concern, tell me, we can run. I'll go with you if you really think you're next at any point. I love you, Princess Azula, and I won't lose a third child." He whispers, cupping her cheek.

"Just know if things begin to get too bad, you have a way out. You can get out. I won't let thay man put you through the same thing as he did to your brother. I promise."

Azula just nods once, taking a sip of her tea.

Several minutes pass before ahe says anything again. "Thank you, uncle Iroh. Thank you."
