## Chapter 9

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

I start my last hitch tomorrow and then I go back home to NC. I'll see my mom for a hit and then am moving into my appt, so, exciting.  
I added some things in here ppl have been wanting for a bit, also, when I get home I'll try and draw a basic layout of Kani and Chen's house (like shitty blueprints bc I can't draw) i had tried to draw Cabbage, but I can't draw:( he baby. Just yell at me for shitty blueprints if I forget, I should be getting home on evening of the 27th

### Text

Zuko had disobeyed just about every rule Kani and Chen had given him. He had even screamed at them and hit Chen. He had lied to them and hidden stuff from them. He still isn't sure if he should come clean about the jerky or sneak it back to storage when they aren't looking.

He ends up keeping it in his bag, unable to shake the fear of being starved even as the likelihood of that declines dramatically.

Despite that, every day he gets a little less nervous about the other shoe dropping. About them punishing him once he finally settles.

It gets easier to breathe, to sleep, even to eat a little more. It's still difficult, but it's getting easier.

True to their word, the farmers have listened to what Zuko needs without question. They didn't get upset when Zuko needed to eat away from them, when he needed to be touched while he ate, when he needed to drink tea or meditate before eating, or when he could barely get anything down.

No matter what, they were never be angry. The three of them would clean up from the meal and Zuko would receive several affectionate touches and words reassuring him of his place in his new home.

With regular meals, fear of pain and punishment slowly dissipating, and residual non-chronic symptoms of his burn healing, he feels so much better. It's easier to think clearly without going into a wild panic over nothing. When he does panic, which is still pretty often, it's so much easier to calm down. So much easier to breathe.

Today, Kani and Chen are letting Zuko off a little early. Zuko had promised Fao that he would teach his new friend how to use dao blades. That Zuko would show the other boy his real blades and let him hold them.

Zuko had warned Fao that he doesn't know if he'll still be as good. If he'll even be able to still use his swords. Zuko is sure that he'll need to relearn some after going so long without practicing. He'll definitely need to relearn now that his left field of vision isn't nearly as wide or clear.

Zuko had noticed that his balance had been a little off, and Kani had done her best to test Zuko's hearing. Zuko had tried not to cry when she told him his hearing in his left ear was damaged pretty significantly and isn't sure how no one had noticed yet. Zuko attributed it to them being too preoccupied with his fragile mental state.

Kani had told Zuko that hearing is a big part of balance and he'll need to relearn more precise movements. Something that makes up such a large portion of sword fighting. She said he could do it and still be skilled, but it would take time.

As soon as he was alone, Zuko found Cabbage, sobbing into her soft feathers. He still doesn't understand why his father hates him so much that he would cripple his own son and leave then him for dead with no time to heal. Do it all just to make a point.

He doesn't understand.

Even if Zuko did return to the Fire Nation with Avatar in hand, learning to fight around his injury, his father would find a way to make it a weakness. He would find ways to humiliate Zuko during training. Train opponents in finding Zuko's blind spot and taking him down.

Even if it took 100 times for training opponents to figure out exactly how to use Zuko's new disability against him, that many chances to use it against him never being probable in the real world, Ozai would use that against him. If Zuko failed at a *single* thing due to needing to relearn fighting patterns around new scanning and balance methods, Zuko would be a failure within himself.

He can already see Ozai banishing him once again on the grounds that his firstborn, the heir to the throne, is a cripple. That he wouldn't take anything besides perfection. That it's the standard Fire Nation nobility, especially royalty, needs to live up to. Even if that isn't true to many nobles and officials. Ozai would just want a reason to hurt and humiliate his son.

Zuko knows it would have nothing to actually do with being partially blind and deaf. It would be an excuse. If something like this had happened to Azula, Ozai would follow the narrative of of his daughter being so strong and resilient that she could be one of the most skilled soldiers without her entire visual and auditory advantaged intact. Zuko knows that his father just hates him and wants him *gone* . He doesn't care why or how, Ozai just never wants to see Zuko again.

There are plenty of high ranking officials in the military and in politics with missing limbs, eyes, or in need of some form of mobile aid. Zuko knows that as far as most people are concerned, if they can do the job, it's theirs.

It wouldn't matter if Zuko were physically perfect. He would be nothing but a failure in the eyes of his father. Nothing but a disgrace. An inconvenience that needs to be dealt with.

Despite the fact that Zuko has Kani and Chen now, people who love him and care for him no matter what, something his own father would never dream of, it shatters his heart. All he wanted is for his father to love him. Fuck it, give half a shit about him and be decent to him. The kindest thing that man ever did for Zuko was comforting him after he had Zuko locked away and starved for days. After Zuko had lost his mind and injured himself into unconsciousness. He still doesn't know if it was manipulation or the only sliver of Ozai's humanity coming through as he comforted his injured, terrified child.

All of it makes Zuko want to scream and cry until he passes out. It makes him want to go back to the Fire Nation and scream at his father that in the first five minutes he knew Chen, the man showed Zuko more kindness than Ozai had in Zuko's entire life.

Chen had *known* Zuko was the enemy, and was a scared, unpredictable, unknown firebender kid. Despite that, he had held Zuko in his arms and taken him into his home with his only request being for Zuko to stop firebending at him.

Even that little interaction was more than he had ever gotten from his own father. That this month has been filled with more love than Zuko thought possible for a lifetime. Even from his mother or uncle. One who abandoned him, and one who Zuko had abandoned before he could be left behind all over again.

He tries to clear his mind of that as he reaches the fort. Not surprisingly, he finds Fao there first, bouncing on the balls of his feet, excitement filling the air.

"Lee!" His friend cries out, grinning wildly, eyes shining in excitement. Zuko can't help but smile at someone so excited for his presence. Something so rare back home. Even when they did want to see him, they were never this thrilled.

Zuko waves to his friend as Fao rushes over, embracing him. Zuko hugs him back, exhaling slowly.

"Are you feeling better?" Fao asks, cocking his head when he pulls away. "Your mom said you were sick and couldn't play." He explains before Zuko can ask. It makes him feel better that Fao had wanted to see him and Kani hadn't revealed that Zuko had been dealing with an emotional breakdown. On top of that, however Kani has talked about him, Fao thinks of her as Zuko's mother.

Zuko nods. "Kani and Chen took care of me. Helped me a lot. Feeling better." It isn't a lie. They had done so much for him. They have been healing him with so much love and care. He would do anything to never have to leave them.

He still doesn't want to think about what could have happened if someone besides Chen had found him. Anyone else. He is sure he would have been locked up despite being half dead. Left to die in a cell cold, terrified, alone, and in agony.

Fao's nearly black eyes almost shine as he looks at Zuko. "Can you teach me how to use swords?" Unable to maintain an ounce of his excitement.

Zuko smiles, nodding once. "I think I said before Kani checked and my vision isn't as good anymore. Also my balance. I might need to relearn a little." He admits quietly, looking down.

"I'm sure you're still amazing!" Fao exclaims, still grinning.

Zuko gives him another small smile. He takes two of the wooden swords from Fao, getting into position, trying to keep himself steady. He's able to with a little extra focus. He can do this. He can learn to do this with practice. After he gets better at balance again, he can learn new ways to scan his field. He doesn't like the shadowy, fuzzy parts of his vision.

"We're going to start with footwork. It's a little boring but it makes fighting far easier." He explains, getting out of position and helping Fao get in proper stance before going back to his.

"It's a balance of being able to stand your ground and move quickly. Too defensive and you'll only ever run, maybe not even effectively protecting yourself. Too defensive and you can get stuck in a situation which could end badly." He explains, showing Fao how to move in a way that allows his swords to remain in the same position without obscuring his target field of vision. Or more of it, in Zuko's case.

He needs to practice on his footing as well. This is the basics. He's having trouble keeping his posture proper and unmoving outside of choice.

Zuko won't be able to teach well if he himself can't properly go through more than the basic stances. He definitely will no longer be able to hold his own in real battle anymore without retraining himself. Hopefully it will be good for him. Hopefully, it will teach him to work around his new disability. He'll be able to learn how to fully function again.

Maybe Chen can help him practice. He really wants to learn to trust the man. Zuko knows full well that Chen is kind, gentle, and would only hurt someone to protect himself or someone he loves. Zuko just needs to learn that on an instinctual level.

He wants to be able to throw himself into Chen's large arms without hesitation and feel safe and protected when pressed against his chest.

He knows that Kani might be able to help, but he already feels so safe with her. Feels like he could have gone completely blind from his injury and felt safe as long as he could feel her hands on his back or shoulders. As long as she was touching him.

As they move, Fao starts to get impatient, wanting to swing the sword. Zuko gives in, showing him a few basic blocks as Zuko makes simple swings towards the younger boy.

They end up stopping when Fao gets a little too confident and charges towards Zuko. More out of instinct, Zuko swipes at the other boy pretty hard.

Thankfully, the swords are wooden and all it does is leave a bruise. It doesn't make Zuko feel any less guilty for hurting his friend.

Zuko drops his sword, running over and embracing Fao, apologizing profusely.

Most of him feels guilty. A little is scared that Gela will have it out for him for hurting her son, even if by accident.

Fao tried to tell Zuko he's fine even as tears shimmer in his eyes. Zuko pulls out one of his real swords, letting Fao look at it, instructing him to be careful of the blade.

The two boys sit side by side for a long time. Zuko has gotten a lot better at making the lizard snake with fire and he really wants to show his friend what he can do...but he can't. It might mean losing his family. Losing the best thing that had ever happened to him.

Instead, Zuko awkwardly wraps his arms around Fao, hoping to bring him some comfort.

"Lee, are you feeling alright?" Fao asks, black eyes meeting Zuko's gold.

Zuko cocks his head, confused. "Yeah, um I guess?" The response sounding like a question.

"You're really warm." He comments, resting a hand on Zuko's cheek.

Zuko nods once, trying to force panic down. "I run warm." He whispers, looking down, knowing that he heats up a lot when trying to focus on the movement of his body. Stoking his inner flame helps bring himself more strength and energy. It also makes him run very warm, far more than any non firebender would.

"There's a lot about me and my past I haven't been fully honest about. Well, I have with Kani and Chen, but I mostly want to forget about who I was." He admits.

It's one of the most honest things he's said while here outside of telling Kani and Chen about what had happened to him.

Lying has never been one of Zuko's strong suits. He's bad at lying and he doesn't like it.

He had grown up around liars. His father and his sister had done nothing but lie and manipulate Zuko from a very young age. He doesn't like people lying to him about anything. After so much manipulation to the point Zuko would have trouble distinguishing between reality and fantasy. Zuko *hates* lying.

This past month, a lot of what he has said is for self preservation, not manipulation. He's the Fire Prince from the Fire Nation who is a firebender. Despite that, he doesn't mean anyone any harm. He isn't trying to build trust only to break it. He just wants to be safe. He just wants to be loved.

Even so, he tries to lie as little as possible. He has been coming clean to Kani and Chen about a few more things. A lot of what he wants to obscure he is honest and says he doesn't want to talk about it. He wants to be able to do something similar with his friends. He doesn't want to be a liar and a manipulator. He just wants to be loved. Wants to be safe.

"Is it because of that?" Fao's voice is quieter now. He puts down Zuko's sword before pointing at Zuko's scar.

Before Zuko can stop himself, he nods once, tears welling up in his eyes. His father had been so horrible for nothing. Had left a permanent scar on his child's face because he *spoke* .

"Lee?" Fao's voice is distant as he wraps his arms around Zuko's waist. "I'm sorry you've had a hard life. I'm sorry someone hurt you " He mumbles softly.

Zuko smiles to himself, grateful his friend is accepting enough to allow Zuko to hide a lot of himself. To not need every answer.

"Thank you." Zuko mumbles, burying his face in Fao's shoulder.

After a few minutes, Zuko slowly pulls away, looking down. "Kani needs me back to start helping with dinner." Zuko whispers quietly. It's true, he does need to help, but he also just feels like he can't be around people all that much longer. He feels exhausted. He just wants to be able to work silently at home.

"Are you good at cooking?" Fao asks as the two boys stand, beginning to walk back towards the village.

Zuko shakes his head. "I don't really know anything about cooking outside of basic survival skills. Kani is teaching me how to cook good meals. Not just cooking a slab of meat on a fire so I don't go hungry." He explains, absentmindedly taking Fao's hand in his.

What he doesn't say is that it brings Zuko a little joy doing things he knows would infuriate his father. That Zuko was cooking not just for himself in terms of survival, but cooking for others. He wants Kani to teach him other basic skills like that. Such as enough sewing to fix a few rips in his own clothes or some healing. He wants to learn.

Fao nods, smiling a little. "Can we play tomorrow?" He asks hopefully as the houses come in sight.

Zuko nods once. "I think."

"At some point you should also meet the others if you wanna be play with them too."

Zuko knows that there are several more children in the village, but he hadn't met them, only seen them briefly. Zuko isn't sure he is able to handle meeting more people just yet. Maybe soon, but not yet.

"Yeah." He replies softly. "At some point. I'd like that."

When they get a little closer to the homes, Zuko reluctantly releases Fao's hand, pulling his friend into a hug.

There had been a few servants, especially the one gardener, who Zuko had somewhat befriended, but aside from his mother, most of the time Zuko had been lonely. Fao is Zuko's first friend.

The two boys pull away and Zuko hurries back to the farmhouse, an easy smile on his face as he runs, finally not feeling perpetually weighed down by the fear of failure, punishment, and abandonment. Finally feeling excited to see people who are taking care of him. People who wouldn't exploit that position.

Happiness is slowly making its way into Zuko's everyday vocabulary. He doesn't think there are words he could use to describe how grateful he is.

In just the last few days, Lee had gotten so much better. He's talking a little more and has even gone as far to set boundaries. He hasn't been assertive about it, but he's communicated what he needs.

Lee had been having a hard morning a few days ago. Chen had rested his hand on the firebender's shoulder but Lee had gently moved Chen's hand off of him. The kid flinched a little after, but relaxed quickly, not trying to apologize while cowering simply because he didn't want to be touched.

He has asked to not be talked to at two meals, and eaten alone at one. Most other times he would just meditate for a little before eating and then drink tea with his meal to calm himself.

It's good to see the kid beginning to communicate what he needs and wants without fear being driven onto his heart.

At one point, Chen had even been sitting on the porch, watching the sun go down and Lee and snuggled up against him. Chen hadn't been able to stop smiling at the sweet little boy finally seeking comfort from him.

Lee had even allowed Chen to gently rub his back as he gripped onto Chen's clothes with thin, crooked fingers.

Considering the kid has been eating a little more at meals and more regularly, he hopes he'll start gaining a little weight soon. He needs it, especially when it starts getting cold.

Chen hadn't told Kani about Lee's real name. If Zuko wants to share that with Kani, he will when he's ready. On top of that, he had made it clear he wants to be called Lee.

Zuko isn't a common name, but Chen has heard it before. It wasn't in passing such as someone's name in the colonies, he is sure that Zuko was once someone important. Maybe he still is.

Chen doesn't want to press Lee about who he once was, he knows the kid wants to forget. What happened to him was absolutely traumatizing even if he hadn't been abused every day of his entire life. He can't make Lee relive his past like that just to satisfy Chen's curiosity.

He also can't exactly go asking for answers around the village, maybe if he's in town, but not here.

If Chen started asking questions like that, people might start drawing connections to the young boy who neither Kani nor Chen had ever mentioned before now staying at their house. A boy whose past has been obscured with a vague story filled with trauma to dissuade them from pushing for answers. A boy who has the golden eyes of a firebender. A boy who is too hot to the touch when healthy, with pale skin and jet black hair. One who had never seen snow.

Kani had told Chen that Gela had figured out that Lee was a firebender very quickly and didn't care. Chen is relieved that she'll accept Lee as any bender as long as he is safe to be around.

Unfortunately, many others won't have the same view. They'll just see a firebender, not a little boy who had the misfortune of being born one.

Gela is particularly perceptive. She could easily be the smartest person in the village, but he isn't surrounded by idiots. Others might pick up that Lee is just a lost firebender kid Kani and Chen know nearly nothing about.

He can't risk Lee's safety for some answers. Anyways, Lee might tell him who Zuko is eventually. When he earns enough of the boy's trust. He can't break that now.

Chen is bringing in some of the ripe vegetables when he sees Lee running towards the house.

He is about to drop the basket of vegetables and run over to his boy when he sees that Lee is grinning. He lets out a breath of relief when he sees that. Worry that something may have terrified Lee dissipating.

Lee hurries up to him, throwing his arms around Chen's waist before he can even say anything, smiling at Lee's new found affection for him.

He had always seen Lee snuggling up against Kani almost constantly. He has been careful to give Lee the space that he needs to recover and settle in his new home. He didn't want to intrude on space Lee had desperately needed and likely never been given.

Unfortunately, that meant up until recently, Chen had to stay outside most of the day and then not spend much time with Kani until bed. However, he made some friends with some critters and reassured himself that Lee was getting what he needed with Chen away from him. Chen isn't about to put unnecessary stress on a traumatized child because he isn't willing to accommodate.

Thankfully, Lee seems to be doing better around him now. It will hopefully make things easier for everyone.

Chen rests his basket down, wrapping an arm around Lee's shoulders and one hand on the back of the kid's head, fringers carding through his thick, soft, inky hair.

"Did you have fun, Lee?" He asks, pressing a kiss to Zuko's head. The kid has really been blossoming the last several days. After he calmed down from thinking Chen had thrown him out, he really started making some improvements psychologically.

Lee nods. "I taught him some sword fighting basics," Lee says quietly.

Chen smiles. He had seen Lee's broadswords, but never knew much about them other than Lee had been professionally trained for battle. Something that doesn't sit well with him, sure that Lee had started by the time he could hold them. Too young to be thinking about war. Too young to be caught in the middle of it.

"Did that go well?" Chen asks, pulling away from the embrace, resting a hand on Lee's shoulder and picking up his basket.

Lee looks down, almost ashamed.

Chen feels his heart sink, worried this one little thing might send Lee back down a dark hole. "What happened?" Chen asks, resting a finger on Lee's chin, coaxing Lee to look up.

Lee moves his head, looking down again. "Balance isn't that good anymore. Hard to see. Makes it difficult. Feel weak and stupid. I said I would train him and It was hard for me to not shift to the side."

Chen can see frustrated tears welling up in Lee's eyes before the kid starts swiping at his face.

Chen kneels down, taking both of Lee's shoulders, making eye contact with the kid. "It's going to be okay, son. I know Kani was telling you that hearing plays a role in balance. Just one of those things you need to relearn for more acute movements like in sword fighting. Luckily your hearing isn't bad enough to mess up your balance too much just around the farm. Either that or you're adjusting." He whispers, kissing Lee's forehead, needing his sweet little boy to know how much he's loved.

"I-I was actually hoping you would be willing to help me." Lee offers, wiping at his eyes again, clearly offering Chen a chance to get closer to the kid. A chance when he's scared and needs help.

"Thank you, Lee." Chen whispers as he stands, knowing what Lee is offering him right now. "I'll do my best." He promises, smiling at his kid.

"Does Kani still need help finishing dinner?" Lee asks, taking Chen's free hand.

Chen shrugs, unsure. "Not sure, let's go see. We can help her if not, if so, let's get you something to eat."

Lee nods, following Chen into the house, a small smile forming back on his face.

Lee slowly sips at his jasmine tea in between taking bites of meat, vegetables, and noodles, occasionally sipping at the broth. He mostly stays quiet but glances up as Kani and Chen talk to each other.

Kani isn't sure if he's putting on any weight yet, it's only been a few days since his eating habits have improved. Hopefully, this continues. He needs it.

As dinner reaches an end, Kani is pleased to see that Lee has gotten through almost his entire bowl of noodles. He didn't just drink the broth and pick out a few solids like he may have before.

Before she can say anything, Chen speaks up. "Hey, Lee, I got you something from the market I thought you might like. I was going to give it to you when I got back, but I got distracted." He explains, not elaborating on Lee's complete mental breakdown.

Lee looks up, an excited look on his face as Chen puts a book and a mask down on the table, sliding a piece of candy across the table as well.

Lee pops the candy in his mouth, smiling and picking up the book. "My mom used to read this to me. We'd always go and see it. Ember island players would always butcher it, but it's my favorite." He says, grinning at Chen, putting the book down and throwing his arms around the man.

What Lee doesn't say is that it was likely one of the few times he was allowed to just be with his mother doing something he liked. Where his father wouldn't harass and ridicule him over nothing. It was likely one of his few memories where Lee got to do something he enjoyed with someone he loved.

Chen kisses Lee's head, rubbing his back as the kid thanks him over and over again.

When Lee finally pulls away, he slowly reaches out, touching the mask Chen had gotten. "My mom's fiance had this mask. She told me about him. Never told me his name. She took the mask." He says quietly, the look in his eyes haunting.

By the look in Chen's eyes, he's just as worried at how Lee is going to react as Kani is, if not more. He looks like he's wishing he never got it.

Instead of breaking down, he picks it up, pulling it to his chest. Kani can see a tear rolling down his cheek, but he isn't breaking down. Thankfully, he's in control.

"I really would have liked to meet him...I don't know if I still can. I like to think she found him again when she left. Even if…" he trails off, wiping at his face.

Lee had talked about not being good enough for his mother before. That she had left because Lee wasn't worth staying in an abusive marriage for. That she left her child alone with a man she knew would hurt him. She left him to be tormented and traumatized.

Kani has so many questions she wants to ask her boy, but she can't. Not yet. If she pushes him, he might break down. He's been having a good day so far.

He's been better at managing his emotions, but he still isn't good. He will either completely clam up and express nothing or express every little thing he is feeling with no control. It's very likely a result of never learning to manage his emotions from such horrible abuse. He had to learn to simply shut them down.

The old woman in town might be able to offer some advice. Kani has sent a letter to Feya, but hasn't heard back yet. Hopefully Lee will be willing to visit Feya with Kani and then be willing to see the herbalist. She isn't sure. All she knows is Lee needs some better help.

"It's alright, love." Kani whispers, wrapping an arm around his shoulders. "Do you wanna talk about your mom? You can if you want, but you don't have to. You can tell us about your life whenever you like. You don't need to keep it locked up." She prompts, not wanting Lee to be near bursting to tell her about his mom but feels unable to just as much as she doesn't want him to feel obligated to.

Lee traces the outline of the mask, looking ahead silently for a little before talking. "She wasn't supposed to tell me anything about her previous life, but she told me a little." He starts, leaning against Kani.

"Her mom was an herbalist. My mom loved growing flowers in the garden to remind her of home. I used to sit with her. I tried to tend to them when she left, but my father made me watch as he burned them." He whimpers, brushing at his face, a small cry escaping his lips. trembling for a few moments

"I-I want my mom!" He finally sobs, burying his face in Kani's shoulder, still gripping the mask. "I-I don't know why she left without me. I-I want my mom."

Kani wraps her arms around Lee, pulling him close, rocking him gently. She wishes one of them could have known Lee might have very emotional attachments to theater. Might still be grieving over his loss of who connected him to it.

"It's okay, love, it's okay. I'm so sorry about what happened to you. Let it out, it's okay, it's okay, it's good for you. Just cry, love. You can be upset." She reassures him.

Chen moves closer, resting a hand on Lee's back, tears rolling down his cheeks. "I'm sorry, son. I'm so sorry. If I knew it would upset you like this I would have never gotten than for you. I'm so sorry." Chen rests his head on Lee's back as he speaks.

" 's okay." Lee chokes, raising his head a little. "I-I just miss her...got worse after. Want my mom." He cries, trying, not very effectively, to calm himself down while also trying to express himself.

He really needs to learn how to control his emotions better. It's going to make recovery harder if he only knows how to clam up (or try to at least) or break down when things get real.

"Lee, love, you don't need to stop yourself from being upset. Even if she had a good reason, she left you with your abuser with no one to protect you. You're just a child. You're just a little boy, Lee. You're allowed to scream and cry because your only protector left you to fend for yourself." She reassures him, patting his back.

"Can I sleep with you again?" Lee finally whimpers in response, breathes beginning to slow down a little. It doesn't seem forced, seems like his breakdown is just coming to an end.

"Of course, love. Of course. I don't know all the details of your life, but we're never going to leave you, hurt you, let someone else hurt you, or deny you something you need. You're such a sweet kid and I'm sorry your father tried to crush you, but you're safe now. You're home." Kani brushes away some of Lee's tears with her knuckle, giving him a smile.

"Home." Lee repeats, clutching her hand in both of his as he sets down the mask Chen got him.

"You're our son, this is your home, and we're your family." Chen's voice is soft as he raises his head, soft brown eyes shimmering. "We'll take care of you as best we can."

Lee is quiet for a moment taking a deep, shaky breath. "You promise you won't starve me? Really promise? I-It hurts so bad. I can't go through that again. I-I don't want to, but I'll leave."

Kani isn't sure if the part about Lee running is an empty threat, but she can't imagine him being able to live with that after a month of being coaxed into eating and having a full stomach regularly, maybe for the first time ever.

Kani shakes her head, kissing Lee's forehead and face several times. "We'll never starve you, I promise. Like we said, winter food gets boring, but you won't go hungry. We'll always make sure you get something to eat, okay love?" She promises, unsure what is going through her sweet boy's mind.

Lee slowly stands, beckoning the couple over. Kani and Chen share a look but follow him over to the fireplace. He opens up his bag, removing old clothes from the top before setting down a small blanket and opening it.

She honestly expects him to have a picture of his mother or something from home, unsure how else it could pertain to the conversation. Instead, it is filled with dried meats, fruits, and vegetables. All things that they would have in storage. All things they had given Lee throughout the day to try and help him gain some weight.

"I-I'm sorry." He whimpers, kneeling near it, lowering his head. "I understand if you want to punish me, just don't starve me, please. I'm sorry I lied and stole I just...I-I couldn't go through it again. Couldn't take it anymore." Lee sobs, clutching his arms.

Kani feels her heart shatter as she falls to the ground next to her broken child. The boy who had been starved so severely and often enough that he had grown terrified of it happening again. So traumatized that the moment he had been given extra food he began preparing for starvation after terror had been so ingrained in his soul.

She can hear herself crying as she clutches Lee's skinny body to her's rocking him slightly, apologizing for letting him think for even a moment that he would go hungry here. That by choice they would let a child starve.

She can feel Chen on the other side of Lee, embracing him as well. Trying to help him feel safe.

"Thank you for telling us this." Kani finally chokes, kissing his head. "You're not in trouble, you're okay. You would never be punished for this."

She continues to cry, thinking about how her sweet child was trying to preserve and protect himself from more pain and terror. How he thought he would be harmed for avoiding twisted punishments that continue to affect his health and perception of the world.

How things such as this had been ingrained so deep in his soul he couldn't think of anything else but what had been done to him. How it became normal in his mind.

Kani cups his tear stained face in her hands, meeting his eyes. "Lee, my love, I am so, so proud of you for showing us this. I can't imagine how stressful it must have been for you." She praises, meeting his wide, scared, sad eyes.

"You're okay, love. You're okay. Why don't you come upstairs and get some rest?" She offers.

She wants to ask about his mother. About her having a fiance but marrying a man as horrible as Lee's father. About her not being allowed to talk about her past but risked her safety to tell her son about it. Wanted him to know about his mother. Yet still left him behind when it really mattered.

However, now is not the time for that. What Lee needs is to be given a calm environment where he can either continue to cry or calm down. Whatever he needs. He doesn't need to be forced to relive this over and over again to satisfy her own curiosity.

Instead of responding, Lee leans forward, wrapping his arms around her neck and butting his head under her chin. He doesn't speak, but he wants to go up.

Chen lets go of Lee as Kani lifts the too light firebender in her arms, holding him close.

It's going to get chilly tonight. The rest of dinner is still in a covered pot. It will be fine. Lee is far more important right now. He can't wait. He needs help right now.

She tries to not focus on the thoughts of Lee being a very difficult child as she carries him upstairs. He isn't doing any of this on purpose, he doesn't want to break down and panic pretty regularly. He doesn't want to have trouble eating and think there's a punishment at every corner.

He isn't rebellious or rude, he's just scared. He's a trauma victim who has never learned a lot of coping mechanisms. He was taught to stay silent and suffer when no one could see or hear him. She knows it's probably terrifying for him to break down in front of her and Chen. He's probably so scared he'll be harmed for having emotions. For being human.

Hopefully, winter can be dedicated to focusing on his well being. Sometimes the most productive thing they can do is stay inside and keep warm. Hopefully they can help him and learn more about his past. It might aid in learning how to help him recover.

Lee may be difficult, but he's suffering and needs help. He's in so much pain and is so scared at what might happen to him at what might happen again if he isn't careful.

Chen lays down on their bed first and Kani rests the trembling little boy in his arms. Lee grips Chen's robes like it's a lifeline as he cries and trembles.

Kani lays down on the other side of him, kissing the back of his head, praying he might recover from everything that has happened to him. That her sweet child will let them help him. That he might finally feel like this is his home even when not being reminded. He needs it.

## Chapter 10

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

At one point she mentioned that 8000 Confederates died in like one of the last actual battles and my friend leaned over and whispered 'That's rough buddy' one of the few times thay has been used in the same sentiment as the original. Also bc a super tiny battle that doesn't have a real name took place at what is now the Walmart, they call it the battle of Walmart

### Text

Zuko had started training with Chen somewhat regularly and it had helped a little. He doesn't flinch as much when he sees the man's hand coming towards him or suddenly sees Chen out of the corner of his eye. Zuko doesn't feel the need to be able to fully predict the man's movements as he comes towards him. He finally begins to be able to convince himself that Chen is simply approaching him. That the farmer's proximity doesn't mean pain, fear, or humiliation.

On top of that, Zuko doesn't pitch to the side as often when making delicate movements. Unfortunately, the moment Zuko's movements become more complicated, that changes. He begins to need to concentrate on his movements a lot more or even stumble and fall.

No matter how much Chen comforts him, tells Zuko that it's alright, that he's still recovering, Zuko has trouble holding back frustrated tears. Has trouble not feeling weak and pathetic. He can't stop feeling like a failure.

He needs to be able to do something he can be proud of. He needs to practice something. He needs his father to be wrong about him.

It's been months since he's done real firebending. Even if he is a pathetic firebender, he should practice. He at *least* wants to practice.

After finishing work, he had told Kani and Chen that he needed some space to clear his head and wasn't hungry, both true.

Chen had insisted that Zuko at least take an apple and some jerky with him in case he changed his mind. Zuko had readily accepted the offer.

Zuko is now walking through the forest with his blue spirit mask in a bag, slowly eating his apple.

He wants to find a clearing, ideally one lined with stone, but grass is fine. He just doesn't want to be surrounded by trees. Doesn't want to start a forest fire. He doesn't wang anyone or anything to get hurt just because he wants some practice.

He doesn't want to be a complete failure. If the day comes, he needs to protect his new family. He will. He was driven out of his first home due to weakness, he won't be driven out of a second. The loss of a second home would shatter his heart irreparably.

He walks at a swift pace for about twenty minutes before he sees a clearing a little ahead of him. Zuko pulls his mask on, obscuring his distinct face before walking out on the off chance someone might be looking.

"Hello?" He calls in an altered voice, checking the area. He gets no answer. He allows his hands to blaze, signifying himself as a firebender before calling out again in the same voice: "Is anyone here?" Again, he hears no response.

Zuko takes a deep breath before going through his most basic movements.

It takes a few tries to get it down, he can easily atteibute that to not practicing for so long and his poor balance. His footing quickly becomes more sure, his balance better, his flames hotter, and is just better focused. It becomes almost like an active meditation.

One of the few rules that Kani and Chen had laid out for him was no firebending. He isn't sure what they would do to him if they found out, but they don't understand, he needs this.

Firebending is different from earthbending. From what Zuko understands, earthbendimg is about connection. As long as an earthbender is on land, they have some connection to their element even if not actively earthbending. They can feel their element against their feet and traveling up their body. They can feel it as they shift ground with their hands such as Kani does with farmwork.

Even when on a ship, they can substitute with ceramic plates, rocks, and other trinkets that could easily be brought aboard. Could be interacted with so they could use their bending for either defense or connection.

An earthbender can be taken from their element, but they can't be severed like a firebender can. Zuko is pretty sure fire is the only element that can be truly severed in a matter of speaking. He isn't positive though. He doesn't know enough to do anything but speculate.

Iroh had talked about the importance of the inner flame. Meditation helps maintain it and keep it healthy, something Zuko hasn't been all that diligent about. He needs to start meditating in the morning and at night. He has been telling himself he would start doing tjay for awhile now. That day has yet to come.

One's inner flame can grow weak with neglect but can also be kept strong in the coldest and darkest of places if nurtured properly. However, it needs to be used. Over time, it will slowly grow weaker if locked inside, even if regularly tended to through meditation.

Zuko isn't sure if it is true that a firebender can actually be *severed* from their bending, but he doesn't want to find out. Iroh had said that a firebender needs to be kept deep underground for an extended period of time, away from Agni.

Severing from firebending like that isn't necessarily permanent, but one would apparently need to reestablish a connection with Agni. Zuko had no idea how someone would even do that. He has always felt the power of the sun inside of him, pulling him. If a firebender doesn't reconnect, they can't bend even if above ground surrounded by flame.

Zuko knows that even if it is possible for a firebender to lose their bending, he isn't in that situation. He is, however, in danger or weakening his inner flame, something he knows is real. Something he doesn't want to happen. On top of that, he has felt his bending being weakened from days locked in the dark underground. He doesn't know how long it might take to completely sever his connection.

All Zuko knows that if he is ever locked away like that indefinitely, he'll kill himself before that happens.

Something Zuko can say for sure is that real firebending feels good. It feels like he's releasing so much pent up anxiety. It feels like pressure is being released from his chest as he continues to go through more complex movements, phasing into moves that Iroh har taught him.

Part of him wants to take Kani up on the offer of sending Iroh a letter. Even all it would reveal is that he is alive, safe, and healthy in the Earth Kingdom, his father might find out.

If Ozai discovered that not only is Zuko alive but not suffering, he might send someone after him to change that.

On the other hand, Zuko wants his uncle to know he's alive so badly. He's sure that Iroh would feel responsible. Sure that Zuko's 'death' is weighing heavily on his heart if not breaking it.

At the very least, Zuko hopes that Iroh has now moved to Azula to help with his pain. It would give his mourning uncle someone to help and care for and it would give his little sister someone who is actually capable of loving her.

He really hopes Iroh and Azula have each other. Iroh needs her and Azula needs to know that Ozai isn't safe. That he'll hurt her. That he'll *kill* her and feel nothing but irritation at needing to dispose of a promising heir. He wouldn't even see it as murdering his own eleven year old daughter in cold blood. He wouldn't fucking care.

After well over an hour of practice, Zuko is drenched in sweat. He didn't mean to practice for so long, but he did. He needs to get home before Kani and Chen start to worry.

Zuko runs from the clearing, grabbing his bag, shoving the mask in as he walks and pulling out the jerky. He eats it while walking, appetite returning as he eats. He can't help but smile.

If this feeling lasts until the morning, he can't imagine how happy Kani and Chen would be with Zuko finishing his breakfast without difficulty. Without needing to take his time to calm down. He might even be able to eat something tonight as well if there is anything left.

He wants to make them proud even if he just did directly disobey them. But what they are worried about is someone seeing him. He had disguised his face and practiced far from the village as to not draw attention to himself. He also hadn't really shot fire up so it could be seen above the treetops. He was carful, it will be fine.

When he reaches home, Cabbage is sitting on the post of the fence, meowing as Zuko comes into sight.

Cabbage isn't allowed inside the house anymore. Kani and Chen had only allowed it for a few days because Zuko was having a full breakdown and was reacting well to the soft, affectionate creature. Cabbage had not taken kindly to that, she keeps trying to get back inside now. He can't help but find it amusing.

Zuko had tried to convince Kani and Chen to allow him to keep Cabbage inside, but they said no. He is *definitely* going to sneak her in when it gets too cold. He likes sleeping with her. He is sure all he'll get is a stern look that will quickly dissipate when he walks around with Cabbage purring on his shoulder.

He nuzzles her noes with her, touching the red rubbery, red crest on the top of her head and scratching behind her ears.

She clucks happily as Zuko rubs his finger under her chin. "I love you, Cabbage." He coos before walking towards the house and opening the door, walking into the house.

"There you are." Lee looks up, surprised that he hadn't jumped at Chen's voice. The two farmers are sitting by the fire, drinking tea, likely staying up to make sure he got home.

"Sorry, I didn't realize how late it got…is there anything from dinner left over?" He asks, still a little hungry even after an apple and two strips of jerky.

Concern turns to relief on Kani's face as she gives him a warm smile. "Yeah, love. It's on the counter. Please eat as much as you want."

Zuko walks over, filling a bowl with stew, walking back over to the table, heating it with his breaths as he walks.

When he begins to eat it, Kani and Chen's gaze are still on him. "What's wrong?" He asks, looking around. He had been here for nearly two months and they never really looked at him like this before. Never so intently.

They seem to want to ask what Zuko was doing and why he was gone for so long, but they don't. The only conclusion Zuko can draw is that they know questions bring anxiety and anxiety brings nausea. They've wanted him to eat more for awhile.

"I'm sorry I was gone for so long. If I'm allowed to do something like that again I'll keep better track of time." He promises, hoping let him. He really wants to practice again. Firebending without fear of his father's scorn felt good. Great, actually.

He wasn't doing his best to try and avoid some horrible punishment, he was doing his best just to do better. He liked that. The consequences of his actions were only that he didn't get as far as he wanted to, not a horrible punishment.

If anything, that freedom made him feel like he could try techniques that he wasn't sure if he could do probably. Most of them he couldn't, but all he would have to do is try again, not face being beaten later.

"Lee," Kani begins. Zuko looks up, hoping she isn't going to pry. Not yet at least. He doesn't think he can lie to them. One: being because he doesn't want to, and two: because he doubts they'll believe whatever he says.

"Chen and I have been talking for a few days. You're going to be staying here indefinitely, and we were thinking that you might start wanting some privacy and space of your own pretty soon. I know it's more of a spacious closet than anything, but we could move the stuff in there to the cellar." Kani offers, giving Zuko a small smile.

Zuko hangs his head, beginning to pick at the last few pieces of his food. He appreciates the offer, it means a lot, he isn't sure how to make it sound like he's as greatful as he is while declining.

"If you don't want me sleeping by the fire anymore, I understand." He says softly, pushing a chunk of potato around with his chopsticks. "I would be willing to stay in the loft in the barn if that's alright...I just don't like small spaces, I'm sorry." He looks down, feeling ashamed.

A hand rests on his shoulder and he looks up, meeting Chen's eyes. "What did that man do to you, Lee?" Chen asks, pain in his eyes as he moves his free hand, cupping Zuko's cheek.

"Would lock me up...days at a time I think. Was always dark and cold. Don't like the dark either. Too small." He whimpers, moving closer to Chen as he feels phantom walls closing in on him, breath picking up.

A hand rubs his back, warm arms wrap around him, he's being held against someone's chest and being rocked gently. "It's alright, son, it's alright. Your suffering is over, we wouldn't hurt you. You don't have to go anywhere you don't want to. We just thought that you might want a little bit of privacy. We don't want you to go anywhere." His low voice sends vibrations through his chest and Zuko repositions his head to feel them more, calming down a little.

"We could also take off the door and hang up a curtain so you don't feel trapped in there. We could also just hand up some curtains in the corner or the living room for you to stay in. You don't have to decide right now, love." Kani offers, kissing the side of Zuko's head.

Zuko exhales slowly, not even able to think about answering that right now. Now he just feels so tired.

"Okay, love, we can talk about it another time. It isn't urgent, we'd probably do it after harvest."

Zuko nods silently, nuzzling closer into Chen's chest. "Thank you." He mumbles. "Thank you."

Zuko has no idea how long he'll be able to practice firebending before Kani and Chen get wise. They already seem to be somewhat suspicious.

Thankfully, he's able to space his firebending out with seeing Fao. He sometimes even stays out a little later than his friend and practices for a bit, feeling like he is getting back to where he was.

Not only does it help with his firebending skills, but it helps with the new limitations of his body. It gets easier to scan his field, compensating for his blind spot. His balance begins to improve a little more as he gets more in tune with his body again. With Agni and his inner flame as well.

For the first time in his life, he begins to feel whole. He feels like he has command and autonomy over his body, feels loved and safe, and he starts feeling healthier both mentally and physically.

It gets easier to practice with Chen and it gets much easier to train Fao. Zuko had even started feeling confident enough to help Chen with blacksmithing, heating and cooling the metal in a way the man could never do himself.

There was an incident where he had dropped something hot, ending in Zuko panicking and Chen needing to take Zuko in to calm him down. Thankfully, something like that only happened once.

Zuko usually doesn't feel as scared when the heat of the fire presses against his face for extended periods of time. He trusts that Chen wouldn't shove his face into the coals and would pull him back if he began to fall. He is confident that he could command the fire away from himself effectively enough if he did fall.

Everything just seems better. Like it's going to continue to get better.

However, every day he continues to see Fao, Zuko feels himself bursting to tell the other boy about being a firebender. He finally has started beginning to like being a firebender after it had been used against him at home for so long. *Really* likes it and he doesn't want to hide it anymore. He doesn't want to keep lying to his friend. His first friend. His best friend.

As he teaches Fao how to move with his sword probably, Zuko wants to show Fao how he can move with fire. Wants to hold a flame in his hands and let Fao huddle by it when they are resting and he complains about the cold.

Every time it gets a little harder for Zuko to not show him. He really wants to share it with him, but he can't. If Kani and Chen found out that he is firebending in private, they might not be happy but likely understand. Kani is an earthbender, she would hate not being able to be herself ever. She would understand that as a firebender, Zuko needs to firebend.

However, if he were willingly revealing it to people, they would be furious. He would have been putting himself and them in danger. They might even throw him out.

He can't think about that. However, he *can* talk to them about it. He wants it to at least be a possibility. He wants to be an authentic version of himself even if by a different name and altered background. He wants to be the Zuko, or Lee, that matters.

Zuko walks into the house after coming home from training Fao, almost instinctively taking over cooking for Kani. It smells good. His stomach grumbles a little as he mixes the soup a little, adding softer greens into it that only need to cook as long.

"How was your day, love?" Kani asks, wrapping her arms around Zuko's waist, kissing the top of his head. "Did you have fun with Fao?"

Zuko nods, grinning, trying some of the soup. He knows it needs something but has no idea. Kani has been trying to teach him to spice dishes this way. She doesn't let him randomly throw them in, but she wants him to guess what he should add.

"It was really fun. Does it need salt?" He asks, doubting he's right.

"Not everything needs salt, love. I'm glad you had fun." She adds, running her fingers through his hair. "Would you like some soap to wash your hair with?" She offers, letting him go, resting a hand on his shoulder.

Zuko nods slowly. He knows his hair is pretty gross. It's close to his skull still, but he needs to actually wash it opposed to just using water. He hasn't felt comfortable taking a proper bath yet. He still feeling like a guest who could be thrown out at any time despite Kani and Chen giving him so many reasons to believe the opposite.

"Can I add some chili powder to it?" Zuko asks, missing the spicier flavors from home. He knows that Kani and Chen's tolerance for spice is much different than his own, but they do like some.

"Add a little, but be careful, it's very strong." She advises as Zuko puts two small, dried chilies in the mortar, beginning to grind them.

"How about you add some cumin?" Kani offers after a little silence, opening the jar of seeds. Zuko nods, allowing her to add a good amount into the mortar, continuing to crush them with a pestle.

"Kani...does anyone else know that I'm a firebender? Besides you, Chen, and Feya?" He asks, adding the spices to the stew, mixing it slowly.

Kani cocks her head, trying to meet Zuko's gaze. "Why? Did someone say something to you?" She asks, concern in her eyes.

Zuko shakes his head, looking down as he tastes the stew again, smiling absently at the taste. "No one said anything. Just curious."

"Gela knows." Kani admits after a few minutes of silence, sounding apologetic. "She guessed. She likes answers and I was worried that if I didn't tell her, she would investigate, possibly looping more people in. She doesn't care. I thought it would be best for it to come from her when you started to trust her a little more. Would be nice for you to know that you're loved and accepted just as you are. I'm sorry I didn't tell you sooner."

Zuko can't stop a grin from forming. Not only that Gela is fine with him being a firebender, but other people already know. It might be okay to tell Fao.

"Can I tell Fao?" He blurts out without thinking.

Zuko is surprised when Kani looks taken aback. "Absolutely not." She replies, looking at Zuko like he's crazy. "I know you don't like hiding who you are, but to a lot of people a firebender is a firebender whether they are a trained soldier or an injured kid. If he told someone...I don't want to think what could happen to you, love."

Zuko nods, looking down. "Yes, ma'am." He whispers.

He can hear Kani telling him that she loves him and wishes things were different but just wants him to be safe. Zuko nods as she talks, but just feels sad. Feels unworthy.

As they eat dinner, Zuko's previous hunger is replaced by nausea as he picks at his food. He's able to eat more than he could only a few weeks ago when feeling like this, but not nearly as much as he has begun to more recently.

He can hear Kani and Chen talking next to him, but for the first time in a while, he doesn't join in.

"Can I sleep in the loft tonight?" He eventually asks, voice quiet. "I wanna sleep with Cabbage." He needs the chicken cat snuggling up under his chin, purring against his chest.

Kani gives him a sad, almost guilty look. "You can bring her inside if you would like, love." She offers.

Zuko nods. He just wants Cabbage with him right now, he doesn't care where he sleeps.

He gets up and cleans his bowl, walking outside directly after and hurrying to the barn.

When he locates his feathered friend, she is beginning to settle down for the night. Zuko feels a little guilty picking her up as she clucks in irritation, but that dissipates as she rests her paws and chin on his shoulder, purring.

"I love you, Cabbage." He mumbles as he walks back inside, finding dinner being cleaned up from, Kani and Chen both giving him worried glances.

He can't bring himself to say anything to them. He knows that they just have his best interests at heart, but he can't help but feel like they are ashamed of him. Ashamed to have a firebender son even if they do genuinely care for him.

As they finish up, they both give Zuko multiple affectionate kisses, reminding him how loved he is before walking upstairs.

As soon as Zuko can't hear them moving anymore, he lays down with Cabbage, stokes up the fire, and cries into the chicken cat's soft feathers. For the first time in weeks, he can feel his heart near breaking.

The next day, Zuko mostly works silently on his own, pulling weeds and picking ripe vegetables. Closer to the end of the day, Zuko starts dinner, cooking vegetables over low heat. He isn't as good as Chen and certainly not as Kani at cooking, but he can make a few meals well that he has memorized. He knows what spices to add, still not fully understanding how Kani can just taste it and know.

"Lee, I know you're upset, but can we *please* just talk about this?" Chen asks, speaking before Zuko had even heard him coming.

It shouldn't be surprising that Kani had discussed Zuko wanting to tell Fao about being a firebender with her husband, but it is. Zuko isn't sure what to say, so he doesn't say anything, just continues stirring the pot.

"Son, can you at least look at me? We can talk about this, maybe come to some kind of compromise." The man offers, a sad tone in his voice.

Zuko wants to ask about how there could possibly be a compromise. He could either tell Fao or not. He wants to know if Chen is talking about waiting longer until Fao trusts Zuko more or maybe just revealing that he's a nonbender from the Fire Nation. However, Zuko regrets what he says as he is saying it. "Are you ashamed to have a firebender kid living with you?" He growls, tears burning in his eyes.

He isn't sure if he is angry, humiliated, jealous (unsure what or who he would be jealous *of* ), ashamed, or something else. He just feels bad and upset. He also has no ides for who or what these emotions are directed. They're just *there.*

He wants to go home. He wants his mom and his uncle. He wants a chance to get to know his sister and even one more chance for his father to love him. He wants to go back and feel the warmth of the Fire Nation, go down to the ocean, eat the spicy foods, and hold the turtle ducks.

He also wants to stay here in the Earth Kingdom with Kani and Chen forever. He wants to send a letter to his uncle, not only telling him that Zuko is alive but begging him to come. Begging him to come, pull Zuko to his chest and never let go. For the two of them to just live in the Earth Kingdom together in this area. He wants to introduce him to Kani and Chen and just be happy. Maybe even Azula could come too. It might be good for her to get away from father. Might give her a chance to be kinder. Give her a chance to be loved.

"Lee, son, no." Chen whispers, moving the pot off of the heat, pulling Zuko to his chest.

Zuko pulls out of his arms, shaking his head, brushing at his tears. "You want to hide the parts you're ashamed of." He whimpers, walking past him towards the door as Kani walks in.

"Lee, what's going on?" She asks, resting her hand on his chest, stopping him from walking out, looking worried.

"I know you guys don't want to deal with having a firebender kid. I can't *not* be a firebender just because you want me to." He whispers, wiping at his face again.

Kani cups Zuko's face in her hand, kneeling down, looking heartbroken. He feels simultaneously more angry and guilty.

"No, love. You're our child and we love you. We're just worried about your safety. We don't even want you firebending, certainly not telling people about it. It's not about us not wanting you ti be a firebender, it's about us not wanting you ti be taken and hurt."

Zuko feels anger flare in his chest for a moment. "I've been firebending in the woods for the last few weeks. It's been making it easier to eat and sleep. It's who I am whether you like it or not."

Kani doesn't even look angry, she looks scared. "Lee, what were you *thinking* ? What if someone saw you? They might have hurt you, th-"

Zuko pulls out of her grip, shaking his head. "That's all you care about? It's *helping* me. All you would talk about is how I needed to eat and sleep and whatever. Only if I do it *your* way it's okay? Any other way and you'd like me to suffer?" He spits. Part of him knows that isn't necessarily true, that he's letting his emotions get the better of him, but he doesn't care. He just feels so angry, stupid, and unwanted.

Before Kani or Chen can say anything else, Zuko runs from the house, sprinting towards the forest, half blinded by tears. His new name is being called behind him. He couldn't care less. All he can do is stay on his feet and run.

"Lee!" Kani screams louder as she reaches the edge of the forest, the little firebender having disappeared from her sight a while ago. She had never realized how *fast* Lee is.

"Lee!" She screams again, beginning to step into the forest when Chen grabs her arm.

"He'll be back. He left his bag, he'd need it. Anyways, he gets emotional easily. We'll stay up and wait for him to come home, make sure he knows that he isn't in trouble and that we just wanna talk. He'll come home." He assures her.

"We just need to make sure he can't just grab his bag and leave for good. We need to make sure he knows this is his home. That he won't be hurt for having a different and difficult life."

Sighing, Kani wraps her arms around her husband. "I didn't know it was upsetting him this much. I didn't know he felt like we were ashamed of him." She whispers, guilt and anguish welling in her chest as she thinks about what has been going through Lee's head.

She had thought that he wanted to show Fao something he thought was cool that the other boy had likely never seen before. At least not up close while not in danger. Worse case, she thought that Lee just wasn't good with keeping up with lies. He's a horrible liar.

She didn't even think that it could be because he felt unwanted and trapped when being forced to say he's a nonbender Earth Kingdom boy. Lee never talks much about his home or his culture outside of mentioning his mom and uncle. She had no way of knowing he felt isolated from his culture and trapped in the Earth Kingdom.

She had no idea that her little boy was suffering and in pain.

"If he isn't back in an hour we tell Gela what happened. If he isn't back in two, we go look for him." She says softly, walking back towards the house with Chen.

He nods solemnly. "I'm going to get Cabbage. Lee might want him when he geta home. I don't want him sleeping in the barn tonight. Don't want him to be alone."

Kani gives her husband a small smile, kissing his cheek. "We'll have our boy back. He'll be okay." She says more to herself than to Chen.

Chen squeezes her hand soflty before running towards the barn. Kani walks back inside to make herself some tea, praying Lee would come back soon.

Zuko runs. He isn't sure where he is going, why he is running, or why he can't seem to have any control over his emotions.

He can barely see, barely feel the branches slicing into his skin, the cold tearing through his clothes as night begins to fall and the warmth of the sun begins to dissipate. As the warmer months continue to give way the slowly encroaching winter.

He has no idea how long he's been running. He just knows that his sides and lungs are burning, his entire body is screaming in pain, and it's almost completely dark.

Despite that, he can't stop. If he stops, he'll have to think. If he thinks, he'll panic. All he'll be able to think about is when he gets home, he'll find the door locked and his bag packed and on the pourch. A signal that Kani and Chen are done trying so fucking hard for nothing. Trying so hard just tor more problems.

As he continues, he feels the ground give way. Before he can even react, white hot pain shoots through his left leg. After that, all he can do is scream.

### End Notes

## Chapter 11

Lee even though we all went down in that murder basement because we heard a spooky sound after multiple people had told us the house we were camping outside of was most definitely haunted by at least one confederate soldier. We also kept hiding in said basement (like in spooky little rooms in it (yes, this basement was like textbook murder basement)) to jump out and scare each other.

I have since said goodbye to my crew. It was a lot of fun and I had a great time.
