You can get a lot of certifications for free that parks systems want, such as I got my S2-12 (A level wild and fire chainsaw certification) through Americorps and they paid for it when I was on a chainsaw crew one summer. Check that guy out, they are really cool and are great for leadership improvement and my boss literally used it to do less drugs becasue he has to be sober for 9 days at a time. So, vibes.

### Text

Zuko can’t stop himself from continuing to cry loudly despite trying to calm himself down. He can’t manage to do so successfully even a little. Pain just keeps shooting through his awkwardly positioned foot so intensely his vision blurs a little, almost feeling nauseous.

He isn’t entirely sure what happened, but he knows that he fell. When he did, his foot must have gotten caught in between the root and the rock; it is still painfully wedged in a bent position.

At least the test of him isn’t isn’t a horribly awkward position. Zuko is able to move so that his foot is only about six inches above the ground.

He manages to get his leg to feel a little *less* painful, however, it’s still excruciating.

Zuko sits up and leans forward, trying to gently get his foot unwedged from it’s position and he can’t stop a new scream from escaping his lips as white hot pain courses through his body.

He tries again and loses all pride, breaking down sobbing all over again.

“Help!” He screams, fully aware he sounds weak, pathetic, and that anyone could find him. That even if he did get out, he doesn’t have anywhere to go now.

Maybe Kani and Chen would be kind enough to let Zuko stay a few more nights. Even just in the barn to let the pain subside a little. Maybe Kani would consent to splint Zuko’s leg so that it could heal properly. Maybe they would give him his bags. If he’s *really* lucky, they might even let him spend the winter in the barn and let him eat what scraps are left over. He is sure they know that if thrown out now, he’ll die in a matter of days.

He is fully aware that he has almost certainly burned that bridge because of getting too emotional. Due to missing a culture, county, and people that had turned their back on him months ago. A home that has been lost to him and Zuko is nothing but a distant memory to at this point.

The stupidest part of him, the part that Zuko can never seem to silence, kept screaming out for home despite receiving the best treatment of his life here in the Earth Kingdom. Despite two kind, patient, loving people taking him in as their own for longer than most people would even consider putting up with him for.

Zuko has now lost everything because he let himself get too comfortable. Because he managed to somehow remember only the good parts of the Fire Nation. The parts that he misses.

Maybe his father was right about never giving Zuko any freedom or showing any compassion. If Zuko had too many choices and felt safe, he would find a way to ruin it all. He would get too confident in himself and destroy everything.

Ozai may be the man of Zuko’s nightmares. He may be the worst man and father to walk the face of the earth, but he isn’t stupid. He knew how to keep Zuko in his place. Knew that he had to control his son because Zuko is incapable of controlling himself in any environment. When given freedom, Zuko will break everything he touches. When shown kindness, he’ll lose every ounce of control.

The simple thought of that shatters his heart.

“Please! Someone! Anyone! Help me!” He screams again, trembling in pain.

He lays down on the cold ground, not sure if his trembling is more from pain and shock or if it is from the cold. Both are definitely factors.

What he is sure of is that he needs to get out of here. That he needs to get somewhere safe. If he is stuck here, he has no idea for how long he’ll last. He isn’t sure if he will even be able to survive if he gets out.

Zuko takes a deep breath and punches his fist upward, shooting a plume of fire high into the sky, praying that it can be seen above the treetops.

When Chen had brought Zuko into his home on the first night, he said that he thought Zuko’s flame was a signal fire for help. Maybe someone will recognize it as one now.

He knows how risky it is for someone to see it. If they get here and realize that Zuko is a firebender, they might just kill him on the spot. They might arrest him. If they do, Zuko won’t fight, he isn’t sure if he can. He’s too exhausted and in too much pain.

If he’s good, they might have someone splint his leg and let Zuko rest even if they leave him in a cell. If they let him heal and feed him, he’ll be so good for them. He won’t fight, won’t try and escape, and will tell them everything that he knows even if his information on the Fire Nation is very limited and possibly outdated.

All he knows is that he can’t stay here. He had good luck with who found him when he was injured and desperate the first time. He might have a shred of luck now. He’ll be grateful if he is taken to soldiers who lock him up but take care of him to some degree and don’t beat him.

Hopefully he’ll get that lucky again.

Kani and Chen both thought that Zuko was younger than thirteen. Closer to ten or eleven. He might be able to use that to his advantage. They might be above beating a child that young even if he is Fire Nation.

His burn is in the shape of a handprint. Even though he is a firebender, he has proof that the Fire Nation has hurt him, too. That as far as they are concerned, Zuko is an enemy.

Now, he has an injured leg. He might be able to take advantage of being an injured child in some ways. He might get sympathy for a little bit in favor of better treatment even if a prisoner.

During that time he can prove he’ll cooperate. That he’ll let guards do what they want to him no matter how degrading and he’ll tell them what he can. He fucked up his chance of a good life. Maybe he can settle for a tolerable one.

He shoots fire out of his fist again before collapsing on his back, crying out in pain from the strain he put on his leg. “Please help me! I’ll do anything you want! Help!” He screams again before his words quickly devolve into miserable sobs.

Zuko wants Chen to come find him again like he did the first night. He needs the man to gently help Zuko get his food out from between the root and rock and then cradle Zuko in his arms.

Zuko wants to go back home to Kani and Chen’s house. He wants to apologize and beg for forgiveness as Kani bandages his leg. He won’t ever bring up the Fire Nation or want to be a firebender ever again. He won’t ask them to share that information with anyone. He’ll be their dirty little secret.

Even if they are ashamed to have him as their kid, to have a firebender living with them, they’ve been kind to him. If the price for affection and love is tamping down Zuko and completely adopting his new identity as Lee, he’ll pay it. He won’t suffer as much that way. Maybe one day he can even forget that he is suffering from hiding who he once was. Maybe one day, the existence of Zuko won’t even matter anymore. He can be dead.

He begins grabbing at any stick, dry leaf, pinecone, and any other flammable object he can reach in his limited range. He is grateful that he is at least in a forest, so those items are relatively abundant. Unfortunately, when one only has a small area to collect those things from, it runs out quickly.

A little tinder pile forms in a matter of minutes before Zuko lights in quickly with his fingers, grateful to be a firebender.

Right now, he does wish that he had listened to his uncle’s lesson more. Iroh had told Zuko that he could keep himself warm even in the Water Tribes with only his breath if he practiced and concentrated. Zuko can do it a little, but never practiced much. If anything, he had used that trick to cool himself down in the Fire Nation heat. He has never found a need to use it to warm himself up.

If he gets out of this, he’ll try. He’ll practice. He’ll become the man that uncle Iroh had wanted Zuko to be even if Iroh couldn't be there to witness it.

Zuko has no idea what he would give for Iroh to come and kneel next to him, lifting Zuko into his arms and cradling him. For Iroh to bring him somewhere safe, heal him, make him tea, and run his fingers through Zuko’s short hair, telling him stories in a gentle voice.

Zuko would be willing to give up the rest of his life if he could just have a few hours of that. He wants his uncle so badly it hurts.

Zuko curls up close to his quickly dying fire as best he can in his current position, crying.

Zuko isn’t sure how long he lays there like that. He would believe someone if they told him twenty minutes or two hours. He had no way of telling time. Every minute seemed to drag on indefinitely and then every moment of it dissipated as the next one started. The only constant between them is growing cold and pain.

He can hear voices coming closer to him. He can’t make out what they’re saying, but it is at least two people talking.

“Hello?” He calls, sitting up a little, whimpering louder in pain. “Is anyone there? Please help me. *Please* .” He begs, peering into the dark.

Almost a full minute passes until he can see a light in the distance. He blinks a few times as it comes closer.

Finally three people come into view of the pool of light given off by Zuko’s fire that is now almost just coals, too exhausted to stoke it.

The first thing he notices is that two of them, the man and one of the women, are holding fire directly in their hands.

Despite his pain, Zuko can’t help but to light up for a moment as he realizes he is in the presence of other firebenders for the first time in months. Firebenders that look like civilian travelers, not soldiers of any kind.

However, his smile does almost immediately disappear when he makes the mistake of sitting up a little more and agony shoots through his leg again and he breaks back down into tears.

“Please help me.” He sobs, laying back down on the ground, looking at the three new people. The people who could be here to help him or hurt him. He has no way of telling right now. All he knows is that there is very little he can do to defend himself right now and he is at their mercy. He needs to pray that they’ll help him. Pray that they’re anything like Kani and Chen and will just help him.

The woman not holding fire walks towards Zuko, setting her bag down, kneeling next to him, looking at his stuck ankle.

“Can you get it out?” He whimpers, looking at her. “It hurts.”

She nods. “Yeah, it’s swelling. It’s probably going to hurt but please stay still.” She says, not looking at Zuko as the other two come closer.

Zuko finds it more unnerving than anything that none of them are saying anything to him at all. He knows for a fact that two of them are firebenders and all of them are wearing red clothing, but it almost feels like they’re ignoring him.

It could possibly be because he looks like an Earth Kingdom child considering he’s dressed like one. They could think that he has an issue with all firebender from the palm shaped burn scar on his face and Zuko might try and do something to them once free. He doesn’t know. It just feels weird and he doesn’t like it.

Zuko props himself up on one of his elbows a little, holding up one hand a little higher and producing a bright flame in one hand, letting the three strangers see it before letting it go back out and curling back into himself. “Please get it out.” He begs before any of the others can say anything.

One of the benders begins to feed Zuko’s little fire with larger sticks he couldn’t reach before and fueling it with more flame as the other one puts out his flame, offering Zuko his hand.

Zuko takes it, clutching it tight, trembling a little again.

“My name is Sai, what’s yours? What are you doing alone in the middle of the Earth Kingdom with…” He trails off, gesturing to Zuko’s Earth Kingdom clothes.

“Lee.” He replies softly. He tries to think of what to reply to for the second question. He isn’t sure if it is safe to say that he isn’t allowed in the Fire Nation and likely not the colonies. Well, he probably is allowed in the colonies, it would just mean his father would be very likely to hear about him. Someone there *has* to know about the banished prince.

He doesn’t know if these people are nationalists and how much about the banished prince they know. He also isn’t sure what he can say about Kani and Chen. Isn’t sure how he can explain that he got into a fight with two Earth Kingdom farmers without making it seem like they were trying to force Zuko to abandon all ties he had to the Fire Nation, to his home and his family. He isn’t sure if these people might try and get Zuko unwanted justice by hurting them.

Zuko knows that Kani and Chen were only trying to protect him. That they didn’t want Zuko to be hurt and taken from them. It didn’t mean that it didn’t hurt to not be allowed to be himself. Not even to his best friend.

Before he can start to speak, someone tugs at his ankle as Zuko can only scream, digging the fingers of his free hand into his side, crying.

“It’s okay, it’s okay, it’s out now, you’re alright.” The bender woman says quietly, giving Zuko a small smile.

Zuko nods, leaning against Sai, still sobbing from the excruciating, but mildly subsiding, pain.

“Hey, kid, are you lost? Are you near home at all?” The nonbender woman asks him gently, looking around the deserted forest.

Zuko swallows, pointing back towards the village he had run from. “I live in a farming village, Naofan, that way.” *Hopefully I still do, though I doubt it. Maybe they’ll let me stay one more night.* *Maybe more if they’re willing.* “Earth Kingdom couple took me in. They know I’m a firebender. It’s close.” He says softly, looking down.

He can already feel the heartbreak of Kani and Chen throwing him out the moment he crawls back to their door, begging for help. Begging them to let him rest there at least for one more night. Begging Kani to wrap his leg properly.

Even if they do allow it, he’ll be thrown out in a couple of days. Left in the cold of winter. He doubts they’ll let him stay the winter even if they know they’re sending him to die. It didn’t stop his own father.

It was one thing to be an injured child with a burn on his face. Zuko could still work for someone. He might be in pain and not have a full field of vision, but he could work. Now he has a broken leg. He can’t walk. Probably can’t even stand. That eliminates most jobs that someone would be willing to give him.

When Kani and Chen throw him out into the oncoming winter, Zuko isn’t sure if he will die from heartbreak or exposure first. He isn’t even sure if he can make it back there. He might just die here.

“Are we close to the village? Like really close?” Sai asks, looking at Zuko. He nods once, tears rolling down his cheeks both from physical pain and grief of loss he hasn’t yet faced.

“I think we can help you get at least a little closer, Lee.” Sai offers, resting a hand on Zuko’s shoulder, giving him a sad look. “You shouldn’t be out here alone and I’m sure you can’t walk.”

Zuko whimpers softly, nodding. “Thank you, sir.” He whispers.

“Hey, Mang,” Sai says, addressing the bender woman, looking like the strongest of the three. “I’ll take your bag if you can carry Lee.”

Mang nods, turning around as Sai lifts Zuko off of the ground.

Despite barely moving his leg as Sai helps Zuko on Mang’s back, Zuko can’t help but to cry quietly even as he wraps his arms around Mang’s unusually broad shoulders.

What he notices as he presses close to her is the warmth that she gives off. The warmth that firebenders give off even without intention. He didn’t realize he had missed the gentle touch of another firebender, just reaching the end of comfortably warm, until he starts crying into her shoulder. He wants to go home. He wants to be held and loved. He wants his family.

Despite everything that had been done to him in the Fire Nation and how much kinder everyone has been to Zuko in the Earth Kingdom, Zuko can’t help but think of the Fire Nation as his home. Kani and Chen’s home is also his home, but just that place, not the rest of the Earth Kingdom.

He wants to go home so badly it hurts. He never wants to think about the Fire Nation ever again. He really doesn’t know what he wants.

Before he can get his thoughts in order, he feels Mang begin to walk.

Zuko does his best to stay on her back while not strangling her and not jostling his leg too much, but it’s hard. It’s near impossible for him to stop making small sounds of pain.

“So, Lee, what are you doing in an Earth Kingdom farming village here?” The nonbender woman asks after a few minutes. “The closest Fire Nation inhabited area is more of an unofficial military base than anything...soldier inhabited village? Whatever you want to call it. The closest civilian village is Gaipan. It’s over a week's journey.”

Zuko is silent for almost a full minute, unsure what to say that wouldn’t immediately incriminate him. “My father was a drunkard, got into a fight with him one night and he did this to me.” he says, pointing to his face. “No one did anything to stop him. Said I was being disrespectful. Maybe I was…but don’t think I deserved that. Maybe being hit…just not this.” He whispers, closing his eyes.

“I ran after that. My dad wanted to fight me again because I barely stood up for myself, just tried to apologize. When the farmers I’m staying with found me I was almost dead. I’m never going back there.” He whimpers, fresh, hot tears welling in his eyes as he hears the phantom cheering going on around him as his own father burns his thirteen year old child’s face.

“I’m sorry that happened to you, Lee, I’d run too.” She replies softly. “I’m Lo, by the way.” She adds. Zuko can hear a smile in her voice despite having his face buried in Mang’s shoulder.

“What are you guys doing out here?” Zuko asks, trying to distract himself from the perpetual throbbing pain shooting through his leg and making its way through his body.

“We’re from Gaipan. It’s been getting more militarized because a group of Earth Kingdom rebels have been attacking it. Isn’t really a nice place to live anymore. We’re making our way up a little further north to the colonies. Probably another two weeks until we make it there.” Sai replies. “Lo and I wanted children but don’t want to raise them somewhere with growing conflict and Mang refused to let us go alone.” He chuckles a little as he talks. If Zuko weren’t in so much pain he might smile.

“Yeah, I let you two travel alone and you’ll get yourselves killed. Three days ago this dumbass wanted to eat some random berries he found and knew nothing about other than he was a bit peckish. They were poisonous. Thankfully he only ate a few before I started yelling at him.” Mang interjects, sounding annoyed but not upset.

“So…Lo and Sai are a couple, are you a friend of theirs? Just curious why you’re going too besides keeping them safe.” Zuko mumbles, growing curious in the lives of people like him. People from a background similar to his own. Even if he has to hide some of who he is from them, Zuko can show the important parts. They can know he’s a firebender. It doesn’t need to be a shameful secret from them like it has to be from the village.

“Sai is my dumbass little brother who landed a girlfriend out of his league. I like her more than I like him.” She teases, hoisting Zuko higher on her hips as he begins to slip down, apologizing as he yelps in pain.

“Thank you for helping me.” Zuko finally whispers after the chatter dies down. “Thank you.”

“Hey, it’s alright. I’m glad we saw your flair and your fire. I’m sorry that happened to you.” Lo offers, resting a hand on Zuko’s back reassuringly.

Zuko nods, grateful he had shot up the fire even if risky. Thankful that gentle people had found him again. That he isn’t being hauled off to an Earth Kingdom prison right not to be tortured for information he doesn’t know and be ransomed to a man who doesn’t want him.

Part of him feels like he could drift off from overwhelming exhaustion. Another wants to just sob. Yet another wants to talk to these people forever. Wants to travel with them and preserve what is left of his connection to the Fire Nation. To his home and to his family. To his mother and uncle. Perhaps even his sister in another lifetime. If only they could be given a second chance.

Before he can decide on how he feels about anything, he can hear his new name being screamed in the distance.

Chen had tried to stay calm when Lee ran from the house after feeling as if he were some shameful stain in their household. He felt as though he had cornered the kid and all but chased him from the house.

It had taken Lee so long to trust him. Chen is well aware that his intimidating stature can entice people to back down from even approaching him at first. On top of that, Lee had been horribly abused by the dominant male role model in his life. It hadn’t been surprising that Lee had been nervous of Chen for both of those reasons.

More recently, Lee has been willing to spend more time with him. He had wanted Chen to train with him to try and tame his fear and drive it into his mind that Chen would never intentionally hurt the gentle firebender.

On top of that, Lee had even shared his real name with him. Something Chen doubts Lee even shared with Kani.

Zuko. He knows that name sounds familiar, but he can’t place it. He’s curious, but it doesn’t matter. The little firebender had made it clear as far as anyone should be concerned, his name is Lee now.

He had tried to not let himself panic that Lee had run off. He had assumed that the boy just needed to be alone for a little and would be back within the hour, trembling with cold and fear. Scared that he would be thrown out just for getting upset and standing up for himself over something Kani nor Chen realized was so important to him.

Like Chen had promised, on the hour, he and Kani told Gela what had happened. Unfortunately, Fao had gotten wind that Lee had run off and refused to settle down or go home. He kept asserting that he would go to bed when they found Lee.

Gela agreed to help look while her wife, Shi, came over to Kani and Chen’s home with a half asleep Kyira in her arms. If Lee were to try to come back and find the house empty, he might grab his bag and run. They would never see the terrified little firebender ever again.

Currently, Kani, Chen, Gela, and Fao are moving through the forest in the direction that Lee ran, screaming for him.

Fao had gone from walking next to Gela and holding her hand to riding on her back, crying quietly, occasionally talking about how he had lost his best friend and he would give up sword fighting and his fort for Lee to come home.

Chen wishes he had just talked to Gela and let Lee tell Fao that he’s a firebender. It really might have helped Lee feel more at home if he had been able to share who he is with his friend. It seems like Fao may be willing to accept Lee as a firebender or not. It might have brought the boys a lot closer if anything.

All he wants right now is for Lee to come home. He wants to tuck the kid in by the fireplace, apologizing over and over again and make sure the boy knows how loved he is.

They’ll figure something out that will make Lee feel like he doesn’t need to be ashamed of who he is, like being a firebender is inherently wrong, and try to give him some sort of connection to his culture while simultaneously keeping him safe. It will be difficult, but most worthwhile things are.

As the small group walks while crying out for Lee, they can see a light in the distance. It looks like fire. This probably isn’t how Lee wanted Fao to find out that he is a firebender, but it’s the end result that he really wanted.

“Lee? Is that you? Please come here, love, don’t run, it’s going to be okay. We’re going to take you home. We’re not mad, we’ll work something out in the morning. Please come home, sweetheart.” Kani calls, walking forward a little faster but still minding her step.

“Kani?” A tiny, broken voice comes from a distance. It’s definitely Lee. Unfortunately, it sounds like he’s been crying. Like he’s upset, maybe even in pain.

“Yes, sweetheart, I’m right here, we’re going to take you home. It’s okay.” Kani replies, sounding like she is trying not to cry. She likely is.

Before Lee can say anything else, three people, none of them Lee, all step into the light of the torches the search party is carrying, the flame in one man’s hand only adding to it.

All three people look to be in their early twenties, all in the clothes of Fire Nation red.

Before anyone can say anything, something on the back of one of the women moves, a head peeking up.

“Lee.” Chen breathes in releaf. “You’re alright, son.” He whispers, moving somewhat hesitantly towards the group of unknown firebenders, needing to see his boy.

Lee nods, whimpering softly.

“We think he broke his leg.” The man says, giving Chen an apologetic look. “We finally got him somewhat comfortable, probably best not to move him too much.” He continues, likely, and correctly, assuming that Chen wants to scoop Lee from the woman’s back into his arms.

“Is Lee here?” Fao mumbles, half asleep with a quiet cry in his voice.

“It’s okay, we’re going to head home, Lee’s okay, you can see him tomorrow. He’s tired and needs some space, okay.” Gela says softly, nodding to the firebenders before turning, probably wanting to hide the firebenders from Fao.

Chen is pretty sure he can hear Fao mumble something about wanting to see Lee, but he doesn’t make any move to get down, likely too exhausted.

“You can come back with us. Thank you for finding him. We haven’t eaten dinner yet if you’re hungry.” Kani offers, gesturing for the trio to follow her, they do.

Chen isn’t sure if it is the best idea for her to be inviting three random firebenders in the middle of a war into their home, but they’re already doing it. It can’t be too much worse of an idea than taking in a strange, incredibly mentally unstable firebender child who has been made an enemy of the Fire Nation.

At this point, all they can do is prepare for the worst and hope for the best.

Lee had been whimpering a little almost the entire trip back to the house and it had broken Kani’s heart. He must be in so much pain and be so scared. She wishes that she would have just listened to him earlier and could have saved him this.

As soon as they get back to the house, she helps get Lee off of Mang's back, laying him down on his mat by the fire as gently as she possibly can, apologizing as he lets out small sobs of pain when his ankle touches the ground.

“I’m sorry.” Lee whimpers softly once Kani lays her little boy down, his face scrunched up in pain.

“You have nothing to apologize for, sweetheart. We don’t need to talk about this right now if you don’t want to. I’m going to need to take off your shoe and bandage your leg. It’s going to hurt. I promise I’ll be as gentle as possible. Can I do that for you, love?” She asks, kissing Lee's head.

Lee nods, letting out a small sob, clutching her tight. “I’m sorry.” He repeats. “I-I love you. Thank you for everything. I’m sorry.”

“I love you too, sweetheart. This will always be your home as long as you want it to be.” She says softly, kissing his head again. “Do you want Chen to hold you while I’m splinting your leg? It will hurt and it will hurt more if you move.”

Lee nods, looking over at Chen, tears rolling down his cheeks. The three firebenders are standing behind her husband, looking at Lee, seemingly unsure what they should be doing right now. Kani honestly doesn’t care. Right now, all that matters is Lee.

Chen walks over, wrapping the little boy in his arms as he keeps crying. Kani can still hear a few apologies coming from his lips. Those stop when she starts to remove his shoe.

Lee almost immediately starts screaming, struggling in Chen’s grip, and begging her to stop but not kicking her with his good leg and not using his bending.

Kani apologizes to him quietly, tears rolling down her cheeks as she removes his shoes and socks, rolling up his pants leg and wrapping his leg in cloth so the splint won’t chafe at his skin.

She forces herself to ignore her child’s pain no matter how much she does want to stop and go and kiss his face, reassuring him with soft words and kisses. She can do that after. He needs to just get it over with and then he can have time to heal. He can rest and recover when she wraps his leg properly.

She wraps his leg just tight enough with enough padding and support to keep his leg immobile but not so tight that it would cut off his circulation.

A broken ankle is bad at any time, but it’s better to have it in the winter. The material won’t be unbearably hot and soon there won’t be too much work to do. Lee could probably just help with cooking so he wouldn’t have to walk around if he felt up to it so both Kani and Chen could focus on the harvest. It might also be good for him in terms of helping him gain a little more weight considering he won’t be able to move around much.

As soon as she finishes, she moves up closer to Lee’s head, peppering his tear streaked face with kisses. “There you go, love, there you go, it’s alright, you’re alright, it’s over. The worst is over, there you go.” She reassures him, gently wiping at his tears with her thumb in between pressing kisses to his cheeks.

Lee just whimpers, butting his head under her chin, clutching onto her robes.

“Are you hungry, love? Can you eat something? Even if it’s just a little?” She asks, pulling her little boy closer to her chest as Chen gets up, walking over to the stove and beginning to put stew in bowls, handing some to the firebenders first.

Kani had gotten some of the story from them as they had walked back to the house and she is grateful they found Lee. Lee had been using his bending to signal for help. If an Earth Kingdom soldier had found him, he very well may have been arrested and locked up despite his injury.

She doubts that he would have been given any kind of trial. He might be used for ransom, interrogation, or just a prisoner. If it were the last two, she doesn’t want to think about what could have happened to her little boy.

She doesn’t know what kind of people would be guarding Lee. They might not even see him as a person, only as a firebender. She isn’t sure what they might do to him if he were just to be locked away in a cold, dark room, constantly on the edge of panic after what his father had put him through.

Her little boy would be next to powerless for what soldiers could do to him if someone like that had found him. If someone hadn’t taken him home where he can be safe and loved.

Lee nods once. “I think I can eat a little bit. I’ll try.”

“I love you so much, Lee. I’m so sorry we made you feel like we were ashamed of you. We’re not, I swear to you. We’re scared someone might hurt you if they were to find out you’re a firebender. We’re just scared people won’t treat you well. I promise that what we feel for you being a firebender isn’t shame. We’ll figure out how to proceed when you’re ready, okay? Just for now, know that this is your home. That you’re so loved here.” She assures her trembling little boy.

The firebenders awkwardly sit at the table as Chen brings food over to Kani and Lee, sitting down near them. “How are you feeling, son?” He asks, running his fingers through Lee’s inky hair.

Lee shrugs, picking at some of the potatoes from the stew. Kani had thought that they were his favorites for a while. She found out later that he doesn’t really even like them, they’re just easy on his stomach.

When he picks out a piece of cabbage, the irritating creature sharing it’s name swats it out of Lee’s chopsticks, eating it off of the ground.

Kani had completely forgotten that the chicken cat was in the house. She must have gotten scared off from the commotion.

Thankfully, Lee’s face lights up when he sees the ridiculous little animal. “Cabbage!” He reaches his hand out as she bumps her head against him, purring.

“We thought you might want your friend here when you come home. We were really worried about you, son.” Chen offers, giving Kani some of the credit for letting cabbage in the house to give Lee some comfort.

“Thank you.” He mumbles, abandoning his bowl and pulling Cabbage into his lap, resting his head against Kani’s shoulder. “Love you.” He mumbles again.

“Get some rest, my love. Get some sleep. You must be exhausted. Everything is going to be okay.” She promises the already half asleep firebender in her arms.

Lee just bobs his head one, groaning quietly. A few minutes later, his breaths begin to even out and slow as he falls asleep.

She gently maneuvers him against Chen’s chest as he lays down, pulling Lee up against him, keeping him safe and comfortable.

Kani smiles at him before taking their bowls and walking over to the firebenders who are talking to each other in hushed voices, occasionally looking over at Lee but mostly minding their own business.

“Thank you for helping him.” Kani says, stepping into their conversation, offering a small smile to the group.

Despite having lived with Lee for about three months, it’s still odd to see the Fire Nation like… this. She has seen Lee at his worst when he’s upset, scared, angry, or overwhelmed. She has seen him at his best when he’s excited to see his friends, wants to play, making friends with the animals, and slowly inching his way closer to Chen.

Lee is Fire Nation but he isn’t like everything she has heard about and seen all of her life. He is sweet and gentle. He’s just a little kid who wants to be loved. Something he didn’t have growing up.

Despite that knowledge, it’s odd knowing that Lee isn’t some kind of exception to that. She’s always known that, but it’s different to see. Different to see firebenders using their fire just to light their way while helping an injured child to safety. A family who is close and cares deeply for each other, crossing the continent to get somewhere safer so they can start a family.

Lo gives her a small smile. “Is he going to be alright? I’m glad he was at least close to somewhere safe…do you know why he was out there?” She asks, clearly having seen how distressed Lee was earlier, not just from the pain. He had thought he was in trouble. Thought he was going to lose his home.

Kani thinks for a moment, trying to think of something she can say that isn’t exposing too much of anything personal to Lee. She wants to say something, these are firebenders living in the Earth Kingdom. If anyone knows about keeping in touch with their culture in some way while living here, it’s them. It might be something that could help Lee.

“I don’t know too much about his past, but I know it’s bad and I know that he can’t go home. He’s still really scared even now but I think what happened tonight is at least a sign that he is feeling more like this is his home.” She begins, wanting to try and see some positives in all of this. If Lee had started a fight about connecting with his culture, he probably doesn’t feel like he is going to be beaten or thrown out with no warning.

“There are a lot of people here who have lost people to the war and very much don’t like anyone from the Fire Nation. Some of them might not care that Lee is just a firebender child looking for a home and not a Fire Nation soldier looking for trouble. We’re worried about anyone seeing him firebending and we’ve told people that he’s an Earth Kingdom nonbender.” She explains quietly, feeling more like she had been denying Lee to be who he is now that she is explaining it to other firebenders.

“He‘s been feeling very isolated from his home, his family, and his culture. He’s too scared to write to family that he is close to out of fear his father will find out he’s alive and send someone to find him, who is apparently powerful, so that’s off the table. He wanted to tell his friend that he’s a firebender and has been practicing his bending in the woods which both of us thought was a really bad idea and dangerous thing to do. Both the firebending and telling his friend. He felt like we were ashamed of having a firebender son and he ran.” She finishes, looking at the table.

“Is there anything that might be safer for him that might help him feel more connected to who he was? We’re mostly worried right now because winter is coming and he’s never even seen snow. If he gets in a dangerous situation here with someone who hates any and all firebenders, it might end up getting him killed if he had to run. Especially now that he’s injured. Are there any foods or traditions that might help him feel even a little more connected with his home? I would assume that you guys know something about staying in contact with your heritage.”

She is glad that at least they don’t immediately start telling her that she’s been horrible to Lee forcing him to hide the fact that he’s a firebender. Even if she may be acting a little harsh, they seem to understand it’s a very nuanced situation. He can’t exactly be living in an Earth Kingdom village while parading around in Fire Nation attire and throwing fire at everything. It would get him arrested if not killed in a matter of hours. Probably not even one.

“Is he from the Fire Nation? Not the colonies?” Sai asks, looking up at her with eyes almost identical to Lee’s. Firebender eyes.

Kani nods once. “I’m not exactly sure how he got here, but I guess he just needed to get out of the Fire Nation and the Earth Kingdom is the closest.” She offers, not wanting to give up too much about him, unsure what Lee may have told them.

“Well, we’ve grown up in the colonies. It’s different from the Fire Nation from what I’ve heard. On top of that, we’re surrounded by people like us. I don’t think it’s traditions or foods that he’s missing, he probably just feels isolated.” Sai offers, giving her an apologetic look.

Before Kani can say anything, Mang steps in. “He can’t get far with his injury and I know winter is a bad time to travel. If he really is upset enough about this to run, it’s putting him and possibly others in danger. We’re going to Yu Dao. I've been in contact with some people there who are going to help us get settled. If Lee were to come there later next year, we could help him find people who would be willing to take him in. It might be what’s best for him to send him, or take him, to live with his own people. He might be happier.”

Kani can’t think of anything to say. That is not at all what she was expecting. She thought that maybe one of them might offer some spices that grow in both nations, some recipes that could be made here, cultural traditions that Lee could still partake in, or maybe even just telling her to be more lenient with letting him firebend in disguise or be allowed to tell his friend. She did not expect the suggestion to be to send her precious little boy away.

A churning feeling starts in her stomach as the other two agree with Mang’s suggestion. They want her to send Lee away. To send him somewhere that his father might be able to find him with such a distinct marking on his face. A place where she wouldn’t know if he would be safe. A place where she might not be able to check on him to be sure that he is alright.

She shakes her head slowly. “No. I’m not letting you take him.” She asserts, unsure if she could fight at least two firebenders and maybe a third skilled warrior. She would do her best to protect her little boy.

“We aren’t going to take him, Kani.” Lo assures him. “First of all, we aren’t going to drag a child away from somewhere if he is safe and wants to stay. I trust that you and your husband are doing your best to take care of him, I just don’t know if *here* is what is best for him. Second of all, we left pretty late in the season and are barely going to make it to the colonies before traveling conditions get bad. Taking someone who can’t walk and doesn’t want to go with use would be… stupid.”

Kani relaxes a little, believing her that these people aren’t going to snatch Lee from Chen’s arms and run off with him. Take him somewhere that he might be in danger of discovery.

“Just think about it. Talk to him about it. He can’t travel for the next few months because of his injury and the weather, you have time to figure this out. Just try and think about what might be best for him. You and your husband saved his life and are helping him get accustomed to life in the Earth Kingdom, you’ve done more than a lot of people ever would even consider doing. The next step might be letting him go. I can imagine that it would be hard, but just try and think about what might be best for him.” Sai adds softly, looking down.

“I know that Earth Kingdom citizens live in the colony as well. You might even be able to come with him if you wanted, but I don’t know what is best for all of you. Just please give him the option of going. He might not even want to, just don’t make him feel like he has to stay here.” Mang suggests, meeting Kani’s eyes.

Kani nods once before standing. “There are some spare blankets in that room.” She points to the spare storage room. “Feel free to keep the fireplace and the stove lit if you're cold. I can provide breakfast early in the morning but then I’m sure you need to leave to make it to your destination on time.” She adds the last part curtly, making it clear she wants them gone tomorrow even if she is offering them a safe, warm place tonight.

“Thank you, for your hospitality, ma’am.” Lo’s voice comes as Kani turns to walk back towards Chen, Cabbage, and Lee. She doesn’t respond.

She shakes Chen’s shoulder gently. “Love, can you get up? I want to take Lee upstairs. They’re sleeping down here.” She says softly, not wanting to leave her husband or child with strangers like this.

Nodding, Chen slowly stands as Kani helps him keep Lee near immobile so that he doesn’t wake up. They don’t want to hurt him anymore. He needs to sleep. He needs to recover.

Once Chen is standing. Kani scoops up Cabbage as the two walk up the stairs. She isn’t sure what to make of what these people had just told her, but it’s definitely something. For now, she’ll push it out of her mind. Lee leaving is a problem for tomorrow.
