### Text

Zuko stays snuggled close up to Kani for far longer than he would have dared stayed in bed since he first recovered from his burn. At this point, he knows that Agni has been up for several hours. He should have started working a long time ago. Despite that knowledge, he doesn’t want her to stop touching him. On top of that, his leg is still throbbing in pain even without moving it. He doesn’t want to aggravate it further.

Chen had gone down earlier to get the Fire Nation trio fed and out the door. He is pretty sure that he had overheard Chen getting Lo to change into older Earth Kingdom clothes that Kani can’t wear anymore.

Apparently the trio will be passing through some areas with a lot of people who want vengeance on the Fire Nation. Likely that they won’t care if it is a group of Fire Nation soldiers or just traveling civilians who just want to pass through. Considering Lo is a nonbender with brown hair and darker skin, she could pass as Earth Kingdom if wearing green very easily.

It might help the trio get to the colonies with less chance of trouble if it looks like two members of the Fire Nation are traveling with an Earth Kingdom civilian. Will likely be more convincing that they don’t want any trouble with anyone they pass by. That they have befriended someone from the Earth Kingdom who doesn’t mind that they’re Fire Nation.

Zuko silently prays that it helps prove their character to others. They had helped Zuko when thinking he was an injured Earth Kingdom child, they were just more receptive to him when they found out that he was a firebender.

Zuko doesn’t try to listen to the conversation and doesn’t ask Kani, not feeling all that invested in it other than the trio’s safety. He is also just so overwhelmingly tired but can’t seem to actually fall back asleep. He can just close his eyes and seek out the warmth Kani’s body is giving off next to him.

He tries not to think about the possibility that Kani and Chen were just acting like they wanted to let Zuko stay in front of the travelers. That they just didn’t want to start a fight with two firebenders who’s skill level is unknown and a third who’s fighting techniques are unknown. They would be outnumbered both by people and benders. They may have been worried that the trio may have taken them throwing Zuko out as a personal insult to all firebenders and the Fire Nation in general. He tries to force himself to believe that they *really* want him here. That they love him even if he is difficult and makes poor choices.

It’s hard, but he tries. Letting himself believe that they think of him as nothing but something to deal with is what has caused every serious breakdown he has had here. He can’t let it happen again.

This is made a little easier as Kani hums softly, running her fingers through Zuko’s hair, occasionally pressing kisses to his forehead.

“Kani?” Zuko finally whimpers, looking up at the woman’s kind face, gripping her arm a little tighter, terrified that she might just disappear. So scared that she would leave him behind or throw him away like so many others have. Like so many more might do in his lifetime that Zuko hasn’t even met yet.

“Yes, my love?” She asks quietly, a sad, almost worried look in her expression.

“I’m sorry about everything I did and said last night. I love you. You can keep me a secret. I understand. I’m sorry I wanted more after everything you’ve done for me.” He whimpers, resting his head against her chest, curling up a little smaller without disturbing Cabbage.

“It’s alright, it’s alright. Chen and I need to talk and then the three of us can talk about what we can do. I know you have a tendency to come up with the worst case scenario, but you won’t be punished for last night. We’ll take care of you. I promise, sweetheart.” Kani squeezes Zuko a little tighter in her arms as she talks.

Zuko nods, letting out a soft whimper. “I love you.” He repeats, needing her to know that everything he had said was out of anger. It wasn’t out of sincerity. He loves Kani and Chen so much. They’ve been so good to him. So gentle. They’ve done their best to make Zuko feel like he belongs somewhere and all Zuko had done was fight back at everything they had tried to do.

“I love you too, Lee.” Kani replies softly, giving him a warm smile. “I’m so sorry that we made you feel isolated. Is there anything that we can do to make you feel a little more at home? Feel more like you belong here?” She asks, brushing her fingers over his cheek.

Zuko looks down, unsure what to say.

The first thing that comes to mind is telling Fao about being a firebender, but that is what had led to this whole mess. That is clearly not an option and he doesn’t want to press his luck. They might now allow for the same mistake a second time in such a small time frame.

He had felt so hopeless while stuck with an injured leg last night. The heartbreak of loss that he hadn’t yet experienced was almost suffocating him. It was unbearable. He wanted to rip his heart from his chest to make the pain stop.

Losing Kani and Chen just because he wants to show Fao who he really is isn’t worth it. Worst case scenario, Fao rejects him as a firebender, turns Zuko in for being the enemy, and Kani and Chen throw him out into the cold because he was disobedient. He can’t risk that.

Another thing that had been on his mind that night was Iroh. Zuko had wanted nothing more than for Iroh to come to the Earth Kingdom and hold Zuko in a warm embrace.

Where Zuko used to grow bored and even a little irritated while playing games of Pai Sho Zuko kept losing while listening to Iroh share long anecdotes and drinking tea for hours at a time, he would give just about anything for that now. He would happily do his best to match his uncle’s Pai Sho strategies that would end up being fruitless just to spend some time with the man who had offered Zuko kindness despite the danger it put him in with Ozai. Zuko would be willing to lose his vision completely to drink jasmine tea he pretends to like more than he does while listening to Iroh share a long, seemingly irrelevant story next to the turtle duck pond.

“Is writing to my uncle still an option?” He asks quietly.

He isn’t sure how he would do it. He couldn’t exactly write ‘Hey uncle, it’s your supposedly dead nephew Zuko who’s fate and life could put a huge stain on my father’s reputation as a leader and a man to the Fire Nation. Also, I’m in the Earth Kingdom in a farming village that is completely vulnerable to organized attack. Hope to see you soon.’

Zuko isn’t sure how thoroughly, or if at all, mail is checked that is coming to the royal family. He isn’t sure if servants just check to see who it is to or if certain ones are allowed to read it to not bother the family with things seen as irrelevant.

That first option doesn’t seem as likely. His father has always liked full control when possible. He wouldn’t want someone else to decide what is worth his time and what isn’t. It wouldn’t be long before he started accusing people of hiding crucial information and having them executed with no real grounds.

The option that *does* seem very likely is that his father wants to see any and all letters to Azula and Iroh. He always wanted to have control over what his children saw, said and did. He might want that control over his brother as well. Zuko never had any friends to write to him, so he isn’t sure what the arriving letters looked like. Whether or not the seal was broken or not.

He knows for a fact that his father doesn’t trust Iroh. He likely wants to try and see what his brother is up to even when it could be something trivial lost in the mail. If Ozai saw anything that might be from Zuko, he wouldn’t tell Iroh. Iroh would never receive that letter. He would only ever know that Zuko had been alive in the Earth Kingdom when Ozai would have Zuko dragged back to the Fire Nation for a public execution.

Iroh probably wouldn’t even be allowed to say goodbye. He might just have to watch his nephew die a second time. The third time he had to learn of the death of a young man he considered his own.

The only upside is that Ozai never really cared to get to know Zuko. He could probably write a letter in some way to write a letter and put some details that Iroh would know Zuko sent.

Maybe.

He wishes that he and his uncle had come up with some kind of code during those three years. It would make this so much easier.

“I’m sure we can do that for you, my love. Are you not worried about your father finding you anymore?”

Zuko shrugs. “I am worried about him. I’m *terrified* …I couldn’t exactly sign my name to it. My uncle knows me a lot better than my father. Maybe I could think of something to let him know it’s me? I’m not sure…I just…” He shakes his head, unsure what to say.

“You want him to know you’re alive? I understand that, love. Even if I never was able to see you again, I would be happy to know that you were somewhere safe and being taken care of. That you were happy, healthy, and loved.” Something in her voice sounds…off when she says that. Almost like dread. He isn’t too sure about that.

Brushing it off, Zuko shrugs again. “My uncle used to be a general.” He begins, not meeting Kani’s eyes, not wanting to see the judgment of Zuko being related to a war lord. If she knew the half of it she would disown him immediately. Broken leg or not.

“Well, he still is a general, just doesn’t actually do anything with that title anymore. His son, Lu Ten, the one I said was my brother, wanted to be just like him when he grew up. He followed my uncle everywhere. Then one day, he followed him into war. My cousin was only 19 when he died. My uncle was never able to even honor his body with a proper funeral.” He explains, feeling tears well in his eyes. Iroh had searched for days for his son’s body and it had never been found. Eventually, Iroh had just taken his troops home with a shattered heart.

The day that they learned of Lu Ten’s death was one of the worst of Zuko’s life. He learned that he had lost his cousin, a young man who Zuko had looked up to and loved despite the decade age difference.

Lu Ten had always been kind to Zuko, finding games that they could play together, showing him cool things he found on his travels with his father. Something Zuko had always wanted to be able to do with his own father. Something that had never happened and never would. A compassion that Ozai was incapable of showing to anyone, especially his own fucking *child* . Zuko can feel hot, angry tears burning in his eyes at the thought.

On top of that, Zuko lost his mother the very next day. He still doesn’t know why she told him that she loved him, to not forget who he is and then *left* him. She *knew* what Ozai would do to him even when people were watching. She left him with no protection and not compassion for several months until Iroh finally came home. By then, Ozai had taught Zuko to keep his mouth shut about what he was doing to his son and not tell Iroh or anyone. Ever.

It was made very clear that Ozai could make Zuko’s life so much worse if he dared to open his mouth.

He is sure Iroh suspected, but the old man never pried. Zuko isn’t sure if it is because where Iroh cared about Zuko and he felt their relationship was worth sticking his neck out for, it wasn’t worth putting his head on the chopping block for. It could also be because every time Iroh asked where Zuko got a burn, cut, or bruise from, where Zuko had been for several days, and why he looked so pale, weak, and would refuse to eat anything, Zuko would panic.

He just wishes he could at least understand. He wants to understand why every relationship he has with someone feels so good, like they love him and want to protect him but then it suddenly isn’t. They leave him, they burn him, they use him as a replacement that could never be as good as what they lost, they’re ashamed of him and can’t let him be *him* even if he isn’t hurting anyone. He just wants it all to stop.

“My father used the fact that my uncle abandoned battle and brought his troops home after losing his son to try and take on a position my uncle was supposed to have. I know my grandfather was furious…I think I told you my mom was gone the next morning, my grandfather dead, and my father took my grandfather’s position. When my uncle came home and found out what happened he really helped me. Think we were both trying to find a way to make losing someone stop hurting so much.” He finishes, lacing his fingers with Kani’s.

“You can write to your uncle, love. We’ll think of a way. My sister will usually come up around the harvest to lend an extra hand and get out of the city and I go visit her in winter to help her out when she has the most patients. She should be coming up in a few days. There are carrier pigeons in town, I can have her send them for you.” She offers, kissing the top of Zuko’s head.

Zuko tentatively nods, giving her a small smile. “Thank you.” He whispers. “Thank you so much.” “We’ll keep you in contact with your old life. Maybe it might make you want to stay.” Kani says more to herself as she rubs Zuko’s back.

He isn’t really sure why she has been saying weird things about wanting him to stay, maybe it is because he ran off? He isn't sure, but he likes it. He feels wanted. Like after thirteen years he had finally found his home.

Kani hadn’t been all that surprised when Lee fell asleep again. She knows an injury like that is exhausting considering how much energy it takes to heal.

He looks so sweet and innocent when he’s asleep. He is slightly curled up with Cabbage snuggled up to his stomach. His mouth is slightly open and the worry that usually pinches at his expression is smoothed out in a neutral expression.

Leaning down, Kani presses a kiss to Lee’s temple before heading downstairs. She needs to talk to her husband. She needs to talk to him about the unanimous suggestion that Lee go to the colonies when he is healed and traveling conditions are good.

Even though she doesn’t want to bring it up to either of her boys, she doesn’t want to hide it from Lee. If he were to *ever* find out that she had kept something like that from him just because she didn’t want him to go, he would likely go out of anger, not because he wanted to go there. That wouldn’t be good for anyone.

She needs to talk to Chen about it though. She doesn’t want to talk to Lee about this with Chen completely in the dark. He deserves to know about it. Then they can tell him together. They can discuss it like a family.

Lee will have plenty of time to think about what he wants. What he thinks is best for him. Kani and Chen will have time to try and make the firebender feel more at home here. Feel like he really belongs. Hopefully even if he is considering leaving, it will make him want to stay.

“Chen?” She calls softly as she steps outside.

Her husband is kneeling on the ground in between rows of plants, picking ripe vegetables and putting them in one of several baskets he has around him. Considering Lee can’t walk or even really stand, there isn’t too much that he can do.

Unfortunately, the boy has a habit of always wanting to be put to work. She doubts it is from actually wanting to and more from a lifetime of abuse and feeling the need to prove himself by what he can do for other people. That he is only worth what he can provide.

Winter will be a good time to teach him how to relax and feel better about not doing much, but now might be a good time to teach him how to pickle vegetables. It is one of the best ways that they can store and preserve vegetables from their garden throughout the winter months. It might not be that good, but a lot better than going hungry or trying to live off exclusively meat.

Chen looks up as Kani approaches him, giving her a warm smile. “Our guests left about forty five minutes ago. Lo agreed to wear the robes you said I should give her. They’ll probably be fine.” He looks back down at his work as he talks, carefully but effectively picking the ripe produce.

“Love, there’s something I want to talk to you about.” Kani begins, not seeing the point in stalling. Better to talk about this now while Lee is sleeping then when they need to step out of his earshot. Also better to talk to him about it sooner rather than later.

“What is it?” Chen asks, cocking his head, slight confusion encroaching on his expression.

“I was talking to our guests last night about Lee. I told them that he ran because he felt like he was an outcast and separated from who he was and still is. I asked them for some suggestions on how to help Lee feel more at home here because they would know best but…” She trails off, trying to think of the best way to phrase it without making it sound like she wants to get rid of Lee or that Lee might want to leave them behind after everything.

“They said they feel connected because they are around other firebenders and descendants of the Fire Nation. No matter what we do here, what we can offer him, or help him with, he will always be the only firebender and have to keep that a secret. They suggested that we send Lee to the colonies next spring so he could be with people like him. That if we did, they would help him find someone who would be willing to take him in.” She isn’t sure what that would entail whether it is Lee working for someone or just letting him stay somewhere. She just doesn’t know and she isn’t sure if they would treat him well enough.

“I don’t want him to go…I know you’ve grown really attached to him as well, but I think we should tell him. I don’t want to keep this from him. If he were to *ever* find out that we kept this from him…I don’t know what he’d do. What do you think?” She asks, a selfish part in her wanting Chen to tell her to just not say anything. The selfish part wanting to keep her little boy here with her where she could know that he’s safe. Where she wouldn’t need to worry if someone is making sure that he is eating enough, that they are helping him calm down when something goes wrong, and that he’s being approached with gentle hands and kind words.

Kani isn’t sure if Lee would be happier with people like him, but she wants him to be happy here too. Even if he is a difficult child to take care of, she doesn’t want him to go. She can’t trust that someone else would take the time to sit with him and help him calm down enough after a bad day so that he could actually eat. That someone else might be willing to reassure him of his anxieties even if most of the time she has no idea where they are coming from.

She can’t be sure that someone else would take care of her little boy in the way that he *needs* to be taken care of. He isn’t just a little boy who needs a home, he’s a trauma victim and needs to be treated as both.

“They said that?” Chen asks after a long moment of silence, not looking up at her. Instead, he holds a carrot in his hand, turning it over in his hands absentmindedly.

She nods. “I don’t want him to go…but I also don’t want to lie to him. He’s made it *very* clear he doesn’t like lying.” Lee had admitted to her that Lee isn’t his real name but didn’t want to share what it is with her. She is pretty sure he had told Chen what it is, she isn’t sure why but never pressed. The more he talks about his family, the more she suspects it’s because Kani knows more about Fire Nation war lords and families.

The fact that it seems like Lee is worried that she might be able to recognize Lee by only his name, just the thirteen year old son of a war lord, is concerning. She is sure that Lee is from a noble family, but his concern makes it seem like he is *very* high ranking. The only name he has ever shared from his family is his cousin, Lu Ten. That is only likely because even though it isn’t incredibly common, plenty of people still share that name.

“They also said that there are Earth Kingdom families in the colonies. That if we didn’t trust that he would be taken care of properly, we could go with him.” She continues before Chen could say anything.

“Kani, I know you love him. I know you don’t want him to be separated from him, but please don’t work yourself up like this. Let’s first just talk to him to see if he even wants to consider going. If he does, we can worry about details then, okay?” He asks, pressing a kiss to her cheek.

Kani nods. “Also, he wants to write to his uncle. I have no idea what he’s planning on doing for that considering he doesn’t want his father to find out. He just wants his uncle to know he’s alive, apparently he likely feels responsible for Lee’s death.” She explains, wishing Lee could just be fully honest about his past. It would make his family history and relations far easier.

“Okay, I’m sure we can figure something out. If he can talk to his uncle, he might want to stay.” Chen reassures her, putting down the carrot and taking her hand in his.

“We can talk to him when he wakes up. Maybe even in a few weeks. He’s exhausted, in a lot of pain, and really stressed out already. My sister being here might stress him out as well and he probably won’t want anything else on his plate. We can give him a few days just to rest and calm down from everything that just happened before Feya comes. Also, try and make sure he knows that he isn’t in trouble for running off like that. I think he’s pretty freaked out he’ll be punished in some twisted way.” She explains, unable to fathom what kind of parent would do such horrible things to their child.

The two of them work nearly silently together, unable to think of anything to really talk about. Lee had only been with them for a few months but the idea of him just leaving them seems nearly impossible. She doesn’t want him to go.

“I’m going to go check on him and leave him a note that we’re just outside. I don’t want him to wake up alone with no explanation after everything that just happened.” Kani finally says, kissing Chen before standing up. Her husband just nods once.

As she stands and turns to go back into the house, she can see someone sprinting towards her from the back of the house. She looks at them for a moment and smiles as Fao comes into view, almost certainly here to see Lee.

He had been so torn up when he learned about Lee running, it might be good for her boy to know how much his friend cares about him. It’s nice to see how close the two have really gotten over the past few months.

Kani waves and Chen raises his head, smiling at the young boy.

“Is Lee here? Is he okay?” He asks, almost out of breath. “My mom helped me make this for him this morning.” He shows her a loaf of sweet smelling bread. “Can I see him?”

“He was sleeping when I left, wanna come up with me? I don’t know if he’s up yet. He’s alright, he’s just really stressed out and in pain. He just needs some time. If he’s up you need to promise to be gentle and stay calm. Can you do that?” She asks, smiling at the kid.

He nods frantically, looking up at her with a pleading expression.

She looks up at the sky as they walk towards the house, the sun is a lot higher than it was when she came out. She and Chen have been talking about Lee and silently working together for nearly two hours now. She just hopes that Lee hasn’t woken up and felt abandoned.

Zuko feels a warm, gentle hand running along his upper arm and a gentle kiss being pressed against his temple. “Mom?” He whispers, groaning softly, trying to make sense of what is going on around him.

“Yes.” A familiar voice replies. “It’s Kani, my love.”

“Mom.” Zuko repeated, clutching her hand tight in his as he blinks a few times, the room slowly coming into focus around him.

“Hey, love, how are you feeling?” She asks, cupping his cheek and smiling at him.

“Better.” He breathes, glad that she’s here. He doesn’t know what he would have done if instead of bringing him back home, they had turned him away at the door when the firebenders tried to bring him home. He would probably be in pain half dead at the edge of the woods right now. Unable to get any further with how much pain he is still in even with his leg properly wrapped.

“I made you pumpkin bread, Lee!” Fao’s voice comes out of nowhere and Zuko can’t help but to flinch a little at the sudden noise.

Before Zuko can even acknowledge his friend, Kani steps in. “Fao, please be calm. I know you’re excited to see him but you need to be calm.” She informs his friend before moving closer to Zuko, embracing him. “Do you want him to stay? You can say no if you want, I understand if you need space.” She whispers so Fao can’t hear her.

“Want him to stay.” Zuko replies, happy that someone had actually missed him besides Kani and Chen when he tried to leave.

“Okay, Chen and I are going to be in the garden, you two boys can stay up here. Lee, you are not allowed to stand, let alone walk, and no, don’t come up with creative ways to get around. When I was looking at your ankle, it didn’t seem fractured, it seemed broken. You can mess yourself up if it hits something. If you need to get somewhere, Fao, come get Chen or I, we’ll carry you, we’ll get you crutches as soon as we can. Lee, if I find that you’ve been moving around, your new cast will be made of solid rock that is stuck to the floor. Got it?” She asks while ruffling Zuko’s hair.

“Yes, ma’am, I promise I’ll stay in bed.” He replies, smiling a little at Kani. The first threat she has ever given him is empty and about his health.

“You better, kid.”

“Okay, I love you.” He mumbles, slowly sitting up, leaning up against the wall as Kani leaves.

As soon as she does, Fao climbs on the bed, offering Zuko the loaf of pumpkin bread wrapped in a colorful napkin. “Want some?” He offers, tearing off a chunk and beginning to much on it.

Zuko nods, taking a piece of it, nibbling on it. “It’s really good.” He praises, smiling at his friend.

“I wanted to make something for you. I was really worried that I wouldn’t see you again when you ran away. I’m glad you’re home, Lee.”

Zuko wraps his arms around Fao, smiling. “I’m glad to be home. I’m sorry I worried everyone. I was just being stupid about something.” He explains, unsure how else to describe it.

“Why did you want to leave? Did something happen?” Fao asks, cocking his head.

Zuko shrugs. “I told you I have to hide a lot of my past for safety. You’re my best friend and I wanted to share some of that with you. Kani and Chen didn’t want me to and I felt like they were ashamed of me as opposed to just trying to protect me.” He explains quietly.

Fao moves closer to him, eyes lighting up. “I won’t tell them that you told me. I’ll keep it a secret.” He promises, grinning as he holds Zuko’s arm.

Zuko isn’t sure what to say. It probably *is* dangerous to share that he is a firebender with Fao. That there is someone capable of destruction in his midsts after seeing so much of what they have done to Fao’s world. To his family and his home. But he wants to tell him something. There are safer things.

“My parents weren’t killed by Fire Nation soldiers.” He begins, looking down. “My father killed my mother…I think, but he wanted to kill me the night that she disappeared. Then three years later he actually tried to kill me. *He* did this.” Zuko points to the scar on his face as he speaks. “I’m from the Fire Nation and he banished me…I ran before it could be carried out properly. I was supposed to go with a crew, but I had to get out of there, so I ran off alone. Kani and Chen found me half dead in the hurricane and have been taking care of me ever since. I never want to go back to the Fire Nation, *ever* . I hate it there. My father will kill me if he finds out I’m alive.” Zuko whimpers quietly, all of it just coming out.

“I promise I’m not with the Fire Nation.” He mumbles, pulling his good knee to his chest. “Kani and Chen know about my past…I think one of your moms, Gela, knows as well, not as much though. I wanna stay here. Like the Earth Kingdom more than the Fire Nation.” He finishes.

That last part isn’t necessarily true, but he loves his home in the Earth Kingdom far more than what he thought was home in the Fire Nation. He has a much better family here.

Instead of replying, Fao wraps his arms around Zuko. “I’m sorry they hurt you, Lee.” He whispers, clutching him tight.

“Zuko.” Zuko corrects before he can think better of what he is about to say. “My real name is Zuko.” He informs his friend, hoping he doesn’t recognize it.

“Zuko.” Fao repeats, smiling. “I like it! Can I call you that?” He asks, excitement in his eyes.

Zuko shakes his head. “It’s a really, really uncommon name. If my father were to ever catch wind that there was a 13 year old boy with a scar over his left eye by the name of Zuko…that would be it. He’d kill me for real. I just want to be safe.” He whimpers, resting his head against Fao’s shoulder.

“You’re my best friend, Zuko, I promise I won’t tell anyone about any of this.” Fao promises.

“You’re my best friend, too.” Zuko replies, warmth spreading from his chest and through his body at the new found acceptance he has now received.

The two boys spend the better part of three hours talking and playing card games involving them both making up rules to try and make the other lose on ridiculous pretenses.

Thankfully, neither of them care about winning all that much, they just want the connection.

All too soon, Kani comes up and tells Fao that his mother wants him home. The two boys embrace one last time before Fao runs down the stairs and out of sight.

Chen eventually picks Zuko up, carrying him back downstairs to the hearth and resting him on his mat. The man shows Zuko what he has done for the crutches so far and tells him that they should be done in two or three days. By then, Zuko will likely have gotten some more rest and recovered from the initial shock of the injury making him more inclined to want to move around on his own again without constant help. Especially considering he won’t be able to walk for a few months, he will want to be able to be somewhat self sufficient.

As Kani finishes making dinner, Chen sits down next to Zuko, resting a hand on his back. “Lee, Kani told me you want to write to your uncle, yes?” He prompts, smiling at Zuko.

Zuko nods. “Want him to know I’m alive.”

“I’ve been putting some thought into it while working today, and I think I have an idea. You can say no if you don’t want to or only partially to some of it. Want to hear it?” He asks.

Zuko nods, giving Chen a grateful smile at his willingness to help Zuko reach out to someone who Chen knows is a warlord who has attacked Chen’s home and nation. Knows people personally who have suffered from generals such as Iroh. All he seems to care about is the fact that Zuko cares about his uncle and wants some connection with him.

“I was thinking you could write to your uncle as a soldier who served under his command when he was attacking the Earth Kingdom. The soldier you would be posing as wouldn’t have just been anyone, but someone who he respected and maybe even befriended. You write to him that you were captured by soldiers and held prisoner up until a few months ago when you escaped. You tell him that you were injured but are now living with Earth Kingdom commoners that are keeping you safe and healthy in return for you protecting them from any Fire Nation troops simply by announcing your presence or whatever you want to write.”

Zuko cocks his head, confused how any of that would help. “I don’t understand how that will tell him that I’m alive.” Zuko questions.

Chen shakes his head. “I’m not done. You need to put in details that your uncle would have never encountered. Very specific details that may not seem too odd to someone else reading them but that never happened to him. You’ll want to add details that he may attribute to you. You aren’t just going to send one letter, you’re going to need to send several, all signed with your Earth Kingdom name. If you’re feeling bold, you can even say that you’re living a three day's journey by foot outside of the harbor town of Si Lang, but I wouldn’t go as far as to say you’re in Gaipan. That is if you want him to try and come find you.”

Zuko nods, tears welling again but not falling. “I want my uncle. Even if I could just see him for ten minutes. I want to see him so badly.” He whimpers. He would allow Iroh to give him a bone crushing hug for as long as he wanted with no complaining or struggling if Iroh would just hug him again.

He should have been more grateful for his uncle when they were together.

“Wanna work on it some? I promise I’ll only read it if you let me.”

Zuko nods, throwing his arms around Chen. “Thank you. Thank you.”

After dinner, Zuko sits down with paper and a brush. He allows Kani and Chen to help him draft it. He doesn’t want to write the final draft in front of them though, it would be impossible to miss the opening line of ‘General Iroh’. It’s a household name in all nations. It’s only in honor and respect in the Fire Nation.

In the Fire Nation, the name of The Dragon of the West is spoken with pride and dignity. He is a soldier and leader who people want their children to take after in time. How they want them to help lead their country to greatness. He is someone who takes initiative and shows strength even in times of hardship.

In the Earth Kingdom and Water Tribes, it is a name spoken with fear, hate, and scorn. He is a tyrant who only seeks to paint the world red in the blood of the nations he tarnishes, only wanting to see the color of his nation strewn across the globe, not caring if there are others who need what paints it in more.

He isn’t sure that this will work, but if it gives him some connection to his uncle, then Zuko is happy. He might be able to find some peace and not feel so guilty about leaving Iroh behind with no warning. He didn’t even leave a letter.

He tries to focus on the fact that Zuko has Kani and Chen now and maybe Azula has Iroh. Maybe Iroh will be able to protect Azula more. He will make sure that she is safe and loved so that she can’t meet the same fate that Zuko and Lu Ten did. He might do his best to keep her safe from Ozai’s cruelty.

Azula really needs someone to look out for her. With all of Ozai’s expectations and cruelty now falling on her shoulders…he can’t even imagine what she is going through now.

Zuko had been his father’s favorite punching bag for years and it only got worse when Ursa disappeared. He probably wouldn’t treat Azula the same way that he treated Zuko, but cruelty doesn’t always come in the form of a blow. It might actually be worse that way. She might not even know she’s being beaten until she can’t get up.

“Do you want something specific for the seal?” Kani asks, holding a smooth rock in one of her hands and a stick of sealing wax in the other. “Something that might signify you to him?”

Zuko thinks for a moment before nodding. “A turtle duck.” He remembers the cute little creatures so eager to eat from his hand and snuggle in them when empty. “They’re my favorite.” He clarifies. “My mother and I and then my uncle and I would feed them together. Thankfully, my father never seemed to care about that.”

Kani smiles, closing her hand around the rock and handing a stamp to Zuko with an outline of a turtle duck standing up on it to be stamped in the hot wax.

“Thank you.”

“Would you like us to stay down here with you when you write your final draft or would you like to be alone? We won’t touch it when it’s sealed. Feya will be here in a few days, she can send it for you when she gets home. Okay, love?” Kani reassures him, kissing his forehead.

“Wanna be alone…not ready for you to know exactly who I am yet. I promise I’ll tell you everything one day. Just not now. You might recognize my uncle’s name. I know it is pretty common to know the names of generals who lead attacks here.”

“Okay, son, we love you. If you need us, just yell and one of us will hear you.” Chen ruffles Zuko’s hair as he speaks.

“Thank you.”

As soon as the couple disappears upstairs, Zuko begins to write the final draft in neater letters, praying his uncle will understand who he is. Hoping he will at least consider coming to find Zuko. Praying that his uncle will understand that even though Zuko isn’t in danger, he just wants to see a loving member of his family so badly it physically hurts.

*General Iroh,*

*I know it has been years since we last spoke, but it has been my first instance that I have been given* *the opportunity to send anything to you. I marched with you into what I thought would be the* *greatest battle of all time and am sorry to hear that it was your last. Heartbroken when I learned* *the reason. Word travels. People talk. I know that there is no amount of words or sympathy that* *could make up for what you’ve lost.*

*I was taken captive during battle and recently escaped imprisonment by a stroke of luck. While* *running, I mostly thought of your long and convoluted life advice. Never thought much about it* *until I had some application for it. On top of that, I never thought I would miss playing Pai Sho* *with you even if you would always win and insist I try new types of odd teas. I should have* *appreciated our time together more than I did.*

*By chance, I have been allowed to reside with an Earth Kingdom farmer couple about three day's* *journey by foot outside of the harbor town of Si Lang. They are giving me a place to stay and* *keeping me safe and healthy in return for some work on the farm and dissuading Fire Nation* *troops from attacking their village, even if unlikely. It’s small with little to gain from occupation.* *They simply offer passing soldiers meals to keep some peace between them. I considered traveling* *to the colonies, but it’s too far of a journey after being injured from battle. However, I am safe and* *happy here.*

*It has been a long time since I have spoken to you and I would like to extend my condolences to you* *for the loss of your son, your nephew , your father, and your throne. I am aware that life hasn’t* *treated you kindly even after everything you tried to bring into the world. I hope you find some light* *in your life even if in the strangest of places such as I have.*

*I hope that we will cross paths again one day, until then, I can only be with you the best and that* *one day I may see the Fire Nation again.*

*Your obedient servant and friend,*

*Lee*

Zuko reads his letter again and then a third time just to make sure that it makes sense. He needs to make sure his uncle gets some of the hints. The letter is just off enough that it wouldn’t likely not raise the attention of Ozai skimming it. If it did, he would likely think of it as one of the odd people Iroh would befriend. His father likely wouldn’t even bother reading it fully after learning it is from some soldier Iroh used to serve with.

It takes lots of considerations before Zuko underlines *nephew* . He makes sure that it could just look like a stray mark on the paper and adds a few more, none underlining words though, just to be safe. He *needs* his uncle to know that his nephew is safe. That Zuko is alive and being taken care of with a very kind Earth Kingdom couple outside of Si Lang.

He might even come looking for Zuko. Trying to find proof that he is alive.

Finally, Zuko rolls it up and seals it with his turtle duck stamp. *Please know it’s me, uncle. Please* *come find me. Please help me. I need you to come find me.* He prays as he finishes his letter, leaving it on the table.

“I love you, uncle.” He whispers before very, very carefully dragging himself across the floor and onto his mat. It doesn’t take long for him to fall asleep, dreaming of drinking warm tea and being held in his uncle’s loving embrace.
