### Text

It has been several months since Feya has last seen her sister. The last time they saw each other must have been late last spring. She usually comes into town before the harvest, but she had been sick in early summer and Chen had done the supply run. Then most recently in autumn, she had stayed back to care for the firebender child she and her husband had taken in.

Since that revelation, Feya had been paying more attention to rumors floating around about the Fire Nation. She never has any idea how much of it is fact, exaggerated, or completely fabricated. Fabrication could either come from fear or propaganda, it’s always hard to trace it back to its source. Word of mouth in a world of fear and hate is fertile breeding ground for any dehumanizing rumor.

One rumor in particular had caught her interest, although she knows very little about it. That seems to be the case for most people talking about it, no matter how much of a hot topic it is.

For better or for worse, the story doesn’t seem to change too much like most rumors do. In most other cases, one week she would hear about how a Fire Nation soldier had passed through and tried to buy supplies from an Earth Kingdom merchant and two weeks later it would be how a group of Fire Nation soldiers threatened the same merchant’s life and how they valiantly fought the group off.

With the crisis that the world is in, that is how most rumors tend to go. It isn’t in the least bit surprising.

That, however, is not the case for the particular rumor that she has heard floating around about the Fire Lord’s eldest son, Zuko. It is likely because despite the boy being the son of the world’s most feared tyrant, he was still just that; a boy. A thirteen year old boy who was murdered by his own father’s hand.

The details surrounding it change, but the essence of the story stays the same. There isn’t much added to it besides speculation. Everyone she has heard speculation from, even those in a daze of pain that she is healing, have made it clear that they are only speculating.

All she knows is that for some reason, that reason varying, the Fire Lord challenged his son to an Agni Kai, a fire duel with the intentions of killing him. Feya doesn’t know too much about Fire Nation tradition, but she knows that Agni Kais are either fought until one opponent is badly burned or killed.

The Fire Lord wanted it to be a fight to the death.

She doesn’t know why it didn’t end that way, she’s heard that the kid refused to fight. Some say he was just a coward, some say he was too young to fully be able to understand what was happening and went into a panic, and some, more heartbreakingly, say he tried begging for mercy while trying to apologize. Trying to make whatever he had done right without violence.

No matter the reason, it ended in the boy’s face being burned until he fell unconscious from pain. She knows that he was cast out of the Fire Nation only days later, too soon to have healed from an injury like that. Likely he was thrown out as soon as he was conscious, almost certainly having trouble even standing.

Some say that he simply died of infection, something that isn’t far fetched for what the intensity and size of the burn he experienced must have been like. That is if she can believe the stories that she has been told. Others say that from pain, humiliation, and despair, the boy took his own life. If that were the case, Feya couldn’t blame him.

If her own father, a man she looked up to his entire life, did something like that to her, she might not be able to bear that burden. Especially at the age of thirteen. She would have probably killed herself as well. Many would. Even if just to escape the physical pain knowing full well they would never be able to recover. That they would just die from it anyways days later.

The more she has thought about the firebender boy, Lee, the more she has felt the need to see what he looks like. She needs to talk to him. She needs to know who he is.

He is the same age as the Fire Prince, has a bad burn, and was forced to flee the Fire Nation in fear. She has gotten some descriptions of what Zuko is supposed to look like, but they aren’t very helpful. She has gotten that he is ‘slight of build, black hair, pale skin, and hazel eyes’. Considering he is a young firebender boy, she could have guessed that herself.

Even if she can’t prove anything to either herself, Kani, or Chen, she at least wants to know the kid isn’t dangerous. She needs proof that all this kid wants is a roof over his head, food, and a safe, warm place to sleep. If that’s all he wants, then fine, she won’t make a big deal about it. She just needs to be reassured that that is really all he is after. That he doesn’t have any ulterior motive.

Eventually, Feya reaches her sister and brother-in-law's home. She brings her ostrich horse to the barn out pack and puts it in the pen before walking around the house, waving to Chen when she sees him in the garden.

Feya walks towards her brother-in-law and smiles at the man.

Before she can say anything, Chen rushes towards her, tackling her in an embrace. “It’s so good to see you, thank you for coming.” He says, laughing a little.

Feya hugs him back, always forgetting how strong Chen is.

“Kani just went inside with a load of vegetables. Lee is prepping brine and fitting vegetables into any jar that we have. I’d like you to meet him. You promise to be nice to him? You don’t have to like him or trust him, but you *have* to be nice to him. He just broke his leg and is still pretty freaked out from his previous life.” Chen warns her, meeting her eyes.

Feya nods once. “I promise I won’t express any negative feelings in front of him.” She means it. If this kid *is* the Fire Lord’s kid, the last thing she wants to do is corner him and make him feel threatened. He might get aggressive and dangerous. Mostly, she hopes she can put her suspicion of his family history to rest. Come to the conclusion that he is just some kid who needed help. Chen begins walking towards the house with a half full basket he had been using to harvest ripe vegetables with. Feya follows him into the home.

Kani is walking up from the cellar when the two walk in, holding more empty jars in her arms despite there being plenty on the table and surrounding the kid, Lee, on the floor, both empty and filled with various vegetables.

“Feya, you’re here!” Kani puts the jars down before rushing over and throwing her arms around Feya. “I’ve missed you, thank you for coming.”

“I’m glad I could make it. It’s been too long.”

Before Feya can say anything else, Kani pulls away and leads her towards the boy cutting vegetables and stuffing them in jars of brine to preserve them through the winter months.

“Feya, this is our son, Lee. Lee, this is my sister, Feya.” Kani introduces the two, kneeling next to Lee, taking one of his hands and pressing a kiss to his forehead.

What Feya can’t miss is the enormous burn scar taking up over a third of the kid’s face, likely damaging his left eye. None of the rumors she heard had specified which side of his face the burn was on. She assumed that it was over an eye considering people talked about how the kid had gone blind before he died. She hadn’t pressed too far into the rumors, knowing the messengers only had so much to tell.

“It’s nice to meet you, ma’am.” Lee’s voice is quiet, almost wavering, as he trains his eyes on the ground at Feya’s feet.

She isn’t sure if the kid’s nerves are simply because of Feya being someone new, because he can sense that she is wary of him, or because he can sense she knows that he is full of shit. No matter the reason, she can almost feel fear radiating from the kid.

No matter how concerned she is, she can’t help but be concerned about the way that he looks. Not just because he matches the limited description of Zuko, but because he is supposed to be thirteen.

Chen had said that he was very skinny and had likely suffered from stunted growth from chronic malnutrition, but she hadn’t expected this. He barely looks ten. He’s very, very small. His face is a little gaunt, his clothes don’t fit around his shoulders properly and she can see a little of the bony frame of his right shoulder. He almost looks chronically ill.

A good part of her wishes that she had brought the kid something. Maybe some candy of some sort or something like that. He’s so thin. So small. So scared. She can’t even begin to imagine what the little boy has been through. Fire Lord’s son or not, he’s been through so much. Too much. &#96;

“Hey, Lee, it’s nice to meet you as well.” She eventually replies, kneeling down in front of the boy as well, offering a small smile. “Chen told me some about you when he visited me last. You can call me Feya if you would like to.” She offers, unsure if he is trying to be polite or if he is scared. She had seen both in children she had been healing or children who had accompanied an injured parent. It is getting far too common as the war progresses.

She still doesn’t know how she feels about the kid. She doesn’t know if he is a liar about who he is, but he isn’t faking his fear. He’s scared. Someone broke this kid and Kani and Chen are just doing their best to hold the pieces together.

“Do you need anything, love?” Kani asks, kissing the back of the boy’s head as he hangs his head low, face hidden in shadow and growing hair. Lee just shakes his head a little, hanging his head a little lower.

“Sweetheart, is something wrong?” She asks, resting a finger under his chin, lifting his face a little.

Out of the corner of her eye, Feya can see tears on the boy’s cheeks for a moment before Kani pulls Lee close to her chest, helping him hide his face in her shoulder. “You two go outside, I’ll be with you in a moment.” Kani’s voice is calm as she rocks the ever so slightly trembling firebender in her arms.

Before Feya can even say anything, Chen rests a hand on her shoulder, leading her out of the room and into the garden.

Kani has no idea what could have set Lee off. She can’t think of anything that had happened besides Feya showing up. Literally all she did was show up and talk to Lee a little. She doesn’t understand what just happened.

“Sweetheart, can you hear me? Are you alright? Did something happen?” She asks, rubbing the firebender’s back, unsure what to do right now. Worried that he is somehow getting worse.

“Sh-she hates me.” He chokes out in a small whimper, gripping Kani tight. “She hates me and wants me gone. She wants to get rid of me.” He cries, trembling a little harder in Kani’s arms.

With Lee’s track record of being abandoned, isolated, and neglected, it isn’t hard to understand that he lives in almost perpetual fear of something like that happening again. Of more people leaving him with no explanation. Of being hurt and forgotten about by people who were supposed to love and cherish him but instead treated him like something that could be tossed out and replaced.

“She doesn’t hate you, love. She doesn’t hate you. I promise she doesn’t want you gone. She might be a little wary around firebenders, but she doesn’t hate you. If she were to even think about hurting you or taking you away, we would tell her she had to leave. This is your home, love, not her’s. No one is going to take you from your home. I won’t let them.” Kani promises, knowing that she is only soothing his fear of the consequence of Feya hating him, not the actual feeling. What he is feeling runs far deeper than anything she can touch right now. It is pain built from a lifetime of trauma and will take years of consistent help to even begin to heal.

Lee seems to have the desire, if not the need, to have everyone like him. Kani can’t say that she is too surprised after being denied friendship, being abused by his father, abandoned by his mother, emotionally isolated from his sister, and now physically isolated from his uncle. It isn’t hard for her to understand that Lee feels the need to have reassurance that people won’t leave him. If they like him, they won’t be as likely to leave him.

Zuko seems to have been loved by his uncle, his cousin, and his mother growing up, three of the main people in his life. It only took one person hating him to ruin his life. He likely feels that if even one person doesn’t like him, they’ll find ways to hurt him in any and every way possible.

“I wish I wasn’t a firebender.” Lee finally whimpers, pulling away from Kani a little, head still down as he brushes at his tears. “I never chose to be a firebender. I’m sorry that I am one. You don’t have to lie and say you didn’t wish I was normal too.” He finally says, voice wavering. “I’m sorry.”

Kani isn’t sure how to respond to that. It’s…horrible. “Lee, do *not* say that, love. Being a firebender isn’t inherently bad. The Fire Nation just so happens to be on the other side of a war we’re in right now. You being a firebender isn’t a bad thing. I’m so sorry that there are people who will treat you like the enemy just because you’re a firebender. I’m sorry that you have to hide your bending. I’m so sorry for so many things, but I don’t want you apologizing for being a firebender. I’m sorry if I have done anything to contribute to this feeling of shame.” She adds, cupping his face in her hands and kissing his forehead.

“I love you. She doesn’t hate you. She knows that if she wants to be here or for us to visit that she needs to be willing to accept you as part of the family. Nothing bad will happen. She knows that the Fire Nation would have nothing to gain by sending in a child spy to an insignificant little farming village in the middle of nowhere. However, If you want, I can just ask her to keep her distance from you, alright?” She offers, giving her little boy a small smile.

Lee nods once. “Is it alright if I can just finish working on this alone? I just…I dunno, need to clear my head.” He says softly, still holding Kani’s hand tight in his, indicating that he really shouldn’t and doesn’t want to be left alone right now.

“Are you sure you don’t want me to stay, love? Your wellbeing is what is most important to me right now. You don’t need to feel ashamed if you need company. No one will be upset with you.” She promises, meeting his mismatched eyes.

Lee nods. “I’m sure…I just need some time to think. Need to be alone.” He says softly.

Kani nods, feeling warry at leaving him alone after watching him break down over absolutely nothing, but she doesn’t want to press him. “Alright, love. We are just going to be outside. We’ll be in and out. Please let any of us know if you need anything at all. Even with crutches I know it might be hard to get around. They take a bit to get used to.” She cautions him.

Lee nods again, letting go of her hand before chopping vegetables and placing them in prepped and labeled jars.

Kani presses one last kiss to her sweet little boy’s head before standing and walking out the door.

Zuko works all but silently throughout the day. He mostly ignores the people who walk in, bringing more vegetables to the table that Zuko is working at. He just washes the vegetables, chops them, and fits them into jars of brine, covering them fully with the liquid.

The look in Feya’s eyes was impossible to miss. He can feel fear and nausea moving from the pit of his stomach and crawling up his chest and throat as his mind creates a mantra that he works to in silence, every movement feeling like his veins are filled with hot lead. Limbs too heavy and searing in agonizing pain.

*She knows, she knows, she knows. She knows who you are, she knows what you are, everyone else* *will know too. She knows. It’s over. You're done. You’ve lost again.*

Part of him is grateful that his leg is broken now more than ever. Even if being the son of the Fire Lord changes how Kani and Chen see him, they likely won’t throw him out yet. Zuko had done things time and time again that warranted it and they had never even threatened Zuko with the possibility of that happening. If anything, they had promised he would never have to fear being tossed out into the cold by their hand.

Kani and Chen might not love him anymore if they find out the truth, but they might not throw him out either. If he were healthy, his new family might change their feelings about kicking him out, but he isn’t. They would know that if they threw him out right now with a broken leg during winter, they would be sending him to die. There would be no way for him to survive in a season he has never experienced in unfamiliar territory and as the enemy with no home or allies.

The others in the village would know that there was a reason that Zuko had been thrown out and confront Kani and Chen. They might do something worse than simply throw him out, they might have him arrested. Leave Zuko to die cold and alone in a cell as they would try to ransom him to a man who would never come for him.

If Feya tells her sister and brother-in-law about Zuko’s family, everything will change. There won’t be any more nights by the fire where one of the farmers runs their fingers through Zuko’s hair, telling him a story. No more warm embraces, kisses pressed to his cheeks and head, or hands ruffling his hair. That would be over.

They honestly might just predominantly ignore him and allow Zuko to either stay by the hearth or in the barn, he isn’t sure which. They would allow him to stay until winter passes and his leg is healed, then it would be over. Then he would be on his own.

At least he can trust that the farmers are too kind to send Zuko to his death. Something his own father wasn’t even kind enough to do.

Zuko silently works throughout the day, occasionally tending to the soup cooking over the fire, but mostly pickling vegetables trying to hold back tears.

The whole day seems to be impossibly short and dreadfully long. He has no idea which is worse. They’re both agonizing in their own way.

When dinner finally comes, he feels far too sick to even think about eating. It’s the first time in a while he’s skipped a meal because of anxiety.

Instead of eating, Zuko buries his face in Kani’s shoulder, letting her run fingers through his hair and occasionally press a kiss to his head as she eats, occasionally trying to coax him to take a bite. He wishes he could, he just *can’t* . She’ll likely understand why soon enough. He just needs one of his last chances for her to hold him like this. One of the last moments that she’ll love him.

He isn’t sure how long he’s been leaning against her when she wraps both arms around him, pulling him onto her lap and to her chest, rubbing his arm as tears he has been trying to suppress begin falling. His breath begins to hitch in quiet cries as he clutches Kani closer, desperately clinging to the fabric on her back.

“Lee, my love, did something happen? I didn’t know Feya being here was going to upset you so much. Is something else wrong?” She asks, worry in her voice.

All Zuko can do is whimper in response, trembling a little harder. There isn’t anything that he could say that wouldn’t immediately expose him. He just has to wait until his life is ripped out from under him all over again.

“I want you to breathe with me. Take deep breaths with me, okay? I don’t understand exactly what’s wrong but we can talk. Just breathe with me first.” Kani instructs, beginning to take slow deep breaths.

Zuko tries to copy her and it takes several tries for him to even calm down enough to take deep breaths. He can hear encouraging words and feel Kani’s hand rubbing his arm. He doesn’t want this to stop. He doesn’t want her to hate him. He can’t bear it.

Finally, even breaths begin to come more naturally and his grip on Kani grows slack as he rests against her, feeling exhausted above anything else, both mentally and physically.

Kani pulls away only a little, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s forehead as she does, meeting his eyes with a sad expression. “Can you talk to us? No one is going to try and hurt you in any way.” She says to Zuko before her eyes fall on her sister. “Feya, I don’t really know what’s happened but a lot of his life before this he has kept secret. He has been very honest about what he doesn’t want to talk about and informs us if something about him isn’t true but wants us to act as if it is. I don’t think you did anything to him or if this is even about you, just please be patient with him. He’s had a very hard life and has his reasons for wanting to keep aspects of it secret.”

“I promise I won’t do anything to hurt you, Lee.” Comes Feya’s voice and Zuko feels so much tension leaving his body just at that, going almost limp against Kani. “Lee, I’m not here out of malice. I don’t want to see you get hurt.”

Zuko nods once, taking a few deep breaths before forcing himself to sit upright in Kani’s lap, looking at the floor near Feya. “Can I talk to you? Alone?” He whispers, wiping at his face with the heel of his hand.

He isn’t sure if he can manage to get through a conversation with this woman without breaking down. It’s clear that she’s intelligent, strong, and not someone to be trifled with. But that isn’t the point. The point is to just be able to stay here even if just for a little longer.

From what he has heard about her, she cares about her family. Even if she does hate Zuko, the point is to protect Kani and Chen. To protect the people around them that she may fear Zuko has ill will against.

At the very least, maybe Zuko can convince her to not say anything to Kani and Chen. Promise that he’ll leave once his leg is healed and the weather is warm. If he doesn’t have to watch Kani and Chen hate him, it will be okay. He can survive if he knows that they still love who they think he is.

“Of course, love. Chen and I will be right outside. You promise you want to be alone? You don’t have to do this just because you think it’s what she wants. Feya knows that you’ve been through a lot and that things will be different until you warm up to her. You don’t need to force yourself to do this.”

Zuko nods, almost breaking down all over again at the care that Kani has put into all of this. How much she loves him. How he’ll never find a family who would be willing to take him in like Kani and Chen again. That it’s all downhill from here.

He allows Kani to gently slide Zuko off of her lap, using all of his willpower not to throw his arms around Kani’s neck and beg her not to leave him. Not to hate him just for who he was born to. Tell her that he would have given anything to be her son and never even dared to even speak his father’s name.

Despite telling them he wanted to talk to Feya alone, Zuko can feel his heart break as Kani and Chen leave the house. He wants to cry out and beg them to come back. Tell them he can’t do this even if it means Feya exposing him in front of them before he even gets the chance to get a word in.

Zuko meets Feya’s eyes only for a moment and it is impossible to mistake the fact that she *knows* *everything* . He doesn’t know where she heard it or for how long she has suspected Zuko’s identity, but it’s terrifying.

She begins to try and formulate words but Zuko forces himself to talk before she can, unsure if he could do this if he hesitated even a moment longer. “You know who I am, don’t you?” He asks all in one breath, closing his eyes, pulling his good knee to his chest, whimpering.

An audible sigh comes from Feya before silence follows.

“Please just say it.” He squeaks, digging his nails into his leg.

“You’re the Fire Lord’s banished son, Zuko.” She finally answers, a voice far more composed that Zuko could ever imagine anyone guessing Zuko being the son of a tyrant who had brought the world to its knees for the lust of power. A man whose influence had gotten Feya’s husband killed.

“I-I’m sorry.” He whimpers, not looking up. “I didn’t want to be his. Would give anything to not be his. I’m sorry. Don’t tell them, *please* . I don’t wanna go. Please. I’ll go when my leg heals, just don’t tell them. Th-they’ll hate me.” He pleads.

“Zuko…can I call you Zuko?” Feya asks, resting a hand on Zuko’s arm.

“I-I like Lee more now.” He whimpers. Truthfully, he likes the way his old name sounds more, it’s more fitting. Unfortunately, it was the name he was called in the worst parts of his life. When he was always terrified and alone even when surrounded by people. As long as he has been Lee, he’s been safe.

“Lee,” She begins again. “I’m not going to punish a child for who he was born to. I don’t think my sister would throw you out because of who you are but I won’t tell her anything. I’m sorry if I gave you the feeling that I didn’t like you, it’s complicated. I know logically that you’re a scared, injured child and have little to nothing to gain outside of what you claim you want from living in an insignificant farming village. It’s just…it’s not you who I have an issue with, it’s your father. I’m not mad at you and I won’t hurt you.”

“Promise?” Zuko whimpers, peeking up from his leg, meeting her eyes.

“I promise, Lee. I don’t hold any ill will against you. Tell me a little about yourself. Might help see you as, well, you, not just things I’ve heard about the royal family.” Feya offers, offering Zuko a smile.

He can’t imagine what the world thinks of the Fire Nation family. They probably just picture soulless monsters incapable of love or any real emotion. Just soldiers who grew up in fear and hate and continue to spread it.

Zuko isn’t sure what he should talk about, unsure what Feya wants to know about him. It really doesn’t make much sense. Nothing does. Everything seems to be spinning around him but also standing still. He isn’t sure exactly what’s going on.

“When my mom was around we would go see plays together.” Zuko begins, looking down. “She always loved the theater, used to be an actress before my dad took her. She’d read me stories about plays and show me costumes. We’d go see a few plays every year together…one of the few things I looked forward to.” He admits, a strong tug at his heart for how much he misses his mother.

His mom would love Kani and Chen. She would be happy that kind people had taken her son in and healed him after what Ozai did to him. That they had kept him safe and healthy no matter how difficult Zuko made that for them.

“We’d also feed the turtle ducks together. They’re my favorite. There was a pond in the garden that my mom tended to. She told me her mother was an herbalist and it reminded her of home…she wasn’t allowed to tell me that or anything about her previous life, but she did. I miss her. I want my mom to come back.” He whimpers.

Arms wrap around Zuko’s shoulders as Feya comes closer, holding him tight. “Was your mother in an arranged marriage with your father?” She asks, Zuko can only nod, not sure about all the details surrounding it. He knows it was more brutal than that, but isn’t quite sure.

“I don’t know how well you’ll be able to travel with your leg, but if it’s doing better and you can ride the ostrich horse, there is a theater by the harbor. It’s pretty common to hold plays in the winter, it’s a good way to congregate and share what we have. If you can travel safely, I can take you to see some of the plays when Kani comes to help me.”

Zuko’s face lights up with that information. “I would love that!” He gets out, vaguely remembering Chen mentioning the theater.

“She usually comes about six to eight weeks after the harvest is over. A broken ankle takes three to four months to heal and return to normal activities. You’ll be able to travel by ostrice horse if for the next several weeks you rest, eat plenty of protein, and are very careful with putting any weight on your foot. Do *not* stand without your crutches. If you do that, I can show you around and make sure you get to see as many plays as possible.”

Zuko nods quickly, tears drying in his cheeks, a small smile forming on his face, and the nausea slowly fading as he begins to feel safe around Feya. Trust that she isn’t here to hurt him or ruin his life for some twisted way of having fun. “I promise I’ll take care of myself.” He means it, he wants to go to the theater.

“We’ll get you to the theater at some point, I can promise you that. I can also promise that your secret is safe with me.”

Zuko meets her eyes, trying to find hints of manipulation of any kind, unable to find any. He wraps his arms around her waist, resting his head against her shoulder. “Thank you.” He whispers, feeling like a burning weight had just been lifted from his chest. Like he can actually breathe now.

“Kani told me that you want me to send a letter to someone back home for you. Can I ask who it's for?” Feya eventually asks, rubbing Zuko’s upper back in small circles.

Zuko nods, smiling a little again. “It’s for my uncle Iroh…he probably thinks I’m dead, I want him to know that I’m safe and being taken care of. I *hope* he understands that. I couldn’t write it directly out. My father doesn’t trust him and I’m worried he might read letters coming in…if he found out I was alive, he’d kill me. I just…I want my uncle.” He admits, thinking about how much the old man would love Kani and Chen as well.

They had taken his nephew in when he needed it most and shown Zuko kindness despite being the enemy. They had looked past Zuko needing to lie about his identity, being a firebender, and being from the Fire Nation. All they cared about was that Zuko needed help. So they gave it to them.

In a different world, Zuko is sure his uncle and the farmers could be close friends.

Tension takes over Feya’s body as Zuko remembers who Iroh is to the Earth Kingdom. How Feya doesn’t know Iroh as the kind, tea loving old man, but as a warlord bent on bloodshed and conquest.

“He doesn’t support the war anymore after he lost his son.” Zuko adds quickly before Feya can say anything about the feared dragon. “He knows that it is because the Fire Nation sends far too many young people to die for nothing and because my uncle was too invested in the war that his son followed him. I’m pretty sure he did a lot to keep my father from sending me to the front lines for the purpose of getting rid of me.”

Zuko had never had anything to confirm that, but he heard whispers that he was never meant to hear. He had been suspicious of it. Part of him is sure that his father only threatened to do so just to keep Iroh in his place. Keep him preoccupied with protecting Zuko that he couldn’t do anything to hurt Ozai.

“You’re scared of him, aren’t you? Your father.” Feya asks, sadly.

Zuko nods, whimpering a little. “I’m so scared of him. I-I’m scared that he’ll kill my uncle, that he’ll hurt my sister. I-I think he killed my mom or is at least the reason she left. I think he killed his father. I’m so scared of him. He’ll hurt me…he’ll kill me if he finds out I’m here.”

“No one is going to find you, you’re safe here, alright, Lee?” Feya whispers, resting her forehead against Zuko’s head, hugging him a little tighter.vx

Zuko can’t stop another small smile from forming as he relaxes into her embrace.

Part of him is terrified that Feya knows everything about him. She could use it against him if she ever changes her mind about Zuko or is actually just a better liar than Zuko thought. Another part of him is relieved.

He can be pretty honest about who he is with Kani, Chen, and Fao. He can be authentic in the presence of Gela even if he doesn’t know the woman all that well other than she doesn’t seem to care that much about Zuko being a firebender. However, there are limitations to what he can say and do in front of those people, all depending on who they are and what they know.

Now, around Feya, he can be completely honest. She knows exactly who Zuko is and what his family has done to the world. She knows that Zuko is still close with his uncle, a man who had laid waste to the capital of her nation. Was born to a man who took her husband from her. In spite of all of that, she isn’t letting him go. She isn’t trying to get him away from the family that she has left.

It would be so easy for this woman to take out her anger of the Fire Nation and the royal family on Zuko and never have to see the wrath of the Fire Nation. Might even see praise from Zuko’s father and those around her, but she doesn't make any move to try and hurt him.

“Thank you, Feya, for everything.” Zuko whispers, snuggling closer to the woman who he had been terrified of only moments before. She isn’t here to take him from his family. She isn’t here to break him all over again. She’s just here.

That might even be a good thing.

Feya had always known that the royal family were just people. That where they may hold a lot of power and do many horrible things with it, they are still just people. She also felt like there wasn’t a drop of human blood in their bodies. Like they were twisted forces of evil with no true face or body, just a husk harboring some dark spirit bent on destruction.

That latter even seems to be what Zuko thinks of the Fire Lord. The kid had seen the man most of his life, been in his presence and is absolutely *terrified* of the man. Doesn't seem to think that the Fire Lord knows or understands compassion or mercy in any form. Wants to see his child suffer for no discernible reason.

Unfortunately, that fear seems to be rooted in some kind of truth. The fact that he was genuinely scared that Feya would find a way to get a traumatized, injured, innocent child thrown out of a place he finally felt safe out of pure spite is a testament to that.

Even though Feya felt wary of Lee when she realized who he was, she wasn’t planning on using that information against him. The most she was planning on doing was talking to Kani and Chen in private about his family and heritage, confident they wouldn’t use it against him either.

The poor kid must have lived a horrible life before this. A life full of pain and terror.

It is an odd thought that Zuko is the son of the most powerful, and one of, if not the most, wealthy family in the world. That his father could have chosen to give him anything in the world and chose to give the kid trauma instead.

If she were to tell anyone that a farmer couple living a decently comfortable life in a tiny Earth Kingdom village could provide a better and safer life for a child than the Fire Lord could, no one would believe her.

Feya has seen many injured, traumatized, and abused children in her life. She has seen children with bruises in places and shapes they could have never gotten from just playing. Seen broken digits and bruises on them before they could even crawl and by extension, unable to injure themselves.

She had seen children who had lost their family to the war and had been left to the cruelty of the world. She had seen children of a parent or parents who had lost someone close to them to this war and succumbed to alcoholism and cruelty.

She knows what the injuries look like, and unfortunately, that has never been the hardest part. The hardest part is coaxing these children into allowing her to touch them after learning the hard way about how horrible touch could be. Coaxing them into eating something after worrying about any kind of vulnerability or need for so long.

No matter how many times she’s seen it, it never gets easier. Even if she can do something to help them, there is no guarantee that their new situation will be better. There is only so much that she can do.

One thing in common is that these children always either crave something that they have been denied or push it away entirely. There is very little middle ground for many of these children. Sometimes, it is out of fear, other times out of anger, and sometimes…well she can’t always place what it is.

Zuko has seemed to perpetually crave physical affection at any and all opportunities. He seems almost scared when Kani lets go of him. Almost like he’s scared that she won’t come back. From what it sounds like, touch has always been something used against him, she is surprised that he seems to almost need it to get through the day. Surprise that not only does he happily accept touch but seek it out like a reptile to heat.

Chen had talked about Zuko having a lot of issues with eating and it likely being a long term problem built from trauma. He really does look severely and chronically malnourished. Feya had kind of thought that he was exaggerating on the kid’s state. Unfortunately, he wasn’t.

Considering who Zuko is son to, it clearly isn’t a lack of ability for him to be fed, it has to be something intentional. Considering there is a lot of cultural diffusion where she lives considering she is a healer in a harbor town, she has picked up plenty of Fire Nation recipes. If Zuko can make it into town this winter, she’ll have the supplies to make plenty of Fire Nation noodle dishes considering flour and rice store well. She can make him as much food as he wants, maybe even put a little weight on his fragile little body. Whatever he has been through, he didn’t deserve any of it.

She pulls the tiny little boy a little closer to her, wanting to protect the kid from the world after all it had done to him. Wants to shelter him from anyone who might want to hurt him just because he is the Fire Lord’s son, something he had no control over. She never wants to let another Fire Nation soldier be even able to *look* at him after everything that country allowed to happen to him. What must have been impossible to miss.

Zuko is royalty and must have been a public figure from before he could walk. It would be impossible to hide how small and thin a thirteen year old is. Clothing can only hide so many cuts and bruises. Can hide ribs but not a gaunt face and stunted growth. Water can only wash away so many tears and so much blood. Only so much acting could hide the unadulterated terror that Zuko clearly holds for his father.

By the time that Kani and Chen walk back into the house, Feya is absentmindedly running her fingers through Zuko’s thick, inky hair with one hand, the other holding him close to her as his head rests on her shoulder, face hidden from her, breaths slow and even.

“What did you do to calm him down?” Kani asks, kneeling next to her. “He was terrified earlier. Pretty much inconsolable.”

Feya shrugs as best she can. “Just talked to him. He was just scared I was going to try to use what I knew about him to hurt him. I promised I wouldn’t share anything with anyone.” She explains, shifting Zuko’s head a little into a more comfortable position.

Kani smiles at her, touching her boy’s cheek. “Well, you must have made an impression on him, he’s sleeping.”

“Is that a good thing?”

Kani nods. “As soon as he was somewhat healed and his fever broke, he wouldn’t go to bed until Chen and I went upstairs and would always be awake when we came down. He doesn’t sleep in front of someone unless he has to or he feels safe. Whatever you said or did worked. Thank you, Feya. I know what the Fire Nation has done to you, but thank you for looking past that, he needed it.” She presses a kiss to Zuko’s cheek, smiling.

“I’ll get him in bed if you get something set out for him to eat if he wakes up later and is hungry.” Chen steps in, gingerly taking Zuko from Feya’s arms and carrying him to a mat laid out by the fireplace where Feya would usually sleep when spending a few nights here. Not *living* here.

“Does he not have a more permeate place to stay?” She asks as Chen tucks in the tiny firebender with a red blanket, probably something to remind him of home.

“We were going to clear out the room over there and move things into the cellar for him,” Kani begins, nodding towards the small storage room. “But he’s very claustrophobic, some other horribly fucked up thing his father put him through. He likes being by the fireplace. At some point this winter we’re just going to hang up some curtains for him to give him some privacy but not make him feel trapped. Best we can really do for him.” A sad look is in her sister’s eyes as she speaks, looking over at the tortured boy sleeping soundly by the fire.

Feya feels a flare of anger in her stomach for the Fire Lord for more than what she has experienced in just her life. No one ever talked about him like he’s a person and that’s because he isn’t. He can’t be. There are bad people in this world, there always have been and there always will be. But Ozai, he is pure evil. Irredeemably *evil* .

There are people in this world who don’t deserve to be parents or ever be near a child, but this seems different. It sounds like Zuko only ever existed as someone for the man to take his anger out on. He forced someone to marry him, forced her to have a child and then tortured him his entire life, warping his perception of reality on such an innate level that it is heartbreaking.

Feya is well aware that as far as healers go, she is more calloused than most and more prone to violence, but this is different. Part of her wants to join the war effort just to see the Fire Lord fall, not for what he has done to the world, but for what he had done to his son. His own *child* .

“I’m glad you're the ones who found him. He needed you badly.” She says sadly, unable to take her eyes off of the little kid. She can’t imagine anyone ever wanting to hurt him for any reason.

“If anyone else found him who wasn’t a trained healer, I don’t think he would have survived the night. He was so sick, Feya. His burn was infected, and he had been in freeing rain for hours, he hadn’t eaten in awhile. We really thought he was going to die.” She can hear the pain in Kani’s voice as she talks, eyes on Zuko’s sleeping body.

Before Feya can say anything else, Kani stands, wiping at her eyes. Her sister doesn’t like crying and doesn't like other people to see when she does. She usually finds a way to move from the issue that’s causing the emotion. This seems to be the case now.

“We should probably get to bed, we have a lot of work to do tomorrow. We decided earlier that Chen would stay down here with Lee if you come upstairs with me.” Kani offers back to Feya now.

Feya nods silently, following her sister upstairs, the tortured firebender out of her sight but still burning in her mind.

### End Notes

#### Chapter End Notes

All Feya had to do was spend 0.05 seconds with Zuko and now she says 'mine'

## Chapter 15

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

I start classes on Monday and have my tattoo consultation later tonight so, woo woo.

### Text

The next several days are nice. Zuko spends as much time around Feya as he possibly can in his current state, much to Kani’s delight.

Feya would help Zuko with a lot of the pickling and cooking when the harvest began to die down. During this time, she would ask Zuko questions about his family and the Fire Nation, something Zuko hadn’t been able to talk about so freely in so long.

Thankfully, she mostly wants to talk about his uncle, she stops talking about his father when she notices that it is upsetting him.

She wants to know what the famed dragon of the west is *really* like as a person and how close Zuko had been to him. How Iroh had done his best to protect Zuko from as much danger as possible, even if there was only so much that he could do.

He knew from the beginning that she was only staying for about a week, but he still can’t stop himself from crying when she leaves.

Even if Feya is kind of cold and not the kind of person most would be instinctively drawn to like Kani, she’s the only person that Zuko can talk openly with. She’s the only one he can share things with that he didn’t even realize were important to him or things he never knew had hurt him. She’s the only person who knows exactly who Zuko is and doesn’t think any less of him because of it.

He wants to think that everyone else would be like this as well. That they wouldn’t care that Zuko is the son of the Fire Lord and that Zuko had been hurt so much by that man, holding no loyalty to him or the Fire Nation. Zuko misses the Fire Nation, but he wouldn’t consider himself loyal. Not anymore.

All he wants is to be able to talk about his past life without feeling ashamed of everything he had enjoyed. Doesn’t want to feel like the Fire Nation is inherently bad, just the ideology is.

Growing up in the Fire Nation, Zuko had been taught that his nation was the greatest and strongest in history and needed to save the rest of the world from itself by spreading its strength across the world. Only upon facing the heartless cruelty of his own father and seeing the way that the world sees the Fire Nation does he understand that it’s wrong. That forcing beliefs on other people is only hurting them and causing them to hate everything the Fire Nation is and stands for.

Civilians just trying to live peacefully in the country think the same thing Zuko once did. They don’t know or understand that what their country is doing is wrong. They don’t know the truth as to what led up to the war or what troops are doing to the world in the name of falsified greatness.

All this war is bringing is misery and shame.

Despite that, the Fire Nation has created many wonderful things. It has beautiful art, some of the best food that Zuko has ever had, and spectacular landscapes. He wants to talk about it with someone without the fear of revealing too much of the truth. He just wants to share the good parts of his life with someone who accepts and loves every part of him even if some of it is difficult.

Zuko knows that he will likely always feel closer to Kani and Chen. They are the ones who took a scared, injured firebender into their homes who had tried to attack Chen from fear as a first impression. They had healed him and taken care of him when he was sick and injured no matter how difficult or dangerous it might be for them. They had lied to the people around them and made up a story to protect Zuko’s identity and help him fit into their community before Zuko could even think clearly enough about what would happen next.

After that, they had continued to find ways to help Zuko heal in ways that he didn’t even know he had been hurt. They had found injuries, carefully pointing them out in ways that they thought would be the most constructive even when Zuko would lash out at them for telling him that he had been broken.

They likely had no idea what to do to help him recover from some things done to him but did their best despite any danger that Zuko might present directly or indirectly to them. Zuko is a trained firebending soldier who could likely take on both of them in a physical altercation. He could also be the reason that they would be ostracized from their community if it was discovered that they were knowingly hiding a firebender who’s father is known to be of importance in the Fire Nation and tendencies of aggression.

They would still continuously do their best to make Zuko feel safe and loved no matter how difficult Zuko made it for them. He knows that he has made it *very* difficult for them.

However, with Feya, Zuko can be completely open. He knows that he could have that same relationship with both Kani and Chen if he were to just tell them the truth, but he can’t bring himself to tell them. There is so much that could go wrong.

Considering the fact that Feya had come with the expectation of having a strained relationship with Zuko but accepting him into her family almost immediately gives Zuko so much hope for the fact that Kani and Chen would accept him as the Fire Prince. Feya had been suspicious of him but when she felt like Zuko could be trusted and was just a scared kid looking for a home, she didn’t care what Zuko had to say after that. All she cared about was the former. She really is a healer and caregiver at heart even if she does have a somewhat prickly outside.

Kani and Chen have had months to be fully aware that Zuko presents no threat to them or anyone else. That he wants to be away from his father and never wants to see the man again. Considering they must know that Zuko at least comes from a noble family, they likely won’t be too surprised that Zuko is the Fire Lord’s son.

Every logical part of him knows that they wouldn’t care and that they would accept him for who he is, but what is stopping him isn’t logic, it’s fear. No, terror.

So many things have gone wrong in Zuko’s life and all it had been was just one tiny little slip. Sometimes, it wasn’t even his fault. If Azula was telling the truth about Azulon demanding for Zuko’s execution because of Ozai trying to usurp Iroh’s throne, then Zuko’s life had begun to fall apart because his father couldn’t keep his mouth shut.

If this were to go wrong now, Zuko could lose everything. He isn’t sure if Feya would allow him to stay with her if Kani and Chen kicked him out. It’s something he can’t bring himself to do.

Even if they don’t throw him out, the disapproving looks they might give him could be too much to bear. It might shatter his heart completely even if they still keep him alive. Now that he knows how it feels to be loved by someone in safety, he can’t go back to just surviving. He can’t go back to someone loving him while the rest of the world wants to see him shatter.

As Feya leaves, Zuko watches her disappear into the early morning, crying quietly, curled up near the barn, clutching cabbage close to his chest.

“I hate to see you this upset, my love, but I’m glad you got close with Feya.” Kani rests a hand on Zuko’s shoulder before sitting next to him. “Is there anything I can do for you that she did that made you so happy?” Kani asks, giving him a sad smile.

“Not yet.” Zuko whispers, unsure how else to put it.

“May I ask what made you feel so secure with her? I know how hard it is for you to trust anyone after what has been done to you. Maybe I can figure something out.” She offers softly.

“She knows who I am.” He whispers, before quickly adding: “She had heard rumors about what my father had done to me in town, then saw me and put two and two together. I didn’t tell her.” He doesn’t want Kani to think that he shared something very personal with Feya because he trusted her more. He needs her to know that it was happenstance, not favoritism.

“You can tell me who you are if you’d like, love. I know you like honesty and I would like for you to be honest with me. You don’t have to, but I love you as Lee and I will continue to love you as whoever you once were.”

“I know.” Zuko whimpers, leaning against her. “I know you wouldn’t use it to hurt me, I just…I’m scared, Kani. I know you wouldn’t, but I’m scared you’ll hate me or throw me out. I know I can trust you and that you aren’t like my father…but I’m scared.” He admits, taking her hand in his and resting his head on her shoulder.

Kani presses a kiss to Zuko’s head. “After everything that has happened to you, you have every right and reason to be scared and upset. You don’t need to tell me now or for a while. I would like to know at some point, but only when you’re ready.”

“I love you.” Zuko finally whispers, pulling Cabbage a little closer when she tries to walk away, she curls up in his lap in resignation, seeking warmth, not seeming to care too much about anything else.

“I love you, too, Lee. I know it’s hard, but remember that you are loved and safe, alright?”

Zuko nods, closing his eyes. He won’t ever forget that. No one could ever make him.

“You are getting quite the hang of this game, Princess Azula, your brother never seemed to.” Iroh comments as he barely beats Azula at Pai Sho. It won’t be long until she beats him.

“Zuzu didn’t like Pai Sho, he liked you, he also wasn’t very competitive.” Azula responds, a sad note in her voice as they set the board up again.

Iroh gives her a sad smile while she isn’t looking. He had always known that Zuko wasn’t the biggest fan of Pai Sho, but it was one of the few things Iroh could offer that his brother wouldn’t care about Zuko doing.

It would allow for his injured and exhausted nephew to rest somewhere his father wouldn’t be. Allow him to have an activity that wouldn’t be interrupted, or at least less likely to be.

Iroh would make Zuko any tea he possibly could to keep away hunger pains when Zuko was being denied food. After the punishments the servants and his mother faced for bringing him food and how Zuko was punished for accepting it, he was far too terrified to eat anything Iroh gave him. Even when no one was looking, he was absolutely terrified.

Those were always the hardest days for both of them. Zuko was suffering for obvious reasons. He was weak, in pain, and hungry. Being denied something he needed just out of the cruelty of the man who was supposed to love him. Iroh just had to watch his nephew suffer. He had to stay strong for Zuko. He couldn’t start crying or get angry, he had to stay calm.

It still breaks Iroh’s heart that Ozai could have given Zuko the world but chose to starve him. That his child was going hungry out of cruelty. That Zuko had grown so terrified of the man that he would obey him even in private.

Zuko had tried his best to be loyal to his father. He had done everything the man asked of him even when he could barely stand from exhaustion, pain, and hunger. He would try his best, no matter how many times he failed. He didn’t lash out even when locked away in the cold and dark, too terrified to even close his bedroom door near the end of his life.

When it got really bad, Zuko would even stay up all night with candles in his room with the door wide open. The guards couldn’t do much besides inform Iroh that Zuko wasn’t sleeping. All Iroh could do for his traumatized nephew was to keep watch over him to allow Zuko to sleep. He couldn’t change Zuko’s circumstances. All he could do was coax Zuko to rest his head on Iroh’s lap and do his best to keep the poor boy’s nightmares at bay.

Zuko had known nearly nothing but terror the last three years of his life. The last three years when Ozai no longer had to hide the severe abuse his son was facing from his father and brother. When Ozai could control everyone Zuko got to see how and everyone treated him, all he had to do was keep cuts, burns, and bruises where clothes could cover them when Zuko would be seen by the public, something pretty easy to achieve with the need for Zuko to dress formally. He just had to keep Zuko at a distance so people wouldn’t notice that the prince was far too small and pale to be healthy. That the circles under his eyes were too dark and his eyes were almost always red and puffy from crying.

It was all so easy to hide. Zuko’s suffering was kept hidden from the public with everyone far too terrified to say anything.

Iroh had mentioned that he wanted people to know who the Fire Lord really is. That he doesn’t care for his country, his people, or his family. That he only cares for power. This was two years ago and Zuko had begged Iroh not to, terrified at what Ozai would do to him.

Iroh had tried to get Zuko to understand that if Ozai wasn’t respected as a leader, Iroh could take the throne and protect Zuko and Azula from harm.

Opposed to even considering it, Zuko threatened to kill himself if Iroh ever brought it up again. Iroh still isn’t sure if Zuko was bluffing, but he knows that Zuko was more terrified of his own father than of death itself.

At night, Iroh wishes that he had killed his brother. Whenever he sees Ozai, he wishes he had killed him before he had taken Zuko’s life. Iroh still considers it as his brother continues pushing Azula further and further, reaching her breaking point, something Ozai surpassed long ago with Zuko.

If Iroh had killed Ozai, he doesn’t really care if he would be imprisoned. His niece or nephew would have taken over as Fire Lord. If it would have been a bad look for them to pardon Iroh so soon after killing his own brother, it would look like conspiracy.

Even if Iroh spent the rest of his life in a prison cell unable to ever see his niece or nephew again, he would rest easy knowing Ozai could never touch them again. Knowing that they could have recovered together, found ways to cope with the abuse that they faced and learn to be happy in a new world they would help build.

It’s too late to help Zuko. All he can do is remember his sweet nephew and do his best to protect Azula. He can’t let her die by her father’s hand as well.

“He also at least pretended to like his tea. It’s good, you’ll like it.” Iroh comments, looking at her barely touched tea as she makes her first move.

“He was always a people pleaser.” Iroh moves as Azula talks. “I really miss him, Iroh.” She finally admits, looking down, swiping at her face quickly.

Iroh reaches forward, taking her hand. “I miss him, too. All we can do for him now is not let his memory die and not let your father go unpunished for what he did.”

Azula nods, moving one of her pieces, squeezing Iroh’s hand, not letting go as she takes a sip of her almost certainly cold tea. “Jasmine was his favorite, wasn’t it?” She asks, looking down at her cup.

Iroh nods. “That’s at least what he told me.”

The two play three more rounds over the course of almost two hours, Azula winning the third much to Iroh’s dismay, but at least she is smiling. That’s what matters.

They stop when a servant walks into the room bearing a letter. “General Iroh, I have a letter for you.” He bows as he hands the scroll to Iroh. A scroll marked with a green ribbon but not bearing a lotus seal. He can’t remember the last time he received a letter from the Earth Kingdom that wasn’t from King Bumi.

“Thank you.” Iroh replies, waiting for the man to exit the room before setting it down.

“Read it.” Azula prompts, blowing on her tea to heat it up, sipping on it and making a face. “You have a secret Earth Kingdom girlfriend?” She teases, trying to lighten the mood from talking about her dead brother.

Iroh chuckles softly, opening it and reading it, furrowing his eyebrows as he does. The letter doesn’t make much sense. He served with several young men by the name of Lee, but only one of them he had befriended and he is still in contact with that man. He lives in Caldera City. The whole letter seems kind of…odd.

“What’s wrong? Is it bad?” Azula asks, cocking her head.

Iroh shakes his head. “No, just…odd. It’s from a young man who I never served with even though he claims we did who just escaped prison. Also, he fought in Ba Sing Se which is in the eastern Earth Kingdom but is now on the west coast of it but claims to be too injured to travel to the colonies which isn’t far.” He explains.

Azula stands up, leaning on the table, looking at the letter, quietly reading it out loud so that only she and Iroh can hear:

“General Iroh, I know it has been years since we last spoke, but it has been my first instance that I have been given the opportunity to send anything to you. I marched with you into what I thought would be the greatest battle of all time and am sorry to hear that it was your last. Heartbroken when I learned the reason. Word travels. People talk. I know that there is no amount of words or sympathy that could make up for what you’ve lost.”

“I was taken captive during battle and recently escaped imprisonment by a stroke of luck. While running, I mostly thought of your long and convoluted life advice. Never thought much about it until I had some application for it. On top of that, I never thought I would miss playing Pai Sho with you even if you would always win and insist I try new types of odd teas. I should have appreciated our time together more than I did.”

“By chance, I have been allowed to reside with an Earth Kingdom farmer couple about three day's journey by foot outside of the harbor town of Si Lang. They are giving me a place to stay and keeping me safe and healthy in return for some work on the farm and dissuading Fire Nation troops from attacking their village, even if unlikely. It’s small with little to gain from occupation. They simply offer passing soldiers meals to keep some peace between them. I considered traveling to the colonies, but it’s too far of a journey after being injured from battle. However, I am safe and happy here.”

“It has been a long time since I have spoken to you and I would like to extend my condolences to you for the loss of your son, your nephew , your father, and your throne. I am aware that life hasn’t treated you kindly even after everything you tried to bring into the world. I hope you find some light in your life even if in the strangest of places such as I have.”

“I hope that we will cross paths again one day, until then, I can only be with you the best and that one day I may see the Fire Nation again. Your obedient servant and friend, Lee.”

They both are silent for a long moment before Azula speaks again. “What is the seal?” She asks, glancing at the broken wax.

Iroh had really only looked to see if it was a lotus, not thinking of anything else. He had assumed that maybe it was from some Earth Kingdom general letting him know how much he is hated in the Earth Kingdom or something like that. He didn’t really think too much of it.

Iroh connects the two pieces together, squinting at it.

Azula takes it from him, her young eyes better than his. “It’s a turtle duck.” She says softly, looking at him with a torn expression. “What part of the Earth Kingdom has a turtle duck seal?” She asks, handing it back to him.

Iroh shakes his head. “None that I’m aware of.” He opens the letter again, scanning it. “Do you think ‘nephew’ is underlined or if it is just a stray mark?” He asks, looking at Azula pleadingly. He isn’t sure if he is begging her to tell him that he is a crazy old man and that he just wants Zuko to be alive so badly he’s seeing things or if he wants her to tell him that it’s Zuko. That Zuko is alive, safe, and happy in the Earth Kingdom with some farmers. Even just that Zuko is alive and safe. “I don’t know.” Azula whispers, touching the letter softly. “Can we…assume it is? If it is from Zuko and we ignore that…who knows what would happen. If it’s some kind of really messed up prank or something weird and we assume he’s alive…what’s the worst that could happen?” She asks, looking down.

Iroh smiles sadly, looking down. “Yeah…I like that idea. As far as we’re concerned, Zuko is okay.” Iroh whispers, taking his niece’s hand again. Zuko is alive. Even if it’s only in their minds, Zuko is alive.

“I’m sorry I can’t really teach you sword fighting anymore. You were starting to get the hang of the footwork.” Zuko apologizes, glancing at his leg, as he and Fao eat toasted pumpkin seeds removed from the vegetables when Fao and his mom had been preserving them for winter.

Fao just shrugs, smiling. “When we were looking for you I promised that I would give up sword fighting if you came back and you came back. I’m just glad you’re home.” Fao shoves a handful of seeds into his fourth mid sentence, spitting out chunks of chewed seed as he talks.

Zuko can’t help but giggle at the display, something that would have never been allowed back in the palace. The fact that Fao was willing to give up something he loved for Zuko to be here isn’t lost on him, he just isn’t sure how to respond. Even if it’s worded in a very simplistic manner, it’s one of the nicest things anyone has ever said to him.

Opposed to commenting on the sentiment that Fao has shown him, Zuko decides to comment on the fact his friend seems to think it’s appropriate to chew with his mouth open like that. “Gross.” He giggles, popping a seed into his mouth.

Eating has been getting easier. On bad days, he’ll need to meditate before eating or have some adjustment to it, but he only missed that one meal the first night Feya came. He hadn’t missed a meal for almost two weeks before Feya came.

Both Kani and Chen had told Zuko that he already looks so much healthier. Zuko has even noticed that his stomach doesn’t look as devastatingly hollow even if he can still see most of his ribs and that his cheekbones aren’t as hauntingly prominent. Even though he can’t walk now, he feels stronger even after putting on just a little bit of weight.

Despite that, Zuko is sure he couldn’t shove a fistful of food into his mouth without feeling sick not long after. It would probably also be hard to chew and worse to swallow. He’ll eat enough to put on a little more weight and get healthier, but he isn’t going to shove food in his face like that.

“You think that’s gross, try this.” Fao snickers, forcing air into his stomach before burping in Zuko’s face.

Laughing, Zuko shoves his friend away from him. “You’re disgusting, go away. Go home.” He teases, worried for only a second that Fao would actually get up and leave.

Instead, Fao just burps again. “You try it, Lee.” His friend laughs, grinning.

Zuko shakes his head. “No, it’s gross.” He giggles, eating a few more seeds.

Fao just sticks his tongue out at him before throwing a seed into the fire, watching it crackle. “Hey Lee, you said you’re from the Fire Nation…are you a firebender?” The other boy asks, face lighting up, grinning at Zuko.

Zuko hesitates for a moment, unsure if it would be the best idea to admit to that. However, he *has* been practicing making animals out of fire but hasn’t shown anyone yet and he kind of wants someone to see.

Cupping his hands, Zuko exhales, feeling heat swirl in his hands before opening them, presenting a lopsided turtle duck sitting in his hands made of flame.

Excitement shines in Fao’s eyes as he looks at the creature. “That’s so cool, Lee!” He exclaims, trying to feed the bird a pumpkin seed which just crackles a little, falling into Zuko’s cupped hands. “Why haven’t you shown more people this! We have a firebender to protect us if something goes wrong!” Optimism shining through everything, not understanding why Zuko has to keep this quiet. It would make Zuko’s life so much easier if everyone here would be just as supportive and enthusiastic about Zuko being a firebender.

“Kani and Chen don’t want me to…and they have a good point. They’re worried that someone who has been really hurt by the war and by firebenders might not care that I don’t want trouble. All it would take is one person not liking the fact I’m here to put me in a lot of danger. I’ve wanted to tell you for a while. You’re my best friend and I wanted you to know who I am.” Zuko admits, not adding that he had tried to run away because Kani and Chen didn’t want Zuko telling Fao.

“Who else knows?” Fao asks, “feeding” the turtle duck another seed and shoving a handful of them in his own mouth.

“Kani, Chen, Kani’s sister Feya, you, and your mom, Gela. Your mom just kind of figured it out when talking to Kani. I don’t know all the details, she just informed me.” Zuko explains, turning the turtle duck into the lizard snake that Chen had shown Zuko during his first few weeks here.

“Thank you for telling me. You’re my best friend, too.” Fao replies, moving closer to Zuko. Zuko puts out his little fire so that the two boys can hug each other.

Zuko isn’t sure how he got this lucky. Luck has never really been his thing. He was only lucky to be born, according to his father. The odds that he would have been stumbled upon by a man who was willing to take Zuko in and keep him safe, firebender or not, are slim to none. Somehow, Chen had found him. Somehow, Zuko has met people here who are kind to him and accept him for who he is, not caring about his element.

Before Zuko can pull away from the embrace, he feels a kiss pressed to his cheek.

Almost immediately after, Fao jumps up, blushing, grinning, and running towards the door. “I’ll see you tomorrow, Lee,'' he calls, rushing out before Zuko can say anything.

All Zuko can do is smile, blushing softly, touching his cheek with the tips of his fingers, waiting for Kani and Chen to come back inside.

“I think that we should talk to him today. It’s been enough time. I think he’ll understand that we don’t want him gone. If he were to ever find out we knew about an option like this for him and didn’t tell him, he might leave out of anger. You know he hates lying.” Chen argues, looking at his wife with a sad expression.

“Is it lying if we just don’t say anything?” She asks.

Chen knows that Kani has been worried that Lee will leave. That he’ll either feel like the option about going to the colonies is a nice way of Kani and Chen saying they don’t want him anymore or that Lee will want to be with people like him above anything else. Chen doesn’t want him to leave either, but it really doesn’t feel right keeping it from him.

They both feel this way, Kani is just more hesitant to bring it up. She has grown very attached to him and doesn’t want her child to leave. On top of that, she’s worried about not being able to make sure that Lee is being treated properly and looked after in the way that he needs.

Kani had always wanted to be a mother but it wasn’t something that seemed to be in the cards for them. They had tried to have children but it just never happened. It nearly broke Kani’s heart.

When Chen had brought Lee home, he hadn’t been surprised how the two had clung to each other.

Lee was a terrified little boy who just wanted his mother. Kani is caring and compassionate and whoever Lee’s mother is, the woman who must have made the kid feel loved and then left him, must have something like that as well. Lee would always see his own mother in Kani. The expression that would flash over Kani’s face when Lee would call Kani mom wasn’t lost on Chen. She had fallen in love with the little boy at first sight and sworn to protect him from the world.

Lee has come so far in the past few months. He isn’t as skittish, he’s expressing his needs and desires with more ease, he’s eating more and has even put on a little weight. The last time that Chen had embraced Lee, he had noticed that the kid’s ribs didn’t stick into his arms as much as they once did.

Chen has also begun to think of Lee has his own. He can’t even begin to imagine how painfully quiet and empty the house would be without the kid in it. How barren the fireplace would look without Lee’s mat and blankets, how he wouldn’t see lee occasionally trying to sneak the ridiculous chicken cat into the house so Cabbage would sleep him, and how he wouldn’t hear Lee and Fao laughing about something stupid that only young boys think is funny.

“Kani, obscuring the truth by omission is still lying.” Chen replies, taking Kani’s hand. “I know that you know that too. I don’t think that Lee will go. He has just had so little control over his life in the past and I think he needs some options.”

Kani just nods silently as they walk towards the house.

Before they can reach it, Fao rushes out, a grin on his beet red face. He waves to them before running around the house and racing back to his own.

Neither of them think much of it as they walk into the house. Lee is just sitting by the fire, smiling, nibbling on something, likely a seed.

“Hey, son, can we talk to you for a moment?” Chen asks, walking towards the boy. He can’t help but notice a guilty look on the kid’s face.

“You told Fao, didn’t you?” Kani asks, hands on her hips, a small smile on her face.

Lee looks down, shrugging. “He asked…I think he may have overheard something. I told him why it was important for him to not share that information with anyone. Figured it was safer.” He explains, not looking up.

Kani walks up to Zuko, sitting next to him and wrapping her arms around him. “Okay, love. We trust your decisions. Nothing that can be done now.” She says softly, kissing Zuko’s forehead.

“What do you want to talk about if it isn't that?” Lee asks, leaning against Kani.

The two look at each other briefly before Kani speaks. “Well, when the Fire Nation trio brought you back here, we had told them that you were feeling isolated from who you once were and your culture. Considering they are Fire Nation descendants living in the Earth Kingdom they would know better than anyone about how to stay true to themselves while living here. We were hoping that there were some traditions we could celebrate with you or foods we could make here, but they couldn’t really offer too much insight on that.”

Chen moves forward, taking Lee’s hand, needing the firebender to know that he is wanted here. That he is loved so much.

“Okay?” Lee seems confused at the relevance.

“They said that the reason they don’t feel isolated is because they are around people like them. That they can firebend and dress freely without worrying about being discovered. They suggested that when you’ve healed and the weather is better that we take you to the colonies. They’re living in Yu Dao. They would help you find a family who would take care of you and help you assimilate into the colony.” Chen continues, trying to meet Lee’s eyes.

“Are you telling me to leave?” Lee asks after a long silence, a sad note in his voice.

“No, love, no we aren’t.” Kani speaks before Chen can. “We would love to have you stay here. Have you feel like this is your home. Like we are your family. We don’t want to make you feel isolated. We don’t want you to be suffering because you don’t feel like you can be you. This choice is completely up to you. You don’t have to decide now. No matter what happens, this will always be your home. If you decide to leave for the colonies but want to come back a year later, you’re always welcome here. If you just want to stay, we’ll keep you safe. Okay?”

Lee is silent for a long time. “Do you *want* me to go?” He finally asks, looking up, tears welling in his eyes.

“Oh, son, no.” Chen brushes falling tears away gently with the thumb of his free hand. “We want you to stay here where we know that you’re safe and being taken care of properly. We also don’t want to make you feel like you owe us something or that you have to stay here. If you want to be with other firebenders and don’t need to feel like you have to hide, you should go. The last thing we want is to be the reason that you’re suffering. Sleep on it. You won’t be able to travel that far for a while.”

Lee leans his face closer to Chen’s hand, wanting to be closer. “Don’t need to, I wanna stay here.” He chokes out. “Don’t wanna go. Wanna stay.”

Chen can hear a soft laugh come from Kani as she squeezes Lee a little tighter. “That’s so good to hear. Thank you for wanting to stay. I was so worried that you wouldn’t stay. We both were.” Kani half cries, pressing kisses to Lee’s face.

“I’m sorry that we didn’t tell you sooner, love, we didn’t want to say anything right after you came home because we were worried you might think we were trying to throw you out after what had just happened. Then we figured that Feya being here might be hard for you and we didn’t want you to be thinking about two things considering you’ve improved a lot. We weren’t trying to keep things from you, we just wanted to wait for you to be in a good head space so you would understand it was just an option, not a request.” Kani explains, cupping Lee's face in her hands.

“We love you so much, Lee, and we want you to be happy. We want you to be safe. Even as things get difficult, please try and remember that. It’s so important that you do.” Chen adds, ruffling the firebender’s hair.

He can see a small grin on Lee’s face as the kid giggles a little. “I love you too. Anyways, I have to stay so Feya can take me to the theater.” His whole face lights up.

Chen doesn’t really appreciate that Feya had suggested Lee travel while he is injured during the winter, but it has given him incentive to take better care of himself. Feya had informed both Kani and Chen what she had promised Lee and almost immediately, Lee had gotten better at eating more at meals, staying off of his food, and sleeping better. So if that is what it takes to get through to the kid, so be it.

Anyways, Lee is so excited to go to the theater again, they can’t take that away. The very idea of going to a play makes him so happy, Chen isn’t going to be the one to deny his boy one of the things that the kid takes pure joy in.

“Yeah, but you need to continue taking care of yourself until I go see Feya, got it, love? If you’re too injured and can’t travel even on an ostrich horse, you won’t be able to go. Alright?” Kani asks, smiling at the firebender.

Lee nods enthusiastically. “I’ll do so well! I promise! I’ll get better, I wanna go!” Lee’s eyes practically shine with excitement, all fear of not being wanted anymore gone from his mind.

Chen can’t help but to smile at the little firebender in front of him. “I know, son, I know.” He isn’t sure how the stars had aligned for he and Kani to have Lee in their lives, and even the difficulties that it may present, he is sure their lives are better for it.

Lee just snuggles closer to Chen, butting his head underneath his chin.

Chen just rests a hand on the little boy’s arm, keeping him close. Keeping him safe. No one would take Lee from them.
