### Text

Zuko slowly finishes his bowl of soup to wash out the taste of the pickled vegetables. They aren’t bad, but he doesn’t like the taste that lingers all that much. Anyways, fruits and vegetables are limited now, it isn’t for taste, it’s for health. Apparently keeping a balanced diet, especially in hasher seasons, is critical to staying healthy.

“How are you feeling, my love?” Kani asks, resting a hand on Zuko’s back, smiling at him.

Zuko gives her a wide smile, nodding in acknowledgement to her question more than anything. He hopes at this point she can just pick up that he is doing well through body language. He is pretty sure that both she and Chen can.

It’s comforting to know that they can help him even if Zuko doesn’t realize he needs help when he is too wrapped up in his own mind. It’s also irritating and slightly intimidating that even if he wanted to he couldn’t really hide how he is feeling from them.

Winter is odd, especially with the chores changing. During the growing season, they would never be spending this much time inside. It’s only noon and Zuko and Kani only had to tend to the animals while Chen has collected more firewood to make sure they don’t run out. They aren’t in need of any right now, but apparently it will snow later in the season, something Zuko has never seen before.

It is apparently not only important but the neighborly thing to do to collect firewood everyday in smaller quantities opposed to every few days in larger sums. It leaves more fallen wood for families who may be running low and want to be able to keep their family warm and not need to travel too far from home incase of inclimate weather. Also, having enough in store is important for when it starts snowing because it is like solid rain but still wet. Zuko isn’t sure what that is supposed to mean and he is sure that neither Kani nor Chen are used to having to explain it to people. It’s just something they have always known. Zuko is the exception.

Apparently, later in the season groups of men from the village will go out hunting together. No one is facing a shortage of food yet and there is an understanding that if a family is in need, others will pitch in to help them make it through the winter months. However, things may change later in the season when times get harder. When it comes down to being able to feed your friends or watching your children go hungry.

Thankfully, it usually doesn’t come to that. Winter is usually bearable enough to at least keep most people in the village decently fed and alive even if not necessarily happy. If they live through the winter they can recover in the spring, that is what really matters, at least according to Kani.

Zuko has never seen a winter before, he can only trust the villagers know what they’re doing. He has to trust that Kani and Chen understand what is happening and will know better than him in terms of keeping people alive and relatively healthy.

“I was thinking after lunch, we could set up some curtains for you. It will probably help keep you warm as well as providing a little place of your own. If you start feeling claustrophobic for any reason, you don’t have to stay there, alright?” Kani moves a little closer to Zuko, squeezing him gently in her arms.

“Claustrophobic?” Zuko asks, slightly confused, not familiar with the word.

“It’s when someone is really scared of small spaces and when they’re trapped in one, or even feel like they’re trapped, it causes them to panic easily.” Kani explains calmly, pulling away from the embrace and just taking Zuko’s hand in hers. “You said that being in a small space makes you feel really scared. You’re claustrophobic. It isn’t an uncommon fear. Feeling like you’re trapped is always scary.”

Zuko looks up at her, meeting her kind, dark green eyes. “There’s a word for it?” He asks quietly, having been torn down about his growing fear of any closed door in any room by his father over and over again. The more he was scared, the more Zuko was locked away in that tiny, dark room. The more he was shut away from the world, sure every time that he would never see the light of day again, the more small and terrified of not just small spaces, but everything, he became. Sure his father would leave him to die there. “It’s…normal?” He continues, always having assumed he was just too weak to press forward and learn to get past his ever growing fear.

The look in Kani’s eyes is…devastating, she doesn’t even need to say anything, and she doesn't.

Instead, Chen speaks up. “Son, I understand if it’s a difficult subject to talk about and we don’t have to talk about it if you don’t want to. What your father did to you, everything he did to you, was absolutely horrible. I can’t imagine what you’ve been through, and we don’t expect you to fully move on from your past it, but we want to help you recover as best we can. Anyone who would be regularly locked away in the dark, especially as a child, would be terrified of ever even stepping into a dark room again.” The man says softly, resting a large hand on the table, offering Zuko a small smile.

Zuko just nods, feeling tears prick in his eyes, resting his head on Kani’s shoulder, clutching her hand tight.

“Sweetheart, you do know he abused you, right? That whatever he may have tried to get you to believe about him, he didn’t really love you. You don’t hurt the people that you love. Especially not with malicious intent.” Kani’s voice is tentative as she speaks, as if worried she might upset Zuko just by pointing out that his father was a monster.

It had taken Zuko awhile to accept, and he is still trying to accept it, that Ozai never even cared about him. All Zuko had ever wanted from that man, his own father, was his love. Zuko had starved, suffered, and bled for the man and was given nothing in return. Just his own fear and shame.

Part of him still wants to think that maybe if the Avatar was still alive, that if Zuko did capture him and bring him back, that his father would love him. That he might rest a hand on Zuko’s shoulder with no intention of harm and maybe even offer him a smile. Something Chen had done for him when they barely knew each other. When all Zuko had done for that man was take his wife away from him, accuse Chen of wanting to hurt or kill him, and try to burn him.

It makes Zuko feel angry, heartbroken, and defeated that in only a few moments, a strange Earth Kingdom man had been more of a father to Zuko than the one who was supposed to be. Chen had shown Zuko kindness and appreciation just because Zuko existed, not because he actually did anything.

He isn’t sure what he feels towards his father. He knows that part of him still wants his fathers approval, but he also never wants to even see the man again. Better yet, he would never have to *think* about Ozai again.

Unfortunately, it seems like only the former is an option, he can’t keep his father out of his head for long. However, in the middle of an Earth Kingdom village that likely only exists on local maps, his father will never touch him again. He’s safe here.

Shrugging, Zuko looks at Kani, unsure how to respond to Kani’s question. “I know he wasn’t good to me…that what he did was wrong, well part of me does, part of me thinks I deserve it. Please, I don’t want to talk about it. I know you’ll tell me I didn’t deserve it and I just don’t want to talk about it. What I do know is that I like being here, you guys make me feel safe. Make me feel valuable and loved. I know you’ll keep me safe.”

Kani presses her lips against Zuko’s head, nuzzling him gently. “Lee, what you’ve been through takes years to undo. We don’t expect you to be better just because you know we won’t hurt you. You’ve only really recently begun to feel completely safe and accepted in your new home. You’ve just been given a change to rest and learn to trust and be yourself again. You haven’t really gotten a chance to heal. These kinds of things take time. Anyways, when we visit Feya, I’m hoping you’ll be willing to talk to the herbalist. She’s seen just about everything. She might be able to give you some advice on how to proceed with your life.”

Zuko nods, smiling at her again. “I’d like that.” He says softly, squeezing her hand again. “I also want you to know that Fao thinks of you as my mom…and I kinda think of you as that too.” He adds quickly, having wanted to say it for a while but never having a chance to. There isn’t really a natural way to integrate that into a conversation. He just wants her to know how safe she makes him feel.

Growing up, Zuko’s mother was his safe haven. Everything about his life was nearly unbearable, but his mother made it better. She would hold him, tell him stories, make him feel like he could actually be valuable past what he could do. Made him feel like he could be valued as a person.

When Zuko wasn’t sure what his life was becoming, Kani had become his safe haven. Despite the fact it was Chen who had saved him and advocated for him to stay, Zuko had almost instinctively clung to Kani. It had taken him so long to even be able to bring himself to give Chen a real chance.

Before Kani can say anything in response to that, only able to look at him with a mix of surprise and joy, Zuko turns to Chen, resting his small hand on the farmer's large one. “Chen, you showed me more compassion in the first ten minutes you knew me than my father did in the first thirteen years of my life. You’ve been more of a father to me than he ever could be…thank you. I just want you to know how grateful I am for what you’ve done for me. How you just make me feel safe. Thank you…sorry.” He says, smiling a little, looking at the ground.

Zuko isn’t sure if the time that Ozai spent sitting next to Zuko, rubbing his back in comfort counted as compassion. His father had locked him away for days, set Zuko up for failure, and then locked him away again. The fact that Zuko had wound up with broken bones and horrible burns in less than an hour, all self inflicted from unhinged terror, is because his father didn’t care about him. He isn’t sure if that precious and cured night was compassionate or simply guilt fueled. Even if it was guilt, it was the most human emotion his father had ever shown. Even if it does count as an hour of compassion from his father, Zuko doesn’t want it to. It was brought from Zuko’s own pain and terror.

Kani just squeezes him in response, pressing kisses to his face, taking Zuko’s mind away from his father’s cruelty. “That’s right, you’re our little boy now whether you like it or not.”

Zuko can’t help but to giggle as Kani practically smothers him with affection. He snuggles up closer to her as she continues pressing kisses to his head and holding him close.

Chen had mentioned that he and Kani had always wanted children but it had just never been able to happen. He had just kind of assumed that Chen was just saying that. That the man may be worried that Zuko might feel more like a burden than anything and try to run. The interaction now makes Zuko feel more confident that it was a genuine sentiment and not a way to try and make Zuko feel more wanted in his new home.

“Kani, you’re going to suffocate him.” Chen laughs, standing and walking towards the two. “Let’s go get you set up, son.” He ruffles Zuko’s hair as he talks before walking into the storage room.

By the time that Kani helps Zuko off of the ground and the two begin to walk towards the fireplace, Chen is walking out with heavy red cloth in his arms. Zuko can feel himself grinning at the color the farmers had chosen, unsure where they would have gotten it but not really caring. He just feels excitement bubbling up in his stomach. If it wasn’t for the promise of theater, as long as Zuko stayed off his leg, he would run over and throw his arms around Chen.

Instead, he just uses his words. “Thank you!” He yells a little too loud, unsure if it was the best idea for the farmers to be hanging red curtains in their home during the war but really just excited that they want him to feel at home more than anything else.

After Zuko had tried to flee a few weeks ago, feeling like he was some shameful secret, Kani and Chen had done their best to make Zuko feel loved and wanted. They had done as many little things to remind Zuko of home. To make him feel like his home is here now and not just where he is hiding for now.

“We thought you might like them, love.” Kani squeezes him again, keeping him close.

Zuko nods. “I really, really do. Thank you.”

“Come on, son, let’s get these up.”

The trio spends the next half hour getting the curtains up. Well, more Kani encasing the top in rock so it would stay in the ceiling and Chen and Zuko trying to help the best they could and stay out of her way. Zuko can’t really stand right now and both men are shorter than Kani. They can’t offer much help but still feel bad walking away as she sets it up.

When she finishes that, Chen helps move Zuko’s mat, blankets, and bag into the space, not wanting Zuko to do it, worrying he would hurt himself more.

“Can Cabbage sleep with me tonight?” Zuko asks as he climbs into the new space, grinning as he snuggles into the blanket despite having no intentions to sleep right now. He just wants to be able to know what it would be like to sleep here right now. Not having the patience to wait until nightfall.

Chen sighs, pinching the bridge of his nose. “You really love that ridiculous little creature, don’t you?” He asks, sitting next to Zuko, taking his hand.

Zuko smiles, nodding. “She’s soft and snuggly. I love her.” He replies. Cabbage will usually snuggle up under his chin or between his arm and side, purring loudly. She loves him no matter what he is going through as long as he snuggles and pets her. It’s impossible not to love her. She’s so soft, gentle, and loving no matter what is going on in Zuko’s life. He can count on the feathery creature to be there for him when he needs her. She is sort of taking the place of turtle ducks in Zuko’s life now, except she can sleep with him. The turtle ducks wouldn’t want to sleep with him, Zuko wouldn’t be allowed to bring them in, and their feet and beaks aren’t the most comfortable things to snuggle with.

Chen rolls his eyes, shaking his head and smiling. “Fine, cabbage can sleep with you. I assume I couldn’t stop you anyways. I won’t separate you from the stupid chicken cat.” He ruffles Zuko’s hair again, smiling.

Zuko flings his arms around the man, smiling. “Thank you.” He mumbles into Chen’s shoulder, tempted to call the man ‘dad’ but restrains himself from doing so, just snuggling closer to him.

Things were falling apart only a few weeks ago, now, everything is really feeling okay. He really feels like he is going to be okay. He’s safe, and according to Kani, a lot of his fears are somewhat normal and have the potential to be tamed with time. More importantly, he actually feels happy. He finally feels like he can heal in safety and not fear only being harmed further by those who promised to heal and protect him. By those where were supposed to but never had any intention of doing so.

Happiness had come and gone in Zuko’s life before, but never like this.

Back in the Fire Nation, he was happy when he was snuggled up against his mother’s side as they would feed the turtle ducks. He was happy when she would read to him, tell him stories, or sing him songs as he would drift off to sleep. He was happy when he could spend long days with her anywhere, especially if it was a day where he wouldn’t need to train with his father at all. When he could just be free from scrutiny and cruelty for even a little.

After she disappeared, Zuko found happiness with his uncle. When they would play a game of Pai Sho together. Zuko would pretend to like the game and the tea Iroh made for him more than he actually did. He was very happy when his uncle would get him out from behind the palace walls and take him into the city, or even better, on a trip disguised as training. He is sure that his father only allowed it so that Ozai could focus more attention on Azula for a few days, not caring if Iroh corrupted Zuko. He is sure that his father was only waiting for an excuse to get rid of him and finally found it in the war room. If Iroh corrupted Zuko along the way to being thrown out anyways, it would make no difference to that wretched man. All he cared about was strength and power, something Zuko didn’t have enough of. Something Zuko had so little of, Ozai didn’t even see a reason to keep his own son alive.

Despite happiness back in his homeland, there was always dreaded fear hanging over it. There would be brief moments when he would forget about it, but most of the time, terror would be looming just in the edge of his sight. It would only be so long before the harsh reality of his existence came crashing down on him again. When his father made Zuko suffer for the crime of being born. Something Zuko had begun to regret as well, despite having no say in it, as he got older.

This feeling in the Earth Kingdom is different. There isn’t any dread for when this moment will be ruined. He’s aware that something could go wrong that could ruin his day or his week, but Kani and Chen would help him feel better from whatever happened. He wouldn’t have to suffer through the actual issue and then be punished for suffering and being a person with feelings on top of that by his father. Neither Kani nor Chen would punish Zuko just for genuinely feeling whatever is bothering him. He has learned that as long as he at least tries to work with them on solutions or try and help them understand what is wrong, they won’t be upset with him. They won’t take any steps to worsen his suffering like Ozai would have without even a moment’s notice.

If something went wrong now, he would be okay, he would be able to work it out. He wouldn’t just be thrown into a new problem before he could even recover from the last. He can actually breathe now. He feels genuinely happy. He has the capacity to feel it to its full extent, not being crushed and forced to fit into a small space crammed between fear and pain.

Zuko had no idea that the people he grew up around were just cruel. Well, he had known that, but he just assumed that leaders and parents, especially fathers, tended to be cruel. That it was a necessity to push their children and soldiers to greater strengths, unlocking their fullest potential.

Zuko was well aware that so many of the noble families were like that, so many of the war leaders were as well. It only made sense that his own father, someone of royal blood, would need to press even further. Needing his family to meet greater strengths. Needing his children to be what the Fire Nation looked up to and strived to model their children after. That he had a precedent to set.

He knew that his mother was seen as weak in the eyes of his father and grandfather. Considering Azulon didn’t seem to be her biggest fan, Zuko never understood why the man had arranged for her and Ozai to marry. It was never a question Zuko pressed with. He figured he wouldn’t like the answer and it would only make him and his mother feel more miserable and trapped in their lives. He knew that many saw his uncle Iroh as an odd man who never quite followed tradition. He had thought that they were the exceptions to that rule. The rule that strength comes from pushing hard until children and soldiers feared failure more than injury or even death.

Zuko certainly felt that way. There were even times in his life, the lowest points in his life, when he considered taking his own life before his father could realize that Zuko failed at something else. Before Zuko could fail at yet another impossible task that would be out for him, only to be punished later.

Zuko had thought that he was just weak for not being able to reach the expectations set for him, unable to think of another reason why what his father put him through broke him down. So many others seemed to be able to get through harsh treatment. His sister had been able to get stronger despite the pressure, Zuko had only gotten weaker.

Zuko had never even considered that soldiers trained hard during the day were able to go home to a kind, loving family. If they weren’t going home, they would at least have their friends. They would be able to make light of the situations that they were put in while recovering for the next day. It wasn’t something constant, they had support systems for themselves and their friends.

On top of that, they *chose* to be in the military. They were adults who had grown up with a family who had cared about them. Where they may have been pushed hard by their parents, they were actually loved and valued, not tossed away and torn down like they were nothing. They were given a chance to get on their feet before learning to fight. Zuko had just been beaten into a corner from birth and is just learning how to stand.

He snuggles a little close to Chen, clutching his clothes tighter. “Thank you.” Zuko mumbles. “For everything.”

If Chen hadn’t found him, or hadn’t been a compassionate enough man to take Zuko in, he wouldn’t have made it. Chen could have also taken Zuko in until the storm passed and then had him dragged off to the nearest prison to be interrogated for information Zuko wouldn’t know. Everything could be different right now if Zuko hadn’t been stumbled across by someone so understanding and compassionate. By someone who just saw a scared child who needed help, not an enemy firebender.

“You’re welcome, son. I’m so glad you’re here, now. That you’re safe.” Chen replies as if he could understand the thoughts going through Zuko’s head. As if he knew what Zuko was really thanking him for.

Zuko just smiles softly in response. Things are really going to be better. He knows it.

“Please, Kani, can I go? I’ve stayed off my leg, I’ve been eating more, and I’ve been resting. I promise I’ll rest when we’re there, I just *really* want to go.” Zuko pleads, taking Kani’s hand, meeting her green eyes with his wide, pleading, gold ones.

Kani sighs, resting a hand on his shoulder and kneeling down so that they are closer to the same level. “Lee, I know you want to go see the play, and I won’t bar you from coming with me, but I’m not worried about you hurting your leg more while traveling.” She begins to explain.

Zuko cocks his head, not fully understanding that, sure that that was the main reason that she doesn’t want him to come with her into town. She and Chen have been constantly reminding him to be careful of his leg so that it heals properly and he can strengthen it before spring after the bone and tendons heal.

“It’s getting cold, really cold,” She continues. “I know that you’ve been eating more and you’ve gained some weight but you’re still very skinny and this is your first winter. I’m worried that you’ll get sick if you’re out in the cold for as long as you will be tomorrow when we travel.” There is a sad look in Kani’s eyes as she says this, cupping Zuko’s face in her hand.

“On top of that, I want you to know that I am well aware that the main reason you want to go is because of the theater. It’s just kind of a community theater that is used to gather people during hard times, have some entertainment, but it is mostly just to keep warm and share good company and food. The play isn’t really the main purpose of this. Just so you know, it’s decent at best. I don’t want you to risk traveling in these conditions just to be disappointed.”

Zuko shrugs, not caring if the play is far worse than the ember island players. “I wanna see Feya, and I don’t care if the play is bad…just wanna go. The plays me and my mom went to were bad, she just wanted to see the theater again and I wanted to be with her.” He explains, looking down. He wishes that his mom was here. He wishes he could talk to her for even a minute. He wants to know if she’s alive. Wants to know why she left him. Even if the answer hurts him, he *needs* to know why. He doesn’t need an apology or for her to even feel bad about leaving Zuko with the cruelest man to ever walk the face of the earth, he just needs to know why she left him with that man. He needs to know what he had finally done to let her know that he wasn’t worth protecting.

“Okay, love, you can come with me, but you better get a good night’s sleep tonight, eat your meals, and take care of yourself while we’re in town, alright?” Kani resigns, shaking her head in defeat, smiling a little.

“Son, make sure you let Fao know that you’re leaving. You two have been attached to the hip sense you met, I don’t want him following me around asking me why you aren’t here. He has been very upset in the past when I have told him that you aren’t feeling well and can’t play. He’s your friend, you gotta deal with him.” Chen teases, ruffling Zuko’s hair affectionately.

Zuko smiles, nodding, feeling warm at the fact that Fao would actively miss him. That he knows there are people here who value his presence and are saddened by his absence.

“Oh, Lee, one more thing,” Chen adds, reaching up to grab something on a shelf in the kitchen, handing a small, familiar bag to him. “You can get him something, or something for yourself, it’s your money.” Chen reminds him as Zuko remembers begging the man to take the bag of coins months ago when Chen had offered to get Zuko some tea. “I was worried if I gave this back to you too soon you would feel like it might be some sort of rejection. If you want to use it to help Kani and I buy things from the market, you can, if you don’t, then don’t, we make most of what we have anyways. I trust that you’re doing better now in terms of feeling like you belong here. I would just like there to be more transparency between us, okay, son?” Chen asks softly, smiling warmly at Zuko.

Zuko awkwardly moves forward, wrapping his arms around the man’s waist. “Thank you.” He mumbles into Chen’s chest, relaxing as he feels the farmer’s large, gentle hands rub his back.

“Son, you don’t have to thank us just for giving you back what’s yours and treating you right.” The man says softly as he pulls out of the embrace, resting a hand on Zuko’s head again. “Just remember how loved you are. That you’re safe here with us. We won’t ever let anyone hurt you like your father did to you before.” He promises.

Zuko nods again. “I love you…I’m going to go see Fao.” He replies, setting the bag of coins down on the counter, unsure where else to put them before resituating himself on his crutches and leaves the house heading towards Fao’s house.

When he gets there, he knocks on the door, wishing he had actually put on a jacket opposed to trying to prove to Kani that he could make it in the cold and just go out in what he was already wearing. Pride means nothing if he is cold.

If Zuko hadn’t started practicing on using his inner flame to keep himself warm after almost dying in that storm, he would likely be shivering by now as opposed to just being a bit chilly. Unfortunately, it takes a little bit to actually start working and he doesn’t start warming up until he is almost at Fao’s anyways.

Despite the inconvenience of crutches, he is somewhat grateful for the extra support that they are giving him. It would be easier if he could use both of his feet *and* the crutches to keep himself upright. Unfortunately, if Kani saw him standing, she might not let him go into town with her at all. If he didn’t go into town, he wouldn’t get to see Feya or the play. He doesn’t care if the play isn’t good, he just wants to go to the theater again. It could be the worst play that he has ever seen and he would be happy.

Almost more importantly, Zuko wants the chance to talk openly about who he is again. He also somewhat hopes that Kani just kind of finds out on her own and confronts Zuko about his identity. It would make it so much easier. He would get to be his most authentic self without needing to work up the courage to confess his identity to Kani and Chen.

He isn’t proud to be the Fire Lord’s son, but he doesn't want to have to be ashamed of it either. He would like to be able to just treat it as a fact. For it to give more context as to how and why his father was so horrible to Zuko while growing up. He could give a better explanation about his life, his mother, hsi family, and his trauma. It could help Kani and Chen understand him better. Zuko just can’t bring himself to say anything to them. Maybe he can talk to Feya about it. She might know what to do.

Gela is the one who opens the door, giving Zuko a warm smile, dark green eyes shining. “Lee, come in,” She offers, opening the door wider for him to come in.

Before he can even fully get in the house fully, Fao pracally tackles Zuko in an embrace, almost knocking him to the ground.

“Fao, be careful, you’re going to injure him again.” Gela scolds, helping Zuko into the house and closing the door behind him, giving Fao an annoyed look.

Zuko is glad that he has had time to get to know Gela and Fao personally over the past few months and has been taken care of by Kani and Chen. Only a few months ago, that interaction may have sent terror shooting down Zuko’s spine as to what Gela might do to Fao the moment Zuko was gone. The moment the woman had her son alone.

Now, he knows that the scolding would only go as far as he just witnessed. She was simply reminding her overexcited son that Zuko wasn’t in the best physical condition right now and that Fao needs to be gentle with him.

However, Fao just squeezes Zuko tighter, grinning.

Zuko never fails to look over the fact that despite Fao being about a year younger than himself, the other boy is taller than him. It’s likely why Kani and Chen are always so worried about Zuko’s weight, something his own father had never even cared about. All Ozai cared about was making sure Zuko knew that he was a disappointment. That he didn’t deserve what he needed to survive. That he doesn’t deserve to live.

Even if it does get annoying at some points, he knows that they’re just worried about him getting up to a healthy weight so that he won’t be as susceptible to illness and can actually grow more while he still has the chance. It’s just because they care about him and want him to be okay. It’s all from a source of love and concern. His father would just tear Zuko down about everything just because he could.

At least that’s how it felt. It might have been what was really happening. Zuko has no way to know for sure what was going through that man’s mind. If he’s lucky, he’ll never have the chance to ask.

“Lee! Can you show Ma the turtle duck?” Fao is bouncing on his toes with excitement as he talks, grinning widely.

Zuko leans up against the wall for extra support so that he can take his hands off of his crutches, cupping his hand, and channeling the fire into his cupped hands into the shape of a turtle duck sitting in his cupped palms. If it were an actual turtle duck, he would lean down and kiss it’s head, watching it snuggle down into his cupped hands, cheeping with contentment.

Gela smiles at him even as Zuko puts out the fire, not wanting the others to walk in and see that he is a firebender. He isn’t sure how they would react. He wants to have more control over the situation than them just finding out by happenstance. He wants to be ready for more people to know. That isn’t now. Not quite yet.

“Where did you learn how to do that?” She asks, resting a hand on both boys’ shoulders.

“Taught myself. Been practicing the past few months when trying to build up control opposed to just strength.” He explains, not really knowing that was why until saying it.

“Well, it’s beautiful. Maybe you can teach someone else at some point.”

“Thank you, ma’am.” Zuko replies, unsure what else to say.

Fao grabs Zuko’s arm before Zuko or Gela can continue speaking. “Lee, I wanna show you my room!” Zuko realizes that he has never really been in Fao’s house before besides just being on the porch when visiting along with Kani and Chen. Fao had always come to Zuko or they had met in the woods.

Kani had said something when Zuko first started to get to know Fao about wanting to do it on familiar or neutral territory so that Zuko could have more control over the situation. So that he wouldn’t need to navigate an area where someone else was in control on top of meeting someone new. He had felt out of place for a long time and didn’t want to give up that control, even if subconsciously, until he felt a sense of belonging. Something he had only recently really begun to feel when Kani and Chen had accepted Zuko back into their home after he tried to run away and no longer pressed for Zuko to hide his identity. No longer made him feel like some shameful secret.

He is sure that Feya knowing exactly who he is helped a lot with that as well. Her knowledge of his identity yet immediate acceptance and understanding was what he really needed to truly settle. The conformation that Zuko’s identity and family history isn’t something to inherently be ashamed of.

Luckily, Fao realizes that Zuko can’t follow him while he is holding onto Zuko's arm before Fao accidentally yanks him to the ground.

Zuko follows him quickly to a small room with a bed in the far corner, thick carpets on the ground, a window above the bed, and shelves filled with books and toys lining the limited space on the walls.

Fao begins to close the door behind the two but Zuko gently stops the door with his hand. “Can we not close it? Just…I’ve been locked up before. Not many good memories.” He offers, wanting to be honest but not wanting to open up too much for a possible conversation about it. He just wants his friend to understand but he doesn’t want to discuss it. Not yet, at least.

Thankfully, Fao hugs him instead of pressing into Zuko’s past. “I’m sorry, Zuko.” He says softly as Zuko rests his forehead on his friend’s shoulder. “Also, I’m sorry about the other day, I was just really excited about you telling me about being a firebender. Best friends?” He asks, touching Zuko’s cheek with his finger for clarification as to what he meant.

Zuko just smiles, not looking up. “Best friends.” He repeats, feeling a little sad about the just friends bit, but relieved at the fact that their friendship won’t be complicated. For the most part, he still just feels happy when he is around Fao. He’s happy that for the first time in his life, he really has a friend who he can spend time with and just be happy around while being himself.

For a few hours, the two play together in Fao’s room. Fao shows Zuko books that he has collected with intricate drawings, paintings that he and others have created, and toys that he has received and made over the years.

As they play, Zuko tells Fao about how he is going into town and will be gone for about two weeks. This makes Fao a little sad until Zuko promises to bring his friend back some candy or something he can find. That cheers Fao up almost immediately.

Zuko tells Fao about how Feya is going to take him to see a play. He knows that it isn’t necessarily good, but he wants to go. He wants to be reminded of his mom. He tells his friend how his mother was once an actress and had to give it up due to her arranged marriage.

He tells Fao about how he wants to see his mom again. How much he misses her even if it’s been years since he last saw her. Zuko doesn’t tell him about how even if the details of her face are beginning to fade with the erosion of the sands of time. All he can really remember are her bright, gold eyes despite being a nonbender. A rare feature, at least in the Fire Nation. The only nation where it is common for nonbenders and benders to share eye color is in the Water Tribes.

Zuko has never seen a tribesman in person, but he knows that they all have distinct blue eyes against dark skin and dark brown hair. That all of them stand taller than most people in any other nation, built to withstand the harshest conditions in the poles and fight the large polar fauna that live there for food.

What he has been told about them is that they are a people built on savagery, especially the Southern Water Tribe after being stripped of all of their benders, and with it, most of their history, culture, and infrastructure.

Zuko can imagine that the people there might be used to being more aggressive out of need for survival, but he has no idea if savage would be the appropriate word. They probably need a certain amount of hostility for survival, but maybe around their friends and family, they’re nice.

After finding out so much that he had learned to believe about the world is false, he has no idea what to believe anymore. Even if the tribesmen live in tents and igloos, eat with their hands, and hunt with bone weapons, that doesn’t make them any more savage than the Fire Nation. Just because Zuko had grown up in a country with beautiful buildings and clothes, culture that hadn’t been taken, and fought with weapons of steel, that didn’t make them any more civilized.

A savage act is burning your thirteen year old son for speaking out of turn and then sending him off into the world to die, not caring what becomes of him. Only a savage would try to usurp their own brother’s throne when he had just lost his only son and was in mourning. Savagery is sending your own soldiers into a death trap just to exhaust an enemy troop before slaughtering them mercilessly, not caring who gets caught in the crossfire.

Just because the Fire Nation dresses well, has well crafted weapons, and more diverse roles for people to partake in doesn’t make them civilized. The Fire Nation is the worst of them all. Zuko would love to be given the opportunity to help fix any of it. Even if just a little.

Eventually, Zuko wraps his arms around Fao, explaining that he and Kani need to get an early start in case they run into any holdups along the way. He doesn’t add that Kani is mostly adamant about getting Zuko into town before sunset, worried what the night air might do to Zuko. She doesn’t care that Zuko can regulate his body temperature pretty well, she wants to make sure that he is somewhere safe when night comes.

He gets up, thanking Fao and Gela for letting him come over, implying his gratitude for allowing him to be himself with them. For accepting him as a firebender despite everything. For just letting him be a child for the first time in his life. Something even the Fire Lord wouldn’t grant him.

Everything here seems so much better than it was at home. He isn’t sure if it is because the Earth Kingdom is simply better than the Fire Nation or because here Zuko isn’t being scrutinized by the highest authority figure in the nation, if not the world. Here, all he needs to do is show up and he is appreciated. He is loved and taken care of simply because he exists.

He can’t help but wonder if other families are like this in the Fire Nation or if this kind of dynamic is exclusive to the Earth Kingdom. He has only ever experienced small parts of the Fire Nation and Earth Kingdom and only has heard stories about the Water Tribes, so he has nothing to really base his world view on besides a few experiences and lifestyles.

Despite that, Zuko knows that he likes this better. Here, he is safe and loved. That’s what really matters.

When he gets back home, he sneaks Cabbage into the house, knowing that it will be the last time he will see the little creature for a few weeks and snuggles into his bed now hidden behind the red curtains.

Zuko curls up and helps Cabbage snuggle up to his stomach, listening to the little creature purr against him. He has the theater and Feya on his mind, the knowledge that he has a friend who loves him no matter what, and a family that will love and take care of him as best they can. A family that will love him with his strengths and faults all together, praising him for his attributes and helping him overcome, or at least learn to live with, his fears as opposed to scorning him for them and simply labeling them as weaknesses. They are just a part of who he is.

Sleep comes easy with the warmth of the fire moving in through the thick curtains, Cabbage snuggling up against his stomach, and his blankets wrapped around him, keeping his warmth close to him opposed to allowing it to dissipate into the cold room surrounding him.

The thoughts of hot noodle soup cooking over a fire while talking to Feya fill his mind. He might be able to write another letter to his uncle while staying there. Even if they never see each other again, Zuko would like to at least give the old man hope that Zuko is alive and being taken care of by good, kind people. That they are taking care of his needs and making sure that he feels loved and protected despite everything that is going on in the world and the terrors that Zuko has faced throughout his life. He at least needs his uncle to not feel like he has any responsibility for Zuko’s untimely death. At least Iroh might be able to think of it as allowing Zuko the opportunity to live a new life where he can be himself. Where he can be happy, safe, and free. A life he would never have been able to dream of within the palace walls.

Zuko is well aware that Iroh isn’t the reason that he got burned and banished by Ozai and he doesn’t blame him for that. What he is worried about is that Iroh might blame himself, thinking that if he hadn’t allowed Zuko into the war room, none of this would have happened.

Hopefully, his ever perceptive uncle might know and understand that Ozai would have gotten rid of Zuko one way or another for some reason. It would only be a matter of time until he got sick of trying to find a reason and simply forced Zuko into a situation where he would be forced to act in a way that would be unbecoming of the heir to the throne.

This way is better. This way, Zuko has a reminder on his face that his father never loved him and is incapable of ever loving him. He is far less likely to go back to that man, all he has to do is see his own face and have proof that Ozai knows nothing but cruelty.

On top of that. Zuko has been shown what it feels like to be loved without the constant pressure of fear weighing on his chest. He isn’t worried about being beaten or cast away for making mistakes. He has a mother, father, aunt, and friend who love him just the way that he is, flaws and all. All of the dirty secrets that have come up with time have been brushed off as just another part of Zuko’s life.

All Zuko can do is smile softly as he snuggles into his bed. No matter what, he has a promise of love and safety from the people around him. All he can do now is make sure that his uncle knows that his nephew is safe and cared for. As long as his uncle at least knows, maybe he can feel better about what happened. He can know that in the long run, it was what was best for Zuko’s life and wellbeing.

Maybe, with no longer needing to worry about or mourn for Zuko, Iroh can move onto Azula. There is nothing that Iroh can do for Zuko now that kind people aren’t already doing for him. Who doesn't have protection is his sister. His prodigy sister who is now the only focus of Ozai. The child who needs to fulfill all expectations without a second, disposable child to project anger onto.

The last thought that Zuko has in his mind before drifting off into sleep is what would become of Azula.

### Text

The morning that they leave, all three of them get up early. Kani is serious about only wanting to travel when the sun is out for Zuko’s safety. Zuko isn’t sure if she doesn’t believe him about being able to regulate his temperature well enough now after a few months of practice or if she doesn’t care. Either way, she isn’t risking Zuko getting sick in the cold. He isn’t sure if he is more annoyed at the fact she isn’t letting him take care of himself or grateful that she is insisting to keep him healthy.

Chen makes breakfast as Kani makes sure that she and Zuko have everything they need packed away neatly in bags that will fit comfortably on the ostrich horse’s back.

As she does this, Zuko stands next to Chen, resting his head to the side of the man’s chest as he cooks. Even though Zuko knows that he’ll see Chen again in just two weeks, Zuko is going to miss him.

If it wasn’t for Chen, Zuko wouldn’t be here right now. If the man hadn’t been as selfless as he is every day for the past several months, Zuko doubts he would still be able to live here. Maybe they would be kind enough to let him stay in the barn for his first winter, but they wouldn’t be treating Zuko like their own son. Not taking such good care of him and loving him as much as they are now. Zuko could never fully express his gratitude.

“Chen?” Zuko asks softly, trying to get the man’s attention, leaning closer.

“Do you need something, son?” Chen asks, resting a hand on Zuko’s head, smiling down at him.

Zuko shakes his head. “I love you.” He mumbles. “I’m gonna miss you.” Even if it will only be for two weeks, Zuko will miss Chen a lot. He’s gotten really used to the man’s easy, consistent presence in his life. He won’t like having that gone even for just a little bit. Chen calms him with his even, predictable voice and movements. With his gentle hands and even more gentle worlds guiding Zuko though his new life.

Setting down the mixing spoon, Chen kneels down, meeting Zuko’s eyes, smiling at him. “I’m going to miss you too, Lee, but I’ll be right here when you get back. You’re going to have a lot of fun with Feya, you’re going to see a play, maybe meet some other kids to play with until you come back here. You can also write another letter to your uncle while you’re there, to convince him that you’re alive and well.” Chen presses a kiss to Zuko’s forehead.

Zuko grins at the thought of his uncle. He can imagine how the old man might weep over the letter when realizing that Lee is Zuko. That his nephew is safe, loved, and healthy in the Earth Kingdom. That Ozai can never touch him again.

“Hey, Lee, I know you’re excited and you’re feeling more confident, but be careful. Don’t mess around on your way into town today. I don’t want you to get caught in a storm or just be exposed for too long and get sick. I also don’t want anyone randomly to find out that you’re a firebender. I don’t want anyone hurting you for any reason, especially not for just being you. I love you, Zuko, and I don’t want anything to happen to you.” Chen whispers the name softly so that Kani can’t hear.

It’s nice to hear his name again. It isn’t safe to go by, but he likes hearing it from someone saying it with love. How Chen is saying it. The man might not know who Zuko is, but he has Zuko’s real name, and for right now, that feels like enough.

“I’ll be careful, Chen. I wanna come home.” Zuko promises, wrapping his arms around Chen’s neck. “I love you.”

“I love you too. Be good. Be safe. Come home.” Chen instructs, ruffling Zuko’s hair before standing up and finishing up breakfast, pouring it into three bowls, and carrying it to the table.

Zuko sits down next to Chen, hugging his large arm, both waiting to eat until Kani joins them. Zuko just wants to spend a little more time with Chen before he goes.

When Zuko first arrived, he had tried his best to avoid the man at all costs. Now, he doesn’t want to leave the man’s side even though he knows it’s only for a few weeks and that he’ll love being in town. Anyways, he promised Fao he would bring back candy. He has to go. Zuko can’t wait to be able to hide in Fao’s fort, sucking on hard candies of various flavors.

The rasberry and butterscotch had been Zuko’s favorite of what Chen had brought back. He hopes that Fao likes other flavors best so that both boys can have the most of their favorites.

Even if Fao has the same taste as Zuko, all of the flavors are delicious. He just wants something to share with his friend.

It only takes a few minutes for Kani to join them, sitting down, smiling at how Zuko is snuggled up against Chen’s side before beginning to eat.

Instead of eating his breakfast on the table, Zuko puts his bowl in his lap, not wanting to move away from Chen. it's just hitting him now how much he is going to miss the farmer. How much he doesn’t want to be separated from his family for any amount of time.

“Love, you don’t have to come if you don’t want to. Don’t come just because you think it’s what Feya or I want. What we want is for you to be happy. You can stay here with Fao, Chen, and Cabbage if you want.” Kani offers a few minutes into breakfast, smiling at Zuko.

Zuko shakes his head. “I wanna go…just gonna miss home. Hard remembering people are still gonna be here when I get back. That they’re gonna come back.” Zuko admits although he’s sure both farmers know after what Zuko has told them about his mother.

Kani gives him a sad look and Chen wraps an arm around Zuko’s shoulders. “It's not like it was. You’re home now. You’re safe. We won’t leave you.” Chen promises.

Zuko nods, pressing closer to Chen, relaxing a little. “I trust you.” He whispers, meaning it. If there is anyone in this world that he completely and fully trusts, it’s Kani and Chen.

By the look on the man’s face, Zuko’s declaration of trust had meant more to him than his one of love.

Kani had been concerned at first with how clingy Lee had been around Chen this morning. She was worried that somehow someone had accidentally pressured her little boy into doing something he didn’t want to and didn’t feel like he could speak up about it. She was worried that maybe she had done something wrong considering up until this point Lee had almost always clung to her when he had the opportunity to choose.

It wasn’t jealousy that made her worry about Lee clinging to Chen. Okay, maybe a little bit, but he is her little boy. How can she not feel a little jealous about her baby not needing her as constantly anymore even if she *knows* it means he’s recovering? What worried her is the fact that Lee didn’t seem to want to say goodbye to Chen at all. It made her worry that he didn’t actually feel safe staying too far from his new home. That maybe Lee didn’t want to say he didn’t want to leave, wasn’t sure how, or wasn’t entirely sure he didn’t want to leave himself.

Thankfully, that wasn’t the case. Unfortunately, the answer isn’t what she had been hoping for. The fact that Lee is still so caught up in his fear of abandonment is understandable but concerning nonetheless.

Hopefully the elderly herbalist can provide some insight on how to help Zuko in the long run. Kani isn’t sure if the firebender will want her to listen in on his conversation with the herbalist, but she can’t let him go alone. He can’t travel that far in his current state, he doesn’t know the area, and is a vulnerable target. If he got hurt because Kani wasn’t willing to find a way to entertain herself out of earshot for however long he might want to talk to the herbalist, she would never forgive herself. Feya nor Chen should never forgive her either if she allowed for something to happen to the poor boy.

For now, her main concern is keeping Lee warm until they make it into town. He protests a little as she wraps him in another layer before hoisting him onto the ostrich horse, happy to find that it is more difficult to do than she expected even with all of the layers weighing him down.

If the situation were different, Kani might feel a little sad that in not too long, it might become difficult and uncomfortable for her to carry around her little boy for long. However, she should have been struggling to lift Lee when they first met because of his age. He shouldn’t have been the size and weight of a nine year old.

Even if he is still dreadfully skinny, he’s been putting on a little bit of weight. He’s heavier, his face looks a little fuller, his ribs don’t dig into her arms when she hugs him, and he doesn’t feel like almost nothing when she lifts him into his arms. He’s getting healthier. If his health means it’s harder for Kani to pick him up and snuggle him, she’ll find other ways to smother him in affection and embarrass him.

“You two be safe. Have fun.” Chen instructs, squeezing Zuko’s hand and kissing Kani. “Make sure you stop to eat during the trip, but don’t take too long. Don’t let the sun go down on you before you get into town.”

No matter how many times Kani has gone into town, Chen always worries about her. At first, she had considered that it was because he thought that she couldn’t take care of herself but quickly disregarded that idea. Chen is always so supportive and so sure of Kani’s ability to do just about anything. It hadn't taken long for her to realize that he didn’t need a genuine reason just to worry about her wellbeing. Whenever she left for town or Chen went, he would miss her even if they were just separated for a few days.

When Chen’s siblings found out about that, some of them had teased him for being so sappy about being around his wife. Chen had just reaffirmed the fact that he married Kani because he loves her and likes being around her and doesn’t like it when he isn’t. However, he had managed to put it even less eloquently than that.

Either way, Kani thought it was sweet. She still does. She loves her husband and is grateful that she has been able to share her life with them. Even if a lot of it hadn’t turned out the way that she had expected, she is happy. If it had, Lee very likely would have died. If not, he might be locked up somewhere alone, afraid, and growing bitter and cruel as his heart is forced to heal in a twisted shape with sharp edges. He would never get to heal from everything he had been through. He would just be a byproduct of terror and pain fueled only by fear and anger.

“Are you comfortable, Lee?” She asks, climbing up behind the firebender, securing her arms on either side of him as she takes hold of the reins of the ostrich horse.

Lee nods, petting the creature's head, smiling at it.

She can see Chen smiling at Lee’s interaction with the animal. Lee definitely has a strong connection with them. She can only assume that it was born from fear and isolation and is now a natural comfort that he seeks. She is glad that he gets to be around animals here. It’s likely one of the first things that really began to help him settle into his new home.

Lee talked about spending time with turtle ducks with his mother and that they are his favorite animal. He also wanted the seal to be a turtle duck; he must spend enough time around them to be something that would signify his identity to his uncle.

Kani isn’t sure if she finds that more endearing or sad. Maybe it can be both.

“I love you both so much. Be safe.” Chen says, kissing Kani’s hand and squeezing Lee’s one more time before they ride off into the morning making the journey towards town.

As the village fades from view behind them, Kani can only pray that she made the right choice in bringing Lee with her. That he’ll be okay. She knows that he wants this so badly but there is so much that could possibly go wrong. For now, she can only hope that he will get what he needs from this.

Zuko knew that it was going to be cold. Kani and Chen had told him this over and over again, but still, he wasn’t quite prepared for *this* .

The layers had kept him warm and so he had stopped stoking his inner flame not long into the trip. That had been a mistake. It’s far easier to keep one’s inner flame burning bright than it is to stoke it up again. He will need to practice more if he is going to be in this kind of cold.

It’s been a few hours into their journey and Zuko is definitely cold despite the several layers keeping him nearly immobile. He isn’t quite shivering but he is definitely cold. He can’t feel his nose, ears, fingers, or toes despite his hat, scarf, gloves, and warm socks. It will only be a matter of time before the cold spreads.

“How much longer until town, Kani?” He asks, wanting to huddle up next to a fire, drink some tea, and fall asleep. He really appreciates the room that Kani and Chen set up for him. He really loves it. But sometimes, he prefers to snuggle up next to the fire like he had before. He likes the warmth and safety it gives him.

“Still a few more hours, love. Are you cold? We’re about halfway there, we can stop for lunch a little if you want. We can make a little fire, get you warmed up, and let our guy rest.” Kani offers, kissing the back of Zuko’s head.

Zuko nods, snuggling up against Kani. “Didn’t realize it would get so cold so fast. Didn’t regulate my breathing as much as I should have. I’ll be better about it next time.” Zuko promises, meaning it. He doesn’t like being this cold. He didn’t even know the world *could* be this cold.

“Okay, we’ll stop in a little bit and start a fire, alright?” Kani offers.

Zuko nods. He can warm up by the fire and regulate his temperature better once he has some external heat to warm himself from.

“Are the Water Tribes colder than this?” Zuko asks after a few minutes of silence. He has only heard stories about fierce, dangerous savages living among the snow and ice in the most extreme parts of the world. He really would like to meet someone from there. Wants to know if what he has heard about them is wrong too. If he does get to meet someone from the Water Tribe, he really hopes that they’re nice or, at least, not savage.

“I’ve never been to the poles, but I’m sure it’s much colder. Even in the summer, there is always snow covering the ground. I’m not sure how people can manage to live there, but they do. Takes a lot of resilience.” Kani explains as they come to a stop by a rocky formation, Kani then mentions something about how the structure will protect them from the wind.

She helps Zuko off of the ostrich horse, gathering supplies from their bags as Zuko gathers the abundance of fallen branches on the ground, very quickly starting a fire and snuggling up close to it. It only takes a few minutes for warmth and strength to begin to flow through his body.

Kani sits down next to him, opening bags of dried fruits, jerky, and nuts.

Zuko nibbles on the food, more to keep his strength up than because he’s hungry. Then again, he usually isn’t hungry, his body and mind still not quite used to regular meals. Kani had promised him that eventually he would get used to being taken care of and being happy and healthy. She has been right about most things so far, he really wants her to be right about this too.

“Will you and Feya teach me anything about healing?” Zuko suddenly asks, unsure where exactly the question came from, but invested in the answer all the same. He wants to learn how to heal, how to help people in a way that Kani and Chen had helped him. Zuko may be the Fire Lord’s son, but he doesn’t want to be anything like that man. Zuko wants to be kind and gentle, bring healing where he goes, not pain and destruction.

Kani looks a little surprised but smiles. “Sure. We can show you how to make some of the ointments and when we have patients that aren’t in immediate danger you can watch and help some. The world could always use more healers. A firebender healing the people of the Earth Kingdom would be healing in it’s own way as well.” She says softly, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s forehead.

Zuko smiles, syncing his breath with the fire before snuggling up against Kani. “Wanna help people.” He says softly as Kani wraps an arm around Zuko’s shoulders.

“I know you do, sweetheart. I’m sure you can find and learn plenty of ways to help people. You can do so many wonderful things with your life.” Her voice is soft and honest as she holds him closer.

The two stay like that for a little more than half an hour before Kani stands up. “Come on, let’s get going. The days are getting shorter and you don’t want the sun to go down on you out here. It gets so much colder.” Kani warns as she begins to pack their food away again and Zuko puts out their fire.

Kani helps Zuko up onto the ostrich horse and climbs on after him before heading back towards town. This time, Zuko is diligent about keeping his inner flame burning bright.

By the time that Kani and Zuko walk in through the door, the sun is beginning to set over the ocean. Feya had started getting worried that they were going to be coming in late after the sun went down.

Usually, Feya isn’t worried about Kani or Chen making it into town safely. They’re both smart, strong, and resilient people. However, who she is worried about is Zuko. He’s never seen a real winter before and is a concerningly skinny kid. She can’t imagine that even the Fire Lord could be cruel enough to starve his own child as some twisted way to get control. To hurt him. To break him.

When the two get inside, Feya goes to greet them but Zuko throws off the bulky layers of clothes and stumbles over to her as quickly as he can on his crutches, flinging himself into her arms. Feya can only smile at how much the firebender has warmed up to her. He had gone from crying when she came out of fear of rejection to this is a pretty short period of time. She is glad that she must have made an impression on him. Glad that telling him that she knew he was was the right thing to do.

“I missed you.” Zuko mumbles as Feya picks the all too little boy up in her arms, holding him close to her chest.

“I missed you too, Lee.” Feya nuzzles the firebender’s cheek before setting him down on the ground and embracing Kani. “I have soup on the fire. Are you two hungry?” She asks, letting go of her sister and taking the Fire Prince’s hand in hers, smiling at him. This is never the situation she would ever expect to interact with royalty.

Luckily, Zuko nods, grinning.

The three walk into Feya’s private quarters as she locks the door behind them, listening to Zuko excitedly ask about the play and Kani say it’s been all he’s been able to talk about for weeks. The excitement on the little boy’s face is priceless. She didn’t think anyone could be this excited about theater, but apparently she was wrong.

“They’re holding a show in three days, we can go then.” Feya offers, smiling at the kid.

Zuko’s face lights up, nodding quickly. “Please.”

Feys smiles, squeezing Zuko’s hand. She wishes that the boy’s father could see how much happier and healthier the boy could be with just a little bit of love and encouragement. With just taking care of the kids needs and loving him opposed to tearing him down. He just wants to learn, to do good things, and to be happy. It’s what every child should have. It’s what the kid’s father denied him for no reason other than cruelty.

Zuko is just a kid who wants to be a kid. It isn’t an outrageous request. It’s what every child deserves. It’s what every parent should want for their child. Unfortunately, not all do.

“Do Water Tribe…people…tribesmen, I dunno what they would be called, but do they ever pass through here?” Zuko asks, which is not at all what Feya was expecting for the firebender to ask considering it doesn’t tie into any conversation that they had been having prior to this.

“Uh…I think it’s tribesmen, not sure if that is always only referring to men or is generally assumed to be gender neutral. I’ve met a few who had come to join the war effort but they’ve usually been traveling with Earth Kingdom fleets. Not many come this way, why?” She asks, more curious as to *how* this got brought up.

Kani shakes her head, sighing. “He’s been going on about the Water Tribes for the past few days. I think it’s just curiosity. Seen the Fire Nation, seen the Earth Kingdom, not the Water Tribes? That is, love?” Kani asks as Zuko slurps up his noodles.

Zuko nods and shrugs simultaneously. “Kinda. Also, I was told a lot of lies about the Earth Kingdom. That you were horrible people who couldn’t govern themselves and would only destroy themselves and the world along with them if we didn’t take control. I know that isn’t true after living here for a few months. I was told that the Water Tribe is filled with lawless savages who would drink their enemies blood and use bone weapons. I wanna know what they’re really like too.” Zuko explains, taking another bite of his noodles.

Feya smiles. She's sad, but not surprised, that Zuko had been brainwashed by Fire Nation propaganda his entire life but grateful that he is excited to relearn his world view. That he wants to understand what people who are different from him are really like and not just accept what he had been told. If more people were like that, the world would be a much better place.

“Well, I can’t say for sure. The most personal interaction I’ve ever had with someone from the Water Tribe was a man who came in while stopping for supplies with his crew to get a bad cut on his arm cleaned and stitched. He was just as loud, foul-mouthed, and dirty as any Earth Kingdom man living on a ship for months on end, so I can’t say for sure. The others I’ve met have been even briefer interactions and they seemed pretty normal.” She explains

For the most part, Feya had heard pretty similar things about the Water Tribes…well, not the drinking blood part, that’s probably just a dehumanizing thing from the Fire Nation, but most people who have talked about people from the Water Tribe had referred to them as savages. She is pretty sure it is mostly because they live in a more secluded part of the world and not many people go to visit them due to the extreme weather conditions and they mostly stay in the poles.

Feya does not want to share that fact with Zuko. He seems so excited to learn about the world and fix his propaganda oriented world view, the last thing she wants to do is stunt that.

Zuko giggled at the description. “Sailors are really dirty. My uncle told me that he considered going into the navy but he didn’t want to be surrounded by sailors. I’m not sure if he’s joking or not…also, all of the sailors I’ve met are mean. There’s this one guy, Capitan Zhao, who has been in Caldera City to talk to my father but ended up speaking to a courtier of sorts, and he’s a jerk. He’s mean to my uncle and to me because he knows my father doesn't care about either of us and he can. I hate him.” Zuko grumbles, drinking the broth in between sentences.

Even if Feya is not a big fan of people eating and talking a lot at the same time, she is happy that Zuko is opening up and gaining an appetite. He needs it.

“Sounds like one. I’m sorry that happened to you, but you’re safe now. If any sailors try to be mean to you here, you have earthbenders as your mom and auntie, alright?” She half jokes, kissing Zuko’s head.

Looking up for a moment as she sees the light in Zuko’s eyes at Feya referring to herself as his aunt. Unfortunately, she can also see a very questioning and knowing look in Kani’s eyes. Feya isn’t sure if what Zuko just said while letting his guard down around Feya had just revealed his identity to Kani or not. Either way, Kani knows that Feya knows *exactly* who Zuko is.

Not only is her sister not stupid, but she knows how to get answers and Feya isn’t a terrified little kid. Kani is likely more than willing to press for answers from her.

It doesn’t take long for Zuko to get tired. It’s been a long day of travel, he’s still injured, he’s apparently been bending in some form most of the day, and still is getting used to how sleepy a full stomach will make him.

“You wanna go to bed, love?” Kani asks, running her fingers through Zuko’s growing hair. Feya can only imagine that he would have beautiful hair if the boy grew it out. She knows that is very common for Fire Nation men to do as well as in the earth Kingdom.

Zuko nods, yawning, clutching Kani’s hand.

“Hey, Lee, I know how much you love sleeping with Cabbage, so I made you something.” Feya chimes in, getting up and pulling a crocheted turtle duck she had worked on for a few weeks. She isn’t the best at it, but it is calming. Anyways, she is sure Zuko would love sleeping with a stuffed animal even if most 13 year olds might feel above it.

She isn’t surprised when Zuko’s face lights up when she hands it to him. He clutches it to his chest, thanking her profusely. Both she and her sister laugh at the kid’s enthusiastic gratitude. Kani’s pointed concern fading even if just for a moment.

Kani helps Zuko up while Feya sets up a cozy mess of blankets on a cot by the fireplace, hoping it will keep him warm enough.

It doesn’t take long for Zuko to snuggle under the blankets, clutching his turtle duck to his chest, and close his eyes.

As soon as he starts falling asleep, Kani takes Feya’s hand, leading her back into the kitchen, looking at her. “What did Lee tell you? What do you know about him?” She asks, a worried look on her face. Feya doesn’t say anything, not wanting to break Zuko’s trust or do something to hurt her sister.

“Feya, what did he tell you? Who is he? Is someone going to fucking recognize him? Is he fucking *royalty* ? I just brought him, a kid with a very distinct injury that he cannot hide, into a town with a lot of people passing through with people who talk. You need to tell me what you know about him right now because I don’t know if he’s safe here, *especially* if he feels this comfortable talking about his life this freely. I want him to be confident in who he is but he *can’t* be stupid if he has direct relation to the fucking *Fire Lord* .” She hisses in a whisper, anger and fear evident in her expression and voice.

Feya hates that the first thought that comes to her head is the fact that she has never heard her sister swear this much in such a short period of time without being injured. She shakes that from her mind before speaking, trying to calm Kani down even just a little bit. “Kani, you need to calm down, you know him, I wouldn't expect you to care-”

“I don’t give a shit who he is but there are people who *will* . There are people who will take him from me and hurt him. He’ll be tortured for information that he doesn’t know, ransomed to a man who doesn’t want him, and eventually executed or left to die because he’s found to be worthless. Why did he trust you with this before telling us?” Kani asks frantically, shoving Feya’s hand off of her.

Feya shakes her head. “I found out. People talked about the Fire Lord’s kid being burned and banished. He’s the same age, was found around the same time, and has a similar injury, he didn’t… oh…yeah.” She trails off, realizing that it’s worse that way. Feya is well aware that she is intelligent, not out of vanity, but out of experience. Still, that doesn’t mean the people around her are stupid. It would only take so long for them to figure out who Zuko is if they found out the right things about him. There aren’t too many pieces that they would need to put it all together in their heads. Even Kani and Chen had known that Zuko was of nobility long ago. They just didn’t realize he was royalty.

“Yeah, that’s a lot fucking worse. I’m taking him home in the morning. He can’t stay here. Someone is going to find out who he is and they’re going to take my baby.” That's when Feya can see the tears in Kani’s eyes even if only for a moment before she brushes them away.

Feya just looks at her sister blankly, wanting to argue to let Zuko stay, at least long enough to go see the play, that he could stay inside until then, but at least right now, she doubts Kani will listen. She’s upset and scared. Maybe they could talk in the morning.

“Who's gonna take me away?” A small, distinctly raspy voice asks behind them. Feya closes her eyes, wishing Kani had waited more than five minutes after getting Zuko down to talk to her about this. “I don’t wanna go home yet.”

“Zuko, please go to bed. You’re going to be okay. We’re not going to let anyone take you.” Feya says softly, meaning it. If an Earth Kingdom soldier came to take Zuko away, she would send a stalagmite through their chest.

“Come here, baby, it’s okay, no one is going to take you. We’re gonna go home. I don’t want you to get hurt here.” Kani whispers, walking forward as Zuko limps towards her. She wraps him in an embrace, lifting him off the ground, likely not wanting any weight on his ankle.

“I don’t wanna go home. I want to write to my uncle…I want to go to the play. Why can’t I stay? Who wants to take me?” He asks again, resting his head on Kani’s shoulder, likely exhausted.

“Feya recognized you just from hearing rumors…others might come to the same conclusion. I just realized who you are because of how you were talking at dinner. I don’t care who you are or where you came from, I love you and I always will because no matter what. You’re my little boy and that’s not going to change. Some people won’t feel the same way. They might hurt you, my love.” Kani whispers, clutching Zuko tighter.

Feya can almost see the question on Zuko’s lips, wanting to know who would take him. Feya speaks up before he can. “Earth Kingdom soldiers might take you. They could have a lot of different reasons, but they might hurt you. I don’t want you to go…if you’re careful, you could stay for a bit, but you need–”

“He is *not* staying. Love, I’m sorry, I know you wanted to come, but it isn’t safe here. I don’t want anyone hurting you.”

Zuko doesn’t respond, but Feya can see tears rolling down his cheeks. Even though he had only been here for a few hours, it had been easy to tell that Zuko had been looking forward to this for weeks. She wants him to be happy…but he needs to be safe.

It doesn’t take long for Zuko to start struggling out of Kani’s grip, stumbling on the floor and leaning against the wall to stay upright, wiping away tears. “I wanna stay. I promise I’ll be careful…I’ll be safe. I wanna stay.” He whimpers, looking down at the ground.

“Lee, I know you do–”

“You know my name. My real one. You know who I am. Are you ashamed? Do you hate me? I-I never wanted to be his! I didn’t ask to be born! I didn’t…I didn’t want any of this.” Zuko whimpers, sliding down to the floor, tucking his knees under his chest, crying.

Feya takes a step towards the little boy but Kani is by his side almost instantly, wrapping her arms around his shoulder. “Lee…Zuko, my love, please don’t say that. Please don’t say any of that. I love you so much. I’m so sorry that the world hasn’t been kind to you, that you aren’t safe in a lot of places, but it’s going to be alright. I’m not ashamed of you, I promise I’m not. I’m scared for you. I’m scared someone will take you from me and hurt you. I know you already know how cruel the world can be.” She says softly, kissing the red skin around Zuko’s eye.

Feya kneels down in front of the two, looking down. “I think we should discuss this in the morning, but I do think that there are some important things to take into consideration.” She begins, sighing, wishing there was a way Zuko would just…be himself without repercussion. That he could be the firebender who helped start fires for people if they couldn’t find a hot coal in their stove or their neighbors didn’t have one either. He could be the Fire Lord’s son who exposed the man for his cruelty to his own nation and family and denounced the war. He could be a part of healing the world if people just gave him a chance to prove that he just wants a home. Just wants to be loved in ways that he was denied as a child in the Fire Nation.

“I knew that Zuko was a firebender from the Fire Nation. That was the first big thing. I also knew that his father burned him. We could change the story surrounding him, people won’t draw conclusions so fast. On top of that, I knew that your age matched that of the banished prince. People talked about how horrible it was that he was killed or died at 13, whether or not they believed the story. We can use the fact that you look younger than you are to our advantage, say you’re ten.” Feya suggests, well aware that she had been given a lot of the pieces in figuring out who Lee really was. Unfortunately, it wouldn’t take forever for someone to connect the dots. Kani shakes her head slowly, sighing. “I agree…let’s talk in the morning. We’ve had a long day. My love…please be willing to compromise. I know this isn’t what you had hoped for, but we need you to be safe.”

Thankfully, Zuko nods. “I’m sorry I yelled at you. Sorry I said you were ashamed…know you’re not. I love you.” The firebender says softly, snuggling up against Kani.

Smiling, Kani kisses the kid’s head again. “I love you too. Let’s get to bed. We’ll figure this out in the morning. Things will be better then.”

Feya just hopes that her sister is right.
