### Text

*General Iroh,*

*I have finally been able to make it into the harbor town of Si Lang and can send a letter to you* *myself. A friend of the family who took me in sent the previous letter that I wrote and I can only* *hope that it got to you. I would like to travel up to the colonies to get a better sense of home, but for* *now, Si Lang will have to suffice.*

*I don’t know if I will be able to stay for long, but I can see the ocean here, something I have missed* *greatly about the Fire Nation. From where I lived and grew up before following you into battle I* *could almost always see the sea. Even if it’s too cold to swim in during this time of year, the* *familiarity is comforting. I like the sound and the smell. There is a lot that I have tried to find* *comfort in, knowing that it is unlikely I will ever see the homeland again. Thankfully, I have found* *good, kind people who make it easier to make a life here.*

*I am staying with the town healer while here and hopefully I can learn a few things from her.* *Gracious Earth Kingdom healers are the only reason that I am alive today and if I cannot fight* *anymore, I would like to learn to heal. What I can think of now is how helpful of a skill it would* *have been if I knew it at Ba Sing Se. We could have returned with more soldiers still living. I may* *have been able to return at all. I’m not sure if injury or simple bad luck is what got me captured,* *but I would like to think maybe things could have been different.*

*I don’t know if we will ever meet again, but I hope that we can. Everything you had told me before* *that was lost on me is all making sense now. Every piece of wisdom you shared with me I am* *trying to recall and decipher, try and apply it to my life. It may be all of what I have left of before. I* *want to have a life that I can be happy with here, but I don’t want to forget who I was, who I am.*

*What I do know is that you told me time and time again to never give up without a fight. I won’t.* *No matter what happens, if I return to the village, stay here, make it to the colonies, or back to the* *Fire Nation, no one can take any of my life from me anymore. It won’t be stolen through fear,* *imprisonment, or pain. I have spent too much time dwelling on what has happened and what* *horrible things the future may hold, but for now, I’ll try to focus on the present. I will try and focus* *on the fact that I have been taken in by good, kind people who will do their best to keep me healthy.* *That I have forged new relationships with people who I once saw so different from myself. Even if I* *didn’t know it at the time, you knew what you were talking about.*

*I hope that our paths will cross again, your friend and obedient servant,*

*Lee.*

Zuko reads over his letter again, hoping it is decent. It isn’t as good as his first one, but that isn’t the point. The point is to hopefully get his uncle to understand that these letters are from Zuko and that he is safe. That’s the whole point. He needs his uncle to not mourn for him and focus on Azula. Focus on getting her away from Ozai and bringing her somewhere safe where that man can’t hurt her anymore. If Iroh is going to save Azula, he can’t be caught up in his grief for Zuko.

He is well aware that it sounds more patriotic than Zuko feels, but if Ozai sees this, he needs to think that it is a soldier who still loves his homeland more than anything. Not someone he needs to send an assassin after.

“Hey, love, what are you working on?” He hears Kani ask behind him.

Zuko rolls up the letter, setting it aside, shrugging. He understands that she just wants to keep him safe and that she thinks she is doing what is best for him, but it feels like she doesn’t trust him. It feels like she’s punishing him for being royalty.

“Lee, I know you’re upset, I know you were excited, but I’m really worried about what might happen to you. Someone might hurt you even if they just think you’re a firebender from some insignificant peasant family. I don’t want to think about what might happen if the wrong person finds out who you really are.” She says softly, pressing a kiss to his temple.

Zuko feels tears welling up in his eyes as he leans against her. “Can we stay until the play? I’ll stay inside. If you could go to the market to get candy for me and Fao I won’t even go there. We could put a bandage on my face and stain it the night I go so that my scar might look fresh and people wouldn’t think I’ve had months to heal. I *really* want to go. I promise I’ll just stay inside and just help with whatever Feya needs me to do. Please?” He whispers, looking up at Kani, clutching her hand.

“Lee…Zuko…I really don’t know.” Kani says softly, cupping Zuko’s cheek in her hand.

“Please. I’ll be good. I just want to send the letter to my uncle, get the candy, and see the play. Please can I just stay a few days to do that? I’ll be quiet, hidden, and be as helpful as I can. I’ll eat regularly and take care of myself. Please?”

Kani sighs, resting her face in her hand, shaking her head slowly. “Fine, but we leave the morning after the play.” She concedes.

Zuko throws his arms around her, thanking her over and over again.

Kani holds him close, rocking Zuko in her arms, pressing kisses to his head. “I’m sorry things are difficult for you, my love. I’m so sorry that life hasn’t been fair to you. I wish I could make things easier for you.”

Zuko just snuggles closer to her, not sure what to say. He doesn’t really think that there is anything that could make things easier without changing who his father is. Without changing his element and nationality. Without changing the history of the world. There is so much that is just out of his and everyone else’s control.

“Would you like for me to seal your letter for you? I brought the turtle duck stamp I made for you. Still want that one?” She asks, running her fingers gently through Zuko’s hair.

Zuko nods, grabbing the letter from beside him and offers it to Kani as she hands Zuko a stick of red sealing wax. He holds fire at the end of one of his fingers, letting it drip onto the letter before Kani stamps it with the seal.

After they set the letter back down, Kani pulls Zuko back into her arms. “What’s your uncle’s name, love?” She asks quietly, brushing her fingers through his hair. “I thought that the previous Fire Lord only had two sons…but then again, I didn’t hear much about Ozai until he ascended to the throne, I knew more about the Dragon of the West.” Her voice is even and curious. She isn’t trying to pry for the fact that Zuko’s kind hearted, tea loving uncle is one of the most feared Fire Nation Generals in the world. If not one of the most feared people.

Zuko stays silent, unsure what to say to that. Feya had either known that Azulon had only two sons or hadn’t considered the fact that there could be a third one who wasn’t heir to the throne and didn’t do anything notable enough for his name to be shared with Earth Kingdom civilians. It isn’t hard for Fire Nation royalty to earn the title of general. All he would have to do would be to join the army. He wouldn’t have needed to lead any important battles or any at all, for that matter.

“Lee…are you alright?” Kani asks, pressing a gentle kiss to Zuko’s forehead.

Zuko nods slowly, clutching Kani’s arm tighter. “He really did change a lot after Lu Ten died. Everything changed. Lu Ten begged for a command and my uncle gave him one. His death is the reason the forces retreated from Ba Sing Se.” Zuko whispers, burying his face in Kani’s shoulder, not wanting to look at her right now.

He can feel her hand stop moving as soon as those words leave his mouth. He can feel her breath hitch for a moment. Zuko just buries his face closer to her, clutching onto her robes as if he would die if he ever let go. He just might.

“He took good care of you, love?” Kani finally asks after a long pause, going back to petting his hair.

Zuko whimpers quietly, nodding. “Did his best. Tried to keep me safe. Made me feel better when he could. Gave me something to hold onto.” Zuko says quietly, unsure what would have happened if his uncle hadn’t come back. If he had come back even weeks later than he did, things may have been completely different.

It’s uncertain if Ozai or Zuko’s own mind would have gotten to him first, but something would have happened. Ozai might have hit Zuko too hard or pushed him too far and either someone might not be able to help Zuko come back from it. Or perhaps Zuko might just not have been able to bring himself to care enough to have anything done.

Between the time that his mother left and his uncle came back was the darkest point in Zuko’s life. Darker than when his own father had burned and banished him. Part of Zuko always knew that his father never loved him, he had just been too weak to admit it to himself. But his mother…Zuko really had thought she had loved him. Maybe she did, but that was when she was trapped. As soon as she had a chance to run, her son became obsolete.

“I’m worried about my sister.” Zuko finally admits quietly. “She never liked my uncle much. I think it’s because my father doesn’t like him. He’s been keeping Azula, my sister, close as a soldier from before she could really talk. I ended up taking a lot of my fathers anger…he hated me, but I had people to help me. It’s just her now. I-I don’t know what he’s going to do to her, Kani. What if he kills her? He’s going to hurt her but what if he does something so much worse? She isn’t safe and she won’t let my uncle help her and I don’t know how to help her and I’m scared.” Zuko can feel hot tears rolling down his cheeks as he speaks, choking on his words as he tries to talk.

He had tried to keep Azula out of his mind for a long time, but she had been slipping back during the last few weeks. She had been on his mind more and more often. He kept wondering if their father had broken any of her bones, denied her food, locked her away, pushed her beyond her already impressive limits, or some other twisted way of hurting her that man was able to think of.

He really has no way of knowing what punishments their father had strictly reserved for Zuko. He had just absorbed most of the blows between the two and more once his mother left. It was only then that Zuko realized that his mother had been sharing some of the burden of their father’s wrath. He knows how that feels and he has no idea if Azula is suffering though it now as well. He doesn’t know if their father wants someone who can’t leave him to direct their fury onto, if Iroh is taking on that burden for Azula, or if Ozai wants to preserve his prodigy daughter.

Knuckles gently wipe away the tears rolling down Zuko’s cheeks which are very quickly replaced with more as he continues to cry, unable to keep the absolute terror he feels for his little sister contained anymore. He can’t breathe, he feels sick, he can’t keep his thoughts straight as he moves closer to Kani, burying his face in her neck, sobs muffled.

He can feel his body being rocked gently as the woman hums, rubbing his back.

He has no idea how long they stay there, it feels like hours and moments before Kani talks to him outside of trying to comfort him. “I didn’t know you had a sister, love. Is she older?” She asks quietly, carding her fingers through his hair.

“Sh-she’s eleven.” Zuko chokes out. “We weren’t close…father pitted us against each other. Tried not to think about her…she’s been all I can think about the past few weeks.” He whimpers.

Well, technically he has been able to think of plenty of other things, but she had been in the back of his mind. It’s at night when he really couldn’t stop thinking about her. Worrying if she was able to sleep in safety that night, if she was hurt, or scared. He wished he could know. Wishes he could at least talk to her for a few minutes. He needs to know if she’s alright. She *needs* to get out of there.

“Oh, sweetheart,” Kani whispers sadly, holding Zuko closer. “If we could ever find her we would do what we could to protect her, too. I wish we could protect both of you. I wish your mother had stayed. I wish your father was a good man.” Kani whispers into Zuko’s hair.

“I just wanted him to love me.” Zuko cries, aware that, unlike Azula, he actually got the chance to know what being loved felt like. Even if their father was far crueler to Zuko, he had mom and uncle. Now he has Kani, Chen, Feya, and Fao. He isn’t sure if Azula thinks that how Ozai treats her is what love is.

He is well aware of the fact that Azula knows that father hates Zuko, the man never made any attempt to conceal it. He would regularly belittle Zuko in front of Azula and express favoritism. That isn’t what worries him. What worries him is that Azula might really think that their father loves her. That he even cares about her past what she can do for him. That he is even capable of love.

“I know you did, sweetheart, that’s what every child deserves. People fight, families fight, but you should love and protect your children. I’m so sorry you had to go through all of that. I wish that there was something I could do to help your sister.”

Despite everything going through his head, Zuko believes her. All he can picture is the absurdity of both of the children of the Fire Lord living in a remote Earth Kingdom village and being happier than ever. Being loved and cared for by people who had been so hurt by Zuko and Azula’s ancestors, but looking past that and holding them closer.

“Hey, sweetheart, I have an idea of what we can do today. I won’t make you go home just yet, but you *have* to listen to me, okay?” Kani offers, pressing kisses to Zuko’s head.

Zuko looks up, a little bit of excitement sparking in his chest, wiping at his tears that he can’t quite yet get to stop. “You really mean we can stay for a little?” He repeats back to her, trying to give her a small smile but just feeling so emotionally drained right now.

“Yes, my love…also, would you prefer me to use your real name? Do you prefer Zuko?” Kani asks quietly, kissing his forehead.

Zuko shrugs. He does prefer it. He knows that his father didn’t want him alive, that his mother gave him that name. He likes the way it sounds. Unfortunately, it is very uncommon and distinct.

“Lee is safer.” He finally replies, not wanting to think about it too much. “What are we going to do?” He wants to get the subject off of himself while he calms down.

“Remember the herbalist I told you about? The one who could maybe offer you some help? She’s seen a lot, she’s kind of crazy, but does have a lot of wisdom to offer.”

Nodding, Zuko slowly sits up, regulating his breathing. “Do you think she’ll care that I’m a firebender? Do you think that she’ll recognize me?” Zuko asks, looking down at his fingers.

On one hand, Zuko does want to be able to talk about his life, his fears, and everything else with someone who might be able to help him. Kani had mentioned this woman before and had said she would write to her. Zuko had mostly forgotten about her until now.

On the other hand, he doesn’t want to expose himself like that to someone he doesn’t know. She could be anyone. She might hate him and want to hurt Zuko for the crime of being born. The worst part is that Zuko wouldn’t be able to blame her for that.

“I don’t think she will, love. She’s odd, crazy, but experienced and kind. I don’t think she will care who you are. I think she might find it fascinating that the Fire Lord’s son is looking for her help. Even if she does care, I can assure you she won’t do anything about that. Feya is the only person who she interacts with regularly and is likely the only person who knows that she hasn’t completely lost it. The other people she interacts with just make sure she is eating and still okay up there but don’t listen to much of what she says. Worst she’ll do is want you to go. Does that sound okay?”

Biting his lip, Zuko nods once, unsure if it really is. However, he wants to stay and more importantly, he wants these feelings to stop burning him from the inside out. He doesn’t want to feel like this anymore. He doesn’t want to be so scared that Kani and Chen will throw him out or hurt him even after they have proved over and over again that they would never do that to him. He doesn’t want to keep thinking about how much pain Azula might be in, worrying himself into illness won’t help her. Anyways, Azula can help herself more than Zuko ever could help her and Iroh can do far more than Zuko could ever dream of doing.

With Zuko gone, he is hoping that Iroh has latched onto Azula. That he has been annoying her into playing games of Pai Sho, drinking tea, and listening to his long stories that barely seem to have any point. That even though he may be annoying, he’s kind, loving, and isn’t the kind of person to give up on anyone. Once he’s in their corner, he’s there to stay.

He *needs* to believe that Iroh has done everything that he can to show Azula what it is like for someone to love her. How it feels when someone talks to her about her interests as a parent of sorts or gives her advice and wants only for her health and safety.

“I trust you.” Zuko breaths, snuggling back up against Kani, wishing that Azula were here to feel what it is like to be loved and cherished by someone unconditionally. He wishes that she could be here. Wishes she could be safe.

What he doesn’t realize is that he doesn’t just wish that Azula was safe. For the first time in his life, he genuinely misses his sister.

It takes awhile for Kani to get Zuko out the door. They need to eat of course and then Feya keeps trying to bundle the firebender up even more than Kani felt was necessary. Zuko defenaly felt like it was unnecessary and made that very clear as the two women checked that his clothes were engulfing him.

“I look like an ugly marshmallow.” Zuko complains, scrunching up his face.

Kani isn’t sure if he is trying to look irritated or if his face just does that, but he looks pretty cute which is likely the exact opposite of his intentions.

Chuckling, Kani presses a kiss to his forehead. “Well you’ll be warm. That’s what matters. I don’t want you getting sick. Remember how fast you got cold yesterday?” She reminds him. This time, Zuko can’t firebend. People will see if he does.

Zuko grumbles something that is barely audible and Feya just smiles. “While you two are out, can you pick up some food from the market. Don’t really care what. If they don’t have dried fruit, can you pick some pine needles?”

Kani nods, embracing her sister before taking Zuko’s hand and leading him outside.

“What are the pine needles for?” Zuko asks as the two start walking, Zuko insisting that he can use one crutch to support himself now, not wanting to make the ostrich horse take them after traveling so much yesterday. She needs to rest and the herbalist isn’t far.

“We’ll brew them into tea. It isn’t good, but it prevents scurvy if there isn’t any available fruit. Also mitigates the chance of illness.” She explains, smiling at her little boy.

Zuko nods, looking up at her briefly before he sets his eyes back on the road. “What’s the herbalist’s name?” He asks. His constant curiosity is childlike, but from how he acts, Kani can only assume that he was forced to grow up too fast. That this is the first time he can ask questions about anything and not be punished just for asking. That the worst that would happen is refusal to answer if it was something personal.

It all started only a few weeks ago, constantly asking questions about the rest of the Earth Kingdom and the Water Tribes, trying to figure out more about the Fire Nation, and just interest in everything that passes his way. It’s sweet, watching him get to be a child for the first time in his life.

“Her name is Lo. If I remember correctly, she has a cat named Miyuki.” Kani hopes that the firebender will take some comfort from the creature in the same way that he does with Cabbage.

Kani can hear his little gasp of excitement as he looks up at her again, eyes shining.

Despite everything, he is so sweet and pure. So kind. She really can’t imagine looking at a child with eyes so bright and hopeful and even *think* about hurting him. He didn’t deserve any of what happened to him. She would do anything to take an ounce of his pain away. His fear. His hesitance. It’s what any mother would do for their child.

On their way to the herbalist, they send the letter with a carrier pigeon. Kani has very mixed feelings about the infamous General Iroh as of this morning.

She had always pictured the man as a tyrant. Someone who would stand tall over everyone with malice in his eyes and intent in his stance. She pictured a man set on cruelty and destruction. A man who knew nothing but war and bloodshed. Someone whose sole purpose was to perpetrate both.

Then, there was the man who Zuko had described. The man who did what he could to protect the little boy. Who mourned for the loss of his son and got Zuko away from his father when he could. The man who would make tea and play board games with the prince to try and calm his nerves and keep him company. The man who would bandage Zuko’s wounds and hold him close when things got bad. The man who would absorb blows for Zuko when he could, trying to protect the terrified little boy. The man who loved Zuko like a son and was ready to leave his country and everything behind just to follow his nephew into banishment to make sure that he was safe and cared for.

Despite everything that Zuko had told Kani about his uncle, she can’t shake the memories of what that man did to her nation. What he is capable of doing. She is grateful that he gave Zuko something to hold onto, but she doesn't know how she feels about him.

It doesn’t take too long to get to the herbalist’s greenhouse. That’s likely because Kani had Zuko’s cheerful chatter to keep the conversation lively.

The two walk in and the strong scent of dried herbs, flowers, and fruits hits them. It’s pleasant, familiar, but odd. Everything about Lo is a little odd. She is a true crazy cat lady.

“Lo? It’s Kani, Feya sister!” She calls, unsure where the old woman is. She doubts the old woman went anywhere. For the most part, people in town will make sure she has food and bring it up to her if they are worried. She may be odd, but she’s kind and well liked. On top of that, they are all well aware that the fact that there are skilled healers in town becomes obsolete if they don’t have enough of the proper supplies.

Zuko begins taking off some of his layers of clothes, likely heating up with the warmth and moisture in the greenhouse. She doesn’t say anything about it to him. He’s allowed to do what he wants now that they’re someplace warm.

“I’ll be with you in just a moment!” The old woman calls from near the back of the greenhouse, likely hidden by the trees.

Kani reaches her hand out to lead Zuko towards the table in the middle of the room but doesn’t feel him. She looks to her side where he was and finds him sitting on the floor, Miyuki already in his lap, purring as the firebender runs his fingers through her long, white fur.

Smiling, Kani walks over to the two, sitting down in front of Zuko. “You really have a way with animals, don’t you, love?” She asks quietly, resting her hand on Zuko’s.

Zuko nods, scratching the cat’s ear. “They’re nice and much easier to be around. They aren't difficult like people. If you’re nice to them, they’re nice to you.” Zuko explains softly.

It makes sense that Zuko would have sought out the companionship of animals when living in the Fire Nation. He wasn’t allowed to have friends and most people around him were either cruel or couldn’t do anything to help him in any way. They just had to watch a child suffer in pain and fear.

“You can talk to her about anything, you know? Talk to her about how you’re still worried about things going wrong here, about how you feel isolated from your culture and your family. You can say whatever you need, my love.”

Zuko shrugs, nodding. She really hopes Lo can help him. Even if she just gets him to open up about himself and settle into his skin a little better, Zuko’s life will be made easier. Hopefully.

Finally, Lo steps into the center of the room, smiling. “I see you have taken a liking to my Miyuki.” She comments, looking at Zuko snuggling with the cat. “I think she likes you too.”

Kani sighs when she sees the stick going through the old woman’s hair, clearly intentionally placed. Maybe she has finally truly lost it, not just mostly crazy.

Zuko nods, kissing the top of the cat’s head. “She’s really friendly. I like animals.”

Lo nods, sitting on a wooden stool near him, still smiling that is somewhere between friendly and deranged. “So are you the firebender the healer has told me about?”

The firebender freezes for a moment, glancing up at Kani for a moment before nodding. “I promise I’m not here to cause any trouble. I just wanna be safe.” He promises, scratching under the cat’s chin.

“She said you weren’t happy. That you’re scared.” Lo continues, not acknowledging Zuko’s previous statement. “What are you scared of?”

Kani wraps an arm around Zuko’s shoulders, unsure if he isn’t alright with someone he doesn’t know prying into his life or if he doesn’t want Kani to be here. Either way, reminding him of her presence is likely the best she can do right now. Make sure he feels supported.

Breathing slowly, the firebender begins to formulate words in an unsure voice. “Most good things in my life don’t last. Always gets taken away. Scared that I’m going to do something wrong and lose everything. I don’t wanna leave…can’t go back.”

This is a fear that Kani is well aware of. Zuko has expressed terror of being thrown out for no reason. Just for making a small mistake or just for being a child. He seems to think that Kani and Chen are looking for any reason to get rid of him.

Then again, that is exactly what his own father did to him.

“I’m scared that my father is going to find me. He meant to kill me and he likely thinks I’m dead but I’m so scared that he’ll find out I’m not. I’m scared he’ll find me, that he’ll take me back and hurt me. I’m even more scared he’ll hurt the people I’ve met here. People I love.” The little boy whimpers, resting his head against Kani’s shoulder.

The idea that Fire Lord Ozai is Zuko’s father is terrifying to say the least. The firebender had been forthcoming that he was from a powerful and well connected family, but she and Chen had just assumed he was of nobility. Royalty wasn’t even something they considered. Even if they both knew that the Fire Lord was a terrible man, they never considered he would hurt his own children. If anything, they had assumed that the royal family would think that their children were above anyone even of nobility and treat them as such.

Treating them like prisoners was never something that had ever crossed Kani’s mind.

Now that there is a target, a face to the man who had caused her little boy so much pain, her anger feels so much more pointed and focused. She can almost hear her own anger at the man now, barely aware of what is going on in the room around her, just hearing the two soft voices without any cohesive words and can see Lo moving around. She can’t bring herself to focus on them. Zuko seems okay. As long as he is okay, that’s all that matters.

As long as she can protect her sweet little boy, it’s okay.

Part of her wants to find a way to march directly into the Fire Nation and encase the Fire Lord in stone, not caring about the dangers. Not caring about the fact that she wouldn’t even make it to the gates. Logistics isn’t a part of her fantasies.

She wants to find Azula, Zuko’s sister, and take her back to the Earth Kingdom if killing the Fire Lord wasn’t an option. She wants to be able to keep her safe as well. It would probably help Zuko a lot to see his sister again, have them bond and heal after everything that they have been through together.

Not only is it the right thing to do to get another child out of a dangerous and abusive situation, but it would be what is best for the world. Have them understand the cruelty of their ancestors and what kindness looks like. Have heirs to the throne have a better, non nationalized, world perspective. Make it so they could bring this war to an end and try to restore peace and balance.

Kani knows nothing about Zuko’s sister except that she is a scared little girl who is an abuse victim whether she knows it or not. All that she needs to know about Fire Lord Ozai is that given the chance, she will send a stalagmite directly through his heart. No, that’s too kind, maybe just kind of into his spine so he can’t stand or walk but bleed out from his injury. Feel a fraction of the pain that he has caused his children and the world.

If anyone deserves to suffer, it is that man. From everything Zuko has told her about his father, how absolutely terrified he is of that man, Kani has no reason to believe the Fire Lord has a drop of human blood in his body. She wouldn’t be shocked if his heart was made of solid coal.

Maybe the soldiers fighting this war under misguided direction are people with families, feelings, and personalities outside of this war, but the man leading it is made of nothing but bloodshed and terror. His own child knows that. His thirteen year old son had been sobbing into her shoulder hours ago out of fear that he would murder his eleven year old daughter. That he would kill his own brother. That he would come back to kill the son he had already broken.

She begins to take deep, calming breaths, trying to calm herself down. She can’t let herself go down a path of anger. She isn’t a soldier. There are people who have trained their whole lives who have been slaughtered in this battle.

Logically, she knows that the best thing she can do is to mother the boy the Fire Lord had broken into thousands of pieces and thrown away. What she can do is try and help the little boy put himself back together with a lot of time, patience, and care.

She and Chen have been doing their best, but it never feels like enough. Even though she is sure that killing someone brutally in Zuko’s name would terrify the firebender more than anything. He might even attribute that action to his family. It would only set him back as he loses trust in them.

Despite that knowledge, she wants to avenge the kid. She and Chen have never talked about it, but they both share the understanding that they want to destroy the man who broke their child.

Kani forces her eyes open, looking over at Zuko and Lo, trying to push the Fire Lord from her mind. Trying to get the image of her destroying him from plaguing her no matter how much she wants to carry it out.

Tears are still on Zuko’s cheeks, but most of them are dry now. He doesn’t look like he’s crying anymore but is not over it. Miyuki is still sitting in the firebenders lap, fast asleep, purring loudly, likely enjoying the additional heat that Zuko’s body gives off.

Kani can’t help but smile when she notices that there is a Pai Sho board between Lo and Zuko. It doesn’t look like either of them are particularly engulfed in it, but more interested in drinking their tea and Zuko listening to a rambling story about Lo’s late wife. Well, her girlfriend, they were never officially married, but they had a wedding long ago as that counts for something as far as most people in town are concerned. Anyways, Lo has always minded her own business and contributed a lot with her herbs and medicinal skills.

By the relaxed position in Zuko’s posture, this is calming him down. This is what he needs. He needs someone to remind him of people in his life who had been a constant reassurance in his life. One of the few people who did anything to protect him.

Kani has been trying to get Zuko to let go of his old life and move on with his new one. What is becoming more apparent, especially after the incident where he tried to run away, is that he can’t let go of who he was because it’s who he is. He just needs to learn how to live with his identity. She isn’t sure how he is going to manage that, but she needs to stop trying to find new ways to get him to move on from his old life because it isn't necessarily his old life. It’s still his life. Things are just different now.

It keeps getting so easy for her to forget that he doesn’t want to move on from his life in the Fire Nation. He doesn’t want to forget everything that has happened to him. Doing that would mean forgetting his mother, memories possibly being all that he will ever have of her now. It would mean forgetting about how his uncle changed after suffering the loss so many of the Earth Kingdom and Water Tribes did and stepped up as a father figure and protector for Zuko no matter the consequences of himself. It would mean forgetting his little sister, there is likely a very complex history between the two of them, but it really sounds like no matter how messed up their relationship is, he loves her.

Even if Kani thinks it could spare her child a lot of pain to move on from his life, she’s asking him to leave behind so much more than just his abuse. She’s trying to get him to shut away the people who were there for him in the darkest of times. He needs that.

She squeezes the firebender a little tighter with the arm around his shoulders, smiling at him, unsure if he could see her out of the corner of his eye. But it doesn’t matter. What matters is that he already seems to be calmer and more confident. What matters is maybe she has finally found something that could help her child settle into his life as Zuko in the Earth Kingdom.

“So, what did you think?” Kani asks as they head back towards Feya’s house, warmth in her voice even if could feel anger coming off of her earlier.

Zuko isn’t exactly sure how chi works, but he knows that it is the energy flowing within a person, processed by both benders and nonbenders. Benders just have different pathways at which to express it. A way to connect with the elements and make it a part of them. It’s more that certain elements are able to flow through bender’s chi opposed to being able to command it.

Something that Lo had said was odd but made a weird amount of sense during her ramblings, especially as he could feel the anger radiating off of Kani despite her posture being still and relaxed, her expression calm and slack. He could just *feel* it so strongly. It was very directed, but not at either Zuko or Lo. He isn’t sure at who, but whoever it is, Zuko doesn’t want to be them.

Lo had talked about firebenders being aligned with power. That if they could connect with their chi, they could strengthen themselves, and those particularly connected could extend that strength to others.

That had caused Zuko to talk about how he could stoke his inner flame to keep himself warm and it would also keep him strong and alert. However, once he stopped, he could feel that energy being drained. It was really just back down to how he normally felt, but it would feel exhausting by comparison.

The old woman had suggested that Zuko, or Lee, as he had introduced himself to her, try and extend that strength to someone else, see if he could bring strength to them. That it might work better considering Zuko would be using his energy to strengthen their chi and they wouldn’t be draining themselves like Zuko is when warming himself.

He really is excited to try it, but part of him is pretty sure that she is just insane.

“She reminded me of my uncle.” Zuko finally whispers, smiling to himself. “I like her. She just kind of went on long tangents with complex lesions that don’t make much sense and maybe don’t mean anything anymore. My uncle did that too.”

“I’m glad you liked her. Do you feel better?” Kani asks, concern in her voice.

Zuko thinks for a moment before nodding. “Yeah. It helped me. I was just able to talk to her about things and she just listened to me and then comforted me like my uncle used to. I also really like Miyuki, she’s very snuggly and sweet.”

“I’m so happy you’re feeling better, my love.” Kani whispers as they continue to travel towards the market.

Zuko just smiles, nodding once. “Me too.”

When they get to the market, Kani picks up a few things including candy while Zuko waits for her. He really wants to stay longer than just a few days here. Even though he misses Chen and Fao, he likes the change in scenery. It’s nice to be somewhere else where he also feels safe. It makes him feel more like he has the ability to see the world even if he would likely stay with Kani and Chen for as long as possible. Sometimes, it’s the freedom of choice that curbs the need for wanderlust.

It doesn’t take long for them to get back to Feya’s after that. Kani and Zuko chatting as they walk. Now that he has calmed down from last night, the fact that Kani knows who he is and loves him anyways has taken such a huge weight off of his chest. Despite knowing that she wouldn’t cast him aside to begin with, he couldn’t stop the anxiety from gnawing at him.

Now all that is left is to tell Chen. If Chen isn’t as accepting, he is sure that Kani would stand up for him while the man has a moment to think and accept that, but Zuko is less worried about Chen’s reaction.

Chen is calm and predictable, Zuko likes that. It makes the man easy to be around when he’s panicking. It makes the man easier to trust and find comfort in.

When they get to the door, Zuko can hear something that sounds like a baby crying along with a frantic male voice talking along with Feya. “Is something wrong?” Zuko asks quietly.

Kani rests a hand on his shoulder, giving him a small smile. “Someone probably just had a baby. It’s a stressful process for everyone, especially the mother. I’m going to go help, I want you to go upstairs, okay, love?” Despite her reassurance, Zuko can see worry in her expression, like she knows *exactly* what is wrong.

The two walk in, Kani hurrying Zuko as much as she can without hurting him.

When they get into the main room filled with supplies and beds for the injured, he can see a man holding a crying bundle in his arms. Zuko can’t see the baby, but he can hear it just fine. On the bed there is a woman, the mother, is laying on one of the beds, looking to be unconscious… hopefully just unconscious.

Everyone that is around him is yelling as Kani leaves his side, running over to her sister. The two women are busy loudly discussing the state that the woman is in, none of which Zuko understands, just that it has taken a lot out of her.

At this point, the man, likely the father, is sitting on the ground, holding the child to his chest in one arm and holding the woman’s hand in the other, pressing her knuckles to his forehead, looking at the ground.

Despite being told to go upstairs, Zuko can’t stop himself from walking towards the bed, setting his crutch down, at this point used more for support than anything, and sitting on the other side of the woman, across from the man.

Either the man doesn’t care that Zuko is there or doesn’t notice. He stays in the same position he is in, whispering something quietly, silently tears rolling down his cheeks.

Zuko reaches one of his hands out, resting it on the woman’s stomach, praying that the old woman wasn’t crazy, that her late wife really was a particularly spiritual firebender finding new ways to use her bending. Apparently, she had successfully hidden her firebending from everyone but Lo for her entire life. He understands why from personal experience, but things could have been easier for him now if people had known that not every firebender is out for blood. Some just want to be safe and feel loved.

He breathes like he would to try and warm and strengthen himself but trying to reach his energy out.

As he starts to feel like this is pointless, that Lo is just crazy, and he is just going to be stressing everyone out by being in an area with people frantic to save this woman’s life, he can feel a swirling of energy. It’s weak and fading.

Zuko doesn’t know much about childbirth, but he lived most of his life listening to the conversations of servants and guards. Besides his mother, cousin, and uncle, they were the ones who didn’t use their words to hurt or threaten him. They all knew that they could say what they wanted in front of Zuko. That he was just lonely. That he wouldn’t dare speak to his father outside of a direct question and wouldn’t relay anything they said.

What he does know is childbirth is dangerous. That there are people who have lost daughters, wives, and friends in the process. Zuko isn’t sure if it is some transfer of energy to the baby or something he doesn’t understand.

What he does understand is that for whatever reason, the process weakened the woman in front of him. She isn’t conscious and isn’t strong enough right now to recover from injury sustained. He understands that Kani and Feya are trying to keep her alive until she recovers enough to heal on her own, but she might not make it until then. To heal on her own, she needs the strength of another to heal herself.

Zuko feels heat covering his body, energy almost like a slight electrical current but not in a bad way flowing down his arms. He can taste fire in his mouth and smell the smoke. He can hear yelling and footsteps and then…nothing.
