## Chapter 19

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Here we go. I had a lot of fun writing this chapter and I now have a updating schedule (Saturday mornings) now that I am settled into my schedule. Unfortunately, my tattoo appt got cancelled for the third time, but at this point, it's just kinda funny.

### Text

Kani isn’t fully sure what is going on. What she does know is that her sweet, well intentioned, idiot of a son had just started firebending in front of an unknown man. In front of a man who is scared, angry, and irrational. He had been firebending while laying his hands on the man’s wife who no one was admitting likely wouldn’t make it until the next morning. They all knew it, but none of them could say. No one could bring themselves to. The man needs to live in a world where she lived until he can’t lie to himself anymore.

She can hear the man screaming and see him swinging his free arm at her boy even though he’s already down and not moving. Not caring about how any of this makes her look, she rushes forward, clutching the tiny firebender in her arms, shielding him with her body.

Maybe the man thinks that Kani is keeping Zuko from hurting the woman or doesn’t want to hurt a healer, she doesn’t know. Either way, she doesn’t feel him swinging his arm not holding the still crying baby at Zuko.

“He’s just a child!” Kani shrieks at him, not looking up, clutching her unconcious, but steadily breathing, baby to her chest. “He’s not dangerous!” Not sure what the fuck Zuko was doing touching someone while breathing fire in frount of someone clearly greiving and in distress. Someone who is looking for someone to be angry at to deflect their pain. She’s seen it far too many times. She’ll yell at Zuko for being so stupid once she is sure that he’s okay.

“What kind of sick joke is this? Why do you, *healers* , have a fucking ashmaker here?” The man growls.

Kani slowly stands up, still clutching Zuko to her chest, and turns around. The man is holding his still screaming baby close to him in his right arm, anger, fear, and distress all clear on his face. Feya has the man’s left wrist in an iron grip, her expression completely stoic. Kani can only assume that the man hasn’t made any attempt to free himself because doing so might result in injury to his child.

At least he hasn’t let emotions *completely* cloud his judgment.

“He’s a scared little boy with nowhere to go. We found him half dead after someone he trusted tried to kill him. He’s not dangerous, he wasn’t trying to hurt your wife, I don’t know what he was doing, but I promise he wasn’t trying to hurt her. He doesn’t have a malicious bone in his body. He’s a stupid little boy who was being stupid. He just wants safety, that’s it. If you don’t tell anyone about him, I’ll take him out of town as soon as he regains consciousness.” She means it. Zuko has proved to her that he can’t be trusted yet to be in town.

The man glares at her, tugging on his wrist a little, Feya still stone still. “Fine. Just get it the fuck out of here and get *off* .” He snarls at Feya as she finally releases him.

Thankfully, the man kneels next to his wife’s bed, mostly ignoring Zuko, talking to her quietly.

Feya walks up to Kani, worry and anger in her expression. Most wouldn’t notice these emotions. Her sister doesn’t carry how she feels across her face but concentrated in her eyes. “Kani, I love you, and I love him b–”

“I meant what I said to him. As soon as Lee wakes up, I’m taking him back. He promised me he wouldn’t firebend in town and he broke that promise. He’s proven that he can’t be trusted here.” Kani assures her sister.

Feya nods once. “Good. They *will* hurt him, Kani. He’s still just a child and you *know* he can’t take much more. Check him. Just make sure he’s only unconscious, use whatever you need, then take him upstairs. I’ll stay down here and make sure Gaon doesn’t leave.” She nods toward the man kneeling by the bed. “He can’t have any proof of a firebender being here. Lee needs to be gone before he is so that no one gets hurt. Okay?”

Kani nods, not caring if the man can overhear them. They have nothing to hide now. He knows that Zuko is a firebender. As long as they get Zuko out of here and the man never sees the firebender again, she is sure that they won’t have an issue.

The two sisters are silent for a moment as Kani lays the firebender down, listening to his heartbeat and counting his breaths. “How is she?” She asks, eyes flitting to the woman despite already knowing the answer.

Feya shakes her head. “Breathing is shallow, slow, and irregular. Heartbeat is very faint. She’s not going to make it. Baby wasn’t born strong either…if he can make it through the next few days then he stands a chance…but without a wet nurse or some sort of supplement, I don’t think that will even matter.” This Feya says just under her breath. Even if the father knows this in his heart, they need to let him live in the world where in a few days he will be able to take his wife and son home. That the woman might need some help getting back on her feet for a few weeks but that he can nurse her back to health with time, diligence, and care. That they’ll be a family. Not that in a few hours, he’ll lose the woman he loves. And, possibly, in a few days, he might lose his son as well.

“What happened?” She asks, unsure what complications arose to this.

Feya shakes her head sadly. “Baby came almost two months too early. Very dangerous for both the mother and the child.” Kani knows this, but still, has to be said. She wants to comfort the man. He is about to lose everything. She wouldn be angry too if she knew that she was losing Chen and Zuko and there was nothing that she could do but hold onto them for as long as she could. She is almost sure she would lash out at anyone she didn’t fully know or who even just looked at her wrong.

The two women go silent again as Kani carefully examines Zuko’s skinny body, looking for any injuries, occasionally running her fingers through his dark hair. “You’re such a fucking idiot, sweetheart.” She whispers, pressing a kiss to her child’s forehead.

An exclamation comes from behind them and Kani and Feya turn around, almost sure that the man had just heard his wife’s last breath.

Instead, they hear him start half crying, half laughing, still clutching the baby in one arm, leaning over his wife with his head pressed to her shoulder and the woman’s hand limply resting against the back of his head.

“What’s going on? Is her condition changing? Let me see her.” Feya insits, kneeling by the other side of the bed peering at the woman’s face.

Before Feya can do much of anything, the man speaks. “She’s awake. Kya is awake.”

It’s a much longer night than Kani had anticipated. Gaon goes between accusing Zuko of trying to kill his wife, demanding to know if Zuko had done something to wake her up, or just trying to talk to the woman and get her to become more lucid. Feya continues to tend to Kya, doing her best to keep her strong enough to pull through. Even if she is never the same, never back to her strength before the child, it is far better than dying.

Kani does her best to help her sister. Most of that involves tending to the baby the best that she can while tending to her own child.

Thankfully, no matter what is going through his head right now in the midst of grief, confusion, and fear, the man makes no further attempts to bring any harm to Zuko. As long as that continues, there is no need for there to be any form of altercation.

It’s a little before midnight when Zuko starts stirring again, slowly opening his eyes and orrenting himself in the room.

As soon as he does, the man starts demanding answers from the barely lucid firebender. He stops when Feya threatens him.

Kani holds him to her chest, humming quietly, running her fingers through his hair, and quietly talking to him as he slowly becomes more aware of his surroundings. She isn’t sure exactly what had happened or what Zuko had done, but it had drained him instantly and almost completely. He had passed out around late afternoon and is finally waking now.

“My love, can you hear me?” Kani asks quietly, running her fingers through her sweet boy’s hair. “How are you feeling, sweetheart? You alright?”

“Hmmm. Just tired. Also hungry. Do we have food?” He asks, still resting against her chest but now eyes focused on her face, a warm look in his eyes.

“Yeah, of course.” If anything, she is grateful that Zuko is actually asking for something to eat without being prompted first. If her memory is correct, this may be the first time he’s done that. That’s progress. He’s still in trouble for firebending in front of complete strangers, but not until she is completely sure he’s alright. He needs to be safe and healthy before she scolds him for putting himself in so much danger even if he was just trying to help.

“Is she alright?” Zuko asks before Kani can even get up to see what Feya has that is just available to eat, assuming neither of them really want to cook right now, especially just for one person.

Kani cocks her head, unsure exactly what he is asking, wondering if he is worried about Lo. “The mom…is she alright? She was weak.” Zuko continues, snuggling a little closer to Kani but expression filled with concern.

“Did you do that? Did you wake her up?

Zuko jumps a little at the man’s unfamiliar voice, likely thinking he was just with family. He quickly sits up straighter, still pressed against Kani, eyes flitting between the man sitting by the bed and the woman lying in it.

“What did you do to her? You did something?” The man continues, curioriosity and mistrust both apparent.

Zuko shrugs, pressing against Kani. “Something I heard about. Can strengthen my own chi when I need to…heard that can be extended to others. Transfer strength and energy.” He whispers, interlacing his fingers with Kani’s.

Silence comes over the room before the man speaks again, appearing very conflicted with his words. “Can you do it again? She was barely breathing…then like, I dunno, ten minutes after you did you ashm–firebending, she woke up and talked to me for a little.” His words are frantic.

“She’s unconscious now, but her breathing is more regular, her heartbeat is stronger, and even if she is still a little cold, she is much closer to a healthy temperature.” Feya adds in, giving Zuko a warm smile.

Kani clutches her child closer to her chest before he can even say anything. “Even if he’s willing to, he needs to rest. He’s exhausted and still injured. If he can’t do anything more and you tell a single person that my child is a firebender, it will be the last mistake you make.” Kani threatens. She means it.

“Mom.” Zuko whispers, pulling her gaze from the man and back down to Zuko’s half focused golden eyes. Even if he looks dazed, his eyes look brighter and more beautiful than ever.

Firebenders and many Earth Kingdom nonbenders both have hazel eyes. However, the undertone of Earth Kingdom hazel is earthen and calm. Like Chen’s. The undertone of firebender eyes is gold. Upon a quick glance, not many can tell the difference. Most people have learned to identify firebenders by uniform, bending, or top knot, not by the difference in eye color.

Kani hadn’t been able to tell the difference before Zuko. She had never seen a firebender close enough to see their eyes up close. She had spent so much time gazing at the little boy’s face when healing him and trying to understand what was upsetting him. Trying to understand her baby a little more. At this point, she is sure she could distinguish a firebender among a crowd by eyes alone. She now knows the distinct shape and glint of them.

“What is it, Lee?” She asks gently, needing to make sure that Feya and Zuko are sure to use Zuko’s Earth Kingdom name in front of these people. If Zuko can help them and they think he is just some peasant firebender kid with a terrifying past who just wants to get a chance to be a child in the Earth Kingdom, they’ll very likely keep their mouths shut. No reason to get a kid who means no harm killed.

However, even if they do believe that he just wants safety and love, being the Fire Prince might make that obsolete. The son of the Fire Lord is an enemy to them. Royals never really get to be children, especially when their father is a tyrant. It’s why, even if it can be irritating some days, Kani is always so happy to see Zuko do stupid things with Fao that only 12 year old boys would think to do, or sneak in the chicken cat because he wants something to snuggle with. She loves watching her baby who was forced to grow up the moment he had a cohesive grasp on life learn to be a child.

“It’s fine. I want to try at least. Was only ever taught how to use my bending to destroy. Want to use it to heal. Help people.” He mumbles, closing his eyes, resting his forehead against Kani’s neck. “In a bit. Tired.”

Kani smiles, rubbing his back. “Do you still want something to eat? I’m sure there is something.” She offers.

When Zuko nods, she lays him on the bed, hesitant to leave him with the man who can’t seem to figure out or express exactly how he feels about Zuko. He had been furious for a firebender existing in his vicinity and accused a child of trying to kill his almost dead wife and is now begging for Zuko’s help. Despite the fact that Kani completely understands where he is coming from, knowing she wouldn’t be rational in his position, it doesn’t mean she trusts him with her nearly defenseless child.

At least Feya is here. The man is a nonbender as far as Kani is aware. Even though neither her or her sister are trained in fighting, she doubts the man is either. By the stark differences in his skin color on his arms, she can only assume that he is a fisherman or farmer, likely the former if he lives in town. Anyways, someone throwing a rock is still throwing a rock.

“Kani, do you think you could boil some eggs for everyone? I don’t think this is going to be over anytime soon. We all need our strength.”

After eating and discussing for a while, everyone that is conscious agrees that it would be best for everyone to go upstairs to Feya’s home. The apprentices and assistants will take over downstairs for the day, taking care of anyone who comes in with general injuries. If someone has a question, Feya can go downstairs.

Neither Kani nor Feya got a chance to sleep last night and will take turns sleeping while one makes sure that Zuko is alright. On top of that, Feya doesn't fully trust Gaon to not freak out on Zuko again.

No one can see Zuko firebending. The people who know have to stay in these walls. It has to be a secret. It can’t spread through the town that the healer is harboring a firebender. People might want to hurt him or he might become a spectacle.

If the wrong people saw him, it would only be a matter of time that the word got around that Lee is really Zuko. Town wouldn’t be safe for him anymore. The village might not even be safe for him. There might not be anywhere that Zuko could hide the moment the Fire Lord caught wind that his son is alive. If the Earth Kingdom army wants to capture him and try and get information out of him or ransom him to the Fire Lord thinking they could turn the tides of the war.

When Zuko is up and walking again, Feya takes his shoulder, gazing into his eyes, needing the truth. “Are you ready to try this again?” She asks.

Zuko nods. He is far more enthusiastic than she would like him to be about showing off his firebending to someone who has made it clear that he hates all firebenders. Soldier or civilian. Man or boy. On top of that, Zuko seems to have very little idea about what he is doing and is figuring out either a new or obscure subelement of firebending that Feya has never even heard of before.

The little firebender walks back over to the mother, resting his hands against her stomach as flames come from his mouth and his arms and hands turn a glowing red.

Iroh knocks on Azula’s door, hoping that his niece is awake. Hoping that she is alright. He doesn’t know much, but he knows that it was another brutal training session today and that she is absolutely exhausted. At least today Iroh has something that will hopefully cheer her up.

Earlier, he had gone down to the kitchen while Azula was bathing and changing, asking for some servants to bring up a pot of ginseng tea with two cups, a bowl of noodle soup, and a fruit tart. His niece needs to eat and rest.

“Come in.” Azula calls in a halfhearted tone likely more from exhaustion than apathy as Iroh walks in.

Azula is laying on her bed, propped up against pillows, a book in her lap but it isn’t open. She likely was going to read but found herself too exhausted to even try. Her eyes are closed even if she clearly is conscious enough to be somewhat aware of her surroundings.

Sitting on the side of her bed, Iroh takes his niece's hand in his own, looking down at her slack expression. “How are you feeling, Princess Azula?” He asks.

“Shitty.” She mumbles. She certainly does have a mouth for an eleven year old. Likely because she has grown up around seasoned soldiers most of her life who constantly forget to watch their language. They figure that if someone is old enough to watch their fellow soldiers die, they are old enough to hear a few curse words.

Iroh chuckles at her response instead of telling her to watch her tongue. She has enough restrictions in her life. He gently cups her cheek, examining her face before talking. “The servants are bringing you something to eat and drink. Eat what you can. Once they leave, I got another letter from a carrier pigeon, with an Earth Kingdom ribbon, and a turtle duck seal.

At that comment, Azula’s eyes finally open. “Zuzu?” She whispers.

“Maybe. I don’t know if it is really him. I don’t know why he wouldn’t just sign his name. I don’t know if he thinks this is funny I–” Iroh cuts himself off, wiping tears from his eyes as two servants walk in, setting trays on a table.

One tries to approach Iroh but he brushes them off, needing them to leave. He needs to be able to talk to Azula.

Iroh doesn’t know if he really thinks it’s Zuko but just has doubts or if he knows deep in his heart his nephew is dead and can’t admit it to himself. Can’t admit that he has allowed a second son to perish while trying to give in to a request that they had begged for with so much enthusiasm. When they had just wanted to prove themselves.

Even if it *is* Zuko, Iroh doesn’t actually think that Zuko is doing it as a joke. He isn’t cruel. Even if some days Iroh is angry at Zuko for leaving without him, he knows it wasn’t out of malice, it was out of fear. He was terrified, humiliated, confused, and in agony. Zuko had been incapable of rational thought when he ran. He was operating purely on instinct.

Up until the first letter, Iroh had been sure that instinct had gotten his sweet nephew killed. Now, he isn’t sure. He doesn’t know if the false hope is worse.

“Uncle, remember, we promised that we would assume he is alive. We would assume that he is with a loving Earth Kingdom family where they are taking such good care of him. Where he is safe from father. Maybe he’s even in Ba Sing Se.” Azula jokes, squeezing Iroh’s hand.

“He’s outside of Si Lang. I checked, it’s a harbor town off of the west coast. That’s on the opposite side of the continent from Ba Sing Se.” Iroh corrects her, smiling.

Azula sticks her tongue out at him. “I know, uncle, I’m not an idiot.” She mumbles, making a grabby hand at the soup.

Iroh chuckles, carefully handing it to her as she props herself into a better sitting position.

“Read it to me. Wanna know what Zuzu said.”

Iroh smiles, carefully breaking the seal and beginning to read the contents of the letter allowed to Azula as he reads it for the first time as well.

“General Iroh, I have finally been able to make it into the harbor town of Si Lang and can send a letter to you myself. A friend of the family who took me in sent the previous letter that I wrote and I can only hope that it got to you. I would like to travel up to the colonies to get a better sense of home, but for now, Si Lang will have to suffice.” He begins, stopping for a moment as he takes in the possibility of having an actual location for his nephew even if just for a little. He *needs* to know if Zuko is alive, and if he doesn’t find him, he can always tell himself that Zuko had left for the colonies or returned to the village. He could still have that false sense of hope.

“I don’t know if I will be able to stay for long, but I can see the ocean here, something I have missed greatly about the Fire Nation. From where I lived and grew up before following you into battle, I could almost always see the sea. Even if it’s too cold to swim in during this time of year, the familiarity is comforting. I like the sound and the smell. There is a lot that I have tried to find comfort in, knowing that it is unlikely I will ever see the homeland again. Thankfully, I have found good, kind people who make it easier to make a life here.”

“I am staying with the town healer while here and hopefully I can learn a few things from her. Gracious Earth Kingdom healers are the only reason that I am alive today and if I cannot fight anymore, I would like to learn to heal. What I can think of now is how helpful of a skill it would have been if I knew it at Ba Sing Se. We could have returned with more soldiers still living. I may have been able to return at all. I’m not sure if injury or simple bad luck is what got me captured, but I would like to think maybe things could have been different.” Iroh now has a particular person to look for that people of the town will easily be able to point to. Every town knows where their healer lives off the top of their head. They never want to try and figure that out when injured. Iroh could really get an answer. For better or for worse, he could know for certain if his nephew is safe.

“I don’t know if we will ever meet again, but I hope that we can. Everything you had told me before that was lost on me is all making sense now. Every piece of wisdom you shared with me I am trying to recall and decipher, try and apply it to my life. It may be all of what I have left of before. I want to have a life that I can be happy with here, but I don’t want to forget who I was, who I am.”

“What I do know is that you told me time and time again to never give up without a fight. I won’t. No matter what happens, if I return to the village, stay here, make it to the colonies, or back to the Fire Nation, no one can take any of my life from me anymore. It won’t be stolen through fear, imprisonment, or pain. I have spent too much time dwelling on what has happened and what horrible things the future may hold, but for now, I’ll try to focus on the present. I will try and focus on the fact that I have been taken in by good, kind people who will do their best to keep me healthy. That I have forged new relationships with people who I once saw so different from myself. Even if I didn’t know it at the time, you knew what you were talking about.”

“I hope that our paths will cross again, your friend and obedient servant, Lee.”

After he finishes reading, Iroh goes silent, looking at the paper in dispealeaf, fresh tears rolling down his cheeks. He has something that looks so mundane but could contain something to bring a part of his heart that died with Zuko back to life. Something that could reunite Azula with her brother now as someone who misses him deeply opposed to relishing in his suffering. He could have more of his family back.

It could also lead to devastation if Zuko isn’t really there. It could shatter his heart all over again if he really believes that Zuko is living and he finds nothing. It will be like losing his sweet nephew all over again.

“You're going, aren’t you?” Azula asks, voice flat, face expressionless.

“To Si Lang?” Iroh asks, rolling up the letter, turning it over in his hands.

Azula nods. “Please go. You need to know if he’s alive. I need that, too. He needs to know that you still love him and would do anything for him. He needs to know how sorry I am for everything I put him through. That we’re happy he has found a home. Please…I need to know if it’s him. He said so himself, he won’t be there for long.” She says softly, sipping at her broth.

“Would you be joining me?” Iroh asks after a long pause. He really would like an excuse to get his niece away from her father even if for two weeks. She needs to stretch out without her father’s presence crushing her at every turn. Without him refusing to let her grow and change.

Azula shakes her head. “Father wouldn’t allow it. Anyways, I don’t think you can come up with any reason to bring me to a discrete town in the Earth Kingdom. He can’t know that you're hiding where you're going. Just tell him about Lee and how he was your friend and that you want to help him get back to the colonies or the Fire Nation or whatever. Go on some long, emotional tangent so that he stops listening to you and is practically begging you to go just to get rid of you.”

Iroh rests his hand on her forehead, looking at Azula sadly. She is too smart for her age. Usually, that would be good, but it isn’t just because of her natural intelligence, it is because she was forced to grow up too soon. She is being treated like a woman, like a soldier, when she is still just a girl.

Azula is smart, strong, and brave, but she is still only eleven. She should be playing with dolls, with her friends, or whatever little girls do. One thing they shouldn’t be doing is planning a real stakes operation around deception with the most powerful and dangerous man in the world to try and find someone who is supposed to be dead. That is not what any little girl should be expected to do.

“I *will* get you out of here, Princess Azula. When the time is right, I will take the throne from my brother. Then I’ll bring you and your brother back here. You’ll be safe. You’ll be able to live.” He promises, pressing a kiss to his niece’s temple. He can’t lose her too. She is everything to him now if Lee isn’t Zuko. If it’s some kind of cruel prank. He can’t risk anything happening to her while going up against Ozai. His brother has proved that he will not spare his children in his desire for power.

Unfortunately, Azula shakes her head. “He’ll kill you, uncle. You know he will. You know how strong he is. You know he doesn’t care about you. When the time comes, I’ll be bigger and stronger. He’s turning me into the ultimate weapon and I’ll use that against him. He won’t be able to take both of us. I need to at least *try* and get vengeance. For me. For Zuzu.”

Sighing, Iroh rests his hand on her arm as her hands are occupied with her bowl. “I will have old friends to help me. Friends who want your father gone as much as we do. We’ll talk about this another time. I have a lot to tell you. If I had just been completely honest with your brother, then maybe…” He trails off, closing his eyes.

Maybe if Zuko knew about the White Lotus, if he knew they were waiting as long as they could for the Avatar, if he knew about the end date of the war predetermined in the cosmos coming up far sooner than Ozai has let slip to more than his most trusted generals, things might be different. He might still be here. He might not have a burn so terrible it kept him unconscious for four consecutive days. Iroh might not be grasping at letters coming from someone who thought that they were closer to Iroh than they really were in hopes of some kind of favor. He might not be pretending that some forgotten soldier is his dead nephew.

“Well maybe you should start to tell me.” Azula argues, setting her bowl to the side. “It sounds like there is a lot of history so just tell me a little bit about it. Please, uncle. Help me understand or when the time comes, whatever that is supposed to mean, I won’t leave. I’ll stand by your side doing my best while in the dark. I’m not leaving you unless you have a damn good reason.”

He meets Azula’s golden eyes and she is being completely sincere. She doesn’t make threats lightly. Not to anyone. Especially to the few people she doesn’t want to hurt. As far as Iroh is concerned, that list is now exclusive to himself, Mai, and Ty Lee.

Sighing, Iroh digs around in his robes before pulling out the worn white lotus Pai Sho tile, pressing it into Azula’s palm.

Not surprisingly, Azula raises an eyebrow. “Are you starting a secret Pai Sho club?” She teases, turning the piece over in her hand. “Your favorite one, if I remember correctly.” She mumbles.

Iroh chuckles sadly, shaking his head. “As I’m sure you know, after Lu Ten died, I didn’t return along with my men to the Fire Nation. I wandered for almost six months until I could bring myself to come home without my boy.” He begins, remembering how he always felt like he was being followed by someone but couldn’t bring himself to care enough. If they killed him, at least he would be with his son again. If anything, he felt more like it was the people whose deaths he had caused over the years, following him, demanding that he know he got more than just *his* son killed. Demanding that he grieve for the families that he tore apart and destroyed. Grieve for those whose bodies were never found and families lived in denial, waiting for them to come home when they never would. Demanding he understand the real weight of war.

“When I returned to the Fire Nation, before I could even make it into the palace, I ran into your brother’s sword master, Piando. He gave me this and told me about how I was being observed as I traveled. He told me about an organisation made up of old masters doing their best to keep balance in the world without the Avatar. The order of the White Lotus.” He explains. He is well aware that he is making it out to be far more simple than it actually was. It had taken hours for Piando to convince Iroh to actually listen to him after he had admitted that members of this organization were following him to gather what kind of man he was becoming. To see how his son’s death has changed him.

Azula grins, holding the tile tighter. “If you told me that Pai Sho was connected to treason, I would have been far more interested in the game.” She jokes, moving closer to Iroh, wanting to know more. He can see the childlike excitement in her eyes. He wishes that she could look like this about games or seeing her friends, not about an organization that could very well get themselves killed with one wrong move. For the billionth time, he wishes that his niece could just be a child, not a soldier.

Chuckling softly, Iroh smiles a little at her. He should have just shared a lot more of his life with Zuko. It would have made things easier for both of them. “People had been watching me. They knew that I had lost my son and that was why I pulled my troops out of Ba Sing Se. They wanted to see if I was willing to accept a completely different narrative of the war besides something I believed in and would be proud that my son gave his life for. Also, it would make it easier if they had a member of the royal family with them. Could make it easier to plan for the right time. When it’s time to stop waiting for the Avatar and move on without them. Accept that we no longer have one and need to balance the world ourselves.”

Azula grins, flipping the tile in the air and catching it. “Were they also in desperate need of a firebender?” She asks, a genuinely curious look in her eyes, not mocking. That question is likely more targeting the fact that Iroh is a feared general in the Earth Kingdom and a member of the most hated family in the world. He doubts that she is making any jab at his skills like she would have only a few months ago. He really wishes that they could have just gotten closer with time and effort, not over Zuko’s death.

“Ironically, they already have a firebender, a deserter by the name of Jong Jong. Out of the five lead members, three of us are Fire Nationals.” He explains, having been surprised at that himself. Almost all of the supporting members working as entail and backup are Earth Kingdom. He is still surprised at how quickly they were willing to trust firebenders. The Dragon of the West at that.

Smirking, Azula meets his eyes, almost like she is trying to hide her excitement and interest in what Iroh is saying. “You should have told me sooner. I would have thought you were cool ages ago.” She jokes, but at the same time, he is pretty sure that she is being genuine. “What else? Do you go out every night committing treason? Do you have a home in Ba Sing Se? What else is there about your super secret lotus life.”

Iroh smiles at his niece, feeling closer to her. “That’s enough for now. I’ll tell you more. I’ll teach you what I can. Just promise me you’ll never share any of it with your father.” Iroh whispers, running his fingers through some of Azula’s long, black hair.

“Uncle, he would kill you if he found out. I’m not letting him take anyone else. Anyways, even if I did only care about myself, I know that I’m only a few wrong moves away from ending up like Zuzu. He doesn’t give a shit about me and I’m not stupid enough to think otherwise.” She admits, a distant, sad look on her expression.

“I hope you know that your father doesn’t love you because he’s a monster with a black, twisted heart, not because you aren’t worthy of love. I love you so much, Azula. I couldn’t protect my son or Zuko. I gave into requests that they made over and over again that I always felt was a bad idea. If I’m begging you to not do something, it isn’t because I don’t trust you or because I don’t think you can handle it. It’s because I don’t trust your father. I can’t lose you, too, Azula. I know you’re becoming a very strong, intelligent, and capable young woman, but please, let me protect you. If your brother is dead, you’re the only family I have left. Let me keep you safe.” He pleads, knowing Azula could certainly just ignore everything and inadvertently put herself in danger. Get herself killed.

Like his nephew had.

Like his son had.

Azula doesn’t answer for a moment, and Iroh half expects her to tell him to piss off and that she isn’t a child even though she is. She’s never been allowed to act like a child and no longer sees herself as one. Doesn’t understand that at eleven, she is just a little girl still.

“I take it you don’t consider father your family?” She eventually asks, taking his hand in hers, looking at the ceiling.

Iroh shakes his head. “No. I’m ashamed to be related to him. Even if he is my brother, he isn’t my family. You are.”

Azula looks back at him, a grin back on her face. “I’m your brother?”

“Shut the fuck up, kid. You know what I meant.” He grumbles, trying to hide a small smile. His niece has been developing a sense of humor the last few months. It suits her.

“But seriously, uncle. You need to talk to father today about taking a small crew to… what’s it called? Si Lang? You said so yourself that he might not be there for long. I need to know if he’s alive. I need to know if he really is okay. Please find him.” She practically begs, eyes wide.

Iroh gives her a sad smile. “I will. Do you want me to ask him if I could bring you with me? It would be a brief trip and I could say something about teaching you to sail in winter on a low stakes journey and also possibly give you a chance to see the colonies.” Iroh offers, hoping that he could reunite the siblings even if for a few short days.

Azula sighs, frowning. “I dunno. I want to go…but father doesn’t like that I’m spending time with you. I told him that you’re easy to boss around because you’re lonely and desperate. That it’s more of a relationship of convenience than anything now that Ty Lee is traveling with the circus and Mai’s father is more busy and I don’t really have any better company. If he asks me if I’m going, I’ll have to act like I don’t care. I do…but I can’t. I’m sure you know why.” Azula says softly.

Iroh knows exactly what she means. It would mean a lot of pain for everyone if Ozai were to find out that Azula and Iroh were actually close. If that man *ever* found out that Azula is closer to her uncle than her father, it could be Iroh’s execution and Azula’s life made so much worse.

“I understand, Azula. Thank you for doing what you can to protect yourself.” He means it. He would rather Azula insult Iroh to his face than to put herself in danger by hinting that Iroh is better at anything than Ozai besides at making tea. It could even end up getting her killed. That is a line that Ozai has proved that he doesn’t seem to think exists

“Thank you.” She says softly, smiling. “I need to sleep. Talk to him. We need to find Zuko. I need to know if he’s okay. Please.” She whispers, closing her eyes.

Iroh silently stands, taking the Pai Sho piece back, kissing Azula’s temple again and leaving the room praying that she will be alright. Praying that she will see her brother again.

Now for the hard part. He needs to look his brother in the eyes and speak to him for the first time since that man had killed Iroh’s sweet, sensitive nephew.

He needs to find a way to speak to that man without lunging at his throat and getting himself, and possibly Azula, killed. Iroh can’t leave her alone. She’ll either break or become someone cruel and unrecognizable. Ozai can’t take Azula too.

It takes a few days to get Kya and the child out of danger. Zuko still isn’t completely sure what he’s doing. He is sometimes able to preserve his own strength and sometimes passes out from exhaustion. He isn’t sure how he is making it so he can have enough energy to be able to talk and eat while getting back to full strength, but is determined to figure it out. He is going to figure this out. He is going to learn how to preserve himself and make this a more effective form of healing that doesn’t take three consecutive day to get a grown woman to a state where she will need to rest and be taken care of for a few weeks and an infant to be healthy enough to survive and strengthen in his own time.

All Zuko can do now is lay down by the fire, holding his crochet turtle duck as Kani sits next to him, gently playing with his hair, humming the tune of an Earth Kingdom lullaby quietly. It feels nice. Helps soothe his nerves and helps him collect his scattered thoughts. It makes it easier for him to just rest.

He can hear Feya and Gaon talking in the next room, but he can’t bring himself to pay attention to what they’re saying. It’s likely either more instructions as to how the man will have to care for his wife until she makes as full of a recovery as she can or threatening him if he exposes Zuko as a firebender. It could be a mix of both. Either way, he trusts that she is making sure that Zuko will be safe and Kya and the baby will be cared for.

The man had made it clear that he hated all firebenders in the beginning and that Zuko was no exception. However, over the last few days, he had slowly started to come around to Zuko as his wife and son gained strength. As he had watched the woman he loved slowly come back to life with Zuko’s fire.

He had brought Zuko blankets, wrapping them around his shoulders when he just had to collapse against a wall, unable to get himself somewhere more comfortable. Gaon had sat next to him, occasionally talking to him, learning more about each other's lives.

Zuko had learned that Gaon is a fisherman living by the coast with his wife. That this is their first child and almost certainly their last with the compliations. Gaon goes out fishing most days and Kya is a baker.

In the summer, late spring, and early fall, she’ll make tarts, pies, jams, cakes, cookies, and bread. In the winter and when luxury foods are scarce, if not completely unavailable, she makes bread and buns with whatever she can find. In years where the town nearned famine near the end of the season, she would cut the flour with sawdust. Everyone who eats it is well aware of the contents, but apparently she is good enough to make it almost impossible to taste it. The bread is just a little gritty. But when people are hungry, they’ll happily eat it and feed it to their hungry children until there are options.

They sell both of their goods at the market and use it to sustain their family, compiling foods they make and catch with their neighbors who have a small, but surprisingly productive garden behind their home.

It sounds like a nice life. That the child is going to grow up in a loving home with parents who care for each other. Something Zuko didn’t have until Chen found him.

What Zuko finds most comforting is that once Kya is out of danger, any hint of the man’s previous anger completely dissipates. It is comforting that Gaon is not regularly an angry man. That he was reacting on instinct and trying to protect his family from someone he perceived as a threat after adopting the narrative of firebenders as the enemy into his schema likely since he was very young.

Zuko doesn’t share as much information about his life as Gaon shared about his. He doesn’t really want to and it also isn’t safe to. He can’t go around sharing the fact that he is the Fire Lord’s son. He can’t even give information that could lead to that conclusion in an area where so much information gets around.

Zuko tells the man that he had to flee his home after someone who he thought cared about him attacked him with the intent to kill him, heavily implying, but not explicitly saying so, that he is from the colonies opposed to the Fire Nation. Zuko tells him that Chen, Kani’s husband, found him half dead in the woods during a storm. That the couple has been caring for him for the past few months and Zuko wants to learn how to heal people and help them like Kani had done for him. How she had saved him when he was on the brink of death.

When Gaon had asked what his life was like before, Zuko just shook his head, affirming that he didn’t want to discuss it. That he wanted to just forget about everything that happened to him before he was taken into a safe, loving home.

Even if Zuko knows that Gaon is grateful and has stated several times that he wouldn’t tell anyone about Zuko being a firebender, he can’t stop the anxiety from welling up in his chest about what might happen if the man is toying with him. If he gets home and decides that he doesn’t care if Zuko helped his family and that he is still a firebender. An ashmaker.

“Are you doing alright, my love?” Kani asks, still carding her fingers gently through his hair, not leaving his side for even a moment.

Zuko shrugs, not really wanting to discuss exactly what he is feeling and is confused if he feels safe and accepted or in danger and manipulated. He really doesn’t know what the future will hold and he is trying to keep it from stressing him out too horribly.

“Guess we missed the play anyways.” He settles on saying, smiling up at Kani.

Kani laughs softly, pressing a kiss to the top of his head. “I know you were excited and I’m sorry you missed it, but you saved two people. Also, you were stupid to firebend in frount of a random person. It was reckless, dangerous, and so incredibly stupid…but I’m glad you did it. I love you, sweetheart, and I don’t want anything to happen to you. I was so scared he was going to tell someone and the military was going to take you from me before I could get you somewhere safe.” She explains softly.

Kani calling him stupid feels completely different that when when his father would.

When Ozai did, it was about breaking Zuko down, making him feel small and worthless. Making him feel more of a need to prove himself to a man who would always see him as less. As a failure. As nothing but a stain on the family tree that needed to be removed.

In Kani’s defense, what he did *was* pretty stupid. He heard of a new subelement of firebending from a woman who very likely could just be completely insane and immediately tried it out in front of a panicked and grieving husband and father who has grown up learning to fear firebenders.

Despite that, Kani isn’t tearing him down for his choices. She isn’t making him feel like a complete idiot or that he is incapable of doing anything right. She is making him understand that she was *scared* for him. Scared that something might happen that she couldn’t protect him from as a result of his choices.

“Are we going to stay long enough for another one?” Zuko asks hopefully, almost sure that as soon as he gets back to strength Kani is going to take him home and decline to bring him back again because of the danger he put himself in.

“I’m not sure, we’re gonna see. I’m not going to promise you anything, but this might change things. You could help a lot of people.” She whispers, smiling down at him.

Meeting her eyes, Zuko can’t help but to smile a little. “You mean I could stay? Try and get better at this?” He asks, unsure if he actually wants that or not. He really wants to find ways to use his bending to help people, to undo some of the pain his family has caused the world, but he is also sure that Kani will need to return to the village. No matter what he can do, he is very hesitant to be separated from Kani and Chen for whatever reason that may be.

“I’m not sure. There’s a lot that we aren’t sure of right now. Where did you learn to do that, anyways?” She asks, raising an eyebrow.

“Lo mentioned that her…that she knew someone who was able to transfer energy to another person. So I tried it.” He explains.

Frowning, Kani takes a deep breath. “So a woman I told you was going insane told you about some obscure bending technique and you decided to use it at the first opportunity?”

Zuko nods, not even trying to defend himself on that one.

“You’re a fucking idiot, sweetheart. I’m glad that it worked, but that was a stupid move. I know you want to help people, and you did good, but if that hadn’t worked, things would be very different right now.” She repeats, taking his hand. “I can’t lose you, my love. You’re family now. You’re my child.”

“I’ll be more careful, mom. I promise.” He means it. He doesn’t want to ruin the life he has now. The second chance at being happy, safe, and loved he finally has.

Kani smiles, pressing another kiss to his forehead. “Thank you. I love you so much, Zuko.” She whispers under her breath so that Gaon and his family can’t hear her use his real name.

The two sit quietly for nearly an hour, Zuko falling half asleep by the fire, Kani laying down next to him, holding him close, lazily running her fingers over his arm, keeping him safe.

Zuko is sure that he could just fall asleep right here, curled up next to the fire, his mom holding him and keeping him safe. On top of that, he is feeling absolutely exhausted from generating and expending so much energy when he still isn’t sure how to do it efficiently, or really even properly.

He is pulled out of that when he can hear Kani and Feya talking to each other and feel Kani let go of him, moving away. He doesn’t want her to go. He wants her to keep holding him. He wants to fall asleep curled up in the safety of her arms.

As she moves away from him, Zuko slowly sits up, leaning against the wall, feeling like he could eat three dinners and sleep for days. He watches as Kani, Feya, and Gaon stand together, talking about something he can’t quite make out. If he’s being honest, he isn’t particularly invested. All of their facial expressions look slack and casual, likely not discussing anything of great importance.

The turtle duck keeps him occupied until Gaon comes over to him. Zuko just runs his fingers over the creature’s head, appreciative that Feya had used a soft yard that felt somewhat like a turtle duckling’s head, just less warm and wet.

“Lee?” Gaon asks softly as Zuko looks up, meeting the man’s dark brown eyes, not the typical hazel of the Earth Kingdom nonbenders.

“Hmm?” Is all he replies, still half occupied with his turtle duck, still trying to settle on a name for it.

“Thank you, for everything.” He whispers, thanking Zuko for what he is doing and what he had done for the upteenth time. He is hesitant, but eventually, Gaon rests his hand on Zuko’s shoulder, giving him a small, but grateful smile.

“Thank you for saving my family. I’m sorry for lashing out at you when we first met. I thought you were going to hurt her.” He explains even though this is something that Zuko fully understands. He knows just as much as anybody how losing a person who anchors you so suddenly can affect you. As much as he tries to forget about it, he can’t push what he did to himself, tried to do, and considered to do when his mother left. He is well aware that Gaon was just grieving even though he hadn’t quite lost his wife.

Neither Kani nor Feya have told him explicitly, but he has over heard bits and pieces of their conversations the past few days. They were both pretty convinced that the mother, Kya, was going to die from this. That even though the son was weak he could grow strong with time, likely just look a little younger until he hit puberty, much like Zuko but for different reasons. However, if the mother died, that chance would decline if the father couldn’t find a way to feed the baby properly.

Now, this has changed to the mother likely recovering in two to three weeks with proper bed rest and her only task really consisting of feeding the baby and herself. With the mother living, the baby will almost certainly live without some other unseen or unpredictable variable.

“You like turtle ducks?” Gaon eventually asks, looking at the toy still in Zuko’s lap as he continues to absentmindedly run his fingers across the crochet creature.

Zuko nods, smiling. “They’re my favorite. They kept me company before I came here.” He explains, touching it’s beak with the tip of his pointer finger.

“Did you not have many friends back…where you’re from?” Gaon asks, looking down at Zuko.

“Wasn’t allowed to have friends. Didn’t deserve them.” He answers quietly before he can stop himself, inadvertently dampening the mood.

Clearly, Gaon has no idea how to respond to that as he just goes quiet for a few moments. “Feya has contacted a friend of mine to bring a carriage over here to help my wife get home, she’ll be here soon.” He says instead, a way of saying that he’ll be leaving soon. “I know that there is a lot of hatred for firebenders, no matter who they are, something I have contributed to as well. I was wondering if you want me to tell anyone that a firebender saved Kya. I wouldn’t give your name or anything, could say you showed up or something. Just wondering if you want people to know that firebenders can be healers. That they can help the people of the Earth Kingdom and not stand with the war.”

Zuko looks over at his bag, silent for a moment before putting the turtle duck down, digging through it and pulling at his Blue Spirit mask, examining it. The mask he had used to disguise his identity while firebending in the woods near Kani and Chen’s house. The one Chen had given him for reasons Zuko is still unsure of. However, there is a complete possibility that the man just knew Zuko loves theater and thought the mask looked cool.

“The Blue Spirit.” He whispers. “You can refer to me as The Blue Spirit.”

### End Notes
