## Chapter 20

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

My roommate is a big batman fan and so she was showing me some movies and shows because disney ruined marvel so I guess I need a new franchise. I have recently learned that a) there are multiple Robins, b) they are all pretty much batman's son as in like they live with him and he raises them and whatever, and c) he is a child. My entire life I have just been vaguely aware that a good amount of people have said that they're a couple, and because their costumes make it hard to distinguish age, I naturally assumed that Robin was a grown ass man. So I am still emotionally recovering from the fact that Robin is a child and not a twink.

More importantly: I ordered tea and it came. They have these blends styled after the Avatar characters and I got the Uncle Iroh blend (along with just like a good amount of normal tea like lemongrass and jasmine) and it is really good

### Text

“Kid…why do you have that mask? I mean, I guess it’s helpful if you want to disguise your face *now* , but why did you bring it when you *didn’t* know you were going to be putting your life on the line with no forethought?” Feya asks once the family leaves, pinching the bridge of her nose.

“Chen got it for me. I miss him.” Zuko explains, which is mostly true. That *is* why he thought to bring it. He also brought it in case he got a chance to practice his firebending and needed to hide his face no matter how unlikely that would be. He really had mostly just wanted the sentiment.

Kani gives Zuko a sad look, resting a hand on his shoulder. “Zuko, my love, I know you’re still in the beginning of recovery. You need to tend to what you need before anything else. I know that we implied that you could help people while staying here, but if you need to come home and finish healing yourself, please come.” She assures him softly. “If you want to see Chen, come home. You’re still just a little boy. You need to take care of yourself first. It’s only been a few months and you’re recovering from a lifetime of abuse while trying to learn how to live as a different person in a different place and leave behind everything you knew. We can’t expect you to be ready to change everything because of a subelement you discovered.”

Zuko nods his head, really having no idea what he wants. There have been so few times in his life that he has had real options with unforeseen risks and benefits, he doesn’t know how to go about this.

When he was back in the Fire Nation, people pretty much made all of Zuko's decisions for him. What he was allowed to wear, where he was supposed to go, how he had to talk, when he trained, when and what he ate, and who he could see. Deviation from the confines of what he was allowed to do would result in punishment directly from his father. Sometimes he wasn’t even sure if he messed up but had learned quickly not to defend himself. It only made things worse.

So much worse.

Then, when Zuko was with Kani and Chen, he had choices, but they were limited. Most of that restriction wasn’t intentionally placed there by the couple and it was never out of malice. However, all of the decisions he could make throughout the day were minor and with the bigger ones, there was really only one good option.

He had the choice to put his life in Kani and Chen’s hands where they could do anything they wanted with him and Zuko couldn’t stop them or he could run back into the storm when sick and injured. He could see his friend or he could be alone. He could hide and lie about so much of who he is through repressing everything about his very nature or risk being chased out and arrested.

As the thoughts of how Zuko found a compromise for the last one through firebending in the woods with the mask on flow into his head, he feels a tugging of guilt in his stomach, looking down. The other reason why he brought the mask with him.

“Kani?” He begins, looking up at her but quickly averting his eyes.

“What is it, love? Are you alright?” The farmer asks, gently cupping Zuko’s face in her hands as she kneels down to be at eye level with him.

“When I was practicing firebending back at home in the woods, I was wearing this to hide my face in case anyone saw me. I *did* bring it here for something to remind me of Chen, but also in case I could practice firebending again. *Real* firebending, not just lighting fires in stoves. It helps calm me.” He explains, unable to meet her eyes.

He can hear Kani sigh but still can’t look at her. “Zuko…you know that’s really dangerous, right?” She asks calmly. Zuko can’t bring himself to answer as he feels his eyes burn. He pulls his face out of her hands so he can look down and places his hands in hers instead.

Squeezing them gently, Kani starts talking again. “It was different when you were back home. There were less people that could see you, almost no soldiers, and your leg was okay. There is a very high possibility that an earthbender properly trained in martial arts, not in forms of construction or tilling, but in real fighting, might find you. Even worse, a soldier could and you can’t outrun them like this. You understand that, right?” She whispers, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s forehead.

Zuko nods, extracting his hands from hers and embracing her. “I love you. I’m sorry.” He mumbles.

She holds him for a long time, running her fingers through his dark hair, rubbing his back, humming softly. It’s nice and calming.

“Mom?” Zuko whispers after a few minutes, looking up at her.

“What do you need, love?”

“I was wondering if we could go into town today. Get some fresh air, it's been a few days since I’ve been outside. Wanna look around.” He asks, doubting she’ll even consider letting him go.

Not surprisingly, Kani shakes her head. “No, love. You’re exhausted and I really don’t know if the town is safe for you. Some people already know that you’re a firebender and there are too many rumors.” She explains, gently touching the rubbery skin of Zuko’s scar, indicating what people know about the banished prince.

Zuko just snuggles closer to her, not shocked by the answer but still a little upset. He really wanted to be able to get a change of scenery. It *does* look a lot different from the Fire Nation even if Zuko had always lived in a city by the ocean. It’s just similar enough to remind him of home.

Zuko nods. It would give him a chance to get his mind off of all of this. He could look around, see cool things, maybe even find a gift for Chen. He isn’t sure what he wants in the long run, but maybe this can help today.

“Oh, come on Kani, let him go. He needs to go get some candy, look around, and be a normal boy for once.” Zuko is surprised at Feya coming to his defense, but pleased.

Shaking her head and shooting a look at her sister, Kani holds Zuko closer. “I’m not putting him in danger like that.” She argues.

“Come on, he needs this. Protecting him is one thing but you’re smothering him. I’m not saying you let him run off on his own. You two should go look around together, tell him about growing up here. He’s been cooped up in this room for three days, let him stretch his legs.”

Finally, Kani concedes when Zuko pleads with her again, giving her the biggest turtle duck eyes he could possibly muster. “Fine, but you need to wear a hat and have your hair cover as much of your scar as possible, alright?”

That’s a compromise that Zuko can live with.

Unfortunately, town doesn’t last long. He is able to get some hard candies as well as some maple candies for him and Fao to share when he does get home. Some good news is that he found out that there is going to be another play in six days. Maybe he can convince Feya to convince Kani to let him stay long enough to see it.

It’s called *The Secrets of the Oasis* . Apparently, it’s an Earth Kingdom adaptation of a Northern Water Tribe folk tale. Maybe he can convince Kani to let him go by giving him more cultural exposure considering he’s wanted to learn more about Water Tribe culture for a while. He doubts it will work, but it’s worth a try.

The main reason why they need to head back is that Zuko feels exhausted. He thought that he had rested enough earlier, but the healing must have drained more out of him than he thought. He really hopes that this isn’t going to be chronic. He also needs to find a way to conserve his energy more if this is going to be doing this for people more often.

Even though Zuko is pretty sure that he could walk home on his own, Kani insists on carrying him, worried that he might aggravate his injury. Kani scoops him up into her arms, holding him tight, walking back with him to Feya’s. He isn’t sure why Kani has been so insistent about carrying him the past little bit, but she *had* said something about him getting bigger and heavier before they departed for town. Maybe she is just carrying him while he is still small enough. He likes the way this feels, but it will be nice to actually be closer to the size he is supposed to be.

“Do you think we can go to the play?” Zuko mumbles, not surprised when Kani shakes her head.

“My love, we need to get you home. I love you so much and I want you to be happy, but I need you to be safe, as well. I know you like it here, but the village is safer. I promise you’ll get to see a play at some point, but I don’t think we’ll be here long enough for you to go. I’m sorry, sweetheart.”

“I understand.” Zuko replies. He really does, but that doesn’t mean he’s happy about it.

Every rational part of him knows that getting home safe to Chen is so much more important than a stupid play. Above everything else, keeping the fact that Kani, Feya, and Chen are knowingly and willingly harboring a firebender, and not just any firebender but the Fire Prince, under wraps is important. Zuko is well aware that they could all be arrested for treason depending on who caught them. Depending on if the deciding party actually saw that they were just giving a scared, injured kid a home or if they saw Earth Kingdom citizens harboring a potential threat.

However, the little kid that just misses his mom and his home wants nothing more than to see any kind of theater production. He wants anything that could remind him of the small bits of his mothers life that she was able to share with her son. The moments where the two were able to be the closest. The plays that neither father nor Azula wanted to attend. When Zuko and his mother could just be safe and happy even if just for a few hours.

The times that Zuko spent with his mother in the theater, with her in the courtyard and in the gardens are really the only times he was actually happy. Even after Iroh had come, no matter what the old man did for him, Zuko knew that he was nothing more than someone who could fill a Lu Ten shaped hole in his uncle’s heart. That he was disposable. His own mother, one of the few people who had ever claimed to love him, had proved that he wasn’t worth staying for.

The next time Zuko had ever truly felt happy after his mother left was when he finally felt safe with Kani and Chen. When he finally trusted that they didn’t have some kind of twisted long con meant to drag information he didn’t have from him.

Then, once he truly believed that they had no intentions of hurting him when he messed up or disappointed them in any way…he still isn’t sure how to describe that feeling. Peace, maybe? Whatever it is, he had never known that happiness like that existed. Not fearing what may happen later, not worrying about what he had failed at earlier, just feeling safe, happy, and loved.

Eventually, they make it back to Feya’s. Before they walk in, Kani sets Zuko down on his feet, helping him balance himself on his crutches so that he doesn’t strain his ankle. Zuko hasn’t felt any pain in it for almost a week. However, both Kani and Feya have insisted that even though it feels better doesn’t mean it is better. That it is healed but not back to full strength and can easily be sprained, fractured, or even broken if used too soon.

Even though Zuko has some doubts about that and wants to be able to walk normally, they are trained healers. Anyways, it’s not like he needs to do anything particularly straining considering he is being taken care of and mostly stays in the house. It doesn’t mean it isn’t annoying just because he doesn’t *need* to be back to full capacity.

A thought that can’t leave his head is that his father would never give Zuko this much time for an injury Zuko inflicted upon himself, even if by accident. Instead of continuing to dwell on that thought, he tries to remind himself that he isn’t in the Fire Nation. That his real father is Chen and even if he isn’t here right now, he would always give Zuko whatever he could to keep Zuko safe and happy. That Kani would protect him from anything that may come into his life.

It does work some, but it’s hard. Although, Lo *had* told him that changing his mindset takes time and that he can’t rush himself. That sometimes even just reminding himself that he should try is all he can do some days. After that she had started talking about how Miyuki once bit and chased a Fire Nation soldier who had never seen a full bred cat before while yowling. Zuko still isn't sure if the soldier was yowling or the cat was or how that story had pertained to her advice, but the first bit is helpful, so he can’t give the second part too much thought.

When they walk in, there are three healers along with Feya tending to patients. Zuko hasn’t had the chance to really talk to any of the apprentices or assistants. They’ve always been busy or Zuko hasn’t been around when they are here. He’s pretty sure all they know about him is that he’s Feya’s nephew. He has no idea if they know he’s adopted or not. He really should ask so they have a consistent story. It would seem suspicious if one of them talked to him and he told them something contradictory to what Kani or Feya had said. Other than that, he doesn’t think that any of them are particularly interested in what he does.

Each of the four women are tending to someone, but luckily, none of the injures look particularly bad. They all seem to be having some kind of conversation and don’t appear to be in too much pain. Thankfully, they’ll all likely return to their homes for some rest tonight. Zuko hasn’t seen anyone that has come to the healing hut who has died. He doesn’t want that to change.

The difference today is that all but one of them are Earth Kingdom soldiers. Two more are standing in the room, seeming to be unharmed, likely just there with their fellow soldiers or with more minor injuries.

No matter their reason for being here, and even though they really only glance at the door when Zuko and Kani walk in, Kani still holds him close, bending down so she can be near his ear. “Love, I want you to just go upstairs. Go eat some candy and read your book with your turtle duck. I’ll be up with you in a few minutes, okay?” She whispers, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s forehead.

He understands why she doesn’t want him to be around the soldiers, but he can’t help but feel disappointed. He hasn’t really gotten any information on the war for the past few months, or at least nothing helpful. He is used to knowing where troops are headed, headcount of those who have lost their lives, prisoners, and such.

Very little of what he knew had been explained to him, but he had lived in the palace and people talked. The highest ranking military personnel would be in and out, discussing tactics while walking down the hall, sharing victories and losses over meals, and making plans when standing around. None of these people would go quiet if they saw Zuko peaking around the corner, interested in what they were saying. For the most part, they just ignored him.

Mosty after his mother left and especially before his uncle came home, almost all of Zuko’s social life was lived between the gossip of servants and war stories of soldiers. He would try and live some of his life from what they were doing with theirs. Get an idea of what it would be like to be real…sometimes he wasn’t even sure if he was real. That he was just a spirit somewhat tangible in the physical world, unable to fully appear but unable to return.

Usually, Zuko wasn’t listening in on these conversations out of interest in what they were saying, he just didn’t have many people to talk to or even listen to. If his mother wasn’t around, and even more commonly, when his uncle wasn’t around, he was lonely. Even if his voice wasn’t to be heard and no one was talking to him, he just wanted to listen. Wanted to feel like he was a part of something. He would come up with answers in his head that he would never share, wishing that his father might be proud of him for learning about military tactics and trying to engage himself in the politics of war as much as possible without direct exposure.

Only now he realizes how stupid that was. That Ozai would likely ignore anything Zuko said, brush it off, or ridicule him for any stupid idea he might have. He’s glad that he never spoke up about it to his father. It was always just a fantasy that lived in his head where his father began to see worth in Zuko as a soldier and a son.

Even if it wasn’t the war that had interested him before, he really does want to know now. He doesn’t like being in the dark even if that is how most of the people around him feel like. Even if there is nothing he can do even if he does know exactly what’s going on. It makes him feel like he has some control over his life even if he doesn’t.

Instead of going upstairs, Zuko walks towards the soldier with the most friendly looking face, waving to him, thankfully, he’s being treated by Feya. “Are you winning?” He asks, unsure what to say without sounding like he knows too much. He can see both Kani and Feya’s expressions. Kani looks exhausted and Feya looks mildly irritated. However, neither of them say anything to him.

The soldier looks up at him, opening his mouth and then closing it when his eyes fall on the burn over the left side of Zuko’s face. It’s still a bit odd to have people’s gaze focused on him like this, he hopes at some point he will get used to it, but it has only been a few months. He can’t be sure what will happen in the long run yet.

Luckily, in this scenario, his scar might be useful as to why Zuko is pressing for information about the war. It is very clearly a burn scar following the size and shape of the hand of a grown man. It wouldn’t be too much of a jump for the soldier to assume that Zuko is an Earth Kingdom child who was attacked by a firebender soldier. That he wants to know when the world might be safe again, not when he can see the people he left behind in the Fire Nation again.

“Shit, kid, they got you good.” The soldier says more to himself than to Zuko, sharing a look more of sympathy and sorrow opposed to just pity.

“Sir, I’m going to need you to watch your language in front of my nephew. He may have seen some bad stuff but he doesn’t need a mouth on him too. He’s ten and doesn’t know how to mind his own business.” Feya warns, pressing her fingers down against the wound that she is stitching when the man had almost subconsciously reached his hand out towards.

It wasn’t aggressive, it seemed more curious than anything, maybe even sympathetic. However, Feya isn’t the kind of person to give an unnecessary chance that no one would gain from for Zuko to be hurt.

Kani comes up behind Zuko, resting a hand protectively on his shoulder. “I’m sorry, he’s finally coming out of his shell after…everything that happened and has a naturally curious mind. Come on, Love.” She gently nudges Zuko in the direction of the stairs but doesn’t force him nor lead him there. She still stands behind him as Zuko continues looking up at the soldier, unsure what to say. He just wants to know something. Anything.

“Mom, can I stay down here for five minutes? Please? Then I’ll go upstairs, I promise. Please.” He turns around, giving Kani big, pleading eyes and he clutches at her robes.

Kani sighs, pinching the bridge of her nose and shaking her head in disbelief. “You are unbelievable, so you’re lucky you’re cute.” She presses a kiss to the top of Zuko’s head. “Just a few minutes, love, then the nice man needs to get some rest and so do you.” She ruffles Zuko’s hair before walking away, walking up to one of the soldiers who isn’t being tended to.

Zuko can hear the man chuckle softly as he turns back around. His smile is warm and friendly. Zuko doesn’t really know anything about the man, but he seems friendly.

Unfortunately, it’s impossible to miss the fact that he can’t be much older than Lu Ten when he left for war. Zuko can only hope that he doesn’t meet the same fate as his cousin.

“I’m Lee, what’s your name?” Zuko asks, cocking his head.

“Rulan.” The man replies, giving him an awkward nod as a form of greeting. Even though he is in a sitting position, Feya *is* stitching up a long, deep, gash in his arm and he likely doesn’t want to pull on it, or worse, irritate Feya. “What did you want to ask, kid?”

Zuko bites his lip, looking down for a moment before meeting Rulan’s eyes again. They’re green, meaning he is almost certainly an earthbender, but he can’t tell for sure. Some nonbenders do have bender eyes…but that isn’t particularly common. “What’s going on? Anything that civilians can know. We’re just visiting my aunt here, I live out in a small village with my mom, we don’t get much news there.” He explains, hoping it gives more innocent reason for his curiosity.

In all honesty, Zuko doesn’t have anything nefarious in mind; he just doesn’t want to be in the dark. It feels weird, it makes him feel stupid and helpless, and he doesn’t like it.

Rulan gives him a sad look. “There are still several major cities in the Earth Kingdom that have not fallen to the Fire Nation and will prevail. Most importantly, Ba Sing Se has not yet been touched. On top of that, the Northern Water Tribe has fended off any and all threats that the Fire Nation has presented. There isn’t too much more I can tell you, sorry, kid.” Rulan gives him a sympathetic look.

Zuko nods. “I understand, national security.” He responds, knowing full well that the Fire Nation had used propaganda to minimize information getting out to civilians and even many soldiers. Entire frontline battalions, in some cases.

He is about to go when he looks back at the man, the question of what the rest of the world is like still in his mind. “Have you ever met a waterbender? Or anyone from the Water Tribes?” He asks, smiling.

Rulan shakes his head. “I’ve never met anyone from there, but I’m going to in the next few months. We’re going to be meeting up with navel forces from the Southern Water Tribe. I’m not at liberty to say exactly where or when, but we’ve been in communication with them for a while.”

Zuko can’t help but smile at that. If the Water Tribe Navy is coming up to meet with the Earth Kingdom, maybe he’ll end up meeting some people who end up wandering inland. He knows that it is unlikely, but still, he can hope.

“Lee, I think it’s time that you go upstairs. Get yourself something to eat and get some rest. Please, you’re so close to being healed, I don’t want you hurting yourself again.” Feya instrusts, glancing at the door.

Zuko nods, thanking Rulan, quickly embracing Feya before heading up to the apartment above.

Iroh had managed to bring together a small crew of people he could trust. By trust, he meant people who he knew wouldn’t question him or argue about staying on board the ship while Iroh looked for Zuko.

All of them have respect for the royal family and worship the almighty Fire Nation ban. People who only respect money aren’t the type of people Iroh would usually associate himself with, but their loyalty is easy to buy.

As far as many of these sailors are concerned, Iroh is paying them to sit around on their ship, get drunk, and play games for a few days while Iroh is in town. He had briefly mentioned his old friend to them, but hadn’t gone into much detail, claiming it was personal. On top of that, it wasn't his crew that he was worried about convincing, it was his brother.

Surprisingly, Ozai hadn’t been hard to convince. It was likely simply because he didn’t care and wanted Iroh to leave him alone, much like Azula had said. Iroh had expected some mocking criticism of Iroh's priorities now that he had no family or power, but the Fire Lord had paid him very little mind.

However, when Iroh had mentioned the possibility of Azula coming, *that* is where the criticism came in. He had said that Azula didn’t need Iroh’s influence of tea and failure outside of the palace without the company of a proper instructor. That some of the most important years of Azula's life weren’t to be wasted on a leisure trip, even if for only for about two weeks.

Now, all that is left is to leave his niece, his child, alone with her father. A man who had so cruelly cut down his own son for nothing and who likely would do the same to her given the reason and chance. He doesn’t want to leave Azula alone, even if for just a few weeks, but she is the one who had begged him to go. They both know that they need to know if Zuko is alive or dead.

If Zuko is alive, it means that Iroh doesn’t have to mourn him, it means that he can move on. If he knows that Zuko is somewhere that he is safe and loved, he can focus all of his energy on Azula and do everything that he can to make her feel at least loved. He can’t grant her safety as long as her father walks the face of the earth.

He just needs to say goodbye to her, promising that he’ll be back before his departure. He can’t just abandon her even if she would know and understand why he is leaving for the Earth Kingdom.

He finally finds her kneeling by the turtle duck pond, looking down at it blankly.

Iroh sits next to her, resting a hand on her shoulder. “Princess Azula, are you alright?” He asks, worried for his niece's wellbeing.

Azula just leans her head up against Iroh’s shoulder, continuing to gaze straight ahead. “Will you tell Zuzu that I’m sorry? For everything I said and did that made his life harder? Tell him I’m sorry that father was so horrible to him?” She takes a deep breath before continuing to speak. “Thank him for keeping me safe for so long. I wish it didn’t take him suffering so horribly…but I need him to know that he protected me for a long time.”

Iroh wraps his arm around Azula’s shoulders, pressing a kiss to the side of her head. “Of course. You’re going to see him again one day. You two are going to be safe and happy when we rebuild this nation as a family. It’s going to be alright. I know I haven’t told you everything, but I will. We have a little more than two years until we can’t wait for the Avatar anymore. You just need to stay strong until then, then you’ll be free. Can you do that?” He asks, knowing that it is a lot, but having an end date can make things easier to get through. Knowing how you need to budget your strength.

“I can do that, uncle.”

A few minutes pass before Azula digs though her pocket, pulling out a pin. It’s gold with the Fire Nation emblem on it, a small ruby placed in the bottom where the three spikes of the flame converge.

Iroh turns it over in his hand, examining it. It looks like a pin that would be used to hold a woman’s shawl in place. Definitely a noble woman or at least one from a wealthy background. Even though that description fits Azula, this isn’t the kind of thing she would ever wear. The only jewelry he has ever seen his niece wear is her crown and occasionally a simple banded ring or a thin bracelet, nothing this ornate.

“What is this for?” He asks, unsure what else to say.

“It’s for Zuzu…it was mother’s.” She doesn’t offer any more information as to how she got it, why she still has it, or why she had never given it to Zuko before. However, Iroh doesn’t press.

“I think he’ll be very grateful.” He praises. He isn’t sure if Zuko would be more grateful to have something that belonged to his mother or to know that no matter their past, Azula loves him.

“Please come back soon, uncle…I don’t want to be alone with him.” Azula admits, holding Iroh’s hand tight.

Iroh can feel his heart ache for the girl next to him. “I don’t have to go if you need me here. I don’t want to leave you. I can stay.”

Azula shakes her head. “I *need* to know if it’s him. Whatever happens in the next two weeks, it won’t hurt as much as not knowing, just please, be as quick as you can.” She pleads, Iroh can see a hint of fear in her expression even if most of her face is obscured.

“Can you invite your friends over? Even if just for a few days? Mai lives close, she could keep you company. At least act as a buffer between you and your father.”

“She’s away. She’s been away for a while with her parents. Her father is getting more involved in politics and that means that he’s traveling. Ty Lee is getting more involved in the circus. I miss them.” She says softly.

Sighing, Iroh holds the little girl closer. “I’ll be back as soon as I can. Stay strong for me, I know you can do it. Once I get back, I won’t ever leave you with that man again. I promise.” He means it. He won’t leave her again of his own free will. He needs to protect Azula. He can’t fail again.

Azula gives him a small smile. “I trust you. Be careful. Make sure Zuzu is safe.”

Iroh presses a kiss to Azula’s head again before standing and walking away, trying to ignore the twisting in his heart as he leaves his child alone with her tormentor. He prays that she’ll be okay until he gets back. She needs to be.

“Are you *seriously* saying that he should stay for a theater production? You *know* who he is. You’ve *seen* how he isn’t being as cautious around people anymore. I’m sure you can take a pretty good guess as to what they’ll do to him if *anyone* finds out who he is. They’ll hurt him even if they just know that he is a firebender. I know you aren’t as cautious, but this is ludicrous.”

Kani can’t believe that her sister is trying to argue for Zuko to stay for the play taking place almost a *week* from now. That is plenty of time for Zuko to make one small mistake at the wrong time in front of the wrong person.

“Yes, I am. He’s getting a lot more confident which is a *good* thing. He wasn’t being stupid when talking to that guard, little kids are curious and never shut their fucking mouths. I can assure you, the only thing that that soldier will remember about Zuko in even a few days is how sad it is that someone so young got such a horrible burn from this war. Then it will fade into all of the other violence that he sees every day.”

Kani pinches the bridge of her nose, trying to ward off the forming headache from these two. She loves Feya and Zuko so much, but they aren’t taking this seriously. They don’t seem to understand that if the wrong person discovers that Zuko is a firebender, they will haul him off to a prison, not caring that he has clearly been attacked by his own kind and is just a child seeking safety.

“Didn’t you get mad at Rulan for saying ‘shit’ in front of me? Why can you say ‘fuck’?” Zuko asks, looking up at the two, the turtle duck in his lap with the blanket wrapped around him. He has no right to look as adorable as he does. This is probably how he has been able to talk her into letting him do stupid things.

“Well, first of all, he doesn’t know that saying a couple of bad words isn’t the worst thing that has ever happened. Second of all, I said ‘fucking’, not ‘fuck.’” Kani is surprised with her restraint for not punching her sister for that comment. “Also, I’m your aunt, I’m supposed to be a bad influence on you.” She jokes, ruffling Zuko’s hair.

Kani rolls her hers. “Zuko, don’t fucking repeat that shit.” She grumbles, the irony lost in her exhaustion with these two.

“Why can you say it?” He asks, cocking his head.

“Because I’m an adult and am allowed to make bad decisions. Also, because you two are giving me a headache with how little concern you have for your wellbeing. I’m not trying to be mean, love, I’m just worried that something bad is going to happen. I can’t have anyone taking my baby from me. I don’t know what I would do if someone hurt you.”

The two go silent for a moment and Kani begins to foolishly think that this is the end of the discussion. That Zuko will come back home the next day or the day after, even if a little reluctantly, but will soon enough be snuggled up with Chen by the fire, telling him about everything that has happened in town with Cabbage curled up in his lap.

“What’s the story that we’re saying about me? I just don’t want to say anything that is contradictory to what one of you has told someone. Like my age, what happened, if I’m adopted, or anything else.”

Kani feels stupid for not having thought of that sooner.

“Well, I said you were ten today and I think that we should stick with that. It distances Lee from Zuko by three years difference and it would make people pay less attention to you. Hold less weight to anything that you do or say.” Feya begins, sipping on a cup of tea far too casually.

Kani sighs, looking at the little firebender sitting in front of her, looking up at her with such an innocent smile despite everything that he has been through. Despite knowing how horrible the world can be.

Sitting down next to him, Kani pulls him into a hug. “I think we just refer to you as my son and Feya’s nephew. That we act as if you were born into this family unless someone asks. If someone brings up the fact that you don’t really look like us or something like that, we say that we took you in after you were attacked and you didn’t want to give more reason for people to ask why you aren’t living with your birth parents. Don’t give any more information than that. Say you just wanna forget about it and Feya and I will say that it isn’t our story to share. How does that sound, love?” She asks, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s forehead.

“Works for me.” Feya shrugs, smiling down at Zuko. “Would work better if I could take him to the play.”

Kani glares at her sister, not wanting this discussion to be brought up again. “Please, this isn’t out of cruelty and his safety isn’t a joke.”

“I don’t think she’s making it out to be a joke.” Zuko adds, snuggling up to Kani and resting his chin on her shoulder.

“You just think that because you wanna go. I’m not stupid, love.”

Zuko just gives her an almost sarcastically innocent look. He really is coming out of his shell.

If she wasn’t so grateful that he hadn’t been permanently broken by what was done to him, she might find him a little annoying. Maybe this is what parents have meant when talking about the unconditional love for their children. Zuko drives her up the wall with stupid things that he does every day, but she can’t help to love him. On top of that, she is well aware that this is the first time in his life he has been allowed to behave like a child. It might take him a few months to start acting more his age. He needs to live some of the life he never got a chance to even if an abbreviated version of it.

“Come on, if I thought that someone would recognize him as the prince without taking a few precautions, I would have never invited him to come to town. I had a lot of information about him to help draw that conclusion that really no one else will have. It would be quite the jump to make. Some kid who was taken in by farmer peasants with a burn on his face to said child being the banished Fire Nation prince who everyone thinks is dead isn’t the most natural conclusion. You gotta be pretty certain before you accuse someone of that. Again, everyone thinks he’s dead. Everyone knows about it because it is kind of like a cautionary tale that the Fire Nation won’t spare you, not some kind of man hunt.” Feya throws her hands up in the air in exasperation, almost dropping her tea.

Sighing, Kani rests her forehead on top of Zuko’s head. “Fine, he can stay.” Kani resigns, giving up on fighting these two. Before she can lay down the surly implied rules of Zuko needing to be careful he throws his arms around her neck, thanking her profusely.

“You’re lucky I love you.” She grumbles, rubbing Zuko’s back.

“I love you, too, mom.” Zuko mumbles quietly into her shoulder.

Kani will never let a bad thing happen to this child ever again. If anyone even *thinks* about hurting her child again, she’ll do whatever she can to make sure that it is the last mistake that they ever make.

Things have gotten a lot less interesting now that Lee and Kani are in town. Considering really all of the work that Chen needs to do is tend to the animals and to the small bed filled with vegetables that can survive through the winter, there isn’t all that much to do.

He has read some of the books that he and Kani had collected over the years. There aren’t a whole lot meant just for entertainment. There are a few earthbending scrolls considering Kani had never been formally taught outside of a few sporadic lessons with various earthbender she had met throughout her life. Most are medical books filled with research from previous healers, instructions to treat less common illnesses and injuries, rare or foreign medicinal plants, and several drawings of the human body.

There are only a few books that are meant for entertainment, and most of them Chen has read multiple times before this.

After reading got boring (which didn’t take particularly long), Chen started sketching pictures of what others and Lee had described the Fire Nation to look like. Not the war torn battlefields that most would picture, but the landscapes only existing at the equator.

He quickly realizes that he has no idea what the Fire Nation looks like outside of some pictures he has seen of the capital city. He can only assume that is where Lee has lived most of his life.

In the end, Chen ends up drawing multiple iterations of Caldera City. He knows the shape of the volcano and the winding path that leads up the jagged mouth of a place that few would dare to build their most important buildings in. He knows the basics of Fire Nation architecture and does his best filling in in the mouth of the volcano with what he could imagine the layout would be. He had really only paid attention to the volcano in pictures, not caring much for the man made architecture. The fact that people would choose to live there is what impressed him above anything else. They may be at war, but Chen has to admit, the Fire Nation has got some balls.

After completing that, he makes iterations of the capital city filled with almost minuscule landscapes so that there could be a thriving ecosystem so different from the rest of the world existing in only the most unique place. He makes another one with Earth Kingdom farmland and trees filling the spaces around the edge. Even if it would be so different from home, Chen could imagine living in a place like this would be spectacular.

At least for now, he can only hope that it gives Lee a sense of home.

Chen mostly stays to himself for the first several days of Kani and Lee’s departure. He is mostly alone except when someone besides Gela coming to see how he’s doing and inviting him over for dinner or Fao asking if Lee is back yet.

Most of the people that he is still in regular contact with live either in town or in the village. However, Lee and Po are two friends that live a good distance outside of the village that he sees when he can. They live about half a day’s journey by ostrich horse in the opposite direction of town making it so there is little opportunity for him to see them which is why he is pretty surprised when they show up in the later afternoon one day.

Most of the time he actually does see them, they are spending the night on their way into town considering it would be ludicrous and cruel to the animals to try and travel that far in one day.

Most people traveling that far would leave someone at home to make sure no one broke in. However, the two live in a cave. Several years ago when they had answered as such when Chen had asked where they were living, he had thought that they were joking. However, the two *literally* live in a cave that Po seals off with his bending before they leave.

Their cave is surprisingly homey. He’s been there a few times and it really is nice. Not much natural light even when the cave is open, but nice all the same. It’s not where Chen would live by choice if he had better options, which as far as he is aware the couple do, but they have always been odd.

At first, Chen had assumed that they lived there out of safety. It’s far easier for two women to live together without those less stuck in the past questioning their relationship. He is aware that there are people who don’t know that Gela and Shi are a couple despite it being very obvious, but then again, people see what they want to. On the other hand, with Lee and Po, he actually believes at this point that they are just odd and choose to live there.

“Shit, I don’t think I’ve seen you two since…fuck, what was it? Early spring? Dunno, it’s good to see you, come in.” He opens the door wider, letting the two in.

Po looks about the same as he always has. Long brown hair pulled up into an Earth Kingdom style bun, dark green eyes, and tall and gangly. Lee has actually let his hair continue growing, it now hanging loose around his broad shoulders. Everything about Lee is dark to his jet black hair, almost black eyes, and dark skin. He’s usually friendly but has always been the one to try and get Chen to grow his hair out. Chen had kept his as close cropped as he could without it being shaved for the past several years.

“There isn’t too much good food here. I have some rising bread dough, a bunch of pickled vegetables, dried fruit, jerky, and some liquor.” He offers, knowing full well that the two are aware that winter food is limited.

“Whatever is good, you know neither of us care, but more importantly, we heard you have a kid now.” Po responds, grinning, opening his arms and embracing Chen as he speaks.

Nodding, Chen meets his friend’s eyes, unsure who had said something. It’s not that Chen minds that people know he has a kid, it’s that Po and Lee are pretty much hermits who really only enjoy each other's company most of the time. There are only a few people who they interact with, and even then, visits are few and far between. They have plenty of time to be lonely, middle aged men in the middle of the woods.

“Yeah, we do. His name is also Lee.” Chen looks at Lee when he says that. The other man only responds by tilting his chin upwards and grinning. “Where did you hear that?” Chen continues.

“It’s a good name. Anyways, your neighbor told us.” Lee replies.

“Gela?” He asks, not even aware that she *knew* Po or Lee.

“No, her wife, Shi. She brought us some spider rats.” Po answers, sitting down by the fire.

“Why would she bring you…you know, never mind, I don’t wanna know.” Chen sighs, sitting with his friends, almost sure that the two had let the spider rats loose in their cave.

“So, she told us the kid was like 13, can’t be yours, where did you find him?” Po continues, getting to the point.

Chen sighs, unsure what to say. He knows that these two wouldn’t care that Lee is a firebender, but he doesn’t know what might happen if someone else finds out. They don’t see many people, but when they do, they usually drink. A lot. They’re both very chatty drunks. Chen can’t risk his son’s safety because of two drunks who can’t keep their mouths shut.

“I found him in the woods during a storm. His family was killed by Fire Nation soldiers and they burned his face. He was almost dead and absolutely terrified. We took him inside to heal him up and get him something to eat and we grew really fond of him.” He explains, not wanting to give too much more information.

“Fuck…poor kid.” Lee answers, shaking his head sadly. “So young, too.”

Chen grimaces, feeling the same way. They would be even more mournful if they knew the kid’s own father did that to him.

“Didn’t the Fire Lord kill his kid around the same age? Really always easy to forget how young that is…just imagine.” Po chimes in, looking at Chen.

Chen cocks his head, having no idea what his friend was talking about. “The Fire Lord killed his kid? When?” Chen asks, never having heard about this. Ever.

“Dude, *we* know about this. Everyone’s talking about it. This happened a few months ago… sometime in the summer, I think, not sure on exact details, though.” Lee answers.

“Some soldiers were traveling through and we hosted them for a night. They were excited to get out of our cave but better than sleeping in the cold.” Po adds before Chen can ask where they heard news in their remote location.

“Apparently, the Prince spoke out against the war and the Fire Lord challenged him to some kind of fire duel to the death. The Fire Lord killed him or, like, burned the shit out of him and he died of complications. Either way, he very intentionally and very personally killed his thirteen year old son.”

Chen isn’t sure what to say. He can’t say that his son was also burned by his father for the same crime. That Lee is almost certainly from at least a noble family. That his name isn’t even Lee. That he has a very distinguishable name that Chen is sure that he has heard before.

He takes a slow, deep breath, the new question burning in his mind. The idea that shouldn’t change anything but does. Not that he wouldn’t still care for the boy as if he were his own but…he isn’t sure *what* might change.

“Do you know what the kid’s name was?” Chen asks evenly, looking between the two men.

It is Po who meets Chen’s eyes in response, uttering only one word without realizing the weight that it holds: “Zuko.”

## Chapter 21
