### Text

Chen isn’t sure how to respond to the information that his friends had just revealed to him. He knows that it doesn’t change the fact that he loves Zuko and will protect and care for him as his own son. However, it does change the situation that they’re in.

Before, if the wrong person were to discover that Lee was in fact not a nonbender Earth Kingdom child but a firebender, it likely wouldn’t go down well but he was pretty confident that things would blow over. They would likely be able to convince whoever it was that Lee was from a nationalist, peasant family in the colonies who had attacked and thrown him out for not supporting the war. Whoever it was may not be happy about Lee living in the Earth Kingdom, but with persuasion and getting to know Lee as a kid opposed to as just a firebender, they would likely leave him alone.

However, Lee isn’t just some kid who needs a bit of help. He was marked as the enemy upon his birth as heir to the world’s tyrant. To the person children grow up learning to hate and fear.

“Chen…you alright?” Po asks, raising an eyebrow, looking at him.

Chen nods, swallowing. “Yeah…yeah, just really fucked up is all. Poor kid.” He whispers, trying to make his voice sound somewhat normal with little success. He at least needs to try and make himself sound mournful and not fearful.

“Leave him alone, he’s a dad now, it’s different.” Lee shoves his partner, getting Po to stop looking at Chen so intently.

Chen looks between the two, unsure what to say. He knows that neither of the men are particularly judgmental, they don’t have strong opinions on most people, good or bad. However, that might be different for firebenders. Firebenders from the royal family at that.

“What do you guys think of firebenders? Like as people…not just the soldiers…if you’ve ever met any.” He asks before he can stop himself, unsure what he even wanted out of this conversation.

Well, he does. He wants to tell them about his son Lee being Zuko who is apparently the Fire Prince. He wants to be able to talk about this with someone. Wants to be able to come to terms with it before the little boy comes home. So that Chen can make sure that Zuko knows that he knows about Zuko’s real identity and still loves him and wants him to be able to be himself as much as possible. To be safe and loved in his home.

Unfortunately, that isn’t something he can do. Lee would feel betrayed and Kani would be furious. He can’t expose his child like that. Even if it might make Chen feel better about this, he can’t put Lee in danger like that. He can’t betray his son’s hard earned trust for temporary comfort. He knows that Kani had shared the fact that Lee is a firebender with Gela, but she doesn’t consider people a threat without personal reason, not stereotypes. Also, Kani had just informed the woman of Zuko’s element and heritage, not his lineage.

Po shrugs. “We’ve actually met a few groups of Fire Nation soldiers. Always small groups of low ranking soldiers considering the fact that they’re traveling through the rural Earth Kingdom. They also have nothing to gain from starting a fight with two random men in the woods with no help around for miles, so they’ve never bothered us.”

Chen opens his mouth, unsure what to say, not at all expecting that. He doubted either of the men had ever had a close encounter with a Fire National, let alone one that was actively not bad.

“One group of three even stayed a few days during that storm a few months back…I think only one of them was actually a soldier and only the youngest civilian was a firebender. She could really only use it for domestic purposes, never formally trained, so, helpful, but not particularly dangerous.” Lee adds, grinning.

At that, Chen *has* to say something. He can’t exactly tell his friends that bringing in random firebenders is a bad idea, considering he brought in one that attacked him; but, still. not the kind of thing he expected from the couple. They aren’t particularly careful, but they aren’t stupid.

Okay…they are kind of stupid and this *is* the kind of thing he would expect from them, but it just seems so far from what most would do. Then again, Chen is harboring the Fire Lord’s son and raising him as his own on a farm in the rural Earth Kingdom. Letting in some Fire Nationals for a few days isn’t the strangest thing someone in this room has done.

“What made you go from not starting fights to letting soldiers into your house?” Chen settles on asking, looking between the two men.

“Well, only one of them was a soldier and it’s not like we were gonna let three people die in a storm. Anyways, Fire Nationals usually carry good liquor and weird but good food.” Lee answers while Po simply answers with: “The soldier guy was hot.”

“The guy I said I was going to leave you for?” Lee asks before Chen can even think of something to say to that.

“What other guy, dumbass?” Po asks, playfully shoving Lee. Chen has never understood their sense of humor. Honestly, if he didn’t know that they had been together through a lot for the past fifteen years he might…he has no idea what he would think of them. He’s known them for a long time and still doesn’t understand them most of the time. Maybe that’s a good thing. They *do* choose to isolate themselves in the woods in a cave opposed to building a house, something he knows both men are capable of.

“So bottom line is neither of you hate firebenders, Fire Nationals, or people affiliated with the Fire Nation just because. They gotta be assholes for you to have an issue?” He asks, not wanting to get into them joking about leaving each other for some random guy. There probably is a joke in there he just doesn’t understand either from difference in life experience or personality.

Both nod. That's good. Chen knows that if they ever do meet Lee, he’ll be safe with them. It won’t be often and they won’t know everything, but, still, just the kid knowing that there are more people out there who know he’s a firebender and don’t care could do him a lot of good. Might make him feel more at home living in a new nation on a new continent.

“What makes you ask?” Lee asks as Chen begins to stand up, ready to put the dough in the cob oven.

Chen tries to think of a good answer as he starts the fire, wishing that Zuko were here to start it up. After living with a firebender for months, he had gotten used to someone else starting the fires in a fraction of the time.

He isn’t sure what he can tell his friends. He certainly can’t say that Zuko is the supposedly dead Fire Prince. Even if they don’t have any issue with low level firebender soldiers and civilians with ties to the Fire Nation, royalty may be different.

If Chen hadn’t gotten a chance to get to know Zuko properly as Lee for a few months, he probably wouldn’t want the son of the Fire Lord anywhere near him or his family. Chen had been given time to trust that Zuko is just a scared kid who wants a family who will love him and care for him. He has seen Zuko break down revealing the scars embedded deep in his heart from injuries carved into his skin and his soul by a man who was supposed to protect him. Chen has seen the kid get so excited over learning to cook, to be able to play with his friend, to snuggle with Cabbage by the fire, and be so happy when he’s pulled into an embrace.

Despite coming from a man who knows nothing but cruelty, Zuko wants to learn how to be kind, to be treated well, and treat others in the same way. He can trust that Zuko would sooner live as their son on their farm, marry a nice Earth Kingdom girl, and live the rest of his life as an Earth Kingdom peasant than show an ounce of loyalty to the Fire Lord or Fire Nation.

“My kid…he has some ties to the Fire Nation…very personal ties. Or he did. They really hurt him…I know it could put him in a lot of danger but he wants to be honest with people. He really feels out of place here and I can barely begin to understand what he’s feeling. A few people know about his past and still accept and care about him and it’s helped him a lot. If you meet him in town, both Kani and Feya know about him. It might be good for him to meet new people who don’t see being a Fire National as inherently bad. He’s a really good kid…just has a lot of trouble feeling okay.” Chen explains, putting the bread in the oven and grabbing a bottle of wine from one of the high shelves before walking back over to his friends.

“Kani and Chen taking in a Fire Nation kid, not what I would expect, but I’m sure he has a good home now. Does he stay there?” Po asks, gesturing to the red curtains hanging in the corner.

Chen nods, pouring three glasses of wine and passing two of them to the couple. “He doesn’t want to go back there after everything that has happened to him, but he does miss parts of his culture and sometimes misses family that disappeared a while ago. Unfortunately, I’ll sometimes find him sleeping with the stupid chicken cat that he named Cabbage that he isn’t supposed to bring in from the barn.” Chen chuckles, wanting to make sure that the men knew that the most rebellious thing Zuko would do is snuggle with farm animals.

Well, technically there were some other things, but those were more fear response and feeling disconnected from everything he defined himself as. Chen couldn’t blame him for that. Anyways, most of those stories involved the fact that Zuko is a firebender. Chen doesn’t think that his friends will care after what they have told him, but it really isn’t his to share. Anyways, he doesn’t want to give them much to talk about if something were to happen. He doubts they would be able to give enough information while inebriated to identify Zuko as a farmer’s son, but if anything got out about Zuko being the dead Fire Prince it would end in a manhunt.

The three chat for a while longer until the bread is ready. Chen takes it out, serving it with some pickled vegetables and jerky. Not the best, but not the worst. They can’t be picky in winter.

“When we reach town tomorrow, we’ll make sure to give your wife our regards and hopefully get a chance to meet Lee. We’ve been wondering what he would be like since Shi told us about him.” Po says, finishing the wine Chen had poured for them.

Chen smiles at his friends. “I think you’ll like him. Just make sure that he and Kani are still doing well when you’re there, you can spend the night here on your way back home as well.” Chen offers, wanting to make sure that everything is still going smoothly in town.

He is sure that if something had happened, Feya would have written to him, but he can’t help but worry about them. They’re the most important people in his life. With his understanding of Zuko’s true identity, the worst that could happen is so much worse.

“I really don’t want to let him go off alone. What if something happens? What if someone recognizes him? What if he gets hurt? Wha-”

“Kani, you need to calm down.” Feya instructs, sipping on her tea. “Lee is going to be fine. He’s a smart kid, a trained soldier, and he’s walking a little outside of town. If he gets hurt, someone will be able to hear him yell for help. No one will recognize him, he’ll wear his hat and is in Earth Kingdom clothes. He’s just some kid to just about everyone here. Most people won’t even acknowledge him unless he interacts with them.” Feya assures her sister, really wishing Kani would just understand that where Zuko is a trauma victim and does need more support than most children his age, he isn’t a little kid, he’s a teenager and isn’t going to enjoy being coddled forever. Eventually he will see it as smothering.

“He’s an injured kid. He’s intelligent but he’s an idiot. You *saw* what he did. He heard about some discrete subelement of firebending from some crazy old woman and immediately tried it out in front of people. What if he does something stupid? Anyways, naval troops pass through here pretty regularly, what if they know what the Fire Prince is supposed to look like?” The panic in her voice is evident.

“Kani, please, no one is looking for him. The reason why everyone is talking about Zuko is because it’s a really messed up story, not because they’re looking for him. It’s warning people to keep even their children away from any and all Fire Nation soldiers because they will not take pity. No one is looking for Lee. If I had the slightest bit of doubt that he wouldn’t be safe, I wouldn’t let him go out on his own. Fuck it, I wouldn’t have even wanted him to come to town. I don’t want anything to happen to him, but he needs to be a kid for once.” Feya reminds her sister, taking her hand, giving her a small smile.

Sighing, Kani looks over at Zuko on the far side of the room. Feya had removed his splint this morning and replaced it with a brace so he can walk with just a little extra support. Technically he is healed, but re-aggravation isn’t hard. However, he is really enjoying being able to walk around with free hands again even if it is just from side to side of the empty room.

“Kani, look at me.” Her sister compiles but still glances over at the firebender occasionally.

“Zuko is a trauma victim and you and Chen, especially you, were his protectors. You told me it took awhile to even get him off of the property with kids you knew very well. You couldn’t even come into town and be gone for two days even if he would be at home with Chen because he was too scared for you to be away from him that long. You told me he was constantly following you around because he couldn’t bear to be separated from you. He’s finally stopped doing all of that. He can be away from you for a little and not feel like his world is going to fall apart or like you won’t be here when you get back. It isn’t because he doesn’t think of you as his mom anymore or doesn’t still need you, it just means he feels safe. I know it’s hard, but give him some space. This is a *good* thing.”

Kani frowns, nodding. “I know…I’m happy he’s feeling more confident, I’m just worried he isn’t safe. I’m not trying to stop him from being himself. I want him to be more independent when we’re back home, but I’m *scared,* Feya.”

Feya takes her sister’s hand, giving her a sad look. “Kani, if you’re worried about him, I’m sure he’s scared too, if he doesn’t feel safe, I don’t think he’d want to go. Anyways, he’s a teenager, he’s thirteen, most kids his age aren't this close to their parents. He’s asking for a little bit of freedom, he just wants to go see Lo on his own. The furthest he’ll stray from just doing that is probably looking at the beach or going to the market. He’s not asking for much. Preventing him from doing little things like this isn’t protecting him, it’s smothering him. If you don’t give him some space to grow he’ll rebel to get it. Just…please listen to him. Give him a little bit of space. If it goes poorly, he’ll let you know. The kid is incapable of lying to you. It’s going to be okay. Just let him go.”

Kani sighs looking over at Zuko solemnly before calling the firebender over.

Zuko walks over to them, his gait is a little off but it will take a little to get used to the brace. Ironically, not too long after he gets used to it will be around the time that he'll be able to start strengthening his leg and walking without aid again. Thankfully, the kid just seems to be happy to have both of his hands free again, a cup of jasmine tea in one hand and his turtle duck in the other.

Considering the kid is thirteen, Feya hadn’t expected Zuko to like the turtle duck this much, he is getting old for stuffed animals. Unfortunately, it was likely something he was never allowed to have growing up. On top of that, it isn’t hard to tell he loves casual affection and likes it when people hold him. He probably just wants something to hold while sleeping and has been growing attached to it.

With how positive his reaction to the animal is, she’ll have to think of another Fire Nation creature that she thinks he might like. Or maybe just another turtle duck that looks a little different. He might like snuggling with more than one.

Zuko looks up at Kani, smiling brightly at her as if he hadn’t seen more horrors as a child than most adults would see in their lives. She has to admit, the kid is resilient. She wasn’t sure about him at first when he panicked and broke down upon being in the same room as Feya for a few minutes but he’s come around in a very short period of time. Then again, he had been safe and cared for months before Feya had arrived. He had already started settling.

“Do you still want to go on your own to see Lo?” Kani asks, kneeling down and cupping the firebender’s rounding face in her hands. He’s gained a good amount of weight, but still not enough. He’s still so thin. But he just looks scrawny, apparently he used to look so much worse. Feya is grateful she didn’t have to see the boy when he was starved.

Zuko grins, nodding. “Can I? Please? I’ll come right back and I promise I’ll be careful. I won’t do anything else but go talk to Lo.” The firebender pleads, looking up at Kani with wide, hopeful eyes.

Feya remembers how sad and scared Zuko looked when she first met him and that was even after a few months of a good home. She hopes that she never has to see a kid that looks that broken again. She’s grateful she didn’t have to see him when Kani and Chen first found him. She still can’t believe that that same kid is this happy now. She can’t imagine what the Fire Lord must have done to him to smother the light that shines so bright in that kid. She can’t imagine how someone could be able to look at someone who wants to shine so bright and even *think* about hurting him. About even denying him anything.

Reluctantly, Kani sighs. “Fine, you can go, but you *need* to be careful. You promise me? I can’t lose you, love, You need to come home safe. Bring your swords. If you need to defend yourself for any reason, use those, not your bending. Okay?”

Zuko nods, running up the stairs as fast as his brace allows him to grab them.

“He’s going to the other side of town, Kani, not on a journey. He’s going to be fine. You need to stop worrying about him so much. He’s been able to survive some of the worst that the world can throw at him, he can make it through a rough patch or two now that he has a loving and supportive family to take care of him.” Feya reminds her sister, feeling like she was being a bit too overprotective of him.

Kani glares at her, shaking her head. “I know that the odds of anyone finding out who is is are very slim, but if they do, they will torture him for information that he doesn’t know, try to ransom him when they realize he doesn’t know anything, and then kill him when they realize the Fire Lord doesn’t want him. The price is far too high. Nothing can happen to him.” Kani replies, glancing to where Zuko disappeared to as she talks.

Sighing, Feya rests a hand on her sister’s shoulder. She does have a reason to be concerned, but the little kid is going to be fine. He knows the dangers that being discovered could present him with. He knows that there is only so much of the world that is safe for him.

“I understand your concern, but just let him be a kid. He is easily excitable and sometimes does stupid things but he isn’t a complete idiot. He doesn’t want to be discovered either.” She assures her sister as Zuko hobbles down the stairs, swords strapped to his hip, the biggest smile shining on his face as he throws his arms around Kani’s waist.

“Come home safe, alright?” Kani eventually whispers, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s head.

Zuko nods, looking up and smiling at her. “I promise, mom. I’ll be really careful. Thank you, I love you.”

“I love you too, sweetheart.” Kani whispers, pressing another kiss to Zuko’s head before the little firebender hurries out the door in the direction of the greenhouse.

Zuko hasn’t ever been in the town by himself before and despite it not inherently being exciting, he can’t help but feel ecstatic.

He knows that Kani is letting him know that she trusts him to go out alone and to not break the rules that she had put in place for him and he knows that he isn’t going to break her trust by immediately doing everything he promised her that she wouldn’t. However, it is still the freedom that he *could* run down the beach and look for anything washed up on the shore, go to the market, or run into the forest with no one stopping him that is exciting.

Despite his ability to do any of those things, he continues on course towards Lo’s greenhouse. He still can’t go as fast as he used to with the brace on, but certainly faster than he could with his crutches. He loves having freedom with his hands again. It makes everything so much easier. He could actually walk and carry things if he wanted to besides what he could pinch in his fingers.

With this new freedom of both his choices and his body, it doesn’t take long for him to reach Lo’s. He’s happy because he’ll be able to talk to her, but he also likes walking through the town. Likes seeing the people walking around him going about their days.

When he reaches the greenhouse, he walks in slowly, scanning the room to see if anyone else is in there. “Hello? Lo? It’s Lee…Feya’s nephew.” He calls. It would be more descriptive to refer to himself as ‘the firebender’ but he isn’t sure if anyone else is in earshot. He can’t give his identity away. Kani would be heartbroken.

He walks further into the room, but before he can say anything, Miyuki rubs up against his ankles, purring loudly. “Hey kitty.” Zuko picks up the fluffy, troublesome cat, scratching her behind the ears. “Where’s your mom? I came to see her.” He asks the cat, pressing a kiss to her nose.

Miyuki mews, snuggling her head up under Zuko’s chin, purring.

Not long after that, Lo walks out of the back of the room, smiling, stick still through her white hair. “It’s good to see you again, Lee. It looks like Miyuki thinks so too.”

Zuko nods, walking towards the old woman, looking up at her. “I tried the bending technique you told me about a few days ago. A woman and her child weren’t doing well, I helped heal them. They were going to die pretty soon but they’re alright now. Do you know anything else about it? Anything that I could do to be better at it? I was able to help them but it took three days because I kept falling asleep between healing sessions. Drained me a lot.” He admits, wanting to get straight to the point, sure that Lo would go on some long tangent before getting to ask Zuko why he was here.

He wants to hear about her life, but learning to heal is so important to him. He wants to hear what she has to say about that and *then* have her tell him about some obscure story from ten years ago. Even though it’s barely past noon, it gets dark early here in the winter, Zuko isn’t sure that he likes that. Even though Kani hadn’t been explicit this time, he knows that the general rule is that she always wants him home before sunset. He wants to get what he came for and then listen to what Lo has to say about anything else. He doesn’t want to leave before she can tell him more.

The old woman smiles, resting her hands on Zuko’s shoulders. “I wish Song could have lived long enough to meet you, she would have been so happy to know that someone else was here to learn the artform she was most proud of. She would have loved to teach you herself. However, I do have the next best thing. You just have to promise to be careful with it to to bring it back when you’re done reading it. It might be helpful to transcribe the pages, I just want the original. It’s one of the few things I have left of my Song.” Lo says, letting go of Zuko and gesturing for him to follow her.

“I promise I’ll be very careful with it and bring it back as soon as I can.” He means it. He wishes that he had something of his mother’s to hold onto. Something that *actually* belonged to her, not things that reminded him of her or things she used occasionally.

She never felt at home in the palace and never did much to make herself at home. Most things in her room were cleaned out by the time Zuko even knew that she was gone. He wasn’t sure if his father ordered for them to be gotten rid of or his mother took them with her.

He had managed to beg one of the servants to let him take the sheets from her bed and switch them with his own. His parents never even cared about each other and Zuko can only assume that they only ever shared a bed twice. His mother had her own space, away from her husband. A place where Zuko used to be able to hide from him when she was around.

Unfortunately, it didn’t take long for the faint scent of his mother to be replaced by his own. He knew he should have hidden the sheets opposed to using them, but his father would have found them and he wanted to feel like his mother was holding him. Like she was still there to protect him from the worst that the world had to offer. That her arms were still his safe haven.

Lo leads Zuko into a smaller hut with a similar shape to the greenhouse but is filled with appliances and furnishings that would be found in a home. He can only assume that she lives here and just usually chooses to spend time in her greenhouse. Maybe she needs to tend to the plants or just likes it. He isn’t sure.

She pulls out a box from a cubby, setting it on the floor and pulling out something wrapped in cloth, handing it to Zuko.

Zuko carefully opens it, revealing a leather bound notebook. The Earth Kingdom emblem is colored in green with a rising sun in red on the right corner of the emblem. Zuko can’t help but smile at the creative way of mixing the two nations together in a way that would protect Lo and Song from anyone who saw it immediately assuming that one was a firebender, but also allowing Song to announce and be proud of her heritage.

Carefully opening it and scanning the pages, Zuko smiles.

There are drawings of the human body in many ways and how air circulates through it and is turned into energy. There are drawings and descriptions of the best ways to create large amounts of energy and then expelling it in a way so that it strengthens others with maximum efficiency while mitigating exhaustion of the healer.

There are descriptions of teas that strengthen chi especially when consumed by a firebender and can help with energy transfer. There are drawings and descriptions for the best placement of hands depending on ailment. Zuko can only imagine that this was Song’s life’s work and was never able to share it with the world. If he can learn from her writings, he won’t let her discovery go to waste or take generations longer to be discovered when more could have been saved.

“Thank you.” Zuko whispers, in awe at what Lo is sharing with him. She is trusting him with likely one of her most valued possessions with the hope he can carry on her wife’s legacy. That a part of her can still live on. “I’ll be careful with it. I wish I could have met Song, but I’ll do my best to integrate her discovery into the world. It can help a lot of people.” He promises. He means it.

Lo smiles, resting a hand on his head. “I know you will, but be careful. The reason she couldn’t teach people her art was because of fear. You can’t jeopardize yourself while hiding in the Earth Kingdom. Help who you can, but don’t get yourself killed because you trusted the wrong person.” She warns. Zuko can only assume that she knows that from experience.

“Don’t worry. I already promised my mom I would be careful.” He can’t let Kani down. He can’t let her fears become reality.

Lo smiles, offering Zuko her hand. “Well, let me make you some tea. You can snuggle with Miyuki. Can you stay for a little?”

Zuko nods, taking her hand. “I just need to be home before sunset or my mom worries and she might not let me go off on my own again for awhile.”

Lo chuckles, leading him back into the greenhouse, making him a cup of jasmine tea as Zuko sits down with Miyuki listening to her talk about her life long ago.

Azula knows that she is the one who had wanted Iroh to leave. She had wanted to know if Zuko was alive or not. She knows that as soon as he gets back with the information of his safety or the fact that they had gotten their hopes up, it will be better. Knowing that he is dead is better than being stuck in that state of uncertainty. She just needs to know if he is being taken care of, if he is safe, if no one is going to hurt him again. At least if he’s dead, he can’t be hurt.

Despite knowing that neither Mai nor Ty Lee would be here, she couldn’t help but to write to both of them a while before Iroh left. Even if she doesn’t see them for months or even years, she wants to be able to stay in contact with them. She wants them to know that she knows that she wasn’t the best friend to them and wants to treat them better in the future. Wants to be given a second chance after having time to reconsider who she is and who she wants to be.

As soon as either of them are willing to see her… *if* they are willing to see her, she needs to prove that she’s changed. She needs to prove that she won’t try to humiliate them, take advantage of them, or generally be dismissive of them outside of what they can do for her. She wants a chance to get to know them again as someone who’s life doesn’t revolve around protecting herself from her father. What she thought was simply winning his favor all these years was nothing but survival. Something Zuko understood long before she even understood the concept of that.

Luckily, her father hadn’t been in charge of her training today. He has been satisfied with her progress and had a master train her while Ozai was attending a meeting. Or at least that’s what he said. For all she knows he’s just sitting in the dark surrounded by fire waiting for someone to come in like some kind of freak.

Frankly, she doesn't care. Right now, she just wants to rest and eat. Maybe read some, she isn't sure. What matters is her father didn't pay any attention to her today. If she can have enough days like this, she can survive until her uncle gets home.

She isn't sure how long she has been in her room after bathing, but it can't be too terribly long...but then again her judgment of time isn't that good right now.

A knock comes at the door. She sits up, looking at it. "Yes?" She calls, unsure who would be here. She hadn't asked for anything recently. Really no one would be here unless something had happened.

"Someone is here to see you, Princess Azula. May I send her in?" Someone calls as Azula stands up, making sure that her hair and clothes are straight before turning towards the door and replying: "Yes, please."

Her uncle has always been kind and friendly to most of the servants, thanking them for their service even though it was their job to serve them. However, Iroh is the one who had told her that she should be kind and treat even those below her with respect. That they're people too and want to be respected. Her father is the one who had always taught her through actions to treat them like they are below her and don’t deserve her respect. She has known to be one way most of her life, but she also knows which man she wants to be more like.

It's been taking some getting used to, but it is slowly becoming more habitual. Hopefully it will continue to get easier with time.

The door slowly opens. She isn't sure who she was expecting to be but it's actually someone *wants* to see.

“Mai.” Azula half whispers, feeling a smile tugging at her lips, walking towards her friend, unsure if they should embrace or not. Mai isn’t much of a hugger and Azula really has never been either until recently. Ty Lee is the one who had initiated almost all physical contact.

“It’s really good to see you, it really is, but…what are you doing here? I thought you were with your family to support your father’s political career.” Azula says slowly as the guard walks away from the girls.

Mai sighs, leaning against the door frame. “I got your letter, used it as an excuse by saying it was a summons. You know my father would do anything to please the royal family. His urgency for me to reply was the most interest he has shown in anything I have done in months.”

Azula looks down at the ground and then back up at her friend. She still definitely isn’t good at these things. “I’m sorry, Mai. Would it be alright if I hugged you?” She asks softly, unsure how else to initiate something like that.

Mai nods, taking a step towards her as Azula wraps her arms around her friend, feeling tears burn in her eyes as she rests her forehead on Mai’s shoulder.

“Azula…are you okay? None of this really seems like you.” Mai asks as she pulls away, dark eyes meeting Azula’s. “Your letter was kind of unexpected and, well, you don’t seem like yourself.”

Azula walks around Mai, peering down the empty hall before closing the door and facing her friend again. “I’m not okay…not really. Things haven’t been good since…well I’m sure you know when.”

Azula had always known that Mai had a crush on her brother, she hadn’t been able to hide it very well, and she is sure that as soon as Mai heard about Zuko’s death it broke heart. Even if Zuko is alive and well in the Earth Kingdom now, he didn’t deserve what their father did to him. Nobody does.

Mai just looks down at the floor. “What happened? I’ve heard the stories, but what *really* happened?” Mai finally asks.

Taking her friend’s hand, Azula leads her to her bed, letting her sit down. She knows Mai isn’t the most emotional person and processing this would probably be hard for her. On top of that, Azula still isn’t sure of what she should tell her friend. There is just so much all mixed up in her head.

“I don’t know the exact details of what Zuko said, but he spoke out in a war meeting and had some issue with how the war was proceeding. He was challenged to an Agni Kai and when he refused to fight my father burned off half of his face. He was banished the day after he regained consciousness and he ran away on the ship he was supposed to take that night without uncle or his crew. We’ve only been able to assume he died for a while.” Azula squeezes Mai’s hand as she talks, sure her friend needs the kind of support that Azula isn’t sure how to offer.

Silence follows for a few minutes, it’s only when Azula is about to open her mouth to speak again that she sees tears shimmering on Mai’s cheeks.

Awkwardly, Azula wraps her arms around her friend’s shoulders, trying to offer the kind of comfort her uncle would offer her on bad days. That is most days now.

“The Fire Lord…your father…he just killed him. Just like that! For nothing! He killed him! He–” Azula clamps her hand over Mai’s mouth as her voice begins to rise to an uncharacteristically high level, worried someone might hear.

“Yes. My father killed his own son without an ounce of hesitation. If I’m not really careful, I might be next. The only thing protecting me besides being in his favor as of now is that it would be a hassle to…create a new heir. I can assure you that he won’t spare you. It’s not safe here.” Azula warns her friend, slowly removing her hand from her mouth.

“So you’re not safe either, are you?” Mai asks sadly, wiping tears from her face with the back of her hand.

Azula shakes her head. “No. I’m not. It’s why I need to be careful. Really careful. There is only so much my uncle can do to protect me.”

Another long silence follows before Mai breaks it again. “Should I stay here for a little? With you? I don’t really want to deal with my dad and pretend to be a happy family when we hardly ever even look at each other and I don’t want you to be alone here. I’m worried about you, Azula.”

Azula knows that she should tell her friend to go, that it isn’t safe here, that she needs to run, but she already knows that. She just doesn’t seem to care. She wants Mai to be away from here, to be safe. She also selfishly wants Mai to stay here with her. Even if her friend couldn’t offer any protection, just knowing that there is another friendly face in the palace could help a lot. Just knowing someone else would be there for her.

“Mai…I want you to know that staying here might be dangerous for you. I don’t want you getting hurt but I would love to be able to know that you’re here. Just, if you do stay, no matter what, you *can’t* stand up for me. I know my father won’t care that you’re here, he doesn’t care what I do as long as he doesn’t think that it is distracting me from training or making me less loyal to him. Just stay away from him and if he tells you to do something, do it. If he is ever angry with me, don’t protect me, don’t defend me, don’t come to my aid in any way, he will not spare you.” Azula warns, looking up at her friend.

Right now, she wants to tell Mai about the possibility that Zuko might be alive. That he might be alive and well in the Earth Kingdom with some peasant farmers or something. It isn’t that she doesn’t trust Mai to keep it a secret, it’s that she doesn’t want to give her friend false hope. She doesn’t want to tell Mai that Zuko might be alive only for Iroh to come home a little less than two weeks later just to say he’s dead. He can’t die twice for her. If he’s alive, she’ll tell her everything. If those letters weren’t from Zuko, then it won’t matter anyways.

“I promise I won’t do anything to put you or myself in more danger. You said you wanted to change. Show me by letting me into your life. Let people be there for you. I’m worried you won’t be okay if left alone.”

Instead of saying anything, Azula wraps her arms around her friend again. For now, she feels like things are going to be okay. The world is crumbling around her, but she feels like she is going to be okay. It’s going to be okay.

## Chapter 22

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes
