I hope that you guys like this.

### Text

It doesn’t take Zuko long to get home once he leaves Lo’s. For one, he stayed a bit later than he should have and needed to get back to the house before the sun began to get lower in the sky. Secondly, he really wants to look at the book that Lo had lent to him in greater detail.

He isn’t all that sure about the condition of the woman that he had kind of healed a few days ago, but maybe he can practice some of the techniques on her if she still isn’t back to full health. Both she and her husband know that Zuko is a firebender and doesn’t mean any harm. On top of that, he can possibly help her get back up to strength sooner than she would with just rest and time. That can only go so far as he has come to learn.

When Zuko gets back into the healing hut, he can see Feya and Kani talking to two men that Zuko has never seen before, neither looking injured and he isn’t sure why they would be here. However, the first thing he needs to do is get this book out of sight of strangers and lower the risk of ruining it down here. He is sure that Lo would be devastated if anything were to happen to it.

He can hear Kani talking to him but Zuko quickly hurries up the stairs before he can fully catch what she is saying to him. He’ll apologize for running off later. He’s sure that as soon as he explains to her what he is hiding and why she’ll understand and be grateful that he had the forethought to hide a book on firebending from strangers. Strangers who shouldn’t know that Zuko is a firebender.

As soon as he carefully tucks the book in his blankets under his turtle duck that Feya had made for him, he can hear footsteps coming up the stairs behind him. “Lee? What are you doing? Are you alright?” Kani asks, coming into view, looking concerned.

Zuko nods, standing up with a little bit of difficulty, but it is much easier with the brace opposed to the splint. He can deal with this a lot easier. He walks over to Kani, wrapping his arms around her waist. “I’ll tell you when they leave. Nothing bad, just about firebending.” He mumbles, doubting the men could hear him from downstairs but doesn’t want to get caught over something this stupid. It’s likely the same reason why Kani is referring to him by his alias despite knowing his real name.

“Ok, love.” Kani replies, pressing a kiss to the top of Zuko’s head. “The people downstairs are actually some old friends of Chen’s. I know them pretty well, but would you like to meet them? They’re odd, but they’re friendly and won’t hurt you.” Kani promises, carding her fingers through Zuko’s hair.

Zuko thinks for a moment. He wants to dig through the book that Lo gave him right now, but he isn’t sure when he’ll get another chance to meet more people who had been important parts of Kani and Chen’s life. Eventually, Zuko tentatively nods, smiling up at Kani.

Kani takes Zuko’s hand in hers and leads him back down the stairs to where Feya and the two men are now sitting on the ground in the vague shape of a circle, sipping what he can only assume is tea. Zuko just waves to them, unsure what else to say or do.

“Sweetheart, this is Po,” She gestures to the tall, lanky man with dark brown hair pulled up into a surprisingly neat Earth Kingdom style bun. His piercing green eyes suggest that he is an earthbender but Zuko can’t say for sure.

“And this is Lee.” She gestures to the larger man with shoulder length, jet black hair, dark skin, and almost black eyes. Zuko had never seen anyone who looked quite like him. Then again, the people of the Earth Kingdom tend to vary more in physical appearance than people in the Fire Nation or the Water Tribes for that matter, heavily due to the sheer size of the nation.

Zuko is grateful that it isn’t the other way around, it would have made it far more difficult to blend in and hide with the masses. People who know more about firebenders might think that Zuko might have come from an area close to the colonies or simply think that he looks a little different than most people found in the Earth Kingdom.

Luckily, with the topknot gone and now being dressed in Earth Kingdom green, it's much easier for eyes to simply scan over him if people aren’t looking for the subtle differences between the Earth Kingdom hazel and Fire Nation gold in his eyes. Don’t pick up on the stark difference between Zuko’s pale skin and black hair. It’s not a look exclusive to the Fire Nation, just far more common. It’s even easier considering no one is searching for Fire Nation spies in a small harbor town or an insignificant farming village.

“Po, Lee, this is Chen and I’s son, Lee.” She introduces Zuko, squeezing him a little closer to her side, more as a gesture of comfort and affection than protection. Zuko doesn’t think he could ever express the gratitude he still feels that it was Chen who found him. That the couple who had taken care of him is so loving, generous, patient, and compassionate. He isn’t sure what he would do in most other situations he may have found himself in.

“It’s nice to meet you, Lee. Your neighbor, Shi, told us a little about you when we saw her last. When we saw Chen he told us about you as well.” Po says, eyes landing on Zuko’s scar. He isn’t sure if that is supposed to signify that Chen had told then men about his injury, if he had left it out and they’re surprised, or simply because it is such a large injury in a place that Zuko could never dream of covering it out without heavy makeup that would be clear to everyone he was wearing.

Zuko nods, really unsure what to say to that considering he doubts that Chen would go on to tell these men that Zuko is a firebender from the Fire Nation who Chen is sure is from a noble family or at least wealthy, high ranking peasants. He really has no idea what Chen could have told them about him other than the fact that Zuko is adopted. He doesn’t want to say anything that may contradict something that the two think that they know and raise suspicions.

“Lee, my love, they know that you’re from the Fire Nation, it’s okay, they don’t care, you’re safe.” Kani says gently, likely feeling the uncomfortable tension in Zuko’s body as she holds him to her side.

Zuko quickly glances up at her, meeting Kani’s eyes, making sure that he had heard that correctly. He only needs to look at her for a moment before she gives him an encouraging smile. He looks back at the two men, eyes flitting between them a few times before finding his voice. “Anything else you know specifically about me?” Zuko asks, needing to know if they know that he is a firebender. There is a big difference between just being a kid from the Fire Nation and being a firebender kid from the Fire Nation.

The two men look at each other and shrug before Lee meets Zuko’s eyes with a surprisingly soft gaze. “Not much. Just said you were pretty freaked out when he found you, you’re from the Fire Nation, and that you don’t want any trouble. Nothing crazy. Why?”

Zuko shrugs in response, not sure how to say that he wants to know how much they know about him so he can see if they are anywhere close to figuring out that he is a high level Fire Nation fugitive and an enemy in Earth Kingdom territory. Judging by their statement, that would be quite the conclusion to jump to, so it’s unlikely. “Used to knowing more about what is going on around me. Want as much information as possible.” He says quietly, looking down, just close enough to the truth that the lie doesn’t burn in his throat.

“Sorry, he is still trying to adjust to a very new life, he can say and do some odd things every so often.” Kani explains, defending Zuko’s behavior. Hopefully, they won’t press.

Considering the fact that they very easily move onto a completely different subject, he doubts that their minds have even lingered on it. It helps ease Zuko’s nerves as they talk about nothing. Just simple conversation. To them, Zuko is just some Fire Nation kid who wants a family. Good.

It isn’t that the men make him feel uncomfortable or that he doesn’t want to be around them that Zuko feels the urge to leave the conversation. It is almost entirely about the fact that he has a book containing a barely discovered form of firebending upstairs just waiting to be brought back into existence. The energy of that fire is just waiting to be used for strength and health opposed to force and destruction. A way that firebending likely hasn’t been used in so long. Maybe even never before Song.

He can tell himself that he is so desperate to learn this technique to bring a part of Lo’s late wife back to life in some way. In some ways, that is completely true. He wants to honor what the woman had done for him and the comfort that she had offered him despite knowing nothing about him other than he was a child who needed help and who Kani and Feya cared for deeply. She could have turned him in, told him to leave, or told people about him. However, she had gone out of her way and repeatedly done as much as she could to help him settle into his new life. Help him a connection between who he once was and who he is.

“Mom, can I go upstairs? Just feeling tired.” Zuko explains quietly, tugging on Kani’s sleeve, not wanting to make the men think that he was leaving because of them. Well, technically he is, he could just show the book to Kani and Feya if they weren’t here, but it’s more of a safety thing than Zuko not liking them.

Kani looks down at him, cups his cheeks in her hand, and presses a kiss to his forehead, nodding. “Just make sure to eat something before you go to bed. I know that you haven’t eaten dinner yet.” She instructs.

Zuko nods, quickly wrapping his arms around her waist again before hurrying upstairs as fast as he can in his current situation.

He knows far too well that as soon as he picks up that book he will be engulfed in it and unable to bring himself to do much of anything else. So instead of going directly to his book, he makes his way to the kitchen first.

He isn’t sure if Kani and Feya have eaten yet, but there is a pot of soup hanging over the glowing embers with just enough heat to keep the contents up to temperature but not burned. The good thing about being a firebender is that even if it had been cold, he would be more than capable of heating it back up with a few breaths.

Zuko ladles out a bowl, eating it as fast as he can without risking making himself sick. He doesn’t want to risk spilling food on Lo’s book. He can’t do that to her after she has put so much trust in him with something that holds so much sentimental value that she could never even dream of replacing.

As soon as he finishes, Zuko quickly washes his bowl and carefully dries his hands before hurrying back over to the other side of the fireplace facing the living room.

Zuko pulls out the book and begins to pour over the contents of it, needing to know what he could be doing to strengthen this. To be able to do more. To help heal the world with the element that injured it.

There is so much more detail in here than Zuko thought was possible to discover in one lifetime when he skimmed through it earlier. Even from just the first few pages, diagrams, and drawings, it feels like far more of a refined skill than a desperate prayer for life in the form of fire.

He learns that it is most effective for him to “overcharge” himself as Song had put it before even beginning when treating someone who is particularly ill or injured. That he should try and heat and grow his inner flame until he can begin to feel his chest and stomach become uncomfortably hot, but not painful, before placing one hand on their navel and the other on their chest and that he should use that energy he has built up to sync the patient’s breath to his rapidly and effectively. This is especially important if whatever ailment they are facing is respiratory or weakening them to the point of obstructing airways.

The book is careful to note that whenever he is healing a patient, he should keep his eyes open and head held up. Considering flames will be coming from his mouth, even if only a few inches, if too close, he could scorch or even burn the person that he is trying to help. Or, as Song had noted, he could catch nearby drapery on fire, a story he will have to ask Lo about when he returns the book.

For patients who aren’t close to death he should try and connect with them in a more meditative way. It is similar to how he would connect to the energy of a flame that would rise and fall with his breaths. First energy needs to connect, then breath. It is advised that he should “overcharge” himself when unnecessary as he will exhaust himself faster. It is more a technique to get someone out of immediate danger so they can be healed later than healing them all at once.

Once connected, for both patients close to death and not, it is noted that he should move his hands with each breath about four inches in each vertical direction on an adult. He should move down when inhaling and up when exhaling.

There is also a note instructing that he be aware as to where his hands will be falling when moving, not because anything particularly bad would happen, but more to mitigate the chance of awkward encounters for both parties. Despite having lived the life of a soldier, Zuko is still a 13 year old boy and can’t help but giggle at that comment while making a mental note of it.

It goes on to make notes on different breathing patterns depending on the number of heartbeats that the patient has in a minute. He isn’t sure what that has to do with anything, but he’ll make sure to do it. It is suggested that someone counts to fifteen seconds while Zuko counts heartbeats and they tell him when to stop, then he multiplies that number by four. This is not necessary when “overcharging”. There is a chart below as to how many seconds in, out, and between Zuko should breathe depending on the range that the heart rate it falls into.

He is pretty sure that he’ll learn the most from actually *doing* some of these things. Hopefully he can. He would rather practice now and understand what he is doing in a non-dire situation opposed to trying to figure it out when there is more pressure on him to do this right. When the minutes it might take to reposition himself and restart could be the difference between a full recovery and chronic pain. The difference between life and death.

He is fully engulfed in copying down some of what Song had written onto paper, hoping to make his own field notes later when he jumps at the touch of a hand on his shoulder, more surprise than anything else.

“What are you doing, love? I thought you said you were going to bed?” Kani asks, sitting down next to him, wrapping an arm around Zuko’s shoulders. “Is everything alright? It’s not like you to lie about things like this.” Her voice isn’t accusational, it’s purely curious. By ‘things like this’ he can only assume she means situations that aren’t for his own protection considering there is almost nothing he can bring himself to lie about that he doesn’t absolutely have to. He had even come clean to Kani and Chen in the first few weeks that a lot of his personal information was a lie and he just wasn’t ready to talk about it. He couldn’t ever bring himself to lie to Kani or Chen for long. It hurts in so many ways.

Zuko picks up the book Lo had shown him, handing it to her. “I didn’t want to tell them that I’m a firebender but didn’t want to make them think I hated them. I really wanted to read this. Song, Lo’s wife, made this.” He explains before he can stop himself, unsure if Kani knew that the woman Lo had spent so much of her life with was a firebender. He knows that Kani won’t mind, he just isn’t sure if it is information that he should be giving out.

Kani carefully looks through the pages, reading the script intently for a few minutes before turning to Zuko, giving him a small smile. “So *this* is what Lo had told you about? This is how she knew?”

Zuko nods, smiling. “I was hoping that maybe I could visit Gaon and Kya. Feya said that Kya would take a few weeks to fully recover so she still is probably in bed. I want to try and see what works on someone who is out in immediate danger and knows what I am. I also might be able to help her as well.” Zuko suggests quietly, meeting Kani’s hesitant eyes. “I’d want to go with you or Feya, I don’t want to go alone. I get he was grieving and scared, but I don’t want Gaon to get mad at me again and not have you there.” He adds quickly, snuggling up against Kani.

“We’ll talk about it.” Kani finally says after an elongated silence. “Feya knows them better than I do, we can talk to her and see if she thinks that they won’t say anything if you seek them out. How does that sound?”

Zuko nods, he can live with that compromise.

“Thank you.” Zuko mumbles after a few minutes, smiling as he closes his eyes, resting his head against Kani’s shoulder.

“For what, love?” Kani asks, pressing a kiss to the top of his head, absentmindedly running her fingers up and down Zuko’s upper arm.

“Just for everything. Not many people would have done what you and Chen did for me. Not just healing me but taking me in. For being patient with me. I was thinking about it today. Even if you healed me and then just sent me off, I really don’t know what would have happened. Was in a really bad place emotionally and I think I would have died or just become the worst version of myself. I don’t wanna hurt people, but I think I would have.” Zuko admits quietly.

Anger is the easiest way to not deal with emotions such as grief from losing everything that one identifies themselves as. He doesn’t like breaking down so easily right now, there are times when he can feel anger at the edge of his mind wanting to take over, wanting to protect him. It hasn’t happened in awhile, but he knows that he would have succumbed to it if he hadn’t been given a safe place to break and then heal properly. Not heal with a twisted heart. If he hadn’t been given safe, loving arms to hold him as he fell apart into the most basic and vulnerable pieces. What would have happened if he didn’t have people slowly helping him put himself back together again.

The process can be stressful, irritating, humiliating, and even dehumanizing at times. All he can hope for is that eventually he can be whole again. That he won’t break down from insecurities and fears finding their way into his mind or someone not taking kindly to his very existence. He needs to hope that after all of this, he’ll be whole again and will be able to stand his ground against opponents in the world and against himself in his mind.

“Well I’m grateful that Chen managed to talk me into marrying him, few people are as kind as him. I’m glad he found you and brought you home despite everything. I’m grateful he talked me into letting you stay even after you healed. I’m so happy to have you in my life, love. I know that your life has been hard and it could have been even harder, but that’s over now. You’re safe.” Kani says softly, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s forehead. “I love you so much, Zuko.”

Zuko hadn’t realized that Kani was particularly hesitant to have him stay with them for so long. Despite that, she had done so much to make sure that Zuko didn’t know and cared for him anyways. Making sure that he felt safe and was cared for no matter what previous opinions she may have had on firebenders. She had been kind and caring when he needed her most and that is what matters.

He vaguely remembers her brief hesitance when Chen first informed her that Zuko was a firebender that first night before she had begun to comfort and heal him. He hadn’t thought much about it, assuming it was just his nerves or she rightly needed a moment to process the fact that her husband had just brought an unknown firebender into their home.

“Thank you for caring for me despite everything.” He says quietly, looking up at her, he means it. He doesn’t care if Kani had hated him in secret for the first few days, he has heard how she talks about him now when she doesn’t think he’s listening.

No matter what she once felt, she cared for him until he was healthy and had then begun to love him unconditionally. Began to love him in the way he thought that his real mother loved him.

No, not his *real* mother, his first mother. Kani is his real mother even if she had only been that for a handful of months. In that time, she had shown him more compassion and love than Zuko had felt in his entire life. He trusts that Kani wouldn’t leave him behind as soon as he was no longer worth loving. As soon as she was offered something better. Zuko had already shown her his worst and she had stayed.

“Thank you for trusting me.” Kani says softly, pulling Zuko a little closer to her, making him feel secure and loved.

Eventually, Zuko can hear aggressive footsteps coming up as Feya comes into view, looking exhausted and irritated. “Zuko, I hope you know that I will love you no matter who you decide to be with or what you want to be in life, but *please* don’t be like those two.” Feya grumbles, pulling a jug of wine from a high shelf and pouring a cup for herself before joining Kani and Zuko by the fire.

Zuko cocks his head, under the impression that Feya liked the two men downstairs, not understanding. “What did they do?” He asks.

“They’re both perfectly nice people, they’re just crazy. It’s fucking freezing outside and I told them that they could stay downstairs because it’s pretty warm, but no, they want to go build a fucking rock tent in the damn cold woods and sleep *there* . I can’t deal with them.” She grumbles.

Zuko giggles at the thought. However, he can agree with his aunt that it is a weird thing to do out of choice and not necessity.

“Feya, Lo gave Zuko a book where someone had collected a bunch of research on his healing firebending. He was wondering if you think it would be safe to go back to visit Kya and practice some of the more refined techniques on her. I’m sure she’s still weak after what happened and it could help her. One of us would go with him, but I’m not sure if having Zuko seek them out might result in one of them saying something about him being a firebender.”

Luckily, Feya smiles. “I think that would be a great idea. If Zuko wants to learn more about this, that’s great. He could help a lot of people if he learns how to do this properly. Anyways, you don’t need to worry about them saying anything about him. I made it very clear that if they put my family in danger I would make sure everyone who works with me knows, along with Lo, to turn them away if they were to ever need medical assistance again.” She explains flatly.

A shocked expression comes over Kani’s face as she looks at her sister. “What is wrong with you? You can’t do that. That’s horrible.”

Feya just shrugs. “I can and I will. All they have to do to prevent that from happening is not sell someone out who was just trying to help. It would be their own fault if that were to happen.”

Zuko really isn’t sure if Feya would actually turn them away if they told someone about Zuko and then were later in dire need of help. Feya is tough, but she isn’t cruel. Then again, she is protective and from what he has heard, she can hold a grudge.

With that in mind, he really is surprised that she has taken a liking to Zuko so easily and quickly. She has never really talked about her late husband in front of Zuko before but he knows that he is presumed dead by the hands of the Fire Nation. He can understand that she wouldn’t take out her loss on a random firebender child, but he doesn’t understand how she couldn’t hate the Fire Lord’s son. Hate him for being a part of the family who took someone she cared for from her.

“Are you going to go with him?” Feya asks, looking at the flickering flames, the light casting oddly on her face.

Kani nods. “Of course I’m going with my baby.” She kisses Zuko’s head again before beginning to stand. “You should get some rest, love. It made you so tired last time, even if it might not be as hard on you this time, I want you well rested for tomorrow.” She explains.

Zuko just nods, snuggling up under his blankets and pulling his turtle duck to his chest as Feya gets up as well, both women walking towards Feya’s bed.

With all of the excitement of being able to learn more about himself, bring the spirit of someone back to life, and maybe even help turn fire into an element of warmth and growth opposed to destruction buzzing in his chest, he is surprised that he can fall asleep at all. Despite that, sleep slowly presses down on him, lulling him into it easily with safety, comfort, and warmth.

The next morning, Zuko is up before Kani and Feya as usual. Zuko had talked about how it's pretty common for firebenders to rise and fall with the sun and she can only take his word for it.

He’s a very odd child, but considering everything he’s been through, he is surprisingly well adjusted. Kani can’t imagine many other kids his age suffering through the kind of abuse that Zuko had and still being capable of learning how to love and trust after having those emotions being taken advantage of for so long.

On top of that, if really any other person had told Kani the horrible things that they had endured, she would assume they were exaggerating at the least. She of course would never say that, invalidating a trauma victim is always worse than pitying someone seeking the attention and care that comes with it. However, if she knows anything about Zuko, it’s that he isn’t a liar. If anything, she is worried that he hasn’t told her everything that he had endured. He might not be sure how to bring it up or too humiliated to do so.

Despite his quirks and heritage, Kani can’t help but to love the kid. He’s nothing like the Fire Nation soldiers she had been warned about for so much of her life. He is nothing like the twisted, faceless monster engulfed in scorching flame as she could only ever imagine the Fire Lord as. It’s even harder to not picture him like that after the horror stories that Zuko has shared with her. Everything that he said only confirmed that idea that the Fire Lord didn’t have a drop of human blood in his body.

Zuko is sweet, gentle, and curious. That curiosity can be quite irritating at time and worry her that he might do something stupid in hopes of understanding something. No matter what, nothing he has ever done has been out of malice. He had gotten angry before and even aggressive with Chen at one point. She wouldn’t go as far to call it violent considering how Chen described the incident in the barn made it sound like Zuko just wanted Chen away from him or to get a reaction opposed to trying to hurt him.

All of the kid’s anger has been from fear or feeling like he is somehow less. A feeling that Kani hates she had fed into for a while. At least he used his words *after* he broke his ankle. She is grateful that they were able to find ways to resolve the issue relatively easily considering she was worried that she would be giving her baby up to the colonies in a matter of months.

When she fully walks further out of the room and towards Zuko, she is able to get a better look at Zuko and she smiles.

He is sitting in a meditative position, the fire rising and falling with his breaths. She isn’t sure if he is trying to gather strength for later today, trying to calm himself, or if it is just something that makes him feel better. His reasons for meditating seem to jump around a lot, but it seems to help him. Makes him more calm and focused.

She doesn’t bother him and quietly walks down the stairs into the healing hut. Hopefully her sister will sleep in even for just a little for once and Kani can begin to set up for the day. She is sure that Zuko will want to go try and help Kya as soon as possible and with Feya’s conformation of his safety (even of she doesn’t necessarily agree with the method) she is excited to see what these adjustments will do for both his and Kya’s overall health.

She begins to boil water in the sanitary kettles so that they can have as clean as possible water to clean open wounds and organize any supplies that weren't the night before. No one wants to be caught in a situation where they have a patient in immediate need of assistance and not being able to find what they’re looking for.

She works in silence for about half an hour when she hears a knock on the door. She doubts that it is one of the other healers coming here at this hour, but she can’t be sure. She hopes it isn’t someone in need of medical assistance, she isn’t fully prepared right now, but it’s not like people can time a medical emergency to the convenience of healers.

Walking over quickly, she opens the door, almost relieved to see Po and Lee. Almost. It’s not that she doesn’t like them, it’s that it’s just too early to deal with their shit. Sometimes she wonders how the two had managed to survive together in the middle of nowhere for so long, but they must be doing something right.

Or at least not doing something wrong enough to get themselves killed.

“How can I help you?” She asks, unsure what the two men would be doing here this early if they didn’t need something. Neither looks injured, but some injuries can be hidden pretty easily considering it’s not now that they’re dangerous but it’s when they are allowed to fester that they become a real issue. Even the smallest cuts in the right conditions can lead to death if left to infection, illness, and death.

“When we were talking to your sister last night she briefly implied that you and your son would be here longer than expected. Do you want us to relay that to Chen so he doesn’t start to worry?” Po asks, giving her a small smile.

Kani honestly hadn’t even considered that with everything going on.

Usually, she makes sure that she gets home in the timeframe that she told her husband she would be back so that he wouldn’t worry that something had happened. However, every other time she hadn’t been trying to deal with the fact that her adopted son is Fire Nation royalty while not letting the kid know that it’s taking her time to *actually* accept. She knows that she loves Zuko and wants him to stay, but she doesn’t like the fact that he is the Fire Lord’s son. She doesn’t like it at all.

Despite the fact that she knows that it isn’t his fault and that he is nothing like his family, it isn’t easy. She will need to ask Zuko if she can talk to Chen about this. This isn’t a secret she wants to keep from him, unsure what it might do if left unspoken. They would never throw Zuko out over something he couldn’t control when he has been so gentle and happy while living with them, but they will need to *truly* accept this.

“That would be very helpful. There’s been a lot going on and still so much I need to figure out and then do so again when I get home.” She explains quickly, wanting to give some kind of reason, hoping Chen might understand that the lack of specifics meant it was about Zuko. She isn’t sure though, it’s really too early for this.

The two men look at each other briefly before turning back to Kani. “We could ask him if he wants to come down here to talk to you. We’re not in any rush to get back, nothing that needs immediate attention back home. We could take care of your animals for a few days and he could take one of our ostrich horses down here and talk to you in person.” Lee offers as Po offers her a small smile.

Kani looks between the two men, really unsure what to say to that proposition. That actually might be ideal. These two might not be the most careful with a lot of things, but they do care about animals. Anyways, she would be impressed if they could break her stone house. More importantly, if things don’t go well with Kya and Gaon today she can send Zuko back with Chen for his safety and still be able to help her sister for a little longer. “That would actually be really helpful, thank you.” She replies, offering the two a smile in return.

“Okay, we’ll let him know this evening.” Po says before he and Lee leave down the road. She has no idea if the two even did what they came to do in town nor does she have any idea what they were doing. However, she has enough things to question about them and doesn’t need anymore. She doesn’t have the energy for that.

With that in mind, she walks back into the room and finishes setting up, praying that things go as smoothly as possible with the couple today.

Zuko isn’t sure exactly how long he had been in a meditative state when he feels a hand resting on the back of his shoulder. He is sure that even a month ago, he would have flinched at the sudden contact. But that was then. Since then, he has come to understand that unexpected touch can be good. It can be gentle and affectionate opposed to malicious and painful.

He opens his eyes, looking up at Feya who is now standing behind him. “You want something to eat? You’re going to be using a lot of energy today.” She reminds him, offering him a hand to help him stand up.

Smiling, Zuko takes her hand and she leads him into the kitchen where she has the pot of soup back on the fire, heating it up again. He can tell that Feya was in charge of making breakfast this morning.

Kani thinks that there are different foods that one should eat throughout the day. That it’s better to start with something easier on the stomach such as jook and that protein should be increased throughout the day. Feya on the other hand sees food as food. If she likes it, she likes it. Soup or jook, if it’s good enough for dinner, it’s good enough for breakfast.

As far as Zuko is concerned, if he is eating and is around people who he loves and he knows actually care about him during meals, he could be handed the worst meal of his life and he would be happy.

Kani is already in the kitchen and eating soup from a bowl, giving Feya a dirty look as she eats it, likely not pleased that her sister made breakfast soup.

Zuko quickly ladles a bowl of soup out for himself before hurrying over to Kani and snuggling up next to her by the table.

“Hey, love, how are you feeling? Still want to do this today?” She asks, nuzzling Zuko’s head before going back to eating her soup.

Zuko nods, barely able to contain his excitement. If he can heal people more effectively and not drain so much from himself, he could change things. Maybe not on a huge scale at first, but he could teach other firebenders how to do this. Teach the world that firebending isn’t all about destruction. Remind firebenders that the purpose of their bending is to create warmth and light, not to burn everything uncontrollably. That is something that everyone had forgotten when the war started. When firebenders were taught to fuel their fire with hate, anger, and desire for power.

“I’m excited.” He finally says, remembering that Kani hadn’t only asked him a yes or no question. “I hope I can help her. I hope I can help more people.” He admits, eating a few bites of his soup. Honestly, it’s better than it was last night.

“I hope you can help her, too. Considering everything, I’m still not sure how you’re so compassionate and hopeful.” Kani tells him, running her fingers through his inky hair.

“It’s because you gave me a chance.” He admits, thankful he hadn’t succumbed to the pull of anger to hide everything. Thankful that he had been saved.

Feya joins them after that, sitting across from them, beginning to eat as well. “Tell me if they give you trouble, kid. I’ll fuck ‘em up if they do.” She offers.

Kani just glares. “Stop swearing in front of him like that. I don’t need him going around talking like a sailor.”

Feya just shrugs.

“Oh, Feya, Po and Lee stopped by this morning and they offered to watch over the farm for a few days so Chen could come down here. I told them that there was just a lot going on after they offered to let Chen know Zuko and I were safe, we just might come home later. I hope that’s alright with you.” Kani says after a brief moment of silence.

Zuko can feel his face lighting up, really hoping Chen could come down here. He really misses him. Chen is easy to be around and he just makes Zuko feel safe and secure when he’s close. He wants that again even if he doesn’t feel afraid right now.

“I mean, even if I did care, it's not like I could stop him. Also, don’t act like you care if I mind or not.” Feya grumbles, a small smile forming in the corner of her mouth. Kani just rolls her eyes.

It doesn’t take long for them to finish eating and clean up from breakfast after that. The three head downstairs. Feya joins the two healers that have already come in, ready to start working. Kani and Zuko greet them while also saying goodbye before heading out.

After Zuko had successfully made it to Lo’s and back by himself, Kani doesn’t insist that Zuko hold her hand on their way through the empty streets, most of the town not quite up yet.

They walk for about fifteen minutes when they reach a house and Kani knocks on the door, Zuko just moves a bit closer to her, unsure what to expect.

It takes a few minutes for the door to open and Zuko can only assume it’s because Gaon was in the middle of something. The anger and fear that Zuko had seen on the man’s face before is just replaced with exhaustion. He can’t begin to imagine how difficult it must be to be needing to take care of most of a newborn’s needs, nursing his wife back to health, and making sure that his family makes it through the winter.

He looks at Kani briefly before his eyes fall on Zuko for an extended period of time, possibly trying to figure out what Zuko could want.

“Lee may have found resources explaining more refined ways to do…whatever it is that he was doing to heal your wife last time. He was hoping that he could see if it works better and if he can help her recover more. He really only got her out of danger last time, he didn’t exactly heal her.” Kani explains, although Zuko is sure that the man is already aware of the last part of her  
statement.

Thankfully, Gaon nods, opening the door for them. “It’s not like you can make her any worse.” The man mumbles as the two walk in. “You *did* manage to save her last time.” He adds quickly, not quite smiling at Zuko, but softening his expression a little.

Kani rests a hand on Zuko’s shoulder as they follow Gaon to the back of the house to where Kya and the baby are resting. Some color has come back to Kya’s face but she’s likely still weak from the strain that had been put on her body. Zuko doesn’t understand too much about pregnancy or giving birth, but from what he has heard from Kani and Feya, if even the slightest thing goes wrong it can be very dangerous for both the mother and child.

Kneeling next to the bed, Gaon rests a hand on Kya’s stomach and she opens her eyes. He can only assume that she wasn’t actually asleep and just resting if she woke up that easily.

“Hey, Kya, do you remember Lee from the healer’s home? The firebender?” Gaon asks his wife. The woman nods, giving Zuko a warm smile. “Thank you, Lee. For everything.” She says softly.

Zuko isn’t sure how to respond to that. Well, technically he does, he knows that he should say ‘you’re welcome’ but the words aren’t able to form in his mouth in any way, he isn’t sure why, it’s not like he has any issue with it. It might just be his nerves.

Instead, he moves onto his purpose. “I was hoping that I could try to do more for you with some new techniques I read about. I thought it best to practice on someone who knows what I am and hopefully I can help more people. I’m hoping I can also help you get even a little stronger.”

“I would be very grateful for anything you could do. It would be nice to be back on my feet sooner rather than later.”

He has to say that he was worried that Kya might not want him firebending near her and her son, healing or not.

He pulls out the book, flipping through the pages carefully to find the chart about the heartbeats and breaths. Kani had told him that she would help him find Kya’s pulse and teach him how to take it. Considering he has already healed Kya before, he doubts that she’ll be worried that Zuko doesn’t seem to know the basics about being a healer, but he doesn’t want to scare others when they have no idea who he is.

“Does the baby have a name?” Zuko asks, looking at the tiny person sleeping against his mother’s arm. The last time Zuko was around a baby this young was when Azula was born and he doesn’t remember any of that being a baby himself. It’s odd to think that people started off that small and wrinkly. It’s cute in a potato-ish sort of way.

“Well, he wouldn’t be here without you, so we actually named him Lee.” Kya responds, smiling down at the little baby.

Zuko can’t help but feel a slight blush in his cheeks at that.

Before he can say anything, or even think of anything to say to that, Kani takes Zuko’s right hand, maneuvering it around Kya’s wrist and helping him find the pulse. Once he finds it, she counts silently to fifteen while Zuko counts the number of pulses he feels. He quickly multiplies them and gives her an answer. Kani double checks his work considering it is his first time checking someone’s pulse and confirms his answer.

Gaon takes baby Lee from Kya so that Zuko wouldn’t need to worry about accidentally burning the baby while trying to help Kya.

Eventually, Zuko begins placing his hands, trying to connect to Kya’s energy. He had read that it takes practice to learn how to find it quickly but it will get easier with time.

Several minutes pass before he can feel a slight electrical tingle running through his arms as he holds more energy in himself than he necessarily needs.

He focuses on his breathing in a way that he would when meditating. He reaches out to Kya’s energy and breath like he would reach out to a flame and fuel its need for breath with his own. Fuel it as an extension of his own life but also simply connecting with something apart from him. Something just as capable of breathing life and energy into him.

It isn’t quite like Zuko is breathing for Kya and it isn’t quite them breathing together or Zuko matching her breaths. It’s like he has managed to coax her to match his breath without using any form of social cues to communicate it, just the energy in their bodies. Like their breathing for each other. The energy around then turning into something that they can absorb directly into their own forces.

After a few minutes, Zuko pulls away, gasping for breath and leaning against Kani despite not feeling deprived of air. It’s a less severe reaction than the first time, but he is already feeling exhausted.

Kani rubs his back, holding him close as he can vaguely hear Gaon say that he’s going to get him something. Zuko just needs to wait a few minutes before he can really care about much else but trying to draw energy into himself. He also figures it will take a few minutes for Kya to feel a difference in her health like last time.

As his head begins to clear and his breathing begins to return to a normal rate, Gaon walks back into the room with baby Lee cradled to his chest with a large piece of yellow cloth and holding a cup in one hand and a bowl in the other.

He hands both to Zuko before walking back to the other side of the bed, sitting back next to Kya, taking her hand.

The cup is ceramic and is painted green and yellow, the circular stone with a square in it that Zuko has seen around the Earth Kingdom despite not being the emblem. He is pretty sure it is what is on the Earth Kingdom military uniforms as well. It is something different from the Fire Nation but far from the most jarring thing, he isn’t sure why he is focusing on it at all with all of the changes in his life.

He takes a sip of the hot liquid and relaxes a little. Ginseng tea. It’s his uncle’s favorite. Zuko doesn’t have a strong opinion on the tea itself, it’s just the few good memories of his home that are attached to it.

The bowl has a thick slice of bread that is still hot, likely recently baked along with a peeled hard boiled egg.

He takes a bite of the bread, it’s good, really good. He vaguely remembers that Kya is a baker and maybe she made this. If she didn’t, which is likely, Gaon must have picked up plenty of skills from her.

Zuko pulls off a piece, offering it to Kani. “Want some? It’s really good.”

Kani shakes her head. “You eat it, you need your energy, love.” She assures him.

Zuko nods, taking another bite before setting it back in the bowl and leaning towards Kya. “Do you feel any better, ma’am?” He asks, unsure if what he did was effective enough.

Thankfully, Kya nods. “Yeah, pain in my lower back and abdomen is less sharp and severe and I feel less short of breath.”

Zuko can’t help but smile at that. “Can I do another round?” He asks, reading his hands above her.

Kya consents before Zuko rests his hands on her chest and navel, repeating the process.

Not many people have come in during the day. For most business models, that wouldn’t be good. However, Feya can’t help but be glad that a large number of people don’t need medical attention.

It’s been made clear that if someone is unable to pay for treatment, they won’t be turned away. It’s not exactly a small town, but there isn't any assistance besides Lo for miles around. Anyways, most people pay and when Feya and the others have been struggling in the past, the town has done what they can to take care of them.

Only one patient is currently being tended to and Feya uses the break to step outside for a breath of fresh air and a moment alone. She loves her sister and new nephew, but she does like her space as well.

She begins walking down the street. She doesn’t plan to go far, there is a cliff a few minutes walk from her home that overlooks the ocean. It isn’t an uncommon place for people to go. It usually isn’t crowded, but people will slowly trickle through the area, looking at the sight throughout the day.

It is a beautiful day outside even if it is a bit chilly. Where she had despised Chen for a few years for stealing her sister away from her, she can understand the draw to a life out in the country. She knows that farmwork is hard work, but one gets to be outside everyday. They can work on their own time and generally do what they please.

Considering she has only helped Kani and Chen with their farm and never actually lived on one, she is well aware that she is romanticizing the idea of rural life. She is sure that people who grew up knowing nothing but farmland might romanticize the idea of life in a town or even a city. Places where people congregate and can share ideas and customs. That is true, but there are downsides.

Feya does like the town that she lives in, but she could never imagine wanting to live in a city. Any city. She is sure that there is so much going on there that would constantly be there for entertainment, she is sure that there are far more downfalls as well. If there is crime in poverty in a town where people know each other and are more likely to help one another, she is sure issues like that are far more prevalent in the cities.

She has never been and she doesn’t plan on changing that. But then again, she didn’t plan on caring about a firebender let alone a royal. She will be willing to admit if she is wrong if she is to ever find herself in a city and likes it.

When she nears the cliff, she is surprised to see a relatively large group of people standing on the cliff murmuring amongst themselves. She can’t really understand what they are talking about so she hurries over to join them.

She looks over the water and sees it. A Fire Navy ship.

This has happened before, but it isn’t common. Every time it does, it brings panic into the people, all unsure if it is people looking for supplies and rest or soldiers coming to destroy them.

Most Fire Nation soldiers that pass by the town travel by foot. Even though it is a harbor town, most crews must deem the town too small to risk stopping in enemy territory for. Usually only those who are in desperate need of supplies come.

Even if their forces are weakened if they’re stopping here, Si Lang isn’t a big enough town to justify having large amounts of soldiers or any at all depending on the year. Most of the time, there is the understanding that merchants will sell supplies to Fire Navy troops and then the troops will leave unharmed. It is understood that far too many lives of the townsfolk would be lost fighting trained soldiers even if the town would likely win due to vastly outnumbering the soldiers.

Feya doesn’t come any closer at that, she hurries back the way she came. She needs to let the others know. For now, she needs to pray that her overprotective sister will smother that firebender so those soldiers won’t even look at him. It will be fine. It has to be.
