### Text

When Zuko leans limply against Kani’s chest almost sounding like he is gasping for air is when Kani doesn’t allow him to heal Kya anymore. She is surprised that the contents of the book was so helpful in keeping Zuko’s energy up for this much longer while healing Kya just as, if not even more, effectively.

Considering Kya is in long term pain (she wouldn’t go as far as to say chronic with the information they have now), it is hard to tell how much she has been healed in the long term. However, she is able to sit up without struggling and able to hold baby Lee without partially resting him on the bed.

She can only hope that this improvement lasts and that with a little more time and rest she will be able to get around the house and do some of the basics. Hopefully by spring, she will be mostly back up to her full health.

As of now, Zuko’s eyes are closed and he is not moving from Kani’s chest but he is still mumbling about how he can still do more. That he wants to at least do one more round of healing to help Kya a little more.

Kani shakes her head even though the firebender can’t see her. “No, love. You’re exhausted. You can come back another time and do more. The only thing you’re doing for the rest of today is getting something to eat and getting some rest.” She informs the little boy, pressing a kiss to the top of his head.

Zuko moans softly and sleepily in protest but makes no move to get towards Kya or even away from Kani.

“We’re gonna go home in just a little bit, my love.” Kani promises, gathering him up in her arms and standing. Zuko is heavier than he was, but he’s still too light for her liking.

Thankfully, Zuko doesn’t make any attempt to protest as she moves him into a more comfortable position, careful to hide his face in the crook of her neck. She doubts anyone would recognize him, but complacency could lead to her son’s arrest and death.

“Thank you, Kani. Please let your son know that when he wakes up. He’s saved our family and done more.” Kya says softly, smiling as Gaon sits next to her, offering a finger out to baby Lee who takes it in his tiny fist, giggling a little.

“I will, thank you for letting him. He was so excited last night.” She tells the couple, smiling down at the boy in her arms. “I’m so proud of him. He’s going to help a lot of people.” She says softly, sure that being able to save people and teach other firebenders how to heal, to lead them away from fighting, pain, and war would help him feel more in place. Would raise his far too low self esteem even if it has been improving.

“When is his birthday? There aren't many abundant luxuries in winter, but I can make him something special when more starts growing.” Kya offers, giving Kani a warm look.

A small, guilty pit forms in Kani’s stomach as she realizes she has no idea when Zuko was born. She and Chen had been so focused on figuring out what trauma Zuko had suffered in the past so they could mitigate triggers for him and just trying to get him healthy and feel safe that they hadn’t even *considered* the small things like that.

“I don’t know.” Kani admits sadly. “We’ve only had him for a few months and, well, he has a very haunted past. There’s a lot we don’t know about him just because we were trying to focus on the important things and that sort of thing just didn’t come up. I’ll ask him later.” She promises. She means it.

Gaon gives her a quick, sympathetic look. Luckily, neither of them even look at her with a hint of accusation. Considering how Zuko had interacted with the couple and what he had told Gaon when Zuko was first learning to heal, they know that the firebender has known very little kindness before the Earth Kingdom.

“What kind of treats does he like?” Kya moves on, not dwelling on Kani’s shortcomings as a mother.

“He loves anything you could give to him. He didn’t grow up with a lot of food and I haven’t ever seen him ever not be completely enthusiastic about eating something.” She can’t tell this couple that Zuko was intentionally starved by his father. First of all, it is a very sensitive, traumatic, and personal topic for the firebender and isn’t any of their business. Second of all, it would insinuate that he had access to food and was in a household where he could be denied it. That isn’t the kind of thing you see in peasant families often. Peasants typically don’t just see their children as heirs or like an item to show off. They’re *children.*

Also, Kani has seen Zuko turn down food far too often. However, he hasn’t been doing it recently. She can only draw the conclusion that he isn’t picky and his appetite is almost completely defined by his anxiety level. After the boy started to learn that eating was something social and would never be weaponized in their household, he had begun to really enjoy cooking and eating.

Zuko is far from mentally healthy, but he isn’t convinced that he is going to be beaten, starved, or thrown out just for making simple mistakes. He is so much calmer now that he is trusting again. A consistent schedule, regular meals, and affection at no cost had done a lot for the boy.

“I’ll be sure to think of something special for him. Let me know as soon as you can.” Kya answers, waving at Kani.

Nodding once to the couple, Kani walks out the door, Zuko’s likely sleeping body resting comfortably against her’s. Even if it takes her the rest of her life to fully accept that her sweet little boy is the Fire Lord’s son, she will love him with all of her heart every day. It’s what she needs. It’s what Zuko needs.

No matter what obstacles they encounter, it is going to be okay. They’ll figure this out.

With that in mind, Kani begins the walk back to the healing hut.

It’s hard to explain to his crew why Iroh is leaving the ship as a Fire Nation royal and general dressed like an Earth Kingdom commoner. Eventually, he settles on telling them that he has an old friend stuck here who he doesn’t want to put in danger and that Iroh is paying his crew to get him here and back safely, not to argue with him.

Usually, he wouldn’t speak to people like that, but he can’t choose his values over his nephew’s safety. Over his life. If Zuko is really alive and living here and even one member of his crew found out, it would all be over.

Ozai would send someone to kill Zuko or to capture him and bring him back to the Fire Nation so he could be imprisoned or executed. Iroh would likely be imprisoned or executed for going to see Zuko and saying nothing. That would leave Azula all alone to fend for herself in an incredibly dangerous situation with her father angrier than ever. With Ozai watching her every move to prevent the last member of his family from turning against him.

Iroh can’t do that to his niece and nephew. They’ve already been through so much. Too much. They can’t handle any more.

As Iroh is walking through the town, he can see people walking around like they likely would normally, but talking in hushed voices and casting nervous glances towards the Fire Nation ship.

This certainly isn’t a town with high priority to be protected by the military. They probably have some kind of law enforcement and basic protection, but nothing to fight off a fleet of soldiers. Their defense is likely just for Fire Nationals who strayed away from their group while traveling through the Earth Kingdom. For stays who are looking for trouble or at least don’t respect the people who they run into.

It isn’t unreasonable for these people to be terrified of what a Fire Navy ship could want. He doubts one ship could level this town, but they could certainly do some damage and take a lot of lives.

After looking around for a while, Iroh walks up to a couple who doesn’t seem particularly busy at the market, giving them a friendly smile hoping it might ease their nerves even for a moment about his ship even if there is no way that they could attribute it to him. Hopefully. He doubts people in a town like this would be able to recognize a firebender on sight when not wearing the distinctive red robes or uniform.

“I’m not from around here, just traveling through, I was wondering if either of you know where the local healer is by any chance?” He asks, looking between the two.

The woman nods, pointing to Iroh’s right. “If you go follow the main street and then take the left fork when you get to a large, old oak tree and then continue that way for a few more minutes you’ll find it. There are signs for it and it is impossible to miss, it's a large, stone building.”

Iroh is about to thank her when the woman points in the other direction. “However, if you need an herbalist, Lo lives up on the top of that far hill.” She explains.

Iroh hadn’t been expecting there to be options, but Zuko did say the healer and not the herbalist. Then again, there are only two options, if he isn’t at the first one Iroh can just go to the second one. It isn’t a big deal. Despite that, he can’t help but feel anxious at the idea of not knowing exactly where Zuko should be. Of having a larger area to cover to find his boy.

“Thank you ma’am, have a good day.” He answers, careful to give them an Earth Kingdom bow with his arms by his sides opposed to the Fire Nation one he is so used to doing. He can’t make himself obvious in the first twenty minutes here. It would force him to return home with no answers and possible suspicion. He would definitely raise suspicion if he were to make the same odd journey again. His brother doesn’t pay much attention to what Iroh does so long as it is away from him, but Ozai isn’t stupid. Ozai doesn’t trust Iroh for shit. The only reason his brother has become more complacent is because he has begun to see Iroh as a sad, lonely old man trying to find company with his neice through a stupid board game.

With that, Iroh walks off in the direction of the healing hut praying that Zuko will be there.

There are only two other healers with Feya now opposed to the usual five. Three have young children at home and Feya had been clear that she would hold no ill will against them if they wanted to return to their families until this passed. Not many people would come seeking medical help unless it was urgent and where she may be tough, Feya isn’t cruel. She doesn’t want their families to be worrying that a soldier may come into the healing hut seeking care and the visit and take a turn for the worse. She doesn’t want her healers worrying that there may be a portion of the crew not caring about safety and looking for trouble and their children, husbands, friends, or parents being the target out of misfortune.

Nothing like that has ever happened with any visit that a Fire Navy ship has made. The worst it ever got was a yelling match between a likely somewhat drunken sailor and a prideful merchant. Thankfully, the situation has been deescalated on both sides, neither wanting a battle. The Fire Navy crew would almost certainly all perish and far too many loved ones in the town would be taken with them.

Despite that, reason can’t get rid of fear. The Fire Nation has done so many unspeakable things in the past that it is hard to disregard the anxiety. Nearly impossible to not think that this is the time where the sailors attack for whatever reason. No one can be sure and no one wants to take any chances.

No one.

It’s still a little too soon for Kani and Zuko to be back, but Feya can’t help but glance out the window every few minutes hoping to see the two coming back up towards the house.

She knows that Kani will not let anyone look at the little firebender let alone touch him. On top of that, any Fire National would need to get a good look at the kid’s face to recognize him as the banished prince. They would need to take a close look at him to even realize that he is a firebender, something they likely wouldn’t do. They aren’t going to go around looking for Fire National children walking willingly along with Earth Kingdom mothers. They certainly aren’t going to assume that some kid is someone who is supposed to be dead without good reason.

She knows that everyone who knows Zuko knows him by the name of Lee and that he has always been dressed like an Earth Kingdom boy. She knows that it won’t be suspicious for a mother to be hurrying her young son back home while there is an enemy ship in the docks. However, she can’t stop herself from imagining the worst case scenario. Can’t help imagining her sweet nephew being snatched and being dragged back to the nation he is so terrified of.

No patients are in the healing hut now. Most injuries that people come in with don’t need immediate attention but need to be tended to within a few days before they get dangerous. Most people who are injured now are likely finding home remedies to hold themselves throughout the day and come tomorrow. She can’t blame them for not wanting to risk coming outside for something that they can survive.

As Feya busies herself with any work that she can find, be it cleaning, sharpening, or preparing bandages, the door opens.

When she sees the man who walks in, she immediately knows that he isn’t from town. Being the town healer, even if she doesn’t know everyone by name, she can recognize everyone in town and attribute a personality type or injury to them. She can’t do that for this man.

He walks up to the closest healer and begins talking to her. They’re too far away for Feya to hear them well. Anyways, from their tones and body language it seems like they are having a pretty standard conversation and so she doesn’t spend much time observing them, going back to her work.

She hadn’t noticed any obvious injury, definitely not something that would be worth coming here with a Fire Navy ship in the harbor, but then again, he is likely a traveler and doesn’t know. Even if he does know, it’s not like hiding outside of the town with no one around would be any safer.

The man is mostly out of her mind when she hears a voice behind her. She turns around facing the newcomer. “How can I help you?” She asks more out of habit than anything before taking a quick, startled step back.

If it hadn’t been for getting used to Zuko, she wouldn’t have even noticed, but it is screamingly obvious to her now. When she meets the man’s eyes, they have the gold glint in them. The distinct eyes of a firebender. She isn’t sure if this man came with the ship or if he is just passing through and it is a coincidence, but he can’t be here. It’s not that she has an opposition to helping him, it’s that he can’t see Zuko. If he gets a good look at the boy, he will immediately know that Zuko is a firebender. He might even know who he is.

Before saying anything, the man pulls out two scrolls with broken seals but tied back up with green ribbon. “I’m looking for my nephew, Lee, he was burned pretty badly over his left eye when I last saw him and it would probably be a pretty large scar by now. He wrote to me and told me that he was staying with the healer in this town and I was just informed that you have a nephew by the same name and description.”

The older man’s voice is too calm. He can’t be here. Even though he isn’t dressed in Fire Nation clothes, someone is bound to recognize the Dragon of the West. Not everyone knows what the man looks like, Feya didn’t until now, but she is sure that those more attuned with military and foreign politics could recognize him on sight.

He isn’t at all like she imagined, not that she spent much time trying to picture General Iroh. She certainly didn’t think he would be only a little taller than Zuko, fat, and have a friendly face. She expected all lean muscle and a glare so intense and permanent that it cut into his skin. She even half expected to see burn scars along his hands and arms from the extended and forceful use of fire. But he really just looks like…some guy.

Pushing the thought from her head, she snatches one of the scrolls out of his hand before he can say or do anything more, needing confirmation. The letter is in Zuko’s handwriting, it is addressed to General Iroh, and signed with the name Lee. This is definitely Zuko’s uncle and definitely someone who can not be here.

Glancing at the other two women in the room, she quickly grabs the man’s arm, silently demanding he follow her. Both by tugging his arm roughly and shooting him a menacing glare. He is surprisingly compliant as she leads him through the door and up the stairs that leads to her apartment.

Despite his appearance and compliance, she has heard the stories. She is sure that he could kill her in a few seconds. The fact that Feya is an earthbender likely wouldn’t make much difference considering she lacks military training. As far as she knows, this man has been trained to be a soldier from the day that he could walk.

“What the *fuck* are you doing here?” She hisses when they reach the top of the stairs and close the door at the top, out of earshot of the other healers.

“I’m here to see my nephew.” Iroh replies as if he isn’t putting that kid in so much danger just by being here.

“Most people here just think that Zuko is some kid my sister took in after being attacked by a firebender. The people who know he’s a firebender think he’s from a fucked up peasant family and is, again, just some kid my sister took in. The world thinks he is dead, that’s why he is as safe as Lee. If the wrong person sees fucking… *you* next to a kid with a palm shaped burn scar on his face, it won’t be hard for them to figure out exactly who he is. Get the fuck out of here right now. By just being here, you are putting him in danger,” Feya spits, keeping herself from punching the man, sure that it would only end badly.

The look that the old general gives her is one of shock. She isn’t sure if it is because Feya knows that Lee is actually the banished Prince Zuko or if he just isn’t used to people talking to him like this. She doesn’t care. The longer he is here, the more likely someone is to find Zuko.

Anyways, it’s not like there is much that the old man can do to her. If he were to attack her, people would know who he is. Also, if he really cares as much about Zuko as much as the kid claims that he does, he wouldn’t endanger the boy like that.

“Why are you looking at me like an idiot? Get the fuck out of here.” She growls, pointing at the door. “Get. Out.” She annunciates her words by punching her finger in the direction of the door with each word.

“Please, ma’am, I need to see him. I need to make sure that he’s alright. That he’s safe. I need to talk to him. Just for a moment.” The man pleads, taking Feya’s outstretched hand.

Feya snatches her hand back, making a fist with her other one. Before she can think through what she is doing she punches the man in the face, glaring at him. Even as the weight of her actions falls on her mind, she holds her ground, unwilling to let the general know she felt even an ounce of fear from her actions.

Iroh clutches his face, she can see blood on the side of his hand. Either his nose is broken or he split a lip. She doubts she is strong enough to have punched his tooth out. His expression is that of shock, clearly not expecting a violent reaction. A lot of people have that misconception.

“What kind of healer *are* you?” The man demands, but not retaliating to her blow, just straightening himself and meeting her eyes.

Feya glares. She doesn’t know what to say to him, but she is willing to stay in a standoff with him. Considering the amount of time the man spent in the Earth Kingdom, she is sure that the man is aware that the Earth Kingdom is known for perseverance and stubbornness. He probably knows that Feya’s legs will give out from exhaustion from standing before she walks away from something she has set her mind to.

Iroh digs around in his pocket, pulling out a cloth and pressing it to his face, likely to staunch blood more than mitigate pain before he takes a deep breath. “I’m not here to fight you or your family, I just want to see my boy. I need to know if he is really being taken care of. I just need to see that he is safe and happy. Then I’ll go. We need to know.”

Feya’s expression hardens at the ‘we’. “Who is ‘we’?” She demands, needing to know who this man wants to drag into this. He might have never cared about Zuko or might not understand how terrified the kid is of the Fire Nation discovering him.

“Nothing to worry about, just his sister. It wasn’t safe for her to come with me, her father might think we were up to something if she enthusiastically came with me. I just want confirmation that Zuko is safe and I don’t need to worry about him anymore. That I can focus all of my energy on Azula. As long as her father is alive, she isn’t safe. I can assure you that the only reason my brother has done nothing to hurt Azula is because she is an asset to him. He does not see her as a daughter just as he did not see Zuko as a son.”

Feya crosses her arms, inhaling, and closes her eyes before she meets Iroh’s golden eyes again, trying to calm herself no matter how much she wants to lash out at the man again. He clearly isn’t going to leave until he sees Zuko and the kid has been worried about his sister. Worried enough to start sobbing.

“Zuko said ginseng is your favorite tea. We got him some because it reminds him of you. Would you like a cup?” She offers, not wanting to glare at the man until Kani and Zuko come home. Just because she can stand her ground for that long doesn’t mean she wants to.

“I would appreciate that.” Iroh replies, a warm look in his eyes.

Feya isn’t sure if she doesn’t trust him just because of his past, because someone shouldn’t continue to be gracious when attacked, or because he simply isn’t trustworthy. She can’t be sure yet, but appearing to have let her guard down might make him genuinely let his guard down, especially when with Zuko. She will have to observe carefully then.

She puts water on to boil before turning to the man. “Did I break your nose?” She asks, unable to see the damage she had caused under the rag. She really does need to stop choosing impulse over logic in the heat of the moment. However, at 46, she doubts that her habits will change.

As he removes the cloth from his face, Feya peers at the damage. Luckily, his nose is only bleeding, not broken. There isn’t any bruising or crookedness that would already be apparent with that kind of bone or even cartilage damage. She likely just ruptured a vessel with the pressure. She isn’t surprised that she split his lip, though.

“I’ll get you something for that. Will help with pain and swelling and lessen the chance of infection.” She explains flatly. “Stay up here. I’m going to go get something from downstairs. Don’t go anywhere, don’t touch anything, just stay exactly like that. I’ll only be a few minutes.” With that, she hurries down the stairs.

It doesn’t take her long to locate the salve that she is looking for and inform the other healers that she has unexpected issues to attend to but that they can continue using the space for as long as they need.

When she gets back upstairs she is annoyed (but isn’t surprised) to find Iroh kneeling by Zuko’s bed by the hearth, looking at the turtle duck that she had made for her nephew.

Grumbling to herself, she takes the boiling water off of the fire, puts ginseng tea in the diffuser, grabs two cups and walks over to the &#93; man, standing over him, placing the tea and cups down and crossing her arms again, resuming glaring at him.

The general must have felt her presence and turns around, looking at her. An easy smile passes over his face as he stands up, holding Zuko’s turtle duck. It’s all Feya can do to keep herself from snatching the toy from his hands. Just because he doesn’t seem violent to her as of now, that doesn’t mean that can’t change if he loses his temper. She also doesn’t need to make a powerful and feared enemy.

“Is this Zuko’s?” He asks, smiling at the stuffed animal.

Feya nods once. “I made it for him, he doesn’t like being alone.” She replies curtly. Just because she isn’t trying to piss the man off and make an enemy doesn’t mean she needs to please him and make a friend.

“Well it would make sense for an artist so beautiful to make her art the same way.”

Feya just scowls at the man, unsure if he is actually trying to flirt with her or just trying to get her to soften up a little. To be honest, she doesn’t care. She isn’t going to let her guard down until she sees how he and Zuko interact with each other. Also, he’s probably about ten years older than herself.

She shoves the jar of salve towards him in response, trying to keep herself from saying anything but fails. “Put this on your lip, drink your damn tea, and shut your fucking mouth. It’s not too late for me to break your nose.” She threatens.

Thankfully the man just nods, taking it from her and sitting by the fire, pretty much ignoring her now. Good.

Iroh can’t help but feel worried. Zuko had claimed to be safe but that might be relative. Just because the healer might not beat and starve him like Ozai would doesn’t mean she is good to him.

Considering she made Zuko a turtle duck, which is in a haphazard but comfortable bed by the fire, it brings him some comfort that she at least genuinely cares about Zuko to a certain extent. It comforts him that it seems more like her problem is with Iroh and not firebenders or even the royal family in general. Zuko isn’t the one who waged war on the capital city for 600 days, taking many lives and ruining far more.

However, no matter what this woman’s opinion on Zuko or himself is, he won’t get anything from her by trying her clearly very short temper. Considering that is a clear part of her personality, he isn’t sure why she decided to become a healer. He is sure that she needs to deal with many trying people every day.

He isn’t sure how long he has been sitting by the fire in silence, occasionally sipping tea as the healer drinks her own on the far side of the room when he can hear the door open.

The woman sets down her cup and walks over to the sound, talking to whoever had just come in. Their voices aren’t hushed but they aren’t talking loudly and from the other side of a wall, he can't make out much of what they are saying.

Soon enough, a second woman walks into view holding something pretty large bundled in cloth, likely to protect it from the cold. She and the healer look very similar and could possibly be related. Iroh knows that the healer’s sister took Zuko in, but he isn’t positive it this is her even if it is likely.

Despite their similarities in features, they both look how Iroh would expect Earth Kingdom women to look and could just know each other.

They both have long, dark brown hair but the new woman has her’s in a loose braid down her back, some of the shorter hair near her face hanging loose where the healer’s is in a tight, neat bun likely held with multiple pins almost certainly for practicality. Loose hair isn’t something good to have as a healer.

There is a possibility that both women are benders. All earthbenders have green eyes but not all people with green eyes are earthbenders. Both women have green eyes, the healer with much darker eyes and the new woman with brighter one. If it wasn’t for the scowl on the healer's face she would be very beautiful.

The new woman appears to be a few years older but seems to be stronger with darker skin but slightly bleached hair at the top of her head like she is in the sun a lot. He can’t tell too much more considering he has only interacted with the healer and she had given him almost nothing personal about herself other than her temper.

The older woman gives him a small, nervous smile that she seems to be trying so hard to make friendly while walking towards the fire. “Excuse me sir, can you move a little, just need to get my son down. He exhausted himself earlier and doesn’t do great in the cold.” She explains.

She kneels next to the fire as Iroh moves, gently laying the bundled child on the bed, coving him with the blankets and placing the turtle duck in his arms. Iroh forces himself not to push the woman away to get a look at her son’s face when she gives him the toy the healer had made for Zuko. He’s waited months to see Zuko again. He can wait five more minutes.

“There you go, sweetheart, you’re home now. You get some rest, alright?” She says softly more to herself than to her son, pressing a kiss to possibly-Zuko's forehead before turning around. She doesn’t stand, still blocking Iroh’s view of her son. He isn’t sure if it is intentional.

“What are you doing here, general?” She asks, not meeting Iroh’s eyes, gaze much softer and less direct than the healer’s. Despite that, it isn’t hard for him to tell that she doesn’t like him. She doesn’t like him one bit.

“I’m just here to see my nephew. I just want to talk to him. Need to see if he’s alright. Once I get to talk to him, I’ll leave. Is he awake? Is he okay?” Iroh asks, trying to look behind the woman to see Zuko with little success.

“He’s asleep. He’s exhausted. Let him rest. Leave him alone.” She meets his eyes for the first time, resting a hand on Zuko’s leg.

“What’s your name?” Iroh finally asks, figuring he isn’t going to get any further with Zuko right now. He is still pretty sure that the two of them are sisters. Zuko had referred to the healer as the farmer’s sister (and the darker skin and bleached hair from sun exposure would match for a farmer) and the healer had referred to Zuko as her nephew, but he can’t be sure. Not yet. Jumping to assumptions when he is moments away from definite answers is never a good idea.

“I’m Feya and this is my sister, Kani.” The healer says coldly from behind him. He has to say that he is surprised that she is the one talking considering how cold she has been during this whole interaction.

Iroh looks between the two briefly, unable to pay much attention to anything except for the fact that his supposedly dead nephew is only a few feet from him and Iroh can’t see him. That he can’t hold Zuko’s hand, see the damage that the boy’s own father did to his face, and just try and bring the boy comfort even if he’s asleep.

“Can I *please* see him? I won’t hurt him or do anything. I just want to see my boy again. As soon as I had any reason to believe that he was alive It’s been impossible for me to not worry about him. Please.” He finally says softly, trying to look at Zuko.

Kani gives him a look that Iroh can’t quite decipher before standing and walking next to her sister.

Iroh almost immediately moves next to Zuko’s head, cupping Zuko’s scarred cheek in his hand. The scar that Ozai had left is horrible. It extends as far as the burn did and is now covered in rubbery, red skin.

He brushes back a bit of Zuko’s hair that has gone from shoulder length, to shaved, and is now just below his ears. The left ear is now slightly misshapen, Iroh wonders if Zuko can hear as well out of that ear or at all. He is almost positive that Zuko is visually impaired in his left eye if not completely blind in it.

After Iroh gets over the shock of the scar taking up a third of his boy’s face, he can’t help but notice that Zuko looks healthier. His cheeks look a little rounder like he had gained a good amount of desperately needed weight.

“He looks healthier.” Iroh comments, fighting the urge to bundle Zuko up in his arms and hold him close. He can only believe that Zuko is exhausted and needs his rest although he isn’t sure from what. Ozai had always pushed Zuko to limits that someone his age, or really anyone at all, should be able to even come near. He knows at this point Zuko can stay up for days with little alteration to his abilities. It’s bad.

Silence follows for a long moment before Kani speaks. “He was severely malnourished when my husband found him. He told us a lot of what the Fire Lord did to him as he got more comfortable around us over time. He’s been eating and sleeping more. He also has been talking more, panics less, and doesn’t think that he is going to receive some unthinkable punishment for making a mistake. He’s doing a lot better all around.” She says softly, a smile forming on her face as she moves closer and looks at Zuko as if forgetting her dislike for Iroh for a moment.

Iroh just nods, looking down sadly at the abused child he couldn’t save. Iroh still isn’t sure if he didn’t step in truly because there were bigger things at play or because he was too weak or too much of a coward. He honestly doesn’t know the answer to it and isn’t sure if he would want to know if it isn’t what he tells himself.

No matter the reasons for not defending his sweet, innocent nephew from a man Iroh still can’t believe made such a child, Iroh can’t stop the guilt from gnawing away at him that this is the price that Zuko had to pay to be loved. That he had to be burned so horribly that the world thought him dead when he became too terrified to think straight. That he had to be thrown from his own country and be a ghost inhabiting a false vessel to even try and find a place to belong.

He should have fought his brother for the throne. He should have searched for an ounce of evidence of foul play in his father’s death. It isn’t just because he would want the throne as a birthright as the eldest or for power but just to stop all of this pain. Even if he couldn’t peacefully end the war for years to come, Zuko wouldn’t have been forced to flee his home in absolute terror.

“Thank you for taking care of him.” Iroh whispers, trying to hide the pain and guilt in his voice as he runs his fingers through Zuko’s thick, growing hair, now a bit thinner where the scar likely travels along the scalp.

“He’s a good kid…he’s talked about you a good amount.” Kani says after a brief silence. “He also said that his mother left him. He’s still really upset about it and hasn’t said much more than what he has repeated a few times, but, do you know what happened to her? That really messed him up I think and maybe if he had confirmation it wasn’t his fault it might help a little.” She adds sadly.

It isn’t news that Ursa’s disappearance had completely shattered Zuko’s heart.

Iroh had come back from war six months after his men, still mourning for the loss of his son looking for anything to numb the pain. He had found some solace as he slowly traveled back to the Fire Nation in ways he could help end the war that had gotten his son killed. That still didn’t bring Lu Ten back.

When Iroh had finally returned, he had found Zuko almost completely numb to the world around him and really only reacting to what he needed to. He would train, study, and eat, but not much more. For the most part he just isolated himself when he wasn’t required to do something.

Zuko had just turned ten at that point and was a poor actor and even a somehow even worse liar than he is now. Even though Zuko tried to hide it, by the way that Zuko talked, interacted with people, treated himself, and by places he would or wouldn’t go in the palace depending on his fluctuating mental state, it wasn’t hard for Iroh to figure out that Zuko had at least seriously considered suicide.

He isn’t sure if Zuko actually made any attempt at taking his own life as the boy would shut Iroh down if he even tried to hint at his concern for Zuko’s mental state. However, Iroh had tried to look for cuts, scars, or bruising that might be tell-tale signs of a failed attempt when he had the opportunity and never found any. Unfortunately, there were plenty of places on his nephew’s tiny body that evidence could be hidden with formal clothes.

As soon as he could, Iroh had clutched the broken child to his chest trying to breathe any amount of life into him. It had taken time, but Zuko had finally started talking past the bare minimum again, doing the few things he was allowed to enjoy, smiling again, and just spending time with Iroh between lessons.

“I’m not completely sure, but I do think there was foul play in my father’s death which led to my brother taking the throne. Zuko had said something about my brother requesting to be heir to the throne after my son died. Zuko stayed to listen to the conversation until his grandfather got angry and that’s when he left. Azula, Zuko’s sister, told him that my father demanded that my brother take Zuko’s life to know the pain of losing a firstborn son or to leave the palace with no inheritance or titles. I asked Azula about that later and she swore she wasn’t trying to mess with Zuko. I wouldn’t put that past my brother or father, but I have no idea what happened after that.” He whispers, looking down at Zuko’s slack, peacefully sleeping expression.

“When my brother married, Ursa, my sister-in-law, lost everything. She wasn’t allowed to see her family or speak of her past life ever again. Zuko was all she had and the only person that she truly loved. I can only assume that she had done something to protect her son, but I’m not sure.” He admits, wishing he had an answer to give his nephew when his mother’s disappearance had shattered him.

Neither of the women say anything to that, they both just look sad. In their defense, there isn’t really anything to say. It’s just horrible. All that can be done now is try and help the kid move forward. Iroh can only hope that they’ve done that for his sweet boy.

Zuko isn’t sure exactly what had happened but he’s pretty sure that he fell asleep and Kani brought him home. He doesn’t feel anywhere near as exhausted as he did when he was trying to keep himself awake while half conscious resting against Kani’s chest mumbling about doing more.

He could still use more rest, but he would like to eat something, spend some time with Kani and Feya and then go back to bed. It’s probably close to dinner time.

He can smell the faint scent of soup coming from the direction of the kitchen. It smells good and now he just needs to bring himself to get up and get some but he’s just so comfortable and tired.

The heat from the fire is perfect as he is snuggled into his blankets and can only assume that he has his arm around his turtle duck. One of the women must have tucked it in with him or maybe Zuko had grabbed it in his sleep. He isn’t sure and doesn’t really care. Either way, he’s happy.

He can feel a gentle hand resting against his cheek. He smiles a little at the casual, gentle affection. It is something that he has gotten used to over the past few months and has come to love.

He used to associate touch with being bad, humiliating, and painful save only a few people. Now he almost always feels himself craving a hand on his shoulder, fingers running through his hair, or a gentle, loving embrace. He has only come to back away from those he doesn’t know or trust. He likes being able to associate most touch with something good, gentle, and affectionate for the first time in…ever.

As he slowly becomes more conscious, he can hear voices around him. He has gotten used to Kani and Feya’s voices and knows they’re both here before he can even hear what they are saying.

However, he hears a third, low voice belonging to a man. It isn’t Chen’s voice but it is familiar. So familiar that he should just know it without even thinking, but it barely even seems plausible.

With that, Zuko begins forcing himself to wake up, whimpering a little as his body wants to stay curled up and half conscious by the fire. Even though he isn’t going anywhere, it is hard to pull himself out of sleep.

When he finally opens his eyes, he blinks a few times, following the source of the voice to a kind, familiar, and comforting face. Zuko can’t help but whimper again as he raises a reluctant arm, clutching onto the unfamiliar green fabric of the man’s clothes.

“Uncle?” He whispers softly, unsure if he is seeing things.

Before he can come to a conclusion, he is gently, but far too suddenly, pulled from his cocoon of warmth and pulled into a familiar embrace that he hadn’t realized he had desperately needed for so long.

Zuko can’t bring himself to say anything. All he can do is cry.
