## Chapter 24

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

I made this chapter a little longer to make up for last week. Midterms are done and I have just started fall break and am home to see my parents and kitties

### Text

Zuko has definitely gotten a lot bigger in the almost five months since Iroh had seen him last. He is still very small for his age, but he seems so much better. His nephew’s ribs don’t push as sharply against Iroh’s arms as he holds Zuko’s trembling body. When Iroh rubs his hand in small circles on Zuko’s back, Zuko’s shoulder blades don’t feel like they’re cutting into his skin and thankfully, he can’t feel Zuko’s spine unless he were to actually press down.

Zuko is still so skinny, but he is so much healthier.

Almost impossibly healthier.

As Zuko cries, for the first time in years, the sound doesn’t break his heart. This one of the few times that his nephew's quiet sobs seem to be that of just being unable to properly express his emotions. Almost sounds like relief. It isn’t the normal cries of pain, grief, terror, and humiliation that Iroh has gotten so used to hearing from the boy over the years.

“I’ve got you nephew, I’m right here, I’ve missed you so much.” He whispers into Zuko’s good ear, trying to comfort him more than console him.

“I’ve been so worried about you. I’m so happy that you’re safe. I’m so grateful that you found good people to take such good care of you.” Even if Iroh has some mixed feelings about Feya, she and her sister have Zuko in a soft, warm bed, wearing warm, clean clothes, with a toy of his favorite animals and probably twenty pounds heavier than before. Iroh isn’t sure if these women have treated Zuko as well as Iroh would have away from Ozai, but they are taking care of his boy.

“I-is she okay?” Zuko whimpers after a few minutes, cries subsiding as he calms down, snuggling up a little closer up to Iroh, looking up at him with wide, far too innocent eyes.

“Is who okay, nephew?” Iroh asks softly, cupping Zuko’s cheek in his hand, still having trouble believing that he is holding his deceased nephew right here in his arms, emotions scattered or not.

“ Azula…has he hurt her yet, too?” Zuko asks nervously, gaze landing on the ground.

Iroh pulls Zuko closer. “No, nephew. He hasn’t hurt her yet. We’ve actually been getting closer since you disappeared. We all thought your father killed you and that he just didn’t care. She started growing wary of him then.” He explains softly, not wanting Zuko to think that Iroh had replaced Zuko the moment he was gone. He needs him to know that Azula had approached Iroh out of fear and Iroh had done what he could to protect her.

Thankfully, Zuko smiles. “I was worried that she’d be alone. That he’s hurt her and she wouldn’t have anyone.”

“We both needed to know if you were okay. You *are* okay, right?” Iroh asks, needing to hear the confirmation, even if he would need to ask again without Feya and Kani here. Zuko might not feel like he could be honest if the answer is no.

Zuko perks up, grinning, wiping away residual moisture from crying earlier. “Kani and Chen have been taking care of me, Feya lets me do cool things, the herbalist, Lo, had a firebender wife and she learned how to heal and I’m learning too, and I have a best friend!” Zuko says excitedly, eyes lighting up as he talks.

Iroh chuckles, ruffling Zuko’s hair. “Who’s Chen, Lo, and your friend?” Iroh asks. He isn’t exactly sure what Zuko means by healing with the herbalist, but he does know that firebenders do make particularly potent and effective salves and medicines because of the consistent and high heat that they can keep their products at. That is likely what Zuko has been doing. Finding ways to help people with an element that has been used only for destruction for so long.

“Fao is my friend, he's our neighbor back home. He’s really nice, I’m teaching him how to use swords. He also knows that I’m a firebender and thinks it’s cool. He also has a younger sister and two moms. I didn’t know someone could do that. But Lo did that too, not that she had two moms, but she had a wife.” He says quickly.

Iroh isn’t sure how to respond to that, but Zuko seems excited about it and doesn’t seem at all upset. That’s all that really matters.

“Chen is…” Zuko trails off, not seeming upset, more like he’s thinking. “He’s my dad.” He finally settles on. “He found me in a storm and I was scared and I attacked him but he still brought me home. He saved me. I pushed him away and just wanted to be around Kani for a while, but he’s been really good to me.”

Iroh really isn’t sure how to feel about any of this. He’s of course happy that Zuko has been taken care of and is safe and happy. He is happy that Zuko seems to have met really good, kind people. However, from what it sounds like, after only a few months, Zuko is already replacing his family.

He had referred to the farming village that he hadn’t named in his letters as ‘home’. It would make sense if there were other people in the room besides those who know exactly who Zuko is, but it’s only himself and the two other women almost out of sight in the kitchen, talking in low voices that Iroh can’t understand.

He is well aware that Zuko had not had a happy childhood in the Fire Nation, but there were things that were very near and dear to Zuko’s heart. He had expressed his love for the beach and the ocean both directly to Iroh when back home and in his letters. He had loved the gardens and the turtle ducks enough to want one here.

On top of that, Feya had referred to Zuko as her nephew and Kani had referred to him as her son to Iroh when alone. He hadn’t thought much of it when the other healer had described Zuko as such, assuming that she wanted to make sure that people didn’t think it weird that members of the family didn’t accept an adopted child as one of their own, during a war no less.

However, when he says it, it sounds like Zuko is very much a part of their family and almost forgetting about his past life. Replacing it with this one.

What had shocked Iroh the most is that Zuko had called Chen his dad. It isn’t that Ozai had been someone who Zuko should look up to and should never be replaced but it is a position that has created a very deep wound. The fact that Zuko feels like he can just push his abuser from his life and replace his position with someone he trusts so suddenly is almost concerning. From the way Zuko described Chen as his dad, Iroh doubts that Zuko has ever referred to the man as such before. It isn’t that Iroh doesn’t want Zuko to have a good, kind, and supportive father figure in his life, it’s that he is worried that Zuko is just shoving down everything he’s gone through the last 13 years of his life and trying to move on from there.

Then again, Zuko is young. The mind of a child is elastic and surprisingly resilient. He is also a child soldier who has gotten used to surviving unimaginable abuse and trauma. He could just be far better at compartmentalizing than Iroh imagined and has just finally gotten a chance to catch his breath and calm down. Finally gotten a chance to heal.

Ozai never once gave the poor kid a break. Maybe that’s all he needed to just learn to have better control over his emotions and feel less scared and trapped.

As he is trying to think this through without letting his nephew know that he is conflicted, Kani, the woman who acts far more like a healer, walks towards them, holding two steaming cups, offering them to both Zuko and Iroh.

“He told me ginseng was your favorite if you would like some, general.” Kani says, not quite looking at Iroh, eyes focusing more on Zuko.

Iroh can’t blame her for not trusting him. He *did* lead an attack on her nation’s capital for nearly two years. He still would like to see a more social and loving side of her that he assumes she has, less for himself and more to see how she interacts with Zuko. How she has been taking care of him.

Zuko takes his cup quickly, clasping it in both hands, sipping it and smiling. “Thank you, mom.” He says quietly, smiling up at Kani.

So it isn’t just Iroh looking too deeply into the few interactions he has had with the people he has no choice but to leave his nephew with. He was hoping that he was just paranoid about the fact that anything he could try and do to help Zuko would almost certainly backfire. It isn’t that Iroh doesn’t want Zuko to have a family, it’s that…well he isn’t sure what it is.

It could be anything. It could be fear that Zuko is just forgetting about his past life and just completely abandoning who he was opposed to just trying to grow and heal with time. It could be something as simple as Iroh is having trouble recognizing his nephew. He has always known Zuko to be timid, quiet, anxious, sad, and scrawny. He is grateful that Zuko is different, so he isn’t sure what is wrong. It could also be something as stupidly selfish as jealousy. Jealousy that Zuko doesn’t need him anymore. That Zuko is happily replacing members of his family this rapidly.

Happily replacing his mother. Replacing Ursa after the grief of her disappearance almost literally killed him. Had almost completely destroyed his ability to love and trust people.

Iroh isn’t sure if Zuko just genuinely feels a very strong connection to Kani as she had loved him the past few months, if he is referring to her as his mother as some form of subconscious revenge on Ursa for abandoning him with Ozai, or a mix of both. Or, possibly, something completely different.

It’s really difficult to unpack all of this, he will have to talk to Azula about everything. She is young but has one of the most perceptive minds of anyone he has ever met. Also, discussion makes things easier to understand.

Iroh takes the cup from the farmer, quietly thanking her as she kneels down, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s cheek as he closes his eyes and giggles at the contact, something Iroh had never seen him do.

“Hey, sweetheart, I don’t know if you're hungry but I want you to eat something. It doesn’t have to be a lot if you can’t take much. You’ve done a lot today. Will you eat some soup and cornbread?” She asks, likely understanding Zuko’s difficulty around food. Even when he wasn’t being denied food, after what Ozai had done to him, Zuko had always been weird around food. Sometimes he would refuse to eat in front of anyone.

Iroh can’t even begin to fathom how much difficulty she has gone through to get Zuko to gain as much weight as he has. He has no idea how much more difficulty she will go through to help him start practicing healthy eating habits.

Surprisingly, Zuko nods with enthusiasm. “I’m actually really hungry. Do you need help?” He asks, beginning to get up. As he does, Iroh notices a brace around his left ankle, wondering what could have happened but doubting it being too severe considering it is mostly well wrapped cloth and what he assumes is metal sewn in for support.

“No, love, you stay here. I know how much you’ve missed your uncle. You just spend time with him while he’s here.” She assures him, affectionately nuzzling him before standing and glancing in Iroh’s direction. “Would you like some as well?” She offers.

Iroh nods, offering her a friendly smile to try and help sooth her nerves. “I would greatly appreciate that, ma’am. Thank you.”

Kani just nods once, walking back towards the kitchen. What Iroh is mostly grateful for is that he got to see Kani offer Zuko affection so casually and almost instinctually. It is the kind of touch that Iroh knew Zuko craved growing up but was terrified to ask for or initiate after so much experience with cruelty.

“What happened to your foot, Prince Zuko?” Iroh asks quietly as Zuko settles back into his arms, snuggling close again.

He is quiet for a moment, making Iroh’s stomach clench, worry returning that these people were only nice by comparison to what Zuko had endured. It isn’t hard to be less cruel than Ozai. Even if these people beat him, it would seem like kindness if they fed him and showed him affection. He is so used to abuse that he has likely come to accept it as his fault.

“I was running in the woods and I fell.” He finally answers, looking down.

Iroh glances at the kitchen, the two women are out of earshot. He pulls Zuko closer and moves his mouth close to Zuko’s ear. “Did someone hurt you? Did someone do that to you? I won’t do or say anything unless you want me to, but I just want to understand your situation.” He whispers, not wanting to make things worse if someone *did* do something.

Zuko moves his head, resting it against Iroh’s chest as he curls up a little. “No, I promise no one did anything. I wanted to tell Fao that I was a firebender and Kani and Chen didn’t. I eventually did anyway even though they didn’t want me to, and I felt like they were ashamed of me as opposed to trying to keep me safe. I was also firebending in the woods and they got upset because it was dangerous. They just told me they were disappointed and that it was dangerous, they didn’t even yell at me. They certainly didn’t hurt me. I just got really upset and ran into the woods while it was dark and tripped. We worked some things out after that to help me feel less separated from the Fire Nation and my element after they found me and put a splint on. Still not the same, but it got better.” He assures Iroh, his voice even, just a little sad.

Iroh has always known that Zuko is a horrible liar and after the manipulation he faced from both Azula and Ozai all of his life, he *hates* lying to people. Never wants to put people through what he faced.

Either Zuko had gotten over that and had gotten much better at lying or he is being honest. He’ll ask Zuko again tomorrow to give him the story of what happened when he isn’t fully alert. If the story changes, he’ll worry. If it doesn’t, he’ll drop it.

“Okay. I’m glad that they found you and helped you again. I’m sorry that you feel isolated…I actually have something for you that might help a little.” He says softly, digging around in his pocket and pulling out the broach, pushing it into Zuko’s palm.

“Make sure to keep it hidden, it is something that clearly belongs to a high ranking Fire National, but I Azula thought you might want it. She’s had it for the past three years, but it was your mother’s. I know it’s not all that personal, it’s probably something she was given after marrying your father, but she wore it pretty regularly when you were younger.” Iroh presses a kiss to the top of Zuko’s head when he finishes talking, feeling like the kid needs all of the affection that he can get.

Iroh had actually never seen Ursa wear this, but then again, he didn’t pay all that much attention to any jewelry that his sister-in-law would wear. It might be good for Zuko to believe that she at least may have once worn it more often when he was younger. Considering he had lied to his nephew about much bigger things throughout the entire time they had been close, the fact that Zuko wouldn’t want to be lied to about anything at all after how maliciously they had been used to manipulate him doesn’t even cross Iroh’s mind.

“Azula is giving it to me?” Zuko asks quietly, turning it over in his hand, smiling a little.

Iroh nods. “She wanted you to have a piece of the person who meant the most to you back home. She also wants you to know that she’s sorry for making your life worse growing up.” He knows that Ursa had meant so much to Zuko and that he was so dependent on her for…everything. With that in mind, it is almost heartbreaking how quickly and easily Zuko had been able to replace her with a new mother.

Zuko snuggles a little closer to Iroh, tucking the pin safely in his robes. “Tell her I forgive her. It was horrible, but I understand that she was trying to protect herself even if she didn’t know it. It’s father’s fault, not her’s. He’s the one who made life unbearable. He’s the one who made it seem pointless.” Zuko says sadly, hiding his face, likely trying to keep himself from crying.

Iroh just pulls his sweet nephew a little closer, rubbing his hand in small circles on Zuko’s back. “Azula will be so grateful to hear that. Thank you, nephew.” He murmurs into Zuko’s hair as Kani walks towards them holding two bowls balanced on plates, setting them down by the fire.

“General Iroh, my sister wants to speak with you in the kitchen for a moment.” She says, coaxing Zuko out of Iroh’s arms and into her’s with a surprising little amount of protest from Zuko as he snuggles up to her.

Even if there are other things he should be thinking about, all he can think of is how Zuko had replaced his entire family so easily with strangers in only a few months.

“He’ll be right back, love.” Kani assures Zuko as Iroh begins to stand and walks towards the kitchen.

Feya is standing over the stove, not cooking anything, but aggressively jabbing a fire poker into the cookstove fire.

“What would you like to talk to me about, ma’am?” Iroh asks, figuring it best to use his manners even if the healer seems like she couldn’t care less. What he is more trying to avoid is pissing her off as opposed to getting on her good side. He doesn’t know if she has one.

She pulls the red hot poker out of the embers, turning to Iroh, holding it in a far to causal manner. Especially for someone who isn’t a firebender. “Exactly how long were you planning on staying?” She asks him, suddenly making fierce eye contact, causing Iroh to take a step back in surprise.

“Uhh, a few days? I won’t be here long. I *need* to make sure he’s okay. He’s my boy and…and I’m not going to see him again for years.” He explains, hoping that the stoic healer could have some compassion towards that. He isn’t sure if she is a mother. She appears to be mid to late forties. If she had a child around the time that she was twenty they could have already moved out and living their own life now. He silently prays that that is the case. She might be more likely to allow Iroh to stay a little longer if she understands what it feels like to be separated from her child.

The healer looks at him with a silent expression on the sour side of unreadable, before speaking again. “You have three nights at maximum here. Tonight counting as one. I will make it clear that the only reason you can is because of how much Zuko has talked about you. How much he’s missed you.” She says flatly.

Iroh can’t help but to smile at the fact that Zuko hadn’t replaced him. He isn’t happy that Zuko was unhappy with separation, but Zuko is still his sweet boy. He is about to thank Feya when she moves the poker towards his chest, jabbing at him with it only about six inches from him. Considering her mannerisms and the fact she would know how to not make an injury severe but painful, he wouldn’t put it past her to burn him.

“I am going to lay down a few ground rules for you. You break a single one of them, you will need to leave. If you don’t, Kani will return home with Zuko because I don’t trust you to not put him in danger, even if unintentionally.”

Iroh is about to argue with her that he isn’t going to put Zuko in danger when she starts talking again.

“You are not allowed to leave the upstairs of this building. I don’t care if you want to go somewhere or if Zuko wants to show you something, if I so much as catch you peeking around the door at the base of the stairs: out. You are not allowed to firebend. If any fires need to be started, Zuko can do that. I trust him to be careful and not draw attention to himself. You also have to be quiet, no yelling or anything like that. You draw attention to yourself: out.” She growls, jabbing the poker a little closer to him both times that she says “out”.

He doesn’t let himself step back or even flinch from the poker, but it doesn’t mean it isn’t particularly intimidating. Any retaliation he could make may genuinely injure the healer. He is well aware that Zuko would never forgive him for that.

“Look, I get that you don’t like me and I am not going to expect you to, but Zuko won’t want to be up here all day. I’m not going to bring attention to myself going out with my nephew. I–”

Feya cuts him off by moving the poker a little closer but towards Iroh’s face. This is when he takes a step back, wondering why such a violent and angry person wanted to be a healer.

“What time of day did you get off of your ship?” Feya demands, narrowing her eyes.

Iroh cocks his head, confused. “Ma’am, I don’t see how this pertains to–”

“What. Time. Did. You. Get. Off. Your. Ship?” She growls through gritted teeth, shaking her poker with each word, the orange glow dying but still certainly hot.

“Uh…noonish?” Iroh says more as a question, still unsure what her point is.

“So, you aren’t the most distinct looking person in the world, but if someone were to see someone in Earth Kingdom attire leave a Fire Navy ship, they would pay attention to what you look like. I can assure you, a short, elderly, fat man is not a description for many people in this pretty small town. You may not be noticeable at a glance but you will be the second someone hears that description.” She explains flatly, glare returning, some of what she is saying making sense.

“You left your ship in broad fucking daylight during a time when many people are out by the docks and are definitely close enough to see someone dressed in green leave an enemy ship and maybe even see his face. On top of that, there are people who may recognize you on sight. The only reason I knew you were a Fire National is because I have gotten used to what firebender eyes look like from Zuko. However, there are enough people here who have served in the military or are more involved in politics who would know who the Dragon of the West is by looks alone.”

“Many men in this area who were already in the military were called to Ba Sing Se during your attack. Many more enlisted when the attack on our capital began as they couldn’t be on the sidelines any longer with that injustice. Some returned either injured and no longer able to serve or couldn’t bring themselves to be on the frontlines anymore. *All* of them would recognize you. They know who caused many of their comrades to fall, my husband likely among them. No one saw him after.”

Well that would definitely explain the healer's dislike of him. The fact that she hadn’t gouged his eyes out on sight is impressive. Where she still definitely has a temper and isn’t what one would expect from a healer, Iroh has to respect her self control. Her calm, even if venomous, clarity.

Sighing, Iroh nods once. “I promise, I’ll do what you say.” He concedes, not going to start arguing with a woman who he had widowed.

“Good.” She replies sharply, mercifully putting her poker back in the fire.

Iroh thinks for a moment before speaking. “I wanted to apologize for that. I know it doesn’t change anything. But I can safely say that not only was Ba Sing Se my greatest military disgrace but also my biggest personal mistake. My son, Lu Ten, followed my footsteps and lost his life on the six hundredth day. The day I ended it.” He explains, unsure if she already knew that Lu Ten’s death had been what forced Iroh to reevaluate his choices and end that bloody conquest.

Feya stops for a moment and Iroh can’t help but hope that maybe for a moment, the two would be able to see eye to eye. Maybe even form some kind of relationship, even if rickety.

Instead, Feya slowly turns, meeting Iroh’s eyes and speaking words that almost stop his heart: “And who’s fault is that, Dragon?” She says in the calmest, most venomous voice Iroh has ever heard in his life, and he had spoken to his brother.

Feya had managed to convince Kani to allow Zuko to go see the play showing soon. *The Secrets of* *the Oasis* . Zuko can barely contain his excitement as Kani shows Zuko beautifully painted pictures in a book containing scenes and storylines from many different plays as they wait for Iroh to come back.

He can’t keep the grin off of his face as she tells him about it.

Kani had seen the play with her father while growing up and had enjoyed it but has mostly read about theatrical productions after his death. Her father enjoyed theater far more than she did and she mostly enjoyed accompanying him.

Zuko can’t help but feel like he is going to be seeing a bit of his mother even if she wouldn’t be here. Like for a moment, it would feel like she has her arm wrapped around his shoulder, holding him close, whispering lies about always being there to protect him.

This time, he’ll have Kani holding him close, running her fingers through his hair and pressing affectionate kisses to his head. He can be reminded of the good parts of his old home while knowing that the only people that matter back in the Fire Nation know that Zuko is safe, happy, and loved. Know that they don’t need to worry about him.

When Iroh walks back into the room, Zuko’s smile fades a little, looking at his uncle with some concern. He looks upset. Not blatantly, but something happened. “Uncle, are you alright?” Zuko asks, still snuggling up next to Kani but raising his head some.

Iroh gives him a sad smile, nodding and sitting close to Zuko and Kani. “I’m alright, nephew.” Iroh says softly, eyes moving away from Zuko’s for a moment.

Zuko can feel his heart sink at that. With how supportive and kind Iroh had been to Zuko all of his life, it had been easy to forget and overlook when Iroh lied to him. He wouldn’t do it for manipulation or out of malice like father and Azula would, but it still didn’t feel good. However, it had been easy for Zuko to overlook it when back in the Fire Nation.

Now, Zuko has lived with people who have been completely transparent with him for the past several months. He knows how much better it feels to have people be completely honest with him. How much easier it is to trust, to feel safe, and to just generally recover from everything that had been done to him in the past. It makes it so he isn’t waiting for the other shoe to drop when things start getting better.

The very few times that Kani, Chen, or Feya had lied to or withheld information from him, they would come clean before Zuko had to press for answers and explain why they hadn’t told him immediately. They would apologize and make sure that Zuko felt safe and loved and that they did what they thought was best for him in the moment and let him know that they didn’t mean to break his trust.

“Oh…okay.” Zuko says softly, resting his head against Kani again as Iroh begins eating his soup. He can’t unpack this right now. This will be the last time he sees his uncle in years. Maybe ever if things go wrong.

Kani lays the book down, holding him close, possibly understanding what had upset him as he can feel tears burning in his eyes that he can’t allow to fall.

“I don’t want you lying to my son, general.” Kani says after a few minutes, surprising Zuko. “If you’re going to bring back old traumas to him, especially as someone who he will let his guard down for, while he is just starting to really recover, I am going to need you to go.” Kani says flatly with far more confrontation than Zuko has ever heard from her.

Zuko is about to try and protest, wanting to explain that he doesn’t want Iroh to go even if he does some upsetting things. He needs his uncle here for a little longer. Luckily, before he can get almost certainly incohesive words out, Kani continues, meeting Iroh’s surprised and defensive gaze.

“Just be honest with him. You’re upsetting him even if he loves you and wants you here. Be honest with everything. If you don’t want to talk about it, just say so.” She says softly.

“You’re not his mother.” Iroh snaps, glaring at Kani.

“Stop. Please…stop. Please don’t do this. Please stop.” Zuko whimpers, covering his ears, feeling a fight beginning. Can hear the voices rising, can feel the tension on Kani’s body and sees it in uncle’s. Even though he knows he would be protected by these people, that they have issues with each other and not Zuko, he can’t help but prepare himself for the anger to be directed at him for just being here.

“I’m sorry, sweetheart.” Kani says after a brief moment, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s forehead.

“Zuko, I’m worried about you. You’re acting…weird. Are you alright? Did something happen?” Iroh asks, abandoning his soup and moving closer to Zuko.

“I finally have people who are honest with me. I don’t like lying.” He mumbles, wondering if Iroh had changed or he himself had to make it so they weren’t getting along so easily. It could also be the sudden wave of emotions they’re both probably feeling or something else.

It’s hard to think about it properly with Iroh’s comment about Kani not being his mother still in his head.

Sighing, Iroh offers Zuko his hand. “I’m sorry for hurting you, nephew. Is it because of your father?”

Zuko just nods, still resting against Kani, unable to gauge Iroh’s sincerity. He isn’t sure if Iroh is apologizing because he understands that Zuko wants to move away from being lied to and manipulated and Iroh just brought some of that back even with something he didn’t think was a big deal or that he knows that he is expected to say it.

“Mom, can I just go to bed? Been a long day.” Zuko mumbles, snuggling a little closer to Kani. He genuinely is tired and will probably fall asleep soon. He also just wants to be alone with Iroh for a little. Everything said seems to turn into a fight between Iroh and Zuko’s new family. Granted, they’re only doing what they think is in Zuko’s best interest, but he doesn’t like the fighting.

“Of course, my love.” Kani responds, smiling and pressing another affectionate kiss to his temple.

“Can my uncle stay with me tonight? I missed him a lot. Not gonna see him again for a while.” That is also true. He wants to be able to remember what Iroh’s embrace feels like, what his voice and breath sounds like. If something were to happen to Iroh before Zuko could see him again, he knows that it would break his heart to start forgetting the details of his uncle. He had cried for hours when he realized he was forgetting the details of his mothers face less than two years after she disappeared.

Maybe if she had told him that when she came into his room that night it was goodbye, it would be easier. He would get a chance to remember her with intention one more time. He would get to say goodbye. He could ask why she was leaving. He wouldn’t be stuck searching for any trace months after her disappearance, unable to believe that she had truly left him as he sank into deeper and deeper depression. The only reason he could think that she wouldn’t tell him that she was leaving was because Zuko wasn’t good enough to make her want to stay.

“Okay, just call me if you need anything. I would rather have a bad night’s sleep and for you to be okay than to wake up well rested and something be wrong, okay?” Kani glances at Iroh, likely not trusting him but trusting Zuko enough to know that it’s what he needs.

Zuko nods, offering her a small smile. “I promise, mom.” He whispers, wrapping his arms around Kani’s neck before crawling next to the fire and clutching his turtle duck in his arms.

Kani disappears into the kitchen, walking towards the bedroom with Feya a few minutes later, talking in quiet voices.

Zuko feels Iroh’s hand rest on his arms as he moves a little closer to him. “Zuko, I’m sorry if I upset you. Do you promise you’re alright here? There isn’t much that I can do to help you, but I do have friends in the Earth Kingdom that could come and help you get somewhere safe.” Iroh says softly.

Zuko shakes his head, swallowing, feeling like Iroh just doesn’t get it. Doesn’t want to understand that Iroh had hurt Zuko all these years.

“Uncle? Can you just hold me? I really missed you.” Zuko whispers sadly, moving a little closer to Iroh as the old man pulls Zuko into a gentle embrace, both laying down near the fire.

“I was so, so worried about you, nephew. I mourned you when I heard about the storm. I assumed you had stayed on your ship and…well, I assumed the worst. I’m so glad that you’re alive.” Zuko can hear the tears in his uncle’s voice as he is pulled closer, the desire to talk right now draining.

He can talk to Iroh in the morning. Kani and Feya will likely be downstairs most of the day. Zuko can stay up here and talk to Iroh without fights starting. He will have plenty of time to explain everything to Kani and Feya after Iroh leaves. He’ll be lucky to have more than one full day with his uncle. His new family can wait.

“She *is* my mother.” Zuko whispers unintentionally as Iroh rubs Zuko’s arm absentmindedly. He can’t stop thinking about how Iroh has said that Kani wasn’t his mom.

“The farmer?” Iroh asks after a moment even though he knows the answer to that. “But what about your real mother? I know how much you loved her and how close you were. What happened?”

Zuko can feel the pressure building up in his chest and throat and making a futile attempt to stop the pressure being released with tears pricking in his eyes. “She left me. She came to see me right before she was about to go and didn’t tell me. She left me with *him* because I wasn’t worth staying for. She *left* me.” He half sobs, quietly crying as the pain of abandonment all comes back up.

Iroh doesn’t say anything in response to that, likely not sure what he could say. Instead, he just pulls Zuko a little closer, pressing a kiss to his forehead, offering Zuko physical comfort opposed to words he couldn’t find.

Sniffing, Zuko snuggles up as close to Iroh as he comfortably can, needing his uncle’s comfort more than he is upset with how Iroh has been interacting with Feya and Kani. He is sure that it is just a lot to take in, but it doesn’t mean Zuko is happy about it.

Either way, what matters now is that Iroh is here. Zuko needs to enjoy his presence while he can. “I love you, uncle. Thank you for finding me.” He whimpers, not looking up.

“I love you so much, Prince Zuko. After this is all over, I’ll come find you again and you can come home. You can be safe anywhere in the world. I promise I’ll do whatever I can to make that happen.” Iroh replies softly.

Zuko just nods once, unsure how the idea of that could even be a possibility. However, the empty promise still sounds nice to desperate, tired ears.

Feya hates to admit to herself that Zuko looks so sweet and happy snuggled up in his uncle’s arms the next morning. She doesn’t like the man, but at least this may settle some of Zuko’s residual fears about his sister being hurt as well and his uncle still mourning him when he is alive and well.

Part of her regrets saying what she did about the general’s son. Just because she was right doesn’t mean it wasn’t a horrible thing to say. It had hurt Feya enough to lose her husband. She can’t imagine the pain of losing a child. Someone who you should never have to bury. Someone who is supposed to outlive you.

Despite that, she isn’t going to apologize for it. She simply won’t say it again. Anyways, the man knew the possibilities when he allowed his son to follow him to war. There are far too many people on both sides who don’t come back or at least leave a part of themselves on the battlefield.

All that matters now is that Zuko is okay. That he’s safe and happy.

With that in mind, she makes her way down the stairs to the healing hut to set up for the day.

She works in silence for about half an hour when she hears footsteps coming down the stairs. If it is General Iroh she will break his nose for real. She had made it very clear he wasn’t allowed out of the apartment.

Thankfully, Kani walks into the room, gaze distant and almost sad. When Feya had heard Iroh say that Kani wasn’t Zuko’s mother even from in the kitchen, she had been ready to fight the man. The only reason she didn’t was because she could hear how upset Zuko was getting over the fighting. She wasn’t about to stress her nephew out further. His two worlds colliding definitely have not been going smoothly.

“Do you think it’s safe to leave Zuko alone with that man?” Kani asks, glancing back at the door.

Truthfully, Feya doubts it, but then again, she is the one with a negative image of him. Zuko’s uncle is sometimes all the little firebender could talk about. She doesn’t trust him one bit, but she can believe that he only wants what is best for Zuko. Trust that he knows that there are not many places much safer to put him than a remote town where no one of importance would ever come. Well, except for two Fire Princes.

“I don’t think that he will do anything to hurt or endanger Zuko intentionally nor take him anywhere against his will.” Feya finally answers. “Anyways, General Iroh knows that he isn’t allowed to leave the apartment for Zuko’s safety. I spoke to him last night.”

“By speaking do you mean threaten?” Kani asks, crossing her arms and raising an eyebrow.

“Threaten, of course, who do you think I am?” Feya half jokes, smiling at her sister.

Kani just shakes her head. “You do know his is a household name for a reason. I understand you want to command respect from most, but please don’t mess with him. You *know* how dangerous he is. He could severely hurt or even kill you with little effort.” Kani warns her.

“I’m well aware of that, but he also wouldn’t do anything to hurt me. One, it would give him and Zuko away pretty quickly, and two, he cares about how Zuko feels and knows the boy would never forgive him. I’m not worried about him. Also, when am I going to have a second chance at having the upper hand on a notorious Fire Nation General?” She chuckles.

Kani sighs, rolling her eyes. “I think the fact that he might like you could be playing a role in this. Maybe he has a thing for dominate women. You do realize that, right?”

Feya flips her sister off while continuing to prep the work space. “He wasn’t subtle. Although I think he was trying to use flattery so I wouldn’t throw him out more than genuine flirting.”

Kani just shrugs before joining her.

Iroh still is very unsure about all of this. He doesn’t like how much Zuko trusts these women and how quickly he replaced people from his old life. It isn’t that he doesn’t want Zuko to be able to trust people, it’s that he isn’t sure that Zuko *should* trust them as blindly as he does.

Iroh hasn’t seen Zuko trust someone like he trusts Kani and Feya since Ursa. Iroh had assumed that Zuko would never trust anyone like that ever again after her disappearance.

He knows that Ursa hated her life as a part of the royal family but that she genuinely did love Zuko. She would never tell Zuko so, but he had become her reason for living with everything else taken from her. He has no idea what happened, but he can’t believe that Ursa just left her children behind, especially Zuko, with her abuser without a good reason.

What really surprises him is that Zuko refuses to think that there was anything else besides Ozai had killed her, Azulon had killed her, or she had left because Zuko wasn’t worth staying for.

From what it sounds like, Zuko had given her the benefit of the doubt for a while. He had assumed that she had a good reason for leaving and that it wasn’t out of being selfish. However, he must have begun to lose that hope as his will to move forward slipped away day after day that Ozai destroyed him with nothing to hang onto.

“Nephew?” Iroh says softly, resting a hand on Zuko’s shoulder.

He used to wish that Zuko would sleep more. However, seeing the boy up with the sun, meditating by the fire with the turtle duck in his lap helps him believe that Zuko hadn't changed too much. That he is still the sweet child who was forced to flee in pain and terror months ago from the only home that he has ever known.

Zuko turns away from the fire, smiling at Iroh, moving closer to him. “Thank you for coming.” He whispers, taking Iroh’s large hand in both of his tiny ones.

“I’m sorry for fighting with Kani last night and I’m sorry for saying that she isn’t your mother. I don’t know when I’ll see you next. I promise I won’t mar this meeting with fighting. I’ll do my best to just make good memories.” He promises, cupping Zuko’s face with his free hand.

Just because he won’t say that Kani isn’t Zuko’s mother again doesn’t mean that he doesn’t think it still. Zuko has known her for less than five months and is already making her one of the most important people in his life. Making her the person who he drew so much safety from. Someone who’s absence completely destroyed his world and sense of self.

“Thank you, uncle.” Zuko mumbles, resting his head on Iroh’s shoulder.

“Just let me know at any point if you don’t feel like you're safe here. I won’t do anything unless you ask me to, but I really can ask some friends to come find you and move you somewhere else. They’ll protect you and keep you hidden, safe, and happy in the Earth Kingdom. Just remember that, alright?” Iroh whispers, hoping that Zuko will understand that he has a reasonable out if things start going badly or if he starts to realize things are only good here by comparison.

Zuko nods once. “I won’t need it. I’m happy here. I want to stay. Anyways, I promised Fao that I would be back to teach him sword fighting in his fort.”

Iroh chuckles softly. Even though he won’t get a chance to meet Zuko’s friend, he is so happy that his nephew has found another boy his age to play with. He was never able to have friends growing up and it is definitely something that took a toll on his mental health. He needs another little boy to play dumb games with and just have fun.

“I’m so happy that you’re doing better, nephew. Do you know where Kani and Feya are?” He asks, less because he wants to see them and more because he just doesn’t like the idea of them leaving Zuko alone if this is something they do regularly.

Zuko nods. “They’re just downstairs in the healing hut. Kani said that Feya doesn’t want you to leave the apartment. I wanted to show you the beach, introduce you to Lo, and maybe see if a nice merchant I met is still here. But I’m glad you’re here.”

That is certainly reliving that the women just work downstairs. That if Zuko weren’t feeling well it wouldn’t be hard for one of them to come up every so often to make sure he was still okay and that if something suddenly happened they would be able to hear him. Also, he assumes that Zuko is much happier learning about healing than he was about fighting back home.

“Are you hungry? I’ve learned how to make a few things while here. I’m not nearly as good at cooking as Kani, Chen, or Feya, but some of it is good.” He says with an excited look in his eyes, finally finding something that he was good at and could receive praise for as opposed to constant degradation.

Iroh nods once, more wanting to make sure that Zuko would eat something than for himself. Even if he has gained a lot of weight, his nephew is still far too thin. He has years of malnutrition to make up for. Even if he is still far too scrawny, he looks better.

Zuko jumps up to his feet hurrying over to the kitchen as Iroh quickly follows him.

Iroh has had jook before when he was fighting in the Earth Kingdom but never thought too much about it. It wasn’t bad by any means. It was easy, variable, and filling. However, just the joy in Zuko’s eyes as he mixes the ingredients together and serves a bowl to Iroh makes it impossible not to completely enjoy.

It somehow gets even better when he is able to watch Zuko eat his entire bowl without needing prompting or seeming like he is forcing himself. He just eats it a bit slower than most people would. Iroh has never enjoyed a meal so much in his life.

After they finish eating and cleaning the dishes, something he never thought he and his nephew would be doing together, Zuko snuggles back up to him again. “Uncle, Feya has Pai Sho and cards here. Wanna make some tea, play some games, and we can just talk?” He suggests.

Iroh smiles warmly, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s head. “I would love that, nephew.”

The day moves surprisingly smoothly. A few patients come into the healing hut, spirits higher than they were yesterday.

People are still worried about the Fire Nation ship, but considering no soldiers had made any move to attack or even come into the town, people began to calm down. On top of that, apparently a brave soul snuck a peak at the happenings on the ship and informed the townsfolk that the crew was mostly just drinking, talking, and playing games.

Kani isn’t sure if someone actually did see anything happening, if someone started the rumor to calm peoples’ nerves, or possibly if Feya had even started those rumors now knowing that the crew has no interest in the town and would lose a large amount of pay if they step off of the ship.

When Kani had confronted her sister about it, Feya had denied it. However, she does have access to a large amount of people, doesn’t like chaos, and is really only completely honest with Zuko. It isn’t out of favoritism, it is because Zuko won’t judge her, won’t tell anyone, and lying or withholding information is severely detrimental to his mental health. For most other people, her lies are simply annoying at worst.

Every so often, Kani or Feya will go upstairs to check on the boys. Every time, nothing has been wrong. Zuko has been telling his uncle about the people he’s met, the two have been playing board games, Iroh has been telling Zuko about what is happening in the Fire Nation, or they have just been sitting quietly together drinking tea, eating, or just looking at the fire.

Despite her dislike for General Iroh, she has to say that she is grateful that he has kept his word at doing nothing to hurt Zuko and not even trying to leave the apartment. Zuko seems to be happy just to see someone he has missed so terribly for so long and to rekindle that connection that has left him feeling stranded and isolated from his culture for so long.

Kani had insisted on cooking lunch for them knowing that Feya would work through noon without eating if someone didn’t bring her food and the fact that Zuko only knows how to make a few dishes. Considering General Iroh was also born into royalty, she can only assume that the only thing he knows how to make is tea due to his odd passion for the whole process and that Zuko is the better cook of the pair. She would never say it to his face, but Zuko’s cooking is decent at best, so that is leaving both lacking in skill

She wants to make sure her baby boy eats properly. He hasn’t for so long and deserves to have that now. It will still never not break her heart that she, a peasant woman, can provide so much more to Zuko than the Fire Lord himself. He had been denied so much for so long because of pure cruelty and contempt.

It isn’t hard to tell that General Iroh doesn’t like her very much. Luckily, the feeling is mutual. Despite that, he is respectful and doesn’t say anything like he did the night before.

She isn’t sure if he doesn’t like her because he doesn’t trust her, he is jealous, or perhaps he was close with Zuko’s birth mother. Maybe he feels like Kani is replacing her. No matter what the reason is, Kani isn’t going to leave Zuko alone, especially with someone who would hurt him without her life being taken from her.

Whatever had happened with his birth mother, she left her small, scared, defenseless child with a man she *knew* would hurt him. It would be so much different if Kani were to leave Zuko with Chen. Sure, Zuko would be devastated and miss her, but he would have a man who is gentle, loving, and supportive to raise him. Not someone callous and cruel.

Whatever happened, Kani can only feel like she *should* be replaced by someone who would actually be there for her son and not leave him at the first convenience.

She mostly assumes that General Iroh doesn’t like how close she is with Zuko when she can see the look she is giving her out of the corner of her eye as she holds Zuko in her arms, giving him several kisses goodbye before going back downstairs to work.

The man should just be happy that Zuko has a good, safe home where he is loved, supported, and taken care of. She is well aware that it isn’t a perfect situation with how much Zuko needs to hide. However, with the Fire Nation thinking Zuko is dead, he probably can’t go to the colonies without being recognized. With the war going on, most Earth Kingdom families would never take in a firebender child and love him as their own. Until the world changes, this is really one of the best situations that Zuko is going to find. He is safe, happy, fed, and can be himself behind closed doors with those closest to him.

General Iroh almost seems grateful to see her put Zuko down and leave the room. She knows that Zuko has missed his uncle terribly and he has needed this so badly for so long, but she is glad that he will be leaving soon. Zuko has gotten the relief and connection that he needed even after his uncle leaves and Kani won’t have to deal with the old general anymore.

After that, the day continues going by in a pretty normal and uneventful fashion.

About two hours before sunset, the door opens and Kani can’t help but grin as Chen walks into the room. With everything going on, she had almost forgotten that Po and Lee are staying at their house so that Chen could come and they could figure out this mess together. Unfortunately, it is even more messy now. She isn’t sure if it is better or worse that Chen is here when General Iroh is.

Kani rushes forward, wrapping her arms around her husband as he rests his forehead against her shoulder. “You must have left early to get here this soon.” She says quietly. Chen just nods.

They pull away from the embrace and share a quick, but affectionate, kiss before just holding hands and meeting eyes.

Kani feels like she should inform Chen of what is going on now as opposed to waiting until later. Better to understand now and accept it (or at least be able to keep his dislike of these developments hidden from Zuko) *before* he sees the little firebender.

Sighing, Kani looks at the ground quickly before meeting Chen’s eyes again. “We need to talk.” She says quietly.

Instead of the worried expression that she expected to come across her husband’s face, he just grimaces and nods. “Yes. We do.” Is all he says in response.

## Chapter 25
