### Text

Chen has to say that he is relieved that Kani already knows exactly who Zuko really is. That wasn’t something he had wanted to reveal to his wife. He would have needed to speak to Zuko first of course, let him know that this isn’t the kind of thing that he could keep from Kani in good conscience.

Unfortunately, that wouldn’t have been the most difficult conversation he would have to have with the boy. The more difficult conversation still remains a necessity especially with how perceptive Zuko is with other’s emotions, especially Chen’s. He will still need to look at his boy and make sure that the little firebender knows that where Chen isn’t thrilled, he still loves the kid and wants him to stay.

It is a conversation that he had dreaded as soon as he realized that his dislike for Zuko’s identity wasn’t just shock but more genuine.

He really doesn’t want to admit to Zuko that he isn’t happy about something the boy couldn’t control. Something he likely wishes wasn’t true either considering how much fear Zuko carries for his father even after all of these months.

However, Zuko has made it abundantly clear that he would rather have his feelings hurt than feel like he is being manipulated and exploited through more lies.

There is a lot that Chen could do to ease the pain of damaged emotions. He could spend time with Zuko and make sure that the kid fully understands that he is still loved and has a home even if Chen needs a moment to accept his heritage. It would take time, but with consistency of showing his boy that he’s still safe and loved would likely repair any hurt feelings with time.

Unfortunately, he is sure that if he were to ever break the kid’s trust, there wouldn’t be any coming back from that. Even if they could repair their relationship, Chen is sure that Zuko would always be hesitant to trust him. At best, the damage of concealing how Chen feels about a very important part of the kid’s life would take years to repair.

Where he doubts that hiding the fact that Chen doesn’t like that Zuko is directly related to the Fire Lord would cause the kid to mistrust him, he doesn’t want to risk it. It could make the kid feel like Chen is trying to manipulate Zuko’s feelings around him. What Chen is most worried about is that if Zuko were to discover that Chen was hiding his feelings about Zuko’s heritage, something he has clearly wanted to talk about but been terrified to even mention, he would want to know what else is being kept from him.

At least he doesn’t need to dread having this conversation with Kani. Doesn’t also need to worry Zuko about his mother, the person Zuko has gotten so close to and put so much trust in the past few months, might have altered feelings towards him after this information being shared.

As Kani explains the situation with Zuko to him, Chen listens, but mostly thinks about what he is going to say to the kid. He doesn’t want to come off as calloused or indifferent. Chen needs the boy to understand that this is not something meant to hurt him but to fulfill the promise of transparency.

His attention is pulled back into real time when Kani begins talking about Zuko’s uncle.

Despite having days to think about this without Zuko’s presence affecting his thought process, Chen hadn’t even *considered* who Zuko’s uncle is. The man he had talked about so fondly despite the fact that the kind old man who took care of Zuko growing up stands knee deep in Earth Kingdom blood.

Chen is fairly certain that Fire Lord Azulon only had two children. Two sons. Both with reputations that struck fear into anyone’s heart and names written in blood.

He vaguely hopes that the previous Fire Lord had a third son or a daughter whose husband had grown close to Zuko. Chen doubts that. There is only one person who Zuko’s uncle could be and Chen doesn’t like that one bit. Not in the slightest.

He honestly possibly even hates the fact that Zuko is related to the Dragon of the West. Especially that the man who the kid had talked about making tea, playing board games with, and just keeping the kid somewhat sane is the same man who tried to destroy Ba Sing Se. Tried to bring Chen’s nation to its knees and took so many lives in his attempt.

Despite his dislike for these developments, he manages to stay completely calm. Well, up until Kani reveals that Zuko’s uncle is *here* . The Dragon of the West is upstairs with his kid right *now* .

As soon as he learns that aspect of what is going on, he rushes up the stairs, completely ignoring both Kani and Feya telling him to come back. He isn’t sure if they want to talk to him a little longer or if they don’t want him going up yet or at all.

He doesn’t care. Whatever his feelings about Zuko are right now, he needs to see his kid. Needs to make sure that he’s okay.

He knows that Zuko has had a good history with his uncle, but that is also in comparison to a mother who abandoned him with his abuser, his father who completely destroyed the kid over and over again, and a sister who would get him into trouble and make his already unbearable life worse. Zuko’s comparison for someone kind and supportive in his life is very skewed.

Chen has no way of telling if Zuko’s uncle was genuinely kind or just not abusive. Unfortunately, it could easily be either. Poor kid thought that Chen was the kindest, most gracious person in the world for not leaving a half dead kid outside while injured in a storm, firebender or not, and then not sending him out to die the next day.

Zuko’s judgment of what constitutes a good person can’t really be trusted, especially if it were someone hw met when he was desperate for any kind of help and connection.

“Lee?” Chen calls as soon as he gets to the top of the stairs leading into the kitchen. “Son, are you up here?”

Footsteps hurry in his direction and Chen can’t help but smile as the tiny firebender comes hurrying towards him with a grin on his face. His footsteps are a little uneven with the brace on his left foot, but it’s good to see him walking without crutches again. Chen is sure the kid is even happier about that.

“Chen!” He calls excitedly, wrapping his arms around Chen's waist and resting his face against Chen’s chest. “I missed you.” Zuko mumbles.

“Missed you too, kid.” He replies, lifting Zuko up into his arms, holding him close as Zuko wraps his arms around Chen’s shoulders. He definitely has gotten heavier but is still very easy to hold.

“Chen, my uncle came to see me. Make sure I’m alright. Wanna meet him?” Zuko asks, excited. So excited. It’s impossible to not feel warm at the light in the kid’s eyes.

“Son, is there anyone else up here besides you and him? I would like to meet him but I want to talk to you about something first. I know you don’t like people keeping things from you.” He says softly, feeling a tug at his heart at saying this with so much light shining in the little boy’s eyes.

When Zuko shakes his head, Chen rests Zuko down on the floor and kneels in front of the little firebender, resting his hands on the kid’s shoulders and meeting his eyes. “I want to let you know that I know why you are. I figured it out a few days ago. Some friends were talking about what happened to the Fire Prince and gave me his name. I remember that you shared your real name with me a few months ago when you started to trust that I wouldn't hurt you.”

Zuko’s eyes trail to the ground, staying silent, waiting tensely for what Chen has to say. He can almost feel that Zuko is terrified that he is going to be disowned all over again. That a second father figure is going to toss him away like he isn’t a child who needs and deserves to be cared for no matter what.

“Son, it’s alright, it’s not your fault. Most importantly, I want you to know that I love you and want you to continue living with us. I still wanna teach you some foraging and farming skills. Maybe I could teach you some blacksmithing. I only learned from a family friend when I was younger, far from a master at it, but can do some useful things with it. Most importantly, I want you to know that you will always have a home with us.” He begins, needing to make his love for the kid clear. He can’t have Zuko shutting down because he thinks this is the end. That he’s losing a second home for just…existing.

“If you think that I’m acting odd or different around you, I just need a moment to come to terms with all of this. You can talk to me about how any of this is making you feel, I won’t be upset or offended. I love you, son, okay? It’s on me that I need a moment to think about all of this. Please don’t even think for a moment that you did something wrong. None of this is your fault.” He says softly, raising one hand and cupping Zuko’s cheek affectionately, smiling at him.

“Thank you for telling me.” Zuko whispers after a brief silence, wrapping his arms around Chen again.

Chen can hear the slight quiver in the boy’s voice, sure that the truth had hurt his feelings. A small part of him wonders if he should have kept that part from Zuko, but he is sure it would have been far worse if the kid had discovered the truth later. He would be hurt by the fact that Chen had trouble accepting his heritage and still seeing Zuko as the same regardless of his family and betrayed.

“I love you so much, son.” Chen whispers, resting a hand on the back of Zuko’s head, pulling him a little closer. “You’ll always have a home with us. We’ll always be your family. I just didn’t want to keep anything from you. Didn’t want to hurt you. I’m sorry if I did.”

Zuko nods, but holds him a little closer. Chen hopes it is a sign of understanding and forgiveness. “Wanna meet my uncle?” Zuko finally whispers, turning his head up to look at Chen, the small, innocent smile returning to Zuko’s face.

“Sure. I would love to meet the man who took care of you.” Chen says. He *does* want to meet the man who took care of Zuko when he needed it most. The man who didn’t allow his own loss to harden him to the world, but instead found a child who desperately needed to be cared for and loved. However, he certainly does *not* want to meet General Iroh. The man who had terrorized Chen’s nation and been responsible for the deaths of several people that Chen knew.

Unfortunately, they are the same person.

Slowly standing, Chen allows Zuko to take his hand, leading him to the other side of the fireplace where an old man is standing by the fire, holding a cup of tea in both hands.

When they first round the corner, Chen can see a hard, disapproving expression directed at himself from the old general. When Zuko looks at his uncle, that expression softens, eyes moving from Chen to Zuko.

Where this is how Chen would have expected Zuko’s kindhearted uncle to look, it isn’t at all how he had expected the Dragon of the West to look. He had always pictured someone who’s appearance would strike fear into anyone’s heart, with eyes of fire and a heart of ice. Not a friendly, approachable looking older man.

Chen continues holding Zuko’s hand as he raises his free hand in greeting to the old general, not wanting Zuko to get closer to him despite knowing that Iroh had a plethora of chances to hurt Zuko if that is what he ever wanted to do. In his mind, the man still just isn’t safe, no matter Zuko’s history with him. His intentions and motivations could change at any moment.

“Chen, this is my uncle Iroh. He got my letters and came to see if it was really me and to make sure that I’m okay. He took care of me after my mom left.” The kid explains quietly, leaning against Chen as he talks.

Removing his hand from Zuko’s, Chen rests his hand on the little firebender’s opposite shoulder, pulling him a little closer. Thankfully, Zuko seems to enjoy the contact as he snuggles closer.

“Uncle, this is Chen he’s…he’s my dad. He’s the one who found me and took me in.” Zuko continues, wrapping his arms around Chen’s waist, not looking up.

Chen can’t help but to smile at Zuko’s phrasing. He is well aware that the boy has developed a lot of trauma around his father and can only hope that it is growth that Zuko is willing to replace that man with Chen who would never dream of hurting the fragile little boy. Either way, it seems to mean that Zuko really considers himself a part of the family, something he had been so hesitant to do for a long time no matter how hard Kani and Chen tried to make him feel safe and at home.

By the way that General Iroh is looking at him when Zuko is distracted, Chen can only assume that the man doesn’t fully trust Chen to be around Zuko. It’s in his eyes, how he is scanning Chen’s posture and especially where he makes contact with the little boy clutching him tight.

He isn’t sure if it is because Zuko has had such bad experiences with grown men as people the kid looked up to, Chen’s stature and the fact that neither man knows the other well, or it could be about how the general is used to being to main, if not only, supportive role model in the kid’s life.

Instead of saying anything to the general, Chen just kneels in front of Zuko, embracing him again. “You doing alright, son?” He asks quietly, needing the confirmation, needing to see how the kid reacts to questions around the old man and how Iroh looks at Zuko when he answers it. It is all in the subtleties of emotions. He needs his boy to be alright.

Zuko nods, grinning. “Wanna sit down? Want you to meet each other.”

Zuko’s enthusiasm is too much. It’s impossible to deny him something like this even if Chen wants nothing to do with the man before him and he is sure that the feeling is mutual. Unfortunately, the light in Zuko’s eyes and the fact that the kid has been separated from his family for so long and likely will be for even longer once Iroh leaves.

Sighing, but not allowing his nerves show, Iroh sits by the fire not long after Iroh does.

As soon as they’re on the ground, Zuko runs over to his uncle, snuggling up against the man. If this man had been just about anyone else in the world, Chen would have been thrilled for his boy. Unfortunately, this man is a tyrant.

“Uncle, Chen taught me some about animals and farming. He also helped me feel safe around fire again. He’s a blacksmith. Kinda like a nonbending firebender.” Zuko says excitedly, grinning.

The look at that description of blacksmithing on Iroh’s face matches how Chen feels. He had never heard it described like that before, but Zuko seems overly excited about the description, so neither man questions it.

At least not verbally. They just share a silent look, the first moment of bridging their differences even if just for a split second.

“Interesting way to put it, but I’m happy that I was able to help you.” Chen finally settles on saying, smiling at Zuko but almost pointedly not looking at Iroh.

Iroh nods once, a slight smile appearing but not saying anything.

Zuko starts going on a rambling, seemingly pointless story about Chen, Cabbage, and Fao. Even if it doesn’t have much to it, Zuko still seems happy. Maybe that is the point. Proof to his uncle that Zuko has been happy the past several months. That he has had good people surrounding him.

Luckily, the story does seem to accomplish that as Iroh begins to relax a little, smiling at his nephew while holding him close.

Chen isn’t sure how much time passes when Feya comes into the room, an unreadable expression on her face. “Hey, Lee, can you come down for a minute, we need to talk to you. It’s nothing bad.” She says quickly, turning to Chen before the boy can respond. “Can you stay up here with him?” She nods towards Iroh.

“Uh, yeah, is something wrong?” Chen asks, confused.

“I need to talk to Lee and someone else for a moment, then I’ll let you know. I don’t think that there is anything to worry about though.” She reassures him, beckoning for Zuko to come with her.

Zuko looks a little sad, but he wraps his arms around iroh, saying something to the old man before standing and following Feya back down the stairs.

Chen knows that there is some important information that he has missed in the past few days. He is sure that he will be caught up on everything in due time, but he still would like to know. This is something that likely Kani, Feya, and Zuko are in on. Something Chen had missed out on when he was at home.

“It’s Chen, right?” Iroh asks, breaking the silence after a few minutes.

Chen turns his head, looking at the old general, nodding once. “Do you need something?” He asks, kind of wanting an excuse to leave without offending the man. It isn’t because Chen wants to be respectful to a tyrant but because he is worried about what may happen if he is angered.

Chen can’t put his family in danger of this man for something as stupid and petty as pride. He has no idea how short the man’s temper is and knows General Iroh’s reputation far too well. Every Earth Kingdom citizen does. Even those who don’t keep up to date with the comings and goings of the war due to location, status, or trade.

“I want to talk to you.” Iroh continues, a hard look appearing in his gold eyes.

Chen used to not be able to distinguish firebender eyes without them wearing the Fire Nation uniform, but has gotten used to the refraction of light from Zuko’s eyes when he walks around and smiles.

He had come to think of Zuko’s eyes as the color of honey opposed to anything else. He is beginning to remember why firebender eyes are commonly referred to as ashen flame. Despite Zuko and Iroh having the same colored and shaped eyes, the way that they look at their surroundings is vastly different.

Usually, Chen can see the bright, hopeful look in Zuko’s eyes as he looks around at his new life in wonder. As he looks at what freedoms he now has that he isn’t constrained by his identity and family history. His anger has always been a cover for fear and despair. It has always been sad to see the terror hiding in the depths of the little boys eyes, always so scared at what someone might do to him after so much bad experience with so many people.

Iroh’s expression is much harder. Even when he was smiling, it didn’t seem the same. The fact that he can commit horrible, violent atrocities and walk away from them like he hadn’t destroyed lives shows through in his expression. Chen has the feeling that if Zuko weren’t so attached to the people here, they would not be safe from the dragon’s wrath.

That if attacking wouldn’t permanently destroy the old man’s relationship with Zuko, he would do so in a heartbeat.

“Why would you say that to him? What the fuck is wrong with you?” Iroh eventually snaps, his expression souring further, the calm posture that iroh had been using tensing as the man stands. Thankfully, his full height isn’t that much, he is barely an inch taller than Zuko. Despite that, the man is still terrifying and Chen is sure that he knows that.

“Say want?” Chen asks, confused, standing as well, not wanting to be looking at one of the most feared men in the world. Even if he would certainly lose any fight that could break out, he doesn’t want to feel disadvantaged even if it is true.

“Tell him that you weren’t alright with who Zuko is. I don’t care if you have trouble accepting it, just don’t say that to him. I’m sure you know how much trouble he has accepting himself.” Sparks appear on the general’s lips as he speaks, face darkening, more of who Chen had pictured coming into view.

“He’s very perceptive towards others' emotions, especially mine. He would pick my unease up immediately and feel worse if I had kept it from him.” Chen responds defensively but somehow keeps his voice level.

He is well aware that Zuko had trouble getting close to Chen for a while due to his experiences with his own father and other men in positions of authority over him, no matter how small.

Due to that, the kid had gotten much better at analyzing the minute changes in Chen’s facial expressions and inflections in his voice. Had gotten exceedingly good at reading his body language. It is likely something he had to pick up on a long time ago out of survival. Learning when he should disappear into the woodwork and keep silent as if he didn’t exist until the wave of anger plaguing the very air he breathed passed over.

“I’m sure you are aware that he’s been manipulated most of his life. I don’t know if you are aware how much he was manipulated most of his life and if you were aware that you contributed to that. I’m sure that you were doing everything that you possibly could to help him, but it doesn’t change how he felt.” Chen says, almost immediately regretting it, unsure how the man’s temper is, especially with Zuko gone from the room. Luckily, there is only so much that he can do without permanently destroying his relationship with his nephew.

Iroh takes a step forward, his short stature the only thing that keeps Chen from taking a step back from the man. He had certainly not imagined the great General Iroh to be less than an inch taller than a starving thirteen year old boy. Despite that, he knows the stories about this man. His height hasn’t stopped him from ending and ruining countless lives.

“You have no idea what it is like back in the capital. I’ve done what I can to protect him. I don’t know if I made all the right choices, I’ve tried a different approach with his sister, but she isn’t barely hanging on like he was. I was just doing what I thought was right to keep him as safe as I possibly could in the circumstances we were in. I’d like to see you try and do better.” Iroh spits, smoke coming from his nostrils.

That is when Chen takes one step back, unsure if he should have held his ground. “I never said whatever situation you were in wasn’t hard or that you weren’t trying. He’s living a different life now. It isn’t as complicated. All he has to do is keep his identity hidden and he can live a relatively normal life of a nonbender Earth Kingdom boy. He has some restrictions, but he’s safer here. With that comes more opportunity for personal choice in his life. He has made it abundantly clear that he wants honesty over comfort.” Chen calmly explains, not allowing himself to become emotional. He is sure that that would end horribly.

The general just stares at him silently for a moment, making unbreaking eye contact until footsteps come up the stairs. Both men turn their heads in the direction of the door leading up to the top floor of the apartment.

Feya appears not too much longer after they hear the door leading into the kitchen open. When she walks into the room, she shoots a glare colder than the general’s at the two men, crossing her arms, likely having heard a lot of their conversation. It is always easy to forget that Feya has impeccable hearing. He really is supposed that she decided to continue on and remain a healer considering her personality and gifts.

However, she has helped a lot of people in her current line of work. Chen has never worked up the courage to ask her. Feya isn’t the kind of person to question without good reason.

“You two, put it back in your pants, no one needs a measuring contest here. You’re both adults. Chen, come downstairs, there’s some stuff we need to fill you in on. General, I think it’s time that you left. Get back to your niece. Staying here much longer will only put Zuko in danger.” She says curtly, digging around in Zuko’s belongings before pulling out the Blue Spirit mask that Chen had gotten for the little firebender.

For the life of him, Chen can’t think of a single reason *why* Zuko would have brought the mask with him to town. Then again, it isn’t the weirdest thing that he’s done in his time here. He is an odd child.

“Ma’am, I know you have issues with me, but if you think that I’m leaving my nephew so soon just because you want me to, then you have no id-”

“I didn’t want to let you stay at all. By you just being here, people could discover Zuko. I don’t want him to get hurt, and I’m sure you don’t either. Don’t be selfish or short sighted. You’ll see him again and he’ll be taken care of until that point. You have my word.” Feya explains with little emotion.

Iroh walks towards her, looking like he is about to try and size her up when he remembers that he comes up to the healer’s chest.

He backs down for a moment before talking. “Ma’am, please, I need a reason. Please just tell me and I’ll go.” He sounds genuine. Chen isn’t sure if he really wants an explanation or if he is just trying to make Feya feel guilty about making him leave his nephew.

Faye's expression remains steady and hard for several minutes before she begins to speak, expression softening only the tiniest bit. “There are Fire Nation soldiers at the edge of town, General. They’re seeking medical assistance from the herbalist . I genuinely don’t think that they want trouble but they *will* recognize you. Being dressed as an Earth Kingdom peasant will be suspicious. If you are attributed to me, you will be attributed to Zuko. Where a few people know that Zuko is a firebender and don’t care, they think he’s from some insignificant family. His world will change if more people know who he is and it may get him killed. Get your shit, say goodbye to Zuko, go back to your ship, and go home. Got it?” She growls, looking down at Iroh, expression twisting from that of mild sympathy to anger again as she presses a finger to the old man’s chest.

Chen has to say, watching his sister-in-law stand up to one of the most feared men in the world and not even faltering is probably one of the most terrifying things that he has seen in his life. Then again, Feya has always been fierce and stubborn. When it comes to a stereotypical Earth Kingdom woman, if she were just a little friendlier, he would think of Feya. Hardheaded and fiercely loyal to those she has chosen to protect.

Somehow, it is eerie to see the man just look at Feya silently. Not attacking her verbally or physically for talking down to him.

“You need to go. Now. Come downstairs. Say goodbye and go. I know that you don’t see eye to eye with us. The feeling is mutual. Just know that we only want what is best for Zuko. We’ll do everything we can to keep him safe, fed, warm, and happy. As long as people think that he is just some kid that we took in, we can protect him. If people realize that he has *any* connection to you, the safest thing for him to do will be to run. I don’t know how safe he’ll be on his own when the Earth Kingdom knows he is hiding in their county and the Fire Nation knows that he is alive.” Feya explains carefully with no trace of threat in her voice.

Surprisingly, Iroh steps down, lowering her eyes. “I’ll go say goodbye to my nephew. Please be good to him. He’s had so little kindness in his life and is in desperate need of it. Don’t let anything happen to him. He has put his trust in you. Don’t break that.”

“We’ve all grown fond of the boy. We wouldn’t dream of allowing something bad to happen to him. I promise we’ll keep him safe and happy for as long as we can.”

Iroh doesn’t thank her, he just walks past both Feya and Chen, a dark, almost tangible aura surrounding him as he walks towards the stairs. Chen has to say he is glad he won’t be spending much time with the man. As much as he knows that Zuko loves him, Chen is so grateful to see the man go.

Thankfully, it doesn’t take long for Iroh to depart from the healing hut. He didn’t really bring any bags with him. All he had come to do was see his nephew and that is the only person he felt the need to say goodbye to.

Luckily, Lo doesn’t pay much attention to the general. She knows that there are parts of Zuko’s life that he is intentionally keeping secret for his own protection and she hasn’t pushed those. She has been respectful of Zuko’s space and privacy, something the kid was in desperate need of.

Feya can’t help but feel a little sad as Zuko clutches his uncle tight, crying softly into the old man’s shoulder, quietly begging him not to leave even though they all know that he has to.

Zuko had known from the very beginning that his uncle wouldn’t be here for long. However, Feya is still sure that it hurts to have him leave. Someone Zuko had missed so horribly and then only got to see for a day before he had to leave again.

Feya walks over to her nephew, allowing for Kani and Chen to talk a little bit, only assuming that her sister is giving Chen the basics of what has been going on the past few weeks.

“Lee, it’s alright. You’ll see him again.” She reassures the boy, resting a hand on his shoulder, ignoring the look that Iroh shoots at her, him clearly wanting her away from him when he departs.

She doesn’t care. What matters is Zuko’s happiness, not Iroh’s.

“When this is all over, your uncle can come back and he can bring your sister. You can introduce her to Fao and cabbage and show here where you have been living. I promise that you’ll see your family again.” She promises.

Even if she doesn’t really want the Dragon of the West around anymore, she does want Zuko to be happy. On top of that, she would like to meet Zuko’s sister, Azula. She knows that the young girl has faced just as many horrors as her brother and has never been given the kind of family that Zuko has now.

Even if they don’t get along perfectly, maybe they can at least show Azula what a loving family is supposed to look like. That they are supposed to scold their children using words and give them undesirable chores when they cause trouble opposed to resorting to violence. Spending time with them, learning about their interests, and getting closer, making their way through difficult times opposed to constantly bringing the worst out in each other. That parents are supposed to be there for their children. Help them rise up in the world opposed to beating them down at any given chance.

“I-I think that she would like Cabbage.” Zuko finally says pulling away from his uncle a little, wiping his tears away. “I think you would like her, too.” He continues.

Feya smiles. “I’m sure that I will. What matters now is that we keep you safe. It’s going to be okay. You’ll see your family again. You’ll be safe and loved here no matter what. It’s going to be hard, but it’s going to be okay. I promise that it will eventually be okay.” She assures the boy.

She is sure that it will be okay at some point, but isn’t sure how or when. There are a lot of things that could happen and a lot of time for them to take place. All that matters is that Zuko can keep his head up during it. That he can feel happy and loved even if things get hard.

Feya will do anything and everything that she can to make that happen.

Zuko eventually fully embraces his uncle one more time before stepping away, taking Feya’s hand. “I love you, uncle. Please be safe. Please make sure Azula is safe. Make sure she knows that I miss her and want to get to know her better when we finally see each other again.” He whimpers.

Iroh nods. Stepping forward and pressing a kiss to Zuko’s forehead. “I will, nephew, and I’m sure that she will be very appreciative of that. I hope that we can see each other soon. I love you so much.” The old man says sadly.

Zuko nods jerkily, clutching Iroh’s hand, needing Feya to coax him to let go.

It isn’t until Iroh leaves that Zuko begins to cry again.
