The more I write this, the more I wish I could draw (I am literally on the same level as Sokka) because I want to see smol little bean snuggling with his new family or his turtle duck or Cabbage just because he is the softest little thing to ever walk the face of the planet. It's a vibe.

### Text

Zuko can’t stop tears from falling as he watches his uncle leave. He understands that just by being here, Iroh is putting himself, Zuko, Azula, and Zuko’s new family in danger. That doesn’t mean that it doesn’t hurt to watch his uncle disappear.

He had been longing for his uncle for so long. For the man to hold him, comfort him, and remind him that he is still remembered and loved. Zuko has finally gotten that from this visit, but it feels like he’s losing Iroh all over again.

He can’t stop the fear that this would be the last time he would ever see Iroh from welling in his chest, nearly suffocating him. He needs to be able to see his uncle and sister after all of this is over. Even if they don’t live under the same roof, he needs to be able to see them, talk to them openly, and know that they’re okay.

He knows that it will put Iroh and Azula’s minds at rest to know that Zuko is alright, allowing for Iroh to focus more attention on Azula. He knows that Azula needs Iroh far more than Zuko does, but it still hurts.

Right now, he needs to try and focus on the fact that he got to connect with Iroh again, one of the most important people in Zuko’s life. He has a gift from Azula of something that had belonged to his mother. Even if he has to keep it hidden, he has something tangible that he can hold onto in times of pain.

He needs to focus on the fact that Iroh can go home, hold Azula close and tell her that Zuko is alright. Maybe that even if they are able to flee the country, Azula could have a safe place to stay when Ozai realizes that she is missing.

No one would search for the missing princess in a remote Earth Kingdom village surrounded by peasants. It’s a farming village that is barely on the map and not a destination for anyone. Not many pass through, and not many spread the comings and goings of their neighbors outside of its borders.

He needs to make himself focus on the positives. He can’t let himself fall back into despair.

“It’s alright, son, it’s alright. He’s going to get home safely and take care of your sister. In a few years, if this war ends, we can invite them over. You can introduce your sister to Fao and Cabbage and show her how to make some things you’ve learned.” Chen reassures him quietly, rubbing Zuko’s back gently.

Zuko just nods, wiping at his eyes. “I-I know she needs him and that I have you. That my life is better than it ever could have been back in the Fire Nation, just…I dunno.” he whispers.

“You don’t have to know. He’s someone very important to you and you’re far from home. You can be upset even if you’re happy here and don’t fully understand why. Emotions are complicated.” Chen whispers, still holding Zuko close.

Zuko is pretty sure that Chen isn’t just trying to comfort Zuko but distract him. He doubts that Chen understands why, but Feya and Kani had wanted to talk to Lo alone.

He knows that Lo wants to give Zuko an opportunity to heal someone and teach the skill to other firebenders. She is probably sure that Zuko is already on board with this, but it is Kani and Feya who she needs to convince.

Chen hasn’t seen what Zuko can do yet and has been elected to keep Zuko company while the women are deciding what will be done. They rightly figured that Zuko wouldn’t want to be alone with his uncle leaving. Even if he knew that Iroh had to leave at some point, it doesn’t make it too much easier. He wants Iroh to come back so badly already.

“Fao misses you. He comes over to ask if you’re back yet pretty much every day.” Chen says, distracting Zuko from his grief at the separation from Iroh all over again. From his rising anxieties of being recognized by one of the soldiers as the loss of Iroh lessons.

He knows that it is unlikely for him to be recognized, especially if he will be wearing his mask and bundled up clothing to protect him from the cold. Anyways, there are plenty of children in this town who would steer away from Fire Nation soldiers if they saw them approaching, not just those who didn’t want to be recognized when not wearing a disguise.

It wouldn’t be suspicious for a mother to hurry her child back into the safety of home with even a whisper of the presence of the Fire Nation. He logically knows that they won’t recognize him on any other occasion. It’s just that also with seeing Iroh, he is reminded of how much control his father holds over the world all over again.

“Cabbage misses you, too. Sometimes she’ll squawk at me because she wants to be picked up or to come in and sleep with me. You’ve spoiled that ridiculous little creature.” The man chuckles, gently brushing a tear from Zuko’s cheek. “You’ll see your uncle again, son. It might be awhile, but you’ll see him again. Maybe your mother and I can have a more productive conversation with him after the war.”

Zuko nods numbly, barely registering that Chen had referred to Kani as Zuko’s mother for the first time opposed to just her name like usual. “I’m sorry you didn’t like him. I should have known you wouldn’t get along with him. I know what he did to your country. I just know that he’s changed and has a different view on the world. I’ve seen it. Shouldn't expect you to just forget. I don’t understand how it felt.” He mumbles, doubting he could ever cross his two lives over properly even if this war ends peacefully in Kani, Chen, Feya, and Iroh’s lifetimes. Maybe even in Zuko’s. Many people have lived their whole lives during this age of war. No one knows how much longer it will drag on.

“Zuko, son, you don’t need to apologize. This is something you needed. He’s an important part of your life whether we like him or not. When the time comes, we’ll figure out our differences. At the very least, we’ll figure out how to functionally both be a part of your life. That will be our problem to worry about. All you worry about is taking care of yourself, alright?” Chen says softly, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s forehead.

Despite Chen’s difficulty with Zuko’s heritage, he is keeping true to his promise about loving Zuko just as much as before he knew. Even if it hurt to hear, he’s grateful to know that the man is truly willing to be transparent with him. It eases his nerves as to what Chen has said to him in the past, his promise about continuing to love him, and what Chen will say to him in the future. It’s nice to have proof of Chen’s honesty with him. Something he isn’t familiar with.

“I love you.” Zuko whispers in response as Chen just holds him closer, rubbing his back.

As Chen holds Zuko closer, Kani, Feya and Lo walk in, Kani and Feya looking…odd, but Lo is smiling warmly, never having seemed happier.

Chen puts Zuko back down on his feet and takes his hand as they walk towards the trio, curiosity forming in Zuko’s mind, the grief of Iroh fading a little.

“Lee, I have a favor to ask you. You don’t have to do so, but I think it could be a good opportunity for you.” Lo begins, smiling at him, even though Zuko is already fully aware of what she wants. He figures that she just wants to get him excited in front of Kani and Feya, show them that he is genuinely enthusiastic about this of his own free will.

“She wants you to go firebend in front of some random Fire Nation soldiers who she knows nothing about.” Feya corrects curtly, arms crossed, clearly not liking whatever Lo had told her one bit. The convincing must not have gone too well. Then again, Feya is stubborn and there are a lot of things that Feya doesn’t like. It’s much easier to name the things that she does.

“I want you to heal one of them. I was able to help the other two who were injured with flesh wounds, but there is one who is very ill. He’s wound got infected and he isn’t doing well even after treating the wound as best I could. It would give you an opportunity to teach others what you have learned. Your mother has told me you’ve already started an alias of the healer when you helped the new mother and her son.”

Zuko can’t stop from perking up at that, the slight depression of Iroh’s disappearance evaporating in that moment.

“See, I told you that he would be too excited to put himself in danger again.” Kani huffs, putting her hands on her hips and looking at her sister. That interaction confuses Zuko a little considering he had thought that Feya wasn’t too keen on him doing it either. Then again, he hadn’t heard the whole discussion and Feya usually appears irritated.

“I wanna help people. Maybe this can be a way to change things. If firebenders start to move away from using their bending for power and destruction and move towards warmth and healing, It could start to change the way the world is right now.” Zuko says softly, still holding onto Chen’s hand and looking up at Kani and Feya.

“Wait, wait, hold on a minute, can Lee *really* heal people with his bending? Like actually? I thought that, like, he was good at making a particular treatment because he would keep a constant temperature or cauterize a wound while keeping it sanitary.” Chen says, looking very lost in the whole conversation. Zuko had forgotten how much he had missed out on just being separated for a little less than two weeks.

“I can strengthen their chi with my bending…that is what heals them, I’m just kinda a catalyst. I’m not exactly sure why it works, but Lo told me about it and I tried it.” He explains, holding tight onto Chen’s hand and leaning back on his heels, using Chen’s weight to support him and grinning up at the man.

“More specifically, he learned about some obscure form of subelement of firebending and from Lo who was close with the person who discovered it and then tried it at the first opportunity.” Kani corrects, frowning at Zuko.

“Song and I were together for fifty years and I watched her practice for nearly thirty, I also didn’t think he’d do anything immediately.” Lo chuckles, smiling at Zuko.

“Wait, who’s Song? Was she a firebender?” Chen asks, still behind on…everything and likely still not over the fact that Iroh was just here even if he’s gone now.

“She was my wife. She was a firebender from the colonies who I met when we were young. She was one of the most skilled healers I’ve ever met.” The old woman says fondly.

Chen doesn’t ask anymore questions but still seems deeply confused.

“Wanna do it. Wanna try.” He says softly, standing more upright but still holding Chen’s hand with both of his.

“Wait, wait, so he wants to firebend in front of some unknown soldiers? They might know who he is.” Chen argues, resting his free hand protectively on Zuko’s shoulder.

“I’ll wear the mask you gave me. Already told the other people I healed that’s what they should say if anyone were to ask. Keep anonymity but also build a reputation. I can really help people.” He explains, looking back up at Chen.

“Should we go with you, son? What do you need?” Chen asks reluctantly.

“You guys shouldn’t come with him. I'll take him there and he can stay the night so he can get home safely.” Lo says calmly.q

“If you think I’m letting my son go unaccompanied with no protection to go reveal himself to a group of soldiers, you have really lost your mind. H-”

“If they can attribute the Blue Spirit to us, they can attribute Lee to us and then Lee to the Blue Spirit. She’s right, Kani.” Feya interjects, giving Zuko a look that he can’t quite decipher.

“Please let me go. I promise I’ll be careful. I know the risks of them discovering who I am. I know that better than anyone here. The Fire Nation only has a few more cities to conquer before it claims victory in this war. That’s probably only a handful of years away. That’s the only way I can see this war ending any time soon, as opposed to it just dragging on.”

“If the military can’t take down my…the Father Lord,” Zuko stumbles over the words, forgetting Lo doesn’t know who he is. At least he is pretty sure she doesn’t. “I think the best way to change the direction of this is to influence Fire National’s relationship with their element and how they have been interacting with the rest of the world in a contradictory way to how they were meant to. Please let me do this.” Zuko practically begs, looking up at Feya, sure that she could convince Kani and Chen to allow him to go.

“Chen, you aren’t seen around town much and you really do look like a lot of Earth Kingdom men from a distance. Also, if they don’t see your eyes, they might mistake you for an earthbender.” Feya suggests, folding her arms.

Zuko cocks his head, still agreeing with Lo that it might be the safest in the long run to go alone. “Don’t you think that I-”

“She’s right. Either Chen is going with you aren’t going at all, Lee.” Kani affirms sternly, moving closer to him with that fiercely protective look in her eyes.

Zuko looks up at Chen, unsure. He knows that Kani means it about not wanting him to go alone, but when Feya puts her foot down, there is nothing short of a miracle that will change her mind. Zuko is still wondering how Iroh got her to agree to let him stay. He had arrived while Zuko was unconscious. He could have come and gone and Zuko would have never known.

“Please. Please come with me. I need to do this. Please.” Zuko whispers, looking up at Chen again.

Sighing, the man rests his free hand on Zuko’s head. “Fine, kid. I’m interested to see what kind of healing can be done with firebending. Wanna get to know the most authentic version of you that I can.” Chen finely sighs, offering Zuko a small, but genuine, smile.

“Thank you. Come on. Come on, come on, come on. I wanna show you and, shit, I need my mask.” Zuko says quickly, unable to keep a grin off his face despite being ready to throw himself into danger again and being separated from Iroh all over again. He isn’t sure why *this* is what is making him so happy.

“Lee, what have I told you about that kind of language?” Kani scolds as if that is the worst thing that Zuko has ever done and what has destroyed most of his childhood.

Feya chuckles quietly and hands Zuko his mask, making it so he doesn’t need to answer Kani at all. He gives her a small, thankful smile and she winks at him.

“Come on, before they think that I’ve gone to get soldiers.” Lo urges, waving the two forward.

“Lee, sweetheart, be safe. Prioritize your safety above all else, okay love?” Kani urges, kneeling down and pressing a kiss to Zuko’s forehead.

“I promise, mom. I love you.” Zuko mumbles, grinning.

“Chen, love, take care of him.” Kani continues, turning to her husband, kissing him quickly.

“I won’t let anything happen to him.” Chen promises, squeezing Zuko’s hand a little harder in affirmation.

“You better keep your word.” Kani finishes, stepping away to let the two walk out the door.

As they make their way through the town, Zuko isn’t sure if he is more filled with excitement or fear. Anything could happen, for better or for worse. Anything.

When they leave the town and begin to make their way up the hill, Chen hands Zuko his mask and he pulls it on so that the people in town don’t see Zuko walking around with Chen and Lo with it on, but the Fire Nationals don’t see Zuko’s distinctive face even from a distance.

“Son, this is your last chance to back out.” Chen reminds him as the entrance to Lo’s greenhouse comes into view.

“I want this. Please trust me. I really, *really* think that I can change things. If there is trouble, I promise I’ll run or do whatever else you say.” Zuko replies.

“Okay…I trust you, I just don’t like you putting yourself in danger like this.” Chen says softly, wrapping an arm around Zuko’s shoulders as they walk.

Zuko just nods as he finishes fitting the mask over his face, not wanting the firebenders to hear his distinctive raspy voice. At least not until he gets a chance to understand who these people are. Form a more accurate judgement of the soldiers up ahead.

Lo rests her hand on Zuko’s upper back, leading him away from Chen a little and closer to herself as they walk into Lo’s personal quarters opposed to the greenhouse, somewhere Zuko didn’t think Lo would allow unknown people to stay. Then again, if anyone were to come to try and find her they likely wouldn’t go poking around her home. She likely wouldn’t want them to see Fire Nation soldiers in her greenhouse.

When they walk in and Zuko sees the familiar red uniforms, Zuko almost instinctively moves closer to Chen. Lo grips the back of his robes, likely not wanting to attribute Chen as someone who Zuko is close to and seeks comfort from, but more as someone who is there for protection.

As soon as they enter, several of the soldiers turn to look at them. There are five in total, he is pretty sure that three of them are women and two are men. It is hard to tell with three of them in bandages and hunched over and one of them laying on a pallet, likely the one Zuko has been brought to heal.

“This is The Blue Spirit, a firebender healer.” Lo says calmly as they approach the soldiers.

Zuko has only been around Fire National colonials once since his banishment but has not been around soldiers, nor had he wanted to. He tries to keep his hands from visibly shaking.

“Was beginning to think you had run off and got guards.” One of the women says with a small, almost sarcastic breath of laughter.

“I’m not going to start anything with you. Even though our soldiers would be able to take you eventually, we would lose people too. It’s in everyone’s best interest for you to receive necessary treatment and then move on. Is that something that we can agree upon?” Lo asks, more making a peace agreement than explaining herself to them.

The same woman nods again. “Once he can walk, we’ll be on our way. Don’t want to stay here longer than necessary. Dangerous when we are in such small numbers.”

Zuko walks forward, raising a hand in greeting to the group, unsure how to proceed, not sure if he should speak or not. Considering the fact that they don’t seem to want violence makes Zuko assume that they are usually positioned to enforce territories opposed to being on the front lines. It might be safe to speak around them. Might be fine for them to hear his voice. They likely won’t risk coming into the town and see Zuko without his mask.

Taking a breath, Zuko decides if he wants to pass any of this on, he would need to speak. “Are any of you firebenders?” Zuko asks, raising his voice an octave to hopefully make his gender indeterminate with a mask and loose clothing.

Three of them raise their hands at staggering increments. “Lee here is a firebender, too.” The nonbender man says, nodding to the man on the pallet.

“The firebender who discovered healing passed, she wanted the art to be shared with others but never had the chance to do so herself. It’s not hard to learn, more difficult to refine it to your own strength and inner flame. Don’t have many opportunities to meet other firebenders and practice in safety.” He explains. “Please. It’s all we have to honor her memory. Anyways, teach others, and you could help a lot of people.” He continues when he is met with silence.

After a few moments, one of the women nods. “I’d be willing to learn. Might be more efficient to teach one of us. I could teach the others later. We would be able to figure it out more together while we travel.” She suggests.

Zuko nods once, not wanting to press his luck. Even if he can just pass it onto her and she genuinely does pass it onto the others, it could be the beginning of change.

Zuko slowly walks towards the man on the bed, grateful when the soldiers give him a little space, kneeling next to the injured man. “What happened to him?” Zuko asks, touching Lee’s feverish skin.

“Didn’t see the weapon, but he had a bad puncture wound that was already infected when we found him. Not really even sure what happened. He has a mild temper and I’ve never seen him instigate violence and most of the villages in the area we were traveling near don’t usually pick unnecessary fights with soldiers.” The woman explains.

At least the person who has agreed to allow Zuko to teach her seems the least intimidating. That is likely because she is the one who has been doing most of the talking and has personalized herself far more than any of the other soldiers. He also realizes he doesn’t know the first thing about her, not even her name.

If these people aren’t prone to violence, he isn’t sure why they chose to be in the military. Then again, Zuko had believed that the Earth Kingdom was filled with stubborn, uneducated brutes that would tear Fire Nationals and each other given the chance. They might really believe that they are helping and not destroying lives.

Resting a hand on the man’s chest, Zuko takes a deep breath, praying that this will work. If something goes wrong and his reactions result in Lee’s death, he has no idea what might happen.

The soldiers might understand that it was a mistake, mourn for the loss of their friend, give him as close to a proper burial as they could, and move on.

They might turn on Zuko, Lo, and Chen, accusing Zuko of being a traitor and killing the man intentionally.

Worst of all, they might take their loss out on the village. It could result in the deaths of many people who were unprepared and settling down for the night while not expecting any threat in the relatively quiet town.

“Do any of you know how to stoke your inner flame?” Zuko asks as he begins to do so himself trying to find Lee’s.

He gets a chorus of ‘no’s from the surrounding group which doesn’t surprise him. He had thought that his uncle had invented that but had begun to assume that maybe it was more common knowledge once he learned about Song. If she had invented healing, she must have known about it. It’s likely that more have figured out or learned about Iroh’s breathing technique.

“It’s the first step to healing. It allows you to connect with their energy. Usually you can use it to temporarily strengthen yourself or warm yourself for a longer period of time. It helps you strengthen their chi, giving them more energy to heal. Works better for illnesses opposed to flesh wounds, but still helpful. Will help more with the infection than the wound.” He explains quietly, feeling Lee’s strength and breathing with him.

Thankfully, the soldier is strong even if his flame is fading. It’s still burning. He still has plenty of fight left in him. That will make it easier. Make it more likely for Lee to pull through. For the soldiers to leave them in peace in a few days. The woman will be more inclined to learn the skill. Song’s life’s work can be passed on. He can participate in making a difference to how firebenders connect with their bending. How the war proceeds.

It’s easier this time. He had learned from Song’s book and then learned more when he put it into practice with Kya. It’s only attempt three and he already feels so much more confident in his abilities to effectively do this. With just a little more practice, he could maybe do this better, more efficiently, and without completely draining himself.

He’ll be able to teach people with more ease and understand it better himself. He can start a new legacy for firebending and carry on Song’s spirit.

Hopefully.

With luck, persistence, and time, he can accomplish that.

He goes through seven rounds of healing Lee when the man’s eyes flutter and he has the energy to move a little, slowly coming back into consciousness.

Thankfully it happened then as Zuko’s own strength had been beginning to dwindle. He doesn’t want to be visibly weak in front of strangers even if he doubts that they will hurt anyone. Especially if they are to discover that Zuko is the only bender here and that Chen is here for moral support and not protection.

“Hey, Lee, it’s alright. We’re with a healer outside of an Earth Kingdom village. They’re close with a firebender healer. They said we can stay here until you’re back on your feet as long as we keep a low profile.” The friendly woman explains to Lee, reassuring him before confusion and panic can even set in.

“Neeya, you guys are okay.” Lee whispers, smiling up at the woman.

She just nods, taking Lee’s hand in hers. “We’re alright. You got beaten up the most. You’re going to be fine.” She assures him.

Zuko can’t help but to smile weakly behind his mask at the display of friendship between the two.

He isn’t sure if the others are close as well or if it is difficult to tell because the woman, Neeya, is the most confident and outgoing of the five. He isn’t sure if it is because she is the leader or because it is just her personality.

Lo rests a hand on Zuko’s shoulder and offers him a cup of tea.

Partially pulling his mask up so that it still hides everything above the tip of his nose, his discernible features out of view, he sips from the cup.

He smiles as he drinks it. It’s jasmine. The tea that he had claimed to be his favorite.

It’s not that he *doesn’t* like jasmine or tea in general, he really does like it, just not in the way that Iroh does. He doesn’t have a strong opinion on them. There are teas that help with illness that usually aren’t good but are helpful. Then there are the teas that uncle would make for him.

There are several that Zuko enjoys, it’s just that he doesn’t really have a favorite. As long as he enjoys it to some extent, it’s simply a tea that he likes.

However, having a favorite tea seemed to be important to Iroh. Zuko hadn't really cared too much and claimed that his favorite was jasmine. It had made the old man happy and had given him a default as to what he could bring to Zuko when they would sit together quietly and drink it.

In all honesty, Iroh could have made the most disgusting tea that Zuko had ever tasted and he would be happy. All that he really wanted from that interaction back in the Fire Nation when he had so little to hold onto was his uncle’s company.

As long as the two could sit together, Zuko would be happy. He wouldn’t care if they talked, if they sat silently in the garden, or if they played a game. His uncle’s calming and familiar presence and the occasional arm wrapped around his shoulder, pulling Zuko closer is what made his life bearable.

Even if things hadn’t gone as smoothly between Iroh and Zuko’s new family as he would have liked, they seemed to have the understanding that they cared more about Zuko than their feelings for each other. They could at least coexist and be civil for the most part.

Maybe when the war is over, they can get to know each other better. They could all be a family

He is sure that Azula would love to meet them. She would probably get along really well with Chen and especially Feya. He is sure that she would love Kani as well, just that she would resonate more with the other two.

Both Feya and Azula understand dedication and loyalty to hard work but have plenty of bite as well. Also, both Chen and Azula enjoy long silences if there is something interesting going on around them, be it some odd critter that Chen would find in the garden or just diligently working.

He really wants to introduce Azula to his family. He wants Iroh to get along with them better. He doesn’t want to have to choose between the people that he loves. He needs all of them in his life. Needs them more than words can possibly describe.

Even if Iroh leaving had broken Zuko’s heart, even after just this time, he already feels more whole than he did since…ever.

He has his new family who have given him so much. The people who put so much time and effort into showing Zuko what a kind, loving family looks like. Showing him how he should be treated and teaching him to stand up for himself and be more confident in everything that he does. Teaching him to let his guard down a little and actually get to be happy.

His uncle is the only reason that Zuko made it this far. He really isn’t sure what would have happened if Iroh didn’t return home to the Fire Nation when he did. Over the years, the old man had become such an important part of Zuko’s life. It’s impossible to ignore that.

Just being able to see Iroh again had helped him so much. He feels more connected to his home and his culture than he has since he’s been here. It is a relief to know that his uncle and Azula know that Zuko is alive. That he is safe, happy, and healthy. He is being taken care of by good, kind people who only have his best interests at heart.

People who love him and make him feel better than he ever has in his entire life. It relieves so much guilt from Zuko’s chest.

“Hey, uh, Blue, where did you learn how to do that?” The uninjured man asks, looking at him awkwardly, clearly unsure how to address Zuko. He can’t help but smile a little at the fact his alias is already getting a nickname.

Putting his cup down and lowering his mask, Zuko looks at Lo, unsure if he should tell the man the truth or if it is personal.

Thankfully, the herbalist answers for him. “My late wife, Song, was a talented firebender. She was never a particularly skilled fighter but had a lot of intricate control over her flame. She spent her life learning how to use her bending to heal. I passed on all of the knowledge that she had documented on that skill onto this one when I learned of their element.” Lo says softly, resting a hand on the top of Zuko’s head.

“What happened to her? Your wife?” Neeya asks after a brief silence, the unasked question of her being turned into the military or lynched by civilians handing in the hair.

Thankfully, Lo just smiles and shakes her head. “She got old. Six years ago, she got sick. It’s not like waterbending, you can’t really use it to heal yourself. Or at least not very efficiently. A lot of the aid comes from the healer producing a surplus of energy in themselves and using that to help strengthen the patient’s. If the healer is healthy, they’ll be tired after but not for too terribly long as long as they don’t push past their limits.” Lo explains, shooting Zuko a look.

“However, if you’re weakened by illness and don’t have enough strength to spare, it doesn’t work at all. We learned that the hard way. But she lived a very long and happy life. She tried to heal herself for a few days and passed in her sleep. Death isn’t as sad when it’s peaceful and you’ve had a chance to live your life.” Lo finishes, smiling sadly.

No one responds to that, they just avert eye contact.

“Lee, is it only your puncture wound that's affecting you? I stitched up and bandaged that one, but anything else you need?” Lo asks, giving the soldier a friendly smile.

Lee just shakes his head, fully laying back down in a relaxed position.

“How long have you known how to do this?” Neeya asks, resting her hand on Lee’s stomach now rising and falling regularly with even breaths.

Zuko shrugs. “Not long. About a week. I have been able to stoke my inner flame for a few years now. I’ve gotten a lot better about it the last few months after I almost froze to death.” He explains, looking down at his hands, wishing that he could share how Chen had found him. How a couple who knew nothing about him other than the fact that Zuko was a scared, injured, firebender who needed help had taken him in and raised him as their own son with no hesitation.

“What happened?” The healthy man asks, cocking his head.

“Caught in a bad storm.” He explains simply, not sure how to go into too much detail without giving something up about who he is. Any information that could be used to find him.

“Can you show me what you did?” Neeya finally asks after a few moments of silence after it becomes clear that Zuko has no intentions of continuing.

Zuko nods, sitting on the floor cross legged and offering his hands forward. She mimics his position.

Inhaling, Zuko begins to share anything that he thinks could help.

Zuko doesn’t remember being taken home, but he must have. He can only assume that Chen had carried him.

He doesn’t remember getting particularly exhausted during the night before, but he can’t remember too much past Lo beginning to copy the notes that Song had made along with additional notes that Zuko had to add. Making it so that the firebenders would continue to have a reference while learning and passing on the skill to others that they met.

Zuko sits up, stretching and scratching his head as he comes into consciousness.

The first thing that he notices is the pale sunlight coming through the widows. He doesn’t wake up past sunrise that often. Even though he has slept this late when he has healed before, he thought that it might be different this time due to him being more careful with his energy and had more practice with the skill.

Slowly standing, he picks up his turtle duck and walks down the stairs, doubting Kani, Chen, or Feya are upstairs this late in the morning. They know that the apartment is a safe place to leave Zuko alone and they likely have work to attend to.

“Mom?” Zuko calls, reaching the base of the stairs, almost immediately spotting Kani bandaging a young man’s arm and runs up next to her, hugging her from behind.

“Good morning, sweetheart, you slept in. How are you feeling?” She asks, not turning around, but he can hear the affection in her voice.

“I’m good.” He mumbles, pulling away, hugging his turtle duck and standing next to Kani, awkwardly waving to the man that Kani is treating.

“This is my son, Lee.” She introduces Zuko as she finishes bandaging the man’s arm.

The man raises his uninjured hand in greeting. “It’s nice to meet you, Lee.”

Before Zuko can say anything, Kani rests a hand on his shoulder. “Chen should be right outside if you want to help him. We’re going to go to the play tonight and then he’s taking you home tomorrow. I’ll come a few days after that.” She presses a kiss to his forehead when she finishes talking.

Zuko can feel his face light up. “We’re going to the play?!” he asks, excitement filling him, sure that he would be taken home before he could even step foot in the theater.

“Feya convinced me. Anyways, I know how important it is to you.” She pats his cheek, straightening herself.

“Thank you.” He almost cheers, wrapping his arms around Kani again and hurrying towards the front door, carefully resting his turtle duck on an unoccupied shelf before running outside.

“Chen?” He calls, rounding the corner of the healing hut to where the ostrich horses are put up, figuring that a mix between Chen’s only slightly above average knowledge of medicine and preference of animals over people would lead him there. Be with the creatures to remind the man of home.

“I’m over here, Lee!” Chen calls from the stables, feeding some grain to the ostrich horses and petting one’s neck as it eats.

Zuko runs over to him, hugging the farmer tightly

Chuckling, Chen ruffles Zuko’s hair. “I’m so proud of you, Zuko.” He praises in a hushed voice. “You’re going to do so many great things in your life.”

Blushing a little from the casual praise that he is still trying to get used to after all of this time, Zuko looks up at Chen grinning. “Kani said that we’re going to the play tonight. Are we really?”

“Of course we are, son. We wouldn’t make up something like that, we both know how excited you have been about theater. Are you excited to see Fao tomorrow night? I’m sure if he even catches wind that you’re coming home he is going to break down the door.”

Zuko nods enthusiastically. “I have a bunch of candy to share with him! We’re going to stay up late and I’m going to tell him everything about these past two weeks!”

“No. No you’re not. You’re going to go to bed at a reasonable hour and not eat candy right before that. You can do that stuff during the day with him.” Chen wraps his arms around Zuko’s shoulders, pulling him close in a friendly manner as he talks.

Zuko just grumbles about how a few months ago Chen would have allowed Zuko to eat whatever he wanted whenever if not outright encouraged it. Just because Chen has a valid reason for not wanting Zuko to eat a bunch of sugar before bed and stay up late with his friend doesn’t mean that he has to like it.

“Yeah, yeah, cry me a river kid. We both know I just want you to eat better food and get to bed at a reasonable hour. You can’t do whatever you want forever.” He teases, pressing a kiss to the top of Zuko’s head.

Smiling, Zuko snuggles closer to him. Even if he would like to do what he wanted, he likes the idea of restrictions being put in place for his health and wellbeing. Nothing cruel like Ozai had done to him for years. Nothing that makes him feel like he isn’t loved or valued, just the kind of restriction that feels like he is loved and cared for by someone who just wants the best for him. Something he hadn’t had for far too much of his life. There are drawbacks, but it also feels nice to have someone looking out for him.

“I love you.” He mumbles.

“Love you too, kid. Anything you need or want to do in town before the play tonight? You probably won’t be back until spring.”

“Can I say goodbye to Lo?” Zuko asks, assuming that the answer will be no due to the likelihood of the firebenders there recognizing him.

It wouldn’t take a genius to compare Zuko’s stature to the Blue Spirit’s paired with his friendship with Lo and his Fire National features. He is sure that other firebenders can easily distinguish the Fire Nation gold from the Earth Kingdom hazel. On top of that, Zuko is sure that he let his real, distinctly raspy voice come through as the night went on.

If they recognize Zuko as the Blue Spirit they’ll be able to recognize him anywhere. Maybe even figure out who he really is. It’s hard to disappear when one has such a distinguishable face while in such a unique position.

He also doesn’t want anyone else to see the Blue Spirit mask. Not yet. Worst case scenario, he may attract someone who sees him and they could find the soldiers. They would almost certainly accuse Lo of being a supporter of the Fire Nation and have her arrested or killed. They likely wouldn’t care that she saw the soldiers as people who have been misguided through years of deception.

“No, I’m sorry, son. I don’t want you to get hurt. You can see her again in the spring. I’m sure she’ll understand that it just wasn’t safe for you to see her.” Chen’s voice is apologetic as he rests a hand on the back of Zuko’s head, gently running his thumb across his hair in an affectionate manner.

“Can we go down to the beach? I used to live near the ocean. Not the same as this one, but I miss it.” It would be nice if the water was warm enough to swim in or even if it was more like home at all. He had never seen a rocky beach until he had seen this one. He didn’t know that those existed.

“Of course, son. Let’s go.” Chen lets go of Zuko and offers him his hand.

Grinning, Zuko takes it as the two make their way through the town to the beach, Zuko practically pulling Chen behind him.

Even if his life is immensely different than it had been, Zuko has found a way to reconnect with the people he has been separated from and has found people who genuinely care for him in a way that no one ever has before.

He doesn’t think he has ever been happier than right now.

The last two weeks have been hard for Azula. If she didn’t have Mai here, this time would be nearly unbearable.

Her father had commented on Mai’s extended stay here, making sure that Azula had her priorities straight in his eyes. Apparently, Ozai’s opinion is the only one that matters. However, Azula isn’t stupid enough to refute that. She knows to just obey him until she has a chance to either beat him or get away.

She had assured her father with the fact that Mai had graduated second in their class at the Royal Fire Nation Academy for Girls, right after Azula. That she understands respecting authority and the vital roles that the Fire Nation royal family plays in the proceedings of the war and functioning of the country. That Mai understands the importance of Azula’s position and that compromising her integrity and focus could lead to compromising her country. That Azula is a princess and a soldier first far before a friend.

She had also added that Mai understood that if she were to become a distraction, she would leave without question. That she loves her country and would never want to be the reason for weakening its leaders. If ordered to leave, she would pack her bags and depart from the palace immediately without causing further trouble.

Her father had seemed to buy her nationalist bullshit.

Considering the fact that Azula has been the loyal, obedient daughter all of her life, it will take reason and cause to make Ozai think that her loyalties have faded. That she just needs to get through these next few years before leaving her father to rot and wither away.

As long as she can keep up the believable act of loyalty and continue to excel at any and all practices that she is given by her father, she will be safe. She just needs to keep her head down and obey for now.

Just for now.

Her father had never had much interest in Azula outside of what she could do in his name to strengthen his rule and then what she could do at the time of his death to carry on his legacy. Ozai has never cared about her as a person. Not as a daughter. Just as a soldier, political tool, and powerful heir.

She hadn’t realized that until a few months ago. It hurts, but it also makes it so much easier to betray him. She doesn’t feel shame or sorrow for preparing to destroy her father at the first real chance she gets. If anything, she feels excited for what she could do to him.

As of now, she and Mai are just sitting silently in the courtyard. With her training continuing at its rigorous course, she’s almost always completely exhausted near the end of the day.

Thankfully, in her father’s eyes, Mai has been the perfect guest. She has been quiet and respectful, immediately obeyed the few things he had told her to do, stayed out of Azula’s way when she was training and was needed elsewhere, and her only interactions with the servants was some kind of request.

Before and after training, Azula and Mai would usually read or study together in the library, going over history, old battle plans, and current politics, appearing to take more interest in them than they did.

They really did read and learn about these things, but conversations would drift about an hour into reviewing books, scrolls, and maps towards personal happenings.

Mai had told Azula about how her parents have been talking about having a second child and that her mother might be pregnant. It’s too early to tell if she is actually pregnant and even if she is, she is still in the stage where miscarriage is easy if any stress is put on her mother.

Mai had admitted that she isn’t sure how she feels about it. She had wanted a sibling growing up. Maybe her life at home wouldn’t have been so dull. Even if she didn’t get along great with her sibling, it wouldn’t be difficult for the two of them to keep their distance from each other.

Despite that, she could have had *someone* to be around during long, boring trips or meetings. Someone under the same restrictions as herself and who understood that the only entertainment and companionship available to them would be their older sister.

Now, at the age of twelve, she just feels like she is being replaced. Now that her father’s political career has taken off and he only needs to maintain his image opposed to build it, she has overheard him talking about spending time with the baby. Actually being present in their life and raising them as a child opposed to using them as a political tool.

Mai knows that she had a pretty good life growing up. She was born into a wealthy family and was given whatever she wanted so long as she behaved and was quiet and maintained the image of sophistication and order that her father was building.

Despite that, she can’t help but feel jealous of something that isn’t even a baby yet. It will be someone who gets the parents and family that she had wanted growing up but couldn’t have due to the image her family was fabricating. The image that never really existed. Behind closed doors, they were all strangers to each other.

Azula understands that feeling.

Even though Zuko didn’t replace her, she had been jealous of him a lot of her life. She wasn’t jealous about how their father would break him down verbally and physically at every chance, she was jealous of his relationship with their mother.

Ursa had loved Zuko in a way that no one had ever loved Azula. Then when their mother disappeared, Zuko was the last person to see her. When their uncle came, the old man had immediately chosen Zuko as well without even glancing at Azula. He hadn’t even tried to form a relationship with her in addition to Zuko.

She knew that Zuko needed Iroh more than ever at that time. She had seen how Zuko began to deteriorate in front of her a little more every day after mom had left. He had all but completely stopped eating. She remembers how loose his clothes got. That his lithe figure became impossibly thinner. He always looked sick and got sick a lot.

On top of that, barely slept, stopped talking, would isolate himself, and would regularly stand near the edge of the towers, just looking down for hours.

Part of her had wished that he would jump. Another part wanted to push him, make the decision for him. The smallest part wanted to talk to him.

For better or for worse, she never did either of those things. She still hates herself for thinking of them, though.

She can’t ever forget seeing her brother in so much pain and misery and just wishing him dead over the jealousy of someone who had left them. Someone who had shattered Zuko’s heart along with her disappearance.

Even when Iroh came back, she is sure that their mother took some of the shards of Zuko’s heart with her. Even after years, he was never the same. Never fully recovered even if his health improved.

She can’t think about that too much right now. Can’t think about Zuko.

Usually, Mai and Azula would spend their time after training in the library reading over texts and eating whatever the servants brought them.

For some reason, today, they had felt the strong desire to be outside. It’s a nice day out. Azula had spent time in the courtyard before, but never like Zuko had. She hadn’t understood his infatuation with the turtle ducks, but just being here and watching them is relaxing.

They talk occasionally about what they hope for in the future and what had happened in their past. For the most part, they just sit silently, eating the dishes prepared for them by servants, occasionally feeding some to turtle ducks that come up to them, chirping at them for food. It gets easier to understand why Zuko loved this place so much with every passing moment. It is a relaxing place and a part of the palace that their father rarely had any interest in venturing.

The more the two have spent time together and the more that Azula is reminded of her brother, the more she wants to tell Mai that Zuko might be alive. Not only that, but he might be safe, warm, fed, and happy with a nice, loving Earth Kingdom family. That he is happier and safer than he has ever been in his life.

It’s not that she doesn’t want Mai to know or doesn’t trust her friend to keep her mouth shut. She just doesn’t want to give Mai false hope. If she were to tell Mai about this and then Iroh were to return a few days later to inform her that the letters were from someone else and it had just been wishful thinking, Mai might need to get over Zuko’s death all over again.

If Lee isn’t Zuko, Azula certainly will. For everyone’s sake, Zuko needs to be okay. He needs to be safe and cared for even if she never sees him again. As long as she knows that he is out of their father’s reach and able to live his life for the first time, she can live with that.

After about two hours of eating and silently enjoying each other’s company while occasionally talking, a guard comes into the courtyard, informing Azula and Mai that it is getting close to when the Fire Lord wants her to be in bed.

Azula just nods in response, standing when the man leaves, offering a hand to Mai to help her up who takes it but puts no weight on it.

The two girls silently walk back towards Azula’s room, avoiding eye contact with anyone and everyone that they pass, wanting to be alone again. Mai is the only person whose presence she can tolerate anymore right now. She’s the only one who really *gets* it. If Zuko is alive, she may have a way to thank her friend for her company when Azula needed her most.

When they reach Azula’s room, they change into more comfortable, but less presentable and formal clothes, and climb into Azula’s bed, sleeping on top of the blankets so they can sleep close to each other even with the Fire Nation heat.

“Thank you for coming Mai.” Azula whispers, not opening her eyes, but reaching out and taking hold of her friend’s hand.

Mai doesn’t verbally respond, but she squeezes Azula’s hand and moves a little closer. Definitely one of the few ways that Mai would express some kind of affection towards her friend.

Smiling a little, Azula drifts off, feeling less hopeless about the days to come before uncle comes home. As long as Mai is here, she can make it and maintain her sanity. Another symptom to alleviate and make them more comfortable so the patient can fight through this.

## Chapter 27
