If it ever gets to be pretty past 10 am (EST) and the chapter isn't up, feel free to yell at me on the DM of my instagram (same user name as this) and tell me to give you your chapter. I doubt something weird like that will happen again, but if it does hopefully I can fix it sooner or give you a valid reason as to why it isn't up yet.

### Text

The play had been an emotional experience for Zuko to say the least.

It had been so long since he’s been to the theater. Almost four years have passed. They had stopped going to Ember Island after mom had left. That was really the only chance Zuko got to see something that wasn’t just propaganda or a puppet show.

He hadn’t thought much about the actual passage of time in a while up until then. Things just kind of happened day by day. His life had strict patterns back in the Fire Nation. Since his arrival in the Earth Kingdom, where his days had been structured, events just also kind of…happened. He hasn’t been sure how to describe the thought fully yet.

It was that thought that had reminded Zuko that he would be fourteen in less than two months. He isn’t sure why. It might be the first birthday he would actually celebrate besides quietly with his mother and hiding from his father.

Well, technically, he *had* celebrated his birthday back in the Fire Nation, but it was more for show. Ozai would make it very clear that Zuko’s actions especially with eyes on him would reflect the royal family and, by extension, the country.

With his father’s attention focused so intently on him, it had always been impossible to please him. Zuko could almost never eat at his celebration while feeling so sick with anxiety.

Thankfully, as long as Zuko appeared to be eating something, remain presentable and quiet, his father didn’t care if he actually ate or not. Most of the time he would just sip tea or water while slowly moving things from his plate when people weren’t looking.

After, his mother would always take Zuko to the courtyard and hold him close, rocking him in her arms, kissing his head, telling him how this was the day that she was given the most wonderful gift she could ask for. Trying to remind him that he was loved.

She had sounded honest, but even so, she left him.

Fortunately, even though Zuko has known his new family for far shorter of a time, he has actually begun to genuinely believe that something horrible would have to happen for them to leave Zuko. That Zuko would have to by physically taken from them.

Even if the past hurts, now genuinely feels safe and loved by the people around him. The people who have done so much to make him feel treasured above anything else in the world. People who would be honest with him and do what they could to heal him of past wounds.

His feelings about his past life and his current life really got tangled up at the play, making it even more emotional than he would have been if he had only been reminded of his mother.

Feya wasn’t lying when she said that the play wasn’t really the main purpose of the production and that it wasn’t that good. That it was really about an event to gather a large portion of the town in one place and have some kind of fellowship even in the harsh season of winter.

The actors likely hadn’t rehearsed the production for all that long considering it is choppy and the actors stumble over each other occasionally, but none look embarrassed. They all look like they’re just here for the fun.

On top of that, Zuko isn’t sure if they just didn’t do a good job with the plot or if he just doesn't understand enough about the Northern Water Tribe to get it. It could also be a solid mix of both.

Either way, everyone seemed to have a good time. The actors had fun, they had the audience participate with them sometimes, most of whom brought food, and there was just a lot of bonding and socializing during the hardest point in the year.

That had been what Zuko loved about theater with his mother most.

Yes, he could be snobby about plays and liked them to be well done, but what really loved was that he and his mother could be in their own little world for a few hours. Where they didn’t need to think about their lives and how miserable they were every single day. They just got to dissapear into the world of theater while sitting close to one another and pretend that they could melt into the happy crowd forever.

With theater, they just had each other and something to distract themselves with. Even when the Ember Island Players butchered plays every year, he couldn’t help but smile while snuggled up close in his mother’s arms.

Most of the time while watching *Secrets of the Oasis* , Zuko was being affectionately touched in some capacity by Kani, Feya, or Chen.

They would hold his hand, hug him, have a hand rested on his shoulder, or protectively wrapped around him. It was nice.

The best part of the night had been when they saw Gaon, Kya, and baby Lee.

Kya was back on her feet even if she needed a cane and Lee was bundled in warm blankets and cradled near Gaon’s chest.

At one point, the couple had even let Zuko hold baby Lee. Even though the baby still looked like an ugly potato in a cute kind of way, Zuko hadn’t been able to stop himself from crying when the baby grabbed the tip of Zuko’s finger in his tiny fist and started shrieking with laughter.

Zuko had wanted to hold the baby for far longer but had given him back to his parents out of fear of dropping him. Even if Lee had survived his dangerous birth, babies are fragile and Zuko didn’t want to risk hurting him in any way.

After the play had completely finished, they had stayed for about half an hour before Zuko had started getting exhausted. Despite his protests, Chen had wrapped Zuko in warm clothes and carried him home.

The next morning, Chen had woken Zuko up far too early and wrapped him up in far too many clothes. It had, unfortunately, been one of the few mornings that Agni hadn’t pulled Zuko up far before anyone else.

It could have been because the winter in this part of the world makes Agni weaker as well, or it could simply be because Zuko’s pallet was warm and Zuko was tired. Either is entirely plausible.

Thankfully, Zuko hadn’t needed to do much. Chen had been careful to secure Zuko into the ostrich horse saddle so that he could sleep on the journey home without the fear of falling.

Feya had brought out some packed food for the two to eat on their travels and Kani had kissed both boys goodbye, promising that she would be home in a few days and that she would teach Zuko how to make black bean pottage which is apparently Chen's favorite.

Despite his exhaustion, Zuko couldn’t help but to smile, barely remembering the majority of the journey back home.

By the time the two make it back to the farm house, the sun is beginning to set in the sky. Despite being awake for most of the journey after the first hour, Zuko’s fingers, toes, and nose are numb, he’s shivering, and is exhausted again.

Maybe he could set up a hot bath in the spare room if he lets Chen know what he’s doing. It is a limitation of not being able to close the door behind him in there. It does take away a lot of privacy in a small place like this.

Maybe at some point he will be able to feel comfortable enough to close himself in that room. He might not like it, but he might be able to eventually do it for utility. Trust that he is in a safe place and that even if he is shut in a small space, he will be able to open the door, and if he needs to, he can fall into safe arms, be held and comforted by someone who loves and cherishes him. Be soothed and told that he isn’t weak or irrational for having fears. Something he may need to hear for the rest of his life.

He isn’t sure though, he might just hang some clothes in front of the fire and warm them up and maybe even his blankets before snuggling up in them. He is pretty exhausted and a bath can wait.

Anyways, Po and Lee are here. He hadn’t thought of that until now. He definitely can’t bathe with them here. It’s not that he doesn’t trust them, it’s that he doesn’t know them, and it would just feel weird.

Chen tasks Zuko with bringing some of the bags inside while Chen puts the ostrich horse up in the barn and makes sure that it is fed and cared for. It will likely need to take Lee and Po home soon and needs the rest and care.

Before Zuko can even get to the front porch, he is nearly tackled to the ground in a hug.

“You’re home! You came back! I missed you so much! You have to tell me everything! Also, my mom made some kinda cake, it’s weird but it’s really good and you need to eat some! Why have you been gone so long?” Fao yells in Zuko’s ear, jumping up and down without letting go of him but somehow not toppling them both to the ground.

“Need to put my bags down, then I’ll tell you everything. Some stuff came up, nothing bad, all good, just a lot happened in town. I brought back some candy to share with you. I think you’ll really like it.” Zuko replies, grinning even if Fao is squeezing him a bit tight. He has missed his best friend.

“Give me the candy!” Fao yells half tacking Zuko all over again but letting him go and chasing him into the house, continuing to shriek with laughter.

Dropping his bags near the door, Zuko pulls out some candy and his turtle duck, running over to his bed and sitting down with Fao, offering the bag to him, grinning.

“I got the candy in town and my aunt made the turtle duck for me. They’re my favorite animal from back in the Fire Nation.” He explains, snugging the slightly lopsided toy and smiling.

“It’s cute. We have turtle ducks here, but they’re mean and chase you. We eat them, they aren’t pets.” Fao replies, booping the turtle duck’s beak before beginning to lay different kinds of candy on a piece of cloth, examining them.

Zuko hadn’t even *considered* the fact that people in different parts of the world might eat turtle ducks. There might even be people in the Fire Nation who do.

Once again, he feels the pang of guilt and sadness run through him. Knowing that even though he eats meat, he always has and still does, and knows that all of the meat he has eaten in the past several months have come from animals that lived a good, long, happy life, it still makes him sad.

He’s sure that it is hypocritical of him to feel that way just because he has an emotional connection to Fire Nation turtle ducks and because he doesn’t have the stomach to kill animals himself even if he’ll eat them.

“I won’t eat any turtle ducks in front of you, Lee. Anyways, they don’t really live around here.” Fao takes Zuko’s hand while he talks, must having picked up on the sadness that Zuko had felt.

Zuko just smiles, snuggling up closer to his friend. “You can eat candy instead.”

“What kind are they?” Fao asks, shoving a large piece in his mouth before Zuko can even start talking, declaring that he liked it with his mouth full.

Zuko can’t help but to laugh, especially considering he had cut those chunks into smaller pieces when eating them himself. It being almost too big to fit easily in Fao’s mouth doesn’t stop him from continuing to chew on it.

“That’s caramel. It's really good, the butterscotch is also good, it’s my favorite.” He continues, pointing to the long, lumpy stick of golden candy,

Fao breaks off a chunk of it and adds it to the caramel he is still working on, now smiling and crunching.

Zuko breaks off a chunk as well, putting it in his mouth and sucking on it, smiling at his friend. Even if he has not only gotten better at eating but actually started to enjoy it, he can’t eat as much or as quickly as most.

“That one is mint, that’s some weird but good hardened maple syrup candy, some appleish candy, jelly candy, taffy, and licorice.” Zuko explains, pointing to each other the different pieces.

After Fao’s big mouthful of candy, he isn’t shoving his face anymore. The two boys just pick off pieces of candy while Zuko fills in Fao about what happened in town.

He tells Fao about learning how to heal with his bending and that he was able to help a new mother and her son. He doesn’t tell Fao about the Fire Nation soldiers, not sure if he wants to spread that detail to anyone before more people know that Zuko is a firebender.

If others were to hear about Zuko, a firebender hiding among them, healing Fire Nation soldiers, they may think that he is tied to the Fire Nation in terms of loyalty.

He needs more people to understand that Zuko was hurt by his own family and had come to the Earth Kingdom searching for safety and had found it here. He needs them to understand that where he doesn’t support the war, he does still care about his country and his people. That he just wants them to be better, not dead.

He tells Fao about how his uncle came to visit and made sure that Zuko was safe with good, loving people and that he didn’t need to worry about Zuko’s wellbeing.

He omits a lot of details even if it makes him feel guilty. He reminds himself that it is for his own and Fao’s safety. That he’ll tell Fao who he really is when he’s ready. That he isn’t using this lack of information to manipulate his friend and do anything to hurt him. Zuko would never trick Fao into trusting him as some firebender runaway and then turn on him as the Fire Prince.

What he really wants is for Fao to care about him and trust him as the Zuko that Fao knows now and then understand Zuko’s true past.

Zuko is sure that his friend would take Zuko’s heritage pretty well and might actually think that it’s cool that Zuko is royalty. He is worried that someone might overhear. It is a much bigger secret to keep and isn’t something that Fao would have one of his moms to talk about with. Fao is kind and trustworthy but does like to talk.

Zuko does make sure to add in that Zuko’s father might do what he could if he were to ever find out that Zuko is alive. Unfortunately, he can’t let Fao know how much the Fire Lord could and would do to destroy everything that Zuko had found and come to love before either killing him outright or letting him slowly die in a cell.

Either way, it would mean the end.

He tells Fao about how his uncle is taking care of Zuko’s sister (he also actually tells Fao that he has a younger sister) because even though their father is proud of her, he only wants to use her and doesn’t care about her. That her uncle is doing what he can to keep her safe.

Unfortunately, there isn’t too much that Zuko can tell his friend about his family. Even though he really wants to tell Fao exactly who he is, he can’t. Not yet. He needs to settle into his place here more with the rest of the village.

Instead of responding, Fao just tackles Zuko in another hug, likely not sure how to respond, knowing that Zuko had just shared something important, emotional, and personal with him. It’s not always easy to find the words to respond to things such as that.

“Well, I see you’re doing exactly what I told you not to do, aren’t you, son?” Chen chuckles, walking back into the house, resting his boots next to the door while holding something gently to his chest and walking towards Zuko and Fao. An annoyed expression paired with a warm look in his eyes.

Even a month ago, Zuko is sure that his body would have tensed with fear at even the indication of Chen being irritated in any manner with him. He would have managed to convince himself that the farmer was putting on a show for Fao and then the second the other boy was gone, Chen would descend upon him. That he would know fear and pain all over again.

Now, he is just able to smile up at the man, sure that the worst Chen would do is take his candy, tell Fao to go home, and tell Zuko to go to bed.

“Fao *ambushed* me and *demanded* candy! What was I supposed to do?” He asks, sitting up a little more but still snuggling up to his friend.

Shaking his head, Chen sits down in front of the two, taking one of the maple syrup candies and passes the bundle over to Zuko. The creature bundled up in Chen’s arms immediately squawks and curls up in Zuko’s lap.

“Cabbage!” Zuko scratches the feathery creature behind its ear as it purrs, snuggling close to him while Fao gently touches her little bean feet.

“She’s gotten used to snuggling with people now. She has been annoying Po and Lee the past few nights and so I relieved them of her. Thought you would like to see her again.” Chen explains, trying to make it sound like he wouldn’t just bring Cabbage in just to keep Zuko company.

Zuko kisses her head before looking up at Chen. “Where are Po and Lee? I didn’t see them.”

Sighing, Chen pinches the bridge of his nose, looking like he is trying to ward off a forming headache. “They’ve been sleeping in the barn. Don’t ask me why. I’m not even going to pretend I understand the first thing about either of them. They’re nice guys, just…weird.”

Zuko just goes back to petting Cabbage, unsure what to say to that, having missed both the silly looking creature and Fao.

“Mr. Chen, can I stay the night with Lee? My responsible mom knows that I’m here because he came home! Plleaasee?” Fao asks, dramatically falling on the floor on his back, looking up at Chen, grinning.

“You're not going to leave unless I carry you home, are you?” Chen chuckles, smiling at the two.

Fao shakes his head, clutching Zuko again.

“Fine, only because this is Lee’s first night home and it’s winter, not much to do. You two boys be quiet, I want to sleep well tonight. Don’t stay up too late and don’t eat much more candy. I’m putting you on breakfast, Lee, to make sure you do.” Chen resigns, standing and ruffling Zuko’s hair.

“Thank you. I love you.” Zuko replies, closing his eyes and smiling.

“Yeah, yeah, I know you’re a suck-up.” Chen teases before walking away and climbing the stairs.

“If I build up the fire, wanna drag my blankets out? We can snuggle near the fire.” Zuko offers, beginning to stoke up the fire as Fao drags the thick blankets out and wrapping one around Zuko’s shoulders, hugging him.

“I missed you, Zuko, please don’t leave again.” Fao mumbles before letting go and sitting next to Zuko as the two snuggle up near the flames.

Cabbage jumps from Zuko's lap and curls up closer to the fire, purring as she settles down.

Zuko is silent for a moment, pondering over the knowledge that he would certainly need to go back to town if not travel to other parts of the Earth Kingdom as he gets older and refines his skills further. He isn’t sure what he should tell Fao and how much his friend should know before it could possibly put them both at risk if someone overheard them talking.

“Fao, you’re my best friend in the whole world and I want to stay, but there is something I need to do, but I’ll always come back. Can I trust you to keep a secret? My mom, dad, and aunt know, but I don’t want too many people knowing in case it becomes a bigger deal down the line. Don’t want the Fire Nation to know how to find me.”He says after a few moments of silence.

Fao looks up at him, mixed emotions on his face before nodding. “I promise I won’t tell anyone if you promise you’ll always come back after you leave. If you’re gonna be gone for any longer than this time, promise you’ll write. I missed you.”

Zuko smiles, laying down and nodding, meeting his friend’s eyes as the two boys settle down in front of the fire. “I promise I’ll always come back and always find a way to contact you if I’ll be gone for long. I also promise to bring you back candy if I find it.” Zuko swears, interlocking his pinky with Fao’s.

“I’ll keep it super secret.” Fao reiterates.

Smiling again, Zuko begins to tell Fao the story of the Blue Spirit. Both the theatrical character and how Zuko has adapted that to real lore.

Even if it isn’t the brightest thing to do, he knows that he can trust Fao to keep his secret. He hadn’t told anyone about Zuko being a firebender nor his real name. Even if he does like to talk, he knows what to omit and even if he is eccentric is very honest. He has yet to break his word about anything.

Anyways, they’re in the middle of nowhere and there are few people that Fao could share this information with. Also, even if it were to get out, it would likely turn to rumor and become more ambiguous with time and distance. It isn’t like Zuko’s identity that could spread like wildfire and Fao might be less comfortable with.

No matter the risk that sharing this presents, Zuko can’t help but to feel happy at the ability to share something important and personal with someone he can consider his best friend. With someone he can feel safe with and trust.

The next few days pass quickly. There isn’t all that much to do in terms of work, but Zuko, Fao, and Chen find ways to entertain themselves.

Where Fao loves his family and has lived a very good and happy life with them, he doesn’t always like being the only boy in the family. He had made it abundantly clear that he enjoys being able to loudly burp and laugh about it at the dinner table.

Unfortunately, Chen shut that down pretty quickly as soon as Fao suggested that Zuko try to burp flames. Zuko is also pretty sure that the farmer no longer found it as funny as Zuko and Fao did and was beginning to find it gross.

Zuko had continued teaching Fao how to sword fight and the Earth Kingdom boy was able to keep his footing decent by now. He wouldn’t be able to fend off a real opponent, but it made him happy, that’s all that really matters.

When they are sure that they are alone and hiding in the fort, Zuko would show Fao the few figures he had learned how to make out of fire. They’re still patchy and not always in the right shape, but it’s still cool and Fao’s eyes light up.

What Zuko would really like is to be able to be fully open about his bending within his and Fao’s household. Then maybe more people in the village.

So far, people have been pretty accepting of Zuko’s nationality and element. He isn’t sure if it is because they understand that where Zuko is a firebender, he really just wants a good, loving home and doesn’t want to start any trouble after they get to know him. However, his age and especially his burn scar likely contribute to his less threatening demeanor.

They can see that Zuko has fallen victim to the Fire Nation far before they even speak to him. Can understand that Zuko would never want to inflict the pain that he felt onto another person even if they don’t particularly like the fact that he is a firebender. Zuko has been on the other side of this war to some extent and has no intentions of perpetrating it further. Making someone feel the same pain and humiliation that he felt.

Unfortunately, now isn’t the time. He needs to get to know the people around him better. They need to understand that he loves Kani and Chen, that he has gotten really close to some of the people living here, and that if it weren’t for the eventual role he may have to play in the war, he would want nothing more than to grow up here, settle down with someone and spend the rest of his life in this remote section of the Earth Kingdom.

He isn’t sure when or even if he will play a role in the war besides teaching people to use their firebending for healing opposed to destruction.

If he does need to leave and actually participate, he’ll want to come back here after. Hopefully the villagers would be willing to accept Zuko back into their lives even after learning about who Zuko really is. Not just about his bending, but his heritage as well. The kind of family that he really comes from and why he was so desperate to find a new one.

Maybe he could help with rebuilding the Fire Nation for a little while but then turn the crown over to Iroh or Azula. Likely Iroh, but he isn’t sure. Zuko is only pretty sure that he himself is the heir to the throne as of now. It’s a position he was once so excited about and now it just seems…empty. He would rather be powerless surrounded by people who would love and care for him unconditionally than be one of the most powerful men in the world and have people who are only obligated to check on him. No one to actually care.

Even if the war were to end and he could take Kani and Chen to the Fire Nation with him, he isn’t sure if being Fire Lord is what he would want. Isn’t sure if he would be any good at it after everything. Even if he was sure that he *did* want it. Above anything else, the Fire Nation needs a good leader and Zuko just isn't sure if that is him anymore.

Good intentions don’t always lead to good results, he has learned that lesson the hard way over and over again. Anyways, he has learned that he doesn’t have the best forethought. Most of the good things in his life have happened by chance, nothing he had actually planned. He needs to be able to take initiative as a leader.

Maybe living in the Earth Kingdom wouldn’t only be something he wanted but a sign of peace. A member of the Fire Nation royal family living amongst Earth Kingdom commoners as nothing but a humble farmer. Or a healer. He isn’t sure. But something like that. Something nice.

He isn’t sure what his or the world’s future will hold, but for now, he can hope that he can at least die in a peaceful world knowing that he has finally had people in his life who have genuinely loved and cared about him more than he thought was possible for anyone to be loved.

He has the second one, now he just needs the first. He’ll do what he can to make that happen. He just isn't sure what yet.

Hopefully, time will tell.

It had taken far too long to get to the Earth Kingdom and then back to the Fire Nation. The days that Iroh had spent with Zuko had been far too short, *especially* when compared to the voyage.

All he had wanted to do when he saw Zuko was to clutch his precious nephew in his arms and never let go, but he had to leave far too soon. Leave knowing that he wouldn’t be welcomed back there even if the people taking care of Zuko put on a somewhat friendly face when Zuko was in front of them.

He is pretty sure that Zuko knew that his new family, the people who Zuko had replaced Ursa, Azula, and himself with so quickly, didn’t like Iroh at all. They didn’t hide their dislike for him even when Zuko was there, they just didn’t continue with the dirty looks and threats.

Considering how open they all were with Zuko, he doubts that they would keep something like that from the boy.

He understands why Zuko had liked them being completely honest with him (even if he didn’t agree with saying *everything* unprompted such as the large Earth Kingdom man flat out admitting that he didn’t like Zuko’s heritage as if that was something that Zuko could control) but couldn’t help but be irritated with the fact that they seemed to think that Iroh was trying to manipulate and hurt Zuko with hiding some truths.

Yes, there are some things that Iroh should have told Zuko that he regrets not saying sooner. He isn’t going to make that same mistake with Azula. He is going to tell her what he thinks will aid her in surviving these next few years even if it is risky, but not share unnecessary information.

It isn’t that he doesn’t trust Azula to guard it with her life or to carry out as she would. It certainly isn’t that Iroh hadn’t trusted Zuko. It’s that the palace isn’t safe for sharing that kind of information. Nowhere in this city would be safe to share much information with either his niece or nephew.

Discretion is key with Azula and it had been something that he had been more hesitant to do with Zuko. He loves his boy, but Zuko can’t tell a lie to save his life.

Unfortunately, Ozai is an expert manipulator and would have immediately realized that Zuko was keeping something from him within a few days. It wouldn’t be too hard for Ozai to terrorize that information out of his son considering how much fear Zuko already had for the man.

Azula, on the other hand, is just as good, if not a better, liar and manipulator than her father. She would be able to keep high priority information secret for years without giving Ozai the slightest bit of indication that she had any relationship with Iroh outside of him distracting her from boredom. Ozai would never be the wiser that she held disdain for him and was willingly withholding information.

It had angered Iroh to no end that the Earth Kingdom trio had insinuated that Iroh had spent his life lying to Zuko as if it were some kind of sick game. Acting as if the situations weren’t completely different. Like Iroh had *wanted* to keep Zuko in the dark as some kind of power trip.

Back in the Fire Nation, both Iroh and Zuko were constantly surrounded by eyes and ears that either would spill their own blood on command for the Fire Lord or were too terrified of him to deny him anything. They would report on any whisperings of suspicious interactions between Iroh and Zuko even with little evidence. Failure to do so could lead to imprisonment, banishment, or worse.

Zuko was already always so on edge from chronic deprivation of both food and sleep while living in perpetual terror of his father, somehow convincing himself that it was his fault for being a bad son and not Ozai’s fault for being a horrible father and man.

Zuko is in a completely different situation in the Earth Kingdom.

The couple can control who they interact with and who is in their house. They aren’t constantly being watched by people looking to find anything suspicious about them. So long as they continue doing their work, living their lives, and their new son acts just like a scared little kid adapting to a new home, no one will even bat an eye.

So long as the overly aggressive healer continues to help people and things still run smoothly at the healing hut, no one will think much or anything of her new nephew coming to visit her with his parents.

They have closed doors to speak behind. They don’t have people watching them, waiting for them to make a single mistake to bring their lives crumbling to the ground.

Even more importantly, there isn’t much of an act that they need to put on to keep their cover. So long as Zuko continues going by Lee, mumbles something about not wanting to talk about his prior life because it’s traumatizing while backing it up with his scar, and not firebending in front of random people, the rest of his story is true. There is very little act.

He genuinely is a terrified little boy who has been adopted by a nice Earth Kingdom couple who needs to adjust to his new life and heal from his old wounds.

People aren’t going to press too hard about who he is and where he came from with physical evidence to back up his story. They are going to be gentle and understanding in a way that they wouldn’t be if those in the palace saw anything odd about either of the princes.

Iroh will be the first to admit that he has made many mistakes in his life that he can’t undo. He will admit that he had failed his son and will do everything that he can to make sure as few young men like Lu Ten will need to be taken by this war as possible. He will do what he can to change things, become a better man, make the world a better place, not let his beloved son’s death be for nothing. Not let himself forget that nearly life ending agony of losing his child under his command.

He will be the first to admit that he made mistakes when helping Zuko. He hadn’t done everything right. He had lied about things he shouldn’t have and not stood his ground at times when he should have.

Unfortunately, he can’t undo any of that. All he can do is move forward and do better with Azula. Know that Zuko is somewhere safe and loved even if part of it makes Iroh’s heart ache with a pain he can’t bring himself to admit is jealousy.

What he can’t stand for is the trio acting as if their situations were at all comparable. He wasn’t perfect, but he did what he thought was right under the circumstances. There is only so much that he could have done for Zuko. No matter what Iroh did to alter Zuko’s path in life, it would have been filled with pain and misery so long as Ozai held Zuko in his iron grasp.

As Iroh walks through the place, he keeps his pace slow, preventing himself from asking anyone where Azula might be. Even if it is unlikely that anyone will suspect that Iroh’s trip to the Earth Kingdom and Azula had anything in common, he isn’t willing to risk it. He needs to make sure that he and Azula can get through the next several years without raising suspicions. He can’t put her in danger this early. They likely wouldn’t make it if he does anything questionable.

He makes his way through the places that his niece would normally spend her down time, trying to keep himself from expressing anymore anger about his interactions with Zuko’s caregivers. Even if they had grounds for what they said and did, he can’t help but feel angry.

Well, he feels like all of them were justified except for the aggressive healer, Feya. He understands that she would have more personal dislike for Iroh after losing someone she loved to Iroh’s hand. However, she had chosen to blame Iroh for Lu Ten’s death with the intent of malice and cruelty.

No matter what happens in the future, even if he needs to be civil around her for Zuko’s sake, he doesn’t think he could ever forgive her for that.

He of course blames himself. But she had been the first person to say it to him.

The conformation hurts so much more. He would give just about anything to have a second chance and spare his boy.

Lu Ten, who was too young, too kind, too gentle for his early death.

He tries to push the pain of the past from his mind at least for now as he continues to search for Azula. He can mourn for Lu Ten as he did for Zuko in the privacy of the courtyard. Just not now. He wants to be able to mourn his son properly, not just feel miserable and angry while he has the fates of two living children resting on his shoulders.

Eventually, Iroh wanders into the library, surprised to see Azula’s friend Mai sitting beside her, both sharing a plate of food and looking at maps.

He can’t help but smile at the fact that Azula hadn’t been completely alone even if it means he can’t tell her anything right now. She had someone who her father wouldn’t hate and who Azula could be herself around.

As he walks towards the girls, Azula stands up, hurrying over to Iroh while checking once more to see if anyone else was hiding among the shelves before wrapping her arms around him.

Standing on her toes, Azula whispers in Iroh’s ear: “Is he alive?” She asks, worry in her voice.

Iroh just nods, unsure how to express all of his emotions in a few words. He would need to tell her everything.

He can feel Azula’s muscles relax a little as she lets out a breath she was holding for weeks. “I trust Mai to not say anything about him. She and Zuko were always closer and me and him were. If we close the door and make sure she understands she can’t say anything, I think she would really like to know.” She explains quickly before letting go of Iroh and standing back on flat feet.

Sighing, Iroh touches her shoulder, looking at her intently. “Are you sure?” he asks, needing her to be fully certain about Mai’s loyalty.

Azula nods, giving him a hint of a smile.

Iroh nods, allowing Azula to lead him back to the scholar’s room they were examining the map in, closing the door behind him so that no one would overhear them if they were to step into the library. They would keep the map on the table so when approaching them, it could appear that they were doing something educational. If they were to step into the closed off room, Iroh could make it seem like he was teaching Azula about remote Earth Kingdom geography and sailing routes. Something innocent and mundane like that.

Mai looks up at him, dark eyes already appearing to be bored and like she wanted him to leave and just be with Azula again.

“Mai, we want to tell you something really important that I think you’ll want to hear. You have to promise that you won’t say anything to anyone, it could put people in danger. It’s about Zuko.” Azula explains to her friend before Iroh can even sit down, both hands resting on one of Mai’s shoulders.

The expression that passes over Mai’s face is the most emotion he has ever seen on the stoic girl. She looks surprised, sad, and angry. It’s an odd mix, even odder for someone who would always practice so much poise.

She nods once, eyes on the ground before looking over at Iroh. “Please. Nothing will leave this room. I promise.” She swears, looking almost desperate for half of a second.

Taking a deep breath, Iroh looks between the two girls. “Zuko is alive, safe, and cared for in the Earth Kingdom.”

There is so much to take in as Iroh explains everything to Mai and Azula. She is grateful that her brother is safe and happy…apparently, but there is just a lot. A lot to process in a relatively short amount of time.

Not only is this being explained to her over the course of less than two hours, but all of this change happened for Zuko in under five months. He had always been a creature of habit. It’s odd to hear how quickly he has changed to his surroundings.

She had been nothing but happy when Iroh had told the girls that Zuko had gained some much needed weight, had healed from his burn, and had no more new injuries that Zuko didn’t have a good explanation for, assuring Iroh that it had been the result of tripping and falling.

Apparently, Zuko had a farmer couple looking after him and had been visiting the woman’s sister who was a healer in a small harbor town. That the healer had made Zuko a stuffed animal turtle duck because he missed the Fire Nation. That the family would regularly show Zuko casual affection and remind him to eat throughout the day, making sure that he is healthy and cared for.

That back in the farming village, Zuko has a close friend who Zuko had told Iroh a lot about. The Earth Kingdom boy who Zuko had befriended knows Zuko’s nationality and element and apparently doesn’t care. Something Azula wouldn’t have expected even from a young, naïve, Earth Kingdom peasant.

Zuko has also apparently learned some kind of healing with his firebending from some crazy old herbalist living on the outside of town who isn’t a bender of any kind. She apparently had been married to a firebending colonial who had learned the art.

None of that makes much, if any, sense to Azula.

It’s odd, but the main thing is that he is safe.

Unfortunately, Zuko hadn’t just gotten close to these people. Iroh had made it very clear that Zuko was replacing his family with some people he only knew for a few months.

Azula doesn’t say it, but she can’t blame him even if she can’t even imagine how much that must have hurt Iroh to see. It must have felt like he was losing Zuko a second time. Losing a son for the third.

Iroh hadn’t thought much of how the people referred to Zuko in public so that no one would get suspicious of Zuko’s place as the farmer couple’s adopted child. However, they would continue behind closed doors where everyone knew exactly who Zuko was.

Zuko would refer to the farmer woman, Kani, as ‘mom’ when speaking to and about her.

Azula remembers how horribly their mother’s disappearance had shattered Zuko.How close to death it brought him. That same reasoning is what made Iroh uneasy about the situation as well.

At the very least, Iroh had assurance that it wasn’t a title Kani had demanded of Zuko with the threat of abandonment. Zuko had defended Kani as his mother to Iroh in private more than once and had even gotten angry when Iroh had reminded him of Ursa, stating that she had left him.

Neither Iroh nor Azula can ignore how suspicious it is that Ozai’s ascendance to the throne, Azulon’s death, and Ursa’s disappearance all coincided. Iroh was the one who spoke first, a part of Azula had known that but never acknowledged it until Iroh spoke to her after Zuko’s disappearance.

Even though Azula is sure that Iroh had spoken to Zuko on this, her brother has always been stubborn. On top of that, he would need to admit that both Azulon and Ozai saw him as nothing but a thing that could be used as a lesson or for some kind of exchange. His view of himself is already too low. He can’t take someone genuinely viewing him as a possession on top of it.

Iroh must have felt the most replaced when Zuko had referred to the healer (who apparently has quite the explosive temper with violent tendencies) as his aunt and she had referred to Zuko as his nephew. Not just for a show, but in private too, once again the same as he did with the farmer.

On top of that, the healer had been the one who had known about Zuko’s heritage the longest. Even if Zuko was the closest to the farmers, he sought out advice and consolance from his new aunt.

From what Iroh had seen, the healer, Feya, had been nurturing to Zuko above anything else. She would make sure that he was eating properly, keep him warm and comfortable, and offer what she could to make sure that he felt happy and safe.

However, she had a nearly opposite approach to Iroh. She had made her disdain for him far clearer than anyone else. She had threatened him, insulted him, and even gone as far as to blame Iroh for Lu Ten’s death.

No matter how much or little truth that statement holds, it has been something that even Ozai hadn’t outright said even if the blow would hang in the air when discussing Iroh’s judgment and failures.

It’s what makes her worry about how well the healer actually treats Zuko and what he thinks constitutes as love after years of cruelty. Arms to fall into, a warm bed, and a hot meal after any insults or blows would probably feel like paradise to Zuko after his treatment here.

Thankfully, Iroh had made sure that Zuko knew that he could send people from the Earth Kingdom to find Zuko and bring him somewhere else. Iroh had offered this several times and every time Zuko had refused, assuring Iroh that he was safe and happy.

Azula can only hope that that is undeniably true. There isn’t much of anything she can do for him from here. At least it is better than his circumstances back here.

Finally, Iroh had shared the brief interactions that Iroh had with the other farmer who was taking care of Zuko, Kani’s husband, Chen.

Chen had been the last to discover Zuko’s true heritage despite being fully aware of Zuko’s nationality and element from the moment that they met.

Apparently, Zuko had attacked the man during a storm when he was scared and the farmer had still brought him home and taken care of him.

No matter the little that Iroh and now Azula know about him, even if Chen doesn’t seem to be the brightest person for taking in an enemy child who had attacked him, he sounds like he is a kind man. Kindness and stability are what Zuko needs above anything else.

Apparently, once seeing Zuko, the farmer had informed Zuko that he was still loved even if Chen wasn’t happy about Zuko’s heritage. Something that Zuko couldn’t control and Chen could have kept his mouth shut about with ease.

The farmer had defended himself to Iroh with the fact that Zuko had wanted honesty above anything else. That he would rather be hurt than lied to.

Azula can understand and respect that considering what she and her father did to Zuko growing up. However, there is a difference between lying to someone with the intent of manipulation and keeping your mouth shut about something Chen could get over to avoid hurting someone that he loves.

Luckily, Chen had apparently been able to touch and come near Zuko without her brother so much as flinching. Zuko had even initiated a good amount of touch and had been who Zuko had sought comfort from when Iroh had to leave. Even if Azula can’t fully agree with him, Zuko seems to trust and feel safe with him.

What is a little unnerving, more to Azula than to Iroh, is that Zuko had sparingly, and almost fearfully, referred to Chen as his father.

The fact that Zuko may have trouble trusting other men with an intimidating build in a position of authority over him isn’t in the least bit surprising. However, from the description, Zuko seemed to be exceedingly close with Chen and trusted him completely.

Out of everyone in Zuko’s life who he had been forced to leave behind in banishment, Ozai is still the person who has the fiercest grip on Zuko’s heart.

It isn’t surprising that Zuko is having trouble forgetting about Ozai, but with everything else, it feels concerning.

Zuko had been able to replace his mother with Kani in only a few months. Someone whose disappearance had broken him for longer than he had been gone. If Iroh had returned home even a few weeks later, Azula is almost sure that the grief would have killed her brother. That it would have hurt so unbearably much that he would do anything to make it stop.

He had replaced Iroh with Feya in an even shorter amount of time. Iroh is the person who had done what he could for years to slowly bring Zuko back to life from Ursa’s disappearance. Iroh who had spent so much time with Zuko and was ready to leave the Fire Nation behind so that his nephew wouldn’t be alone.

Despite the ease with replacing two of the most important people in his life, Zuko was unable to replace his father, someone who he had feared for years. Someone who he had tried just about anything to get away from once Zuko learned that he couldn’t please the man.

Despite the worrying undertones of the whole situation, Azula can’t help but relax at the knowledge that her brother is safe and loved. That even if things aren’t perfect, he is in a better situation than he could have ever been in the Fire Nation.

After Iroh finishes talking, the three look at each other in silence for several long minutes.

To everyone’s surprise, likely even her own, Mai is the one to break the silence.

“You mean it? Zuko is alright? He’s safe?” She asks quietly, almost as if she is waiting for Iroh to say that it had been some kind of cruel prank.

He gives her a small smile, nodding once. “He’s okay. Hopefully we’ll be able to see him again. But for now he is safe and cared for.” Iroh promised her.

Azula almost forgets to breathe for a moment as for the first time in…ever, she sees her friend begin to cry.
