### Text

Winter passes relatively quickly. He can understand why Kani and Chen were so insistent about him staying with them at least until spring. Not that they have to twist his arm to stay anymore and haven’t for awhile, but he get’s why they were.

Even if he hadn’t gotten as close to them as he did and couldn’t imagine continuing his life without them, he would be eternally grateful for their forethought and compassion.

Where he enjoys the short days and long nights of making sure the animals are safe, fed and warm, cooking, playing with Fao, and then snuggling up by the fire, he wouldn’t have survived this season on his own. Every week, he keeps thinking that the world couldn’t produce temperatures any lower, but the temperature just keeps declining.

However, In a home with plenty of stored food, two loving parents who make sure that he is bundled up properly (no matter how ridiculous he looks), and a warm bed by the fire, it’s nice. If he were on his own trying to make it through this with nowhere to belong and figuring out how to survive as he went, he doubts he would have made it to his first snow.

The first day that it had snowed, Fao had run into Kani and Chen’s house at a forsaken hour (even for Zuko) uninvited, tracking snow across the floor and soaking the bottoms of the red curtains around Zuko’s pallet, insisting that Zuko come out and play.

Thankfully, he had been loud enough to wake up Chen who made sure that Zuko was properly dressed for the weather before letting him step outside despite his nearly uncontainable excitement to see snow for the very first time. Looking back on it, Zuko isn’t fully sure how Chen had managed to wrestle layers of warm clothing onto him while Zuko was practically jumping with excitement the entire time.

He had never seen anything like it before. It just kept falling and piling up.

Every time it would snow, Fao and some of the other children in the village would show Zuko how to make forts and then have snowball fights.

When the snow got *really* deep, they would make tunnels through it and play in them until they collapsed.

By the end of the day, Zuko’s lungs and extremities would always be burning, his face would be red, his whole body would be trembling, and he would be completely exhausted.

Every time he came home, Kani or Chen would make sure that Zuko removed all of his wet clothes and changed into dry one, was wrapped up in a blanket, sat down by the fire, and drank a hot cup of tea before dinner.

There were so many things that he didn’t know about protecting himself from the cold. He wouldn’t have even considered his weight as a factor if Kani hadn’t told him that it was a big part of keeping him warm and mitigating illness. He certainly wouldn’t know that it was more dangerous to have wet clothes on than no clothes at all when below freezing.

Despite the harsher conditions, after putting on weight and slowly seeing his body fill out to healthier proportions, this is the longest he has gone without getting sick. Despite Zuko being the one that didn’t need to suffer the physical consequences of malnutrition as severely anymore, he was pretty sure that Kani and Chen had been happier about his health than he was.

Chen had invited Zuko to go hunting with him and some of the others from the village but Zuko had to decline, knowing that he wouldn’t be able to do it before even holding one of the hunting weapons in his hand.

Opposed to berating him like Ozai would have, Chen had just ruffled Zuko’s hair and told him that there would be people foraging for the few winter foods in the woods and that Zuko could learn from them as Chen’s knowledge was decent but limited.

It wasn’t long after that people had returned from hunting when Zuko went out with a group to learn how to forage.

He wasn’t particularly good at it, but every time that he went out, he learned a little bit more. By the end of the winter, he was able to identify most of the local edible and medicinal winter plants. He couldn’t help but be happy despite knowing that there would be far more to remember in the spring and summer.

When spring comes, as he predicted, there began to be more to look for.

For the first bit of it, he was able to dedicate a large amount of time to learning about more endemic plants. He had expected that early spring would be more busy than ever with setting up farmland for the growing season, but that is almost exclusively done by Kani.

Earthbenders predominantly take care of removing the cover crops, tilling the soil, removing large rocks, and making sure that it is fertile before planting.

Zuko had never seen earthbending be used like that before.

The earthbenders are careful to not dig past the fertile soil but deep enough to actually make a difference in the soil quality. Families who don’t have any benders will usually have a friend come and do it for them in exchange for a nice meal or so.

It isn’t because nonbenders can’t do it just as well, Zuko knows that the Fire Nation must get along fine without earthbenders to be able to produce crops regularly, It’s that an earthbender can turn a week’s worth of labor into that of an afternoon.

Even though Zuko had known that this was a close knit community, he can’t help but feel happy to see how everyone would come together, help their friends and neighbors get their land ready, and share dwindling stored food. Where more food is going to be available soon, the staples are still what was preserved last fall.

When it comes time to plant, the earthbenders, yet again, dig the rows in straight, even lines. However, the seeds need to be planted by hand. Even if benders theoretically could do it themselves by spreading the seeds throughout the soil, it likely wouldn’t turn out all that good. This is the type of labor that had to be done by hand every year.

It still cuts down on a large amount of work as Zuko already feels exhausted from kneeling in the dirt and placing seeds at equidistant increments, all different depending on the plant, and then hauling water from the well and carefully pouring it along the rows of planted seeds.

That evening he doesn’t think he has been as ravenous during his time here, not even after healing Kya and baby Lee.

Thankfully, Kani and Chen had only smiled at his appetite.

Zuko goes between helping with the planting and learning more about foraging. Even if both are hard work and he goes to bed exhausted, if not sore, he can’t help but be thrilled about his new life.

When he forages on his own, considering Fire Nationals, both soldier and civilian, had been seen passing through the area from time to time, Kani had suggested Zuko take his mask with him in case he were to ever need it. He wouldn’t want to give away his identity if he had any chance to teach anyone how to heal.

For better or for worse, Zuko doesn’t run into any firebenders. He would want to teach people, but he wouldn’t want to risk someone knowing that a firebender lived near here. He clearly isn’t traveling terribly far with his small daypack fulled with water, a handful of dried foods, and harvested plants and fungus not meant for direct consumption.

On top of that, it would likely worry the village.

Even though there is an unspoken rule between any Fire Nationals passing through and the town to pretend that the other doesn’t exist, it wouldn’t still cause a lot of anxiety. It would be stupid for any firebenders, even soldiers, to attack a small farming village with no influence to gain if taken. It would be especially stupid while far away from anyone who would be willing to provide medical aid to them. However, if they did attack, the toll would be high for the families of the village. Everyone would suffer and there would be little to gain.

Once the plots are completely planted and ready by mid spring, Kani and Zuko make their way into town to visit Feya and pick up some goods they couldn’t produce for themselves.

On their first night there, Feya had made a delicious soup and had made another turtle duck with a different colored shell during the winter months and had given it to Zuko.

Zuko had overheard Kani telling her sister that she was spoiling him as Zuko drifted off to sleep, cuddling with both of his turtle ducks by the fire. Even if he’s getting a little old to sleep with stuffed animals, he doesn’t really care. They make him feel safe and happy.

He is able to visit Lo while in town and learns that she had copied down how Zuko and Song described using their inner flame for energy along with Song’s notes and given it to the few firebenders who had passed through.

She had made it clear that it wasn’t nearly as helpful as having someone to actually teach them how to do it, but better than nothing. She had continued with saying that it was an invention of the Blue Spirit, not wanting word to get to the wrong ears that Lo had been living domestically with a firebender for decades and is still doing what she can to treat Fire Nation solders in secret during the war.

When he had returned to Feya’s, Kya and Gaon had come to see them, bringing an assortment of baked goods as a birthday present for Zuko even though he wouldn’t turn fourteen for another two weeks. He hadn’t added that part though. Anyways, it didn’t really matter to him. He was happy.

The six of them (baby Lee sleeping in his mothers arms) had eaten dinner together and shared what Kya had made for him. Even if he didn’t recognize most of the deserts, he had thoroughly enjoyed every one of them that he had tried.

They had made enough for Zuko to bring back home with him. Zuko had carefully set aside the fried dough filled with spices and icing for Fao, sure that he would absolutely love it. It had been Zuko’s favorite of the assortment.

When they got back to the village, Zuko’s new life was pretty repetitive. Repetitive as in predictable and safe as opposed to rigid and boring.

He gets up early every morning and makes breakfast for himself, Kani, and Chen and the three of them eat together at the table. He then cleans up afterwards as Chen tends to the animals and Kani starts in the gardens.

The three of them work for several hours, reminded to frequently drink water, until the afternoon heat begins to get to the couple.

Considering Zuko had faced summers in the Fire Nation, Earth Kingdom summer isn’t nearly as bad by comparison. Even so, he is always thankful for the break.

They would usually break for two or three hours, depending on how hot the day was and how much work they had gotten done.

During this time, they would usually pick fruit growing on nearby trees, eat nuts and legumes that have been foraged, and jerky, no one wanting there to be a fire in the house with the heat. Zuko had offered to hold food over his hands, but the couple had quietly declined.

Mostly, Zuko would put his food in his pockets and he and Fao would go eat in their fort and talk.

When it is just Zuko and Fao, they talk about anything. Sometimes Zuko will tell Fao what it was like growing up in the Fire Nation or what it is like being a firebender. Sometimes they would just tell stupid jokes and continue laughing even as they got dumber and less creative over time.

When Kyira would tag along with her brother, they couldn’t talk as freely, Zuko not knowing Kyira well enough to share his heritage with her, but still enjoying their time together. They would just eat and tell stories and bad jokes.

Sometimes, Zuko would just watch the siblings fight in a way that he wished he had fought with his sister. Not as if he *wanted* to fight with her, but he would have rather their relationship been around petty arguments and go back to being somewhat close. Not fight over things that matter and tear each other down in the process. Knowing that it wasn’t just about who would get to choose what they ate for dinner, who had to wash the dishes, or who had to help with the laundry, but about survival.

Even if neither had said it out loud, as soon as Ozai had taken the throne, both Zuko and Azula knew that the palace wasn’t big enough for the both of them. One of them would have to go. At that point, neither of them knew exactly *what* that would mean, but they knew that it would be bad. Knew that neither of them wanted to find out from first hand experience.

Zuko had been the one to find out first hand (literally) the pain of being the one burned cast aside. Azula is the one who has to deal with being the one who their father will use to perpetrate his will, cruelty, and world view.

Despite Zuko being the one who had been cast aside, he is the one who actually gets to live a good life. Not a glamorous but miserable one like he would have in the palace, but a humble and fulfilling one with farmers who have kind hearts and good neighbors.

After breaking in the afternoon, they would go back to work. It would always be harder to go back to work than to start in Zuko’s mind. Then again, in the morning, he would always think the other way around. He had come to the conclusion that he just wanted to play with Fao all day even if he knew that wasn’t an option.

As evening approached, Kani would go in early and begin to cook dinner, sometimes yelling for one of the boys to bring her something from the garden or for Zuko to deal with the fire.

It wasn’t until late summer that Zuko and Kani were able to make their way to town again.

In the days before going, Zuko had talked about swimming in the ocean because it would be warm actually enough this time as opposed to in the spring not long enough after winter. He hadn’t gone swimming at all and definitely hasn’t been in the ocean since back in the Fire Nation.

Kani had smiled at his excitement about one of the few good things that Zuko could associate with his homeland.

When they got to town, things progressed as Zuko would have expected for the first two days.

He would do what he could to help around in the healing hut, mostly doing tasks that were necessary but time consuming when all of the healers were busy with patients. He would also work on cooking, making sure that there was soup ready for patients who may need to eat something easy on the stomach but full of nutrients while here.

When he could, he would go visit Lo for as long as possible and would stop by to see Kya, Gaon, and baby Lee on his way back. When he saw them, they would usually offer him a pastry of some kind, each one just as delicious as the last.

He had splashed around in the waves one night, Kani not wanting him to go swimming while it was getting dark. Even though he knows that he is a strong swimmer and doubts he would get hurt even in the dark, he hadn’t gone past knee deep, not wanting to upset or worry Kani.

She had done so much for him. He can’t repay her by going against the few, reasonable restrictions that she and Chen have set for him.

In the late morning of the third day, Zuko had convinced Kani to let him go swimming. She had just made him promise to not go too far and to be back in an hour.

Agreeing to those terms, he had left to the beach even if he would like to be gone for longer. Then again, an hour is better than nothing. He still has plenty of time to enjoy himself.

While swimming just out to where his toes no longer touched the bottom of the ocean, he could see an unfamiliar ship on the horizon. Squinting at it, he can immediately distinguish that the sails are blue opposed to the familiar green of the Earth Kingdom or red of the Fire Nation.

He begins to make his way back to the shore, fighting against the tide going out, excitement filling him at the possibility that he could get to see someone from the Water Tribe even just briefly.

By the time that he had reached the shore and pulled his clothes back on (having gone swimming in his underwear) and started making his way towards the docks, he could see the shape of the ship. It has a much more curved shape than any other naval ship that Zuko has ever seen.

It being midday and there being plenty of work to do, Zuko is one of three people anywhere near the docks. Most of the fishermen are out at sea and most everyone else is working back on their farms or for their trade.

Considering there isn’t a steady flow of people in the healing hut as people can’t choose when to be injured, when and how much Zuko is expected to help when in town is determined day by day.

There had been few people today and Feya had mentioned that he was getting underfoot with all of his energy with nothing to do. She had been the one to convince Kani to let him go swimming. Wear him out a little before having him come back in and help.

Feya would consistently remind her sister that Zuko is still a growing boy and even if he has had bad past experiences, he’s doing better and can be on his own for a bit.

Zuko is pretty sure that Feya’s willingness to let Zuko be more independent than Kani is a mix of several factors.

There are just personality differences. Where Feya is a compassionate person, does everything that she can to help people who need her, and mourns for those she can’t even if she won’t let others see, she isn’t exactly what people would describe as nice. Zuko has even seen her be downright hostile to others outside of Iroh.

Between the two of them, Kani is the gentler one by far even if the lives they chose to lead are somewhat juxtaposed in some ways.

On top of that, Feya has almost definitely seen people time and time again, far more frequently and recently than her sister, be in a somewhat similar position as Zuko’s. Be terrified and beaten down after experiencing the bad in the world and expecting to only see the bad again.

With that in mind, she also has likely seen people in Zuko’s position learn to lead somewhat normal lives after recovering from everything that has been done to them. She almost certainly has full faith that Zuko has genuinely made great strides in his recovery and won’t relapse if something small goes wrong when left alone.

If something were to happen that didn’t involve Zuko being taken or being severely hurt, he is sure that a day or two of being around people he fully trusts in a safe environment would go a long way to making him feel secure again. He wouldn’t need to start all over, just recover from the shock.

Then, there is the part that makes Zuko feel sad and maybe a little guilty even though he is not sure where to place the guilt. He has been reminded by several people that he is allowed to feel things and not fully understand why. That he doesn’t need to justify himself to process his thoughts and feelings so long as he isn’t bringing any harm or danger to himself or anyone else.

He is pretty sure that a lot of the difference is that Kani had seen Zuko at his worst.

She had seen him be unable to open his eyes right after his injury, be unable to close doors behind him while sobbing in the dark, watched him break down over tiny mistakes, and flinch if not cower whenever he saw someone move in his periphery and not be positive about the intentions behind it. No matter what happens in his future, he never wants to go back to being that. He doesn’t have any problem with feeling scared for good reason, but feeling that way all the time was exhausting. It also just took so much from his life. He could have done so many things with his life before this if he wasn’t bound by his own uncontrollable terror at everything.

He is never letting fear own him like that again.

It takes a while for the ship to reach the docks. The entire time, Zuko just watches hoping that the people on the ship don’t think he’s dangerous or weird, especially considering the others on the dock and the townsfolk who could see the ship are all but ignoring it. He can only assume that it is out of complacency and not malice. The Water Tribe isn’t an enemy of the Earth Kingdom. He just isn’t sure if they are anything but allies out of necessity, not friends. He doesn’t know enough about Earth Kingdom politics to be sure.

When the ship finally docks, Zuko backs up a bit, giving the sailors space to dock their ship safely without Zuko getting in their way. That’s a way to certainly make a bad first impression.

Anyways, he doesn’t want to anger a crew of waterbenders while on the water.

Soon enough, three men climb off the ship, the one in the middle being supported by the other two, arms slung around both of their shoulders. He seems to be conscious but also not doing so well. His steps seem to be more about supporting some of his weight than actually angling towards anything, most every step uncoordinated. Zuko might think he was dead drunk if it weren’t for the global circumstances.

“Hey, kid, is there a healer anywhere near here?” The man on the left asks, possibly trying to keep his voice even despite there being worry.

Zuko nods, unsure what to say. He doesn’t know what is true or not about what he has been told about people from the Water Tribe. Despite knowing much of it is surly some kind of propaganda to make the Fire Nation appear superior and justified in their actions, one thing that is definitely true is that people from the Water Tribe are *enormous* .

All three of the men are some of the tallest people that Zuko has ever seen with clearly defined muscle and broad shoulders that can be seen even in modest clothing. He isn’t sure if being larger is an advantage when living in harsh, extremely cold climates or if it’s happenstance. Possibly even intentional for cultural or conflict purposes. Given his extremely limted knowlede on anything about the Water Tribe, he can’t say fro sure.

“Y-yeah, my aunt runs a healing hut.” He replies hastily, meeting the man’s bright blue eyes, appearing even brighter against his darker skin and hair. Zuko isn’t sure if it is just a common look or nearly homogenous one as all three have similar appearances. Well, he can assume, he can’t see the injured man’s eyes.

Zuko begins making his way towards the healing hut, rightfully assuming that the trio would follow him, taking it as direction.

Every so often, Zuko looks behind him to make sure that the trio is still following him and that he didn’t accidentally lose them, not wanting to make the injured man wait any longer to get attention. If he can’t walk or even hold his head up properly, Zuko can only assume that he needs medical attention and rest soon.

When they reach the healing hut, Zuko holds the door open for the three men, sure that the injured man is who they needed to focus on, not a door.

When Zuko follows them in, Feya is already helping the injured man onto a bed, talking to the man who had spoken to Zuko earlier. He’s the tallest of the three by almost a full head, leaving him practically hulking over Feya. The only thing that doesn’t make him seem incredibly intimidating is the fact that he is the leanest and has a somewhat friendly expression. It’s hard to read, given Zuko knows next to nothing about the man.

He doesn’t even realize that he is staring at the men until he gets an odd look from one of them.

Thankfully, Feya speaks up for him, sparing him any embarrassment. “I’m sorry, don’t mind him, he’s been curious about the Water Tribe for the past several months.” She explains before looking at Zuko. “Lee, go get me some water and broth. Separate cups, both for drinking. Make sure to heat the broth up pretty well.” She instructs without looking at him.

It doesn’t take long for Zuko to complete these tasks, especially with his bending to heat the broth up to temperature.

When he gets back, Feya has the injured man propped up against the wall with blankets and pillows for comfort. On top of that, the shorter man isn’t there anymore. The tallest man who had spoken to Zuko is still with the injured one.

Zuko hands the broth to Feya, setting the water next to the bed.

“Hakoda, I’m going to go make some tea to help with your pain, drink the broth, it will keep your strength up. There isn’t too much that I can do for you besides having you rest properly and make sure that everything sets back properly.” Feya informs the injured man.

What stands out to Zuko the most is the man’s name. Hakoda. It sounds odd. Likely because the man is from a very different culture than Zuko is from, likely resulting in forign sounding names.

Not surprisingly, Zuko can’t think of anything to say or do that wouldn’t be uncomfortably awkward (just standing here in silence) or rude (walking away without saying anything) so he settles on just waving, pretty sure that it is a universal friendly greeting.

The uninjured man gives Zuko a small smile, raising a hand in return. “I’m Bato, she said your name is Lee, right?”

Zuko nods, trying to think of a way to continue the already awkward conversation, interlocking his fingers and looking down at them before looking up and continuing to talk. “Are you guys from the North Pole? Is it cold up there? How high does the slow get? Does the ocean even freeze over?” He asks without fully thinking, not meaning to say that much, hoping that these aren’t the kind of questions that would annoy them.

The sick man, Hakoda, chuckles a little before falling into a coughing fit, setting his broth down so that he wouldn’t spill it on himself.

Bato just gives Hakoda a look that looks like something akin to smug but almost in a…friendly sort of way. Friendly smug? He isn’t sure if that is a thing. Then again, he’s never been the best with emotions.

“Are you alright, sir?” He can’t help but wonder if it is a stupid question about where the two are from. He can’t find it probable that a nation with no benders would go to war with the Fire Nation. He also isn’t sure if it is common knowledge that the Southern Water Tribe was stripped of their benders. He would rather sound stupid than expose himself.

“No worse than I was before.” Hakoda attempts to joke which only gets him a sour look from his friend. “You just remind me of my son. Always been very curious. We’re actually from the South Pole. We always have snow and chunks of ice float around in the ocean, the whole thing doesn’t freeze. Are you from around here?”

Zuko isn’t sure what to make of any of it. The fact that a tribe of nonbenders have had enough and are ready to likely end their lives to fight trained firebenders on wooden ships. The fact that Hakoda is managing to find humor in his situation while comparing Zuko to someone he must care about and had to leave behind for war.

“Are there really lights in the sky in the South Pole?” Zuko asks after a moment, feeling like the conversation would get more awkward as Zuko has no idea how to proceed without hitting even more of a dead end.

It’s times like these when he desperately wishes he had any communication skills. He also wishes he knew more about the Water Tribes.

Even if Bato and Hakoda, along with the other man Zuko saw, fit the physical description that he has heard, neither of them seem like feral savages who would fight wild animals with their bare hands or drink and paint themselves with blood. Outside of slight, expected cultural differences, they seem like somewhat normal grown men.

Bato nods. “We can see them every night back home. They’re gorgeous. Heard they’re supposed to be even more spectacular in the Northern Water Tribe. Supposed to have a stronger connection with the spirit world.”

Zuko can feel his face light up as he looks up at the men, unsure why he feels so excited about something he would almost certainly never see. Maybe it’s just the fact that the world can hold so many wonders.

Hakoda sets his bowl down before carefully laying down on the bed with the help of his friend, wincing and letting out a few groans of pain as he does. He really isn’t sure exactly what happened to the man but it must be pretty bad. Hakoda moves like someone who is in a lot of pain would no matter how much he is trying to hide it.

Zuko hasn’t spent nearly enough time in the healing hut to be able to narrow down specific areas of pain, but even he can tell that the man must have hurt his back and neck with how he is supporting his head with one of his hands. He doesn’t know too much about those types of injuries other than they can be very dangerous. Spinal and cranial damage can lead to chronic complications even if injuries are minor.

“Um, Mr. Hakoda, sir, do you need anything?” He asks, feeling guilty just standing there and watching the man suffer even though there is little that he can do without endangering himself and possibly making matters worse.

He moves a little closer even as Hakoda shakes his head.

Cocking his head, Zuko looks at Hakoda’s face again, interest still drawn to his blue eyes, a color he had never seen before today. On top of that, even if he has known for some time that what the Fire Nation told him about the Water Tribes was likely just as wrong as what he had been told about the Earth Kingdom, he still hadn’t been sure what to expect. A terrifying image of a large, emotionless, animal-like people is all he had ever been told and had been the picture he had subconsciously formed in his head. It feels strange to see the all-too-human face and warm expression despite being in pain.

Hakoda begins to open his mouth like he is about to say something when his eyes focus on Zuko’s.

He isn’t sure if it is instinct of being self conscious, but Zuko gently touches his scar with two fingers without even thinking about the action. Even though he knows that it is going to be something that draws attention for the rest of his life, he is still getting used to people staring at his scare. He doesn’t like it one bit, but there is nothing he can do now but accept it.

On top of that, both Kani and Chen have told him that no matter how Zuko feels about it, it will keep him safe. Many Earth Kingdom soldiers will overlook a boy with a palm-shaped scar taking up a large portion of his face. They’ll be less likely to suspect him of having any connection with the Fire Nation and will be less likely to try and recruit him into the military when he gets older. They probably won’t pressure someone who has suffered that personally from the Fire Nation’s cruelty.

It takes him a moment to notice that Hakoda’s gaze doesn’t shift when Zuko touches his scar. It’s when he realizes that the man’s gaze was never focused on his scar but on his *eyes* . Likely the color of them.

He feels himself freeze, trying to get words to come out but unable to speak or move. It’s all he can do to continue to breathe. Other people are here. People who don’t know who Zuko is. He can’t let himself panic and he can’t give either of the men reason to panic. He can’t alert the others. It will draw attention to him. Something that could be very bad right now incase this situation escalates.

“Were you born near the colonies?” Hakoda asks quietly and far more calmly than Zuko would have expected. It sounds like he is intentionally keeping others from overhearing him. He is giving Zuko a chance to explain himself and not shove him into danger.

Zuko can’t even think of an answer, let alone say anything. He doesn’t know the first thing about either of these men past surface information. He has no idea how to safely navigate this conversation.

When Zuko doesn’t answer, Bato gets down on one knee, lightly touching Zuko’s shoulder with one hand and resting one finger under Zuko’s chin with the other, tipping Zuko’s head up a little, getting a better look at his eyes for a moment before letting go.

“Hey, Lee, kid, it’s alright. It’s alright. Neither of us are going to do anything to put you in any danger. It’s alright.” Bato quietly reassures him, also keeping his voice quiet, mitigating the chance that someone would overhear them.

“You from near the colonies?” He repeats Hakoda’s question.

Zuko just pushes Bato’s hand from his shoulder, hurrying across the room towards Kani who is busying herself with cleaning and sanitizing tools from a recent patient who had needed shards of glass removed from their arm and stitches for the laceration.

He needs to tell Kani what happened. Tell her that he should have known soldiers would recognize firebender eyes. Even if they didn’t seem to be upset with Zuko’s heritage, perhaps not marking a burned child as a threat, he doesn’t know what others may think if they’re to overhear. He really doesn’t want to wait to find out. He would rather flee like a coward and nothing to go wrong than to stay put and have the Earth Kingdom military notified and coming for him in a matter of hours.

He wraps his arms around Kani’s waist, resting his head against her chest.

He can feel her arms wrapping around him in response before she presses a kiss to the top of his head. “Sweetheart, what’s wrong? Did something happen?” She asks quietly, likely feeling the slight trembling in Zuko’s body.

“They know.” He whispers softly, not lifting his head. “They know what I am.”

The healer, Feya, comes out a few minutes after Lee had panicked and ran to who Hakoda can only assume is his mother. A child’s most innate protector and source of peace and comfort.

She hands Hakoda a cup of tea which must be for the pain that she mentioned earlier.

“For a man who is ready to fight the Fire Nation, I would assume you were smart enough to stay sitting to finish drinking everything. But go ahead, spill tea on yourself, see if I care.” She dismissively raises her hand more in mild irritation than anything.

He wants to ask her about the boy. She *has* to know that Lee certainly has Fire Nation blood running through his veins. If Hakoda hadn’t been able to tell by the boy’s eyes, the way he reacted confirmed any doubt in that suspicion.

He could be from the colonies and he and his mother moved here or his father could have been a Fire Nation soldier as his mother is clearly Earth Kingdom.

Thankfully, Bato keeps him from asking such a loaded question at the beginning of the conversation.

“Feya, is there some kind of mail system here or at least a nearby Earth Kingdom base? Also, would he be allowed to stay here until he recovers or is there somewhere else we can take him? We need to keep moving but Hakoda won’t recover properly on the ship and might even get worse.”

Feya smiles a little, nodding once. Hakoda isn’t sure if that is supposed to be a yes to something and if so, to what.

Thankfully, she actually uses words to clarify whatever she meant by that.

“You can stay here.” She replies, turning to face Hakoda. “My nephew will talk your ear off the second he feels somewhat comfortable around you as long as he’s here, though.” She warns with humor in her voice more than criticism.

“Um, about him,” Hakoda begins, unsure what exactly the kid’s history is but is certain that the very idea of discovery is terrifying to him. Hakoda doesn’t want to leave the boy terrified that he’s going to be reported and arrested for something he had no say in while very likely posing no threat.

“What?” Feya asks, crossing her arms.

With the clear lack of patients she holds for everyone, Hakoda can’t imagine why she chose to be a healer of all professions.

“Neither of us are going to say anything to anyone, and please relay that to him, but is he…does he have any relation to Fire Nationals? Just the way he looks. Won’t say anything to anyone, he seems like a good kid. We’re not going to do anything that would get him hurt.” He says relatively quickly while keeping his voice low.

Feya’s gaze grows hard before going back to neutral and then looking down. It's very difficult to read exactly how the woman is feeling but she seems conflicted above anything else.

“You say anything to anyone, and I promise that it will be the last mistake that you ever make.” She threatens, cracking the floor under her feet and then sealing it just enough to make it clear that she is an earthbender and can and will kill him with her bending.

Healer or not, she cares about her nephew more than her dedication to do no harm.

Hakoda just nods once, awkwardly sipping his tea in his position, not wanting to sit up again, pain shooting through his body at the slightest movements to his back and shoulders. Even if he had confirmation that nothing was truly broken as it was just several strained muscles, fractures, and internal bruising. Despite that, it feels like he’s covered in stab wounds. Who knew being thrown off one ship by a blast of flame and being thrown against the hull of another could hurt this much?

One thing that brings him some comfort is that Sokka would likely find the story funny when he saw his boy again. He misses his children so much and would give just about anything to spend a day with them. Make sure that they’re doing alright. Make sure they know how much he loves them. How it broke his heart to leave them but only did so for the chance that they might be able to see a peaceful world. A world where his daughter might actually be able to learn bending without fearing for her life. Something she has wanted desperately from the first day that she discovered her element.

“Is his father a soldier or something?” Bato asks, pulling Hakoda from his thoughts.

“He’s adopted.” Feya answers after an extended silence. “My brother-in-law found him half dead and scared shitless in the woods awhile back when he was first burned.”

Hakoda can’t begin to imagine how the boy’s life must have been. Must still be. He has been just as much a victim of the Fire Nation as anyone else in the Earth Kingdom but would still be seen as the enemy by many. Assuming a firebender gave him the scar taking up nearly a third of his face, he has a very personal history with his own country’s cruelty.

“What happened?” Hakoda asks, unable to ignore his curiosity. Sokka definitely got that from somewhere.

Not surprisingly, Feya shakes her head. “Not my story to share. It’s very traumatic for him and I don’t know all of it. He’s said several times that he just wants to forget about his old life. Please keep his heritage quiet. His parents and I are more worried that he’ll be taken and hurt by the Earth Kingdom military but he’s absolutely terrified that the Fire Nation will come for him if they find out he’s alive.”

Hakoda can’t imagine that the Fire Nation would redirect manpower to go find and harm a child living in a nearly insignificant part of the Earth Kingdom and Bato must have had the same thought.

“Is that an actual possibility? Fire Nation soldiers would come for him?” Bato asks, cocking his head a little.

Thankfully, Feya shakes her head. “It’s a real possibility in his mind. He lives in absolute terror of being found and everything he cares about here will be taken from him. We figured it best to do what we could to show him that he’s safe now and to validate his feelings. He’s been getting better. A lot better. He just needs more time.”

The three go silent before Feya speaks again. “How long can your crew stay? At the longest? Hakoda, you won’t heal naturally in time, but there is another possibility. I’ll explain it to you if it even can happen.” She suggests nonchalantly as if what she said didn’t sound…creepy, almost.

Hakoda thinks for a moment, trying to account for maintenance that the ship could use that can’t be done at sea and supplies that they could use before answering. “Two or three days. Some repairs need to be done after our last encounter and it would be better to not stop again. Also, what do you mean by an alternative to healing?”

“Good to know. Also, lay on your stomach, not your back, thought you were smart enough to know not to lay on your injury.” Her voice goes back to her sharp, agitated one that is likely more natural with strangers. He can’t help but notice that she almost pointedly ignores his question.

“Drink your tea.” She continues before Bato or Hakoda can say anything before walking away from them and through a door that he can only assume leads to some back room or her home.

Begrudgingly, Hakoda slowly moves off of his back despite the pain, following the healers instructions as best as he could. He still barely knows her, but he knows not to piss her off.

By the time that Feya comes back down, Koaruq had already come back to the healing hut and then returned to the ship again. Koaruq, Bato, and Hakoda himself had discussed the plans about possibly staying a little longer to see if Hakoda could depart with his crew.

Koaruq had agreed that the hull had sustained some damage and even if not immediate, if neglected, it could eventually lead to flooding of the hull if they were to hit any rough waters. Unfortunately, that is likely.

On top of that, barnacles need to get scraped from the bottom of the ship as well. It is a miserable but necessary task of maintaining the wood, speed, and integrity of the ship as a whole.

Hakoda had explained that the healer might have a way to heal him faster depending on what exactly Hakoda’s injuries are. He’s pretty sure that’s what Feya had meant. That if she found what she needed and it was compatible with the injuries, she could help him.

He doesn’t go into detail, confessing that he doesn’t really know what it is either.

Koaruq had eventually told him that Hakoda would have some time to get better, but chief or not, if he was a liability in battle, he would need to stay behind while he recovered. They would rendezvous when they could. It would be made easier with the mail system that is apparently here.

Hakoda had promised that he wouldn’t lie about his condition and would only depart with his crew if he knew that he wouldn’t endanger the men who he has been traveling and planning with. He means it. He doesn’t like the idea of being left behind, but he won’t put his men, his family, in danger over a point of pride.

About twenty minutes after Koaruq’s departure, Feya had retuned, expression once again stoic. The most emotion that Hakoda has seen on her is when she was talking to or about her nephew. Then again, he barely knows her.

“He’s willing to try to heal you. Usually, he tries to keep his identity secret, but given some information you have, we’re worried you may draw your own conclusions and put him in danger. He only wants to help, but you need to keep this quiet and only share what he permits you to, alright?” The healer says softly, a threat hanging in her voice as she leans towards the two men.

The confused expression on Bato’s face is a relief to Hakoda. He hadn’t hit his head so hard that he’s completely stupid or lost his damn mind. He can’t think of a single thing that they know to identify a healer and why it would be dangerous for people to know who he is. Maybe they’ll understand when they actually see the healer.

Assuming his questions will be answered soon enough, he doesn’t press for answers.

Unfortunately, getting those answers *does* mean being moved. After finally getting a chance to properly rest, he feels a lot more stiff while Bato and Feya help him stand. Even though he is well aware that it is a part of the healing process and because he hasn’t been moving his muscles, he can’t help but feel like he is getting worse.

When Bato had implied that they find another man to help Hakoda up the stairs (something that had come to Hakoda’s mind as well) Feya had given the two a look that he is honestly surprised didn’t annihilate them on the spot.

Based on her grip, he is sure she would be more than capable of dislocating his shoulder if either man said anything else to offend her. He has to say, that he is surprised that her grip is as strong as any man’s.

He doesn’t say that though, sure that she would take it the wrong way and throw him down the stairs, snapping his spine. She seems to have a temper.

When they reach the top of the stairs that lead to Feya’s home, he can hear the quiet laughter of a young boy, only able to assume that it is Lee. The Fire National child he had inadvertently terrorized.

He can’t blame the kid for growing cautious. His own nation had turned on him for some reason and he almost certainly isn’t accepted here but has nowhere else to go. Has finally found a family that cares about him but has to find ways to hide in plain sight while needing to create a new identity and repress every aspect of his old one.

He can’t even begin to imagine how hard the kid’s life has been already and how much harder it will definitely get. Needing to assume that everyone who could recognize firebender eyes would hold ill will against him despite bearing a large burn scar on his face and being a child in Earth Kingdom clothes with an Earth Kingdom mother.

Sure enough, Lee is standing over a fireplace in the kitchen with his mother, her arm wrapped around his shoulder as he mixes something in a pot with a long, metal spoon, laughing at something. Maybe his mother is trying to cheer him up and take his mind off of his worries from earlier. Even then, still odd for him to be cooking when his mother is likely fully capable. Then again, it really isn’t his place to say anything.

Feya and Bato help Hakoda down on a pallet near the unlit fireplace that looks like someone else is usually sleeping here. There are two crochet bird-esq creatures near the head of it, making Hakoda assume that this is where Lee sleeps.

The kid seems a little old for stuffed animals, but he certainly has bigger problems than being viewed as immature.

Both he and Bato are confused when Feya instructs Hakoda to lay on his back after she had ridiculed him for not laying on his stomach earlier, but neither man protests. Anyways, they have no idea what she is going to do to help heal him faster or how that is even possible.

“Kani, Lee, can you two come in here?” Feya calls behind her.

Not long after, the boy’s mother, Kani, and Lee walk into the room. Lee is walking close to his mother but not hiding behind her like he had been right after his nationality had been discovered.

“Hey, kid, I’m sorry for frightening you earlier. I promise, neither of us are going to do anything to put you in any danger.” He promises the young Fire National in earnest.

He hadn’t met many Fire Nationals. All that he had have been in combat and have all been trained soldiers. Not scared little kids who want a family and safety.

“Thank you.” Lee responds softly, still leaning against his mother in a way that looks more like seeking comfort and affection than safety that he may have wanted before. “I really don’t want any trouble. Just wanna stay here.”

Before that conversation can continue, Feya steps forward, holding some kind of theater mask in her hand. Hakoda doesn’t have the faintest idea about how this could pertain to the situation at hand in any capacity.

However, even in the short period of time he has been there, he has learned that the healer explains things quickly and doesn’t like stupid questions.

She briefly explains who the Blue Spirit is in some theatrical production that Hakoda has never even heard of before. She then explains who the Blue Spirit is in terms of the real world.

A healer who hides his identity behind the mask and needs to be kept anonymous for his protection.

Not just any healer. A healer who could use bending to strengthen people and focus that energy to heal wounds and bring them back to health.

A firebender healer.

Hakoda can’t keep his gaze from moving back to Lee every so often as Feya talks, unable to think of anything else he knew that would make it difficult to hide this healer’s identity. Could lead to Hakoda putting someone in a lot of danger.

He already knows that Lee is at least of Fire Nation descendants and is hiding from two nations, knowing that being discovered could lead to his arrest and execution. He would be able to recognize Lee’s size and movements with just a few hours between seeing him downstairs and masked here.

The main thing that keeps him from fully thinking that it’s Lee is because he can’t imagine a couple living in the Earth Kingdom during a war would take in a firebender child even if they felt bad for him. He would just present far too much of a threat. The world has already seen how little control firebenders have over their bending. How they turn everything they touch into ash. How dangerous they are.

Even a young child like Lee could be destructive. He could set fields and buildings on fire, injuring and displacing far too many. If anyone were to ever see him holding flame in his hand even with no ill intent, it could get everyone who had known about his element arrested if not killed.

Even though part of him knows exactly who the Blue Spirit is well before his suspicions are confirmed, he still feels a jolt of shock as the young, scrawny boy produces flames from his right hand, holding it out in front of him for all to see.
