### Text

Zuko carefully kneels next to Hakoda, no flames present in his hands anymore.

He had wanted to make it clear that he was a firebender but in the least threatening way possible. Just holding a flame in his hand seemed to be a good way to go about it.

Even if it wasn’t the best, Hakoda and Bato had just stared at him, making no move to back away or to fight him. So that had to be a good sign. Right?

His movements are slow and made very intentional as he is already nervous about approaching someone who has certainly had bad experiences with firebenders and now knows that Zuko is one of them. He doesn’t need to be presenting the evidence for that as well when unnecessary. Evidence that could be used to attack them at any given moment after having years of bad experience with firebenders.

Zuko had been given confirmation and reassurance from Feya that neither man would hurt him. Kani had made it clear that if either of them even tried to lay a finger on her son, Kani and Feya would have the advantage of bending and both being uninjured even if the men are bigger, stronger, and trained soldiers. Despite that, he can’t help but feel nervous.

His eyes keep moving between Bato and Hakoda, unsure what to say or do.

Thankfully, Bato seems to understand Zuko’s anxiety and hold no resentment towards him and sits down a few steps further from Zuko, putting himself in a position where it would be more difficult for him to lunge without warning. A silent promise to Zuko’s safety.

“There’s going to be fire near you…just if you want me to stop, tell me to or tell my family if I don’t respond. They know how I react to things. Don’t want to accidentally burn you if you startle me. I promise I won’t intentionally do anything to hurt you.” He warns quietly, more worried that if Zuko were to unintentionally burn Hakoda while the man was trying to push Zuko away, he would be seen as hostile.

“Hey, kid, it’s alright. It feels a little odd right now, but it’s going to be fine. It sounds like you’ve done this before and you spend a lot of time in a healing hut. I didn’t think you were going to do anything malicious just because you’re a firebender.” Hakoda assures him.

Zuko feels the last bit of air held in his lungs out, relaxing at that sentiment. “Thank you, sir.” He replies quietly, carefully resting his hands on the man’s chest and stomach.

Taking a deep breath, Zuko begins to connect to the man’s energy, praying to anyone listening that he won’t mess this up.

Hakoda had seen very little firebending in his life.

He can’t remember the first time that he must have, he was too young. His father had been a waterbender and had been taken during the first raid. Hakoda doesn’t remember him and certainly doesn’t remember the raid or the firebenders leading it.

The first time that he actually remembers seeing it was when he had lost his wife and his children had lost their mother. He still isn’t sure if losing Kya or being forced to leave his children behind, possibly even saying goodbye to them, tore at his heart more.

He had seen firebending more recently and more consistently now that he left for war. Once again, he had only seen it used for violence.

It had been used to set ships on fire, to burn people Hakoda had known all of his life and cared for along with Earth Kingdom fleets that they had joined.

No matter who he saw get attacked, it was horrible to witness. It was even more ghastly to see the victim once the battle was over. He can still smell the burning flesh even if his own skin is barely scorched. It had been a blast meant to damage a large space, not decimate a small one. The latter is where the burns that could be heard bubbling and could be smelled across the deck came from. The only hope would be that the victim might go into shock or someone could render him unconscious so he wouldn’t feel it until they could be left somewhere on shore with medical aid.

Hakoda has never seen firebending that isn’t destructive in some manner. He *certainly* has never seen firebending that is actively constructive in any way.

If he had put some thought into it, he is sure that he could think of some things that firebending could be constructive in. Maybe melting ice for fishing or when building igloos, blacksmithing, cooking, and pottery.

However, no matter how long he could have put his mind to it, healing would have never once crossed his mind. Not in the slightest. Yet here he is, being healed by some firebender child with the worst burn scar that he has ever seen taking up a large portion of his face.

It feels odd. Not the firebender healing him part (well, at least not completely) but he goes between feeling stronger and more alert than he ever has and then exhausted in a very short amount of time.

Thankfully, the pain slowly begins to fade. The oddest part is that it feels like there is…something seeping into his damaged bones and muscles. Maybe *that* is how the kid heals? He can’t be sure.

His injuries are going down from stabbing pain to feeling like really bad bruising when he feels Lee pulling away, this time for longer than just a moment to catch his breath, eat something, or drink some water.

He looks over to see Kani holding his limp body to her chest, rocking him gently. By the lack of concern on her face, he must just be exhausted and this must be normal. He can’t imagine any loving mother appearing that calm if her child had passed out for no reason.

Lee lets out a small, high pitched whine as Kani cards her fingers through his hair, shushing him. “No, love. I know you want to help, but you’re exhausted. You need to rest. I’m not letting you push yourself too far.” She whispers, pressing a kiss to her son's head.

“Is he alright?” Bato asks, resting a hand on Hakoda’s shoulder while looking at Lee.

Kani nods once. “Yeah, he’s just tired. He likes to push himself too far thinking he can do more until someone has to stop him from really hurting himself. He just needs some rest and a good meal when he wakes up.” She explains absently, smiling down at her exhausted child.

“I know that it might be tempting to tell people about Lee for a number of reasons, and I know you’ve already promised that you would obscure gender and only refer to them as the Blue Spirit, but please remember that. He’s just a little boy. If he ever chooses to reveal his identity, I don’t know if he will, he needs to be able to do so on his own terms. Okay?” Feya’s voice is even and surprisingly calm, no threat hidden in her words this time. She must believe their promise from last time. This is genuinely just a reminder.

Hakoda nods awkwardly in his position and sees Bato do the same out of the corner of his eye. “I promise. He’s done nothing but do his best to help. I won’t do anything to put him in danger.” Hakoda promises sincerely.

Even if Lee is a firebender, and protecting one doesn’t feel completely right after the last 97 years of war, he’s still a child. This instinct that Hakoda had felt the moment that he first held Sokka in his arms overpowers generations of reason to fear any and every firebender. The feeling born of fear to get rid of them no matter what as they would do the same to the rest of the world.

Above being of Fire Nation descendants and a firebender, Lee is a child. A little boy so full of excitement, love, and curiosity despite everything. The fascination with everything and desire to do more than he is physically capable of reminding him far too much of his own son.

His desire to protect and defend Lee at any and every cost overpowers any worry about the boy’s heritage. At what others may say about him for caring about and protecting a firebender hiding in the Earth Kingdom.

Kani slowly begins standing up, holding her son in her arms, the boy looking impossibly smaller. He can hear Lee whimpering a little in protest but wraps his arm around Kani’s neck for support.

It’s hard to gauge the boy’s age. He looks maybe twelve as he comes up just below his mother’s chest, but he acts older when having a legitimate conversation with someone.

No matter his age, the boy is dreadfully thin. His face looks relatively normal from a distance but when taking a closer look, it looks like he has suffered from years of starvation and malnutrition. His hands are bony and his collarbones a bit too defined.

Hakoda can’t be fully sure if he looks like a kid who has started to go without meals or a recovering famine victim. Based on his scar, a past he won’t speak about, and how much Kani and Feya clearly love him, Hakoda can only assume it is the latter.

Feya leans down, picking up both of the turtle duck toys and resting them on Lee’s stomach before Kani walks away, carrying the half asleep boy with her.

“Are either of you hungry? I have curried possum chicken.” She offers in a very ‘you can either eat that or go hungry’ tone.

Hakoda can't be sure if women in the Earth Kingdom are just different from that of the Water Tribe or if Feya is just particularly aggressive and Kani either is as well or became so when she started raising and protecting a firebender child in a country who very well may harm him.

Even though he was well aware that he would be mingling with other cultures in the Earth Kingdom when fighting abroad (even though many of those cultures would almost certainly see Hakoda and his men as nothing but backwards savages, something that had stuck pretty true in many of his encounters) after his first few encounters, he had assumed gender roles were pretty similar.

All Earth Kingdom naval fleets that he had encountered were composed entirely of men. No one had asked, but he had assumed that In the Earth Kingdom, women knew their place and men knew theirs.

The Fire Nation seems to be the only culture that doesn’t abide by that.

Feya is definitely a dominant figure. He isn’t sure if her husband is at war or if she is unmarried. Even if bright and capable, she would be a difficult woman to be married to, clearly used to being in charge with little respect or care for authority.

She also isn’t the most welcoming or hospitable person he has ever met. Far from it. She doesn’t seem like the kind of person many would want to be in a relationship with. Then again, Hakoda can’t speak for her qualities he hasn’t seen yet nor her cultural background. He still doesn’t know that much about the Earth Kingdom outside of its military and what land it takes up.

Both Bato and Hakoda accept the food that they’re offered. It must have been what Lee and Kani were cooking earlier. Which, once again, Hakoda isn’t sure if Lee participating in healing, cooking, and other chores that Hakoda would deem to be woman’s work is a personal preference or cultural from either Fire Nation or Earth Kingdom.

“Hakoda, lay on your stomach. It’s just easier for him to heal you while he has access to your chest. Don’t put pressure on your wounds.” Feya explains flatly, handing both him and Bato a bowl of curry and rice, sitting down with a bowl herself, watching him silently as he rolls back over.

It still hurts to move, but more like intense soreness and aching opposed to sharp pain shooting through his entire body. That is a lot of improvement in just a short amount of time. Even if Hakoda would have thought that healing with fire was impossible, he’ll be the first to admit that Lee is a miracle worker.

“Do you know where he learned to do that?” Bato asks after a few moments, beginning to eat the curry normally opposed to picking at it like he had at the beginning. He must have not been quite sure to expect, unsure how good of a cook Lee would be.

Feya nods once. “I do know. We’ve been asked to say that it was an invention of the Blue Spirit. The inventor is dead and the person who was closest to them and knew that they were a firebender doesn’t want to be discovered for harboring a firebender in the Earth Kingdom for decades. Anyways, all that matters to them is that this art is passed onto others. Lee had said that he could change a lot just by altering the relationship that firebenders have with their bending. Have it be seen as something constructive and gentle opposed to malicious and violent. He believes he can lead enough firebending away from the war effort if he changes how they see themselves in relation to their element and the world.”

Hakoda hadn’t even considered that something keeping firebenders so bent on destruction could be how they were taught to view themselves, their country, and their element. Their relationship to all of it skews how they interact with the world.

“Do you think that would work?” He asks, unsure if it actually would.

Unfortunately, Feya shrugs. “I really don’t know. Lee said that he was fed propaganda his entire life growing up in the Fire Nation. That the Earth Kingdom is nothing like he was told. He’s been so interested in the Water Tribe because he wanted to know what that was really like as well. Unlearn what he’s been taught. I can only assume that other Fire Nationals have skewed world views, but I have no idea if this would rectify it.”

Even if it comes from a muddled past which probably caused the boy a lot of pain, identity crisis, and confusion for the boy, Hakoda can’t help but smile the tiniest bit before taking another bite of his curry.

No matter his background, he had strived to have a more accurate and whole perspective on the world and unlearn old ways no matter how hard that must have been.

“Wait…he’s a Fire National, not a colonial?” Bato asks, picking up on Feya’s wording in a way that Hakoda hadn't.

Feya nods, answering before Hakoda can even open his mouth.

“How did he get here?” He asks quickly without thinking, curiosity getting the better of him, unsure how the kid could have made it here with an ocean separating him. He doesn’t seem to be too fond of the Fire Nation and Hakoda can only assume that the Fire Nation isn’t too fond of Lee. He can’t imagine someone bringing the kid here.

Sighing and shaking her head, Feya just shrugs. “I’m not sure. He’s never lied to us, but there are a lot of things that he just doesn’t want to talk about. That’s one of them. He just says he wants to forget his past and asks us not to press. I can only assume that he snuck onto a cargo ship or something.”

“Please don’t press him for any answers that he doesn’t want to give. He values honesty after a lifetime of lies and manipulation and won’t want to be put in a position where he feels like he needs to give an answer to be given peace. I don’t know if being forced to give an answer he isn’t ready to be being forced to lie would hurt him more. He has a lot of odd boundaries, just trust that he has a reason and don’t press. He needs it.” She continues before Hakoda or Bato can say anything else.

Hakoda just nods again, unsure what else to say to that, glancing in the direction of where Lee and Kani had disappeared to, seeing neither of them.

“I’m going to bed, is there anything else either of you need?” Feya asks flatly before Hakoda can look back at her, picking up the empty bowls from both men.

Both men decline anything. The most they may need would be blankets but both have lived in the South Pole during the harshest of winters. They can easily make it through an Earth Kingdom summer. If it weren’t for the sea breeze taking the edge off, it would definitely be far too hot.

“Hakoda, stay there. I don’t want you getting up. You’re going to hurt yourself more. Don’t undo Lee’s work. You fuck yourself up and can’t continue on with your crew, I’m going to ask my nephew to not waste his strength on you. Anyways, he needs to go home. His best friend harasses my brother-in-law every day until Lee comes home.” She threatens with a soft, not fully formed laugh hanging in her voice.

Hakoda silently agrees, unwilling to argue with this woman about anything else. Part of him is sure that she doesn’t back down unless she has been persuaded or defeated in some capacity.

Feya disappears from view, leaving the two men in the dark.

Normally, they may have made immature jokes despite being grown men, soldiers, and Hakoda being a leader and father. As long as what needed to be accomplished was done so effectively and they weren’t putting anyone at risk, they could be as childish as they pleased.

However, tonight, they both lay in silence, only exchanging a few glances before allowing sleep to take over.

It had been awhile since Zuko had slept with Kani. He’s pretty sure that the last time he did was the next few days following him losing his shit on Chen for no real reason that he can remember and then sleeping in the barn.

He doesn’t fully remember being taken away from healing the Water Tribe man, but he isn’t surprised that Kani had stopped him if he had exhausted himself that much.

He knows that the reason that she brought him into the bedroom to sleep was because Hakoda and Bato were sleeping where Zuko usually would, but he still likes being wrapped up in her arms. Feeling safe, loved, and protected.

He snuggles a little closer to her, not really caring about the heat, smiling a little to himself.

“Hey, sweetheart, how are you feeling?” Kani asks quietly, pressing a kiss to his head. He hadn’t even realized that she was awake.

“Still a little tired, but okay.” He mumbles.

“Well I’m sure you are, love. You just get some rest. Please don’t try to heal him until you feel better. I don’t want you hurting yourself. Okay?” Kani asks, cupping Zuko’s face in hers, pressing another kiss to his forehead.

“I promise.” He half sighs, closing his eyes again and holding Kani’s robes loosely in one of his hands as she gently rubs his back.

“ ‘m hungry. Can we eat something?” He asks after a moment, still not making any attempt to move away from Kani or get out of bed.

“Of course, my love. There’s some rice in the cupboard if you want to make some jook.” She offers.

Despite Zuko having been eating well and regularly for the past several months, he can still hear the relief and joy in her tone at him wanting to eat. It had taken Zuko a long time to get past his relationship with food and Kani likely remembers how horrible it had been.

Zuko certainly does. He never wants to go back to being like that. Being anything like he had when Chen first found him.

“Want me to bring you something to eat?” Kani asks after Zuko doesn’t respond. “You need to rest a bit longer?”

Zuko just grumbles something incomprehensible, unsure what he was even trying to say, holding Kani a little closer, not wanting her to go.

“Wanna stay here a bit longer before we get up?”

Zuko nods, burying his face into her chest.

Kani just holds him a little closer in response, continuing to give Zuko the affection and safety that he still almost always craves despite having both being readily available for the past year. Part of him still either isn’t used to it or worried that it might disappear without any warning after it had been denied for so much of his life.

The two stay there for about twenty minutes before Zuko’s exhaustion begins to wear off and laying here just makes him feel anxious and bored.

Once he begins moving around, Kani sits up, smiling at him affectionately, a hand still on his shoulder. “Come on, love. Let’s get you something to eat.”

Zuko nods, getting out of bed and hurrying into the living room where the two Water Tribe men were sleeping.

Hakoda is still there, appearing to still be asleep on his stomach. Bato is gone. Zuko can only assume that he had duties to attend to with his crew. Just because his friend is injured doesn’t mean he can abandon his responsibilities.

By the time that Kani gets into the kitchen, Zuko has portioned out two bowls of curry and is heating them up with his bending.

“Your aunt is rubbing off on you too much.” She grumbles, pressing a kiss to Zuko’s head as she wraps her arms around him. “I still love you even if you have no sense of when food should be eaten.” She teases, smiling at him.

“Food is food! Stop being so picky!” Feya yells from the staircase, appearing at the top a moment later, carrying a box of salve-filled bottles in her arms.

Kani grumbles something under her breath and shakes her head, not arguing with her sister any further.

“Do you want me to heat you up some curry as well?” Zuko asks Feya, looking up at her and smiling.

“I’m good, I already ate. Make sure your mother does as well.” Feya teases as she puts her box down, earning a face from Kani.

Feya walks up to him and Kani, leaning down and nuzzling Zuko’s cheek as he giggles at the contact.

“Well, I’m going to be a civil person and make some jook. If you want to eat curry, Lee, go ahead. As long as you eat, I’m happy. Go ask Hakoda if he wants the other bowl. Protein will be good for him.” Kani suggests, pressing another kiss to Zuko’s head before pulling away.

He can see Feya roll her eyes at Kani’s desire to make something separate for breakfast on the grounds that it isn’t proper breakfast food.

Zuko has never particularly cared about eating different foods at different points in the day (outside of not eating something sugary first thing in the morning), but then again, even after a year of regular meals, the luxury to be picky will still occasionally surprise him after food being used as a weapon against him for so long.

Grabbing both of the bowls and two sets of chopsticks, Zuko hurries into the other room, setting both bowls down by the unlit fireplace before kneeling on the ground and peering at Hakoda’s face, resisting the urge to poke him to wake the man up.

“Mister Hakoda? Sir?” Zuko asks in a voice just a tone below normal, unsure if the man is conscious and resting or genuinely fast asleep. Either could be possible with his injuries.

When he gets no response, Zuko rests his hand on the man’s shoulder, needing to know if he’s alright. “Sir?” He asks again a bit louder, thankfully feeling the Water Tribe man move a little.

“Everything alright, kid?” Hakoda grumbles half opening his eyes, looking at Zuko with an unfocused gaze.

“I brought you some food.” Zuko offers, pushing a bowl towards him. “I also wanted to know how you’re feeling. I can heal you more in a little.” He offers, having given up trying to hide the excitement in his voice.

Hakoda gives Zuko a small smile, taking hold of the bowl and begins eating it.

Zuko sits back down cross legged, picking up his own bowl and eating his curry, still watching the man, hoping he isn’t coming off as creepy.

“Hey, Lee, how old are you?” Hakoda eventually asks a few minutes into eating.

“I’m fourteen.” Zuko replies, ready for the man to comment on Zuko’s size or at least be surprised as he likely thought Zuko was younger. Most people do. Kani and Chen had thought he was nine or ten at thirteen. He probably looks twelve now. Maybe thirteen. He isn’t sure.

To his surprise, Hakoda just smiles at him. “You’re a bit older than my son. I think you two would get along if we lived in a different world.” He comments softly. A world where there wasn’t a war putting Hakoda an ocean between himself and his family and branding Zuko as the enemy.

Zuko just nods in response, unsure how to respond to the sentiment. “What’s the Water Tribe like? What’s it like to live there? How do you guys stay warm? I could barely stay warm here during the winter.” He asks, very unsure how someone could be tough enough to live in the snow all year long. He can’t imagine anything growing there, so he has no idea what they would even be able to eat outside of meat. Even with that, Zuko isn’t sure how many animals there are living in those harsh conditions.

Laughing, Hakoda looks up at him, giving Zuko a good-natured smile.

“Well, we live in both tents and igloos. Tents are better for storage and congregating. Keeps the wind and snow off of you but there is more room to move around and to stand up. Igloos are better for sleeping in to keep warm. We have a pit in the center for the fire which is also where cold air rests. Warm air likes to be closer to the top. The fire melts the first layer of the ice blocks while it’s going and then it refreezes when the fire goes out, providing more insulation. We then just have a good amount of furs on the ground to put a layer between us and the ice. It’s really nice.” Hakoda explains patiently, not sounding patronizing or condescending.

“We don’t have day and night through 24 hour periods like you do here, we have about six months of day and six of night. It’s beautiful when it’s night and the moon shines on the snow and lights up everything with it. When it's a new moon and the aurora isn’t out, it’s almost pitch black and you can just see outlines of large landforms. It makes you feel small but…like in a good way.” He shrugs awkwardly while speaking, smiling at Zuko.

Zuko is sure that his face is lighting up in wonder. “That sounds amazing. Do you miss it a lot? Not just that your family is there, just the place.” Zuko asks, being sure that asking if Hakoda missed his family would be a stupid question. Of course he did.

Hakoda just nods, looking almost sad and like he isn’t sure what to say or do.

“Can’t really help you get back to your family…but I can help you get back to your crew.” Zuko says softly after a moment of silence. “Want me to try and heal you a little more? Really not much more I can do.”

Thankfully, Hakoda consents to Zuko’s offer, rolling over on his back with a lot more ease than he had even just the day before. Zuko can only hope that means improvement.

Resting his hands against the Water Tribe man, Zuko once again begins to find, redirect, and strengthen any energy that he could transfer and find.

Early the next morning, Hakoda is able to rejoin his crew. He isn't back to 100%, but he can get work done, take care of himself, and at least not be a liability for about the next week or so until he finishes recovering with time.

He had explained his condition to his crew for them to make the final decision if they saw Hakoda as a liability or not.

Most of them had been content with the fact that Hakoda could clearly move around and carry things with only mild discomfort. Koaruq, on the other hand, had clapped Hakoda on the back pretty hard, watching his reaction.

When Hakoda had only winced and started hurling every obscene word and gesture at him while Koaruq just laughed, inviting Hakoda back on board.

It took Hakoda reminding himself that he is a soldier, a global leader during a war, and that Earth Kingdom civilians would only think less of Hakoda if he were to push his friend into the harbor while boarding their ship.

While getting out of the harbor and maneuvering their ship back into the wider ocean, his crew predominantly just looks over at Hakoda, watching his movements with puzzled expressions, but none say anything. It isn’t until the workload lessens as current and wind take over that the questions begin to start.

“ ‘Koda, you weren’t even able to stand on your own three days ago. How are you doing this well?” Hakoda can’t say that he is surprised that it is Koaruq who started the interrogation.

“The bender healer was able to…I’m not quite sure what they did or why it worked, but it did.” Hakoda almost refers to Lee as a ‘he’ before remembering to keep even his gender ambiguous. Lee needs to be able to hide as best he can. Hakoda can’t say that he blames the kid.

“You already told him that.” Dormaq interjects, crossing his arms and giving Hakoda an accusatory, but not quite irritated, look.

Sighing, Hakoda looks around at his crew, sure that he can’t get out of explaining this soon. He had fully intended on telling them about the Blue Spirit, it’s the least he owes the firebender. He just wanted to wait a little longer just so his crew would see that Hakoda had suffered no ailment.

On top of that, even though he knows it is incredibly unlikely, he is somewhat worried that his crew may want to turn around to try and find the firebender, not fully understanding. They didn’t see the gentle little boy who so happened to be a firebender. The kid who just wanted to help and atone for some of the sins of his country.

“I need you guys to keep an open mind about this, alright?” He warns them, knowing that he is already loading the atmosphere with that sentiment alone.

Not surprisingly, faces around him harden, most with worry the moment that he says that.

“What happened?” Koaruq prompts, expression unreadable.

“They had no intentions to bring any harm to anyone. The healer knew how to contact them relatively quickly and they came to her. It apparently isn’t uncommon for healers who somewhat know them to ask them to come help. They can strengthen and transfer energy…I’m not sure how, but they can. They’re a firebender under the alias of the Blue Spirit. They’re trying to heal people and to teach other firebenders how to use their bending for healing opposed to destruction.” Hakoda explains in an even voice, watching the expressions of his crew carefully.

One thing about Lee’s age that will protect him is that no one would suspect that he was some mystic firebender healer. Hakoda likely wouldn’t have believed it if he hadn’t seen it himself.

Hakoda had figured that he would either be met by panicked, if not aggressive, yelling about Hakoda allowing himself to be vulnerable to and be touched by a firebender while injured or stunned silence.

He is met with the latter. Likely, no one is sure what to say.

“Firebenders can heal?” Koaruq finally asks in a quiet voice, looking somewhere between surprised and confused.

“We both kind of thought the healer was fucking with us, but the Blue Spirit was helpful and non-violent, and, well, you can see for yourself how Hakoda is doing.” Bato explains with a small shrug, giving Hakoda a friendly smile.

Hakoda has to say that he is grateful that his friend was there with him to see Lee heal with bending. Not just for someone else to understand that the small boy who had the misfortune of being born a firebender wasn’t a threat in any way, but for someone else to be able to recount the events of the past few days. Remind Hakoda that he hadn’t started to lose his mind and hallucinated a firebender healer.

Not just that, but a Fire National firebender healer with a scar taking up a third of his face, hiding in the Earth Kingdom with an Earth Kingdom mother and aunt and apparently an Earth Kingdom father who apparently hadn’t been in the town.

Despite having been interacting with Lee for several days, telling him stories about the Water Tribe and what it had been like to live there, the kid’s eyes filled with wonder for the duration of every tale, no matter how mundane.

Hakoda had tried to ask the kid about the Fire Nation, but Lee had only shared a few, vague stories. Most of them were about feeding turtle ducks (the species of his weird duck toys), playing a board game that Hakoda has heard Earth Kingdom soldiers talk about but has yet to see for himself and drinking tea with his uncle, and the ocean.

Lee hadn’t talked much more about his life, stating that he only wanted to remember the good parts of his past life and those were few and far between and wasn’t willing to share too-personal stories. On top of that, Lee had explained that he only wanted to remember just enough so he wouldn’t forget about who he was and the few people he lived with back in the Fire Nation.

Other than that, he just wants his old life to fade into oblivion.

Hakoda can’t imagine anything all that much sadder. Then again, Lee’s life has been, and likely will continue to be, filled with pain. He just is in a better situation now with a family who loves and supports him as best they can.

“What else did you learn about this healer?” Dormaq finally asks, expression softening. Being one of the older members of the crew who had lived during this war for so long, who was old enough to remember the southern raiders coming, Hakoda is surprised at how calm the man looks.

“Not much.” Hakoda lies. “They’re worried that Fire Nation soldiers may identify them and come to eliminate them for acting against the Fire Nation’s interest. They’re also worried that the Earth Kingdom military will come and arrest them for just being there as a firebender even if they mean no harm. They wore a mask and gave little away about who they could be.”

How Kani and Feya explained it, that is usually how he goes about healing people while maintaining his cover.

“So at least we have one pretty powerful ashmaker actively not against us.” Someone grumbles too quietly for Hakoda to make out which member of his crew said that in the crowd.

“Don’t call them that.” He sighs before thinking it through, only able to think of the bright eyed little kid who just wanted to understand and help the world.

No one says anything to that, but Koaruq raises his eyebrows. Hakoda can’t say if he appears more confused, surprised, or judgmental.

Pinching the bridge of his nose, Hakoda closes his eyes for a moment before speaking. “I think that they were originally from the Fire Nation, not the colonies, and had said that they were fed a lot of propaganda growing up. They mostly just wanted to know about Water Tribe customs and culture as a way of unlearning a lot of what they had been taught. If they’re willing to hide while being treated like an enemy but still try to learn what the world is really like, I’m willing to try and not see every firebender in existence as the enemy and not hurl slurs at them.” He explains, not wanting to go into too much more detail. It’s hard to articulate when his crew hadn’t met Lee and seen the actual human being opposed to the firebender.

There isn’t much response to anything after that as his men look at him, clearly unsure what to say from there, a lot of mixed feelings hanging in the air after the Fire Nation had taken so much from them.

Far too much.

Pushing the thoughts of the tiny firebender with so much light in his eyes from his mind, Hakoda walks through the crowd and towards the bow of the ship. “We have a long way to travel and should do it as fast as we can. We don’t need to make a bad first impression on General Fong by being late or at least not to be the last ones there. Fire Nation isn’t the only country that looks down on us.” Hakoda reminds his crew, looking back at them.

Hakoda can feel some of the tension drop as the subject of the firebender healer is allowed to dissipate and they begin moving about more familiar tasks in territory that they know how to navigate properly.

It is far easier to push forward where the situation doesn’t contradict a large amount of what they have seen to be true for so long. What they need to do now is end this, they can see firebenders in a different light another time.

Far more innocent lives are at stake with the violence continuing.

Zuko only stays in town for two more days after he heals Hakoda.

He has a chance to visit Lo and just tell her about what had happened the past few days. He also gets to snuggle with Miyuki as she tells him stories that don’t always have a point or even a conclusion in any way.

Either way, what he mainly wants is the ability to see her again and to snuggle with Miyuki.

She makes him an assortment of teas during the few hours that he spends with her and insists that he eats several fruits that she hands him.

All of the teas are really good. They even play two games of Pai Sho together. She is the person who he had really wanted Iroh to get to meet. Unfortunately, it could have put Zuko, Iroh, and his new family in a lot of danger if anyone were to ever recognize General Iroh in the Earth Kingdom.

Once this is all over, maybe Lo and Iroh can actually meet. They can share their favorite teas and play Pai Sho. Zuko can introduce Azula to Miyuki and show her the new skills that he has learned with his bending.

He could teach her the one that is actually important and show her how to heal and help people. Then, maybe he could show her how to make shapes with her bending even if Zuko is still working out the kinks.

Considering Azula has always excelled at firebending, once she gets a hang of the basics, she will likely surpass Zuko within a few months. Without their father driving them apart with competition vital to their survival, Azula being better at something she didn’t even know about not long ago probably wouldn’t bother Zuko nearly as much as it once had.

It would just be about learning and bonding, not undermining and belittling each other. Well, Azula undermined and belittled Zuko while he would hide, hate her, and wish that he had stayed an only child.

With Azula having a chance to have a father figure who actually cares about her as a person opposed to what she can do for him, she may be a kinder person even if she and Zuko may have their differences.

With Zuko having a loving family who does everything that they can to make Zuko feel safe in his new home, he likely won’t take everything Azula says and does so personally. He probably won’t get upset at every little thing.

On top of that, they both have people who genuinely care about them who’s attention and love they don’t need to fight over. Azula has Iroh all to herself. Not that the old man isn’t mourning for or worrying about Zuko, he can focus all of his energy and attention on Azula. Zuko isn’t even there in spirit anymore to take that away from her.

Zuko has Kani and Chen to himself. Also Feya when he sees her. Even if she needs to focus on patients, she gives them care and attention in a very different way than she gives Zuko. he trusts that Kani is never going to leave him behind. She has a good home, a loving husband, and has proved time and time again that she loves Zuko just as much as she would if she had birthed him herself.

Then he has Chen who was the first man and father figure to Zuko to prove that Iroh wasn’t the exception to supportive fathers. That Zuko had just been surrounded by warlords and politicians who raised soldiers and public figures opposed to children. Iroh hadn’t been the odd, overly emotional man Zuko had been led to believe. He was just the only one who was human.

Still, to this day, the worst Chen has ever done is express irritation with Zuko. he hadn’t ever even raised his voice, let alone a hand. The man would almost always offer Zuko easy praise and affection. Reminding Zuko that he has a good, safe home now.

No matter what happens, Zuko really wants Azula to meet his new family. It will likely be years in the future when that can actually happen. At that point, he likely will feel even more secure and won’t feel jealous or threatened by Azula just because she might be getting along with the people who had saved Zuko a dozen times over.

He really wants to be able to merge his lives. Even if just a little.

With Azula, he could introduce her to his family immediately as she is in a very similar situation as Zuko. An abused child who so happens to be the daughter of the Fire Lord.

Considering Zuko already knows that Zuko’s family won’t get along with Iroh, he might really only be able to introduce his uncle to Lo. Even if she is the only person in Zuko’s new life that Iroh can bond with, it will still mean a lot. She has done so much for him and has been the inventor behind the Blue Spirit. A nonviolent entity that Zuko can hide behind while still contributing to the war effort in a way he can only pray will have some effect.

After seeing Lo, he gets a chance to see Gaon and Kya. Most of that is spent just taking care of baby Lee as the little boy shows Zuko his toys by mostly flailing them in his hand while sitting in Zuko’s lap.

He’s still less than a year old but has grown so much. Then again, he was incredibly tiny when first born. Zuko doesn’t know too much about the growth rate of babies. By the lack of concern of the couple, Zuko can only assume that this is normal.

Kya occasionally brings Zuko something that she has baked, insisting that he try some of it, asking if he had ever had it before. Most of the time, Zuko had never had what she offered.

Despite growing up in the palace, Zuko hadn’t eaten many sweets. He did when he was younger, but once food started being used as a punishment, he had completely stopped enjoying eating until a few months ago.

Even though he had plenty of opportunities to try any assortment of sweets, he would stick with basics like soup, bread, rice, vegetable, and meat. He couldn’t bring himself to eat much at meal times starting at a pretty young age, so he would eat only what he needed to so that he could ward off hunger and not make himself sick from malnutrition.

Zuko had told both Kya and Gaon that he didn’t need anything, they both insisted that he take home some baked goods that they had made, insisting that he would like them. Zuko isn’t sure if they are just generous people, if they still feel like they owe Zuko something for saving Kya and baby Lee, a mix of both, or something else entirely.

Despite having the ability to see some of the people he only gets to when in town, he isn’t surprised that it doesn’t last long. They need to get back to Chen and Zuko needs to share Fao the new baked goods and candy he had collected in town with Fao.

Zuko enjoys seeing the town and the people who live there, but he really loves being able to return home. To snuggle with Cabbage no matter how many times Chen says the animal isn’t allowed in the house, work on the farm, and play with Fao. He always misses that when he’s in town even if he’s perfectly content. It’s still an odd feeling that he is getting used to. Being completely happy and safe but still thinking about other things that make him feel the same way.

It isn’t a luxury he had back in the Fire Nation.

Once again, early in the morning, Kani and Zuko get up, grabbing their bags they had mostly packed the night before, bidding Feya farewell and heading out towards home. Even though Zuko had been referring to the farm as home for awhile, he had only started to really believe it himself in the most recent months. Believe that it is really his home that isn’t going to be taken from him.

Even as they leave town and Zuko knows he won’t see the people he cares about there for a while, he can’t help but smile as they make their way inland.
