## Chapter 30

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

I just had my last full week of classes and on Wednesday morning I'm going to go to my parent's homes and see my little kitties and give them 100 kisses which they will hate but they'll tolerate bc they want treats and my body heat.

We finally come to an event as to what people have wanted for awhile:)

### Text

Zuko’s life continues to move forward smoothly. Far smoother than he could have ever thought his life could be as the Fire Prince hiding in the Earth Kingdom with farmers. Back in the Fire Nation, he didn’t think it was possible to be this happy. He thought that he lived a good life behind the safety of the walls of the palace and more wealth than most people in the world.

All he really needed was gentle touch, encouraging words, friends, good meals, and people who he could love and trust. He couldn’t care less if he now sleeps in the corner of a small home and works in fields a good portion of the day.

The people he lives with actually cherish and protect him, making him feel like he is glowing some days with how happy it makes him.

When he has time to, he is still able to learn more about medicinal and edible plants in the area and how to use them. It’s a slow process, but he is actually learning and isn’t terrible at it.

Usually, he gets to see animals in the forest. Even if they run away from him, they’re still cute. It makes him happy just to get to see them. Some of the people who are teaching him about local flora smile and shake their heads at his childish behavior towards animals he sees, but they never say anything.

Zuko never finds out if it is because they know that he had come from an abusive home where he was never allowed to be a child, if they just know something about him is off but not dangerous and don’t question it. Or if they simply really don’t care as long as he is helpful and doesn’t get himself or anyone else hurt.

At one point, he comes across a small group of wild Earth Kingdom turtle ducks. Excitement taking over and clouding his judgment, he hurries over to them to try and hold one of the turtle ducklings following their mother or at least pet them.

However, before he could ever touch them, the mother bites his hand and ankle several times hard enough to draw blood before chasing him out of the forest, hissing and squawking at him.

He doesn’t cry even if Earth Kingdom turtle ducks have *really* sharp beaks , but it isn’t the physical pain that upsets him even if it *does* sting. He really just missed turtle ducks and the first ones that he’s seen in over a year weren’t socialized. Not just that, but they were *mean* .

Kani had to remind him that the turtle ducks in the Earth Kingdom forests are wild and are used to people hunting them; that the mother thought that Zuko was trying to hurt her babies, not that he just wanted to say hi as she cleans and bandages his hand.

Not long after that, she tells Zuko that it was a stupid thing to do and that he should never approach wild animals like that as they could be carrying some kind of disease. On top of that, the last thing he should do is approach a mother and her babies of any species. Even docile animals will attack when they feel as though their babies are being threatened.

It’s the same thing that Zuko’s own mother had said to him years ago. A promise that she would protect him at any cost as Zuko was her child and she would do anything for him.

A promise she had broken only weeks later, leaving Zuko alone with his father to endure his cruelty with no one to stop him. With all the power in the world, Ozai only had to hide physical evidence of his cruelty from the public, a task so easy to do with formal clothing and a little make up.

Unlike his birth mother, Kani has kept every single promise that she has ever made to Zuko. She has proven her love for him over and over again.

She even had insisted on monitoring his bite for a few days as the turtle duck had broken the skin and she had no idea what had been in her mouth beforehand. Thankfully, it healed relatively normally and didn’t get infected. The care that she puts into everything that she does for him is what means the most to him, necessarily or not.

The summer slowly fades into fall and the harvest begins again. This time, he is actually able to help gather vegetables opposed to just cleaning, chopping, and preserving them. Despite being able to help in other areas, he still does plenty of that.

After the harvest is fully gathered, stored, and the fields are planted with a cover crop, Zuko’s days are pretty much free. All that really needs to be done is taking care of the animals, gathering and chopping firewood, tending to the single plot of land that grows winter crops (where barely any weeds grow, thank Agni) , housework, and foraging for what he can with the others.

Luckily, with less work comes more time for him to spend with Fao and some of the other children their age in the village. He and Fao play with the others for group games, but most of the time it is just Zuko and Fao. They’re best friends, after all, and Fao actually knows Zuko’s secrets.

Well, all but two. That he is the Fire Prince and that he is the Blue Spirit. Two things he actually allowed Kani and Chen to talk him out of telling Fao opposed to running away and then telling Fao anyways.

During the first snow of the year, Zuko is in Fao’s room, showing his friend some cool new shapes he could do with his bending and shapes that he had improved on. He usually practices at night when he can’t sleep but doesn’t want to meditate. Or when Kani or Chen ask Zuko to give them a little heat and he decides to be smart about it and make a shape.

Kyira comes in without knocking to bring Fao and Zuko some warm bread and sees the decently formed dragon made of fire flying around Zuko’s hands. Unfortunately, her mom, Shi is the only adult in the house and that is who Kyira goes to with that shocking discovery before Zuko or Fao could say anything. Could even think of anything to say in Zuko’s defense.

Fortunately, Shi had been able to reassure her daughter that it is alright, believing that Zuko would have hurt Fao a long time ago if he *ever* had any intentions of doing so.

On top of that, she is well aware that there would be nothing for the Fire Nation to gain by sending a little boy into a remote Earth Kingdom farming village. She believes Zuko when he explains that he had run away after his own father had turned on him for reasons Zuko refuses to specify.

That night, Kani, Chen, Gela, Fao, Kyira, Shi, and Zuko all have dinner together, disgusting Zuko’s bending and answering questions that Kyira and Shi have that Zuko is fine with people knowing.

Well, for people who already know that he is a firebender. ‘

Things mercifully don’t change too much at first, just slight tension from Kyira and Shi. No resentment or anything, just needing that moment to accept Zuko’s bending after only knowing it as the enemy’s element their entire lives.

That disappears when Gela starts asking Zuko to reheat leftovers, heat up blankets, start fires, and maintain baking heats for her while he so happens to be over seeing Fao. He’s pretty sure that the domestic use of firebending has pushed a good deal of prejudice Shi and Kyira had for what fire bending looked like.

Even though Gela refuses to admit it, Zuko is sure that she knew what she was doing. Intentionally giving Zuko a platform to use his bending for common purposes.

Not long after that, Shi and Kyira begin to come over to ask Zuko to restart their hearth if their coal went out during the night and would bring him things to heat up when he is over at their house and talking to Fao or playing a board game with him.

As they get further into the winter, Kani and Chen once again insist on bundling Zuko up excessively even though he has already been through an Earth Kingdom winter, is healthier than last year, and can actually regulate his temperature.

His second winter is a lot more fun than his first now that he knows what to expect, he’s gained more weight which keeps him warmer and more alert, and more people know that he is a firebender. He, Fao, and Kyira build snow forts and then the siblings snuggle up against Zuko as they sit in it and Zuko radiates heat.

They stay there until Zuko begins to heat the floor of the snow fort enough to begin to soak their pants, causing them to tremble with cold, leading to a retreat back to Fao and Kyira’s house, Fao excited that Zuko can now be himself in both homes and wanting to spend more time showing Zuko his room, books, and help his moms with baking.

However, by ‘helping’ with baking, Fao means snagging anything that is left unattended on the counter and munch on it by the fireplace with Zuko and, occasionally, Kyira when she isn’t playing with her own friends.

Considering the two boys start spending more time with Fao’s sister, Zuko begins to learn how to make flowers out of fire. The only one that he is able to do somewhat well is a fire lily. He is sure that Iroh would find the notion of a fire fire lily amusing.

Considering the fact that there are very few plants to forage for in the winter months, Zuko begins to be able to memorize all of the common and relevant ones in this part of the Earth Kingdom. Sure, there are a lot more edible plants out there (few of which Zuko knows of) but edible and good are not the same thing. Eating things such as shaved pine is in the event of getting near starvation, not just putting a little extra food on the table.

Due to that, Zuko is able to go out and forage on his own, promising Kani and Chen that he would be careful.

The main reason that he goes out alone is in case he runs into other firebenders. Some that maybe he can teach healing to.

He hadn’t had any luck last year (even though he likely wouldn’t have been able to do anything anyway while surrounded with people who thought Zuko was a nonbender), but that isn’t going to stop him from still being hopeful.

Anyways, it’s easy to just throw his Blue Spirit mask into his bag. He has started making a habit of carrying it everywhere in the event that he might need it.

For over the first half of the winter, he doesn’t see a single firebender.

Surprisingly, as the weather is beginning to warm a little bit (well, slightly less cold even though Kani keeps insisting it is getting warmer) he does run into a group of soldiers consisting of maybe nine men and women sitting around a fire with a few tents set up, likely taking a day to rest after traveling for awhile. It can be hard to press on for days at a time, especially in the winter. As far as Zuko knows, there isn’t a town for days in the direction they are traveling from.

They don’t really seem too interested in Zuko, they really just tell him to go away if he doesn't want any trouble. It’s likely more that they don’t want to deal with an Earth Kingdom teenager bothering them or that they don’t want someone to think that they have any intentions of hurting some kid.

That changes when Zuko holds out his right hand and produces a small flame, eyes falling on the ground, unsure if he should accompany his bending with words.

After that, Zuko awkwardly joins them after being invited, all of them interested as to why a firebender child is living in the Earth Kingdom. They become even more surprised when they realize that Zuko is a purebred Fire National and not a colonial.

Zuko goes with the story that his father had been a high ranking military deserter. As his father had managed to evade capture, and by extension, evade punishment. That Zuko and his father were the only benders in the family and Zuko was willing to participate in an Agni Kai to fight for his family’s honor so that they all wouldn’t be banished in dishonor for his father’s crimes.

Zuko had lost (an unspoken explanation for his burn scar), but even though the terms had initially been that if Zuko lost, his family would be banished, the accuser had commended Zuko’s bravery, loyalty to his family, and honor, allowing for his family to stay in the Fire Nation if Zuko were to leave after recovering. He alone absorbing the shame that his father brought upon their family.

He explains that he had traveled, looking for work in the Earth Kingdom, not feeling like he could go to the colonies under banishment and had been taken in by a kind family. He makes it very clear that the family is well aware that Zuko is a firebender and completely accepts him as so in case these soldiers feel the need to address that with Kani and Chen, not wanting them anywhere near his family.

On top of that, he makes sure that they know that Zuko is very well loved and cared for and is in no danger at all. That really the only thing that they want from him is to help assure any soldiers that the village has never had any intentions of fighting as they would lose due to size and remote location. When the war is over, they want to lose as few people as possible and change who’s rule they are under without struggle.

As he spins the lies about his past, he is surprised at how easy they come to him. He still doesn’t *like* lying, but he can do it without feeling sick.

He isn’t sure if it is because no one has used lies to manipulate him in so long, that he knows he is only trying to protect himself and his family in this situation with the point of this entire conversation having absolutely nothing to do with his past and only his knowledge, or if he is beginning to slowly get over the idea that any form of lying, no matter for what purpose, is inherently horrible and cruel.

Eventually, he begins to tell them about the Blue Spirit.

Considering the fact that they had seen his face before he had seen them, he couldn’t exactly pull on the mask and pose as the Blue Spirit before he had even started talking to them. The moment they saw his face, it was too late for that. Despite that, he could still pass on the message.

He tells them about how the man who took him in grew dreadfully ill last spring and that a nomadic firebender healer by the alias of the Blue Spirit had saved him.

Zuko had said that he couldn’t tell the healer’s age or gender, but is able to describe what the mask looks like.

He explains that while the healer was staying with them, he had passed this art onto Zuko, asking only in return for saving Chen (although he didn’t give the soldiers Chen’s name) that Zuko would pass on this skill to other firebenders he may come across. That learning one’s true potential could help reveal their true relationship with the world.

He begins to explain all the workings of it, writing some of the instructions down on paper, informing the soldiers to first practice stoking their inner flame. Not only would it help for healing, but it would help them fend off the cold and learn how to better regulate their internal body temperature.

By the time that he finishes writing what he can down, explaining everything he can think of, and giving a few demonstrations on soldiers who had slight colds or other common ailments, the sun is low on the horizon.

By the time that he makes it back home, it is dark.

The soldiers had insisted that Zuko stay the night as it was getting dark, but Zuko had told them that his caretakers would worry about him if he were out too late and there may be a search party due to the cold. Neither Earth Kingdom peasant nor Fire Nation soldier would want to cross paths.

It had felt wrong to refer to Kani and Chen as simply his caretakers opposed to his parents, but he doesn’t want these people to think that he has moved on from the Fire Nation. They still need to think that Zuko views it as his country no matter what. That he is simply living in the Earth Kingdom out of convenience right now.

When he finally gets home, Kani is the one to scold him for staying out so late, saying how worried that she and Chen had begun to get. Unsure if Zuko had been hurt and unable to get back home in the cold, got lost, or if something terrible happened.

She just ends up nearly crushing Zuko to her chest and pressing kisses to the top of his head before Zuko can even begin to apologize.

He is able to tell Kani and Chen all about the soldiers that he had run into earlier, assuring them that they were under the impression that the Blue Spirit had simply aided Chen when ill and Zuko had learned healing as a way of thanks and to improve his own skills.

Chen tells him that it was dangerous and ill thought through about revealing that he is a firebender to random soldiers and talking about the Blue Spirit with such a distinguishable face, making Zuko promise to never do something like that again.

After that, they come up with a plan in case the worst were to happen. How they would hide Zuko and pretend as if he had never been here if anything were to happen.

Kani starts by telling Gela, Shi, Kyira, and Fao to deny that anyone who matches Zuko’s description or any firebender at all lives here or had ever lived here if anyone were to ask. They are able to spread quickly around the village that Zuko had seen someone who reminded him of his attacker and to deny that anyone matching that description had ever been here.

Thankfully, no one asks questions, believing that Zuko is just a young boy terrified that his past will come back for him.

After settling that, they began to come up with a way to hide Zuko if anyone were to come looking for him house by house.

Eventually, after trial and error, they settle on hiding Zuko in the cellar.

It is very difficult for Zuko to go down there, but eventually, Chen settles on going down with him, not feeling the need to unnecessarily traumatize Zuko any further. If anyone were to ask, Kani would just say that her husband is in town or something similar.

Anyways, Chen looks like the kind of person who would be more violent and soldiers may be more wary and even aggressive towards him where Kani appears more docile despite actually being the one who would fight if soldiers came looking for trouble.

On top of that, Kani would be able to hide the cellar door with her bending and not need to use any guess work at when the soldiers are gone if she can see what is going on above ground. Being hidden without a door gives little place for anyone to search for Zuko.

Being locked in the dark is still incredibly hard for Zuko, but it is made much easier when Chen just holds him close, rubbing his back, allowing for Zuko to hide his face in the crook of Chen’s neck.

All Zuko needs to do is stay calm and quiet. Just focusing on that with the comfort he has makes it bearable. Chen makes sure to remind him that he isn’t alone and that he’ll be able to get out soon in a hushed voice as often as possible, soothing Zuko’s fears. That he won’t be locked in here for long. That he isn’t along.

Thankfully, they never have to use it outside of practice. Staying down there while getting Zuko used to just not panicking only lasts a few minutes, calming down at that point as Chen just does what he can to comfort him.

On top of that, every time it gets a little bit easier. Not much, but he continues to make progress. His terror slowly begins to subside to anxiety.

He has Chen with him the entire time so he isn’t isolated while down there. Not only that, but every single time, as promised, Kani gets them out and pulls Zuko into her arms, pressing kisses to his face, telling him that she loves him and that she would never dream of leaving him down there, apologizing that they need to face his fears to keep him safe in the worst case scenario.

After that, the three of them will sit by the fire, sipping tea. Sometimes talking, sometimes remaining silent. Either way, they’ll enjoy each other’s company, both Kani and Chen making sure that Zuko is okay with words and by watching his body language.

Zuko has no idea if the soldiers ever passed on the art of healing or even ever used it, but no consequences come from it. He never has to be locked in the cellar for more than five minutes and doesn’t need to worry about endangering the people he cares for.

For better or for worse, he doesn’t meet any other firebenders to teach that winter. Zuko can’t help but feel disappointed at that but Kani and Chen can’t hide their relief.

The next spring is very similar to the last. They share food with neighbors and work long hours to gather what food they can, remove the cover crops, till the soil, and plant the seeds.

Once again, as soon as they finish the planting and the work begins to taper off for a little bit, Zuko and Kani travel into town to visit Feya.

Zuko is able to help make salves and do other basics when there are more people who need help. When not many are around, he is able to go down to the beach and look for shells and cool rocks (he does step in the ocean but it is far too cold to even keep his feet in for long), visits Lo, and is able to see Kya, Gaon, and baby Lee.

While at the market looking at candy to bring home, he overhears two people talking. It is the first time he has heard anyone talk about the Blue Spirit who Zuko hasn’t helped or who doesn't know his alias.

They didn’t say too much, they are really only talking about the Blue Spirit and if the other believes that a firebender healer even *could* exist to begin with, and if they do, *why* they would be helping the Earth Kingdom.

It sounds a lot more like a lot of speculation and not being sure what to believe, but it means that the word has been spreading. Sure, he is in the town where it all started, but people are talking and no one speculates it being Zuko. No one has even turned an eye towards Feya.

He buys his candy and hurries up to Lo’s, knowing that he can’t talk about it with Kani or Feya right now. Too many prying ears and he needs to tell someone that moment or he’s sure he’ll explode with excitement.

He excitedly tells Lo about it even if there isn’t much to the story. Despite that, she is happy for him and expresses that while giving Zuko a pot of water to boil for tea.

The two drink their cups of tea with Miyuki hogging Zuko’s lap for body heat as the two play a game of Pai Sho and just chat.

When Zuko finally makes it home, Kani is very irritated that Zuko came home after dark when he had said that he would only be gone an hour or two.

Feya had managed to lessen Zuko’s punishment to scrubbing out all of the cast iron pans until they left opposed to not being allowed to go out the next day on the ground that Zuko is a teenager and that’s what teenagers do.

Anyways, he had just been at Lo's greenhouse drinking tea, something neither woman needs confirmation to believe. They know Zuko well enough that he doesn’t like acting like an adult when he doesn’t need to after being forced to when so young and just wants company.

Despite still being allowed to run around town, that doesn’t stop grumbling the entire time he washes dishes, making faces at Kani as she passes him.

Kani just presses a kiss to his cheek and tells him to be more conscious of the time as it could get dangerous for him at night, clearly not feeling in the least bit bad about creating reasonable consequences. He just sticks his tongue out at her and she playfully splashes him with the dirty water, getting some in his mouth.

It is one of the few times that Zuko has heard his aunt genuinely laugh from humor. Even if he doesn’t like doing the pans, he still like the companionship that Kani and Feya offer him for the duration of his sentence, something Kani just rolls her eyes at, telling Zuko he is too into theater for describing being made to wash the grossest pans as if it is a prison sentence.

It isn’t long before they need to go back again. Even if he always misses his home in the village, he always misses town and is sad to go.

As the spring turns into summer, Fao gets good enough at the wooden swords to move onto the real ones. Unfortunately, Zuko only has one set and they’re supposed to be used in pairs. Gela fixes that, much to Shi, Kani, and Chen’s dismay, by filling two, small metal pipes with rock to approximate the weight and length of Zuko dao blades.

It isn’t exactly the same, but better than any alternative Zuko or Fao could have come up with. Anyways, even if that weren’t the case, the look on Fao’s face would have made it worth it.

A little after the summer solstice, a day Zuko is given off of work for spiritual reasons, giving him a chance to wander into the woods for meditation and prayer, growing closer to Agni and stronger in his element, Zuko discovers that his hair has grown long enough to put up again, now coming down about two inches above his shoulders.

It had been long enough to put into a Fire Nation top-knot for a while, but he couldn’t exactly do that safely. The Earth Kingdom top-knot is a lot larger and rounded, taking up the majority, if not all, of the hair on someone’s head.

Despite not usually wearing one herself, Kani helps teach Zuko how to properly put his hair up, tying it in place with a thick, green ribbon lined with yellow. It isn’t exactly the same as getting to practice his own customs from his own culture, but it’s a close enough adjacent that still allows him to live safely in the Earth Kingdom and feel some connection to what he misses about his old life.

Kani, Chen, and Fao’s moms find Zuko’s excitement and enthusiasm very amusing, but are happy for him, doing what they can to understand and support his desire to hold onto parts of a culture that had harmed, rejected, and abandoned him.

It’s hard to explain why he still feels attachment to parts of his culture, but thankfully, no one demands an explanation from him. He is assured that as long as no one is getting hurt or put in danger and it makes him happy, he doesn’t owe them anything.

As the seasons begin to turn again, Zuko and Fao spend more time in the woods before the harvest begins, looking at the brilliant colors in wonder. Despite seeing them last year, that had been the very first time that Zuko had seen autumn leaves like this before coming to the Earth Kingdom. Even the second time, he still isn’t used to the brilliant colors. Nothing like this ever happened in the Fire Nation.

He is able to take in the landscape more this time. It helps that he isn’t trying to take in everything at once, that he can see out of his left eye, and he isn’t busy launching his anxiety through the roof.

As the weather continues to grow cold and the harvest approaches, Feya comes up again to help them. On the first night, she presents Zuko with a third, bigger turtle duck, but this one is filled with lavender to help him sleep and calm him down if he is to ever need it. Warming it up with his hands would help enhance the smell.

Chen just grumbles about how Feya is giving Zuko enough turtle ducks to start a crochet farm of his own. Feya simply ignores him, pressing a kiss against Zuko’s temple.

He knows that most kids his age wouldn’t want their family members to be this affectionate with them at fifteen, but most kids his age had a family to smother them with affection when they were little and needed it. Zuko had his mother, but that could only go so far. She was just his safe haven in the dark, terrible world shadowed and controlled by his father even before that man stole the role of Fire Lord.

Anyways, if he gets too many turtle ducks out of this, he’d let Feya smother him even if he hadn’t been deprived of affection for most of his life.

While the four of them are cleaning and canning vegetables (Zuko having now figured out the perfect temperature and force to hold the lids making the process exceedingly faster without the need for wax and boiled water), Feya hands a rolled up piece of paper to Zuko, smiling at him somewhat deviously.

It takes a second for Zuko to realize what he’s looking at, but his face lights up when he does.

There is a drawing approximating the Blue Spirit mask along with a description referring to him as a defector and attempting to leverage the Fire Lord’s power.

He can’t help but feel happier when he realizes that the bounty is only if he (or his body) were to be turned into the Fire Nation, not the Earth Kingdom. He isn’t sure if that means that the Earth Kingdom considered him an allie, but at the very least, it means that they don’t see him as a big enough foe to be hunting down, firebender or not.

Feya explains (at least from what she has heard from travelers passing through) that there have been reports that firebenders have begun to be able to heal their injured comrades more effectively in larger amount as the skill of healing, along with the rumor of the Blue Spirit, began to be passed around incredibly quickly and individuals began to refine the skill in their own way.

At first, many high ranking officials in the Fire Nation had taken it as some kind of sign that the path that they are on is a righteous one and that their success is inevitable with not only the strength and destruction that fire can bring but also holds the power to mitigate the number of their fellow soldiers to fall.

However, as trained soldiers began to learn to heal more people and come to the understanding of what it takes to heal something opposed to breaking it, a larger and larger number don’t want to fight.

Not only that they didn’t want to see their friends fall to war, but not wanting to be responsible for cutting others down others, now that they have been presented with the opportunity and need to spend time with the aftermath of battle on people who they know and care about. Not just see the fallen bodies of strangers who they have made out to be their enemy.

This had really started when a Fire Nation soldier had healed an Earth Kingdom soldier who he thought to be too young to be fighting in this war and couldn’t bear to see die. Feya admits that there are stories that the soldier was executed, arrested, or defected before he could face the consequences. She has heard all three.

All she knows is that this war had nothing to do with sharing the Fire Nation’s greatness and bringing order and prosperity to the world but rather the desire to have control and nearly limitless power over the world that the Fire Nation would willingly sacrifice their own for no reason other than to promote that ideology.

That is what led to more defectors and people refusing to fight, finally understanding that they mean nothing to their superiors and that they will continue to mean nothing even after this war.

By the time that officials no longer wanted this new subelement being passed around, it had already reached the mainland in large enough quantity that it couldn’t be stopped without the appearance of inhibiting power of the nation so those in positions of power wouldn’t need to worry about their hold of control on the world and on their country.

Enlistment has gone down considerably, prisons holding war prisoners aren’t as secure, some even rumored to have guards just allowing prisoners to escape. Not that they help prisoners, but that more and more don’t stop them from doing so if they cause enough trouble and make it far enough as more and more Fire Nation soldiers are thrown into these prisons for refusing to fight or trying to leave.

Feya can’t confirm that as true, it’s just what she’s heard.

On top of that, where desertion isn’t particularly high, infighting and arrests have grown rapidly as soldiers and officers fight over ideology.

Even if that still means people are getting hurt, it means there are less soldiers marching in on the Earth Kingdom. It’s diverting energy from the war effort even if the majority still stand where they had before.

Both Kani and Chen are happy for Zuko that what he has been striving for is working, however, both are reasonably concerned.

Zuko had *wanted* to hang his ‘wanted’ poster on the wall but Chen shuts that down before Zuko can even finish asking.

They question him as to why he is so happy about a wanted poster if he was already succeeding at his real goal.

Zuko expresses that it feels nice to be wanted.

Kani immediately shoots back that not when it was by the law. Well…more so than he already would be if the wrong person were to find out who he is.

What really does matter is that learning how to change the relationship of firebending to firebenders is beginning to change loyalties and world views. Even if there are only a relatively small amount so far, it is enough to create a stir in the order that the Fire Nation has created.

Unfortunately, Zuko is forbidden from telling Fao about this and from healing as the blue spirit close to home. Someone may be able to recognize Zuko, or at least trace some of this back to him. If he wants to heal someone, they’ll need to be quite a ways from the village or in Lo’s greenhouse as there are many random people who come through to see her.

Anyways, very few would want to deal with arresting a crazy old lady who seems to understand nothing but plants and her cat. She likely wouldn’t be seen as worth the trouble after going on a third tangent about her cat’s personality to the Fire Nation soldiers trying to arrest her.

Under other circumstances, Zuko might be upset, but he can’t help but grin. Whether this puts him in danger or not, he’s getting to play his role in changing the world.

It isn’t until mid spring that Zuko gets a chance to travel into town again. The times when he and Kani are pretty consistent, but it always feels longer between visits than it really is.

The first three days that he is there go about the same as they have the last several times that he has been here. Even if it's repetitive, he still enjoys it.

He helps Feya, visits Kya, Gaon, and baby Lee, sees Lo, and wanders around town when he isn’t needed.

The first indication of change is while he is walking along the edge of the cliffs overlooking the ocean, taking in the view while eating a stick of butterscotch candy, some large, fluffy creature *flies* through the air, landing near the town.

He isn’t able to get down to the beach in time before the creature and the people with it are gone, but he does hear the rumors. That is what confirms that not only his life, but the world is beginning to face change. Feya had heard whispers of this rumor lately, but she nor Zuko have ever dared to believe it, sure that it is people grasping at the frayed edges of what is left of hope as the Fire Nation continues to take over land even if progress has been hindered lately by internal factors.

For the first time, he hears whispers about the Avatar that isn’t just false hope of someone who saw something in the distance that they couldn’t quite explain. People talking about how this rumored possibility had just been standing among them moments ago as if they weren’t the symbol and force of hope that the world has been waiting for the past century.

Zuko can’t even begin to figure out how to perceive that. It’s far too much to even begin to make something of that.

Traveling hasn’t been nearly as smooth as Aang had even dared to hope in a possibility with more complications. So much has gone wrong and everywhere they go, Zhao has left destruction behind them in attempts to capture Aang and possibly even deter his hope as he sees the world crumble around him. Sees that everywhere he goes, the people he tries to help suffer just for existing in the vicinity of Aang.

Sokka has tried his best to cheer Aang up with some success. He jokes about Zhao’s horrible, nearly freakish sideburns (something Aang can’t understand why the man thinks looks good to that extent) and the fact that a grown man has actually *growled* at them on more than one occasion while wildly throwing fire at them with seemingly no control.

Even Aang has to admit that the man is a freak even though he doesn’t usually try to insult people. Zhao is chasing them around the world with the strongest military in the world to back him. Having a twelve year old insult him isn’t going to destroy the man and he has worse coming.

Aang, Sokka, and Katara are three kids who have pretty much no experience with the world. Neither Sokka nor Katara have ever left the South Pole even if they understand the politics and history of the war. Aang traveled the world a lot before, but nothing is the same, it is a whole new world. The world he understood and the life that he had is gone. Barely a memory written in the dust left behind for a century of neglect.

The life he had, along with just about everyone and everything he knew and loved, that he lost and allowed to crumble from the selfish desire to not be separated from Gyatso is gone with not even the most foolish man’s hope of return.

If Aang had just left and trained elsewhere, he would have actually been able to see Gyatso again even if it was years in between. He wouldn’t have lost everything else.

So many others wouldn’t have lost far too many loved ones, land, and culture.

The world would have still had a fourth nation opposed to an individual to carry on the entirety of it from nothing but a failure and a distant memory.

Aang could possibly have done something to stop this if he had just played his part and just hadn’t refused to put aside his own desires for a few years, putting a stop to Sozin before he could do something truly irreversible, things would be so much different.

Just because the fisherman was a jerk doesn’t mean that he’s wrong. It hurts, but maybe it’s something that Aang needed to hear.

Sokka had left with the fisherman despite Aang pleading with him not to. It was less about Aang’s personal feelings towards the man and more about the sinking feeling that something was going to go horribly wrong. Sokka had only brushed it off as superstition and ‘avatar junk’.

Katara had done everything that she could to try and cheer Aang up while they were in the cave together, and that had worked pretty well. Or at least until the storm started picking up and all he could think about is his dream and losing the last few people he has.

Katara had only been able to think of Sokka’s wellbeing, worried that she would lose her brother. One of the dwindling members of her family, her tribe, and her culture that she has left in this world.

At least they were on the same page as to what needed to be done even if it meant people being in danger.

Fortunately, both the fisherman and Sokka were returned safely to shore, relatively unharmed. Unfortunately, the next day, Sokka is running a fever and is so delusional that he thinks that he’s an earthbender.

If it weren’t for both siblings getting sick with an illness that Aang has no idea the severity or duration of, it might be funny. They can laugh at that and mock Sokka when the siblings are back to full health. Only when Aang is sure they both will be okay.

Thankfully, it is pretty easy to locate a nearby herbalist who, at the very least, could offer some advice on how to care for Sokka and Katara and make sure they don’t get worse. Maybe she could also tell them where he could bring them for treatment. However, ideally, she would know what’s wrong and tell Aang exactly what to do.

The sky threatens another day of bad weather, but at least not as bad as yesterday. Reluctantly, Aang leaves his glider behind, sprinting down the winding trails built into the cliffs on the edge of the town. He’s surprised that people decided to settle here in such large numbers, but it’s nice and it works. On top of that, earthbenders are probably responsible for a lot of the planning, engineering, and maintenance, making this layout easier to stay.

He’s always enjoyed being an airbender, but when he needs speed and can’t fly, he’s even more grateful for the extra speed that it gives him when he can use the wind to his advantage.

Soon enough, he reaches the top of a tall, grassy hill with three, circular buildings on the top. He can’t imagine why an herbalist would choose to build up here considering the people coming here would be sick or injured and might not be able to make it up here. However, he isn’t here to give architectural advice.

He runs into the nearest one, looking around quickly.

It’s a greenhouse filled with a wide variety of plants in full bloom despite it only being spring. “Hello?” He calls, still looking around.

The first person he sees is a boy about Sokka’s age crouching near one of the trees, petting a large, white cat who is purring loudly.

He looks up, meeting Aang’s gaze, pulling the cat into his arms and halfway raising a hand as a friendly gesture.

Aang can’t help but immediately notice the large scar taking up an enormous portion of his face. He tries not to stare, sure that the boy is sick of attention being drawn to something that Aang can only assume is a terrible memory burned into his flesh, but eyes still fall on the distinctive mark all the same. It’s impossible to simply look over.

“My friends are sick. They have really high fevers and one of them is completely delusional and I don’t know what to do. One was caught out in the storm yesterday and the other got sick from him.” He explains quickly.

The boy turns around, looking towards the back of the greenhouse. “Lo! Someone needs your help.” He calls, voice unusually raspy, especially for someone his age.

Aang had *thought* that it would be odd for a boy clearly under the age of 18 to be an herbalist, but he’s seen stranger and has no intentions of making assumptions that may slow him down. He wouldn’t want to offend the boy if he took it personally.

An old woman with her hair up high and a stick through it walks towards him, smiling and resting her hand on the boy’s shoulder. Aang can’t help but wonder if he is her grandson.

“Lee, can you get me a plum blossom for me?” She asks, taking the cat from Lee’s arms and walking towards the table, resting the cat down before mixing various ingredients into a mortar, humming softly as the cat rubs against her arm.

Lee comes back, holding the flower out to Lo who mashes it in with the rest of the ingredients.

“Thanks for the cure!” Aang says quickly, impatience getting the better of him as he tries to grab the mortar from Lo.

“What do you think you’re doing?” She snaps, swatting Aang’s hand with a spoon and taking it back.

“Uh…taking the cure to my friends?” He isn’t quite sure what else to say to that.

Lo starts laughing and Aang can’t help but really wonder if she has completely lost it. “Oh, no, this is Miyuki’s dinner. Plum blossom is her favorite. What your friends need are some frozen frogs from the river and then suck on them.” She explains with a wide smile.

“Suck on them?” He asks, disgusted, not wanting to do that to either of his friends.

Thankfully, Lee must have seen his dislike of that idea and speaks up. “My aunt is a healer…she’s close by.” He offers, voice quiet.

Aang lets out a breath of relief at the knowledge that he won’t need to make his friends suck on frozen frogs while sick. “I’ll be able to bring them down on Appa. I’ll meet you back here in fifteen minutes.” He says quickly, rushing out the door before Lee can even respond, valuing his friend’s wellbeing over his manners. He can apologize to Lee for being rude *after* Sokka and Katara are getting treatment.

He can see Lee watching him run from the greenhouse out of the corner of his eye but keeps running forward but the boy is quickly out of Aang’s sight and barely on his mind as he rushes back towards the cave to get Sokka and Katara as fast as possible, using every advantage that he has.

He isn’t even over the crest of the hiss when arrows pin him to the ground by his pants.

He is able to free himself just in time the first time, but despite his agility, arrows keep flying at him, snagging at his clothing and sinking into trees or the dirt, slowing him down significantly.

He tries to ditch the archers in any and every way possible. He jumps off a high cliff, using his bending to slow him down, thinking that his pursuers won't be able to get down in time to see which way Aang goes, but they use arrows on rope to swing down, landing with nearly impossible grace and precision.

He tries losing them in the forest, throwing up mud, leaves, and branches to evade them, but arrows keep flying at him with accuracy that shouldn’t be possible for anyone of any nation or any element to succeed at. His only thought for how he could possibly escape these people is to run and try and get them to run out of arrows, then he might have a chance to get away from them. Unfortunately, he has no idea how many arrows they carry and what their protocol for running out of arrows is.

However, no matter what Aang thinks, it keeps happening. Denying it won’t stop the archers from gaining on him.

Arrows keep flying at him until all four limbs are pinned and he is surrounded.

## Chapter 31

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Next week will be our last chapter of this section of the story before we actually dive into the actual adventures with the Gaang with a mentally healthier Zuko who isn't wanting his heatless father to love him.

Also, if this chapter seems like it has less typos and generally bad writing, that is because for this chapter, Periphyton reviewed and did a really good job on it. i will need to edit some of the other chapters as many of them were written on mobile in the car, in my tent, or during my lunch break in the dirt.

### Text

By the time that Zuko manages to get anywhere near the archers, they’re already swinging off of a high cliff from ropes attached to arrows with agility that Zuko can’t imagine to be possible even as he watches them do so right in front of him.

The kid, the fucking *Avatar* , can believably make that jump. He has the tattoos of an airbending master and can almost certainly maneuver himself down to the ground quickly and safely.

However, the archers, likely the Yuyan archers (he can’t imagine anyone else having that much skill) aren’t even benders. Even if some of them are, he doesn’t think that they are using it.

To be sure of that, he would need to touch their skin, feel their breath, or look into their eyes to have any idea, none of which he is able or willing to do.

By the time that he makes his way down the cliff, the archers already have the avatar in shackles. His arms are bound behind him and then to his sides so he can’t fight. It’s likely hard for him to even move especially when being held above the ground. His only free appendages swing uselessly in the air.

Zuko silently watches the group, turning his good side towards them, trying to find an opening to do *anything* . Maybe he could at least give the Avatar a chance to run. His legs are free. Even if he can’t do much, he can at least run. Someone in town could help get the shackles off. There are a few blacksmiths that could at the very least do that. Even if the person the Avatar went to get aid from has hard feelings towards the Avatar after his disappearance, they have harder feelings towards the Fire Nation. After all, the enemy of their enemy is their friend.

If nothing else, he could at least try and figure out where they’re going. Wherever it is it will be an ideal environment for a firebender, and they won’t be expecting another firebender to attack them. Not in their own territory. Even if deserter numbers have been growing, they’re just that: deserters. Not the type to be expected to come back and attack their former allies.

Anyone who has defected from the Fire Nation military is brave. Anyone who comes back to attack out of nothing but spite is stupid. Zuko knows that plenty of people in his life have called his actions stupid. In this instance: they’re right. But something’s got to give, there has to be something he can do.

Unfortunately, nothing gives.

As the group moves out, the Avatar continues struggling pretty successfully for a kid half their size and a third their weight. Instead of doing more to bind him, a man in a Fire Nation military uniform walks in front of the Avatar, hitting his head hard enough to make Zuko flinch. He stays still, forcing himself to remain quiet in the shadows of the trees, sure that the archers are skilled in tracking and situational awareness.

The man starts talking, and Zuko is sure that his voice sounds familiar, leaning a little closer to try and get a look at his face.All he needs to see is the cruel glint in the man’s golden eyes and the horrible sideburns to compensate for his hairline, which only brings more attention to both attributes in the worst way.

Zhao hadn’t really been a big part of Zuko’s life growing up, but he had been in and out of the palace. He stood out to Zuko because of how self righteous the man has always been, and how once Zhao realized that Ozai couldn’t care less about Zuko, he had always treated him cruelly.

Fortunately, either no one notices Zuko’s presence or no one cares if they are aware that an Earth Kingdom child can see them. It is almost certainly the former. Zuko is well aware that the Yuyan archers are known for their accuracy, not their mercy. They wouldn’t leave a witness alive, child or not. Zuko follows behind them as they walk away as silently as possible, keeping a good distance. He is grateful that it is windy out to cover the sound of his footsteps on the dry leaves. He wouldn’t be able to stay silent on a still night no matter how light he stepped.

Thankfully, the group moves at a quick pace. He can’t sleep even if they stop which will only keep him up longer, making him weaker and slower. He won’t have any idea if they move out while he is out and even worse: they could find him.He doubts that they would hesitate to injure, arrest, or even kill an Earth Kingdom child they found following them.

Zuko is thankful now more than ever that Kani has insisted that Zuko bring his dao blades wherever he goes. It gives him the opportunity to defend himself without using bending. He really isn’t sure which will be better as of now. He’ll need to see where they go.

It’s nightfall by the time that they reach a Fire Nation base that is close enough to the town that Zuko wonders how he didn’t know about it sooner. He is fairly certain that people would have discussed it more often or would have at least *mentioned* it. He watches as the archers bring the Avatar into the base surrounded by and almost certainly filled with far too many soldiers.

He can’t go in there with his face showing. Someone is bound to recognize him. Zhao will almost certainly recognize him if he gets a good look at Zuko’s face. The man had been present for Zuko’s Agni Kai, cheering as Zuko blacked out from pain and the inability to breath despite gasping. Zhao should have an idea as to what Zuko’s scar looks like.

Zuko has grown and looks different from when Zhao last saw him, but even if Zhao is a despicable man who always seemed really creepy, he isn’t stupid and is incredibly observant. He’ll likely be able to recognize some of Zuko’s features from when he was thirteen. Pairing that with the shape, placement, and size of his scar along with firebender eyes, it won’t take too much mulling over for Zhao to realize who had come to free the Avatar from the base. Then it would be but a matter of days before Ozai would learn that his despised son is alive. Only so long before he would come to rip everything that Zuko had come to know and love away from him all over again.

Zuko is well aware that as soon as he steps out of the safe little part of the world that he has been living in and steps back into the pain, fear, and suffering that was his previous one, it will only be a matter of time before someone recognizes him. That his father still learns that Zuko is alive and well. That his father will send someone after him to take everything that has made Zuko feel so safe and happy for so long. He needs to prolong that for as long as possible. He can’t just announce the fact that he is alive and is standing against his father. That he is standing with the Avatar. He needs to deter his father from discovering his well being for as long as possible.

He isn't sure what he can do. He really doesn’t want to step out of the first place that he has ever felt safe in his life. He can’t risk destroying that and going back to how his life used to be for so unbearably long. Unfortunately, the life he has now might not exist for all that much longer if the Avatar, the world’s last true source of hope, is to spend the rest of his life locked under the ground guarded by hundreds of soldiers. Even if he doesn’t want to admit it, the influence of the Blue Spirit will only go so far. A large sum of firebenders have stopped fighting, defected, or even gone as far as to turn against the Fire Nation troops, but it isn’t enough. It will never be enough. It’s not that rebranding firebending isn’t isn’t important, it’s just that it’s too little too late.Far too many still stand for the Fire Nation and his influence came too late. It came when the Fire Nation already had the world wrapped in its clutches and now all it needs to do is squeeze hard enough to turn it to dust. To destroy and dominate it completely.

That won’t take too much longer.

Slipping off his bag, Zuko begins to look through it, trying to find anything that could help disguise him. He has his Blue Spirit mask, but that really could destroy the message that he’s worked so hard to create. Destroy the symbol of peace and healing that his alias is supposed to stand for.Even though Zuko has no intentions of severely hurting, let alone killing, anyone in the base, he is both a widely respected and hated symbol depending on who is asked, both of whom have strong opinions. He worries that many people who look up to that are risking if not sacrificing a lot and may easily be swayed back if they feel as though the Blue Spirit isn’t what they thought. Even if he were to only leave a couple of cuts and bruises on a handful soldiers that were easily treatable,, within a month the story would be about how the Blue Spirit had decapitated, maimed, and beaten everyone that he could get his hands on with no rhyme or reason. Without understanding the meaning of mercy, let alone justice.

It could destroy everything that this symbol has already created for so many people. It could undo the beginnings of change.

Taking a deep breath, he takes his Earth Kingdom style top-knot out, braiding his hair back and tying it with the green ribbon. He then begins to change into black clothing, shoving his Earth Kingdom robes into his bag. He can’t attribute this infiltration and attack on this base to the Earth Kingdom. He can’t let the people, *his* people, suffer for his actions. The Fire Nation might blame the town for what happens here and march on them, leveling it.Where the people could hold their own against a ship of soldiers even if the damage would be devastating, they would be wiped off the face of the earth with at least a Fire Nation battalion if not a brigade. He isn’t sure how many soldiers are inside the base, but from what he can see from here, there are already far too many.

Whatever he does, he needs to be sneaky. He can’t take all of these people out. By the time he could take out a small group, the rest would be coming to his location to neutralize him. With that in mind, he rips some fabric, cutting holes out so that he can see as best he can with what he has before wrapping it around his face, obscuring his features just enough so that onlookers will only be able to identify a young, firebender male. He is sure that he looks incredibly stupid, but that isn’t the point. All that matters is that his face can’t be seen. Taking a deep breath, Zuko sets his bag by a tree, straps his swords to his back, and begins to make his way towards the base.

He circles the base a few times before finding a storm drain.Wrapping his hands around both ends of one of the bars, he heats the metal for as long as he can, weakening it before wrapping cloth around his foot to dampen the sound, stomping on it several times, wishing he could use his swords without making noise.

Even if Ozai destroyed Zuko’s self-esteem and overall mental health, took away just about everything that he loved, smothered his hope and joy for so long, and overall just made Zuko’s life miserable, he *did* make sure that Zuko knew how to use every bit of his weight, strength, and momentum to his advantage. Right now, that’s what he needs. He can’t undo a lifetime of cruelty and terror, but he can at least use what he’s learned to do something good for once. The best thing that Zuko can do with that training is use it against his father.

The bar begins to give and he grabs it before it can hit the ground, surprised that his reflexes are still this intact after years of only practicing his firebending when no one was looking and when he had the time. He still of course practiced with his swords with Fao, but it wasn’t the same as training back in Caldera. Silently slipping down into the shaft, he through the tunnel, glancing up whenever he has a chance to try and figure out where he is. He needs to at least have an idea what area he may be in, needing to try and find the Avatar as soon as possible. He needs to get him out of there before something irreversible is done to the kid, security gets tighter, or someone discovers Zuko.After about two hours of wandering through tunnels and marking walls and corners to figure out how to leave as quickly as possible, he’s pretty sure he is close. As soon as Zuko liberates the kid, the entire base will sweep every corner of this place until they find the Avatar.

Both of them need to already be on their way out before someone notices that the kid is gone. They need to be out before guards have swarmed every inch of this place, making it impossible for anyone to get in or out without detection. Even between the Avatar and a skilled firebender, they might not be able to fight their way out of an armed force like this.

As soon as the hallway is clear, Zuko pulls himself up, hurrying through the hallways, keeping his footsteps light and keeping in the shadows. It takes him a little bit to figure out where exactly they are keeping the Avatar, listening to conversations from metal beams and pipes that he jumps to on the ceiling when he hears someone coming.

He wishes that he could just stay up there the whole time and find his way around. Unfortunately, it would take far too long and likely draw attention to his presence. If he is detected before he is even able to free the Avatar, that’s it.Even if Zuko isn’t able to make it out of here, the Avatar has to. The world needs that kid far more than it needs Zuko.

Zuko thinks of his father to keep on going. He reminds himself of an uncaring man who would only shake his head in disappointment if Zuko were to die on a failed mission of his own design. He would simply be irritated that his son is too much of a failure to even complete a simple search and rescue mission with someone who should easily be able to help Zuko find his way safely out. That is what keeps the fear away. Keeps him from turning back and going back to his safe, comfortable life with people who love and cherish him.

He can’t let himself think about how his real family would react to Zuko’s death.

He forces himself to think of Ozai’s uncaring demeanor to obscure the vision of Kani and Chen holding each other, grieving for the loss of their child. Likely having a traditional Earth Kingdom ceremony to celebrate his life even if they couldn’t recover his body. They might possibly even try their best to approximate what they know about Fire Nation funerals with only the few who knew about Zuko’s heritage.

He does what he can to push out the image of Fao still coming to check if Zuko were home, living in denial of his absence even though he is old enough to have understood the concept of death for years. He would likely do that until he could no longer lie to himself. Zuko has never seen his friend truly upset enough to grieve, and he has no idea how the other boy would truly react.

He can easily picture Feya going about her day normally just in more silence than normal. Once alone, she may allow herself to scream or cry. He can’t be sure. He can even imagine her giving two of Zuko’s turtle ducks to Kani and Chen, keeping the third as a keepsake.

Then again, he knows that she had once been married but has never seen any trace of her husband in her home. She may burn everything that reminds her of her nephew and try to push forward, shouldering more grief.

It doesn’t work entirely, but drowning out his family's imagined grief with Ozai’s indifference at least helps Zuko keep focused on his task, helping him to continue to push forward.

It is surprisingly easy to lure the guards away from the door, but that certainly isn’t going to be the hardest part. The hard part is going to be getting out of here in one piece. The moment that one of the guards gets someone’s attention or someone notices that the Avatar is gone, they’re in for it. He even apologizes to the soldiers he had bound to the walls, promising that he doesn’t want to hurt or kill them as he slips past them, walking into a large room with the airbender standing in the center of it.

The kid has his arms and legs bound apart with chains in a position that doesn’t look painful but can’t be particularly comfortable. He walks forward, drawing his swords and raising them.

The Avatar begins to protest, likely thinking that Zuko is about to use his swords to hurt him opposed to free him.

In other circumstances, Zuko would assure the kid that he has no intentions of hurting him, but right now they don’t have enough time. The airbender turns his head and closes his eyes as Zuko brings his swords down, cutting through the chains holding the Avatar’s hands and feet. He’s grateful now more than ever that Fao had pestered Zuko to teach him how to sword fight. Zuko’s aim would have been off if it weren’t for the years of maintaining balance, aim, and grip, even if his actual battle skills may be somewhat rusty.

“Wow, you’re *really* strong.” The Avatar comments, grinning up at him. “My name’s Aang, what’s yours?” He continues, voice too loud.

Zuko grabs Aang’s arm, pulling him forward for a moment, indicating that they need to go *now* before letting go and hurrying out the door. Thankfully, the Avatar follows close behind him, at least understanding the importance and severity of the situation to a degree. They are able to make their way halfway to the grate that Zuko came up from when Zuko can hear voices behind them. They haven’t gotten nearly as far as Zuko had reasonably hoped that they would, but further than he thought they would. Unfortunately, Aang tries to take the lead of this operation even though he seems to have no clue about what he is doing.

Fortunately, none of the soldiers have any idea how to fight an airbender as it hasn’t been a bending form for nearly 100 years. Very few people alive have ever met an airbender, let alone fought one. So it's easy for Aang to throw soldiers back away from them and deflect flame. Unfortunately, they can’t get back into the drainage system without being seen. If they get caught in the maze of tunnels, they will have no way of fighting back when cornered.

They make it out into the open ground surrounded by walls with a lot of Zuko keeping fire away from them, aiming near soldiers to just get them away, and Aang moving them up and forward with relative ease. Zuko still isn’t fully sure how they make it out of the base, but in a haze of dust and fire, Aang pretty much carries Zuko to the tree line, feet barely touching the ground, partially sure that the airbender might rip his arm off with the force and speed that they are going at, only able to get away with the cover of dust hiding their direction.

Aang barely gives Zuko a chance to grab his bag as they continue to hurry through the woods, maneuvering through the uneven, hazardous terrain as quickly as they can, not losing time to look back to see if they’re being followed. It’s not like there is much they can do to make a difference and lose them.

Zuko used to be able to run incredibly far and fast. Cardio endurance had been one of the many things that Ozai had demanded from his children. One of the many things that Azula had surpassed Zuko in incredibly quickly.

He’s still been very active during the last three years, but not in the same way. He’s used to running very fast through the woods with Fao, chasing Cabbage or other farm animals to get them back home, or running out to grab something from the garden after the sun goes down, not wanting to be caught in the dark for longer than necessary. But running around at home isn’t the same as training, running for miles in the Fire Nation heat in an allotted amount of time, and now he is struggling to stay anywhere near Aang when once it would have been a lot easier with much less effort.

“Aang…they’re gone.” Zuko manages to say between breaths as the first rays of gray light begin to make their way through the foliage. Zuko slows down but doesn’t stop, knowing they need to continue covering ground to make good time. At least walking is a bit easier and will at least allow for him to catch his breath before they need to start climbing up the steeper slopes leading towards town.

Mercifully, Aang begins to slow down, giving Zuko a chance to catch up to the airbender, pulling his mask off and stuffing it into his bag and pulling out the cloth that was tying his hair back, not having the energy to put it in a top-knot. Aang grins at him, not seeming to be at all phased by physical exertion he just accomplished, but then again, Zuko isn’t sure how airbenders can use their element to their advantage besides a few his uncle had talked about. Apparently running inhumanly fast is one advantage airbending gives them.

“You’re Lee, from the healing hut with the crazy lady, right?” Aang asks.

Zuko can’t remember sharing his name with Aang, but Lo may have mentioned it. Anyway, it’s good that Aang knows his safe name. The one he doesn’t need to worry about how he heard it and from whom. The one that he doesn't need to figure out what he intends to do with. He nods once in response, his breathing becoming more regular as they continue to walk.

“If you don’t mind me asking…why are you living in the Earth Kingdom as a firebender?” Aang asks. It’s a completely reasonable question even if it does come off as somewhat loaded.

Before Zuko can start to answer, Aang continues talking. “I mean, not that you *can’t* , I think it’s cool you’re living here and am glad you were there, but I’ve only gotten to know a few different people from the Earth Kingdom and most of them *really* don’t like firebenders and don’t really care who they are.”

The Avatar is certainly right there. There are people Zuko has seen that he is almost sure who would turn him in without a second thought if they were to discover his element. It wouldn’t matter if it were now or when Zuko was thirteen, they wouldn’t care about how young he is. They wouldn’t care that he has been learning and spreading ways to heal with fire, wouldn’t care that he wants to war over too, or that he has Earth Kingdom parents. They wouldn’t even care that he had a burn covering a third of his face.

All the wrong person would see is an ashmaker.

“I had to run from the Fire Nation. Someone powerful wanted me dead. A really nice couple took me in when I was thirteen and took care of me. Most people think that I’m an Earth Kingdom nonbender who was attacked by a soldier and came to live with my aunt and uncle for safety.” He explains quickly, unsure what else to say.

“Do you like it here?” Aang asks, sounding like he wants to ignore the fact that Zuko is wanted in the Fire Nation and was likely attacked by his own people.

Zuko nods again, smiling a little. “It’s beautiful. I live in a village about a day outside of town. My family has been really good to me and I have good friends in both places. My best friend lives in the village, though,” he answers, picking up his pace a little.

“You’re the Avatar, right?” Zuko asks, knowing the answer but also wanting the confirmation. He also doesn’t really want to talk too much about himself so he doesn’t give Aang a chance to ask more questions.

“Yeah, I’m on my way to the Northern Water Tribe to learn waterbending with my friends. I need to learn the other three elements and defeat the Fire Lord by the end of next summer,” Aang explains. He looks at Zuko as he says that, likely implying that he also needs a firebender teacher, which is going to be the hardest one to find.

“Come on, we need to get your friends help before they get worse.” Zuko deflects, not able to talk about this yet. He would need to talk to Kani before Aang begins to outright ask Zuko to teach him.

Thankfully, Aang allows for Zuko to brush off his request this time. He really needs to get home before the airbender gets impatient and starts wanting an actual answer.

It takes about another hour and a half to get up to the caves where Aang had left Sokka and Katara. Fortunately, they aren’t too much worse. Unfortunately, they aren’t doing any better either.

Sokka is giggling to himself and Katara is talking to Momo, saying incomprehensible words while making hand gestures at the lemur as if trying to communicate with him. Aang can’t be sure if it is out of desperation or delusion.

Turning to Lee, he is about to ask his possibly new friend to help him move Sokka and Katara so that they can begin to make their way toward the healer.

Before he can say anything, the firebender walks forward, kneeling in front of Sokka, resting a hand on his friend’s stomach, breathing and moving his hands in silence. Fire dances on Lee’s lips as he holds his head high, likely trying to avoid burning Sokka with his eyes closed.

After a few minutes, Sokka’s gaze begins to focus and his gibberish becomes a little more cohesive. Aang isn’t sure what Lee is doing, but it seems to be helping Sokka at least a little bit. Smiling, Aang begins walking forward to check on his friend and to ask Lee what he did when Sokka jabs Lee in the eye with his middle finger, feeling for his boomerang laying close to him on Appa’s side.

“Ow. Fuck.” Lee grumbles, rubbing at his bad…well good…or the eye that Sokka jabbed that isn’t…well, likely blind.

“Katara! Momo! Katara! We’re under attack!” Sokka yells in a voice that isn’t exactly scared, maybe more confused, surprised, and irritated more than anything else. Then again, his friend has been delirious for the last day and a half and still likely has no idea what's going on.

“Hey, Sokka, calm down, it’s alright, this is Lee, he’s my friend.” Aang explains quickly, trying to defuse the situation, not exactly wanting to call Lee a ‘good firebender’ within his earshot, unsure if it may offend him, implying that the default for firebenders is bad, evil, or dangerous. He has no idea what kinds of things Lee has seen and heard while hiding in the Earth Kingdom, hiding something this personal about himself, and has no idea what would upset him.

When Aang looked at him, implying that Lee could teach him firebending, the older boy seemed hesitant about the idea even if not expressing that directly. Offending him would only hinder any progress that he could make with convincing Lee to come with them. It may be hard considering how happy he sounded when talking about his family and overall life here even if he almost certainly faces oppression at every turn.

Sokka just grumbles something, laying back down against Appa, seeming unhappy with the situation but at least he isn’t trying to throw his boomerang at Lee or cause any trouble. Once he’s better and has a clear mind, he is sure that Aang can explain the situation to him and his friend will move on to trying to befriend the firebender through bad jokes and generally antagonizing him.

By the time that Aang has finished with Sokka, Lee has already rested his hands on Katara, doing whatever he had to Sokka to her as well.

Aang rests his hand on Katara’s, lightly holding it. He can justify it by saying that he wants to make sure that Katara doesn’t attack Lee as well in a daze of confusion by offering her familiar touch, but he really just wants to hold Katara’s hand. If it so happens to be that it helps his rescuer not get jabbed in the eye again, win-win.

“I’m sorry about Sokka, he’s impulsive and delusional. You’ll have a chance to drag an apology out of him personally when he’s doing better.” Aang assures the firebender, grinning.

“Stuff like that’s happened before. It’s alright. I got used to it.” Lee replies softly as he pulls away from Katara, standing up. Aang has no idea what to say to that.

Instead, Aang and Lee help the siblings up. Aang tells Lee to help Sokka, justifying it that Sokka is at least aware that Lee isn’t a threat and won’t do anything else to attack him, especially now that Aang is with them. He doesn’t add that he wants to help Katara and that she is the one who Lee should watch out for when she’s angry or scared. *Especially* when she’s angry. There is no deterring her there. He genuinely thought that she may have killed Jet when she thought that he had killed her brother if Sokka hadn’t shown up when he did.

“What did you do?” Aang asks as they help the siblings onto Appa’s saddle.

Shrugging, Lee looks down at his lap. “I learned how to heal with my firebending a few years ago. I’ve been getting better at it. I can do more now and it takes less energy. That was to just hold them in check until we get them to a proper healer. Moving them could make them worse in that condition. Don’t have enough strength to heal them fully right now.” He responds, his emotions difficult to read. Aang can’t be sure if Lee doesn’t like talking, is still shaken up from the fight, or is just bad around new people.

“Anyways, my mom is already likely worried sick about me. I was supposed to be home before the sun went down. I stayed late at Lo’s and then was out all night with you. If I come back home half conscious from expending energy while this close to home, she’ll have my head.” Lee adds, a breath of fond laughter in his voice.

As Appa takes off, Lee directs them towards his aunt’s healing hut. Thankfully, it doesn’t take too long to get there..

Sokka begins sitting up, somewhat leaning against Lee for support, still likely weak from his illness.

“What do you want?” Lee grumbles, still annoyed by Sokka jabbing him in the eye after Lee had helped him. Aang can’t help but feel sad that that wasn’t the first time that Lee had been attacked when trying to help someone just because they could see he was a firebender, not able to understand that he could be kind and caring, not just calloused and cruel.

Sokka begins cracking up again and Lee just frowns, looking at him with mild irritation.

As Lee begins to turn his head, Sokka pokes the scar tissue around Lee’s left eye, cracking up more as Lee silently swats his hand away. Aang wants to tackle Sokka to the ground to get him to stop messing with the first, and possibly only, firebender who may be willing to teach Aang. Not only in fighting, but *healing* .

On Kyoshi island, he heard some people share that urban legend of the Blue Spirit that had been floating around. None of them seemed to believe that there was such a thing as a firebender using their bending for healing, roaming the Earth Kingdom and teaching other firebenders the gentle touch of fire, but it was interesting to hear all the same.

Aang thought it was a cool story, but sided with the girls, also believing that it was nothing more than urban legend.

Despite how impossible it may seem, *someone* had to have taught Lee how to do that. Even if all of the story isn’t true, that likely means that there is someone out there teaching firebenders how to heal. Lee does live in the perfect place to make use of a skill like that being related to a healer and all.

Sokka chuckles again like someone had told a particularly funny joke before poking the scar around Lee’s eye again.

Thankfully, Lee doesn’t really do anything to actually retaliate, just gently pushes Sokka back onto the saddle, easily keeping him there with one hand on his chest in Sokka’s weakened state.

“I’m sorry about him, he’s like the annoying older brother. In Katara’s case, that is *actually* what he is. He’s usually annoying, just less so, but he can be smart and really helpful when he wants to be.” Aang tries to make Sokka sound more tolerable and make Lee understand that he has good qualities too, not wanting Sokka being annoying to be the reason Lee refuses to come and train him.

Finally they land in a small, stone clearing, just big enough for Appa to comfortably land in and carefully remove Sokka and Katara from his back.

It doesn’t take long to get the siblings off of the bison and into the building right next to the clearing, walking into a long room lined with tables and shelves lined with herbs, jars, pots, bandages and other things that would be expected of a healer’s home. There are beds on the other side of the room for patients.

Before Lee can even set Sokka down on a bed, a tall woman with dark brown hair tied in an Earth Kingdom style top-knot, dark skin, dark, piercing green eyes, and a menacing stride walks towards them, grabbing Lee’s upper arm, appearing to be angry. Aang can’t help but worry that she may have discovered Lee’s heritage and that he may be in danger until she starts speaking.

“Where have you *been* ? Your mother and I have been worried sick about you. Go upstairs, get something to eat, make sure your mother knows you’re still alive, and get comfortable because you’re not going anywhere for awhile young man.” She nearly snaps, gaze hard.

Aang takes Sokka from Lee and helps his friend onto one of the beds as the woman pulls Lee into her arms as the firebender begins to apologize in a voice that almost sounds to be on the edge of tears.

“We thought they found you. Thought they took you.” The woman breathes into Lee’s hair, likely not meant for Aang to hear. He isn’t sure if she thought that he couldn't hear her, or if she is just so preoccupied with Lee that she forgot about him entirely.

“Go up and see your mother and beg for her forgiveness. Are you alright? Are you hurt? Do you need anything?” She asks, appearing worried as they pull away from the embrace, cupping one of Lee’s cheeks in her hand and smiling at him sadly.

“I’m alright, Feya. Just need to eat something and get some rest. After I make things right with Kani, I’ll explain everything. I promise I wasn’t just being stupid and inconsiderate. They need help. They also know about my bending.” He says quietly before disappearing through a door, footsteps disappearing.

Aang looks over at the Earth Kingdom woman, genuinely unsure what to say or even to expect. She seems to love and care about Lee, meaning that he isn’t in danger, but she seems to have a temper. His only guess is that this is Lee’s aunt, he had mentioned that his aunt is in charge of the healing hut. The main thing that is putting Aang off from thinking that she is a healer is her clear violent tendencies that she hasn’t even tried to hide.

“Um…ma’am, Lee saved my life, I’m sorry I kept him out late, but my friends are sick. Lee made them a little better but they’re still bad. The herbalist said that I should have them suck on frogs, which I didn’t want to make them do unless they really have to.” Aang explains, bowing to the woman with what he is pretty sure is the traditional Earth Kingdom bow.
