Thankfully, the woman smiles a little, a ghost of humor passing over her expression. “Lo has always had effective but interesting methods.” She comments, walking over to Katara, opening one of her eyes, examining it quietly before doing the same to Sokka.

“No blue tinge, your friends should be fine, pretty common illness this time of year. I’ll be able to make a tea that isn’t exactly good by far more pleasant to drink than frog slime for them. That and some rest should have them back on their feet in two days.”

Aang lets out a sigh of relief for her being more friendly than he thought she may be, Katara and Sokka will be fine, and that he doesn’t need to give his friends frogs.

“Are you Lee’s aunt?” Aang asks as Feya puts water on to boil and puts herbs into a diffuser. “He mentioned that his aunt lives here.”

Feya turns to look at Aang, nodding once. “Yes, I am. What was my nephew saving you from that kept him out so late?” She asks, pouring cups, helping Sokka and Katara into sitting positions and handing them cups. Aang is surprised that Sokka doesn’t pour the liquid all over himself.

“I was captured by Zhao and some Fire Nation military personnel, he broke into the military base and saved me.” Aang explains quickly, very grateful that Zhao hadn’t gotten a chance to start whatever he meant by keeping him just barely alive. If that man knows anything, it’s cruelty.

Feya stares at him in silence for a moment, Aang beginning to think that she didn’t believe him. Thankfully, her reasoning is a lot more valid than Aang had feared. He was unsure if there were any mixed feelings about Lee being a firebender even if she cares for him.

“Lee broke into a military base? Why that little…” She grumbles more to herself, words turning into incomprehensible grumbling. “He’s an idiot. Can’t let him do anything by himself. Dumbass.”

Aang can’t help but wonder if Lee has done something like this before, putting himself in danger to help someone else, based on Feya's reaction.

He begins to open his mouth to say something when Feya cuts him off with a look. “You’re the Avatar, aren’t you? Those are airbender tattoos, right?” She asks, nodding towards Aang’s head.

Aang just nods in response, smiling.

“Keep Lee’s bending quiet. We’ll talk when your friends actually know what’s going on. That will likely be later today. Please don’t press him for or about anything, no one can know about him. We have no idea how the wrong person may react.” She says harshly, with a sad look on her face. Aang can’t help but notice that she is incredibly observant, calm, and composed with everything even if she chooses to strike fear into the hearts of others, her demeanor is cold and calm, not how he would usually expect someone filled with rage to react.

“I promise, ma’am, I won’t breathe a word about him.” He replies, bowing to her. “It’s the very least that I owe him. I’ll make sure that my friends know they can’t ask anything about him until you say otherwise.” He means it. The last thing he would want to do is thank Lee by having Earth Kingdom soldiers appear at his doorstep and drag him off somewhere that he may never see his family again.

Feya doesn’t respond, but seems to be relieved even if she doesn’t say so before disappearing up the stairs.

The day passes slowly which, for the first time in a while, Aang is grateful for.

Luckily, where Feya’s healing hut is placed, there is enough space for Appa to comfortably lay in, napping and eating grass. At first, Aang is worried that Appa will be lonely considering he needs to be around Sokka and Katara, because he’s worried that they are too sick to understand that they can’t say anything about Lee being a firebender. One of them may even directly ask ‘where’s the firebender?’ That would raise concern.

Even if they didn’t get a good look at Lee, Sokka had definitely noticed Lee’s scar as he seemed to enjoy poking it and laughing at it for some reason, Aang still doesn't know why. If either of them describes the firebender as a young man with a large scar over the left side of his face, it will undeniably lead people to Lee.

That guilt dissipates as the nearby children come closer, wanting to see the Avatar’s bison. Aang is happy to tell them what Appa doesn’t like and how to play with him nicely. Thankfully, no one wants to anger a ten ton bison, herbivore or not, and just climb on his back, petting his head or snuggling up on one of his many legs, giving him the company and attention that he needs while spending his well earned day lounging around in the sun.

More healers begin to come into the healing hut after the sun has risen and all of them seem very nice and knowledgeable. Different women will make fresh cups of tea, bringing them to Sokka and Katara and bringing all three of them soup as the day continues. Feya comes down a few times, assisting with patients, citing her absence as ‘family trouble’. Luckily, the others hadn’t pushed for more details, understanding that Lee is a teenage boy and is at that age where he makes stupid decisions. This isn’t even the first time Feya has had to take time off because her beloved nephew was a bit of a dumbass sometimes. Everyone knows that the toughest healer in the town has exactly one soft spot: her nephew. Nobody wants to take the brunt of her wrath when she’s feeling particularly protective of him.

As the day continues, Sokka and Katara get more conversational and aware of their surroundings even if they are too weak to travel. They both ask about Lee, but Aang quickly shuts them down before anyone can hear them, promising that they can talk to Lee and his family directly when given a chance.

In the evening, Feya invites the three upstairs for dinner and Aang hopes that he can finally have a chance to talk to Lee when they aren’t running for their lives, exhausted, or dealing with sick Water Tribe siblings.

When they get upstairs, Feya hands the three bowls of spicy bean chili before beckoning further into the apartment.

When they get into the living room, Lee is sitting in the living room by the fireplace leaning against a woman who looks a lot like Feya but taller, tanner, older, and stronger. He can only assume that she is Lee’s mother, Kani, is what he’s pretty sure Feya had called her. Momo is sitting curled up on Lee’s lap, holding something about half his size in his little lemur arms. Aang hadn’t even known Momo had been up here. He thought Momo was with Appa or was just entertaining himself. Momo usually wanders for an hour or so at a time, exploring the area.

“Thank you again, Lee. Sorry Sokka poked you.” Aang says, sitting on the ground in front of Lee. Sokka and Katara sit a little further away but still close enough to not appear rude. They are sitting down more out of exhaustion than any desire to be social.

He wishes that the two would get that Lee isn’t presenting the slightest sliver of a threat. Then again, Aang’s first introduction to him was Lee heroically saving him from an armed base while putting his own life on the line. Sokka and Katara’s introduction to Lee was him breathing fire in their face while they were half conscious and nearing death. That was pretty scary, even if he was only helping them with no intentions of harm. Hopefully seeing Lee in such a domestic situation with a loving Earth Kingdom family will make a good enough second impression to make them change their minds about him even if their view had been concocted while delirious.

“I’m glad you’re alright.” Lee says softly to them, and then turns back to his mother. “I’m sorry for scaring you so badly, mom, I couldn’t let them hurt him.” He snuggles a little closer to the Earth Kingdom woman and Aang is surprised that Lee is so willing to show affection towards his adoptive mother in front of strangers, especially at his age.

“Why are you in the Earth Kingdom? Aren't you like…ya know?” Sokka asks, making fwooshing sounds while punching his fists, likely mimicking firebending. Katara just looks like she wants to lock her brother’s head in a block of ice, or at least throttle him.

“I spoke out against the war back in the Fire Nation and was burned and banished. If they ever find out that I survived and am living here, I really don’t know what they’ll do to me.” Lee responds softly. It is definitely a much sadder version of the story that Lee had shared briefly with Aang as to his situation.

“Did I poke your scar earlier?” Sokka asks, and Aang really wants to tell his friend to shut up and stop making this more awkward than it already is. Even if Lee has helped them and been friendly, he’s still a stranger. If Aang even wants a chance for Lee to teach him firebending, to leave his home and come with them, Sokka really needs to stop saying and doing dumb shit like this.

Thankfully, Lee smiles a little when he nods. “Yeah, poked my good eye too and wanted this guy to attack me.” He scratches Momo behind the ear while talking as the lemur purrs at the affection.

“Will you teach me firebending?” Aang blurts out as Sokka begins to open his mouth again, before his friend can say anything. It’s not what Aang had intended to say. But the words just slipped out; it was on his mind so much of the day.

Instead of saying anything, Lee looks down, still petting Momo as Kani rests a hand on her child’s shoulder, giving him an encouraging smile. “It’s alright, love. Say and do what you want. I promise it’s alright.” She assures him even if Aang can see the pang of sadness behind her expression at the thought of Lee leaving.

“We have until the end of next summer to defeat the Fire Lord…you’ll be gone for a little over one year, then we can make sure you get back home. I know it’s a lot to ask, It’s just…” He trails off, unsure how to say ‘most firebenders are out to kill me’ without making it sound like ‘most firebenders are evil’ and offending one of his few chances of having a teacher.

“I’m one of the only firebenders who won’t attack you. I know.” Lee says quietly, looking down as Momo chitters, letting go of the toy and jumping from Lee’s lap onto his shoulder.

“Aang said that you’re a healer. We heard a little bit about the Blue Spirit on Kyoshi Island…do you have any idea where we could find them? Or what they look like besides the mask? Assuming that’s who taught you.” Katara asks, setting her empty bowl of chili down, leaning against the wall for support but appearing more poised and attentive.

Lee is silent for a moment, looking over at his mother who presses a kiss to his forehead, giving him another encouraging smile.

With that, Lee grabs his bag that he had in the forest after rescuing Aang, digging through it before pulling out a mask that looks pretty close to the descriptions that Aang has heard about the Blue Spirit, sliding it across the floor to Katara.

“Did you beat ‘em up and steal it from him?” Sokka jokes as Momo runs over, trying to eat Sokka’s chili.

Katara just glares at her brother, elbowing him hard.

“The herbalist’s late wife invented it. Lo let me borrow her notes and shared what she had seen her wife do when alive. Lo didn’t want me to credit her for it, worried for her safety if it were ever discovered that she was harboring a firebender for decades.” Lee explains.

“Wait, so *you’re* the Blue Spirit?” Aang asks to make sure that is what Lee is saying, and he’s not hearing things.

Lee nods, setting the toy Momo had been playing with in his lap, touching the creature’s head with his pointer finger.

“I’m sorry, I know it’s a lot to ask for you to leave your home and your family to face the Fire Nation again, but *please* . I need someone to teach me and I’ve already seen that you can handle yourself well in a fight. Sokka is the closest we have to a trained fighter even if he’s never really fought anyone, and he’s more of the plan guy.” Aang explains. Even if Lee were a nonbender he would be incredibly helpful. He is skilled with his swords and incredibly agile.

“Hey! I’m the fiercest warrior in my village!” Sokka retorts, sticking his tongue out at Aang, clearly having given up on fighting Momo for his chili and is sharing it with the lemur.

“You’re the *only* warrior in our village, Sokka, Zhao took you down in two seconds without his bending when you tried to attack him and you aren’t even that good at catching fish.” Katara laughs, teasing her brother. “Also, you’ve already resigned your spoils to Momo who you failed to catch and eat.”

The conversation between the two consists mainly of sibling bickering and then further devolving into petty name calling within less than a minute.

Aang just ignores them, looking back at Lee. “Please…we don’t have much time. A comet will give the Fire Nation the ability to win the war and I don’t know what will happen. I know that’s what happened when…when the war started.” Aang whispers, thinking about the air temples filled with nothing but bones, scorch marks, the shadows of those who once lived there long ago, and the echo of screams still ringing in the walls as if they had been embedded in the very rock holding the structures together.

“I’m sorry for what you lost.” Lee says with real sympathy in his voice. “I want…I don’t know. I know everything I’ve found here will be destroyed, just…I’m not sure that I’m the kind of person that you guys would want in your group.” Lee finally says, giving more of a straight answer than he has so far. He’s been jumping around these questions the entire time as if not sure what they would think about the real answer.

“If this is about Sokka attacking you or just either of us not reacting well when we first saw you, we were pretty out of it and most of the firebenders we’ve seen were trying to kill us.” Katara assures Lee, giving him a friendly smile. “I’m sure he really just thought that you were going to attack him. Get to know him and he’s tolerable and won’t do anything like that again just because you’re a firebender.”

Thankfully, Sokka doesn’t say anything to combat Katara’s statement, mostly because he’s too busy keeping Momo’s paws out of his mouth.

“No, no, it’s nothing like that. It’s not even that I’m from the actual Fire Nation and not the colonies. I’m from…from a very high ranking family who is very personally involved in the war. My father burned me and tried to kill me, and thinks that I’m dead. All because I spoke out against some plans for the war the first time I was allowed in the war room. Once it’s out that I’m not actually dead, it will put more of a target on your back.” Lee says sadly, leaning against his mother to counter the bad memories associated with his admittance of his past.

“Lee…” Aang begins, really unsure what to say to that. He can’t exactly say that he doesn’t care who Lee is related to, even if it will put him in more danger. The issue is that Lee can’t exactly hide in the crowd. He has an unmistakable face with the scar covering so much of it. He also can’t just leave it at that and go. No matter who Lee is, they *need* him. Not learning firebending will prove far more dangerous than traveling with any ex-noble imaginable.

“Zuko.” Zuko corrects, briefly making eye contact. “Zuko is my real name. Too distinct to go by here.”

“Zuko.” Aang repeats, looking at the older the boy, the name sounding somewhat familiar, but not enough to place it anywhere. “Who exactly *are* you related to? I understand that going with us is putting you in danger, but like you said, if the Fire Nation invades during the comet, they’ll destroy what you have here. If we know who to hide you from we might be able to keep you hidden for a little longer,” Aang suggests.

“Ozai.” Zuko admits just above a whisper, going back to petting his toy critter. “He’s my father.”

“Is that a joke?” Sokka asks after a solid moment of silence, looking at the firebender.

Even though Aang believed Zuko as soon as he had said it, he is still surprised as the firebender shakes his head, denying any falsehood of the statement.

“Well then you can teach Aang firebending and tell us what to look out for and maybe even have some insider tips about how to take down your dad. Anyways, if it comes to it, you probably know your way around the Fire Nation pretty well and know a whole lot more about the local culture than any of us do.” Sokka continues, finally adding something helpful to this whole situation.

At this point, Aang has come to learn that Sokka can really only make things better or make them worse, and can't really keep the situation at a homeostasis. Thankfully, from the small smile on Zuko’s expression, he is at least making some headway with the firebender.

“I…I need to talk to my family.” Zuko finally says. “My dad isn’t even here…he’s back home, I wouldn’t even be able to say goodbye to him if I leave now.”

“We’re not talking about…crazy evil dad…right?” Sokka asks, appearing confused.

Zuko shakes his head. “No, I’m talking about Chen. He’s the one who found me and took me in. He’s been more of a father to me than the one who was supposed to be.”

“How far away does he live? You said that you live about a day from town. Is that by foot?” Aang asks, remembering their conversation from earlier when they were walking back from the base.

“By ostrich horse. It’s all day. We get up early and make it here a little before sunset.” Kani corrects Aang.

Aang is glad that Zuko has a kind, loving family in the Earth Kingdom. Unfortunately, it means that he will be less likely to leave. He really does seem to be nearly attached to his mother. Most kids his age or even younger wouldn’t allow either parent to hold them like that for so long, especially in front of others.

“We could probably make that on Appa in just a few hours. We’ve gone further out of our way for less. I need to learn firebending and you really might be my only chance to do that.”

After what feels like an eternity, Zuko finally nods, a simple gesture that fills Aang with relief. “Okay…I’ll come.”

### End Notes

#### Chapter End Notes

I have gotten some wonderful suggestions for what the next part of this should be called and I am always open to more suggestions. If anyone has anything for series, I would love to hear that as well!!

## Chapter 32

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

I'm sorry that this is a day late, I had finals and finished it later than expected and my beta had important family and celebration things. This is going to be the last chapter of this part. I am going to post a summary of this story at the very end of this at the same time that I start the second part of this, so stay tuned for that.

### Text

While Zuko was in the apartment with Kani, she had started by reprimanding Zuko for his actions, putting himself in danger like that. She told him how worried she had been, scared that the wrong person had found out about him and turned him in. That he had been dragged off to an Earth Kingdom prison and that she would never see him again.

It’s a relief that for the first time in his life he doesn’t feel terror as an authority figure expresses clear dismay over his actions in any way. Back in the Fire Nation, Ozai’s disappointment was never just verbal blows; physical violence always followed. For the first several months with Kani and Chen, Zuko was still terrified, expecting everything to change over a mistake or misunderstanding. Even after he settled into his new life and knew that he would never be beaten, banished, or starved for his failures, Zuko had still been very careful, never doing anything to genuinely upset his parents. The most they ever did to punish him was make him clean out all the stalls for coming home after dark or something similar.

Now, he just feels shame instead of fear, and above all else: overwhelming sadness as Kani expresses how upset she is with him and how horribly he had scared her. How she hadn’t been able to sleep and had spent so much of the night walking every path to Lo’s and asking anyone she saw if they knew where her son was, panic growing in her heart as his disappearance got longer and longer.

Zuko spent the first hour apologizing over and over again for scaring her so horribly as Kani reprimanded him for his actions. It didn’t take long before she simply held him in her arms, softly crying, reiterating how much she loves him and how it would shatter her heart if she were to ever lose him.

Once she had calmed down and was just holding him close, running her fingers through his hair, Zuko was finally able to tell Kani about the Avatar. Tell her that he was pretty sure that Aang wants him to leave his home to teach him firebending, and he genuinely doesn’t know what to do and is more confused and scared than he has been in a long time. That he doesn’t know if he will be of more aid or danger and if he can even bring himself to leave his safe haven, no matter how selfish it may sound. Now that he finally has a place to call home he wants to hold onto it as tight as he can, terrified that it will dissipate as soon as it slips from his grip, never to be seen again.

They had talked about the possibilities for a while, interrupted only when Feya came back up followed by the flying lemur. As soon as Momo saw Zuko, he jumped in his lap, turned around three times to get comfortable, and fell asleep, chittering while settling down and closing his little eyes.The fact that the Avatar has a large, friendly, fluffy creature and a small, snuggly creature are definite pulls that make Zuko want to go. Even if he doesn't have the comfort of home while away, he would have companions when he couldn’t be around people who weren’t Kani, Chen, Feya, and Fao.

Feya is the one to flat out say that she thinks Zuko should go. She is the one who always knows how to tell Zuko what he doesn’t want to hear without hurting him too badly. Zuko wishes he had her confidence, because she always knows what she needs to do and isn’t afraid to step forward. She isn’t preoccupied with what is to come as so many others are. She understands how to think in the moment, not dwell on the past, and think rationally as to what she needs to do in that moment. It provides an opportunity for her to provide counsel for others.

Kani reassures Zuko over and over again that no one else could make this big of a decision for him and that she would support whatever he chose, loving him all the same. But they both know that if he didn’t go, everything very well may be destroyed if they couldn’t have a fully realized Avatar to defeat the Fire Lord. Despite her reassurances, she can’t hide that she would be worried sick the entire time that something would happen to him. It was clear that she didn’t know what Zuko should do either. That if they switched places, she would be just as lost and confused as him, not sure what to do next no matter how high the stakes are with the Fire Nation's forces creeping closer and closer every day.

Thankfully they have Feya, who has always been good with using logic. For her, emotions are just one thing to consider, and she doesn’t let it rule her thinking, something either her sister or brother-in-law seem to be well versed in if at all. She is the one who makes it clear to Zuko that it genuinely was his decision and that they would neither blame him nor take it personally. They know he has a bigger destiny to fulfill than being a small town healer’s assistant, a farmer’s son, or even the shadow of an urban legend slowly changing a century’s worth of thinking. However, she offered him a legitimate option.

She convinces Zuko and Kani to not take just their council on this issue. She convinces Zuko to look at the Avatar and his friends for guidance in this decision. They know more about what they are up against and how Zuko’s life will change than kani, Feya, or Zuko could ever guess. She is also the one who had assured Zuko that even if it may hurt Chen, he wouldn’t be personally offended if Zuko has to leave right away and may not get a chance to say goodbye. That he would still think of Zuko as his son and invite him back home after the war. That they would be a family again no matter how long Zuko was away.

Thankfully, Sokka, the boy who had tried to poke Zuko’s eyes out, proved that he did indeed have a brain cell to spare, and told him that there was no way he was leaving without saying a proper goodbye to his dad. He explained that traveling with a sky bison meant they could do so much more than if they only had feet or ostrich horses, so it wouldn’t take a lot of time for a quick trip back home to see his dad one last time before setting out. They could spend the night here and leave first thing tomorrow.

Zuko had to smile at the fact that even if they may not know each other and that Zuko is from a nation and family that has caused Sokka and the others so much pain, they are willing to reach out compassion towards him. Not only did they care about Zuko’s wellbeing and happiness but were willing to go somewhat out of their way to provide that for him. It had definitely been one of the things that made him feel more confident about his decision to go.

It had been a surprisingly short conversation with far less emotion than Zuko had feared. He had thought that he would need to take long breaks, forcing himself not to cry at the idea of leaving his family behind. Leaving the best thing that has ever happened to him and going into a war zone to face the man who had destroyed Zuko’s face, hope, heart, and soul. But while talking with his family and Aang and the Water Tribe siblings, Zuko didn’t feel an oppressive fear nearly suffocating him as he spoke. He genuinely felt like when he returned home, he would be welcomed back with open arms. He isn’t terrified that he will return home to find that his family has found a replacement child who wouldn’t be such a disappointment to them, like Azula had replaced him in Ozai’s eyes. He wouldn’t come back to find Kani and Chen and Feya just gone, or that leaving Zuko the moment they have a chance to, like his first mother did. He genuinely trusts them to keep their word and be there for him no matter what.

On top of that, Aang convinced Zuko to go with them a lot easier than Zuko would have ever expected. Maybe Feya had done something to sway Zuko before the Avatar even came up to practically beg Zuko to join him. Maybe Zuko already knew what he had to do long before Aang even opened his mouth, and he just needed a little time to get over the residual fear of abandonment that left him unable to move forward in the world no matter how desperately Zuko knew that he needed to.

After Aang had managed to convince Zuko to come with them, Feya had set the three up by the hearth where Zuko usually slept, making sure that they were comfortable and less accessible than they would have been downstairs as if forgetting that the kid’s ten ton bison was outside, unable to be hidden. However, Zuko had been pretty sure that Feya had done it as an excuse to drag Zuko into bed with them even if it was too small to sleep three grown people comfortably, despite Zuko still being particularly skinny. Even if he was a bit squished, he loved the feeling of his mother’s and aunt’s arms wrapped around him, memorizing the feeling of their gentle embraces, knowing that it would be the last time in a long time that he would feel it. He had forced himself not to think about how it could be the last time ever if things were to go badly. That would only lead him down a dark path with no actual purpose.

Despite everything that had been on his mind, he had managed to find sleep while tucked between two of the people who he has sought so much comfort from the past few years. Who he would likely always think of in times of need whether that be courage, strength, or peace.

It’s hard to say goodbye to Kani and Feya. He feels like he had the first few weeks with Kani and Chen, when he and Kani had been nearly inseparable. He would clutch at her robes to try and stop her from leaving him even if she were only going across the room. Back then he had to pry his fingers from Kani’s clothing to allow her to walk away from him even if she were to remain in sight. But now it isn’t about the all-consuming feeling of terror that had defined him when Chen first picked him up in that storm. It is about…well he isn’t sure *exactly* what it is about, but the child who had been left by his mother and never allowed to be a child doesn’t want to be separated from his new mother no matter the reason. From the woman who had chosen Zuko against all odds and freely chose to love him, as opposed to being forced to have him, and loving him when he was her only option for any form of genuine human connection. Kani had not left her son suffering alone when he needed someone there for him. He still didn’t know why Ursa had left him to suffer at the hands of a man who she knew would do nothing but torment and abuse him.

It’s hard to pack up his life to leave with Aang, even if he does it every time he travels between town and the village. He’s less possessive about his things than he was before, but he still doesn't like to leave parts of him behind to be snatched away like everything else from his life before had been. He only has a few things anyway, and the only luxury items that he carries with him are his three crochet turtle ducks.

Perhaps the difficulty of packing this time is that he knows that every other piece of home will be left behind. Everything that he has used to repair the cracks and missing pieces of his soul is in the people and the land he will be leaving. Despite having a stable image of himself and trusting that his family won’t leave, he still feels like the moment that he steps away from everything, the fillings will fall loose and crumble, no longer holding him together. Leaving nothing but the broken boy who had come crawling to Chen’s feet, begging for help, or the mercy of a quick kill.

He packs his smallest turtle duck, the first one that Feya had made for him, not really caring if the other made fun of him for sleeping with a stuffed animal at sixteen. He wants to bring all three of them, but he knows that it isn’t practical and he doesn’t want to risk losing them. He wants to continue sleeping with them even after the war whether he is in the Earth Kingdom or Fire Nation. On top of that, if he only takes one, Kani can take one home to remind herself and Chen of Zuko for the next year and Feya can keep one here.

It gets easier as the things he packs have less personal meaning to him. The things that he has finally come to understand are communal and won’t be snatched away from him or he’ll be deprived for fun or out of pure spite. Even if it gets easier, that doesn’t necessarily make it easy. No matter how the small connection that he has to possessions such as swords and a whetting stone, it’s a reminder that he can’t pack any of what really matters. Any of what he so desperately wants to take with him that he can practically feel his heart break at the mere thought of it.

While he packs his clothes, mask, and swords, Feya looks through old belongings of her husband’s that Zuko had never seen before. She had been keeping them in a cedar chest that Zuko had always thought was just for storage, not realizing it had been sentimental storage, never being curious enough, or brave enough, to look through her things. He had never thought of her as a sentimental person, but then again, she really only allows herself to show vulnerable emotion when she is alone. When there isn’t anyone there to see her fall apart. Not even her brother-in-law, her nephew, or even her sister.

She gives Zuko an older sleeping bag to keep him warm, a heavy coat that is almost comically big on him, thick socks, and gloves, all of which were her husbands. She also provides him with a water skin, herbs for common illnesses and wounds, and emergency rations, reminding him to eat what he needs to and not fall back into bad habits. That he will only end up hurting himself and by extension, his group.

After packing everything on Appa’s saddle, he stays in Kani and Feya’s arms until the last possible moment when Aang calls him to get on. Even though he had felt his heart break when saying goodbye to Iroh, this feels so much harder, despite only knowing them for three years. He isn’t sure if it is because he can have such an honest and safe relationship with these women, or if it is something else. Something that he couldn’t have back in the Fire Nation .All he knows is that he feels an almost impossible amount of pain well in his chest as they fly away as Zuko forces himself to keep a neutral face, clutching his turtle duck for support.

It’s afternoon by the time that they reach home. He can’t even see his house clearly when Appa begins to draw attention from the village, people looking up, gathering, and pointing up at the sky, talking amongst themselves about what could be flying over them at that size, and running out to look at Appa before they even have a chance to land. If Zuko saw this sight and wasn’t traveling with this group, he would be intrigued as well. So little happens in this village. Zuko will be eternally grateful for that. It gave him a chance to miss out on excitement in his life and just get to rest, recover, and be a normal boy for a few years.

When they land, Aang is held back by the growing crowd of farmers who never really have visitors, especially someone of importance. Of anyone of importance, really. Certainly not as important as the Avatar, the last hope that the world has for restoring balance, love, and peace.

While Aang and his friends are swamped by what looks like nearly everyone in the entire village, Zuko struggles through the growing crowd, looking for Chen. In the three years that he has spent here, he has never seen this many people in one place. They usually gather in small groups and mingle and meander around the area, entertaining and overall enjoying themselves.

Due to the small size of the village, Zuko knows that news travels incredibly fast, however, this seems ridiculously fast. But just about everyone saw Appa long before he landed, unable to hide his enormous body and everyone screaming at one another to come meet near the west edge of the village.

As soon as Zuko gets free, it only takes him a few minutes to find Chen who had also stopped working to see what the commotion is about. The moment that Zuko sees him, he throws himself into the farmer's large, safe arms, clutching at his robes, needing to remember exactly how safe and comfortable he feels when Chen holds him close, a silent promise that he would do anything and everything to protect Zuko from the world.

He can hear Chen asking some questions, mostly about what Zuko is doing here, what’s going on, and where Kani is, but all Zuko can do is bury his face in Chen’s shoulder, remembering the feeling of being held like this and all it had meant the past three years of his life. The best three years of his life. Needing to remember how lucky he is to have been found by such a kind man who had done so much to make Zuko feel safe, loved, and happy despite how difficult Zuko had proven to be the first few months. How lucky he was to have been found by a couple who had so desperately wanted to be parents but had been unable to conceive, making it so easy for them to want to take Zuko in as their own. Loving him, raising him, teaching how to expect kindness, and providing him with the first space that was truly safe for him where he didn’t need to lie to himself or hide his face from the world.

After several long minutes of Chen just holding Zuko close, running his fingers through Zuko’s loose hair, comforting him while trying to get answers out of him, Zuko begins to tell Chen everything as quickly and accurately as he can about the Avatar, and Zuko’s role in the war. It’s hard to get everything out as he tries to play down how much danger he put himself in, but then he would feel guilty for obscuring some of the truth to Chen, of all people, who had always been honest with him even when it had been hard. Then he felt guilty for sharing all the details and scaring his father who actually *cares* about Zuko’s wellbeing, and not just how Zuko can be used as a political prop in public and a punching bag in private.

It’s impossible to miss the sad look in Chen’s eyes at the mere thought of Zuko leaving, even as the man tells Zuko how proud he is of his son for playing such an important part in saving the world, commending him for his bravery and dedication to others. Zuko wishes that he could find a way to stay even though he is making the conscious choice to leave the best parts of his life behind.

Honestly, Zuko has somewhat expected Chen to be angry at the idea of Zuko just getting up and leaving with so little warning after all the couple had done for him for years. As Chen continues reminding Zuko how loved he is and to be safe, he realizes that a small part of him had *wanted* Chen to be angry.

It isn’t like the farmer to get angry, let alone express it, especially in front of Zuko despite Zuko having learned years ago that Chen would hardly ever raise his voice at Zuko or anyone, let alone a hand. Despite part of him having known that everything was going to change the moment that he stepped into that base whether or not Zuko could be identified, part of him didn’t want that to be true. He still wants to believe that he could have just helped Aang, made sure that he and his friends were alright, and then go their separate ways.

Over the past few years, Zuko has found family, friends, stability, and overall safety, something he had only ever had before when hiding in stolen moments in his mother’s or uncle’s arms. Even if he always knew that it wouldn’t last forever, and that his little world would be destroyed if he stayed and allowed the Fire Nation to win the war, he doesn’t want to step out of the first place he has ever truly felt safe. He doesn’t want to leave, even though he knows that it will make the world a better and safer place for many more people including himself and his own family. He knows that it is horribly selfish, but a part of him had wanted Chen to demand that Zuko change his mind, changing his path in life. He wanted Chen to hold Zuko in place, forbidding his son from walking out the door, choosing his destiny for him. He feels like the only way he could ever leave is if he is forcefully dragged out or if it is destroyed around him. Despite that, here he is, ready to step out of his own free will.

It isn’t until Chen walks over to the Avatar with Zuko, to get a chance to meet who Zuko would be spending the next year of his life with, when Sokka spots them from right outside the crowd. “Hey Zuko, hey Zuko’s dad!” The water tribe boy calls, waving and grinning at them. He looks a lot more friendly without the sarcastic smirk, delirious laughter, resting bitch face, or scowl that he has had the whole time that Zuko has seen him.

Zuko just awkwardly waves back, still standing close to Chen.

“Hey, kid, you one of the people my son is going to be traveling with?” Chen asks, offering Sokka a warm smile.

“You are looking at the Avatar’s personal bodyguard, the best warrior in the Southern Water Tribe, and the executive director of…plans and navigation.” Sokka replies with an over exaggerated bow with one arm in front of his stomach and the other out to the side. A style that Zuko has never seen and has no idea is part of Sokka's culture or if the other boy is just messing around. By his expression and the fact that neither Bato nor Hakoda did anything like that, Zuko can only assume that it is that latter. From what Zuko knows about the other boy’s personality, it checks out.

Zuko is somewhat surprised that Chen isn’t getting on Sokka for using Zuko’s real name. Then again, Zuko is about to leave and it’s not like it will be a secret for long. Zuko is easy to identify by description and likely isn’t just going with the Avatar as an inexperienced Earth Kingdom healer. There has to be a legitimate reason for Zuko to be going and the story of the Avatar’s firebending teacher dressed like a young Earth Kingdom man with the handprint burn across the left side of his face will inevitably reach back here.

Chen chuckles at Sokka’s description of himself, wrapping an arm around Zuko’s shoulder as he does. “By the time you guys head out, you’ll only be able to travel a few hours before it gets dark. What do you say to spending the night here? I can make sure you kids get something to eat and a good night’s rest before leaving tomorrow. Also I think your…pet can fit comfortably in the barn if you want. If not, it should be a nice night and he’ll be fine on the grass.” Chen offers, clearly completely unsure what to refer to Appa as. In his defense, Zuko still isn’t fully sure either.

Sokka doesn’t even think before answering, face lighting up with excitement . “Do you have any meat?”

“Of course we do. We live by the forest. We don’t just grow our food.” Chen reassures the Water Tribe boy.

“Katara! They have meat!” Sokka screams back at his sister who just gives him an irritated look. “They also have vegetables Aang if you want to sadly eat lettuce from the garden! It’s perfect!” Sokka adds even louder.

By that statement, Zuko can only assume that the airbender doesn’t eat meat. He doesn’t know too much about Air Nomad culture, but the belief that all life is sacred matches with the refusal to use another’s body as fuel for your own. Taking one life to sustain another’s. Zuko likes the idea but he isn’t sure how an entire culture strictly lived by that. Zuko had felt guilty with the knowledge of eating an animal he couldn’t dissociate from meat, but that doesn’t mean he fully understands an entire culture cutting it out. Then again, it may have made sense to people living in a time when Air Nomads did. Maybe they ate a lot of beans instead. He can already hear Fao making a joke about beans and fart bending in his head.

Aang doesn’t seem to hear Sokka as he is just sitting on his bison’s head, talking to the group of people who have formed around him and are all talking loudly. Zuko has no idea how long this group has been traveling together and Aang may have just learned to tune Sokka out most of the time. Zuko isn’t sure if Sokka is more fun or just annoying. Maybe he can be both. It’s really too early to tell and most of Zuko’s interaction with him is Sokka either trying to poke his eye out, or giving him good advice about his dad.

When people start turning to look at Zuko occasionally along with gestures and whispering, Chen brings Zuko inside. Sokka follows with the promise of meat, talking about how they have gotten to eat so little of it because Katara does most of the cooking and Aang is a vegetarian. The only meat Sokka has had a chance to eat is when he is able to hunt or fish for fresh meat and jerky that he can make or buy, the latter being more common. Sokka doesn’t have much time to hunt when they are making camp and his ability to find the time to make jerky is even more lacking.

Zuko can’t be sure if Sokka doesn’t notice the looks people are giving Zuko, is just ignoring them, or trying to distract Zuko from it. He doesn’t know the boy well enough to judge him properly. No matter the reason, it is nice to have Sokka’s voice to tune out that of the villagers. If Aang has mentioned that Zuko is going to be teaching him firebending, an idiot can put two and two together and realize that they have been living with a firebender in their midsts for three years. None of the voices sound angry, but they are judgmental and gossiping. He doesn’t like the idea that the people he has gotten to know, befriended, and love over the past three years are talking about him like he is a completely different person than the one they know. Like he still isn't just Lee who may be a firebender but had to lie about it for his safety, never once presenting any threat to the people around him. He was just trying to live. To be safe and happy like anyone wants. Like everyone needs.

Chen offers Sokka some jerky that they have in store under the condition that Sokka won’t raid Zuko’s bag for jerky in the night. It isn’t hard to tell that Chen is just messing with Sokka, not thinking that the boy would *actually* eat all of Zuko’s food, but he hadn’t seen the Water Tribe boy scarf down the chili like he hadn’t eaten in days and talk about meat like it was gold or the only thing that he could eat at all and not just something he likes. Sokka promises to keep his hands off of Zuko’s jerky as Chen fills a bag with various kinds for the Water Tribe boy. The look on Sokka’s face looks like the one of a man whose bag is being filled with bars of solid gold or being given the answers to the universe, not pretty average tasting jerky from a variety of common animals living in this part of the Earth Kingdom.

When Aang and Katara walk into the house, escaping the crowd, Sokka is just holding his bag open, laughing with excitement while Chen continues filling it with jerky, giving him an odd look. In Chen’s defense, Sokka *is* acting like a madman over a very common and accessible winter staple food. Chen makes sure that Katara has food as well and is even able to find some older dried sweet potatoes and beans for Aang, assuring the airbender that now that they have one less mouth to feed, the group doesn’t need to worry about putting Kani and Chen in any danger of malnutrition.

Even if that is true, that doesn’t mean that Zuko is not going to worry about his family. He’s going to miss curling up by the fire with Cabbage and his parents near him, talking quietly or absentmindedly resting a hand on Zuko’s arm or back to express love and affection. To remind Zuko that physical touch can be kind after years of seeing it as something cruel.

Aang explains everything to Chen as the man starts making dinner, listening to everything that the airbender says, finally giving in and allowing Zuko to help with preparations after trying to get his son to relax, go find Cabbage, or get to know his new friends. It’s less about Zuko not feeling like he can’t talk to the people he is going to spend at least the next year of his life with, and more about the fact that this may be his last domestic moment like this in this house. The last time that the man who saved and raised him mixes vegetables in a pan that Zuko cuts, occasionally resting a hand on Zuko’s shoulder, smiling at him. It all feels so familiar and yet so foreign. He is surprised that he hasn’t had to force himself to not cry.

They are almost done preparing dinner when Fao hurries into the house, tracking mud on the floor, holding Cabbage in his arms, setting the creature down on the ground before hugging Zuko. “You’re really leaving, Lee? Please don’t go.” His friend says, sounding like he is on the edge of tears. Between the two of them, Fao has definitely changed the least, going from eleven to fourteen. Then again, he plans on becoming a farmer like his moms, marrying a nice Earth Kingdom woman, and leading a pretty similar life to the one that he does now. There isn’t all that much that needed changing.

“It’s alright, Fao, I’ll come back, I promise. I told you that if I ever had to go I wouldn’t be gone forever. Anyways, if we stop the war, maybe I can show you the Fire Nation. And introduce you to turtle ducks that *don’t* bite when you try to pet them. I can also show you my favorite places and foods.” Zuko promises, really wanting to share the good parts of his home with his friend. He is sure that Fao would love to see where Zuko grew up and what he likes about his home.

The Fire Nation may be filled with horrible memories, but there are things that he really loved. Things that he still loves and misses. It will be nice to reminisce about those times in a new age for the world with his first real friend. If he needs to spend more time in the Fire Nation for awhile as Iroh ascends to the throne and begins undoing the last hundred years of damage, he’ll want someone there to remind him of his real home considering Kani, Chen, and Feya can’t really leave for an extended period of time without massive preparations.

“You promise?” Fao asks, not looking up or letting go.

“I promise. I’ll even let you throw rocks in the palace. Maybe even at the Fire Lord’s empty throne. I’m close with the person who was supposed to ascend to the throne instead of my– instead of Ozai.” Zuko corrects himself, unsure why he could tell three strangers about his heritage but not his best friend. Fao already knows so much about Zuko, just not that last little bit. Even if it takes Fao a moment to accept, he is sure that his friend will come to terms with it and still want to be friends. Understand that Zuko is nothing like his father and has personally seen and experienced the cruelty of that man.

“Really?” Fao asks, looking up at Zuko, both tears and excitement shimmering in his eyes.

Zuko nods and smiles. “Really.” He promises, meaning it. It may be one of his few good memories in the palace. If he needs to stay there longer than he would like to, he will need to make some new memories to push out the old. He needs something to drown out the screams from the ghosts of the past.

“Fao, do you want to stay for dinner? Lee is leaving in the morning. He’ll be back, but it may be awhile.” Chen offers, beginning to set dinner on the table, smiling warmly at Fao, understanding how close the two boys have gotten over the past few years.

Fao nods, sitting close to Zuko at the dinner table, Cabbage jumping into Zuko’s lap, yowling like he is some kind of famine victim when Zuko starts to eat his food, trying to swat it out of his hand.

Much to Chen’s dislike, Zuko gives little pieces to the cute, feathery creature. However, he doesn’t say anything, just looks at Zuko, unable to say the words knowing that his son would be leaving the very next day. All of it is difficult to work through. The last meal he will have here for a long time if at all if something happens to his home. The last time he’ll see his dad, best friend, and Cabbage in more than a year. He’s already had to say goodbye to his mom and aunt and even that is beginning to really set into his mind, the reality weighing on him more and more.

As they eat, Fao and Aang seem to get along pretty well as Fao tells Aang about how he should try and see if Zuko could burp fire because Zuko never had done so and Chen said no as well. Aang and Sokka seem to find that idea spectacular while Katara just looks exhausted with the two boys that she has been traveling with. Hopefully she’ll appreciate the fact that Zuko has no intentions of burping fire and has actually been taught to and enjoys cooking, taking some of the responsibility from her if she would like.

As they talk, Fao once again proves that he is nearly incapable of not talking with his mouth full as he tells Aang about Zuko teaching him sword fighting, bringing him candy, and making sure that Aang knows to make sure that Zuko eats. Zuko doesn’t really *want* these people to all know that he sometimes has trouble taking care of himself but he trusts that Fao means well and just wants to make sure that Zuko stays strong and healthy without Kani and Chen to soothe his anxiety when eating is nearly impossible. Zuko doesn’t say anything, not wanting to bring any more attention to the matter than necessary.

Thankfully, Fao doesn’t go into any more detail about Zuko not eating, only explaining that Zuko just sometimes forgets to or feels too tired to. He doesn’t talk about how Zuko’s anxiety will get so high that the very thought of eating makes him feel sick. Fao doesn’t know nearly as much about Zuko’s relationship with food as Kani and Chen do, but he understands that it is heavily tied to Zuko’s emotions and when he’s upset he’ll go as far as to starve himself when left to his own devices. That it’s something Zuko has very little conscious control over when he lets his emotions go unchecked. It’s embarrassing, but Zuko appreciates that his first best friend wants to make sure his new friends will take good care of him.

As the evening comes to an end, Chen suggests that Fao go and ask his responsible mom if he can stay the night so that he can certainly say goodbye to Zuko in the morning and will be able to spend more time with him. Fao rushes out the door and sprints back to his house to do just that before Chen can even finish talking.

Aang announces that he will be sleeping outside with Appa and Momo because he doesn’t want Appa to spend the night alone again. The siblings stay inside, Zuko offers his pallet up to either of them, wanting to sleep upstairs with Fao and Chen for the last night that he is going to be here for at least a year. It may not even look like this anymore when he gets back. He has no idea how this war will continue to unfold as time goes on. He needs to remember his home like this as best as he can.

Sokka calls dibs on the pallet immediately, flopping down on it and sticking his tongue out at his sister who tackles him only seconds later. Zuko can only assume that after years of sibling fighting they know each other’s limits well. Zuko smiles at them, but is once again jealous of the relationship that someone else has with their sibling. Bickering is nothing like fighting. Teasing isn’t the same as taunting. Scuffling isn’t anything like vicious attacking. Messing with someone isn't the same as manipulation. He really hopes that he has a chance to restart his relationship with Azula. Even if they aren’t particularly close, he wants to be able to talk to and spend time with Azula without walking away with fear, tears, or bruises.

Katara leaves the house and comes back in with a sleeping bag, laying it out by the fireplace, deciding to sleep inside while she has the chance, knowing that it won’t be particularly common on the open road. She sets it up near her brother, the two talking quietly like nothing had happened. They were only fighting over something relatively meaningless, not the kind of thing that weighs on either of their minds.

When Fao finally comes back he follows Chen, and Zuko up the stairs of the house with Cabbage walking behind them. Fao talks the entire time they walk up the stairs and settle into bed. Cabbage curls up against Zuko as if she knows that Zuko will be gone in the morning and this will be her last night to snuggle with him for awhile. Chen and Fao fall asleep on either side of Zuko, making sure that he feels safe and loved ,reminding him that he will be deeply missed while away and they will welcome him back with open arms when he finally comes home. Chen loosely wraps an arm around Zuko, keeping him close, not wanting to let go of his son while Fao just curls up facing his friend, not liking being touched in his sleep.

Even if it is going to be the last time he sees some of the people most important to him for a while, Zuko smiles at the reminder of how much his life has changed in the past few years. How his life is filled with people who love him unconditionally.

No matter how long it takes, no matter what happens or what changes, Zuko will come back here even if he’s convinced himself that they never want to see him again. He’s convinced himself of many things that don't hold a shred of truth. Things that his father’s venom fabricates in his mind, altering Zuko’s perception of himself and the people around him, warping his reality into something twisted and cruel. That’s how Ozai sees everything, and he did his best to break his son to make him see the world in the same way. Now Zuko needs to trust that these people will continue to be here for him. That he can leave and that they will still be here for him with open arms when he finally comes back. That he will stay in their minds and in their hearts until that day arrives and he is finally able to come home.

For one of the few times in his life, he can actually believe that without cruel, twisted lies working their way into his mind and soul. He knows that his new family would never cast him aside, but anxiety is nearly impossible to tame and Zuko has always been particularly bad at taming his emotions. The strong ones always prove far more difficult. As he drifts off to sleep between two people who have only shown him kindness the past few years, he almost feels as if his spirit may sing because he is able to enjoy a rare moment that he feels unconditionally loved and worthy. The goodbye is hard.

Making and eating breakfast seems to take forever but as soon as the moments pass, it feels as if they never even happened. Zuko remembers vividly cooking with Chen’s arm around his shoulders and Fao playing with Cabbage on the floor, but those moments all mash together blurring into a few moments. He remembers the Avatar and his friends talking loudly and discussing travel plans at the table as they eat while Zuko is barely able to pay attention, trying to just remember Fao, Cabbage, and Chen, but he feels as if he blinks and it is all passed. None of it feels real. Even though he is aware of every moment that is passing and tries to cherish it, it feels as if it was all a distant dream the moment that it passes and blends together with the past ones, no discernible memories of them.

All too soon, he says his final goodbyes to his family, Chen holding Zuko tight to his chest, Fao holding Zuko’s hand, nearly a third of the village gathered around, finally aware of who Zuko has really been this entire time and unsure how they should feel about a firebender living with them unsuspected for so long.

By the time that Chen lets go of Zuko, his vision is blurry with tears he refuses to let fall. He can’t say goodbye like that. He needs to hold himself strong, knowing that he will come back no matter how long it takes. He’ll be with his family again and they’ll be safe. He can publicly be a firebender and the village won’t need to worry that he may do something to harm them or, more likely, that the military will harm them for knowingly harboring him.

Forcing himself to picture the future for himself and his family, Zuko walks away from the man who had saved him in so many ways these past several years, allowing Sokka to help pull him onto Appa’s saddle.It isn’t until the village disappears from sight that Zuko allows his first tear to fall, unnoticed by anyone, promising himself he’ll find his way back here no matter what it takes.

### End Notes

#### Chapter End Notes

I still have exactly no idea what I am going to call the series. Any suggestion at all even if it is half baked I can at least build off of that. I am bad at things. Halp.

## Chapter 33: Summary

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

This is a summary of this whole story, don't read it if you want parts of this story to be a surprise.

If you have read this and there is something that you think that I have missed, let me know and I'll add it, I am very bad with summaries of any kind.

### Text

Important Characters and points:

Kani: Earth Kingdom woman living in the small farming village of Naofan as a farmer by trade but was trained as a healer back in her hometown Si Lang (harbor town that the episode ‘the storm’ took place in). She married a farmer, Chen, moving out to her current farming village and is Zuko’s adoptive mother. She is an earthbender who was never formally trained by through sporadic lesions from people she has met throughout her life she has become skilled in tilling fields with her bending and has honed basic construction skills. She is the one who healed Zuko and slowly helped him learn how to trust other people after he pretty much imprinted on her. She and her husband were so willing to take Zuko in as their son because 1) they felt really bad for him and were pretty confident that he wouldn’t survive out there alone and by the time it would be safe for him to leave they were attached to him, and 2) they had both wanted to be parents but one or both of them were likely infertile (never specified because they wouldn’t know unless they were cheating cheaters and it doesn’t really matter and they really only even told Zuko that they wanted but couldn’t have children so he would understand that the actually want him and they don’t feel obligated to take him in) and were more than happy to adopt a son who needed a safe and loving home. She teaches Zuko cooking and healing basics which he gets decent at and really enjoys.

Chen: Earth Kingdom man and is Kani’s husband. He is from a different village or rural area that I never specified because it was never important but comes from a very large farming family, making it easy to keep Zuko safe under the guise that he is one of Chen’s many nephew’s as no one could ever hope to keep track of all of them and certainly hadn’t met many of them. He told people that his nephew, Lee, was attacked by a firebender soldier when his town was attacked, resulting in the death of his parents and is coming to live with them because he no longer feels safe in his old home. Chen is the one who found Zuko half dead in the woods during a bad storm with his burn badly infected, took pity on him despite knowing that he is a firebender and really not caring because all he sees is a small child. He is also a blacksmith, not by trade, more because everyone lives far away from any truly skilled blacksmiths and if it is something that can be fixed by one of the few kinda skilled people in Naofan it’s worth it to not need to travel a full day by ostrich horse. Zuko helping him keep the forge at an even heat is part of what helps him learn how to not be scared of heat on his face for extended periods of time.

Feya: Kani’s younger sister who still lives in the harbor town, Si Lang, as a healer, taking over the healing hut after her and Kani’s mother died. She tends to be straight forward, aggressive, and incredibly protective over people who she cares about. She was once married but her husband was in the Earth Kingdom Navy, his fleet being called to help provide backup during the siege of Ba Sing Se as they could get there faster than the army and he presumably died there. The military never found his body and was unable to confirm or deny his death but some sailors from his fleet returned due to injury and he wasn’t with them and they hadn’t seen him. Being a healer and being one of the most observant people in the town, she hears a lot of rumors passing through from injured travelers passing by who need aid and the like. All she knows about Zuko when she goes to visit her sister is that he is 13, has a burn scar, is from the Fire Nation, and is a firebender. She is the first to figure out Zuko’s heritage as the Fire Prince, discussing it with Zuko leading to the two growing pretty close after lengthy discussion and weeks of Feya preparing herself for that possibility. She is an earthbender but rarely uses it as she was also never formally trained and she isn’t in a good location to mess around with the ground people are living on.

Fao: Zuko’s best friend who is about 2 years younger than him, lives next door and is a nonbender. Zuko teaches him sword fighting basics which helps him relearn how to balance and scan his surroundings with his new disability from his burn while Fao gets to learn a new, cool skill. Zuko shows Fao his bending, helping him settle more into his new home, feeling less isolated. They mostly just run around in the woods, sit by the fire, and do dumb young boy things, he helps Zuko learn how to just be a little boy for the first time and not need to act like an adult years before he is ready to. Fao has like, one brain cell and uses it to vibe.

Kyira: Fao’s younger sister. She doesn’t come up too much but she and Zuko get along pretty well, but for the most part she has friends her own age and plays with them. Both she and Fao’s biological father is out of the picture and they have two moms.

Gela: Fao and Kyira’s step-mother who is a very beautiful earthbender, lesbian woman who put the fear of God and Satan into men who tried to flip her and convince her that she should marry a man before she settled down with her wife, Shi. Gela is one of the most respected and intelligent people in the village and is the first to realize that Zuko is a firebender very quickly after meeting him.

Shi: Fao and Kyira’s biological mother who is a a nonbender bisexual woman who is just out her vibing, left a marriage that she could tell was going to get bad quickly when the worst hit her old village, fleeing when Fao was a baby and she was pregnant with Kyira. She met Gela who had been helping her get back on her feet, letting her rest while she didn’t need to worry about her children getting taken care of. It was supposed to be for a few months and she would then move on to the next village or town and figure out what she should do but it turned into a permanent situation. The two were never officially married but acted as such and everyone in the village went along with it, not really caring either way and honestly a bit too scared of Gela to fight her on it if they did have an issue.

Lo: The crazy old herbalist lady with Myuki. She is the person who grows the herbs and kinda running a medical practice herself while also providing herbs for Feya and the other healers who she works with. Kani takes Zuko to go talk to her because she has seen just about everything and might have some advice on how to help Zuko settle down in a place where he doesn’t feel like he belongs despite having good people around him and how to work past old traumas. She is the one who informs Zuko about the ability to heal with firebending, providing him with documentation from its inventor so he can try his best to learn and to teach it. Despite Song, Lo’s late wife (they were never officially married but had a ceremony and referred to each other as such), being the inventor, Lo requested that Zuko take credit for inventing firebending healing as the Blue Spirit so that no one would come to the conclusion that Lo had been knowingly harboring a firebending for decades, not wanting to risk the possibility, even if small, of incriminating herself for doing what she saw was right and still stands by.

Song: Lo’s long term partner and the woman who invented healing with firebending. She was a firebender who fled the colonies when she was a young woman and had befriended and eventually fallen for Lo (who knew that she was a firebender and where she was from) posing as an Earth Kingdom nonbender. She documented all of her research but wasn’t able to teach anyone about it, likely out of fear. She died from illness amplified old age a few years before Zuko came to the Earth Kingdom.

Gaon and Kya: Earth Kingdom couple living in Si Lang. Kya had a complicated and dangerous childbirth and was being treated in Feya’s healing hut. She is who Zuko first tried firebending healing on. It had complications at first (for Zuko) as it used a lot of energy and didn’t do too much. He managed to at least get her and the child out of danger before learning more about healing from Song’s notes and went back to refine his skill and help Kya and her newborn son. Both were fine, likely with permanent complications but they are both alive and pretty healthy, so, not much to complain about as they could go about their lives. They named the baby Lee after Zuko (thinking Lee was his real name). Kya is also a baker and made Zuko some baked goods for his birthday. That isn’t necessarily important to the plot in any capacity, but it is soft and he deserves it because he’s baby.

Cabbage: Chicken cat that Zuko befriended after a mental breakdown. Kani and Chen think it’s a dumb, annoying creature and didn’t really want her in the house but she got used to being a house chicken cat when they were letting Zuko sleep with her to help calm him down.

Po and Lee: They aren’t particularly important but they are disaster forest gays who made it possible for Chen to meet Iroh when he came to check on Zuko to see if he was really alive.

The Blue Spirit, Zuko’s alter ego, is a healer and teacher that is trying to redefine firebenders’ relationship with their bending opposed to being an assassin and thief. He heals people when he can and teaches other firebenders when he can who then teach others, spreading the urban legend and more importantly the message and skill, turning some away from violence as they relearn what their bending can be used for (not enough to end the war or anything, but enough to make some kind of impact)  
Iroh came to visit Zuko is Si Lang after Zuko sent a letter to Iroh posing as a soldier who served with Iroh in Ba Sing Se, adding details that Iroh had only done with Zuko, paranoid that Ozai might see the letter and come to find Zuko. While in the Earth Kingdom, Zuko’s new family didn’t like Iroh because of what he had done but were civil for Zuko’s sake. Feya swung a hot poker around in Iroh’s face and pretty much told him to go fuck himself and that Lu Ten’s death was on his hands when he tried to connect with her while Zuko was resting. Azula was horrified at the fact that Ozai couldn’t care less about the fact that he had killed his 13 year old son (everyone thought he was dead) and realized that she meant nothing to him past what she could do for him, getting closer to Iroh.  
Iroh had realized that he had probably done fucked up by not being more honest with Zuko and telling him about the white lotus. Azula doesn’t know everything about it, but she does know that he is ready and willing to make his opposition to the war clear when the time is right and that he won’t be alone in any capacity. Azula is ready and excited, mostly because she wants to commit treason and harm Ozai at this point, it being the right thing to do coming second. My girl has her priorities straight.  
Mai has spent a good portion of the three years of Zuko’s life in the Earth Kingdom in the palace with Azula, not wanting to deal with her father’s political career, her parents having a new child they actually want to pay attention to, and doesn’t want Azula to be around. I assume that Ozai generally couldn’t care less about what Azula does so long as it doesn’t distract her from her studies or training and doesn’t get in his way. Mai knows how to watch Azula to endure verbal and emotional abuse without reacting (because they both know it will make everything worse for her) and how to generally disappear when she knows that the powers at be don’t want to see her.  
Zuko really doesn’t like lying after being lied to and manipulated by Ozai and Azula his whole life and tries to avoid it whenever possible. Kani and Chen knew that his backstory was fake even if he wasn’t ready to share the truth yet by Zuko saying it straight out.

Basic plot:

Zuko flees after he wakes up from his Agni Kai without really thinking, his action driven by fear and shame, ending up half dead in the Earth Kingdom from injury and a bad storm Kani and Chen take him in, healing him and getting him back on his feet. He goes under the alias Lee and begins to learn how to take on the role of a farmer boy.  
It is a very difficult transition, Zuko having a lot of emotional issues due to a lifetime of abuse and feeling like he is a dirty secret despite knowing it is for his own safety and feels very isolated from himself, element, and culture. It takes a lot of work, talking to multiple people, and several breakdowns before he really begins to settle in his new home. Zuko has a lot of issues surrounding trust, abandonment, eating, being in small spaces, trying to be a perfectionist, and generally feels like he is just going to be thrown out for any reason. The first several months are really focused on Zuko’s new family trying to address these issues and help him work through them so they are at least manageable and continue working on them once he can act somewhat normally.  
When Zuko goes to town his first winter, he learns to heal and gets closer with Feya, Kani discovering his heritage when they get into town  
Iroh comes to visit Zuko during that winter, making sure that he is alright, is actually alive and is well taken care of and safe. He and Zuko’s new family don’t really get along but they try to stay civil in front of Zuko. Iroh doesn’t understand why Zuko has replaced his family and takes it somewhat personally but is overall happy that Zuko is with people who treat him well even if they are on bad terms.  
He relays this information to Azula and Mai when he gets back to the Fire Nation. Danger ladies are happy that bean bun is alright and it also means tha Iroh can focus more of his attention on Azula, not worrying about Zuko nearly as much.  
Zuko goes back to town the next spring and meets Hakoda and Bato. Hakoda had gotten yeeted off his ship with fire and jacked up his back. Zuko was able to heal him, make some connection, and hear Feya pretty much call Hakoda a dumb bitch multiple times. By harvest of that fall, the urban legend of the Blue Spirit has spread relatively far and there have been enough acts of desertion, lowered enlistment, and insubordination to cause a stir even if not enough to make a difference in the actual strength of the armed forces. Some firebenders are beginning to see themselves and their relationship with their bending and the rest of the world in a different light and people from the Earth Kingdom are willing to at least ask questions before shooting when seeing a lone or small group of Fire Nationals just trying to pass through.  
The following spring, Aang is captured by Zhao and brought to the base and as far as plot matters, it follows in a similar fashion to in cannon with the exception that Zuko just covers his face with cloth, not wanting to tarnish the reputation that the Blue Spirit has made as a healer with attacking a base and Aang actually takes Zuko back to the cave with Sokka and Katara opposed to making him a cute little leaf bed and having a philosophical discussion with him.  
They take the siblings back to Feya to be properly healed, Zuko says his goodbyes at the healing hut and back in Naofan and than heads on out with the Gaang to travel with them and be Aang’s firebending teacher.
